Needs to be documented.
## project directory
The submission command creates a project directory for the corresponding task, where the and CMSSW configurations are cached for later usage, avoiding interference with other projects. The project directory is named `crab_<request-name>`, where `request-name` is as specified by the parameter `General.requestName` in the configuration. The project directory is created inside the directory specified by the parameter `General.workArea` (which defaults to the current working directory). Thus, using the parameter `General.requestName`, the user can choose the project name, so that it can later be distinguished from other projects in the same working area.The project directory contains:
* A `.log` file, containing log information from the commands that were executed using this project directory.
* A `.requestcache` file with cached information of the task request and configuration.
* A directory called `inputs`, containing:
  + A file named `PSet.pkl` containing a pickled version of the process object from the users CMSSW parameter-set configuration.
  + A python file named  which basically loads the pickled process object saved in `PSet.pkl`.
  + A zipped tarball of the input sandbox with the users code.
* A directory called `results`, where the files retrieved via  `getlog`,  `getoutput` and  `report` are put.
### The .requestcache file
Each project directory contains a file named `.requestcache` with cached information of the task request and configuration. This information includes, among other things, the task name. When a user runs a command  `<command> --dir=<-project-directory>`, will look for that file inside the specified directory, extract the task name from the file and use it as input for the command. If does not find the `.requestcache` file in the specified directory, or the directory itself doesn't exist, it will print a message saying so:
```
Cannot find .requestcache file in  project directory <-project-directory>
```
or
```
<-project-directory> is not a valid  project directory.
```
Or if the task name is not known by the server:
```
Error contacting the server.
Server answered with: Execution error
Log file is <-project-directory>/.log
```
This evidently means that, if the `.requestcache` file is lost or corrupted, the user will not be able to execute commands for the corresponding task. The  [remake](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/CRAB3Commands#crab_remake) command can be used in this case to re-create the project directory, including the (relevant piece of the) `.requestcache` file, so that other commands can be executed again for that task.

##  configuration file
For convenience, we suggest to place the  configuration file in the same directory as the CMSSW parameter-set file to be used by .The expected default name of the  configuration file is , but of course one can give it any name (respecting always the filename extension `.py` and not adding other dots in the filename), as long as one specifies the name when required (e.g. when issuing the  submission command).In the configuration file is in Python language. It consists of creating a `Configuration` object imported from the `WMCore` library:
```
import CRABClient
from WMCore.Configuration import Configuration
 = Configuration()
```
Once the `Configuration` object is created, it is possible to add new sections to it with corresponding parameters. This is done using the following syntax:
```
.section_("<section-name>")
.<section-name>.<parameter-name> = <parameter-value>
```
##### Abbreviated configuration definition
Those lines can be simplified a bit by using instead the following which already defines all the `.<section-name>` objects, but the more
explicit above is more clear and it is the one most commonly used
```
import CRABClient
from CRABClient.UserUtilities import
```
###  configuration sections
The table below shows what are the sections currently available for  configuration.
| [Section](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/CRAB3ConfigurationFile?sortcol=0;table=2;up=0#sorted_table "Sort by this column") | [Description](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/CRAB3ConfigurationFile?sortcol=1;table=2;up=0#sorted_table "Sort by this column") |
| --- | --- |
| `General` | In this section, the user specifies generic parameters about the request (e.g. request name). |
| `JobType` | This section aims to contain all the parameters of the user job type and related configurables (e.g. CMSSW parameter-set configuration file, additional input files, etc.). |
| `Data` | This section contains all the parameters related to the data to be analyzed, including the splitting parameters. |
| `Site` | Grid site parameters are defined in this section, including the stage out information (e.g. stage out destination site, white/black lists, etc.). |
| `User` | This section is dedicated to all the information relative to the user (e.g. voms information). |
|  | For experts use only. |
#### Predefined  configuration file with empty skeleton
To simplify life a bit,  provides a function  that returns a `Configuration` object with pre-defined sections. The function is in the `CRABClient.UserUtilities` module. Users can import and use the function in their  configuration file:
```
from CRABClient.UserUtilities import  = ()
```
```
from WMCore.Configuration import Configuration
 = Configuration()
.section_("General")
.section_("JobType")
.section_("Data")
.section_("Site")
.section_("User")
.section_("")
```
###  configuration parameters
The table below provides a list of all the available  configuration parameters (organized by sections), including a short description. Mandatory parameters are marked with two stars (\*\*). Other important parameters are marked with one star (\*).
| [Parameter](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/CRAB3ConfigurationFile?sortcol=0;table=3;up=0#sorted_table "Sort by this column") | [Type](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/CRAB3ConfigurationFile?sortcol=1;table=3;up=0#sorted_table "Sort by this column") | [Description](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/CRAB3ConfigurationFile?sortcol=2;table=3;up=0#sorted_table "Sort by this column") |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Section `General` |  |  |
| `requestName (*)` | string | A name the user gives to it's request/task. In particular, it is used by  to create a project directory (named `crab_<requestName>`) where files corresponding to this particular task will be stored. to `<time-stamp>`, where the time stamp is of the form `<YYYYMMDD>_<hhmmss>` and corresponds to the submission time. The maximum allowed length is 100 characters, according to the formati in [RX\_TASKNAME![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/3801feebcb7f8c795c358ca4af05f53040754448/src/python/CRABInterface/Regexps.py#L24). Task submission will fail with "Incorrect 'workflow' parameter" if other characters are used. |
| `workArea (*)` | string | The area (full or relative path) where to create the  project directory. If the area doesn't exist,  will try to create it using the `mkdir` command. to the current working directory. |
| `transferOutputs (*)` | boolean | Whether or not to transfer the output files to the storage site. If set to `False`, the output files are discarded and the user can not recover them. to `True`. |
| `transferLogs (*)` | boolean | Whether or not to copy the  log files to the storage site. If set to `False`, the log files are discarded and the user can not recover them. Notice however that a short version of the log files containing the first 1000 lines and the last 3000 lines are still available through the monitoring web pages. to `False`. |
| `failureLimit` |  | The number of  that may fail permanently before the entire task is cancelled. Disabled by default. **Note:** a very dangerous parameter, for expert use, do not touch it unless you are sure of what you are doing |
| `instance (**)` | string | The  server instance where to submit the task. For users please use `'prod'`. |
| `activity` | string | The activity name used when reporting to . For experts use only. |
|  |  |  |
| Section `JobType` |  |  |
| `pluginName (**)` | string | Specifies if this task is running an analysis (`'Analysis'`) on an existing dataset or is running MC event generation (`'PrivateMC'`). |
| `psetName (*)` | string | The name of the CMSSW parameter-set configuration file that should be run via `cmsRun`. to `'pset.py'`. |
| `generator` | string | This parameter should be set to `'lhe'` when running MC generation on LHE files. Automatically set if an `LHESource` is present in the parameter-set. |
|  | list of strings | List of parameters to pass to the CMSSW parameter-set configuration file, as explained [here](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideAboutPythonConfigFile#Passing_Command_Line_Arguments_T). For example, if set to `['myOption','-param1=value1',--'param2=']`, then the  will execute `cmsRun JobType.psetName myOption -param1=value1 --param2=`. **NOTE:** No blanks allowed in `'param=value'` see the note about  below. |
| `inputFiles` | list of strings | List of private input files (and/or directories) needed by the . They will be added to the input sandbox. The input sandbox can not exceed 120 MB. The input sandbox is shipped with each job. The input files will be placed in the working directory where the users' application (e.g. cmsRun) is launched regardless of a possible path indicated in this parameter (i.e. only the file name at right of last / is relevant). Directories are tarred and their subtree structure is preserved. Please check the [FAQ](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/CRAB3FAQ#How_are_the_inputFiles_handled_i) for more details on how these files are handled. |
| `disableAutomaticOutputCollection` | boolean | Whether to disable or not the automatic recognition of output files produced by PoolOutputModule or TFileService in the CMSSW parameter-set configuration. If set to `True`, it becomes the user's responsibility to specify in the  parameter all the output files that need to be collected. to `False`. |
| `outputFiles` | list of strings | List of output files that need to be collected. If `disableAutomaticOutputCollection = False` (the default), output files produced by PoolOutputModule or TFileService in the CMSSW parameter-set configuration are automatically recognized by  and don't need to be included in this parameter. If publication in DBS is requested (the default) file names must obey DBS lexicon rules, in particular end with `.root`. If `Data.publication` is set to `False` any reasonable string will do. |
| `eventsPerLumi` |  | Deprecated. Use `Data.lumisPerFile` instead. |
| `allowUndistributedCMSSW` | boolean | Whether to allow or not using a CMSSW release possibly not available at sites. to `False`. |
| `maxMemoryMB` |  | Maximum amount of memory (in MB) a job is allowed to use. to 2000. The more memory you request, the more difficult will be to find a slot where to run your . Maximum for single core  is 5000. for multiple cores can be up to 2500\*numCores |
| `maxJobRuntimeMin` |  | The maximum runtime (in minutes) per job.  running longer than this amount of time will be removed. to 1315 (21 hours 55 minutes), see the note about `maxJobRuntimeMin` below. Not compatible with `Automatic` splitting. |
| `numCores` |  | Number of requested cores per job. to 1. If you increase this value to run multi-threaded cmsRun, you may need to increase `maxMemoryMB` as well.   In the CMSSW parameter-set configuration you may require also the number of streams to be larger than one per thread, which affects the memory consumption too. |
| `priority` |  | Task priority among the user's own tasks. Higher priority tasks will be processed before lower priority. Two tasks of equal priority will have their  start in an undefined order. The first five  in a task are given a priority boost of 10. to 10. |
| `scriptExe` | string | A user script that should be run on the worker node instead of the default cmsRun. It is up to the user to setup the script properly to run on the worker node enviroment.  guarantees that the CMSSW environment is setup (e.g. scram is in the path) and that the modified CMSSW parameter-set configuration file will be placed in the working directory with name `PSet.py`. The user must ensure that a properly named framework job report file will be written; this can be done e.g. by calling cmsRun within the script as `cmsRun -j FrameworkJobReport.xml -p PSet.py`. The script itself will be added automatically to the input sandbox. Output files produced by PoolOutputModule or TFileService in the CMSSW parameter-set configuration file will be automatically collected ( will look in the framework job report). The user needs to specify other output files to be collected in the  parameter. See [CRAB3AdvancedTopic#Running\_a\_user\_script\_with\_CRAB](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/CRAB3AdvancedTopic#Running_a_user_script_with_CRAB) for more information. |
| `scriptArgs` | list of strings | Additional arguments (in the form `param=value`) to be passed to the script specified in the `JobType.scriptExe` parameter. The first argument passed to the script is always the job number |
| `sendPythonFolder` | boolean | Obsolete. The 'python' folder in the CMSSW release ($CMSSW\_BASE/python) is always included in the sandbox |
| `sendVenvFolder` | boolean | Determine if the [=venv= folder![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cms-sw.github.io/venv.html) in the CMSSW release (`$/venv`) is included in the sandbox or not. Contrary to other , symbolic links found in `venv` are not dereferenced. to `False`. |
| `sendExternalFolder` | boolean | Determine if the 'external' folder in the CMSSW release ($CMSSW\_BASE/external) is included in the sandbox or not. See [https://hypernews.cern.ch/HyperNews/CMS/get/computing-tools/1972.html![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://hypernews.cern.ch/HyperNews/CMS/get/computing-tools/1972.html). to `False`. |
| `externalPluginFile` | string | Name of a plug-in provided by the user and which should be run instead of the standard  plug-in `Analysis` or `PrivateMC`. Can not be specified together with `pluginName`; is either one or the other. Not supported yet. |
|  |  |  |
| Section `Data` |  |  |
| `inputDataset (*)` | string | When running an analysis over a dataset registered in DBS, this parameter specifies the name of the dataset. The dataset can be an official CMS dataset or a dataset produced by a user or a Rucio DID as explain in [this FAQ](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/CRAB3FAQ#Can_I_use_CRAB_to_process_data_d) . |
| `inputBlocks` | list | A list of DBS block names in the `datasetname#uuid`. If present only those blocks will be processed, instead of the full dataset. The dataset in the block names must be the same as indicated in `inputDataset`. |
| `allowNonValidInputDataset` | boolean |  to run over (the valid files of) the input dataset given in `Data.inputDataset` even if its status in DBS is not VALID. to `False`. |
| `outputPrimaryDataset (*)` | string | When running an analysis over private input files or running MC generation, this parameter specifies the primary dataset name that should be used in the LFN of the output/log files and in the publication dataset name (see [Data handling in ](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/Crab3DataHandling)). |
| `inputDBS (*)` | string | The URL of the DBS reader instance where the input dataset is published. The URL is of the form `'https://cmsweb.cern.ch/dbs/prod/<instance>/DBSReader'`, where `instance` can be `global`, `phys01`, `phys02` or . The default is `global` instance. The aliases `global`, `phys01`, `phys02` and  in place of the whole URLs are also supported (and indeed recommended to avoid typos). For datasets that are not of `USER` tier,  only allows to read them from `global` DBS. |
| `splitting (*)` | string | to use to split the task in . When `JobType.pluginName = 'Analysis'`, the splitting can either be `'Automatic'` (the default, please read the dedicated [FAQ](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/CRAB3FAQ#What_is_the_Automatic_splitting)), `'FileBased'`, `'LumiBased'`, or `'EventAwareLumiBased'` (for Data the recommended is `'Automatic'` or `'LumiBased'`). For `'EventAwareLumiBased'`,  will split the task by luminosity sections, where each job will contain a varying number of luminosity sections such that the number of events analyzed by each job is roughly `unitsPerJob`. When `JobType.pluginName = 'PrivateMC'`, the splitting can only be `'EventBased'`. |
| `unitsPerJob (*)` |  | Mandatory when  is not `'Automatic'`, suggests (but not impose) how many units (i.e. files, luminosity sections or events - depending on the splitting - see the note about  below) to include in each job. When  `= 'Automatic'` it represents the  target runtime in minutes and its minimum allowed value is 180 (i.e. 3 hours). |
| `totalUnits (*)` |  | Mandatory when `JobType.pluginName = 'PrivateMC'`, in which case the parameter tells how many events to generate in total. When `JobType.pluginName = 'Analysis'`, this parameter tells how many files (when  `= 'FileBased'`), luminosity sections (when  `= 'LumiBased'`) or events (when  `= 'EventAwareLumiBased'` or  `= 'Automatic'` - see the note about "" below) to analyze (after applying the lumi-mask and/or run range filters). |
| `lumisPerFile` |  | When `JobType.pluginName = 'PrivateMC'`, this parameter specifies how many luminosity section will be presetn in each output file. It should be used only in very special and well motivated use cases. Note that every job starts with a fresh luminosity section, which may lead to unevenly sized luminosity sections if `Data.unitsPerJob` is not a multiple of this parameter. to 1. |
| `useParent` | boolean | Adds corresponding parent dataset in DBS as secondary input source. Allows to gain access to more data tiers than present in the current dataset. This will not check for parent dataset availability;  may fail with xrootd errors or due to missing dataset access. to `False`. |
| `secondaryInputDataset` | string | An extension of the `Data.useParent` parameter. Allows to specify any grandparent dataset in DBS (same instance as the primary dataset) as secondary input source.  will internally set this dataset as the parent and will set `Data.useParent = True`. Therefore, `Data.useParent` and `Data.secondaryInputDataset` can not be used together *a priori*. |
| `lumiMask (*)` | string | A lumi-mask to apply to the input dataset before analysis. Can either be a URL address or the path to a file on disk. Default to an empty string (no lumi-sections filter). |
| `runRange (*)` | string | The runs and/or run ranges to process (e.g. `'193093-193999,198050,199564'`). It can be used together with a lumi-mask. to an empty string (no run filter). |
| `outLFNDirBase (*)` | string | The first part of the LFN of the output files (see [Data handling in ](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/Crab3DataHandling)). Accepted values are `/store/user/<username>[/<subdir>*]` (the trailing `/` after `<username>` can not be omitted if a `subdir` is not given) and `/store/group/<groupname>[/<subgroupname>*]` (and `/store/local/<dir>[/<subdir>*]` if `Data.publication = False`). to `/store/user/<username>/`.  creates the `outLFNDirBase` path on the storage site if needed, do not create it yourself otherwise the file stage-out may fail due to permissions inconsistency.   **Note:** even if publication is disabled, the LFN needs to be a valid LFN name for DBS. So keep in mind that 1) name of first subdir after `username` (or `groupname` ) must start with a letter, not a number 2) do not use dot as separator inside names 3) LFN must end with `.root` |
| `publication (*)` | boolean | Whether to publish or not the EDM output files (i.e. output files produced by PoolOutputModule) in DBS. Notice that for publication to be possible, the corresponding output files have to be transferred to the permanent storage element. to `True`. |
| `publishDBS (*)` | string | The URL of the DBS writer instance where to publish. The URL is of the form `'https://cmsweb.cern.ch/dbs/prod/<instance>/DBSWriter'`, where `instance` can so far only be , and therefore it is set as the default, so the user doesn't have to specify this parameter. The alias  in place of the whole URL is also supported. |
| `outputDatasetTag (*)` | string | A custom string used in both, the LFN of the output files (even if `Data.publication = False`) and the publication dataset name (if `Data.publication = True`) (see [Data handling in ](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/Crab3DataHandling)). |
| `ignoreLocality` | boolean | to `False`. DO NOT USE |
| `userInputFiles` | list of strings | This parameter serves to run an analysis over a set of input files, as opposed to run over an full dataset from DBS. is: `Data.userInputFiles = ['file1', '', 'etc']`. When this parameter is used, the only allowed splitting is `'FileBased'`. There are two ways to use this.   **1)** as a fileMask, analogous to `inputBlocks`. If specified together with `Data.inputDataset` it must contain a list of LFN's and only the listed files will be processed from that Dataset. An error will be raised if some LFN does not belong to the input dataset.   **2)** as a pure "list of files" in case `Data.inputDataset` is missing. In this case 'fileN' can be an LFN (i.e. a string starting with `/store/`), or PFN (i.e. a string starting with `protocol-prefix://store/` like e.g. a pointer to an xrootd redirector [ref](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookXrootdService)). One could also have a local text file containing the list of input files (one file per line; don't include quotation marks nor commas) and then specify in this parameter the following: `Data.userInputFiles = open('/path/to/local/file.txt').readlines()`. Also, since there is no input dataset from where to extract the primary dataset name, the user must use the parameter `Data.outputPrimaryDataset` to define it.  will not do any data discovery and user must specify the locations where to run the  via the `Site.whitelist` parameter. |
| `partialDataset` | boolean | Allow to process input dataset that is only partially on disk. Normally, when  finds out that some files of the input dataset are not fully replicated on disk,  will issue tape recall to Rucio and wait for all files to be on disk before running the task. If `partialdataset` is `True`,  will submit task to condor immediately without request tape recall and process the files currently on disk. |
|  |  |  |
| Section `Site` |  |  |
| `storageSite (**)` | string | Site where the output files should be permanently copied to. See the note about `storageSite` below. |
| `whitelist` | list of strings | A user-specified list of sites where the  can run. For example: `['T2_CH_CERN','',...]`.  will not be assigned to a site that is not in the white list. Note that at times this list may not be respected, see this [FAQ](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/CRAB3FAQ#Why_are_my_jobs_submitted_to_a_s) |
| `blacklist` | list of strings | A user-specified list of sites where the  should not run. Useful to avoid  to run on a site where the user knows they will fail (e.g. because of temporary problems with the site). Note that at times this list may not be respected, see this [FAQ](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/CRAB3FAQ#Why_are_my_jobs_submitted_to_a_s) |
| `ignoreGlobalBlacklist` | boolean | Whether or not to ignore the global site blacklist provided by the Site Status Board. Should only be used in special cases with a custom whitelist or blacklist to make sure the  land on the intended sites. |
| `requireAccelerator` | boolean | to `False`. Set to `True` to request node for the . Please see [CMS Submission Infrastructure: GPUs monitor![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://monit-grafana.cern.ch/d/2qoPfS0Mz/cms-submission-infrastructure-gpus-monitor?orgId=11) to check sites and GPUs availability. |
| `acceleratorParams` | dictionary | to `{}`. When `Site.requireAccelerator` is `True`, this parameter dictionary will be used to specify detailed resource requirements for the . Please see [CMS Submission Infrastructure: GPUs monitor![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://monit-grafana.cern.ch/d/2qoPfS0Mz/cms-submission-infrastructure-gpus-monitor?orgId=11) to check 's `Memory`, `Capacity` and `Runtime` availability. See Example parameters below. |
```
.Site.acceleratorParams = {
    "GPUMemoryMB": "4000",
    "GPUMinimumCapability": "7.0",
    "GPUMaximumCapability": "8.0",
    "GPURuntime": "12.1"
}
```
|  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Section `User` |  |  |
| `voGroup` | string | The VO group that should be used with the proxy and under which the task should be submitted. |
| `voRole` | string | The VO role that should be used with the proxy and under which the task should be submitted. |
|  |  |  |
| Section |  |  |
| `oneEventMode` | boolean | For experts use only. |
| `asoConfig` | list of dictionaries | For experts use only. |
| `scheddName` | string | For experts use only. NB if you select a schedd on the ITB pool, remember to change the `collector` accordingly! |
| `extraJDL` | list of strings | For experts use only. |
| `collector` | string | For experts use only. |
![note.gif](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/note.gif) **Note for**  `= 'EventAwareLumiBased'`
When  does data discovery of the input dataset in DBS, the number of events is only known per input file (because that's the information available on DBS) and not per luminosity section.  can therefore only estimate the number of events per luminosity section in a given input file as the number of events in the file divided by the number of luminosity sections in the file. Because of that, `Data.unitsPerJob` and `Data.totalUnits` should not be considered by the user as rigorous limits, but as limits applicable on average.![note.gif](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/note.gif) **Note for** `maxJobRuntimeMin`
We strongly encourage every user to tune their splitting paramenters aiming for  to run for a few hours, ideally 8-10 hours, and set the `maxJobRuntimeMin` accordingly.
Having many  increases the chance of failure, since the number of problems is roughly proportional to the number of run . Moreover, short  suffer of start/end overheads resulting in poor CPU/Wall-clock ratio, which impacts negatively CMS and makes it harder to secure additional resources.![note.gif](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/note.gif) **Note for** `pyCfgParam`
Either `=value" ]` or `", "value" ]` are fine (the latter somehow more correct), but  `value" ]` will not work. You can use python's `shlex.split` to convert args from "the way you time them when running cmsRun interactively" to the correct . Example
```
import shlex
args = '--arg 1 --another-arg "my name"'
.JobType. = shlex.split(args)
```
results in
`['--arg', '1', '--another-arg', 'my name']` i.e. it correctly preserves quoted spaces etc.N.B. there has been reports years ago that params with double dashes may break things. Most likely it was due to (now very old and unsupported) old python and/or CMSSW versions. But if you get odd errors you may check for this and report.
![note.gif](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/note.gif) **Note for** `storageSite`
In the output files of each job are transferred first to a temporary storage element in the site where the job ran and later from there to a permanent storage element in a destination site. The transfer to the permanent storage element is done asynchronously by a service called AsyncStageOut (ASO). The destination site must be specified in the `Site.storageSite` parameter in the form `'Tx_yy_zzzzz'` (e.g. `''`, `'T2_US_Nebraska'`, etc.). The official names of CMS sites can be found in the [CRIC![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cms-cric.cern.ch) web page. The user MUST have write permission in the storage site.
## Passing  configuration parameters from the command line
It is possible to define/overwrite  configuration parameters by passing them through the command line when the ` submit` command is executed. Parameters can be set with the convention `<parameter-name>=<parameter-value>` and can be sequentially listed separating them with a blank space. Here is an example on how one would pass the request name and the publication name:
```
 submit -c my_crab_config_file.py General.requestName=my_request_name =my_publication_name
```
![note.gif](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/note.gif) **Note**: Currently it is only possible to overwrite the parameters that take as value a string, an , a float or a boolean. Parameters that take a list can not be overwritten this way.
## Converting a CRAB2 configuration file into a configuration file
is essentially new compared to CRAB2; it is not just a re-write. As a consequence, the configuration is different and there is no direct trivial translation that can be done automatically for every CRAB2 configuration file into a one. There is only a basic utility, called `crab2cfgTOcrab3py`, meant to help the user to convert an existing CRAB2 configuration file into a configuration file template. The user has to provide the name of the CRAB2 configuration file he/she wants to convert and the name he/she wants to give to the configuration file (both arguments have default values; `.cfg` and  respectively).
```
crab2cfgTOcrab3py [crab2confgiName.cfg] [crab3configName.py]
```
Instead of blindly taking the produced configuration file and run it, the user should always inspect the produced file, understand what each parameter means, edit them and add other parameters that might be needed, etc.Here we give a usage example. Suppose we have the following CRAB2 configuration file with the default name `.cfg`:
```
[]
jobtype                 = cmssw
scheduler               = remoteGlidein
use_server              = 0
[CMSSW]
datasetpath             = /GenericTTbar/HC-CMSSW_5_3_1_START53_V5-v1/GEN-SIM-RECO
dbs_url                 = global
pset                    =
number_of_jobs          = 100
events_per_job          = 20
output_file             = output.root
[GRID]
se_white_list           =
se_black_list           = T2_IT_Legnaro
data_location_override  =
[USER]
ui_working_dir          = my_CRAB_project_directory
return_data             = 0
copy_data               = 1
storage_element         = T2_IT_Legnaro
user_remote_dir         = my_remote_directory
publish_data            = 1
publish_data_name       = my_publication_name
dbs_url_for_publication =
```
If we run the tool without specifying any input parameters:
```
crab2cfgTOcrab3py
```
it will create a file  with the following content:
```
from WMCore.Configuration import Configuration
 = Configuration()
.section_('General')
.General.transferOutputs = True
.General.requestName = 'my_CRAB_project_directory'
.section_('JobType')
.JobType.psetName = ''
.JobType.pluginName = 'Analysis'
. = ['output.root']
.section_('Data')
.Data.inputDataset = '/GenericTTbar/HC-CMSSW_5_3_1_START53_V5-v1/GEN-SIM-RECO'
.Data.publication = True
.Data.unitsPerJob = 20
.Data.publishDBS = 'https://cmsweb.cern.ch/dbs/prod//DBSWriter/'
. = 'EventBased'
.Data.inputDBS = 'https://cmsweb.cern.ch/dbs/prod/global/DBSReader/'
. = 'my_publication_name'
.section_('Site')
.Site.blacklist = ['T2_IT_Legnaro']
.Site.whitelist = ['']
.Site.storageSite = 'T2_IT_Legnaro'
```
and it will show the following screen output:
```
Convertion done!
crab2cfgTOcrab3py report:
CRAB2 parameters not YET supported in :
CRAB2 parameters obsolete in :
```
As we already emphasized, the template configuration file produced by the `crab2cfgTOcrab3py` utility should not be used before carefully looking into its content. Along this line, one can see for example that the parameter  was set to `['output.root']`. If `output.root` is defined in the CMSSW parameter-set configuration file in an output module, then it doesn't have to be included in the  list (although it doesn't harm).
##

## Certificates, proxies and all that stuff
###  command fails with `to retrieve proxy from myproxy.cern.ch ...`
Show  Hide
can be due to a stale credential in `myproxy`.  client always tries to keep a valid one there, but there are some known edge cases where fails, e.g. [https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/5168![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/5168).Therefore you should remove credentials from `myproxy` and then issue the  commad again.
To remove stale credentials:
```
grep myproxy-info < project directory>/.log
# example:  grep myproxy-info crab_20160308_140433/.log
```
you will get something like
```
 command: myproxy-info -l ec95456d3589ed395dc47d3ada8c94c67ee588f1 -s myproxy.cern.ch
```
then simply issue a `myproxy-destroy` command with same arguments:
```
# example. In real life replace the long hex string with the one from your .log
myproxy-destroy -l ec95456d3589ed395dc47d3ada8c94c67ee588f1 -s myproxy.cern.ch
```
If things still fail after than, send the following in your [request for support](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideCrab#Getting_support), replacing the long hex string with the one that you found in .log (ec95456d3589ed395dc47d3ada8c94c67ee588f1 in the above example):
* output of `voms-proxy-info -all`
* output of `myproxy-info -d -l -s myproxy.cern.ch`
* content of you .log as an attachment
###  commands fails with =Error [UsernameException](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/UsernameException?topicparent=CMSPublic.CRAB3FAQ;nowysiwyg=1 " topic does not yet exist; you can create it."): Error contacting CRIC. =
Show  Hide
In particular  output contains something like
```
Error UsernameException: Error contacting CRIC.
Details follow:
  Executed command: curl -sS --capath /etc/grid-security/certificates --cert /tmp/x509up_u8516 --key /tmp/x509up_u8516 'https://cms-cric.cern.ch/api/accounts/user/query/?&preset=whoami'
    Stdout:
    Stderr:
      curl: (35) error:1407742E:SSL routines:SSL23_GET_SERVER_HELLO:tlsv1 alert protocol version
```
is known to happen with CMSSW\_7\_\* and very likley older releases as well both in and SL7.
The problem is with the version of `curl` binary in CMSSW release, which is not up to date with security requirements in modern https servers.Best is of course to use a more recent CMSSW release, but if you are really stuck in the past a workaround is
to issue command right after `cmsenv` **BEWARE WILL MAKE  WORK BUT BREAK YOUR gcc ENVIRONMENT**
 **YOU WILL NOT BE ABLE TO COMPILE OR scram build UNTIL YOU OPEN A NEW SHELL**
```
# for
source /cvmfs/cms.cern.ch/slc6_amd64_gcc700/external/curl/7.59.0/etc/profile.d/init.sh
# for SL7
source /cvmfs/cms.cern.ch/slc7_amd64_gcc630/external/curl/7.59.0/etc/profile.d/init.sh
```
##  setup
### Does  setup conflict with CMSSW setup
Show  Hide
No.  client runs within the CMSSW environment.
Make sure you always `cmsenv` before using
### I need to use a (old ?) CMSSW release where  client fails, what can I ?
Show  Hide
 is currently tested and compatible with any SL7 CMSSW release: CMSSW\_8,9,10,11,12
It is possible to use  for releases CMSSW\_7\_x using CMSSW singularity/apptainer container `cmssw_cc6`
There is an important caveat though:
* the CMS container does not have the `myproxy-*` commands, therefore from there `` commands can not create the long lived credential in myproxy.cern.ch needed to run a  tasks , nor verify it
* therefore if you need to use  on , you need to:
  1. take care of `myproxy` in separate SL7 session by executing a `` command at least once a week (e.g. ` createmyproxy`)
  2. make sure to have a valid local grid proxy to use in the container to connect to CMSWEB via `voms-proxy-init -voms cms -rfc -valis 192:00`
  3. tell  to use proxy and skip any attempt to check myproxy credentials
     + `` export X509_USER_PROXY=`voms-proxy-info -file` ``
     + ` submit --proxy=$X509_USER_PROXY ....`
     + and similarly for any other  command always
     + `  --proxy=$X509_USER_PROXY ...`
The same procedure as above can work for earlier CMSSW versions on , but those are not currently validated.,More information about CMSSW singularity containers at [http://cms-sw.github.io/singularity.html![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cms-sw.github.io/singularity.html).
##  configuration file
Documentation about the  configuration file: [CRAB3ConfigurationFile](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/CRAB3ConfigurationFile).
### What is the maximum memory per job (`maxMemoryMB`) I can request?
Show  Hide
 requests by default a maximum memory of 2000 MB. is the maximum memory **per core** all sites guarantee they will run. Some sites, but not many, offer a bit more (typically 2500 MB); and some sites even offer 4000 MB for special users. OTOH the pilot overlay framework (aka [GlideinWMS](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/GlideinWMS?topicparent=CMSPublic.CRAB3FAQ;nowysiwyg=1 " topic does not yet exist; you can create it.")) which CMS uses now allows to run also jobs which require more Memory at the cost of potentially leaving some CPU's ide. Idle resource are a problem for CMS and negatively impact our possibility to get computing resources, therefore requesting more memory than absolutely needed should be reserved for well justified cases.  still enorces reasonableness limits at =5+2\* ( -1)=GBytes.Users should try to stay with the default and only if needed increase it after having made sure that there are no memory leaks and no memory allocation bugs.![note.gif](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/note.gif) **Note**: In case of a multi-threaded job (`JobType.` > 1) most likely the default memory value is not enough. The user share of computing resources accounts for the requested memory **per core**.
### What is the `'Automatic'` splitting mode?
Show  Hide
The `Data.splitting` parameter has [now![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://hypernews.cern.ch/HyperNews/CMS/get/computing-tools/3578.html) a default value: `'Automatic'`.
With such a setting the task processing is split into three stages:
1. A "probe" stage, where some probe jobs are submitted to estimate the event throughput of the CMSSW parameter-set configuration provided by the user in the `JobType.psetName` parameter and possible further arguments. Probe jobs have a job id of the form `0-[1,2,3,...]`, they can not be resubmitted and the task will fail if none of the probe jobs  successfully. The output files transfer is disabled for probe jobs.
2. A "main" stage, very similar to the conventional stage for other splitting modes, in which a number of main jobs (automatically determined by the probe stage) will process the dataset. These jobs can not be manually resubmitted and have a fixed maximum runtime (specified in the `Data.unitsPerJob` parameter), after which they gracefully stop processing input data. The remaining data will be processed in the next stage (tail) and their jobs labelled as "rescheduled" in the main stage (in the they will always appear as "failed").
3. Some possible "tail" stages. If some main job does not finish successfully ("rescheduled" in the previous stage) or does not completely process the amount of data assigned to it due to the automatically configured maximum job run time, tail jobs are created and submitted in order to fully process the dataset. Tail jobs have a job id of the form `n-[1,2,3,...]`, where `n=1,2,...` represents the tail stage number. For small tasks, less than 100 jobs, one tail stage is started when all jobs have completed (successfully or failed). For larger tasks, a first tail stage collects all remaining input data from the first 50% of completed jobs, followed by a stage that processes data when 80% of jobs have completed, and finally a stage collecting leftover input data at 100% job completion.
   Failed tail jobs can be manually resubmitted by the users.
Once the probe stage is completed, the plain ` status` command shows only the main and tail jobs. For the list of all jobs add the `--long` option.In the short format of ` status` command the total number of jobs is computed by removing from the list of main jobs those which "failed" and are being "rescheduled" and adding the current number of "tail" jobs. Note that the total number of submitted jobs will increase at every "tail stage" and that the grafana will instead show every job : probes plus main plus tails, therefore the total number of jobs in the will be different from what printed by ` status`. As usual: when in doubt, trust ` status` output.**IMPORTANT NOTE** : there is evidence that ` resubmit` does not work well with automatic splitting. We can not fix in the current code. Hopefully a long-due rewriting of how jobs resubmissions are managed will make it possible in the near future. In the meanwhile users can use the new ` recover` command to create a new task which will process what could not be done by the automatic machinery.
### Should I use Automatic splitting or or ... ?
Show  Hide
PRELIMINARY WRITEUP
 tries to support these two use case. For which the only solution was `--` when we initially introduced and so many users are stickting to it
1. quick check that runs with
2. some preliminary look at time/memory usage for tuning splitting
But other tools are now availalbe (` preparelocal` and `Automatic Splitting`) which are better suited for :
1. can be done with preparelocal, but we need to write down some details on how to it and possibly add some options to make it easy. Work currently planned for 2022.
2. one of the main for introducing automatic splitting (by the way by the very same people who developed --) was the fact that does a poor estimate of running time and memory needs, since it only samples the first events of the first file. Many datasets show large variations from one lumi to another for those, and there are also variations due to the hardware jobs are executed on. So automatic splitting runs 5 jobs which sample random files and run about 15min each, and has a refined way to recover jobs which did not fit the initial guess. latter part is the real strong point for automatic splitting.
    Of course there are times when the automatic split machinery may be an overkill, and running on a handful of events is good enough to decide how to organize the processing. One could certainly submit a  task which only processes one lumi. Or simply run cmsRun locally. Of course performance on lxplus can randomly be much better of much worse than on the grid, and so any estimate obtained there or on a local desktop should be taken with care before extrapolating to a possibly large task.
    A "probe" task on a small fraction of a large dataset is always a very good thing.
### Can I use  to process data described only as a Rucio container ?
Show  Hide
Yes. You can indicate a Rucio DID (`scope:containerName`) as input to a  job in the `Data.inputDataset` configuration parameter:
```
JobType.inputDataset = 'user.belforte:/GenericTTbar/belforte-crab_20230306_162534-94ba0e06145abd65ccb1d21786dc7e1d/USER'
```
Important Notes:
* feature is meant to address the use case of dataset produced by previous  tasks, but not saved in or files simply placed in `/store/user/username/...` at some site leaving to the user the creation and fillings of the Rucio container. A properly formed Rucio container is also a byproduct of running standard  tasks using Rucio for Asynchronous Stage Out (i.e. sending outpu to `/store/user/rucio/username/...`
* is not meant to be an alternative way to access official CMS data described in .
* Proper creation of a Rucio container is not described here
* Each file replica must be registered on a **disk** CMS RucioStorageElement (RSE)
* There is no tape recall
* The `containerName` needs to follow CMS dataset naming syntax (like all DIDs in CMS instance of Rucio). Then  will use Rucio to find blocks (in term) location and file names and create jobs as usual.
* ![, important](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/.gif ", important") Since Rucio does not have run/lumi/event information, you can only use `fileBased` splitting, and can not ask for parents or secondary datasets which rely on lumi information to connect primary/secondary files.
* ![, important](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/.gif ", important") Since there is no tape recall, if some Rucio-datasets/-blocks not have full disk replica(s), they will be skipped and  will process what's available
### My dataset is (partially) on tape (and partially on disk), how can I process it with ?
Show  Hide
When the input dataset is not fully on disk,  automatically creates Rucio's rule to CMSRucio to copy data from the tape site to any site with available disk space.  task status will change from `NEW` to `TAPERECALL`.
Every 4 hour,  pickup `TAPERECALL` task and check Rucio's rules. If the rule changes state from `REPLICATING` to `OK`,  will change the task status back to `NEW`, waiting for the main thread to process it like the usual tasks.
We call procedure **"automatic tape recall"**.Note that recall of the whole dataset in  works only for `AOD` tiers. other data tiers are usually very large, and hardly needed in their entirety.Another option is to force  to process only data currently available on disk via `Data.partialDataset = True` parameter to skip all tape recall procedures.As an example of use of `Data.inputBlocks` parameter: let's assume we want to recall `/ZeroBias/Commissioning2021-v1/RAW#214fbb11-2d5c-4b8c-8ee5-b68de1d89153` and `/ZeroBias/Commissioning2021-v1/RAW#8760f6e6-6c5e-4c65-854d-02d4bc3312c5` from [/ZeroBias/Commissioning2021-v1/RAW![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cmsweb.cern.ch/das/request?instance=prod/global&input=block+dataset%3D%2FZeroBias%2FCommissioning2021-v1%2FRAW) dataset. will be:
```
JobType.pluginName = 'Analysis'
Data.inputDataset = '/ZeroBias/Commissioning2021-v1/RAW'
Data.inputBlocks = [
    '/ZeroBias/Commissioning2021-v1/RAW#214fbb11-2d5c-4b8c-8ee5-b68de1d89153',
    '/ZeroBias/Commissioning2021-v1/RAW#8760f6e6-6c5e-4c65-854d-02d4bc3312c5',
]
# or provide only block UUID
#Data.inputBlocks = [
#    '214fbb11-2d5c-4b8c-8ee5-b68de1d89153',
#    '8760f6e6-6c5e-4c65-854d-02d4bc3312c5',
#]
```
##  cache
### User quota in the  cache
Show  Hide
**There is no quota on  Cache anymore**The  User File Cache, or  cache for short, is the place where:
* the  client puts the user input sandboxes when submitting a task to the  server;
* the  client puts the `.log` files when they are uploaded via ;
* the  server puts the archives produced by the dry run submissions;
* etc.
### What is the maximum allowed size of the user input sandbox?
Show  Hide
120 MB.
### What are the files  adds to the user input sandbox?
Show  Hide
 adds to the user input sandbox the following directories/files, when a directory is incuded all the containted subdirectories are also recursively included:
* The directories `$/`, `$/biglib`, `$/module` and `$//SCRAM/hooks` . One can also tell  to include the directory `$/python` by setting `JobType.sendPythonFolder = True` in the  configuration. One can also tell  to include the directory `$/venv` by setting `JobType.sendVenvFolder = True` in the  configuration.
* Any `data`, `interface` and `python` directory recursively found in `$/src`.
* All additional directories/files specified in the  configuration parameter `JobType.inputFiles`.
* The original  configuration file (added as `debug/`).
* The original CMSSW parameter-set configuration file (added as `debug/originalPSet.py`).
* The tweaked CMSSW parameter-set configuration file in pickle format (added as `PSet.pkl`) plus a simple `PSet.py` file to load the pickle file.
All symbolic links found in those directories are dereferenced (i.e. replaced with actual file content) to make sure that when sandbox is restored on grid nodes nothing is missing. **Except** the content of `$/venv` directory where symbolic links are preserved
### How are the inputFiles handled in the user input sandbox?
Show  Hide
**Note**
* The user application (be it `cmsRun` or `scriptExe` ) is executed with current directory set to the intial working directory of the job, usually `/srv` in the "Singularity era, circa 2022/3.."
* The user sandbox is expanded in the `$` directory in execution machine. Usually `/srv/CMSSW_X_Y_Z/`. So that all files and directories tarred from the original scram tree on the client are restored in the right place.
Depending on whether filenames or directories are used in the `JobType.inputFiles` parameter, the directory structure inside the sandbox may be different and affect where the files are placed in the working directory of the job.
* Specific file names are always added to the root directory of the sandbox, whether an absolute or relative file name is used. For example, both `/afs/cern.ch/user/e/erupeika/supportFiles/foo.root` or `myfiles/foo.root` will appear as `foo.root` in the sandbox and will be extracted as `foo.root` to the job's root working directory.
* The directory structure inside each additional input file directory is maintained in the sandbox. The additional directories themselves will be located in the root directory of the sandbox. For example, if a directory `foo` with files `bar1` and  inside it is specified in the inputFiles parameter, the sandbox will contain `foo`, `foo/bar1` and `foo/` (the working directory of the job will therefore also contain a directory `foo` with files `bar1` and ).
* For example if your application expects to find `mydir/file1` you should put in  configuration `.'` and of course avoid having extra stuff in that directory. While if you put `Data.inputFiles='mydir/file1'` your application needs to open `file1`
## Stageout and publication
Documentation about (input/output) data handling in : [Crab3DataHandling](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/Crab3DataHandling).
### What are the allowed stageout LFN paths with ?
Show  Hide
 allows only the following LFN directory paths for stageout:
* `/store/user/[rucio/]<username>[/<subdirs>]` where `username` is the CERN primary account username;
* `/store/group[/rucio]/<groupname>[/<subdirs>]` where `groupname` can be any already existing directory under `/store/group/`.
If not publishing, `/store/local/<dir>[/<subdirs>]` is also allowed.If `/rucio` is present,  will use Rucio for stageout. User will need to have Rucio quota at the destination storage site.These are all the allowed paths that can be set in the  configuration parameter `Data.outLFNDirBase`. If any other path is given, the submission of the task will fail.
### Can I stage out my files into a `/store/user/` area that uses a different username than the one of my CERN primary account?
Show  Hide
Short answer: No.
Explanation and details:
 will look up for the user's username registered in CMS (which is the username of the CERN primary account) using for the query the user's DN (which in turn is extracted from the user's credentials) and will try to stage out to `/store/user/<username>/` (by default). If the store user area uses a different username, it’s up to the destination site to remap that (via a symbolic link or something similar). The typical case is Fermilab; to request the mapping of the store user area, FNAL users should follow the directions on [the usingEOSatLPC web page![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://uscms.org/uscms_at_work/computing/LPC/usingEOSAtLPC.shtml#createEOSArea) to open a ServiceNow ticket to get fixed.To prevent stage out failures, and in case the user has provided in the `Data.outLFN` parameter of the  configuration file an LFN directory path of the kind `/store/user/[<some-username>/<subdir>*]` (i.e. a store path that starts with `/store/user/`),  will check if `some-username` matches with the globally unique username extracted from the credential. If it doesn't, it will give an error message and not submit the task. The error message would be something like :
```
Error contacting the server.
Server answered with: Invalid input parameter
 is: The parameter Data.outLFN in the  configuration file must start with either '/store/user/<username>/' or '/store/group/<groupname>/' (or '/store/local/<something>/' if publication is off), wher...
```
Unfortunately the " is:" message it cut at 200 characters. The message should read:
```
 is: The parameter Data.outLFN in the  configuration file must start with either '/store/user/<username>/' or '/store/group/<groupname>/' (or '/store/local/<something>/' if publication is off), where username is your username as registered in CMS services (i.e. the username of your CERN primary account).
```
A similar message should be given by [ checkwrite](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/CRAB3Commands#crab_checkwrite) if the user does ` checkwrite --site=<CMS-site-name> --lfn=/store/user/<some-username>`.
### Why is  not transferring an output file?
Show  Hide
First of all, does  know at all that the job should produce the output file in question? To check that, open one of the job log files linked from the task monitoring pages. Very close to the top it is printed the list of output files that  expects to see once the job finishes (shown below is the case of job number 1 in the task):
```
======== HTCONDOR JOB SUMMARY at ... START ========
 ID: 1
Execution site: ...
Current hostname: ...
Destination site: ...
Output files: my_output_file.root=my_output_file_1.root
```
If the output file in question doesn't appear in that list, then  doesn't know about it, and of course it will not be transferred. doesn't mean that the output file was not produced; it is simply that  has to know beforehand what are the output files that the job produces.If the output file is produced by either PoolOutputModule or TFileService,  will automatically recognize the name of the output file when the user submits the task and it will add the output file name to the list of expected output files. On the other hand, if the output file is produced by any other module, the user has to specify the output file name in the  configuration parameter  in order for  to know about it. Note that parameter takes a python list, so the right way to specify it is:
```
. = ['my_output_file.root']
```

###  submit fails with `"Block ... contains more than 100000 lumis."`
Show  Hide
The message is self explaining.  server will die due to lack of memory if it needs to process luminosity lists with millions of entries per block.
There are two known cases where can happen:
* MC datasets which have been created with improper use of lumisections. MC lumi sections have no relation with luminosity but are used only to allow processing less than a file in one job via split by , in case it makes no sense to have more lumis than events.
* or similar super-extra-high compact event formats where one year of data fits in a few files
Those dataset can only be processed if  can ignore the lumi-list information, i.e. using `Data.splitting = 'FileBased' **and** avoiding any extra request which would eventually result in the need to use lumi information. means no run range, no lumi mask, and no secondary dataset (since  will need to use to match input files from the two datasets). Note that `useParent` is allowed since in that case  uses parentage information stored in to match input files.In practice your file must have:
```
Data.splitting = 'FileBased'
Data.runRange = ''
Data.lumiMask  = ''
```
( the paremeters with an assigned null value ``` `` ``` can be omitted, but if present must indicate the null string )and must **NOT** contain the following parameter
```
Data.secondaryInputDataset
```
###  fails to resubmit some jobs
Show  Hide
It is important that you as a user are prepared for to happen and know how to remain productive in your physics analysis with the least effort.
While there is a long tradition of "resubmit them until they work", is hardly useful any more. And while we can't prevent users from trying we can not guarantee that it will work, nor that resubmitted jobs will succeed.In the case where the missing data sample is important, the best recommendation we can give to users is to
**USE GENERAL/GENERIC RESCUE PROCEDURES, RATHER THEN TRY AT ALL COSTS TO REVIVE A DEAD TASK**.
We will always welcome problem reports and will try to improve when resubmission failures can be due to  internals, but surely you not want to hold your breath in the meanwhile.The safest path is therefore:
1. let running jobs die or  and dust settle
2. use  klill to make sure everything stops
3. take stock of what's published in at that point and make sure that it matches what's on disk
   * if your output is not in , you can use ` report`, but while information is available forever,  commands on a specific task may not
4. assess whether it is more important to get the last percentage of statistics or go on with other work. you **really** need 100% completion in task ?
5. if full statistics is needed, create a recovery task for the missing lumis and run it writing to the same dataset as the original task.
Recovery task is an important concept that can be useful in many circumstances. Please find instructions [in FAQ](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/CRAB3FAQ#Recovery_task)At the other extreme there's: forget about , and resubmit a new task with new output dataset.
In between it is a murky land where many recipes may be more efficient according to details, but no general simple rule can be given and there's space for individual creativity and/or desperation.

###  code 50660
Show  Hide
 code 50660 means "Application terminated by  because using too much RAM (RSS)" (as documented [here](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/JobExitCodes)). The amount of RAM that a job can use on a grid node is always limited and if memory need keeps increasing as the job run (so called "memory leak") the job will need to be killed. Grid sites used by CMS guarantee at least 2.5 of RAM per core, so allowing for some overhead,  default is to ask 2GB per job. is usually enough to run full RECO and user jobs should not normally need more. So the user first action when getting error is to make sure that code is not leaking memory nor allocating useless large structures. If more RAM is **really** needed, it can be requested via the `JobType.maxMemoryMB` parameter in  configuration file. Uselessly requesting too much RAM is very likely to result in wasted CPU (we will run less jobs then there are CPU cores available in a node, to spread the available RAM in fewer, larger, chunks), so you have to be careful, abuse will be monitored and tasks may get killed.Each user is responsible for her/his code and needs to make sure that memory usage is under control. Various tools exist to identify and prevent memory leaks in C++ which are not in  documentation scope. Generally speaking when investigating memory usage you want to make sure that you run on the same input as one job which resulte in memory problems, as usage can depend on number, sequence and kind of event processed. User may also benefic from the [ preparelocal](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/CRAB3Commands#crab_preparelocal) command to replay one specific job interactively and monitor memory usage.An important exception is in case the user runs multi-threaded applications, in particular CMSSW. In that case a single job will use multiple cores and not only can, but must use more than the default 2GB of RAM. It is up to the user to request the proper amount of memory, e.g. after measuring it running the code interactively, or by looking up what Production is using in similar workflows. As a generic rule of thumb, (1+1\*num\_threads) may be a good starting point.

##  Client API
### Multiple submission fails with a CMSSW "duplicate process" or "A different CMSSSW configuration was already cached" error
Show  Hide
The general problem is that CMSSW parameter-set configurations don't like to be loaded twice. In that respect, each time the  client loads a CMSSW configuration, it saves it in a local (temporary) cache identifying the loaded module with a key constructed out of the following three pieces: the full path to the module and the python variables `sys.path` and `sys.argv`.A problem arises when the  configuration parameter `JobType.pyCfgParams` is used. The arguments in `JobType.pyCfgParams` are added by  to `sys.argv`, affecting the value of the key that identifies a CMSSW parameter-set in the above mentioned cache. And that's in principle fine, as changing the arguments passed to the CMSSW parameter-set may change the event processor. But when a python process has to more than one submission (like the case of multicrab for multiple submissions), the CMSSW parameter-set is loaded again every time the `JobType.pyCfgParams` is changed and may result in "duplicate process" errors. Below are two examples of these kind of errors:
```
CmsRunFailure
CMSSW error message follows.
An exception of category 'Configuration' occurred while
   [0] Constructing the EventProcessor
   [1] Constructing module: class=...... label=......
:
Duplicate Process The process name ...... was previously used on these products.
Please modify the configuration file to use a distinct process name.
CmsRunFailure
CMSSW error message follows.
An exception of category 'Configuration' occurred while
   [0] Constructing the EventProcessor
:
MessageLogger PSet:
in vString categories duplication of the string ......
The above are from MessageLogger configuration validation.
In most cases, these involve lines that the logger configuration code
would not process, but which the cfg creator obviously meant to have effect.
FATAL ERROR: A different CMSSSW configuration was already cached.
 Either configuration file name or configuration parameters have been changed.
 But CMSSW configuration files can't be loaded more than once in memory.
```
One option would be to try to not use `JobType.pyCfgParams`. But if is not possible, the more general *ad-hoc* solution would be to fork the submission into a different python process. For example, if you are doing something like documented in [Multicrab using the crabCommand API](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/CRABClientLibraryAPI#Multicrab_using_the_crabCommand)
then we suggest to replace each
```
submit()
```
by
```
from multiprocessing import Process
p = Process(target=submit, ,))
p.start()
p.join()
```
(Of course, `from multiprocessing import Process` needs to be executed only once, so put it outside any loop.)

## More on  tasks
### Recovery task
Show  Hide
#### Recovery task: What
Recovery task is an important concept that can be useful in many circumstances.The general idea is that a  task has run to completion, all re-submission attempts done, but some of the necessary input data was not processed.
A recovery task will run the same executable and configuration on the missed input data, and will add results to the same output destination (and dataset) as the original task.
#### Recovery task: Why
 developers try hard to give you a tool with perfect bookkeeping and full automation which brings each task to 100% success. Similarly strive the operators of the global CMS submission infrastructure (aka HTCondor pool, aka glideIn) and the administrator of the many sites that contribute hardware resources for CMS data analysis. Yet at times things can go wrong, and we may not be able to investigate and fix every small glitch, and surely never within hours or days.It is to guarantee that a given task will always  to 100% success in a short amount of time. At the same time it is to make sure that all desired input data is available when the task is submitted.
Moreover both good sense and experience show that the larger a task is, the larger is the chance it hits some problem. Large workflows therefore benefit from the possibility to run them sort of iteratively, with a short (hopefully one or two at most) succession of smaller and smaller tasks.
#### Recovery task: When
A partial list of real life events where a recovery task is user's fastest and simplest way to get work done:
* Something went wrong in the global infrastructure and some jobs are lost beyond recovery
* Something went wrong inside  (bugs, hardware...) which can't be fixed by ` resubmit` command
* Some site went down for longer than it make sense to keep jobs in the queue
* Some data was not available and had to be retransferred and took longer than... see above
* More data have been added to the input dataset since the original task ran (pretty much as the above)
* A new lumimask was prepared were lumis declared bad earlier are now good
* ... more ...
#### Recovery task: How
You must of course have around the original
* scram project area
*  configuration file including the pset and any other file referenced in there
* original  project directory if you did not publish output in
The procedure to generate a recovery task is based on these simple steps:
1. issue a ` kill` . Killing the current task will guarantee that no change happens anymore
2. make a list of lumis present in the desired input dataset (listIn)
3. make a list of lumis successfully processed by original  task A (listA)
4. submit a new  tasks B which process the missing lumis (listB = listIn - listA)
Details are slighly different if you published output in or not:
**output in**
:   follow the procedure in  [FAQ](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/CRAB3FAQ#Dealing_with_a_growing_input_dat)
**output not in**
:   follow the procedure in  [example](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookCRAB3Tutorial#Re_analyzing_the_missing_luminos)

Show  Hide
While data taking is progressing, corresponding datasets in and lumi-mask files are growing. Also data quality is sometimes improved for already existing data, leading to updated lumi-masks which compared to older lumi-masks include luminosity sections that were previously filtered out. Both of these situations lead to the common case where one would like to run a task (lets call it task B) over an input dataset partially analyzed already in a previous task (lets call it task A), where task B should skip the data already analyzed in task A.can be accomplished with a few lines in the  configuration file, see an annotated example below.
```

from FWCore.PythonUtilities.LumiList import LumiList
()
General.requestName = 'TaskB'
...

JobType.psetName = <TaskA-psetName>
...
# and of course same input dataset
Data.inputDataset = <TaskA-input-dataset-name>
Data.inputDBS = 'global'  # but  will work for a dataset in  as well
# now the list of lumis that you successfully processed in Task-A
# it can be done in two ways. Uncomment and edit the appropriate one:
#1. (recommended) when Task-A output was a dataset published in
#taskALumis = getLumiListInValidFiles(dataset=<TaskA-output-dataset-name>, dbsurl='')
# or 2. when output from Task-A was not put in
#taskAlumis = LumiList(filename=<the  file from running  report on Task-A>)
# now the current list of golden lumis for the data range you are interested, can be different from the one used in Task-A
officalLumiMask = LumiList(filename='<some-kosher-name>.')
#  is the main trick. Mask out also the lumis which you processed already
newLumiMask = officialLumiMask - taskALumis
# write the new lumiMask file, now you can use it as input to
newLumiMask.writeJSON('')

Data.lumiMask = ''
Data.outputDatasetTag = <TaskA-outputDatasetTag> #  add to your existing dataset
...
```
**IMPORTANT NOTE** : in way you will add any lumi section in the intial data set that was turned from bad to good in the golden list after you ran Task-A, but if some of those data evolved the other way around (from good to bad), there is no way to remove those from your published datasets.
### Using pile-up
Show  Hide
Important Instructions:
Make sure you run your jobs at the site where the pile-up sample is. Not where the signal is.
requires you to overrdie the location list that  would extract from the `inputDataset`.Rational and details:
The pile-up files have be specified in the CMSSW parameter-set configuration file. There is no way yet to tell in the  configuration file that one wants to use a pile-up dataset as a secondary input dataset. That means that  doesn't know that the CMSSW code will want to access pile-up files;  only knows about the primary input dataset (if any). means that, assuming there is a primary input dataset, when  does data discovery to figure out to which sites should it submit the jobs, it will only take into account the input dataset specified in the  configuration file (in the `Data.inputDataset` parameter) and submit the jobs to sites where dataset is hosted. If there is no primary input dataset,  will submit the jobs to the less busy sites. In any case, if the pile-up files are not hosted in the execution sites, they will be accessed via AAA (Xrootd). But reading the "signal" events directly from the local storage and the pile-up events via AAA is more inefficient than doing the other way around, since for each "signal" event that is read one needs to read in general many (> 20) pile-up events. Therefore, it is highly recommended that the user forces  to submit the jobs to the sites where the pile-up dataset is hosted by whitelisting these sites using the parameter `Site.whitelist` in the  configuration file. Note that one also needs to set `Data.ignoreLocality = True` in the  configuration file in case of using a primary input dataset so to avoid  doing data discovery and eventually complain (and fail to submit) that the input dataset is not available in the whitelisted sites. One can use [DAS![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cmsweb.cern.ch/das/) to get the list of sites that host a dataset.

### How  finds data in input datasets from
Show  Hide
The following remarks apply to the main input dataset provided to  via the `Data.inputDataset` configuration parameter:
* **Dataset status**: Datasets in can have different status. is controlled by Production and the norm is to use VALID datasets. Datasets with different status may occasionally be useful, e.g. for comparison or dedicated study of the problems which led them to be deprecated. In order to run over a dataset whose status is not VALID, one has to set `Data.allowNonValidInputDataset = True` in the  configuration.
* **File status**: Files have a `is_file_valid` flag in , usually set to False when file is lost or corrupted.  considers only valid files in the dataset. Invalid files are skipped.
* **Data location**: A dataset in is divided in blocks. Blocks can be migrated with , and is the only service that knows about the current locations (host sites) of a dataset block. Therefore  queries to retrieve the locations of the blocks in a dataset. Next, a data location (aka PNN = ) is turned into a site where to run (aka PSN = Prosessing Site Name) using CRIC. If a block has no valid locations in or no PSN associated in CRIC,  skips the block.
* **User datasets**: For datasets created by users and published in  instance, the above is modified as follows:
  + Dataset status and File status flags are initially set to VALID by  when the dataset is published; then can be changed by the user.
  + Data block location is tracked as `origin_site_name` in and data are assumed to never move. If datasets **are** moved, the user can update the `origin_site_name`. There is no way to have multiple locations.
### How many jobs can I run at the same time ?
Show  Hide
 runs jobs on the Grid using a global HTCondor pool created via glideInWms machinery, think of it like a global batch system whith execution nodes all over the places. The most important thing which controls how many jobs you can run is the overall number of execution slots (CPU's) available for your jobs, i.e. that match your requirement of data access, memory and running time. Then HTCondor tries hard to give to every user the same share of computing resources, i.e. equal resources to everyone at any given time. You are not penalized for having run more jobs yesterday, and not rewared either for not having used your share in the past.
To assess the user share, HTCondor considers only the number of cores that you are using (until May 2017 also the number of RAM 's was accounted for).Beware thus of asking for much more memory **per core** than you need (see [What is the maximum memory per job (`maxMemoryMB`) I can request?](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/CRAB3FAQ#What_is_the_maximum_memory_per_j)).

### How much time to I have to  a task
Show  Hide
Tasks are purged from the system 30 days after submission to make room for new ones. You need to actively follow up on submitted tasks, make sure your output is collected and bookkeeping completed before that time.
#### What I if my task can not  in 30 days
If things are not done by than, changes are that somehting in the task submission was wrong or jobs critically depend on one particular site and that is down or overfull. In any case usually after a week or so every job in the task was submitted at least once. Better to stop, take stock of the available output, review things and submit a new task for the remaining data, possibly improving something.  automatically retries jobs up to 3 times in cases where the error message hints to a possible transient problem. There is also evidence that user resubmittion of jobs which failed becouse ot too much wall clock time or too much memory can sometimes succeed after resubmission (as long as those are isolated cases). But blindly hitting " resubmit" button in the hope that things change is a pointless waste of resources and will only delay completion of your workflow. We have see jobs resubmitted tens of times and every time failing with same error !
#### Why are tasks removed after 30 days
High level information on each task (name, . param, input..) is kept almost forever in  [DataBase](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/DataBase?topicparent=CMSPublic.CRAB3FAQ;nowysiwyg=1 " topic does not yet exist; you can create it."). But in order to run a task we need to have a working DAGMAN process on an HTCondor scheduler machine, which takes memory and disk space. We can not keep those around forever, the system would grind to halt. So we need to have a time after which "everything goes". is currnetly configured to be 30 days based on our operational experience in order to keep the system smoothly running.

### How to list/copy/remove files/directories in a storage element area?
Show  Hide
You can use the `gfal-*` commands from a machine that has GFAL2 utility tools installed (e.g. lxplus). You have to pass Physical File Names (PFNs) as arguments to the commands. To get the Physical File Name given a Logical File Name and a CMS node name, you can use the `lfn2pfn` .
LFNs are names like `/store/user/mario/myoutput`; note that a directory is also a file name.For example, for the LFN `/store/user/username/myfile.root` stored in `T2_IT_Pisa` you can the following (make sure you did `cmsenv` before, so to use a new version of `curl`), where you can replace the first two lines with the values which are useful to you and simply copy/paste the long curl command:
```
site=T2_IT_Pisa
lfn=/store/user/username/myfile.root
curl -ks "https://cmsweb.cern.ch//datasvc/perl/prod/lfn2pfn?node=${site}&lfn=${lfn}&protocol=srmv2" | grep PFN | cut -d "'" -f4
```
which returns:
```
srm://stormfe1.pi.infn.it:8444/srm/managerv2?SFN=/cms/store/user/username/myfile.root
```
Before executing the `gfal` commands, make sure to have a valid proxy:
```
voms-proxy-init -voms cms
Enter GRID pass phrase for  identity:
 [/DC=ch/DC=cern/OU=computers/CN=voms2.cern.ch] "cms"...
Remote VOMS server contacted succesfully.
Created proxy in /tmp/x509up_u<user-id>.
Your proxy is valid until <some date-time 12 hours in the future>
```
The most useful `gfal` commands and their usage syntax for listing/removing/copying files/directories are in the examples below (it is recommended to unset the environment when executing `gfal` commands, i.e. to add `env -i` in front of the commands). See also the `man` entry for each command (`man gfal-ls` etc.):List a (remote) path:
```
env -i X509_USER_PROXY=/tmp/x509up_u$UID gfal-ls <physical-path-name-to-directory>
```
Remove a (remote) file:
```
env -i X509_USER_PROXY=/tmp/x509up_u$UID gfal-rm <physical-path-name-to-file>
```
Recursively remove a (remote) directory and all files in it:
```
env -i X509_USER_PROXY=/tmp/x509up_u$UID gfal-rm -r <physical-path-name-to-directory>
```
Copy a (remote) file to a directory in the local machine:
```
env -i X509_USER_PROXY=/tmp/x509up_u$UID gfal-copy <physical-path-name-to-source-file> file://<absolute-path-to-local-destination-directory>
```
Note: the starts with `/` therefore there are three consecutive `/` characters like `file:///tmp/somefilename.root`
### Why are my jobs submitted to a site that I had explicitly blacklisted (not whitelisted)?
Show  Hide
There is a site overflow mechanism in place, which takes place after  submission. Sites are divided in regions of good WAN/xrootd connectivity (e.g. US, Italy, Germany etc.), then jobs queued at one site A for too long are allowed to overflow to a well connected site B which does not host the requested input data but from where data will be read over xrootd. Rationale is that even if those jobs were to fail due to unable to read data or a problem in site B, they will be automatically resubmitted, so nothing is lost with respect to keeping those jobs idle in the queue waiting for free slots at site A.
The site overflow can be turned off via the `Debug.extraJDL`  configuration parameter :
```
section_("Debug")
Debug.extraJDL = ['My.CMS_ALLOW_OVERFLOW=False']
```
Note: if you change configuration option for an already-created task (for instance if you noticed a lot of job failures at a particular site and even after blacklisting the jobs keep going back), you can't simply change the option in the configuration and resubmit. You'll have to kill the existing task and make a new task to get the option to be accepted. You can't simply change it during resubmission.
