### Doing lumi-mask arithmetics
Show  Hide
There is a tool written in python called `LumiList.py` (available in the [WMCore library![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/dmwm/WMCore/blob/master/src/python/WMCore/DataStructs/LumiList.py); is the same code as [cmssw/FWCore/PythonUtilities/python/LumiList.py![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/blob/CMSSW_8_0_X/FWCore/PythonUtilities/python/LumiList.py) ) that can be used to lumi-mask arithmetics. The arithmetics can even be done inside the  configuration file (that's the advantage of having the configuration file written in python). Below are some examples.**Example 1**: A run range selection can be achieved by selecting from the original lumi-mask file the run range of interest.
```
from WMCore.DataStructs.LumiList import LumiList
lumiList = ')
lumiList.selectRuns([x for x in range(193093,193999+1)])
lumiList.writeJSON('')
Data.lumiMask = ''
```
**Example 2**: Use a new lumi-mask file that is the intersection of two other lumi-mask files.
```
from WMCore.DataStructs.LumiList import LumiList
originalLumiList1 = ')
originalLumiList2 = ')
newLumiList = originalLumiList1 & originalLumiList2
('')
Data.lumiMask = ''
```
**Example 3**: Use a new lumi-mask file that is the union of two other lumi-mask files.
```
from WMCore.DataStructs.LumiList import LumiList
originalLumiList1 = ')
originalLumiList2 = ')
newLumiList = originalLumiList1 | originalLumiList2
('')
Data.lumiMask = ''
```
**Example 4**: Use a new lumi-mask file that is the subtraction of two other lumi-mask files.
```
from WMCore.DataStructs.LumiList import LumiList
originalLumiList1 = ')
originalLumiList2 = ')
newLumiList = originalLumiList1 - originalLumiList2
('')
Data.lumiMask = ''
```
### How can I tell  to run jobs on a non-x86 worker node ?
Show  Hide
Quick instructions for running the jobs of a task on ARM nodes, if they are available on the global pool:
* login into `lxplus8-arm.cern.ch` or `lxplus9-arm.cern.ch`
* if you want or need, start a singularity container with `/cvmfs/cms.cern.ch/common/cmssw-elX`
* then run the usual commands: `cmsrel`, `cmsenv`, `scrab b`, ` submit`.
is because at the moment,  support for non-x86 architectures has the following limitations:
* a task can target a single architecture.
*  selects the architecture for a task from the value of the  environment variable where ` submit` is run in.
means that if you want to run a task on an ARM node, then you need to login into an ARM machine and run the  client from there.Keep in mind: once you login into an arm machine, you can use the cmssw singularity images to get different  from the ones provided by the lxplus-arm host. For example:
```
> ssh lxplus9-arm.cern.ch
> which cmssw-el9
/cvmfs/cms.cern.ch/common/cmssw-el9
> cmssw-el9
Singularity> echo $
el9_aarch64_gcc10
Singularity>
> /cvmfs/cms.cern.ch/common/cmssw-el7
Singularity> echo $
slc7_aarch64_gcc10
Singularity>
```
References:
* [dmwm/CRABServer 7208![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/7208)
## Obsolete/Deprecated stuff (kept here as permanent documentation just in case)
### User quota in the  scheduler machines
Show  Hide
Each user has a home directory with 100GB of disk space in each of the scheduler machines (schedd for short) assigned to for submitting jobs to the Grid. Whenever a task is submitted by the  server to a schedd, a task directory is created in space containing among other things  libraries and scripts needed to run the jobs. Log files from Condor/DAGMan and  itself are also placed there. (What is not available in the schedds are the cmsRun log files, except for the snippet available in the  job log file.) As a guidance, a task with 100 jobs uses on average 50MB of space, but number depends a lot on the number of resubmissions, since each resubmission produces its log files. If a user reaches his/her quota in a given schedd, he/she will not be able to submit more jobs via that schedd (he/she may still be able to submit via other schedd, but since the user can not choose the schedd to which to submit -the choice is done by the  server-, he/she would have to keep trying the submission until the task goes to a schedd with non-exahusted quota). To avoid that, task directories are automatically removed from the schedds after 30 days of their last modification. If a user reaches 50% of its quota in a given schedd, an automatic e-mail similar to the one shown below is sent to him/her.
```
Subject: : Reaching your quota
You are using <X>% of your disk quota on the server <schedd-name>. The moment you reach the disk quota of <Y>, you will be unable to
run jobs and will experience problems recovering outputs. In order to avoid that, you have to clean up your directory at the server.
Here are the instructions to  so:
 https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideCrabFaq#How_to_clean_up_your_directory_i
Here it is a more detailed description of the issue:
 https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideCrabFaq#Disk_space_for_output_files
If you have any questions, please contact hn-cms-computing-tools(AT)cern.ch
 support
```
e-mail has a link (<https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideCrabFaq#How_to_clean_up_your_directory_i>) to the instructions on how to clean up space in the user's home directory in a schedd. A user can follow the instructions in that page, or alternatively use the [ purge](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/CRAB3Commands#crab_purge) command.
### `-env-bootstrap.sh` script to overcome the and CMSSW environment conflicts
Show  Hide
To overcome the vs CMSSW environment conflicts, you can use the following script available in CVMFS (`/cvmfs/cms.cern.ch//-env-bootstrap.sh`) without need to source the environment. You could something like :
```
cmsenv
#  NOT setup the  environment
alias ='/cvmfs/cms.cern.ch//-env-bootstrap.sh'
 submit
 status
...
# check that you can run cmsRun locally
```
Details:The usual way to setup is to first source the CMSSW environment using `cmsenv` and then source the environment using `source /cvmfs/cms.cern.ch//.(c)sh`. setup procedure has the disadvantage that, depending on which CMSSW version is used, once the environment is sourced the CMSSW commands like cmsRun will stop working (also other useful commands like `gfal-copy` will not work). Solving at the root and make the  client RPM compatible to the CMSSW ones is not possible for the way the tools in the COMP repository are built, and because cmsweb has its own release cycle independent from CMSSW.To overcome limitation we are now providing a  bash script that can be run in place of the usual  command.  script will take care of setting the environment in the correct way before running the usual  command, and will leave the environment as it was when exiting. The script will be soon available in the CMSSW distribution under the name '' and its usage will be transparent to the user: you will just run the  commands as you would have done before. In the meantime, the script is available for testing here: `/cvmfs/cms.cern.ch//-env-bootstrap.sh`.
### ERROR: SyntaxError: invalid syntax (Mixins.py, line 714)
Show  Hide
The problematic pset is FWCore/ParameterSet/Mixins.py from CMSSW:
```
[line 714] p = tLPTest("MyType",** { "a"+str(x): tLPTestType(x) for x in xrange(0,300) } )
```
uses dictionary comprehensions, a feature available in python > 2.7. While CMSSW (setup via `cmsenv`) uses python > 2.7,  (setup via `/cvmfs/cms.cern.ch//.sh`) still uses python 2.6.8. To overcome problem, don't setup the  environment and instead use the `-env-bootstrap.sh` script (see  [FAQ](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/CRAB3FAQ#crab_env_bootstrap_sh_script_to)).

## v3.3.1707 (released on July 11, 2017)
### Improvements, enhancements, changes
* Removed \*old commands (`statusold`, `resubmitold`, `reportold`, `getoutputold`, `getlogold`)
* Events per lumi information of ' output files now being propagated to DBS during publication.
* Improvements for managing the task's lifetime length.
### fixes
* Introduced a check for output file LFNs (maximum length not exceeded and correct ) before the submission of the task.
##  (released on June 13, 2017)
### Improvements, enhancements, changes
* Changes to how task status is reported in the CRABClient API.
  + Intended to make the `status` key in the return status dictionary backwards compatible with the old  `status` logic.
  + Documentation can be found here <https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/CRABClientLibraryAPI#crab_status_API_description_and>.
* Introduced a limit to the amount of lumis (100k) that each input dataset block has.
  + If a dataset contains blocks bigger than 100k lumis, submission will be refused by the CRABServer.
### fixes
* Output publication fixes
* CRABClient code refactoring for downloading files used when constructing overall status. Also addresses the issue when  `status` would not work outside of CERN.
## v3.3.1705 (released on May 2, 2017)
### Improvements, enhancements, changes
* Making the new command implementations the default.
  + The commands that were previously called "=status2, ...=" are now called:
    - `status`
    - `resubmit`
    - `report`
    - `getoutput`
    - `getlog`
  + The old implementations are still available under these names:
    - `statusold`
    - `resubmitold`
    - `reportold`
    - `getoutputold`
    - `getlogold`
### fixes
* Fix for publication when using the new Oracle implementation and direct stageout.
## v3.3.1704 (released on April 4, 2017)
### Improvements, enhancements, changes
* `status2` now has a `--jobids` option.
  + Can be used together with the `--long` and / or `=--sort` options. Specific jobids or a range of jobids can be passed to only display the `--long` or `--sort` results for those jobs.
* Fail the task and upload a warning if task's webdir upload during the bootstrapping step on the grid scheduler.
* Show a better error message when the Data.userInputFiles parameter is incorrect.
* Check that the size of the sandbox is under 100MB before uploading, not after.
### fixes
* Renew proxies for completed tasks, previously one could not force resubmission of a completed task after the proxy had expired.
* CRABMon webdir link fix, previously would not work from outside CERN.
* Don't send additional input files list to the server.
## v3.3.1703 (released on March 8, 2017)
### Improvements, enhancements, changes
* Prototype client commands `status2`, `report2`, , `getlog2`, .
  + The new implementation of the commands should reduce the load on the CRABServer backends. Specifically,  `status2 --long` should be much faster and should be used instead of the old  `status --long`.
  + They rely on a task\_process that runs alongside each task on the grid scheduler. The process iteratively computes and caches the status of each task, looking only at new information with which the status needs to be updated. This happens every 5 minutes for each task independently, meaning that the information displayed by status2 (on which the other commands also depend on) may be up to 5 minutes old. However, we do not foresee this to be a problem. Otherwise, one should expect these commands to behave exactly the same as the regular commands.
* New tab in Monitoring UI with status of transfers for tasks which use [OracleASO](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/OracleASO?topicparent=CMSPublic. "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.").
* Print traceback when catching [StageOutMgr](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/StageOutMgr?topicparent=CMSPublic. "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") initialisation exceptions.
* Report number of requested cores to .
### fixes
* Fix file metadata upload in the [PostJob](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/PostJob?topicparent=CMSPublic. "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.").
* Fix issue when the list of additional input files is too large for the database column.
## v3.3.1702 (released on February 7, 2017)
### Improvements, enhancements, changes
* now takes e-groups into account when deciding if the user is part of the local site .
* to purge tasks in SUBMITFAILED fixes,
* Add link to CRABMon in status,
* Print used memory in message to user when a job is killed due to memory usage,
* Error summary generation code optimization,
* Metrics based scheduler picker function.
### fixes
* Site blacklist doesn't update on resubmission,
* Task process / status2 fixes,
* Make number of cores in config and number of threads in pset consistent,
* Use 'python', not 'python2.6' in dag\_bootstrap\* scripts,
* CRABMon fixes.
## v3.3.1611 (released on November 14, 2016)
### fixes
* Minor fix for python 2.6 compatibility
* Make Task Worker sleep between queries if CRABServer cannot be reached
* CRABMon minor improvements
* Log working directory file sizes when a job is killed
* Report, resubmit hotfixes
## v3.3.1608 (released on August 24, 2016)
### New features
* task submission for partial datasets
  + A message will be displayed notifying the user of this behavior in case only a partial dataset is found. This is mostly relevant for new datasets that are in the process of being distributed and therefore are still incomplete.
* Ignore global blacklist option
  + If the user is sure that the site(s) is able to run jobs successfully but it is blacklisted for some reason, it is now possible to get around the blacklist by adding a config parameter `config.Site.ignoreGlobalBlacklist = True`.
### fixes
* Fix error when the schedd list is empty after retries
* Truncate warning messages
## v3.3.1607 (released on July 13, 2016)
### New features
### fixes
* Protect against missing LFN in input file.
* Separate Ops monitoring files into another tarball
* Clarify `--priority` option, correct description for `--checksum` option
* Fix resubmit returning 'None' error to the client
* Fix concurrency issue when creating log directory
* Log unexpected errors in subprocesses
* up a new schedd only after retries for current one are exhausted
* `cfipython` folder should now be included if `sendPythonFolder` option is enabled.
## v3.3.1606 (released on June 7, 2016)
### New features
A new feature intended for  operators is available:
* Slow job release for  tests.
  + Instead of submitting multiple tasks per hour for each site, a single task can be used for a longer period of time to continuously release jobs into the site, reducing the overhead load. Documentation on this feature is available [here](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/CRAB3TipsAndTricks#Slow_job_release_for_Hammer_Clou).
### Improvements, enhancements, changes
* All tasks will now be removed after 30 days. Resubmission will not be allowed after 23 days.
### fixes
* some code for backwards compatibility with old tasks and Clients
* Report local/fallback/direct stageout to
* unnecessary debug printout in [RenewRemoteProxies](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/RenewRemoteProxies?topicparent=CMSPublic. "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.").
* Protect the [/bin/edit/CMSPublic/TaskWorker?topicparent=CMSPublic. "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") from main loop crashes
* Adjust logic in kill after TM refactoring.
* Protect [PostJob](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/PostJob?topicparent=CMSPublic. "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") from empty defer\_num.\*.\*.txt file
## v3.3.1605 (released on May 10, 2016)
### New features
### Improvements, enhancements, changes
* Operators can now kill user tasks, which is useful in rare cases. A reason for the kill will also be provided, which is displayed when doing  `status`.
* Better input parameter validation for MC generation.
* The problem with files being mysteriously deleted after the transfer should occur much less frequently now.

## v3.3.12 (released on December 9, 2014)
### fixes update (released on December 19, 2014)
This is a patch release (version 3.3.12.patch1) of the Server backend component and the client that fixes some bugs listed below.
* Implement work-around fix in for oracle triggered when uploading a long file metadata to the server.
  + The oracle error was/is happening in jobs that analyze a large amount of lumis. The symptom is that all jobs are shown as  with exit code 0 and failure at the post-processing (in  `status`, and GlideMon). In this case jobs are automatically retried (up to 2 times), but fail at every retry. On the other hand, output files are actually present in the user's destination storage. Furthermore, in all the cases we have investigated, the file metadata was actually present in the server database, meaning that publication (which needs the file metadata of the outputs) was able to run. Therefore, we ended up telling to that they can ignore the failure if the publication was ok (or of course, in case the outputs were not intended to be published, if they were present in the destination storage). Eventually we were suggesting to use a finer job splitting in the configuration file.
  + The fix implemented in consists in: whenever get back an error uploading a file metadata, check if the file metadata is available in the server or not. If it is, ignore the error and proceed normally.
* Fix publication for output files that are staged out directly from the worker node to the destination storage (i.e. output files not staged out via the ASO component).
  + Direct stageout is the fallback method used by in case the initial stageout to the temporary storage in the running site fails. (This was happening last week for example with jobs running at CERN.) There was a preventing the publication for those output files.  `status` was showing the jobs in `finished` status (which is correct) and publication in `idle` status all the time (it is ok to have the publication in `idle` status for even some hours, but shouldn't be so for more than 8 hours).
* The  `report` command was enhanced to also work when the task produces output files of a type other than EDM.
  + Before, this command was only working if the task produced an output file of EDM type (i.e. produced an output file via PoolOutputModule). Now it also works for tasks that, within cmsRun, produce an output file via TFileService or (in principle) via any other module. The most important output from the  `report` command are the luminosity summary (`lumiSummary.json` and `missingLumiSummary.json`). Before, the file `lumiSummary.json` was produced by parsing from the framework job report produced by cmsRun the list of luminosity sections reported in the "output" section of the report, and that section existed (if we are not wrong) only for output files produced via PoolOutputModule. Now, the file `lumiSummary.json` is produced by parsing the list of luminosity sections reported in the "input" section of the framework job report, which should be valid for all output files produced in the workflow and should be the same list as in the "output" section.
  + Warning: The information shown by  `report` about the number of files processed is not correct when the task doesn't produce an EDM output file.  `report` will show "0 files have been processed". On the other hand, the information about number of events processed and written should be always correct.
  + Warning: Tasks (that produce an output file of type other than EDM) submitted before this deployment, will not benefit from this patch. will need to submit a new task if for them it's critical to get the correct `lumiSummary.json` file.
  + Feedback in case of inconsistencies in  `report` is very much appreciated.
* Fix in  `status` command showing `Output dataset: /FakeDataset/fakefile-FakePublish-5b6a581e4ddd41b130711a045d5fecb9/USER` when an output file of type other than EDM is produced.
* Don't clean the environment when running `scriptExe`.
  + The problem here was that, by cleaning the environment, some critical information were lost, like the `X509_USER_PROXY` which defines the user's proxy file location. As a consequence, jobs were not able to access for example remote input files via xrootd.
  + We kindly ask to report back to us in case this fix has introduced some other unexpected problem.
### New features
* A new parameter named  has been introduced in the configuration file.
  + This parameter allows to specify how many events should a luminosity section contain when generating MC events. The previous behaviour was to create one luminosity section per job.
* A new parameter named `Data.useParent` has been introduced in the configuration file.
  + This parameter has the same behaviour as `use_parent` in CRAB2.
### Improvements, enhancements, changes
* Don't inject transfer requests to ASO until the local stage out for all the files in the job were successful.
* When staging out the files from the worker node, use the same stage out policy (either local stage out or remote stage out) for all the files.
  + In practice: 1) try local stage out first and, if it succeeds for all files, inject transfer requests to ASO; 2) if local stage out fails for at least one file, clean the local temporary storage (keep the logs archive so that the user can retrieve it with  `getlog`) and try direct stage out for all files to the permanent storage in the site specified by the user; 3) if the remote stage out fails for at least one file, clean the destination directory in the remote permanent storage and the job is (will be automatically retried).
* Move the upload of the logs archive file metadata from the post-job to the stage out wrapper in the worker node, and do the upload even if the job fails.
  + This allows the user to retrieve the logs (with  `getlog`) even if the job fails.
* Implement the new CMS global LFN namespace policy.
  + can only write into `/store/user/<username>/` or `/store/group/<groupname>[/<subgroupname>]*/<username>/`, where `username` is the user's username registered in SiteDB (which in turn is the user's CERN account username). If publication is off, the user can also write into `/store/local/<dirname>[/<subdirname>]*`.

  + the exit code and reason will also be shown during  `status` now

### fixes
* Don't retry a job in case the job wrapper exit code is 80000 (or 128).
* Update locations of log/output files when the jobs that generates them are retried. Less failures in  `gelog` and  `getoutput` commands should be observed now.
## v3.3.11 (released on November 18, 2014)
### fixes update (released on November 26, 2014)
This is a transparent release (compatible with current client version 3.3.11) of the ASO and Server backend components that fixes some minor bugs listed below.
* Save the luminosity sections that a job should analyze into a json file.
  + Before, this list of luminosity sections were directly saved in the condor input file, with a limit of 128000 characters, and indirectly limiting how many luminosity sections a job could analyze. Now jobs can accept any list of luminosity sections to run on.
* Change (relax) the check on the CMSSW release name.
  + Before was accepting only `-9X]){3}(_[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+)?`. Now it accepts `CMSSW[a-zA-Z0-9-_]*`.
* Save only the first 1K lines and the last 3K lines of the cmsRun stdout to the job log.
* Fix ASO submission problem to FTS.
* Improved error messages for some corner cases (e.g.: datasets only on tape)
### New features
* MC generation from LHE files.
* The  `status` command shows an error summary for jobs.
* Improved report of jobs in transfering state (a new state called `transferred` has been added).
### Improvements, enhancements, changes
* Error messages from the server backend and the server frontend have been improved to better tell user what is going on and what they have to do.
* Some of the configuration parameters have been renamed.
  + E.g. `Data.saveLogs` was renamed to `Data.transferLogs`, `Data.transferOutput` was renamed to `Data.transferOutputs`, `JobType.` was renamed to `JobType.`, `Data.dbsUrl` was renamed to `Data.inputDBS`, `Data.publishDbsUrl` was renamed to `Data.publishDBS`.
* Don't exit the PostJob until all the file transfers are in a terminal state.
* Improve screen output of `getoutput` and `getlog` commands when `--dump` option is used.
  + Print not only the PFN of the files that would be retrieved, but also the LFN, and organize the output by jobs.
* Renamed option `--skip-proxy` to `--proxy` in all client commands.
* Renamed `checkHNname` command to `checkusername`.
* Renamed client function `getHyperNewsName` to `getUsernameFromSiteDB`.
  + And the renamed function `getUsernameFromSiteDB` has been improved: a) avoid error when scram is not available, b) check existence of valid proxy, c) improve messages to user.
* Use the new client function `getUsernameFromSiteDB` in the `checkwrite` command when it needs to retrieve the username.
  + When the `--lfn` option is not specified, the `checkwrite` command assumes that the user wants to check its write permission in `/store/user/<username>`. In that case the command retrieves the username from SiteDB. Until now it was doing it via the client class `CredentialInteractions` (which in turn uses SiteDBJSON from WMCore). Now it uses the client function `getUsernameFromSiteDB`.
* Disable the default automatic kill of tasks.
  + was killing tasks for which at least 10% of the jobs had a fatal error.
* Disabled CMSSW MemoryCheck warnings ([https://hypernews.cern.ch/HyperNews/CMS/get/computing-tools/150.html![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://hypernews.cern.ch/HyperNews/CMS/get/computing-tools/150.html))
* Always return the output dataset name, even after the tamporary data have been deleted from the database.
### fixes
* People should not get the "This server is not configured to publish; no publication status is available" error anymore. See [https://hypernews.cern.ch/HyperNews/CMS/get/computing-tools/218/1/1/1.html![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://hypernews.cern.ch/HyperNews/CMS/get/computing-tools/218/1/1/1.html)
* Removed blocking calls in the condor python bingings that were causing occasional DatabaseUnavailable problems.
  + Under some circumstances commands were immediately returning DatabaseUnavailable errors. This should not happen again, please report it if you see this happening.
* Don't make a transfer request for a file that is already in transfer.
  + This situation was sometimes happening when jobs were being automatically retried by and the PostJob left the transfers go on even if it decided to retry the job. This was causing the these jobs were reported as successfully finished, but the corresponding (output or log) file was actually missing in the permanent storage.
* Fix job-retry-count indexing problem in `postjob.<jobid>.<retrycount>.txt` files.
  + The was causing that PostJob log files were missing for jobs from manual resubmission. The user was seeing `"Post-job is currently queued."` even if the post-processing step was finished.
* Strip `file:` from the output file names in `jobReport.json`.
  + When a user was adding the protocol prefix `file:` in the output file names in the pset, this was passed to the job report and cmscp was unable to match the local file names in the job report.
## v3.3.10 (released on October 5, 2014)
### New features
* Possibility to run a user script instead of plain cmsRun.
  + Two new parameters have been added to support this functionality, namely `JobType.scriptExe` and `JobType.scriptArgs`. A short documentation can be found in the twiki  [configuration file](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/CRAB3ConfigurationFile).
### Improvements, enhancements
* The  `getlog` and  `getoutput` commands are now able to retrieve files from the temporary storage when the corresponding transfers to a permanent storage were disabled (to remember: the transfer of the logs is disabled by default).
* Check if a dataset is on tape when looking for the locations of the dataset.
* Automatically upload the log file to the CRABCache for unhandled exceptions.
* Various improvements in the `crab2cfgTOcrab3py` script, so to better translate a CRAB2 configuration file into a configuration file.
* Do not print colors if the standard output if it is redirected to a file.
### fixes
* Add file size to job report for the additional output files.
  + The file size (for the additional output files) in the job report was so far set to 0. This information is used for example by the  `getoutput` command to determine what is the "expected" size of the output files. When a user executes  `getoutput`, the command first checks if the corresponding output files already exist in the local destination directory (the `results` subdirectory in the task project directory). If they already exist, the command compares the actual size of the files with the "expected" size, and if the sizes differ it retrieves the file again from the corresponding storage. Having the file size set to 0 in the job report had the obvious undesired behaviour that  `getoutput` was always retrieving all the additional output files again whenever the command was executed.
* Pass `CMSRunAnalysis` exit code as argument to `cmscp` (the wrapper the takes care of local transfers). Use it as the exit code in `cmscp` if not 0.
  + The exit code reported by in case of job failure should be now consistent with the exit code reported in the job log file.
* Strip the `file:` string from file names where the user specified `file:` in the CMSSW parameter-set or the configuration files.
  + This was causing that files specified by the user with a `file:` prefix were not found by .
## Other Topics
* Local Resource Provisioning: the access to local resources such as sites with no grid access (e.g.: CAF at CERN, LPC at Fermilab), opportunistic sites, etc, is not possible yet with . The and the Submission Infrastructure teams are evaluating different proposal of how to better integrate this use case in the client/server architecture (<https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/CompOpsLocalSubmission>). The idea is to include this type of submission into the central system, improving the CRAB2 direct submission model. A timeline for implementing the use case has not been set yet.
-- - 15 Oct 2014

#  Client Cheat Sheet
## Recap
you need 2 things
* code : either use CMS's `/cvmfs/cms.cern.ch//setup.sh` or `pip install `
* configuration : `/cvmfs/cms.cern.ch//setup.sh` takes care. Otherwise do `export RUCIO_CONFIG=/cvmfs/cms.cern.ch//x86_64/el9/py3/current/etc/.cfg`. Then do `` export RUCIO_ACCOUNT=--username--` ``
##  transfer script on schedd user spool dir
only python client is needed so we simply add  to PYTHONPATH. Also on schedd hosts we already put  config file in `/opt//etc/.config` and take care of  account in python client initialization.
```
su crabtw
cd /home/grid/---HN username---/---TASKNAME---/SPOOL_DIR/
export X509_USER_PROXY=`pwd`/`ls|egrep  [a-z,0-9]{40}`
# BE CAREFUL! these instructions could be obsolete, check with what is done inside =task_process/task_proc_wrapper.sh=
export PYTHONPATH=`pwd`/task_process:`pwd`/CRAB3.zip:`pwd`/WMCore.zip:$PYTHONPATH
export RucioPy3=/cvmfs/cms.cern.ch//x86_64/rhel9/py3/current/lib/python3.9/site-packages/
export PYTHONPATH=$PYTHONPATH:$RucioPy3
cp task_process/RUCIO_Transfers.py task_process/RUCIO_Transfers.py_old
echo "#!/usr/bin/python3" > task_process/RUCIO_Transfers.py
```
then you are ready to run any test script you want (task\_process/\_Transfers.py\_old included).
## Using  client on lxplus
following takes care of code and config, but be aware that it clashes with CMSSW envirornment
```
voms-proxy-init --voms cms
source /cvmfs/cms.cern.ch//setup.sh
export RUCIO_ACCOUNT=$USER
```
##  client from docker container
do `pip install `
## Useful command example
###
>
### Check my quota
>  list-account-limits dciangot
### List my datasets
>  list-dids user.$USER:\*
### List files inside a dataset
>  list-content user.$USER:/mydataset
### Check the status of a transfer for files in my dataset
>  list-rules user.$USER:/mydataset

|  |  |

Contents:
* [architecture and task workflow](#CRAB3_architecture_and_task_work)
  + [architecture](#CRAB3_architecture)
  + [Typical workflow sequence](#Typical_workflow_sequence)
## architecture
The following diagram shows (a very simplified version of) the current architecture of the system.![](/twiki/pub/CMSPublic/CRAB3TaskFlow/CRAB3_architecture_simple.png)
## Typical workflow sequence
The arrows in the previous diagram represent a typical workflow, starting from the submission and ending with the publication in DBS. Below we enumerate the steps involved in such a typical workflow.
1. The CRAB client submits the request to the CRAB server (and uploads the user's input sandbox to the CRAB Cache -also in the CRAB server-).
2. The CRAB Server inserts the request as an entry in the Task (Oracle) DB.
3. A subcomponent of the CRAB Server called the Task Worker constantly monitors the Task DB for new requests.
4. The Task Worker grabs the new request and sends it to the submission infrastructure (GlideInWMS).
5. The submission infrastructure looks for available and submits the jobs to them.
6. The jobs run at the .
7. When a job finishes, the Worker Node copies the output files to the temporary storage of the site.
8. The AsyncStageOut service transfers the output files from the temporary storage to the permanent storage.
9. Once the transfer is done, the AsyncStageOut service publishes the output dataset in DBS.
-- - 23 Oct 2014

body:

# and tricks about CRAB
|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| : ![3](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/pub/CMS/WebPreferences/complete3.png) | Go to [SWGuideCrab](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideCrab) |
Contents:
* [and tricks about CRAB](#Tips_and_tricks_about_CRAB)
  + [and tricks about CRAB](#Tips_and_tricks_about_CRAB_AN1)
    - [Retrieving the CERN username in the CRAB configuration file](#Retrieving_the_CERN_username_in)
    - [Dynamically changing the request name in the CRAB configuration file](#Dynamically_changing_the_request)
    - [Slow job release for Hammer Cloud tests (useless for regular users)](#Slow_job_release_for_Hammer_Clou)
## and tricks about CRAB
### Retrieving the CERN username in the CRAB configuration file
**IMPORTANT**: **DO NOT USE IT**. This should only be used if absolutely needed in very special use cases (scripts wrapping CRAB commands to be used by others e.g.), normally users should simply type their CERN account name. If in doubt about what it is, use `crab checkusername`CRAB provides a function  (available in the `CRABClient.ClientUtilities` module) that retrieves the CERN username from the user grid credential (proxy e.g.) possibly via a central CMS information database (CRIC e.g.). This function can be used in the CRAB configuration file in cases where the usename is not known a priorty (like a scritpt wrapping crab commands which will be used by many people). Normal users should simply type their CERN primary account name. Below it is shown how to import and use the function in the CRAB configuration file.
```
from CRABClient.ClientUtilities import ,
 = ()
## Define a variable with the CMS HyperNews username.
my_cern_username = ()
...
...
## Use the variable my_cern_username in the Data.outLFN parameter.
.Data.outLFN = '/store/user/' + my_cern_username + '/bla'
...
...
```
![note.gif](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/note.gif) **Note**: Using the function within CRAB is safe in terms of proxy validity, because the `crab submit` command checks before loading the configuration file if the user has a valid proxy and creates one if not. Using the function outside CRAB requires the user to have a valid proxy; if not, the function will raise `ProxyException`.
### Dynamically changing the request name in the CRAB configuration file
The fact the the CRAB configuration file is written in python gives to the user lot of flexibility when defining the CRAB configuration parameter values dynamically. Below we give an example where we added some lines of code to the CRAB configuration file in order to define the parameter `General.requestName` as `tasknumber<index>`, where the `index` is a non-negative integer number that follows a sequence and is helping to organize a bunch of tasks that have otherwise the same name. The code starts by setting the index variable to 0; it then starts a loop where it checks if the CRAB project directory corresponding to the current index already exists, and if it does increments the index by 1 and if it doesn't stops the loop.
```
from CRABClient.ClientUtilities import  = ()
. = 'crab_projects'
## --- Auxiliary code starts here --- ##
## We want to define .General.requestName = 'tasknumber<index>'
import os
index = 0
base_request_name = 'tasknumber'
while os.path.isdir("%s/crab_%s%s" % (., base_request_name, index)):
    index += 1
## --- Auxiliary code ends here --- ##
.General.requestName = base_request_name + str(index)
...
...
```
##
### Slow job release for Hammer Cloud tests (useless for regular users)
Slow job release is a feature intended for lowering the overhead of HC tests. Instead of creating multiple tasks to test the availability of a site, a single task can be submitted with an extraJDL parameter specifying the timeout between job releases. It utilises the HTCondor PRE script DEFER option. Each PRE script will check if the release timeout has been specified, and if it is too soon to be released, it will exit to be retried after `timeout * jobId` amount of time.If the timeout is set to be 2 minutes and the task has 3 jobs, the first job will be released after 2 minutes, the second one after 4 minutes and the third one after 6 minutes.The timeout in seconds can be specified in the crab configuration file like this:
```
.Debug.extraJDL = ['+CRAB_JobReleaseTimeout=120']
```
-- - 2015-01-08

![CRAB Logo](http://cmsdoc.cern.ch/cms/ccs/wm/www/Crab/img/crab_logo_3.png)
# Troubleshooting and guide
|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| : ![3](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/pub/CMS/WebPreferences/complete3.png) | Go to [SWGuideCrab](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideCrab) |
![Tip, idea](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/tip.gif "Tip, idea") This page explains what to do if your CRAB task is not successful. Most of the times users can diagnose and solve problems themselves. This is quicker than asking for help.
Contents:
* [Troubleshooting and guide](#CRAB3_Troubleshooting_and_Proble)
  + [Expected flow](#Expected_flow)
  + [How to deal with problems](#How_to_deal_with_problems)
## Expected flow
Once you have run the code interactively on a significant number of events, the picture below illustrates the way should be used.![CRAB_flow.png](/twiki/pub/CMSPublic/CRAB3Troubleshoot/CRAB_flow.png)Important points are:
* Majority of tasks manages to with 100% success (CRAB already tries to resubmit failed jobs and failed file transfers whenever this makes sense and the capabilities in this area are constantly being improved)
* CRAB has extensive (and expanding) retry logic already. And some errors are very well reproducible (like most software !)
  + blind resubmission is more more likely to waste resources than help
* Still CRAB retry logic may not be sufficient in some cases, like a site having a problem for longer than a few hours. In such situations users can push things along by manually resubmitting failed jobs using `crab resubmit` and possibly use this to specify for a few parameters a value different from the one used in initial task submission, see [crab resubmit command description](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/CRAB3Commands#crab_resubmit)
* Users should not interfere with internal CRAB working, so `crab kill` can only be used to completely halt all CRAB processing to make sure there's a stable picture
* When things are done and all balls stopped rolling, a fraction of the task may still not have been successful. Users should consider the option of a [recovery task](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/CRAB3FAQ#Recovery_task)
* When failures are too many, starting over may be the only solution, but unless there was a global problem in the infrastructure, you need to make sure that the failure is not due to something in your code or configuration
## How to deal with problems
1. make sure you subscribe to the [announcement forum![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://hypernews.cern.ch/HyperNews/CMS/get/cernCompAnnounce.html), to be aware oif scheduled outages and global known problems
2. read the [documentation](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideCrab#CRAB3_documentation)
3. among the [basic](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookCRAB3Tutorial) or [advanced](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/CRAB3AdvancedTutorial) CRAB tutorials those appropriate to your use case, check what is different in your use situation, find what broke things
4. change from the tutorial (or something that works) to your configuration one step at a time, so you can find where things broke
5. check [CRAB3FAQ](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/CRAB3FAQ)
6. check messages from `crab status` command and if they contain a suggestion, follow it
7. if some jobs failed with an exit code, check in the [JobExitCodes](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/JobExitCodes) and try to diagnose the problem yourself, usually this can be done looking at the stdout from one job which failed. You can get this via the `crab getlog --short` command or via the link in the Job column of the dashboard page for your task
8. make sure that your executable works by testing it locally on the same input file(s) as the failed jobs
9. if problem is hard to find, consider running and debugging a failing job interactively using the [crab preparelocal](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/CRAB3Commands#crab_preparelocal) command
10. if nothing helps, and your are really desperate, or suspect a bug in the tool, or a problem in the infrastructure, you can [ask for support](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideCrab#Getting_support)
11. please be aware that bug reports can be followed up upon only if submitted with full details, and a recipe to reproduce them
-- - 2017-07-04

#  user functions
|  |  |

| : ![5](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/pub/CMS/WebPreferences/complete5.png) | Go to [SWGuideCrab](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideCrab) |
Contents:

  + [ user functions](#CRAB_user_functions_AN1)
    - [getUsername](#getUsername)

    - [getConsoleLogLevel](#get_ConsoleLogLevel)
    - [setConsoleLogLevel](#set_ConsoleLogLevel)
##  user functions
All the functions listed below are in the `CRABClient.UserUtilities` module. To use them, the user should import them with, for example, the following syntax:
```
from CRABClient.UserUtilities import functionName
var = functionName()
```
The usage examples shown below correspond to either using the functions inside the python  configuration file or in the context of the  client library API.
###
**Description:** This function has the only purpose of saving the user from typing the definition of the configuration sections in the  configuration file, since these sections are always the same. **arguments:** None.**Returns:**
* A `Configuration` object (from `WMCore.Configuration`) with all sections expected/known by  already defined.
** exceptions raised:** None.**Usage example:**
```
from CRABClient.UserUtilities import
()
.General.requestName = 'my_crab3_task'
...
```
```
from WMCore.Configuration import Configuration
 = Configuration()
.section_("General")
.section_("JobType")
.section_("Data")
.section_("Site")
.section_("User")
.section_("Debug")
.General.requestName = 'my_crab3_task'
...
```
### getUsername
**Description:** This function retrieves the users' CERN primary account username from the grid credential (proxy e.g.), possibly accessing some CMS central information data base.**IMPORTANT**: **DO NOT USE IT**. This should only be used if absolutely needed in very special use cases (scripts wrapping  commands to be used by others e.g.), normally users should simply type their CERN account name. If in doubt about what it is, use ` checkusername` **arguments:** None.**Returns:**
* The username (as a string) if the retrieval of the username was successful; `None` otherwise.
** exceptions raised:**
* `ProxyException` (from `CRABClient.ClientExceptions`): E.g. if the user doesn't have a valid proxy.
* `UsernameException` (from `CRABClient.ClientExceptions`): E.g. if the used with  is not properly mapped to user account
**Usage example:** See [Retrieving the CERN username in the  configuration file](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/CRAB3TipsAndTricks#Retrieving_the_CERN_username_in).![note.gif](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/note.gif) **Note**: Using the function within  is safe in terms of proxy validity, because the ` submit` command checks before loading the configuration file if the user has a valid proxy and creates one if not. Using the function outside  requires the user to have a valid proxy; if not, the function will raise the  client exception `ProxyException`.
### getFileFromURL
**Description:** Loads a file from a user provided URL and writes it in a local file. **arguments**:
* `url`: The URL from where to load the file.
* `filename`: The name of the local file where the content of the file loaded from the URL should be written.
**Returns:**
* The name of the local file (as a string) where the content of the file loaded from the given URL was saved. This is the same as the argument `filename`, which defaults `None` and in which case the basename of the file path in the URL will be used.
** exceptions raised:**
* `ClientException` (from `CRABClient.ClientExceptions`): In case anything goes wrong.
**Usage example:**
```
from CRABClient.UserUtilities import , getFileFromURL
()
.General.requestName = 'my_crab3_task'
...
.JobType.psetName = getFileFromURL(url = 'http://blablabla.com/apset.py', filename = 'myCMSSWPSet.py')
...
.Data.lumiMask = getFileFromURL(url = 'https://blablabla.com/atxtfile.txt', filename = 'myLumiMaskFile.txt')
...
```
### getLumiListInValidFiles
**Description:** the runs and luminosity sections in (the valid files of) a dataset. **arguments**:
* `dataset`: The dataset for which to the runs and luminosity sections.
* `dbsurl`: The DBS Reader URL where `dataset` is published. The following shortcuts are accepted: `'global'`, `'phys01'`, `'phys02'` and `''`. Defaults to `''`.
**Returns:**
* A `LumiList` object (from `WMCore.DataStructs.LumiList`) of runs and lumis.
** exceptions raised:**
* `ClientException` (from `CRABClient.ClientExceptions`): In case of error querying the DBS client or dataset not found in DBS.
**Usage example:** See usage example in [Dealing with a growing dataset](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/CRAB3FAQ#Dealing_with_a_growing_input_dat) .
### getLoggers
**Description:** the current  loggers. **arguments**: None.**Returns:**
* A dictionary with the  loggers. The keys of the dictionary are the names of the loggers and the values are the loggers objects.
** exceptions raised:** None.
### getConsoleLogLevel
**Description:** the current logging level of the `CRAB3.all` logger (console) stream-handler. **arguments**: None.**Returns:**
* The current logging level of the `CRAB3.all` logger (console) stream-handler. The logging level is an integer.
** exceptions raised:** None.**Usage example:** See usage example in [setConsoleLogLevel](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/CRAB3UserFunctions#setConsoleLogLevel).
### setConsoleLogLevel
**Description:** /modify the logging level of the `CRAB3.all` logger (console) stream-handler. **arguments**:
* `lvl`: The new logging level for the stream-handler.
**Returns:** Nothing.** exceptions raised:** None.**Usage example:**
```
from CRABAPI.RawCommand import crabCommand
from CRABClient.ClientUtilities import LOGLEVEL_MUTE
from CRABClient.UserUtilities import setConsoleLogLevel
#  the original  console log level.
origConsoleLogLevel = getConsoleLogLevel()
#  off the logging of  to the console.
setConsoleLogLevel(LOGLEVEL_MUTE)
# Execute some  commands.
crabCommand(...)
...
crabCommand(...)
...
#  back the original  console log level.
setConsoleLogLevel(origConsoleLogLevel)
# Execute some more  commands.
crabCommand(...)
crabCommand(...)
...
```
##

#  client library API
|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| : ![5](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/pub/CMS/WebPreferences/complete5.png) | Go to [SWGuideCrab](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideCrab) |
Contents:
* [ client library )
  + [Version](#Version)
  + [Introduction](#Introduction)
  + [The crabCommand API](#The_crabCommand_API)
    - [Brief description](#Brief_description)
    - [Brief usage examples](#Brief_usage_examples)
      * [Example of submitting a task from the python shell](#Example_of_submitting_a_task_fro)
      * [Example submitting multiple tasks using a python script](#Example_submitting_multiple_task)
    - [ status API description and example](#crab_status_API_description_and)
  + [Multicrab using the crabCommand API](#Multicrab_using_the_crabCommand)
  + [Debugging errors with crabCommand](#Debugging_errors_with_crabComman)
## Version
* 17 July 2014 - Alpha release. Fresh out of the oven.
* 07 Jan 2015 - Improved alpha release. API for raw execution of commands available to the users.
* 04 Feb 2015 - Released production version with  v3.3.13
## Introduction
The CRABAPI library is a python wrapper on top of the client and allows people to easily interact with the server through the same  client interface used by the official client. It is intended for people who would like to automatize the submission of tasks with . With the CRABAPI library you will never have to call the client commands and parse their outputs again!There are two ways of using the library. One is just a small python function, called `crabCommand`, that allows you to run the client commands accepting the same arguments they accept from the command line. Backward compatibility is not guaranteed and error handling is left to the users. The other is an interface which adds some intelligence to the client commands, and, among other things, manipulates the output of the server, guarantees backward compatibility. The latter is not available yet.
## The crabCommand API
This is a thin API that allows easy access to the  client commands. Users who have experience with the  client command line should be able to understand quickly how to use the crabCommand API.In order to use it you shoud make sure to do (replace `sh` with `csh` as appropriate for your shell):
```
cmsenv
source /cvmfs/cms.cern.ch/common/-setup.sh
```
and make sure that your first `import` in your python script is
```
import CRABClient
```
this will trigger addition to `$` of dependencies like WMCore and DBS which are
not in default CMSSW path.
### Brief description
The signature of the crabCommand API is the following: `returndictcrabCommand(command, *args, **kwargs)`**Input arguments:**
* `command`: Takes the name of the  command to be executed (e.g. `'submit'`, `'status'`, `'report'`, etc).
* `args`: Positional arguments to be passed as such to the command.
* `kwargs`:  arguments are considered as (long-name) options to be passed to the command. The API takes care of adding a double hyphen ('--') in front of each  argument so that the command interprets them as options.
**Returns:**
* The return value of the invoked  command, which should be always a python dictionary.
The positional arguments `args` are supported for compatibility with the client command line, where the  configuration file name and the  project directory name can be passed as the first positional argument instead of using the `--` and `--dir` options respectively. The `submit` command is the only one that accepts additional positional arguments; they are used for overwriting  configuration parameters. However, when using the crabCommand API, the overwriting of  configuration parameters can be done before calling the API. So at the end, the usage of the positional arguments `args` should not be needed and for simplicity we recommend using the  arguments `kwargs` only. The recommended syntax for passing options to the command is then the following:
```
crabCommand('<command>', <option1>=<value1>, <option2>=<value2>, <option3>=True, ...)
```
Options that do not take a value in the command line should be specified giving the boolean value `True` in the API. If the boolean value is `False`, the corresponding  argument will be ignored by the API (i.e. the argument will not be passed as an option to the command). The API will then run the equivalent of:
```
 <command> --<option1> <value1> --<option2> <value2> --<option3> ...
```
**Note**: Remember that the `--` option of the `submit` command accepts both the name of a  configuration file and a Configuration object itself.
### Brief usage examples

Description of some of the less obvious keys in the return dictionary
| [Key](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/CRABClientLibraryAPI?sortcol0;table2;up0#sorted_table "Sort by this column") | [Description](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/CRABClientLibraryAPI?sortcol1;table2;up0#sorted_table "Sort by this column") |
| --- | --- |
| `status` | This status combines the task's status on CRABServer as well as on the grid. For example, after task submission, it will show `NEW` or `QUEUED` while CRABServer handles the new task. (These are some of the statuses on the CRABServer side, which are reported separately in the `dbStatus` dict key as well.) If the task submission to the grid succeeds, the status will become `SUBMITTED` (Immediately after submission, the status may show `UNKNOWN` during the task bootstrapping process on the grid). Status will continue to show `SUBMITTED` until the task on the grid finishes. After this point, the status will become either `COMPLETED`, which means that all of the jobs finished successfully, or `FAILED`, meaning that at least some of the jobs failed. (The task states on the grid are also separately reported in the `dagStatus` dict key.) This combined status value reported in the dictionary is currently not reported in the CLI, it exists to improve backwards compatibility with the old ` status` implementation API. Instead, the CLI reports the `dbStatus` and `dagStatus` values separately. |
| `dbStatus` | Status of the task on CRABServer. This is indicates 's progress in handling the task before and during the submission to the grid. It will show `NEW` or `QUEUED` for a new task for example, and `SUBMITTED` if the submission to the grid succeeds. |
| `dagStatus` | Status of the task on the grid. It will show `SUBMITTED` until all jobs finish running. Afterwards, it will either show `COMPLETED` or `FAILED`, depending on whether all jobs completed successfully or some of them failed. |
| `taskFailureMsg` | This will contain a message about a problem that the CRABServer encountered during the handling of the task. For example, if the user's provided lumimask doesn't correctly match the input data and no jobs can be generated by CRABServer, this key will contain a message similar to `"The server backend could not submit any job to the Grid scheduler: Splitting task 170529_102639:erupeika_crab_test on dataset /A/B/C with [FileBased](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/FileBased?topicparentCMSPublic.CRABClientLibraryAPI;nowysiwyg1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") method does not generate any job'"`. |
| `statusFailureMsg` | This will contain a message about the why the `crabCommand("status")` cannot provide all of the usual information about a task. One such could be `"Waiting for the Grid scheduler to report back the status of your task"` which means some information about the task like the state of each job is unavailable at the current time. |
The `crabCommand("status")` will not throw any exception if it has some useful information to return. For example, even though it may fail getting information from the grid scheduler for various reasons, information about a task from the CRABServer task database is still available. It will throw an HTTPException if something goes wrong with the request to CRABServer itself (task not found for example).**Basic `crabCommand("status")` usage example**
```
import CRABClient
from httplib import HTTPException
from CRABAPI.RawCommand import crabCommand
st = {}
try:
    st = crabCommand("status")
except HTTPException as ex:
    print("Problem with status encountered: %s" % ex)
    raise
if st.get("jobList"):
    print(st.get("jobList"))
else:
    print("Status incomplete")
    if st.get("statusFailureMsg"):
        print("Found  for error: %s" % st.get("statusFailureMsg"))
```
## Multicrab using the crabCommand API
Using the `crabCommand` API and a few lines of code it is possible to implement the so-called multicrab functionality in . Here is an example.First let's assume we want to submit two identical tasks on two different datasets (like the example above), but let's also change other parameters in the  configuration file.
What we will do is to call `crabCommand('submit')` twice (once for each task) passing the Configuration object as argument and of course changing the configuration parameters accordingly before each call. For example, one can add the following lines at the end of the  configuration file:
```
import CRABClient
[The usual  configuration comes here]
if __name__ == '__main__':
    from CRABAPI.RawCommand import crabCommand
    from CRABClient.ClientExceptions import ClientException
    from httplib import HTTPException
    # We want to put all the  project directories from the tasks we submit here into one common directory.
    # That's why we need to set this parameter (here or above in the configuration file, it does not matter, we will not overwrite it).
    . = 'crab_projects'
    def submit():
        try:
            crabCommand('submit', )
        except HTTPException as hte:
            print "Failed submitting task: %s" % (hte.headers)
        except ClientException as cle:
            print "Failed submitting task: %s" % (cle)
    #############################################################################################
    ## From now on that's what users should modify: this is the a-la-CRAB2 configuration part. ##
    #############################################################################################
    .General.requestName = 'runB'
    .Data.inputDataset = '/DoubleMuParked/Run2012B-22Jan2013-v1/AOD'
    .Data.unitsPerJob = 2
    .Data.totalUnits = 4
    submit()
    .General.requestName = 'runC'
    .Data.inputDataset = '/DoubleMuParked/Run2012C-22Jan2013-v1/AOD'
    .Data.unitsPerJob = 3
    .Data.totalUnits = 8
    submit()
    # etc ...
```

Warning: If you will use (and change) the  configuration parameter `JobType.pyCfgParams` when submitting multiple tasks, please check first [this FAQ](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/CRAB3FAQ#Multiple_submission_fails_with_a).You can create a file called `multicrab` and make it executable with `chmod 744 multicrab`:
```
#!/usr/bin/env python
"""
This is a small script that does the equivalent of multicrab.
"""
import os
from optparse import OptionParser
import CRABClient
from CRABAPI.RawCommand import crabCommand
from CRABClient.ClientExceptions import ClientException
from httplib import HTTPException
def getOptions():
    """
    Parse and return the arguments provided by the user.
    """
    usage = ("Usage: %prog --crabCmd CMD [--workArea WAD --crabCmdOpts OPTS]"
             "\nThe multicrab command executes ' CMD OPTS' for each project directory contained in WAD"
             "\nUse multicrab -h for help")
    parser = OptionParser(usageusage)
    parser.add_option('-c', '--crabCmd',
                      dest = 'crabCmd',
                      default = '',
                      help = "The  command you want to  for each task in DIR",
                      metavar = 'CMD')
    parser.add_option('-w', '--workArea',
                      dest = 'workArea',
                      default = '',
                      help = "work area directory (only if CMD != 'submit')",
                      metavar = 'WAD')
    parser.add_option('-o', '--crabCmdOpts',
                      dest = 'crabCmdOpts',
                      default = '',
                      help = "options for  command CMD",
                      metavar = 'OPTS')
    (options, arguments) = ()
    if arguments:
        parser.error("Found positional argument(s): %s." % (arguments))
    if not options.crabCmd:
        parser.error("(-c CMD, --crabCmdCMD) option not provided.")
    if options.crabCmd != 'submit':
        if not options.workArea:
            parser.error("(-w WAR, --workAreaWAR) option not provided.")
        if not os.path.isdir(options.workArea):
            parser.error("'%s' is not a valid directory." % (options.workArea))
    return options
def main():
    """
    Main
    """
    options = getOptions()
    # If you want crabCommand to be quiet:
    #from CRABClient.UserUtilities import setConsoleLogLevel
    #from CRABClient.ClientUtilities import LOGLEVEL_MUTE
    #setConsoleLogLevel(LOGLEVEL_MUTE)
    # With this function you can change the console log level at any time.
    # To retrieve the current crabCommand console log level:
    #from CRABClient.UserUtilities import getConsoleLogLevel
    #crabConsoleLogLevel = getConsoleLogLevel()
    # If you want to retrieve the  loggers:
    #from CRABClient.UserUtilities import getLoggers
    #crabLoggers = getLoggers()
    #  the command with its arguments for each directory inside the work area.
    for dir in os.listdir(options.workArea):
        projDir = os.path.join(options.workArea, dir)
        if not os.path.isdir(projDir):
            continue
        #  the  command.
        msg = "Executing (the equivalent of):  %s --dir %s %s" % (options.crabCmd, projDir, options.crabCmdOpts)
        print "-"*len(msg)
        print msg
        print "-"*len(msg)
        try:
            crabCommand(options.crabCmd, dir = projDir, *options.crabCmdOpts.split())
        except HTTPException as hte:
            print "Failed executing command %s for task %s: %s" % (options.crabCmd, projDir, hte.headers)
        except ClientException as cle:
            print "Failed executing command %s for task %s: %s" % (options.crabCmd, projDir, cle)
if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
```

## Debugging errors with crabCommand
With the `crabCommand` API the whole error handling is up to the user. That's because the API is directly executing  commands without the interface of the `` script, so the main exceptions handling present in `` is skipped.
