[Stop running TaskWorker|Publisher ](#Stop_running_TaskWorker_Publishe) + [TaskWorker|Publisher ](#Restart_stopped_TaskWorker_Publi) + [TaskWorker|Publisher logs](#Find_TaskWorker_Publisher_logs) + [Naming convention for images and containers](#Naming_convention_for_images_and) + [Script to pull and run TW/Publisher image](#Script_to_pull_and_run_TW_Publis) + [Deploying new TW release](#Deploying_new_TW_release) + [Publisher\_schedd (on crab-prod-tw02)](#Publisher_schedd_on_crab_prod_tw) + [Useful commands](#Useful_Docker_commands) ## Introduction This twiki explains how to deploy the TaskWorker and Publisher on .**Note:** Legend of colors for the examples: ``` Commands to execute ``` ``` Output sample of the executed commands ``` ``` Configuration files ``` ``` Other files ``` ## Prerequisites ### Get and install a virtual machine See [Deployment of CRAB REST Interface / Get and install a virtual machine](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/CMSCrabRESTInterface#Get_and_install_a_virtual_machin). Make sure to go through the `Machine preparation` steps if you do not plan to install the REST interface on this machine. ### Prepare directories and host cert to be used by the TW running as the service user **NOTE: this section is mostly for documentation, this directory structure is currently enforced via puppet [https://gitlab.cern.ch/ai/it-puppet-hostgroup-vocmsglidein/-/blob/master/code/manifests/profiles/crabtaskworker.pp![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://gitlab.cern.ch/ai/it-puppet-hostgroup-vocmsglidein/-/blob/master/code/manifests/profiles/crabtaskworker.pp)** ``` #sudo mkdir /data/certs # This should have been done already by the Deploy script when installing the VM. /certs/creds /data/certs/tokens.d /data//TaskWorker/logs/ /data//TaskWorker/cfg /data//Publisher/logs/ /data//Publisher/cfg sudo chmod 700 /data/certs/creds /data/certs/tokens.d /data//TaskWorker/logs/ /data//TaskWorker/cfg /data//Publisher/logs/ /data//Publisher/cfg #sudo cp -p /etc/grid-security/host{cert,key}.pem /data/certs # This should have been done already by the Deploy script when installing the VM. ``` For production and pre-production installations: ``` :/certs/creds /data/certs/tokens.d /data//logs/TaskWorker /data//logs/Publisher /data//cfg :/certs/host{cert,key}.pem ``` For private installations: ``` `whoami`:/certs /data/certs/tokens.d /data/certs/creds /data/user/logs `whoami`:/certs/host{cert,key}.pem ``` ### Setup a service certificate for interacting with CMSWEB A service certificate is needed with `=cern/OU=computers/CN=tw/vocms052.cern.ch` (or whatever the correct host name is). As of 2017, this is provided yearly by , who takes care of this for all Submission Infrastructure related machines, but if needed, anybody can do it using the procedure indicated here: The service certificate must be registered in VO CMS and in SiteDB. The certificate and private key should be in `/data/certs/servicecert.pem` and `/data/certs/servicekey.pem` respectively, and should be readable only by the service user.For production and pre-production also do: ``` :/certs/service{cert,key}.pem ``` For private installations: ``` `whoami`:/certs/service{cert,key}.pem ``` The proxy is created for 8 days (192 hours), because this is the maximum allowed duration of the VO CMS extension. Thus, the proxy has to be renewed every 7 days (at least). You can do it manually or you can set up an automatic renewal procedure like is being done in production and pre-production. ### Setup HTCondor IDTOKENS for remote submission to HTCondor (for [/bin/edit/CMSPublic/TaskWorker?topicparent=CMSPublic.CRABDocker;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.")) Submission to HTCondor is authenticated via [IDTOKENS mechanism![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://htcondor.readthedocs.io/en/latest/admin-manual/security.html#token-authentication), not GSI anymore. HTCondor ptyhon API automatically looks in `/data/certs/tokens.d` for a token (in the end, a file) valid for the condor pool being accessed and uses it. Condor tokens are mapped to user `crabtw` inside the sched's and currently never expire. You should get the tokens (one for ITB and one for global pool) from Submission Infrastructure (or copy them from another VM which runs [/bin/edit/CMSPublic/TaskWorker?topicparent=CMSPublic.CRABDocker;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") services) and place them in the target directory, protect them (`chmod 600` and `chowm :`), and delete any copy you may have made around. It is sufficient to do this in the `/data/certs` directory of the VM where containers run. Each will mount `/data/certs` from the host disk and thus have access to uptodate tokens. See below details about mount points used to start containers. In any case there is an additional security layer since the condor pools have a white list of host names which can use any given token. The final setup should look like ``` [root@crab-dev-tw01 ~]# ls -l /data/certs/tokens.d/ total 8 -r--------. 1 249 Jan 18 17:58 crabtw-global-pool -r--------. 1 236 Jan 17 12:12 crabtw-itb-pool [root@crab-dev-tw01 ~]# ``` ### daemon Install the daemon with the following commands ``` sudo yum install -y yum-utils \ device-mapper-persistent-data \ lvm2 sudo yum-config-manager \ --add- \ https://download..com/linux/centos/-ce. sudo yum -ce ``` ### Start daemon Then start the daemon with ``` sudo systemctl start ``` You can check if everything worked correctly with: ``` sudo ps ``` ``` ID IMAGE COMMAND CREATED STATUS PORTS ``` Optionally you can add your user to the group, this will allow you to skip sudo command when using cli ``` sudo usermod -aG your-user ``` ### Testing the service certificate The certificate can be tested via command line `curl` #### check VOMS: ``` curl --cert /data/certs/servicecert.pem --key /data/certs/servicekey.pem https://voms2.cern.ch:8443/voms/cms/info/index.action ``` output is a longish HTML page, ugly but readable, anyhow if it works it will have something like this close to the end ``` Your certificate:
  • is currently linked to the following membership: (166)
    • ``` #### check CMSWEB: ``` curl --cert /data/certs/servicecert.pem --key /data/certs/servicekey.pem https://cmsweb.cern.ch/auth/trouble ``` output will be self-explanatory ``` voms-proxy-init --voms cms --valid 192:00 sudo cp /tmp/x509up_u$UID /data/certs/servicecert.pem sudo cp /tmp/x509up_u$UID /data/certs/servicekey.pem sudo chmod 600 /data/certs/servicecert.pem sudo chmod 400 /data/certs/servicekey.pem ``` ### Contact Analysis Ops for new instances In addition to GSI authentication, operators whitelist the hostnames allowed to submit jobs for . If this is a brand-new hostname, you will need to contact CRAB operator(s) to add this TaskWorker to the list of ALLOW\_WRITE hosts in `82_cms_schedd_crab_generic.config` ## Configuration files ### TW Configuration Create a TaskWorker configuration file and store it in /data//TaskWorker/cfgwith the content of this file: [https://gitlab.cern.ch/ai/it-puppet-hostgroup-vocmsglidein/blob/master/code/templates/crab/crabtaskworker/.erb![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://gitlab.cern.ch/ai/it-puppet-hostgroup-vocmsglidein/blob/master/code/templates/crab/crabtaskworker/.erb)The parameters that you have to change are: | [Parameter](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/CRABDocker?sortcol=0;table=1;up=0#sorted_table "Sort by this column") | [Type](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/CRABDocker?sortcol=1;table=1;up=0#sorted_table "Sort by this column") | [Explanation](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/CRABDocker?sortcol=2;table=1;up=0#sorted_table "Sort by this column") | | --- | --- | --- | | `TaskWorker.name` | string | A name that identifies this TaskWorker. For example the host name. | | `TaskWorker.instance` | string | REST endpoint to use, e.g. [/bin/edit/CMSPublic/TaskWorker?topicparent=CMSPublic.CRABDocker;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.").instance='preprod'. Documentation how to use this parameter (available nicknames, how to set restHost/dbInstance combination) can be found in here: [https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/wiki/INSTANCES:--versions,-REST-hosts,-clusters,-DataBases![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/wiki/INSTANCES%3A--versions%2C-REST-hosts%2C-clusters%2C-DataBases) When 'instance' is set to 'other' the configuration must have one pair of strings indicating the REST host fqdn and the DB instance [prod/preprod/dev]. | | `TaskWorker.restHost` | string | REST host name (only if [/bin/edit/CMSPublic/TaskWorker?topicparent=CMSPublic.CRABDocker;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.").instance='other') | | `TaskWorker.dbInstance` | string | name (only if [/bin/edit/CMSPublic/TaskWorker?topicparent=CMSPublic.CRABDocker;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.").instance='other') | ### Publisher Configuration Create a Publisher configuration file and store it in /data//Publisher/cfgwith the content of this file: [https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/master/src/script/Deployment/Publisher/PublisherConfig.py![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/master/src/script/Deployment/Publisher/PublisherConfig.py)Before running the TaskWorker or Publisher, double check all the parameters. If you don't know what parameters to use, please contact ## Build new image Image built in this section can be used to deploy two services: [/bin/edit/CMSPublic/TaskWorker?topicparent=CMSPublic.CRABDocker;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") and Publisher. Which service will be deployed is decided at the start time. You can build images on your private VM or use cmsdocker01.1. Clone CRABServer github repository ``` git clone https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer.git ``` 2. cd into the directory where dockerfile is placed cd CRABServer/3. Set release version ``` RELEASE_TAG=RPM_RELEASETAG_HASH= ``` . You can get the correct value for RPM\_RELEASETAG\_HASH from [https://cmsrep.cern.ch/cmssw/repos/comp.crab\_master/slc7\_amd64\_gcc630/latest/RPMS.json![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cmsrep.cern.ch/cmssw/repos/comp.crab_master/slc7_amd64_gcc630/latest/RPMS.json) ( or ![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif) if you are using your own RPM ), from the key of the form "cms+crabtaskworker+v3.210301-64d015d49d9815c53bf1a25e3a9043df".4. Build image ``` build . -t ${DHUSER}/crabtaskworker:${RELEASE_TAG} \ --build-arg RELEASE_TAG=${RELEASE_TAG} \ --build-arg RPM_RELEASETAG_HASH=${RPM_RELEASETAG_HASH} ``` * Be aware that ${DHUSER} is a username. Production TW images are stored in 'registry.cern.ch/cmscrab/' * Also,before building image, be aware which for RPMs is used in install.sh script. If you want to use your own , don't forget to change this file. * Finally, if later you are going to push this image to you own , that will require to create a repository called 'crabtaskworker' in . Different name can be used, but then don't forget to change it other places. 5. Check that the image was built ``` images ``` ``` REPOSITORY TAG IMAGE ID CREATED SIZE ${DHUSER}/crabtaskworker 3.3.2004 c312fb512323 5 days ago 5.57GB ``` 6. Push image to ``` push ${DHUSER}/crabtaskworker:$TW_VERSION ``` Every time new image needs to be deployed, steps 2-6 has to be repeated. ## Run new ### Mounted points Below is a list of mounted points used to start the . Since one image can be used to start 2 different services ([/bin/edit/CMSPublic/TaskWorker?topicparent=CMSPublic.CRABDocker;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") and Publisher), be aware that when mounting directory for logs at the start time, you have to specify which one to mount: [/bin/edit/CMSPublic/TaskWorker?topicparent=CMSPublic.CRABDocker;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") or Publisher. | [Mounted point](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/CRABDocker?sortcol=0;table=2;up=0#sorted_table "Sort by this column") | [Source](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/CRABDocker?sortcol=1;table=2;up=0#sorted_table "Sort by this column") | [Target](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/CRABDocker?sortcol=2;table=2;up=0#sorted_table "Sort by this column") | | --- | --- | --- | | /cvmfs/cms.cern.ch/SITECONF : /cvmfs/cms.cern.ch/SITECONF | host machine | | | /etc/grid-security/ : /etc/grid-security/ | host machine | | | /data/srv/tmp/ : /data/srv/tmp/ | host machine | | | /data/certs/ : /data/certs/ | host machine | | | /etc/vomses/ : /etc/vomses/ | host machine | | | /data// : /data/hostdisk/ | host machine | | ### Start new New [/bin/edit/CMSPublic/TaskWorker?topicparent=CMSPublic.CRABDocker;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") can be started by running command: ``` TW_VERSION={Set CRABServer release tag} run --name TaskWorker -d -ti --net host --privileged -e SERVICE=TaskWorker -w /data/srv/TaskManager -v /cvmfs/cms.cern.ch/SITECONF:/cvmfs/cms.cern.ch/SITECONF -v /data/srv/tmp/:/data/srv/tmp/ -v /etc/grid-security/:/etc/grid-security/ -v /data/certs/:/data/certs/ -v /etc/vomses/:/etc/vomses/ -v /data//:/data/hostdisk/ cmssw/crabtaskworker:$TW_VERSION ``` New Publisher can be started by running command: ``` TW_VERSION={Set CRABServer release tag} run --name Publisher -d -ti --net host --privileged -e SERVICE=Publisher -w /data/srv/Publisher/ -v /cvmfs/cms.cern.ch/SITECONF:/cvmfs/cms.cern.ch/SITECONF -v /data/srv/tmp/:/data/srv/tmp/ -v /etc/grid-security/:/etc/grid-security/ -v /data/certs/:/data/certs/ -v /etc/vomses/:/etc/vomses/ -v /data//:/data/hostdisk/ cmssw/crabtaskworker:$TW_VERSION ``` | [Option](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/CRABDocker?sortcol=0;table=3;up=0#sorted_table "Sort by this column") | [Explanation](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/CRABDocker?sortcol=1;table=3;up=0#sorted_table "Sort by this column") | | --- | --- | | --name | name. Containers are name "TaskWorker" or "Publisher" | | -d | Start a in detached mode | | -ti | Allocate a pseudo-tty and keep STDIN open even if not attached | | --net host | Makes the program inside the look like they are running on the host itself, from the perspective of the network. | | --privileged | Give extended privileges to this | | -v | Bind mount a volume | ### Enter ``` #enter TaskWorker exec -it TaskWorker bash #enter Publisher exec -it Publisher bash ``` #### as `root` if you want to in the as `root`, not as (e.g. to add some tool temporary via `yum install`) ``` exec --user 0:0 -ti Publisher_schedd bash # or exec --user 0:0 -ti TaskWorker bash ``` ## Stop Service To stop service ([/bin/edit/CMSPublic/TaskWorker?topicparent=CMSPublic.CRABDocker;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") or Publisher) 3 steps needs to be done: 1. Stop running processes inside the ; 2. Stop running ; 3. Delete old - it is important to delete old so that we could re-use the same name for the next . Importat NOTE You should always ensure that you the [/bin/edit/CMSPublic/TaskWorker?topicparent=CMSPublic.CRABDocker;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") or/and Publisher processes inside that (step number 1) and only then stop the itself (step number 2)!This sequence of actions can be achieved in two ways (if you want to stop Publisher , then in the command replace 'TaskWorker' with 'Publisher'): * manually in into the to use pre-configured stop.sh script to stop the service and then exit the to stop it ``` exec -it TaskWorker bash # in to the ./stop.sh #run stop script ps uxf #check if all slaves were killed exit #exit the stop TaskWorker #stop the rm TaskWorker #remove the ``` * run a command in a running using exec [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARG...] ``` exec TaskWorker bash -c "./stop.sh" #run stop.sh script inside the exec TaskWorker bash -c "ps uxf" #check if TW was properly and all slaves were killed stop TaskWorker #stop the rm TaskWorker #remove the ``` Both steps 1 and 2 are explained in more detailed below: ### Stop running processes To stop the running processes you should use the preconfigured script: ``` sh stop.sh ``` Which executes the following steps: Show Hide first identify the pid of the master process: ``` 29690 5181 0 11:06 pts/1 R+ 0:00 \_ 13459 1 4 ? Rl 46:03 python /data/srv/TaskManager/current/slc6_amd64_gcc481/cms/crabtaskworker/3.3.1507.rc7/lib/python2.6/site-packages/TaskWorker/MasterWorker.py --config /data/srv/TaskManager/c 13466 13459 0 ? Sl 0:08 \_ python /data/srv/TaskManager/current/slc6_amd64_gcc481/cms/crabtaskworker/3.3.1507.rc7/lib/python2.6/site-packages/TaskWorker/MasterWorker.py --config /data/srv/TaskManag 13467 13459 0 ? Sl 0:20 \_ python /data/srv/TaskManager/current/slc6_amd64_gcc481/cms/crabtaskworker/3.3.1507.rc7/lib/python2.6/site-packages/TaskWorker/MasterWorker.py --config /data/srv/TaskManag 13469 13459 0 ? Sl 0:51 \_ python /data/srv/TaskManager/current/slc6_amd64_gcc481/cms/crabtaskworker/3.3.1507.rc7/lib/python2.6/site-packages/TaskWorker/MasterWorker.py --config /data/srv/TaskManag 13471 13459 0 ? Sl 0:15 \_ python /data/srv/TaskManager/current/slc6_amd64_gcc481/cms/crabtaskworker/3.3.1507.rc7/lib/python2.6/site-packages/TaskWorker/MasterWorker.py --config /data/srv/TaskManag 13473 13459 0 ? Sl 0:19 \_ python /data/srv/TaskManager/current/slc6_amd64_gcc481/cms/crabtaskworker/3.3.1507.rc7/lib/python2.6/site-packages/TaskWorker/MasterWorker.py --config /data/srv/TaskManag ``` and then kill only the master process ``` kill 13459 ``` You should wait until all slaves finish.Importat NOTE : the above procedure will make each TW slave stop when it has completed the work it pulled in its queue (2 tasks at most), so that no tasks are left in QUEUED. Tasks in status QUEUED when TW restarts would be automatically failed. But at times it may happen that one slave is instead executing one of the recurring actions (see ), in particular the proxy renewal action can last a long time. In this case it is better not to wait (hours ?) since the proxy renewer script can be safely killed at any time. You can monitor TW winding down progress using `ps fux` and/ior using `tail` on most recent `logs/processes/proc.c3id_*.txt` files. Generally speaking it is usually safe to kill any lingering TW slave after about 5min. If they did not complete in that time, something is wrong, but you should put in the elog the name and last lines of the for the stuck process for investigation.To the [/bin/edit/CMSPublic/TaskWorker?topicparent=CMSPublic.CRABDocker;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.")|Publisher have to use the preconfigured script: ``` # Start the TaskWorker sh start.sh ``` ### Stop running [/bin/edit/CMSPublic/TaskWorker?topicparent=CMSPublic.CRABDocker;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.")|Publisher Stop the running [/bin/edit/CMSPublic/TaskWorker?topicparent=CMSPublic.CRABDocker;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.")|Publisher by running stop command with the name/id ``` stop TaskWorker ``` ## [/bin/edit/CMSPublic/TaskWorker?topicparent=CMSPublic.CRABDocker;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.")|Publisher can be started by running ``` start TaskWorker ``` ## [/bin/edit/CMSPublic/TaskWorker?topicparent=CMSPublic.CRABDocker;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.")|Publisher logs ``` #TW logs are stored on the host machine and can be found in /data//TaskWorker/logs/. The main file is twlog. tail -f /data//TaskWorker/logs/twlog.txt #Publisher logs are stored on the host machine and can be found in /data//Publisher/logs/. The main file is . tail -f /data//Publisher/logs/.txt ``` twlog. and . fils are automatically rotated every day by the service. ## Naming convention for images and containers Suggested naming convention for images and containers: It is suggested to use TW release version as a tag for image and use "TaskWorker" and "Publisher" for coresponding name, see example below. | [Repository name](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/CRABDocker?sortcol=0;table=4;up=0#sorted_table "Sort by this column") | [Image](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/CRABDocker?sortcol=1;table=4;up=0#sorted_table "Sort by this column") | [Tag](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/CRABDocker?sortcol=2;table=4;up=0#sorted_table "Sort by this column") | [ name](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/CRABDocker?sortcol=3;table=4;up=0#sorted_table "Sort by this column") | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | ${DHUSER}/crabtaskworker | ${DHUSER}/crabtaskworker:3.3.2004 | TW release version, e.g. 3.3.2004 | [/bin/edit/CMSPublic/TaskWorker?topicparent=CMSPublic.CRABDocker;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") | | ${DHUSER}/crabtaskworker | ${DHUSER}/crabtaskworker:3.3.2004 | TW release version, e.g. 3.3.2004 | Publisher | ## Script to pull and run TW/Publisher image * runContainer.sh script which can be used to pull image from and run it. Importat NOTE runContainer.sh script is placed in every crab dev|preprod|prod machine's home directory (/home/) so you can source it directly from there. ``` [@crab-prod-tw02 ~]$ ./runContainer.sh -h Usage: runContainer.sh -v v3.201118 -s TaskWorker -v TW/Publisher version -s which service should be started: Publisher, Publisher_scheddy, Publisher_asoless, Publisher_rucio or TaskWorker -r , if not provided, default is 'cmssw' ``` ## Deploying new TW release List of steps which needs to be done every time new TW release has to be deployed: 1. Build new image and upload it to the repository. Note, that every time new release in CRABServer repository is created, image is automatically created and pushed to `cmssw/crabtaskworker` account, read more at: 2. If needed, stop which was running old version of the TW/Publisher and remove the so that name could be reused 3. Start new manually by pasting commands listed in section 'Run new ' or by calling runContainer.sh script (see one section 'Scripts to pull and run TW/Publisher image'). ## Publisher\_schedd (on crab-prod-tw02) These works as of Nov 15, 2020. May change as things are restructured and updated: ``` sudo # stop the contrainer stop Publisher_schedd # remove old so that can reuse name rm Publisher_schedd # start a with new TW_VERSION= run --name Publisher_schedd -d -ti --net host --privileged -e SERVICE=Publisher -w /data/srv/Publisher/ -v /cvmfs/cms.cern.ch/SITECONF:/cvmfs/cms.cern.ch/SITECONF -v /data/srv/tmp/:/data/srv/tmp/ -v /etc/grid-security/:/etc/grid-security/ -v /data/certs/:/data/certs/ -v /etc/vomses/:/etc/vomses/ -v /data//Publisher_schedd/logs/:/data/srv/Publisher/logs/ -v /data//Publisher_schedd/cfg/:/data/srv/cfg/ -v /data//Publisher_schedd/PublisherFiles/:/data/srv/Publisher_files cmssw/crabtaskworker:$TW_VERSION ``` ## Useful commands If the for some reasons crashed, you can use ' logs' command to inspect what has happened ``` logs TaskWorker ``` -- - ## how to build a CRABSERVER container for CMSWEB cluster
If you are not `belforte` just replace your username, favorite directories and  hub username as appropriate
### 1. Build RPMs (as usual)
quick recap from instructions in <https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/NotesAboutReleaseManagement#Releasing_a_CRAB_TaskWorker_rele>
* go to the build node
  ```
  cd /buid/belforte/cmsdist
  ```
* /update as needed
* now change crabserver(cache/taskworker) and wcore version as needed/usual
  + `vim crabserver.spec`
* build and upload (before uploading RPMs, make sure that you are subscribed to cms-comp- e group which will give you required permissions to upload it)
  ```
  cd /build/belforte
  pkgtools/cmsBuild -c cmsdist --repository comp -a slc7_amd64_gcc630 --builders 8 -j 5 --work-dir w build comp
  pkgtools/cmsBuild -c cmsdist --repository comp -a slc7_amd64_gcc630 --builders 8 -j 5 --work-dir w --upload-user=$USER upload comp
  ```
* note the HG version and crabserver etc. version in the rpms
  + e.g. at ![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)
  + or with
    ```
    ls w/BUILD/slc7_amd64_gcc630/cms/comp/|tail -1
    ```
    - etc. replacing `comp` with `crabserver`, `crabcache` etc.
  + or all in one shot
    ```
    for pkg in `ls w/BUILD/slc7_amd64_gcc630/cms/`; do echo $pkg; ls -lgort w/BUILD/slc7_amd64_gcc630/cms/$pkg/|tail -1; done
    ```
### 2. Build container (replaces the installation on VM)
* go to the build node (ask for access)
  ```
  ssh cmsdocker01
  ```
* go to the director where you have cloned [https://github.com/dmwm/CMSKubernetes![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/dmwm/CMSKubernetes) (or your fork of it)
  ```
  cd ~/WORK//CMSKubernetes//
  ```
* /update as needed
* now change VER and `VER=HG1911a-comp` and `=comp.belforte`
  ```
  vim crabserver/install.sh
  ```
There are two ways to build  image:1. You can manually run  commands
* build image
  ```
   build -t sbelforte/crabserver:v3.210301 crabserver
  ```
* push to
  ```
   push sbelforte/crabserver:v3.210301
  ```
* cleanup(IMAGE ID is from ` images` )
  ```
   rmi <IMAGE ID>
  ```
2. Use build.sh script that will build, push,  image
* run script
  ```
  =v3.210301 ./build.sh "crabserver"
  ```
* with e.g.
  ```
   images
   inspect sbelforte/crabserver:v3.210301
   inspect <IMAGE ID> # where <IMAGE ID> is from  images output
   run --rm -h `hostname -f` -v /tmp:/tmp -i -t sbelforte/crabserver:v3.210301 /bin/bash
  ```
  + the latter command logs you in the container and where can examine the `/data/srv` tree
### 3. Use to run this container
we have access to deploy CRAB services to 3 environments:
* testbed cluster
* production cluster
on where you need to deploy your service, you need to use proper KUBECONFIG configuration. Below example how to deploy to test cluster is provided. Details how to access dev clusters can be found here [https://cms-http-group.docs.cern.ch/k8s\_cluster/cmsweb\_developers\_k8s\_documentation/![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cms-http-group.docs.cern.ch/k8s_cluster/cmsweb_developers_k8s_documentation/) ;
cmsweb-testbed can be found here: [https://cms-http-group.docs.cern.ch/k8s\_cluster/cmsweb\_testbed\_cluster\_doc/![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cms-http-group.docs.cern.ch/k8s_cluster/cmsweb_testbed_cluster_doc/) ; and production cluster here: [https://cms-http-group.docs.cern.ch/k8s\_cluster/cmsweb\_production\_cluster\_doc/![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cms-http-group.docs.cern.ch/k8s_cluster/cmsweb_production_cluster_doc/). Service deployment details are provided here: [https://cms-http-group.docs.cern.ch/k8s\_cluster/deploy-srv/![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cms-http-group.docs.cern.ch/k8s_cluster/deploy-srv/)
#### Development Kubernetes clusters
In total 5 clusters are available for developers to test their services which are listed below:
* cmsweb-test1.cern.ch
* cmsweb-test2.cern.ch
* cmsweb-test3.cern.ch
* cmsweb-test4.cern.ch
* cmsweb-test5.cern.ch
Each of these clusters can be accessed by setting
* export KUBECONFIG=/afs/cern.ch/user/m/mimran/public/cmsweb-/config.cmsweb-test1
* export KUBECONFIG=/afs/cern.ch/user/m/mimran/public/cmsweb-/config.cmsweb-test2
* export KUBECONFIG=/afs/cern.ch/user/m/mimran/public/cmsweb-/config.cmsweb-test3
* export KUBECONFIG=/afs/cern.ch/user/m/mimran/public/cmsweb-/config.cmsweb-test4
* export KUBECONFIG=/afs/cern.ch/user/m/mimran/public/cmsweb-/config.cmsweb-test5
* export KUBECONFIG=/afs/cern.ch/user/m/mimran/public/cmsweb-/config.cmsweb-test6
Cluster number 2 is dedicated for and should be used by CRAB team. on which cluster you want to access, you will use different KUBECONFIG value.
#### Access to the cluster
* kubernetes tools are deployed at CERN on CC8 machines
  ```
  ssh lxplus8
  ```
* setup OS\_TOKEN and cluster's [OpensStack](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/OpensStack?topicparent=CMSPublic.CRABK8s;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") confing via
  ```
  export OS_TOKEN=$(openstack token issue -c id -f value)
  export KUBECONFIG=/afs/cern.ch/user/m/mimran/public/cmsweb-/config.cmsweb-test2
  ```
* get pods and verify that your setup is correct, you point to right cluster etc.
  ```
  kubectl -n crab get pod
  ```
#### Deploy new crabserver version
* go to the directory where you cloned CMSKubernetes
  ```
  cd ~/WORK//CMSKubernetes/kubernetes/cmsweb
  ```
* /update as needed
* use deploy-srv.sh script to deploy service to the cluster identified with `$test` (`test1` or `test2` are valid values)
  ```
  ./scripts/deploy-srv.sh crabserver v3.210301 $test
  ```
* ```
  kubectl -n crab exec -ti {POD_ID} bash
  ```
* that `/data/srv/current` points to correct version
  ```
  ls -l /data/srv/current
  ls  /data/srv/current/sw.crab_master/slc7_amd64_gcc630/cms/crabserver/
  ```
##### running crabserver service
```
kubectl -n crab  deployment crabserver
```
#### Create a new crabserver pod
* Clone
  ```
    clone https://github.com/dmwm/CMSKubernetes.
  ```
* Goto the services directory, which contains all .yaml files
  ```
  cd CMSKubernetes/kubernetes/cmsweb/services
  ```
* Create/apply crabserver pod with the help of corresponding .yaml file
  ```
  kubectl -n crab apply -f crabserver.yaml  --validate=false
  ```
  ```
  service/crabserver created
  configmap/crabserver created
  deployment.apps/crabserver created
  ```

kubectl -n crab scale deployment crabserver --replicas=0

####  crabserver pod
* Clone
  ```
    clone https://github.com/dmwm/CMSKubernetes.
  ```
* Goto the services directory, which contains all .yaml files
  ```
  cd CMSKubernetes/kubernetes/cmsweb/services
  ```
*  crabserver pod with the help of corresponding .yaml file
  ```
  kubectl  -f crabserver.yaml
  ```
  ```
  service "crabserver" deleted
  configmap "crabserver" deleted
  deployment.apps "crabserver" deleted
  ```
#### Operations within crabserver pod
Thinks that can be done after logging inside a pod with
```
kubectl -n crab exec -ti <podname> -- bash
```
##### code and version
The currently running code is in
* `ls /data/srv/current/sw*/sl*/`
Almost all that matters are python files in directories below this (note that the directory below `crabserver` has the version number)
* `ls /data/srv/current/sw*/sl*/cms/crabserver/*/lib/pyth*/site-packages`
External depenencies are in
* `ls /data/srv/current/sw*/sl*/external`
##### [GitHub](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/GitHub) clone
The container also contains a ready clone of CRABServer and WMCore GitHub repositories, so you can look at things and checkout different tags/branches for testing (see below). The local is already checkedout to point to the tag used in the build. The known developers forked repositories are already added as remotes. Access to GitHub is read only.

##### crabserver service within pod
the `start` command will kill before staring if it is running, so simply
* = /data/start.sh -c=
##### Stop crabserver service within pod
* `/data/stop.sh`
##### /test/hack crabserver
You can do one or both of the following two things:
1. run the crabserver application using python code from the GH repositories in `/data/repos/` instead of the container version in /data/srv/current
   * `/data/start.sh -c` # start the app from current
   * `/data/start.sh -g` # start the app from Github
2. run the crabserver in  **mode**. Crabserver runs in foreground, instead than as a daemon, with a pool of one single thread, instead of 25, so you can look interactively at messages **AND** play with `pdb` by editing the python and placing `import pdb; pdb.set_trace()` in some ad hoc location. This is most useful when used running from GH (so you do not mess with current code and can restore with  `stash`) but works also with `/data/start.sh -c -d`
   * `/data/start.sh -g -d`
##### With lower level commands
Instead of using the `start.sh` and `stop.sh` scripts "provided by us", the CRABServer application can be managed with standard "cmsweb appl" commands. Following lines do `start/status//stop`
```
sudo -H -u _crabserver bashs -l -c "/data/srv/current/config/crabserver/manage start 'I did read documentation'"
sudo -H -u _crabserver bashs -l -c '/data/srv/current/config/crabserver/manage status'
sudo -H -u _crabserver bashs -l -c "/data/srv/current/config/crabserver/manage start 'I did read documentation'"
sudo -H -u _crabserver bashs -l -c "/data/srv/current/config/crabserver/manage stop 'I did read documentation'"
```

#### service deployment
If for some reason you want to given service deployment, you can do that by using command:
```
kubectl  deployment crabserver -n crab
deployment.apps/crabserver edited
```
### 4. Working with secrets
#### Show all secrets names with basic info within CRAB namespace
```
kubectl -n crab get secrets
NAME                              TYPE                                      DATA   AGE
crabcache-secrets                   x                                        4      23h
crabserver-secrets                  x                                        6      23h
```
####  secret's content
```
kubectl -n crab  get secrets crabserver-secrets -o yaml |grep CRABServerAuth.py:|cut -d ' ' -f4|base64 --decode
```
####  secrets
```
kubectl -n crab  secrets crabserver-secrets
secret "crabserver-secrets" deleted
```
#### Deploy/create new CRAB secrets
It is possible to deploy CRAB secrets only, w/o worrying about the secretes needed for and CMSWEB internal authentication.
Those CRAB secrets are:
* `/data/srv/current/config/crabserver/config.py`
* `/data/srv/current/auth/crabserver/CRABServerAuth.py`
Only the scond file contains actual secrets. The first (`config.py`) could be moced outside secretes whenever we the time/need for.
The procedure to deploy new secrets is described in [https://cms-http-group.docs.cern.ch/k8s\_cluster/deploy-secrets/![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cms-http-group.docs.cern.ch/k8s_cluster/deploy-secrets/) ,
here is a recap :
1. `clone ssh://:7999/cmsweb-/services_config.`
2. `checkout` the correct branch ( `prod preprod test cmsweb-auth ...` )
3. `cd services_config/crabserver` and make sure that it has the correct secret files for the target cluster. Note that `CRABServerAuth.py` is not in ther repository and you need to get it from someone who knows secretes already !
4. `cd` to where you cloned CMSKubernetes, do `cd kubernetes/cmsweb` and run `./scripts/deploy-secrets.sh crab crabserver <path to the services_config clone>`
5. pod to make it pick up new secret files from `/etc/secrets/` and deploy them in `/data/srv/current/`
Example:
```
cd ~/WORK//services_config/  # I cloned already
 chekout test  # will work on e.g. cmsweb-test1
cp ~/private/CRABServerAuth.py-DEV+PRE ./CRABServerAuth.py # has access to DEV and PRE DB instances
cd ~/WORK//CMSKubernetes/kubernetes/cmsweb
K8T1  # my alias to setup  access for cmsweb-test1
./scripts/deploy-secrets.sh crab crabserver ~/WORK//services_config
kubectl -n crab scale deployment crabserver --replicas=0   # stop running pod
kubectl -n crab scale deployment crabserver --replicas=1   # start a new pod w/o waiting for previous one to have terminated
kubectl -n crab get pod  # to monitor pod
```
#### Deploy/create new secrets (full thing)
Following procedure recreates and redeploys all secrets, it is not needed anymore, but it is kept as documentation just in case
* Clone CMSKubernetes and checkout to the proper branch
  ```
   clone https://:@gitlab.cern.ch:8443/cmsweb-/services_config.
   checkout preprod
  ```
* Clone cmsweb-
  ```
    clone https://github.com/dmwm/CMSKubernetes.
  ```
* If you want to change password and or database instance then create [CRABServerAuth](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/CRABServerAuth?topicparent=CMSPublic.CRABK8s;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.").py file with new DB configuration
  ```
  cat ~/git_repos/services_config/crabserver/CRABServerAuth.py
  ```
* Need the following files, I got these from Imran and put into ~/git\_repos/imranFiles
  ```
  ll /afs/cern.ch/user/p/prsharma/git_repos/imranFiles
  ```
  ```
  -r--------. 1 prsharma zh 3044 Apr  9 13:41 cmsweb-hostcert.pem
  -r--------. 1 prsharma zh 1828 Apr  9 13:41 cmsweb-hostkey.pem
  -rw-r--r--. 1 prsharma zh   20 Apr  9 13:32 hmac
  -r--------. 1 prsharma zh 3387 Apr  9 13:41 robotcert.pem
  -r--------. 1 prsharma zh 1828 Apr  9 13:31 robotkey.pem
  ```
* Go to the cmswb directory and execute the following command to create/deploy new secrets
  ```
  ./scripts/deploy.sh create secrets ~/git_repos/services_config/ ~/git_repos/imranFiles ~/git_repos/imranFiles/hmac
  ```
  ```
  ...
  Create secrets in namespace: crab
  secret/robot-secrets configured
  secret/proxy-secrets configured
  +++ generate cmsweb service secrets
  secret/crabcache-secrets created
  secret/crabserver-secrets created
  ...
  crab              crabcache-secrets                       x                                4      55s
  ...
  ```
**Note1**: If you want to change password and database instance for crabserver, then follow the sequence of the following steps:
1.  secrets;
2. Deploy/create new secretswith appropriate changes in [CRABServerAuth](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/CRABServerAuth?topicparent=CMSPublic.CRABK8s;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.").py file;
3.  crabserver pod;
4. Create new crabserver pod.
### 5. Logs
The CRABServer application writes 2  in `/data/srv/logs/crabserver/` directory of the pod:
* `crabserver-YYYYMMDD-crabserver-pod-identifier.log`
  + orginates from the WMCore/REST server library which CRAB builds on and contains record of each HTTP transaction
    1. one line in same format as in [FrontEnd](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/FrontEnd?topicparent=CMSPublic.CRABK8s;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") , which is the basis for the parsing via and the [plots in Grafana![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://monit-grafana.cern.ch/d/cmswebk8s-timber/cmsweb-timber-?orgId=11) in particular our [CRABServer page![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://monit-grafana.cern.ch/d/qUVV6S0Gk/crab-timber-pods?orgId=11)
    2. multiple lines with log of the SQL query (if any) performed via WMCore API at CRABServer request
* `CRAB-YYYYMMDD.log`
  + is the output of python logger from CRABServer application
access to the logs can be currently done in 3 ways, see [this talk![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://indico.cern.ch/event/1075972/contributions/4525199/attachments/2307768/3926376/Persistent%20Storage.pdf) from M. Imran on [Sept 2021![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://indico.cern.ch/event/1075972/)
* directly from inside the running pod (of course)
* for `cmsweb` and `cmsweb-testbed` clusters only, the local `/data/srv/logs/crabserver` directory is mounted on a remote, shared CEPH volume which is then accessible in real time also from any other pod of the cluster and it is also mounted on the VM `vm0750.cern.ch` as `/cephfs/product/crab-logs/` or /cephfs/testbed/crab-logs/=
* for `cmsweb` and `cmsweb-testbed` clusters only, a sidecar in the crabserver pod runs a `filebeat` daemon which continuously send data to a remote `Fluentd` server which uploads a new log fragment to S3 storage (`s3.cern.ch`) every 15 minutes. Those log fragments are then downloaded to and available in `/data/s3/logs/*/crab-logs`
**NOTE** there is no remote access to logs for `cmsweb-test*` clusters, they are only local to the pod and are reset at any pod re-deployment.
### 6. Alerts, Alarms, Restarts
It is possible to setup automatic alerts and alarms based of Pod metrics.Currently implemented:
1. Simplest way is via `PodManager` and : [CRAB Server alerts and automatic pod based on metrics and PodManager](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/CRABServerPodAlertRestartPrometheus)
   * Useful for example when number of open fds is too high.
### 7. Support on
We only have access to CRAB pods, to address issues with nodes (e.g. stuck network connections) need to ask help from  (currently Imran, Panos, , , Andreas )
### 8. Bookkeeping
remember to
* write e-log entry
  + [https://cms-logbook.cern.ch/elog/Analysis+Operations/?cmd=New![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cms-logbook.cern.ch/elog/Analysis%2BOperations/?cmd=New)
* make a PR for CMSKubernetes so that it stays up to date on which image should be deployed
  + example: [https://github.com/dmwm/CMSKubernetes/pull/80![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/dmwm/CMSKubernetes/pull/80)
-- - 2019-10-23

# Submitting to the CERN HTCondor pool
This twiki explains how to use the `preparelocal` CRAB [command](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/CRAB3Commands#crab_preparelocal) to send to the CERN condor pool ([))
Table of contents
* [Submitting to the CERN HTCondor pool](#Submitting_jobs_to_the_CERN_HTCo)
  + [ setup](#Preliminary_setup)
  + [HTCondor submission](#HTCondor_submission)
##  setup
Once you have [setup the environment](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookCRAB3Tutorial#Setup_the_environment), you need to create the [CRAB project directory](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/CRAB3Commands#CRAB_project_directory) for your task.
If you
* have already submitted the task you can
  + simply `cd` to the project directory created at submission time
  + or create it with the `crab remake` [command](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/CRAB3Commands#crab_remake);
* have not yet submitted the task, do it (if you do not want it to run on grid, kill it as soon as it reaches SUBMITTED status)
Once the CRAB project directory is created, and task has reached the SUBMITTED status execute
```
crab preparelocal --dir = <PROJECTDIR>
```
## HTCondor submission
Add `#!/bin/bash` as first line of the `run_job.sh` file in the `<PROJECTDIR>/local` directory.Create a "batch" subdirectory in order to keep HTCondor files separated:
```
mkdir <PROJECTDIR>/local/batch
cd <PROJECTDIR>/local/batch
```
and place the following `task.jdl` example file therein:
```
Universe  = vanilla
Executable = ../run_job.sh
Arguments = $(I)
Log = log/
Output = out/job.$(Cluster).$(Process).out
Error = err/job.$(Cluster).$(Process).err
transfer_input_files = ../CMSRunAnalysis.sh, ../CMSRunAnalysis.tar.gz, ../InputArgs.txt, ../Job.submit, ../cmscp.py, ../gWMS-CMSRunAnalysis.sh, ../input_files.tar.gz, ../run_and_lumis.tar.gz, ../sandbox.tar.gz
should_transfer_files = YES
when_to_transfer_output = ON_EXIT
# Resources request
RequestCpus = 1
RequestMemory = 2000
+JobFlavour = "workday"
#  selection
 I from (
1
2
3
4
)
```
This configuration example will submit only the first 4 of the task.
In order to customise the resources request (number of CPUs, maximum memory, maximum runtime, etc.) and the submission please refer to the CERN Batch Service documentation: [http://batchdocs.web.cern.ch/batchdocs/local/submit.html![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://batchdocs.web.cern.ch/batchdocs/local/submit.html)Create the auxiliary directories and submit the with:
```
mkdir out err log
condor_submit task.jdl
```
You can check the status with:
```
condor_q -nobatch
```
##
Your may need a e.g. if they need to use xrootd to access remote files, either intentionally or due to automatic fallback from local [EOS](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/EOS) read. Reading from [EOS](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/EOS) locally at CERN is controlled via your local username and proxy is not needed for that.HTCondor will not automatically make such proxy available to (sort of obvious, since you can submit w/o creating it), so it is up to you to make this possible. There are (at leat) 3 different ways.
1. place your proxy in your home area, rely on the fact that this is mounted on all batch nodes, and define an env. variable in the job to point there
   * pros: recommended by CERN IT. Simple.
   * cons: you can not use this on a different HTCondor pool where your home is not mounted on WN.
2. pass your proxy to your job as input file and
   * pros: recommended by CERN IT. Will work no matter where your will run (flock to some distant pool ?). You do not need to care about your proxy after you submitted. Will work from any place which offers condor\_submit.
   * cons: complicated. No way to renew the proxy once the have been submitted.
3. place your proxy in your home areas as 1., rely on the fact that local htcondor scheduler mount your home disk (currently true at FNALLPC and CERN) and ask HTCondor to delegate the proxy from there to the running
   * pros: simple. Will work no matter where your will run (flock to some distant pool ?). Proxy on running will be automatically renewed by HTCondor
   * cons: may not work at all sites where HTCondor is available.
In case 1. and 3. you need to use `voms-proxy-init -voms cms` as needed in order to have a valid proxy as long as your may need it. Which is a bit more often than what's required in case you submit via CRAB, since CRAB server has a dedicated machinery to renew your proxy. In case 2. whatever you do locally has no effect on running .The first two methods are documented here: [)
Instructions for the 3rd one (which is very similar to what CRAB does) are below:
```
  1  mkdir -p $HOME/tmp
  2 put your  in your home area with the following line in your login file:
    for .cshrc: setenv X509_USER_PROXY $HOME/tmp/
    for .bashrc: export X509_USER_PROXY=$HOME/tmp/
    (then log out and log in again and do voms-proxy-init ....)
  3. put this in your JDL
  x509userproxy = $)
  use_x509userproxy = True
```
-- - 2018-06-06

# Puppet profile for the CRAB project:
|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| : ![5](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/pub/CMS/WebPreferences/complete5.png) | Go to [SWGuideCrab](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideCrab) |
All questions about TaskWorker and deploying it on private machine should go to For production and pre-production: Local service account used to deploy, run and operate the service is .
Contents:
* [Puppet profile for the CRAB project:](#Puppet_profile_for_the_CRAB_proj)
  + [Introduction](#Introduction)
  + [Repository](#Repository)
    - [Puppet environments vs. repository branches vs. service instances](#Puppet_environments_vs_repositor)

  + [Configure your project environment in aiadmin.](#Configure_your_project_environme)

      * [Creating the virtual machine:](#Creating_the_virtual_machine)
  + [Configure your virtual machine and services via puppet](#Configure_your_virtual_machine_a)

  + [Puppet classes](#Puppet_classes)
## Introduction
This twiki explains how to use the puppet profile for the CRAB project and deploying different type of machines (a.k.a. CRAB Server | TaskWorker | Schedd | ) via Puppet.The basic steps that are usually followed are:
1. Configure your project environment in aiadmin.
2. Create a virtual machine of the proper type with the ai-\* toolset.pre
3. Configure your virtual machine and services via puppet.
**Note:**
Legend of colors for the examples:
```
Commands to execute
Output sample of the executed commands
Configuration files
Other files
```
## Repository
* [https://gitlab.cern.ch:8443/ai/it-puppet-hostgroup-vocmsglidein![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://gitlab.cern.ch:8443/ai/it-puppet-hostgroup-vocmsglidein)
* after you select a branch, host specific configurations are in `data/fqdns` see below about  branches
### Puppet environments vs. repository branches vs. service instances
One thing you need to bare in mind: your machine may exist in which ever puppet environment you wish (it is defined during the machine creation time), but there is a strict mapping between the branch in the gitlab and the puppet environments as follows
```
+--------------------+------------------------+
| gitlab branch:     | Puppet environment:    |
+--------------------+------------------------+
| crabdev            | crabdev                |
| qa                 | qa                     |
| master             | production             |
+--------------------+------------------------+
```
On the other hand the connection between the service instances and the puppet environment is not strict, but it is used to
enforce a policy of good practice for making development and operations easy. As detailed below we want `qa` to be
the place where to validate (`qa = quality assurance`) changes to pupper profile for production machines.
All service instances (production, testbed...) are production from puppet point of , simply with different profiles since
they may e.g. connect to one database or another, one condor pool or another. Already puppet allows for running different
versions of the CRAB services on different machines.
### Puppet organization
We would have liked to follow the policy in the following table, which is supposed to mimic what is done e.g. on lxplus:
| [Puppet environment](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/CRABPuppet?sortcol=0;table=2;up=0#sorted_table "Sort by this column") | [Gitlab Branch](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/CRABPuppet?sortcol=1;table=2;up=0#sorted_table "Sort by this column") | [Used /bin//CMSPublic/CRABPuppet?sortcol=2;table=2;up=0#sorted_table "Sort by this column") | [# of machines in it (for every project)](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/CRABPuppet?sortcol=3;table=2;up=0#sorted_table "Sort by this column") | [Notes](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/CRABPuppet?sortcol=4;table=2;up=0#sorted_table "Sort by this column") |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| crabdev | crabdev | Experiment, learn, test, fool around | 1 | one small private VM, e.g. crab-dev-tw01 and one test schedd which is in the global SI pool but does not normally receives user submissions (vocms059) |
| qa | qa | changes to puppet profiles before deployment in production | (1, 10% of production machines) E.g. TWs: 1 Schedds: 2 | Machines in QA are production machines, identical to others, where we deploy TESTED puppet changes (or very safe and clean ones) in order to avoid large scale damage. |
| production | master | production | All other production machines | Puppet changes here should never result in operational problems. |
 **BUT IT TURNED OUT THAT THIS IS NOT POSSIBLE** because we pick condor configuration from SI repository and in there they have
decided to use `master` for the global pool and `qa` for the ITB pool where to test new HTCondor changes.
Of course that makes sense in a world where the only changes are HTCondor ones.
And since **we can not use `qa` branch in our repository in any other way than how SI uses it** (whichever machine we put in qa branch,
will pick condor deployment from SI qa branch !) this makes life more complicated for managing/testing other puppet changes. As a mitigation,
we introduced the [node.pp file](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/CRABPuppet#node_pp_file_in_CRAB_puppet_repo) which allows to make some changes in only one VM.
A fully satisfactory solution is stille eluding us. Only if that was found, the following notes would apply:Notes:
1. Machines in qa and in production environment are ALL production machines, used in the same way and with identical configuration
2. Schedd’s have slightly different configuration in order to be in global pool or ITB but should still be in production puppet profile, simply there are multiple kind of schedds.
3. Changes to puppet profiles are pushed to qa in order to make sure that they do not disrupt operation machines and after e.g. a few days are moved to master/production.
4. Most of the time qa and master will have exactly same content
## Configure your project environment in aiadmin.
* Login to the aiadmin cluster:
```
ssh aiadmin.cern.ch
```
* Check which OpenStack projects you are associated with:
```
openstack project list
```
The output should like something like this:
```
+--------------------------------------+------------------+
| ID                                   | Name             |
+--------------------------------------+------------------+
| 180ca677-8b4b-4bbd-9b4c-d69652c97638 | Personal tivanov |
| 580b613d-85da-453c-9b59-012549ebfd9e | CMS CRAB         |
+--------------------------------------+------------------+
```
You will see your own project for sure. In case the 'CMS CRAB' Project is missing contact the VOC.
* Create the configuration script (/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](file://) with your project environment for your private openstack project and for the CRAB Openstack project:
```
#!/usr/bin/env bash
projname="crab"
[[ -n $1 ]] && projname=$1
case $projname in
    private)
   echo Setting the ENV for the PRIVATE project
   os_tenant_name='Personal tivanov'
   os_project_id='<-- fill your project Id here -->'
   os_project_name=$os_tenant_name
   ;;
    crab)
   echo Setting the ENV for the CRAB project
   os_tenant_name='CMS CRAB'
   os_project_id='580b613d-85da-453c-9b59-012549ebfd9e'
   os_project_name=$os_tenant_name
   ;;
    *)
   # echo No project specified
   echo  project name $projname
   ;;
esac
export OS_AUTH_URL=https://keystone.cern.ch/krb/v3
export OS_AUTH_TYPE=v3kerberos
export OS_USERNAME=`id -un`
export OS_TENANT_NAME=$os_tenant_name
export OS_IDENTITY_API_VERSION=3
export OS_PROJECT_DOMAIN_ID=default
# With the addition of Keystone we have standardized on the term **project**
# as the entity that owns the resources.
export OS_PROJECT_ID=$os_project_id
export OS_PROJECT_NAME=$os_project_name
unset OS_USER_DOMAIN_NAME
```
Fill the missing gaps and source it with the proper project as first parameter (crab|private):
```
source ~/.openrc private
```
![, important](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/.gif ", important")  NOTE: PLEASE once you source it ALWAYS check to which project your current environment has been set for real - do not trust only the 'echos' from the configuration scrip:.
```
openstack server list
```
You should see only your private machines now:
```
openstack server list
+--------------------------------------+------------------+---------+--------------------------------------------------------+-------+-----------+
| ID                                   | Name             | Status  | Networks                                               | Image | Flavor    |
+--------------------------------------+------------------+---------+--------------------------------------------------------+-------+-----------+
| 15168816-fdba-43c1-8d6d-614ba3e99ee7 | crab-priv-tw03   | SHUTOFF | CERN_NETWORK=188.185.118.157, 2001:1458:d00:b::100:297 |       | m2.medium |
| 74b17e17-a362-4da7-8d3a-d1c164ffe76c | crab-priv-tw02   | SHUTOFF | CERN_NETWORK=137.138.152.94, 2001:1458:d00:13::7d      |       | m2.medium |
| 572b6285-05b9-48a9-8f92-d030c0d6b976 | crab-priv-rest01 | SHUTOFF | CERN_NETWORK=137.138.148.83, 2001:1458:     |       | m2.medium |
+--------------------------------------+------------------+---------+--------------------------------------------------------+-------+-----------+
```
In case you want to switch to the CRAB OpenStack project:
```
source ~/.openrc crab
```
## Create a virtual machine of the proper type with the ai-\* toolset
For every separate type of machine in our project we have different modules/classes in the puppet profile (not all of them evolved to final separate modules, some of them are just classes yet and some of them are really scattered across the whole profile). Few examples how to create instances of different type of machines:
### Deployment of CRAB TaskWorker via Puppet
* Set few variables in advance:
```
hostname='crab-priv-tw01'
foremanenv='crabdev'
openstackflav='m2.medium'
osrelease='cc7'
```
#### Preparing the puppet configurations:
Before creating the machine you need to prepare the .yaml configuration file in the repository of the puppet host group hostgroup:
```
 https://:@gitlab.cern.ch:8443/ai/it-puppet-hostgroup-vocmsglidein.git
cd it-puppet-hostgroup-vocmsglidein
git checkout crabdev
git pull origin crabdev
```
Create the .yaml file for the machine:
```
emacs -nw data/fqdns/${hostname}.cern.ch.yaml
```
Put the following content there, while filling the relevant fields marked with '<-- -->' tags (examples in the comment lines):
```
gwms_type: crabtaskworker
sudo:
   users:
   egroups:
     - cms-service-crab3htcondor-admins
sssd::interactiveallowusers:
   - cmsprd
sssd::interactiveallowgroups:
   - cms-service-crab
   - cms-service-crab2
   - cms-service-glideinwms
   - cms-service-crab3htcondor
   - cms-voc
sssd::filter_users:
   - mlindner
   - tbato
sendmail::masquerade_enable: false
sendmail::root_email:
tw_release: <-- the TW tag/version -->
tw_scram_arch: <-- the TW architecture -->
tw_repo: <-- the cmswe repository for the rpms -->
tw_name: <-- the TW name to be used for identification in the DB -->
: <-- the TW mode -->
tw_nslaves: <-- the number of forked process (workers) -->
tw_resturl: <-- the urls to the cmsweb forntend(valid only in private mode) -->

## Configure your virtual machine and services via puppet
### Migration to CC7
![, important](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/.gif ", important")  NOTE: Before you put the machine you are about to work with on drain in [https://gitlab.cern.ch//CRAB3ServerConfig/![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://gitlab.cern.ch//CRAB3ServerConfig/) What have been mentioned above is the correct sequence of actions to be used for the migration to CC7, but in case one wants to automate things a little bit, then better create the following script (and fill the blanc spaces accordingly):
```
[tivanov@aiadm32 ~]$ cat > slc6-slc7.sh <<EOF
#!/bin/bash
# Set the correct OpenStack project to run in (crab|private)
. ~/.openrc crab
hostname='........' # example: ''
foremanenv='........' # example: 'production'
openstackflav='........' # example: 'r2.2xlarge'
avzone='........' # example : cern-geneva-a
ipv6ready='false' # true or false
osrelease='cc7'
=${hostname}_upgrade.log
="${hostname}_standard ${hostname}_high"
touch $
# redirect everything to
exec &>>$
echo
echo =======================================================
echo : `basename $0` at: `date -Im`
wrapfun (){
 ###
 ### returns error if either the executed command fails or the execution itself
 ### is skipped due to a previous succesfull run of the cutrrent step
 ###
 step=$1
 execute=$2
 echo
 echo -------------------------------------------------------
 echo -e "wrapfun call for: \n step: $step \n exec: $execute\n" >&2
 grep "Step $step done" $ >/dev/null 2>&1
 toexecute=$?
 if [[ $toexecute -eq 0 ]]
 then
     ## found the srting -> we return false and continue
     retval=255
 else
     ## have not found the string -> we execute and return the err value
     eval $execute 2>&1
     err=$?
     [[ $err -eq 0 ]] && echo "Step $step done"
     retval=$err
 fi
 echo -------------------------------------------------------
 return $retval
}
iswaiting () {  [[ $1 -eq 0 ]] && return 0  ; echo Not; return 1  ;}
echo
echo =======================================================
echo "Detaching the "
step=1
for volume in $
do
    wrapfun $step "openstack server remove volume ${hostname} $volume"
    let step+=1
done
echo
echo =======================================================
echo "Kill the VM"
step=3
wrapfun $step "ai-kill ${hostname}"
lasterr=$?
echo
echo =======================================================
echo "$(iswaiting $lasterr) Waiting for the DNS record of $hostname to be cleared"
[[ $lasterr -eq 0 ]] && while (host $hostname > /dev/null 2>&1); do sleep 60; done
echo
echo =======================================================
echo "Rebuild the VM"
step=4
wrapfun $step "ai-bs -g vocmsglidein/crab --$osrelease ---environment $foremanenv  --landb-mainuser CMS-SERVICE-CRAB3HTCONDOR --landb-responsible CMS-SERVICE-CRAB3HTCONDOR-ADMINS --nova-flavor $openstackflav --nova-availabilityzone $avzone --nova-sshkey lxplus --nova-parameter landb-ipv6ready=$ipv6ready -v $hostname"
lasterr=$?
echo
echo =======================================================
echo  "$(iswaiting $lasterr) Waiting for the build process to finish."
[[ $lasterr -eq 0 ]] && until (host $hostname > /dev/null 2>&1); do sleep 10;done
echo
echo =======================================================
echo "$(iswaiting $lasterr) Waiting for $hostname to show up."
[[ $lasterr -eq 0 ]] && until (host $hostname > /dev/null 2>&1); do sleep 10;done
echo
echo =======================================================
echo "$(iswaiting $lasterr) Waiting for $hostname to boot."
[[ $lasterr -eq 0 ]] && until (ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null root@$hostname 'true' 2>/dev/null); do sleep 10; done
echo
echo =======================================================
echo "Re attach the "
step=5
mnt_status=0
for volume in $
do
    wrapfun $step "openstack server add volume ${hostname} $volume"
    lasterr=$?
    let mnt_status+=$lasterr
    let step+=1
done
if [[ $mnt_status -eq 0 ]]
then
    echo
    echo =======================================================
    echo "All  mounted correctly"
else
    echo
    echo =======================================================
    echo "ERR while mounting some "
fi
echo
echo =======================================================
echo "DONE"
echo =======================================================
EOF
```

### distribution.
![, important](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/.gif ", important")  NOTE: This may not be the best place to put the following information but since we have only this page as a puppet dedicated one I will paste it here and the page may be reorganized later. The script that is used to send data to Elastic search is the following: [https://gitlab.cern.ch/ai/it-puppet-hostgroup-vocmsglidein/blob/master/code/files/profiles/crabtaskworker/GenerateMONIT.py![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://gitlab.cern.ch/ai/it-puppet-hostgroup-vocmsglidein/blob/master/code/files/profiles/crabtaskworker/GenerateMONIT.py)The operator maintaining this needs to be sure there is only one instance of the script running at a time, because we do not need redundant data feed to ES and also if the script is placed at a machine which cannot run it properly the cron job starts flooding with emails everybody in the e-group ...... . By design the host supposed to run the script should be the TaskWorker but could also be any other machine (even a dedicated one). So far in order to ensure the single instance of the script we use the following preventive measures:
1. We have the name of the machine supposed to run it hardcoded in the script, which is not the best method but used it just as an extra precaution.
2. We have one parameter in the [TaskWorker](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/TaskWorker?topicparent=CMSPublic.CRABPuppet;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") profile which is read by the hiera function and is used to manage the distribution of the script to the machines supposed to run it. In order to enable the script on one machine in the .yaml file used to configure it (code/qdns/crab--tw0[0-9]\*.cern.ch.yaml) put the following enable/disable flag:
```
enable_generatemonit: true
```
Example: [https://gitlab.cern.ch/ai/it-puppet-hostgroup-vocmsglidein/blob/master/data/fqdns/crab-prod-tw01.cern.ch.yaml#L30![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://gitlab.cern.ch/ai/it-puppet-hostgroup-vocmsglidein/blob/master/data/fqdns/crab-prod-tw01.cern.ch.yaml#L30)The 'hiera' parameter is read here: [https://gitlab.cern.ch/ai/it-puppet-hostgroup-vocmsglidein/blob/master/code/manifests/profiles/crabtaskworker.pp#L13![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://gitlab.cern.ch/ai/it-puppet-hostgroup-vocmsglidein/blob/master/code/manifests/profiles/crabtaskworker.pp#L13)and is used here: [https://gitlab.cern.ch/ai/it-puppet-hostgroup-vocmsglidein/blob/master/code/manifests/profiles/crabtaskworker.pp#L249-262![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://gitlab.cern.ch/ai/it-puppet-hostgroup-vocmsglidein/blob/master/code/manifests/profiles/crabtaskworker.pp#L249-262)

  + [Rules 2021-09-rule-1 and -2: HTTP 503 errors](#Rules_2021_09_rule_1_and_2_HTTP)

# CRAB Server pod - alerts and automatic restart based on metrics
##
It is possible to automatically restart a `crabserver` pod based on the value of various metrics.In particular, we currently have two rules in place:
1. (2021-09-rule-1) If a pod has more than 75 open fds (averaged over 10m), then an alert is raised and an email notification is sent
2. (2021-09-rule-2) If a pod has more than 100 open fds (averaged over 30m), then an alert is raised, an email notification is sent and the pod itself is restarted
## Rules 2021-09-rule-1 and -2: HTTP 503 errors
### The problem
Since a few months, after migrating the `crabserver` to the cluster, when the load on the system gets higher we see that some POST/PUT requests to the `crabserver` fail with error 503. Sometimes the problem affects a single pod and solved itself after a few minutes, while some other times restarting the failing pod was enough to make the problem disappear. However, it happened that restarting the failing pod made the problem move to other pods. In these cases restarting all the pods was the only viable option.We noticed that the http 503 errors are correlated with an increase in the number of open fds per pod.Detailed discussion available at
* [jira/CMSKUBERNETES-80![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://its.cern.ch/jira/browse/CMSKUBERNETES-80)
* [dmwm/CRABServer/6708](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/670 "dmwm/CRABserver/6708")
### The band-aid: automatically restarting the pod based on metrics
While trying to replicate the problem and while looking for a proper solution, we convened that adding some tailored alerts and automatically restarting the failing pods could help us in the unfortunate event that this problem present itself again.The current CMSWEB clusters infrastructure provides:
* retrieval of certain metrics from the pods with
* the possibility to set alerts based on the value of these metrics (Step 1). This creates alerts in  [`alertmanager` ![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cms-monitoring.cern.ch/alertmanager/#/alerts)
* the possibility to send notifications when an alert is recorded (Step 2)
* the possibility to perform some action on the pod that originated the alert, such as restarting it (Step 3)
#### Step 1
References to and alertmanager:
* [https://.io/docs/alerting/latest/overview/![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://.io/docs/alerting/latest/overview/)
* [https://.io/docs/alerting/latest/configuration/![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://.io/docs/alerting/latest/configuration/)
* [Presentation about CMSMonitoring\_AlertManager![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://www.dropbox.com/s/8p2qlr58vduey06/CMSMonitoring_AlertManager.pdf?dl=0)
* Reference of CMS monitoring infrastructure [https://cmsmonit-docs.web.cern.ch/ ![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cmsmonit-docs.web.cern.ch/)
The list of available metrics is retrieved within a pod with:
```
> curl -s http://localhost:18270/metrics | grep crab | egrep -v "HELP|TYPE"
crabserver_cpu_percent 0
[...]
crabserver_process_open_fds 7
[...]
```
The alerts are configured with a `yaml` file ending with .rules. Every alert file can be tested with promtool and the configuration of the test is contained in a yaml file ending with `.test.`If you want to set alerts based on these metrics, it is necessary to change the alert files:
* in [dmwm/CMSKubernetes![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/dmwm/CMSKubernetes) : `kubernetes/cmsweb/monitoring//rules/crabserver.rules`
* in [gitlab/cmsmonitoring/cmsmon-config![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://gitlab.cern.ch/cmsmonitoring/cmsmon-configs/) : /crabserver.rules
The changes in these two repos need to be almost identical. The only diference is that the `host:` directive need to be present only in `CMSKubernetes` repo.The value used to check if an alert should be triggered can be directly the metric or a function of those metrics. A description of the available function is availble on the official documentation, at [https://.io/docs//latest/querying/functions/ . ![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://.io/docs//latest/querying/functions/)In particular, we are interested in `aggregation_over_time`, since we want to smoothen the metric with a rolling average.For example, we wanted to add an alert when the average over time (for 30m) of the metric `crabserver_process_open_fds` is above 100, so we needed to add
```
# crabserver.rules
groups:
- name: crabserver
  rules:
[...]
  - record: avg_open_fds_30m
    expr: avg_over_time(crabserver_process_open_fds[30m])
[...]
  - alert: CRAB server service has high number of fds
    expr: avg_open_fds_30m > 100
    for: 1m
    labels:
      severity: high
      tag: cmsweb
      service: crab
      host: "{{ $labels.host }}"                                      # this line is not necessary in the gitlab repo
      action: Please restart CRAB server on {{ $labels.instance }}
    annotations:
      summary: "CRAB {{ $labels.env }} environment"
      description: "{{ $labels.env }} has high level of fds {{ $value }} (avg 30m) for more than 1m"
[...]
```
Notice that we set two time intervals:
* length of the interval over which to compute the rolling average. Selecting 30m means that the variable used to trigger the alert is the rolling average of the metric crabserver\_process\_open\_fds over the last 30m. This value has to be considered as a generic metric
* lentgh of the interval for which the generic metric need to be over the threshold. Since the data is retrieved every 1m, selecting for: 1m means "as soon as"
It is also necessary to change the test files:
* in [dmwm/CMSKubernetes![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/dmwm/CMSKubernetes) : `kubernetes/cmsweb/monitoring//rules/crabserver.test`
* in [gitlab/cmsmonitoring/cmsmon-config![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://gitlab.cern.ch/cmsmonitoring/cmsmon-configs/) : `/crabserver.test`
```
# crabserver.test
[...]
- interval: 1m
  input_series:
  - series: 'avg_open_fds_30m{env="prod",instance="test-instance",host="-test"}' # no `,host="-test"` in gitlab repo
    values: '101+1x100'
  alert_rule_test:
      - eval_time: 10m
        alertname: CRAB server service has high number of fds
        exp_alerts:
            - exp_labels:
                 severity: high
                 tag: cmsweb
                 service: crab
                 host: -test                                            # this line is not necessary in the gitlab repo
                 action: Please restart CRAB server on test-instance
                 instance: test-instance
                 env: prod
              exp_annotations:
                 summary: "CRAB prod environment"
                 description: "prod has high level of fds 111 (avg 30m) for more than 1m"
[...]
```
The offical reference on alert unit test is available at [https://www..io/docs//latest/configuration/unit\_testing\_rules/![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://www..io/docs//latest/configuration/unit_testing_rules/)While how to set the rules may be straightforward, how to set the correct values for the alert test is not so much. You need to know that:
* test an alert by generating a synthetic set of values that emulate the values of the generic metric over time. We define these values insdide the list argument of the key values: . The first value of the list correspond to time=0, then every element of this list is separated by each other in time by the interval: .  checks that the emulated value of the generic metric corresponding to eval\_time after time=0 triggers the alert, and that the alert that would have been triggered matches the one provided in the unit test.
* `values: 'A+BxC'`: is expanded into the list `[A, A+B, A+2*B, ..., A+C*B]`. This is a nice convenient way of generating the list of values of the generic metric.
* since the interval is set to 1m, it means that the first value (A) correspond to the first minute, the second (A+B) to the second minute, ... the last value is (A+100\*B) correspond to 100m after the beginning
* since eval\_time is 10m, it means that the unittest checks if the alert would be fired with the value `A+10*B`.
* In our case, `avg_open_fds_30m` after 10m is 101+10\*1 = 111, which is greater than 100, so this test passes.
You can check what you have written with
* You can check that the alert syntax is correct with the command (available in lxplus, without sourcing any environment) /cvmfs/cms.cern.ch/cmsmon/promtool check rules kubernetes/cmsweb/monit
  oring//rules/crabserver.rules
* You can check that the alert matches the values that you expect with /cvmfs/cms.cern.ch/cmsmon/promtool test rules kubernetes/cmsweb/ring//rules/crabserver.test
Such changes have been implemented in the PRs
* test values [dmwm/CMSKubernetes/814![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/dmwm/CMSKubernetes/pull/814)
* production-ready values [dmwm/CMSKubernetes/816![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/dmwm/CMSKubernetes/pull/816)
* test values [gitlab/cmsmonitoring/cmsmon-config/11![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://gitlab.cern.ch/cmsmonitoring/cmsmon-configs/-/merge_requests/11)
* production-ready values [gitlab/cmsmonitoring/cmsmon-config/12![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://gitlab.cern.ch/cmsmonitoring/cmsmon-configs/-/merge_requests/12)
#### Step 2
Based on the alerts just defined, it is possible to send notifications. The settings are kept in alertmanager/alertmanager.yaml in [gitlab/cmsmonitoring/cmsmon-config. ![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://gitlab.cern.ch/cmsmonitoring/cmsmon-configs/)It is possible to receive notifications through the following channels
* email
* Whatever supports webhooks, such as slack (already implemented), mattermost, telegram, ...
Example of changes have been implemented in [gitlab/cmsmonitoring/cmsmon-config/13![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://gitlab.cern.ch/cmsmonitoring/cmsmon-configs/-/merge_requests/13)
#### Step 3
It is then necessary to change the PodManager config so that it reacts to the alert in alertmanager. The configuration is kept in the file `podmanager/config.json` in the repo [gitlab//services\_config/ ![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://gitlab.cern.ch//services_config/), where the prod branch contains the configuration for the prod cluster and the `preprod` branch contains the configuration for the testbed cluster. It is necessary to provide a PR for both branches.Reference changes are:
* `preprod`: [109![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://gitlab.cern.ch//services_config/-/merge_requests/109)
* `prod`: [110![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://gitlab.cern.ch//services_config/-/merge_requests/110)
### Other approaches
If this "band-aid" proves not to be efficient, then we may explore other automatic restarting procedures, such as creating alerts based on generic metric available in . This approach may not be too straightforward and has been currently put on hold.-- - 2021-09-17
