body:
If you are experiencing TWiki instability from outside the CERN network, please connect via the CERN internal network - see [KB0010688![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cern.service-now.com/service-portal?id=KB0010688) for details
>![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/web-bg-small.gif) [CMSPublic Web](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WebHome)>[SWGuide](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuide)>[SWGuideCrab](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideCrab)>[CRABStandardCorrectiveActions](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/CRABStandardCorrectiveActions "Topic revision: 11 (2022-10-28 - 00:07:06)") (2022-10-28, )[![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/uweb-o14.gif) Edit](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/CRABStandardCorrectiveActions?t=1777868501;nowysiwyg=1 "Edit this topic text")[Attach](/twiki/bin/attach/CMSPublic/CRABStandardCorrectiveActions "Attach an image or document to this topic")[PDF](/twiki/bin/genpdf/CMSPublic/CRABStandardCorrectiveActions "Create a PDF file for the topic")
# Standard Corrective Actions for known problems
* [Standard Corrective Actions for known problems](#Standard_Corrective_Actions_for)
  + [TW not running](#TW_not_running)
  + [DBS Migrations fail causing Publisher failures](#DBS_Migrations_fail_causing_Publ)
## TW not running
* Diagnosis
  + task pile up in status NEW in [https://monit-grafana.cern.ch/d/000000185/crab-metrics![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://monit-grafana.cern.ch/d/000000185/crab-metrics)
* Cure
  + log on crab-prod-tw01 or wherever appropriate, try to find out what's happeneed, do `sudo`  and restart container
## DBS Migrations fail causing Publisher failures
* Diagnosis:
  + Publication Aquired plot in [PUBLICATION: ACQUIRED (cumulative 10m)![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://monit-grafana.cern.ch/d/CsnjLe6Mk/crab-overview?orgId=11&from=now-7d&to=now&viewPanel=30) develops a significat (>1k) baseline, indicating that some are stuck in Aquired and never get published.
     ![grafana1.png](/twiki/pub/CMSPublic/CRABStandardCorrectiveActions/Screenshot_from_2022-02-25_15-25-27.png)
     This can be due to many reasons, but failed migrations is a known cause and needs to be looked at first. A new cause after we switched to go-based DBS server, is `not allowed for migration Error: dataset ,,, has status '`. Only dataset in status VALID are allowed to migrate. There is no tool to discover and handle this `not allowed` use case. FIguring out requires navigating logs in `$logspath/processes`
  + When data failed to migrate, Publisher will save `migration_input` and `migration_request_id` and timestamp into `$logspath/migrations/TerminallyFailedLog.txt`
     You can read logs using utility script (log mostly duplicate because Publisher has some retries mechanism, in case DBS migrate server are temporary down):
    - Log on inside a running Publisher container
    - `source env.sh`
    - Optionally do a `git pull` on the `CRABServer` directory there if the scripts indicated here need updating
    - `/data/repos/CRABServer/scripts/Utils/FindFailedMigrations.py` (you can use default value of `--file` )
    - Example output:
      Show  Hide
      ```
      [crab3@crab-prod-tw01 Publisher]$   /data/repos/CRABServer/scripts/Utils/FindFailedMigrations.py
      Found 6 unique migration IDs logged as terminally failed
       3126063
       3126064
       3126065
       3126066
       3126067
       3126068
      Check current status
      Found 6 terminally failed migrations
         ID           created                 block
       3126063        2022-02-23 20:41:37     /AlCaP0/Run2018D-v1/RAW#0200ccd7-9dd9-40c3-97ef-a3c8e522b32f
       3126064        2022-02-24 09:01:36     /MinBias_TuneCP5_14TeV-pythia8/Phase2HLTTDRWinter20GS-110X_mcRun4_realistic_v3-v1/GEN-SIM#c93e26df-0587-4f4c-b392-38a63b570549
       3126065        2022-02-24 09:01:37     /MinBias_TuneCP5_14TeV-pythia8/Phase2HLTTDRWinter20GS-110X_mcRun4_realistic_v3-v1/GEN-SIM#badc5989-8a2e-4d58-b664-04ab002cea20
       3126066        2022-02-24 09:01:37     /MinBias_TuneCP5_14TeV-pythia8/Phase2HLTTDRWinter20GS-110X_mcRun4_realistic_v3-v1/GEN-SIM#45a9dd8e-431c-49a6-a558-02c561cdae39
       3126067        2022-02-24 09:01:37     /MinBias_TuneCP5_14TeV-pythia8/Phase2HLTTDRWinter20GS-110X_mcRun4_realistic_v3-v1/GEN-SIM#b0cc5698-6891-45c2-a229-3bcae5831468
       3126068        2022-02-24 09:31:40     /MinBias_TuneCP5_14TeV-pythia8/Phase2HLTTDRWinter20GS-110X_mcRun4_realistic_v3-v1/GEN-SIM#05727681-bcc7-4606-a647-05a3a7742921
      [crab3@crab-prod-tw01 Publisher]$
      ```
* Cure
  + Failed migrations must be reported to DBS experts for investigation `(channel: [/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/dmwm/dbs2go/issues) )`
  + **\*NOTE FOR JULY 2022:\*** there is a known problem with DBS possibly due to mixing new reader and writer with old migration server. Anyhow currently failed migrations can not be fixed, So simply identify affected tasks and blacklist them. You should log into container, do `cd /data/srv/Publisher/logs/migrations` and look at the small script `BlackListTasks.sh` in there for guidance. Better to execute single lines manually with copy/paste and check what you are going to do before doing it.
  + If DBS expert says "go ahead and remove it" or simply we want/need to get rid of the backlog w/o waiting for the expert, we can remove the failed migration ourselves with
  + `/data/repos/CRABServer/scripts/Utils/RemoveFailedMigration.py --id 2987329` or whatever the correct id is
  + The command will check the migration Id, make sure that it is one which makes sense to remove and ask for confirmation before doing it. CRAB Publisher will create new publication requests as needed, but if we want to speed up things it can done now as well, the `RemoveFailedMigrations.py` command prints out instructions for that.
  + Example
    Show  Hide
    ```
    [crab3@crab-prod-tw01 Publisher]$   /data/repos/CRABServer/scripts/Utils/RemoveFailedMigration.py --id 3126063
    migrationId: 3126063 was created on 2022-02-23 20:41:37 by  for block:
     /AlCaP0/Run2018D-v1/RAW#0200ccd7-9dd9-40c3-97ef-a3c8e522b32f
    Do you want to remove it ? Yes/[No]: Y
    Removing it...
     successfully removed
    CRAB Publisher will issue such a migration request again as/when needed.
    But if you want to re-create it now, you can by answering yes here
    Do you want to re-create the migration request ? Yes/[No]: Y
    Submitting new migration request...
    new migration created: 3126069
    [{'migration_status': 0, 'create_by': '', 'migration_url': 'https://cmsweb-prod.cern.ch/dbs/prod/global/DBSReader', 'last_modified_by': '', 'creation_date': 1645785455, 'retry_count': None, 'migration_input': '/AlCaP0/Run2018D-v1/RAW#0200ccd7-9dd9-40c3-97ef-a3c8e522b32f', 'migration_request_id': 3126069, 'last_modification_date': 1645785455}]
    [crab3@crab-prod-tw01 Publisher]$
    ```
  + Python snippet for get status . You can simply execute this at the  prompt and then check more migrationId's or check the same after a delay with `back-arrow + Enter`
    Show  Hide
    ```
    import os
    from dbs.apis.dbsClient import DbsApi
    os.environ['X509_USER_CERT'] = '/data/certs/servicecert.pem'
    '] = '/data/certs/servicekey.pem'
    migUrl='https://cmsweb.cern.ch/dbs/prod/phys03/DBSMigrate'
    apiMig = DbsApi(url=migUrl)
    newId = 3126070 #migration_request_id
    status = apiMig.statusMigration(migration_rqst_id)
    #print(status)
    print(status[0]['migration_status'])
    # possible values of migration_status are:

# CRAB WEB SITE
Following <https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin/viewauth/CMS/CMSEOSWEBsites> there is now a directory on [EOS](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/EOS) where we can put files which are web accessible. There is no explicit quota, but we should limit use to a few GB.[https://cms-docs.web.cern.ch/CRAB/![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cms-docs.web.cern.ch/CRAB/) which shows things from `/eos/project/c/cmsweb/www/CRAB/`
* everybody in CMS can read
* everybody in cms-eos-web-CRAB e-group can write,
  + that e-group currently contains cms-service-crab-operators
details from mail exchange with :
```Ciao Andreas,
it seeems that it does not work yet:
belforte@lxplus766/~> cp /etc/hosts /eos/project/c/cmsweb/www/CRAB/testfile
cp: cannot create regular file ‘/eos/project/c/cmsweb/www/CRAB/testfile’: Operation not permittedor did I misunderstand how to use it ?
Should I write to someone else (too) to make your life easier ?
 08/09/2021 16:34, wrote:
> The space is now set up in:
>
> /eos/project/c/cmsweb/www/CRAB
>
> And two eGroups to mange it have been created:
>
> a) cms-eos-web-CRAB which contains the people who are allowed to write and delete in that directory/area and
> b) cms-eos-web-CRAB-mgt which is the management eGroup for the cms-eos-web-CRAB one.
>
> All members of CMS (via the cms-web-access eGroup) should be able to read from the [EOS](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/EOS) area.
>
> At present both eGroups have the following people/eGroups as member, anyone in this list can add other people to the writer/deleter group:
>
> cms-service-crab-operators
>
> It will still take a while to synchronise everything properly, so if you find issues in the next hour or so, please wait a bit and retry.
```-- - 2021-09-29

title: Introduction
body:
If you are experiencing TWiki instability from outside the CERN network, please connect via the CERN internal network - see [KB0010688![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cern.service-now.com/service-portal?id=KB0010688) for details
>![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/web-bg-small.gif) [CMSPublic Web](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WebHome)>[SWGuide](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuide)>[SWGuideCrab](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideCrab)>[CRABlogstash](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/CRABlogstash "Topic revision: 3 (2021-12-08 - 09:50:46)") (2021-12-08, )[![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/uweb-o14.gif) Edit](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/CRABlogstash?t=1777868574;nowysiwyg=1 "Edit this topic text")[Attach](/twiki/bin/attach/CMSPublic/CRABlogstash "Attach an image or document to this topic")[PDF](/twiki/bin/genpdf/CMSPublic/CRABlogstash "Create a PDF file for the topic")
## Introduction
For parsing CRAB Taskworker and Publisher logs we use filebeat and logstash. Filebeat runs directly in TW/PB container. Filebeat send logs to logstash from `logs/twlog.txt` for TW and from `logs/log.txt` and `/logs/processes/proc.c3id_master.pid*` for PB. Filebeat configuration file, specifying which logs should be parsed, via puppet is placed in each CRAB TW machine under `/data/container/filebeat.yaml` directory: [https://gitlab.cern.ch/ai/it-puppet-hostgroup-vocmsglidein/-/blob/master/code/manifests/profiles/crabtaskworker.pp#L335![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://gitlab.cern.ch/ai/it-puppet-hostgroup-vocmsglidein/-/blob/master/code/manifests/profiles/crabtaskworker.pp#L335) . At a container start time, this file is mounted into container and filebeat is started by docker using [https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/master/Docker/monitor.sh![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/master/Docker/monitor.sh) script.Filebeat sends all logs from specified to logstash. Once logs reaches logstash, [) `.conf` file is used to filter logs. One configuration file is used to parse both TW and PB logs. Logstash runs in CRAB k8s cluster.Below is provided how to to cluster to check logstash pod and how to deploy new `.conf` file for parsing logs.
Contents:
* [Introduction](#Introduction)
  + [to cluster](#Login_to_CRAB3_k8s_cluster)
  + [Deploy new logstash configuration (.conf file)](#Deploy_new_logstash_configuratio)
  + [Useful commands](#Useful_commands)
### to cluster
* to lxplus8
```
ssh lxplus8
```
* Set project name
```
export OS_PROJECT_NAME='CMS CRAB'
```
* Get k8 (do it only once)
```
mkdir -p cluster/crab
cd cluster/crab
openstack coe cluster  > env.sh
cd -
```
* Execute following script before running kubectl command
```
source cluster/crab/env.sh
```
* Check running pods
```
kubectl get pod -n crab-monitoring
```
* to the pod
```
kubectl exec -it -n crab-monitoring {POD_NAME} bash
```
### Deploy new logstash configuration (.conf file)
In case you have new version of logstash log parsing (.conf file) which you want to deploy, then follow below steps in order to deploy it:
1. delete service/deployments/configmap;
2. git clone and cd into directory where deployment files are placed
3. create new config map and start the pod;
```
#1. delete service/deployments/configmap
kubectl delete configmap  -n crab-monitoring
kubectl delete services  -n crab-monitoring
kubectl delete deployment  -n crab-monitoring
#2. git clone and cd into directory where deployment files are placed
git clone https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer.git
cd CRABServer/src/script/Monitor/logstash/deployment
#3. create new config map and start the pod
kubectl create configmap  --from-file crabtaskworker -n crab-monitoring
kubectl create -f logstash-nodeport.yaml
#check logs
kubectl logs -f pod/{POD_NAME} -n crab-monitoring
```
### Useful commands
* List all deployments
```
kubectl get deployments --all-namespaces
```
* Describe configmap
```
/logstash -n crab-monitoring
```
* Check pod logs
```
kubectl logs -f pod/{POD_NAME} -n crab-monitoring
```
* Delete deployment and service
```
kubectl delete services  -n crab-monitoring
kubectl delete deployment  -n crab-monitoring
```
* Describe pod
```
kubectl describe pod {POD_NAME} -n crab-monitoring
```
* Edit config map
```
kubectl edit configmap  -n crab-monitoring
```
--  - 2021-12-07

body:
If you are experiencing TWiki instability from outside the CERN network, please connect via the CERN internal network - see [KB0010688![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cern.service-now.com/service-portal?id=KB0010688) for details
>![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/web-bg-small.gif) [CMSPublic Web](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WebHome)>[SWGuide](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuide)>[SWGuideCrab](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideCrab)>[CompOpsCrab3NewMemberSetup](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/CompOpsCrab3NewMemberSetup "Topic revision: 19 (2022-03-16 - 14:42:08)") (2022-03-16, )[![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/uweb-o14.gif) Edit](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/CompOpsCrab3NewMemberSetup?t=1777869701;nowysiwyg=1 "Edit this topic text")[Attach](/twiki/bin/attach/CMSPublic/CompOpsCrab3NewMemberSetup "Attach an image or document to this topic")[PDF](/twiki/bin/genpdf/CMSPublic/CompOpsCrab3NewMemberSetup "Create a PDF file for the topic")
![CRAB Logo](http://cmsdoc.cern.ch/cms/ccs/wm/www/Crab/img/crab_logo_3.png)
# Team New Member Setup
This document is a checklist of things a new operator/developer should do in order to get started with . For the next steps you should already have a CERN  account in order to access all URLs, if don't have one or even if you don't know what is this, please go to the [Users Office![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://ph-dep-usersoffice.web.cern.ch/ph-dep-UsersOffice/) and finish your paperworks.
* [Team New Member Setup](#CRAB3_Team_New_Member_Setup)
  + [New Operator Checklist](#New_Operator_Checklist)
    - [Accounts etc.](#Accounts_etc)
      * [have a valid CERN computer account in `zh` group (CMS)](#have_a_valid_CERN_computer_accou)
      * [ certificate](#Grid_certificate)
      * [storage space for CRAB output](#storage_space_for_CRAB_output)
      * [ask CRIC administrator (Stephan or ) to give you CRAB Operator role there](#ask_CRIC_administrator_Stephan_o)
    - [Subscribe to HN](#Subscribe_to_HN)
    - [Elog](#Elog)
    - [e-groups](#e_groups)
    - [Access rights](#Access_rights)
    - [Communication Channels](#Communication_Channels)
    - [](#CMS_CRAB3_Monitoring_Links)
    - [Tutorials and other docs](#Tutorials_and_other_docs)
    - [Meetings](#Meetings)
## New Operator Checklist
### Accounts etc.
#### have a valid CERN computer account in `zh` group (CMS)
####  certificate
You need a  certificate to run all commands, if you already have great but if not, please go to [CERN Certification Authority![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://ca.cern.ch/ca/) and get one. As soon as you get you  certificate you will be able to create a  proxy, but for you should be able to issue voms proxy for that you need to become a member of CMS VO. Go to [https://lcg-voms2.cern.ch:8443/voms/cms/user/home.action![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://lcg-voms2.cern.ch:8443/voms/cms/user/home.action) and log in with your new  certificate after that request you membership at least for the group /cms.
#### storage space for CRAB output
You will need to run test CRAB tasks. CRAB tasks produce output which needs to be stored on some T2. As full time at CERN, you are entitiled to a storage space on , as the VOC for it
#### ask CRIC administrator (Stephan or ) to give you CRAB Operator role there
* to be specific, your CERN username should be a member of "CMS\_CRAB3\_Operator(none)"
### Subscribe to HN
Hypernews is a communication channel heavily used by CMS to discuss, announce issues and interventions, etc. For a operator is good to subscribe the following foruns on HN:
* [ tools![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://hypernews.cern.ch/HyperNews/CMS/get/-tools.html) feedback and/or to get support about
* [CRAB Development![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://hypernews.cern.ch/HyperNews/CMS/get/crabDevelopment.html) This forum is for discussions between the CRAB developers.
* [![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://hypernews.cern.ch/HyperNews/CMS/get/cmpAnnounce.html) This forum is used for announcements of the  Project
* [Analysis Operations![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://hypernews.cern.ch/HyperNews/CMS/get/analysisoperations.html) Analysis Operations is responsible for the operational aspects of CMS data analysis. As such it deals with data transfers & validation after transfer, CRAB server operations, group skim merging and uploads into global scope DBS.
* [![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://hypernews.cern.ch/HyperNews/CMS/get/comp-ops.html) The email gateway for this forum is:
* [CERN  Announcements![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://hypernews.cern.ch/HyperNews/CMS/get/cernCompAnnounce.html) announcements of changes, outages and other problems in the  at CERN.
* [ Announcements![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://hypernews.cern.ch/HyperNews/CMS/get/gridAnnounce.html) announcements related to the  infrastructure
* [Web Interface Discussions![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://hypernews.cern.ch/HyperNews/CMS/get/webInterfaces.html) This forum is for discussion of general web interface issues in the CMS offline  and software.
### Elog
Elog is an online log book used to report and keep track of the daily activities, for a operator is important to use ["Analysis Operations"![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cms-logbook.cern.ch/elog/Analysis%2BOperations/) and ["GlideInWMS"![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cms-logbook.cern.ch/elog/GlideInWMS/), when you post your activities on elog you have a chance to get help from other peoples and in the end you will have a full track of everything you did to solve an issue which could be very useful in the future.
### e-groups
go to [https://e-groups.cern.ch/e-groups/EgroupsSearchForm.do![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://e-groups.cern.ch/e-groups/EgroupsSearchForm.do) and subscribe the following e-groups:
| [e-group](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/CompOpsCrab3NewMemberSetup?sortcol=0;table=1;up=0#sorted_table "Sort by this column") | [Description](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/CompOpsCrab3NewMemberSetup?sortcol=1;table=1;up=0#sorted_table "Sort by this column") |
| --- | --- |
| cms-service-crab3htcondor-admins | Admins of the cms-service-crab3htcondor e-group |
| cms-service-glideinwms-admins | Group of the people allowed to manage GlideinWMS / Condor Puppet configuration for all CMS puppet managed nodes |
| cms-service-htcondor-admins | A list of admins for CompOps HTcondor nodes |
| cms-service-kibana | users of the CMS Kibana dashboards AFS area |
| cms-service-crab3htcondor-monitor | Monitor for the services |
| cms-service-webtools | operators and developers of CMSWEB applications like CRABServer and CRABCache |
| cms-service-crab3htcondor | Announcements from IT to -HTCondor Project |
| cms-comp-devs | CMS  Developers (no self subscription, you need to write an email to the ) |
| cms-service-crab-operators | CRAB operatros |
| cms-service-crab-sysadmins | Among other things, access to crab-\*-tw\* |
| cms-openstack-vocmscrab-admins | if you need to manage the CRAB VMs in openstack |
| ai-admins | if you need to manage the CRAB VMs in openstack |
| cmsweb-registry | if you need to push crabserver images to the cern registry |
| es-timber-cmsweb\_kibana | if you need to access ![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif), containing logs of crabserver REST |
You can join to these e-groups by yourself, but if need any help you can ask anyone around since e-groups are quite common.
e-groups serve a dual role in CERN  infrastructure, they are mailing lists, but also many tools allows to use e-groups to assign specific right to people, avoiding the need to individually list all users. You will find e-groups all over the places at CERN.
### Access rights
As an operator/developer you should connect to some machines to see logs, run commands, start/stop services and for do this you should have access to some set of machines like schedulers, HTCondor Collectors, ASO server and TaskManager. To get access to those machines, please a message with a minimum information about who are you, the name of you job position and finally why you need access to that machines to one or more of the following groups :
| [Machine set](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/CompOpsCrab3NewMemberSetup?sortcol=0;table=2;up=0#sorted_table "Sort by this column") | [a message to](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/CompOpsCrab3NewMemberSetup?sortcol=1;table=2;up=0#sorted_table "Sort by this column") |
| --- | --- |
| schedulers |  |
| HTCondor Collectors |  |
| ASO server |  |
| TaskManager |  |
After send the message for one of those e-groups you should wait until some off his members apply the configuration changes and until this changes take place which could take at most 1 hour.If you need to accces the docker engine in the virtual machines crab-\*-tw\*, then you need to ask someone to add you to the list of users in the docker group in those machines, by changing the puppet configuration at [puppet configuration in gitlab.cern.ch![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://gitlab.cern.ch/ai/it-puppet-hostgroup-vocmsglidein/-/blob/b69e5ee3bf2a2563ce8dfca7e1240b0a7fdb433f/code/manifests/node.pp#L22)If you need to execute tests or build/deploy images with dmwm-jenkins, then you need to ask to give you the proper permissions in [https://cmssdt.cern.ch/dmwm-jenkins/![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cmssdt.cern.ch/dmwm-jenkins/)If you need to build docker images, you can either your your private VM or use `cmsdocker01`. If you want to use the latter, you should ask to add your user to the docker group in that machine, otherwise you will not have access to it.If you need to deploy manually the [TaskWorker](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/TaskWorker?topicparent=CMSPublic.CompOpsCrab3NewMemberSetup;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") and the Publisher, you may need to push their docker image to registry.cern.ch. In order to do so, you need to be a member of the team [https://registry.cern.ch/harbor/projects/1891/members![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://registry.cern.ch/harbor/projects/1891/members) . Ask or to add you there.
### Communication Channels
* Slack: cms-submit-infra
* Mattermost: [https://mattermost.web.cern.ch/cms-o-and-c/channels/distributed-analysis![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://mattermost.web.cern.ch/cms-o-and-c/channels/distributed-analysis) (you may need to be invited to join cms-o-and-c )

See [https://monit-.cern.ch/d/000000530/cms-monitoring-project?orgId=11&fullscreen&panelId=20![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://monit-.cern.ch/d/000000530/cms-monitoring-project?orgId=11&fullscreen&panelId=20)Beware that at timed link may change due to the way manages dashboard saves and changes, whenever in doubt check the main index page [https://monit-.cern.ch/d/000000530/cms-monitoring-project?orgId=11![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://monit-.cern.ch/d/000000530/cms-monitoring-project?orgId=11)
* [Production CRAB Metrics![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://monit-.cern.ch/d/000000185/crab-metrics)
* [Schedd's instant load![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://monit-.cern.ch/d/byfWUEhZk/crab-schedds-instant-load)
* [ASO Metrics![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://monit-.cern.ch/d/JQG5D3mZz/crab-asometrics)
* [Overflow via JobRouter![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://monit-.cern.ch/d/DHXo_cuik/crab-overflow-via-jobrouter)
### Tutorials and other docs
* [Tutorial](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookCRAB3Tutorial) Follow this tutorial to get learn how configure a environment to submit jobs to the  and get used with its commands.
* [for Beginners](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideCrab#Documentation_for_beginner_users) all for beginners task flow, guide for , CRAB tutorial (advanced), CRAB commands, CRAB user functions, and tricks about CRAB, frequently asked questions, common errors.
* [Documentation for operators](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideCrab#Documentation_for_CRAB3_operator) Install instructions for backend, frontend and client software
### Meetings
See [https://indico.cern.ch/category/1366/overview?period=week][Indico]]
* [CentralOperation](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/CentralOperation?topicparent=CMSPublic.CompOpsCrab3NewMemberSetup;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") is part of Facilities meeting: Monday 4pm - attend whenever possible, but not mandatory
* General  meeting: Wednesday 3pm - attend whenever possible
* CRAB [DevOps](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/DevOps?topicparent=CMSPublic.CompOpsCrab3NewMemberSetup;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") Meeting: Thursday 3pm - This is absolutely mandatory. Notify in advance if you can't attend
* Submission Infrastructure meeting: Thursday 5pm - mandatory for the operator involved in schedd operations
-- - 2015-06-16

#  and local submission for site with a CE
* [ and local submission for site with a CE](#CRAB_and_local_submission_for_si)
  + [Introduction](#Introduction)
  + [Concept](#Concept)
  + [Implementation](#Implementation)
    - [At the Site](#At_the_Site)
      * [local group](#local_group)
      * [VOMS groups](#VOMS_groups)
    - [In the central submission infrastructure](#In_the_central_submission_infras)
## Introduction
This twiki is for site administrators who would like to give more priority and reserve some resources for their local users (thus the term local resources). It assumes that you have basic knowledge of the [GlideInWMS](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/GlideInWMS?topicparent=CMSPublic.CompOpsCustomizedGlideins;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") system used by  to access Grid resources (you know what a schedd, a frontend, a factory, and a pilot is). The original plan is outlined here <https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/CompOpsLocalSubmission#Site_customized_glideins_in_dept>It goes w/o saying that local control can only be enforced on over-the-pledge resources, while prioritization of resources pledged to CMS stays with central CMS coordination.
## Concept
Access to local resources in  can be done through the GlideInWMS Global Pool deployed at CERN (which is also used for regular pledged resources).In a nutshell, what normally happens is that "user jobs" are sent by  to one or more schedd with their `DESIRED_SITES` list; GlideInWMS frontend looks at these user jobs, and then tells the GlideInWMS factory to send "pilot jobs" to the sites; then matching between available pilots and user jobs is done, and the  job wrapper is downloaded for execution by the pilot. Normally, when pledged resources are requested, these pilots have VOMS FQAN `/cms/Role=pilot` (i.e. `pilot` role in the main `cms` group).In the case of "local users" there is the possibility to tell the the factory to send special pilots with `Role=pilot` in the `local` group (i.e. VOMS FQAN `/cms/local/Role=pilot`) which will be matched only to local users' jobs, giving site administrators the possibility to manage the priority of local users by setting an appropriate priority for the `/cms/local` pilots on their end.Each site indicates which user they consider "local" (i.e. can have access to local extra resources) using groups. One such group has the same name as the site and it is meant to allow sites to list single users as they see fit, but we envisions supporting also other kind of groups, starting with VOMS Groups and CERN e-groups.
## Implementation
Currently (March 2016) two ways to make this work are supported, they can both be used at same time by the site
1. using the local group
2. using one ore more VOMS groups
### At the Site
#### local group
This group will be named like the site (e.g. `T2_US_Nebraska` ) and is populated with CERN computing user IDs.
A site administrator will put the list of local users in `GlideinConfig/local-users.txt` file in SITECONF in CVMFS (see example [1] below). This file needs to be created in the site local configuration [/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://gitlab.cern.ch/groups/SITECONF). From there it will be automatically propagated to the worker nodes when CVMFS is updated. For sites not using CVMFS, they will still have to create this file in the git repository otherwise one of the SAM tests (org.cms.WN-basic) will start failing. In this case the site admin also has to manually make sure that the file is present on the worker nodes. Please contact the site support team at  for more details.The user name must be the same used in  tasks and stageout i.e. the username listed in SiteDB.  will look for this file to set a classAd (named "CMSGroups") in the job submission JDL which specifies the list of sites this user is "local" to. The frontend will then look at this list, and request the factory to send pilots using the `/cms/local/Role=pilot` credential to the particular site.[1]
```
> less /cvmfs/cms.cern.ch/SITECONF/T2_US_Nebraska/GlideinConfig/local-users.txt
bbockelm
jbalcas
mmascher
abean
alja
bloom
cfangmei
clundst
...
```
#### VOMS groups
A site administrator can also choose to define VOMS groups as local to the site, thus avoiding the need to list down individual names. Similar to the previous approach, a site administrator will put a list of VOMS group(s) in `GlideinConfig/local-groups.txt` file in SITECONF in CVMFS (see example [2] below). Note that the proper syntax to identify a VOMS group is `/cms/[/<name]`. When a user will submit a  task,  will look up all the groups associated with the user's certificate and add an extra classAd (named "CMSGroups") into the JDL (for example, see [3]). The frontend will then look at this CMSGroups classAd, and request the factory to send pilots using the `/cms/local/Role=pilot` credential to the particular site.[2]
```
# ls -al /cvmfs/cms.cern.ch/SITECONF/T2_US_Nebraska/GlideinConfig/
total 2
drwxr-xr-x. 2 cvmfs cvmfs   3 Nov 21 04:21 .
 cvmfs cvmfs   3 Apr 27  2015 ..
-rw-r--r--. 1 cvmfs cvmfs  21 Dec  7 20:21 --r--. 1 cvmfs cvmfs 304 May 11  2015 local-users.txt
# cat /cvmfs/cms.cern.ch/SITECONF/T2_US_Nebraska/GlideinConfig/local-groups.txt
HIG
/cms/integration
/cms/uscms
...
```
[3]
```
# voms-proxy-info -fqan
/cms/Role=NULL/Capability=NULL
/cms/ALARM/Role=NULL/Capability=NULL
/cms/TEAM/Role=NULL/Capability=NULL
/cms/dcms/Role=NULL/Capability=NULL
/cms/itcms/Role=NULL/Capability=NULL
 will add:
+CMSGroups='/cms,/cms/ALARM,/cms/TEAM,/cms/dcms,/cms/itcms'
```
### In the central submission infrastructure
 adds and populates a classAd named "CMSGroups" for the local user feature to work.  first looks up the various VOMS groups the user certificate belongs to, and adds them to CMSGroups. Note that VOMS proxies always list all the VOMS groups, differently from VOMS Roles where the user has to explicitely pick one. Next  looks up,using [CMSGroupMapper class![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/1b7e68eebac28f7c3ae1b853075fc89697f246d0/src/python/CMSGroupMapper.py), all the local-users.txt files provided by sites in CVMFS and if the user is "local" to any site, it also appends the CMS site name to the classAd. Basically the site name is treated like another group whose membership is defined via the local-user.txt file. If a user has some VOMS role associated with their certificate and are part of a local-users.txt file, the CMSGroups classAd for their jobs will, for example, look like this:
```
# condor_q cms1446 -af:h CMSGroups | uniq
CMSGroups
T2_ES_CIEMAT
/cms,/cms/escms,T2_ES_CIEMAT
```
If a user is not listed in any 'local-users.txt'  simply adds the VOMS group details. For example:
```
# condor_q cms488 -af:h CMSGroups | uniq
CMSGroups
/cms/uscms,/cms/becms,/cms/escms,/cms,/cms/integration
```
In the glideinWMS frontend, there is a separate frontend group named "local\_users" for sending local pilots configured with VOMS FQAN `/cms/local/Role=pilot`. In the match expression of the frontend group, glideinWMS makes use of ["CMSGroupMapper" class![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com//CMSglideinWMSValidation/blob/master/CMSGroupMapper.py) and compares 'CMSGroups' defined by  with what the site has in their CVMFS local files. If a match is found, frontend requests the glideinWMS factory to send "local" pilots to the site. The frontend adds an extra configuration parameter to these glideins ("CMSIsLocal") and sets its value to true.When a pilot starts running, it runs a list of validation scripts on a worker node. While running 'export\_site\_conf.py' ([link here![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com//CMSglideinWMSValidation/blob/master/export_siteconf_info.py)), the pilot checks if "CMSIsLocal" is set to true. Since this is being set for the "local" pilots, the script then reads local-groups.txt from the SITECONF area on the worker node and appends an extra requirement to the START expression of the startd. For example, in case of Nebraska:
```
stringListsIntersect(CMSGroups,"HIG,/cms/integration,/cms/uscms,T2_US_Nebraska")
```
This extra expression then prevents the pilot from being treated as a normal pilot and allows only the users with appropriate "CMSGroups" classAd to use it.

# Note on site-launched startd's
For a trusted resource, the site should create a pilot certificate from a CA recognized at CERN and send the DN to the Submission Infrastructure group () who will enter the certificate DN in the condor\_mapfile of the central manager, etc. In special circumstances, the Submission Infrastructure group can provide a CMS pilot certificate.
# Creating Pilot and Service Certificates
Every grid job, be it a glideinWMS pilot (glidein) or a user job, needs a grid proxy in order to authenticate at sites. A proxy is created on the frontend from a grid certificate and a key. This page describes how to obtain new pilot certificates from the [CERN Certificate Authority![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://ca.cern.ch/ca/aspx).
## Creating a New Certificate
On the [CERN Certificate Authority![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://ca.cern.ch/ca/) website, go to "New Grid Certificate" and choose "Request certificate using OpenSSL (for Linux machines)" [here![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://ca.cern.ch/ca//Request.aspx?template=ee2host). Create a certificate request with a subject, for example:
```
cmspilot01/vocms080.cern.ch
```
You need to be an owner of the machine at CERN in the certificate request name. You should use a certificate-friendly browser like if you want to not make your life difficult.You will next be asked to generate a certificate-key pair. You can do this on lxplus:
```
openssl req -new -subj "/CN=cmspilot01\/vocms080.cern.ch" -out newcsr.csr -nodes -sha512 -newkey rsa:2048
```
or follow the updated instructions on the CERN CA webpage if they have changed. Once the certificate is generated, download the base64 certificate to a file, which we will call **.cert**.Next we will export the certificate from this file to a **p12** file:
```
dir=cmspilot01
openssl pkcs12 -export -inkey privkey.pem -in .cert -out ${dir}.p12
```
Create cert file and key file from the p12 file and set permissions correctly:
```
openssl pkcs12 -clcerts -nokeys -in ${dir}.p12 -out ${dir}cert.pem
openssl pkcs12 -nocerts -in ${dir}.p12 -out ${dir}key-enc.pem
openssl rsa -in ${dir}key-enc.pem -out ${dir}key.pem
chmod 400 ${dir}key*
chmod 600 ${dir}cert.pem
```
Next verify the cert and key have the same hash:
```
openssl x509 -noout -modulus -in ${dir}cert.pem | openssl md5
openssl rsa -noout -modulus -in ${dir}key.pem |openssl md5 | uniq
```
This should always be the case unless you did something really incorrect like mix the files from two different certificates.
```
openssl x509 -in ${dir}cert.pem -noout -subject -startdate -enddate
```
## Register the Certificate with CMS
For service certificates (i.e. for the frontend), you can skip this step."Lasciate ogne speranza, voi " -In order to use CMS resources, every pilot certificate must be registered with the CMS VOMS group as a member of CMS, as well as get special roles like the **pilot** role. This distinguishes pilot jobs from other types of jobs like user jobs. Follow the procedure to "Add an additional certificate" on the [CMS VOMS administration website![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://lcg-voms2.cern.ch:8443/voms/cms/user/home.action) ( [direct link![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://lcg-voms2.cern.ch:8443/voms/cms/user/request-certificate.action) may work, if it does not, use the previous link and scroll down about a page to find the button on the right side) VOMS administrators are Stefano, and , if you need speedy approval. Note also that as of Summer 2015 the Global Pool certificate needs also the **production** role since fair-share at the Tier-1 sites depends on having it.
## Collector Authorization
As user condor, authorize the new certificate on the collectors:
```
glidecondor_addDN -daemon "cms pilot cert DN" "/DC=ch/DC=cern/OU=computers/CN=cmspilot12/vocms0167.cern.ch" pilot12
condor_reconfig
```
Each glidein needs to communicate with the collector, and cannot do so without authorization in the **condor\_mapfile**. Never update the **condor\_mapfile** by hand! Use the script **glidecondor\_addDN**.
## Certificate Repository
There isn't one.
## Creating a Proxy
You should store the certificate and key files on the glideinWMS frontend. Next you will have to create proxies. The proxies are short-lived versions of the certificate information that can be used more safely on the grid. In the Global Pool, these are found in **:/home/gfrontend/.globus**, and the certificate and key files in the **certs** directory below that. The fundamental procedure boils down to:Create the base proxy:
```
certdir=/home/gfrontend/.globus/certs
idstr=01
voms-proxy-init -cert ${certdir}/cmspilot${idstr}cert.pem -key ${certdir}/cmspilot${idstr}key.pem -hours 72
```
Add the appropriate VOMS roles to the base proxy, for example.
```
export X509_USER_PROXY=${here}/x509_pilot${idstr}_cms.proxy.tmp
voms-proxy-init -cert ${certdir}/cmspilot${idstr}cert.pem -key ${certdir}/cmspilot${idstr}key.pem -voms cms -hours 72 -valid 72:0
```
See the script **renew\_proxies.sh** for the full details. This script is run as a cron job. The resulting proxy files can be used in the glideinWMS frontend configuration xml file.

# Script to simplify certificate creation (July 2016, last rev. March 2020) for all certificates at once.
```
#!/bin/sh
# 24-Mar-2020 Some urls changed since last year
TOP=`pwd`
=`basename $TOP`
if [ $ == "vocms080" ] ; then
  DIRS="cmspilot01 cmspilot02 cmspilot03 cmspilot04 cmspilot05 frontend01 frontend02 frontend03 frontend04 frontend05"
elif [ $ == "vocms052" ] ; then
  DIRS="tw"
else
  exit 1
fi
for dir in $DIRS ; do
  if [ ! -d $TOP/$dir ] ; then
    mkdir $TOP/$dir
  fi
  cd $TOP/$dir
  if [ ! -f .cert ] ; then
    cp /etc/pki/tls/openssl.cnf .
cat >>openssl.cnf <<END
[req]
req_extensions = v3_req
[ v3_req ]
basicConstraints = CA:FALSE
keyUsage = nonRepudiation, digitalSignature, keyEncipherment
subjectAltName = @alt_names
[alt_names]
END
    echo "DNS.1 = ${}.cern.ch" >> openssl.cnf
    openssl req -new -subj "/CN=${dir}\/${}.cern.ch" \
      -out newcsr.csr -nodes -sha512 -newkey rsa:2048 \
      -config ${TOP}/${dir}/openssl.cnf
    echo
    echo "Go to the following url and request the certificate with the"
    echo "information in newcsr.csr for certificate $:"
    #echo "https://ca.cern.ch/ca//HostSelection.aspx?template=EE2Host&instructions=openssl"
    echo "https://ca.cern.ch/ca//Submit.aspx?template=ee2host&instructions=openssl&subject=${dir}%2f${}.cern.ch"
    echo "Download the base-64 certificate and then copy .cert from"
    echo "your desktop to this area:"
    pwd
  else
    echo
    echo "*** Enter when prompted:"
    echo
    openssl pkcs12 -export -inkey privkey.pem -in .cert -out ${dir}.p12
    openssl pkcs12 -clcerts -nokeys -in ${dir}.p12 -out ${dir}cert.pem
    openssl pkcs12 -nocerts -in ${dir}.p12 -out ${dir}key-enc.pem
    openssl rsa -in ${dir}key-enc.pem -out ${dir}key.pem
    chmod 400 ${dir}key*
    chmod 600 ${dir}cert.pem
    openssl x509 -noout -modulus -in ${dir}cert.pem | openssl md5
    openssl rsa  -noout -modulus -in ${dir}key.pem | openssl md5 | uniq
  fi
done
exit 0
```

title: Glideinwms Deployment
body:
#  Glideinwms Deployment

-   Glideinwms Deployment

-   glideinWMS components
-   Requirements for the machines

-   Directory Structure
-   Software:
-   Users and local accounts used on the machines to deploy, run and operate the service
-   Directory structure(old)
-   Deployment instructions

-   Current list of all GlideinWMS Machines

##  glideinWMS components

 A glideinWMS system is composed of 4 components:

-  A central manager/"Collector" (running the user pool collector and negotiator)
-  A submit node/"Schedd" (running the schedd)
-  A glidein factory, and
-  A VO fronted
 There can be any number of each component in the system (but at least one of each), and they several could be co-located on the same physical host. For the purpose of this document, however, we will assume we have one of each, and that each is located on a dedicated node.
 For a high level description see the glideinWMS training at CERN and/or the glideinWMS Web area.

##  Requirements for the machines

  |  Action Item/Service   |  Comments

  |  Central manager/"Collector" (vocms97, vocms097 (global prod), vocms099 (global analysis), vocms159 (itb), vocms165 (hlt) ]

  |  Open the port range from 9620/tcp to 10319/tcp   |  Collector/Negotiator machine, the Collector(s) must be accessible from the WAN, assuming 1+number_of_collectors collectors, i.e. 700 in production currently (Feb 2014)

  |  Open ports 51450/tcp and 41450/tcp   |  Ports used by HA (high availability, 51450) and Replication (41450) daemons

  |  Local OS   |  ulimit -n 16384

  |    |  Local firewall must be shut down

  |    |  ulimit -a; see "virtual memory", should be set to "unlimited" (was 768000 which prevents us run more than 8k)

  |  Software   |  HTCondor

  |  Confirgation files   |  Available up-to-date from:

  |  Local users/accounts   |  _gfrontend:x:100002:100000:GlideIn Front-End:/home/gfrontend:/bin/bash
_condor:x:100003:100000:Condor Pool:/home/condor:/bin/bash
_gfactory:x:100001:100000:GlideIn Factory:/home/gfactory:/bin/bash

  |  Submit node/"Schedd" (vocms[201,202,216,234,235,237,etc, see List of Machines] )

  |  Open the port 4080   |  Condor schedd, the shared port daemon must be accessible from the WAN, see additional settings for config_config on the user schedd side

  |  gridFTP for WMAgent   |  WMAgent runs gridFTP as root on vocms144, we need gridFTP on WMAgent+schedd machine. (Old: Use custom quattor template for this machine.)

  |  Local OS   |  ulimit -n 16384

  |  Software   |  HTCondor, WMAgent

  |  Configuration files   |
Available up-to-date from:

  |  Local users   |
cmst1 login

  |  VO Frontend [ vocms157 (main prod), vocms0157 (global prod), vocms0167 (global analysis), vocms143 (itb) ]

  |  Web server   |  Needs a port open accessible from WAN (both in the CERN firewall and in the local firewall)

  |    |  sudo cat /selinux/enforce # should be 0

  |    |  sudo echo 0 >/selinux/enforce

  |  Generate service certificate   |  service cert for the glideins:

  |    |  subject= /DC=ch/DC=cern/OU=computers/CN=cmspilotjob/vocms{157,0157,0167,143}.cern.ch

  |  Register service cert in the voms /cms/Role=pilot   |  Currently voms role is "production" -- new global pool machines will use role "pilot"

  |    |  need a voms proxy extension: voms-proxy-init --voms cms:/cms/Role=pilot

  |  Software   |  GlideinWMS Frontend, Apache web server

  |  Local users/accounts   |  _gfrontend:x:100002:100000:GlideIn Front-End:/home/gfrontend:/bin/bash
_condor:x:100003:100000:Condor Pool:/home/condor:/bin/bash
_gfactory:x:100001:100000:GlideIn Factory:/home/gfactory:/bin/bash

  |  Glidein Factory [ vocms32 and vocms158 (itb) ]

  |  Web server   |  Needs http port open and as well a port range open accessible from WAN (both in the CERN firewall and in the local firewall). Burt recommends going to at least 1k for safety, i.e. LOWPORT=20000, HIGHPORT=24999 in the condor_config.local

  |    |  sudo cat /selinux/enforce # should be 0

  |    |  sudo echo 0 >/selinux/enforce

  |  Open the port for Globus   |  Needs a range of ports opened for Globus callbacks, TCP/UDP 20000-25000 (both in the CERN firewall and in the local firewall)

  |  Open port for external frontends   |  Open port 9618 in central and local firewall

  |  Software   |  GlideinWMS Factory, HTCondor, javascriptrrd, Apache web server
Reference page here.

  |  Local users/accounts   |
Condor and factory login, plus one account for each frontend that this factory will be communicating with (_fecms{cern,fnal,ucsd})
In the future, there will only be one frontend, possibly _fecmsglobal

 _gfrontend:x:XX:100000:GlideIn Front-End:/home/gfrontend:/bin/bash
_fecmsucsd:x:XX:100000:Front-End CMS UCSD:/data/empty:/sbin/nologin
_fecmsfnal:x:XX:100000:Front-End CMS FNAL:/data/empty:/sbin/nologin
_fecmscern:x:XX:100000:Front-End CMS CERN:/data/empty:/sbin/nologin
_fecmsglobal:x:XX:100000:Front-End CMS GLOBAL:/data/empty:/sbin/nologin
_condor:x:100003:100000:Condor Pool:/home/condor:/bin/bash
_gfactory:x:XX:100000:GlideIn Factory:/home/gfactory:/bin/bash

  |  Common for all hosts

  |  Clean installation of the machines   |  Parrot configuration

  |  Sudo on all hosts for amccrea, klarson1, sfiligoi, bbockelm, jletts, zvada, belforte, dmason   |

  |  Generate host/key certificates   |  available at: /etc/grid-security/

  |  UI software with grid commands   |  source /afs/cern.ch/cms/LCG/LCG-2/UI/cms_ui_env.sh

  |    |  or install it locally (some recent version of two packages: voms-clients; globus-proxy-utils)

  |  Grid certificates   |  should come from quattor, /etc/grid-security/certificates/

  |  Local service accounts**   |  _condor:_gwms (preferred entry in /etc/passwd: _condor:_gwms:XX:Condor Pool:/home/condor:/bin/bash)

  |    |  _gfrontend:_gwms (preferred entry in /etc/passwd: _gfrontend:_gwms:XX:GlideIn Front-End:/home/gfrontend:/bin/bash)

  |    |  _gfactory:_gwms (preferred entry in /etc/passwd: _gfactory:_gwms:XX:GlideIn Factory:/home/gfactory:/bin/bash)

  |    |  _wmagent:_gwms (preferred entry in /etc/passwd: _wmagent:_gwms:XX:WMAgent:/home/wmagent:/bin/bash)

  |  System-wide file descriptors   |  everywhere where condor runs, so better on all machines, here is doc

 *We must be sure that this list is in quattor template, otherwise quattor tools will delete all software which was installed manually.

 **Remark: People operating Factory on respective machines must have added ssh-keys into these local accounts (ask service responsible person). Also, if needed, these people would have sudo privilege.

###  Directory Structure

-  /data

-  /data/certs - local copy of host certificates goes here (chmod 750), also auth files needed for WMAgent (which will not be used in long term) could go here.
-  /data/admin - directory to keep all the scripts and things needed for deployment, monitoring and operating
-  /data/admin/condor - condor tarballs
-  /data/admin/wmagent - for the WMAgent part (deployment scripts goes here and WMAgent.secret can go here)
-  /data/srv - all the software should be deployed here
-  /data/srv/condor - condor installation
-  /data/srv/wmagent - wmagent installation
-  /data/srv/factory - factory install
-  /data/srv/frontend - frontend install
-  /data/srv/vdt
-  /data/srv/sw - additional software or libraries needed, such as javascriptrrd for the factory and frontend

-  /etc

-  /etc/condor - condor config files (in config.d mode)

###  Software:

-  RPMs

-  RPM install instructions/repo locations for glideinWMS Factory and Frontend:

-  https://twiki.grid.iu.edu/bin/view/Documentation/Release3/InstallGlideinWMSFactory
-  https://twiki.grid.iu.edu/bin/view/Documentation/Release3/InstallGlideinWMSFrontend

-  Software

-  Condor: http://www.cs.wisc.edu/condor/downloads-v2/download.pl. Latest stable, Redhat 6 x86_64 stripped.
-  GlideinWMS: Homepage: http://www.uscms.org/SoftwareComputing/Grid/WMS/glideinWMS/doc.prd/download.html
-  javascriptrrd, for Factory and frontend machines only: Download from http://sourceforge.net/projects/javascriptrrd/

###  Users and local accounts used on the machines to deploy, run and operate the service

 Local accounts on the machines. Logging in works on ssh public keys.

-  VO Frontend machines (vocms143 and vocms157): _gfrontend:_gwms
-  GlideinWMS Factory machines (vocms107 and vocms158): Condor as root factory as _gfactory:_gwms
-  User Pool machines (vocms105, vocms159, vocms120, vocms164): _condor:_gwms
 cmst1 account is used on the Schedd machines. Login as yourself and then sudo to cmst1 accout.

###  Directory structure(old)

 We follow current directory structure to deploy and run the services.

###  Deployment instructions

 Need to deploy in this order:

-  [1] glideinWMS Schedds and Collector (root@factory_machine) Instrunctions
-  [2] Glidein Factory (_gfactory@factory_machine) Instrunctions
-  [4] User Pool Collector (_condor@central_collector_machine) Instrunctions
-  [5] User Schedd (_condor@user_submitter_machine) Instrunctions
-  [6] Condor for VO Frontend (_gfrontend@frontend_machine) Instrunctions
-  [7] VO Frontend (_gfrontend@frontend_machine) Instrunctions
-  [8] WMAgent (_condor@cubmitter_machine) Instrunctions

##  Current list of all GlideinWMS Machines

 -- Main.AlisonMcCrea - 12-Sep-2012

##  GlideinWMS/Condor Troubleshooting Guide

 or: Why aren't my jobs running?

 Under Construction as of August 2014!

-   GlideinWMS/Condor Troubleshooting Guide

-   The 8 Steps

-   1. Jobs are submitted.
-   2. The Collector sees the jobs.
-   3. The Frontend sees the jobs (and requests glideins).
-   4. The Factory recieves requests, and creates glideins.
-   5. The glideins start up at the Site.
-   6. The Collector sees the glideins.
-   7. The Negotiator matches glideins to jobs.
-   8. The Job starts running.

###  The 8 Steps

 The 8 steps that need to happen before a job can run.

 To see a list of glideinWMS/condor machines for the Condor pool you are using, see this twiki page: https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin/view/CMSPublic/CompOpsWMSDeploy

 To get a better idea of how the GlideinWMS system works, see the GlideinWMS Guide: https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin/view/CMSPublic/CompOpsGlideinWMSGuide

####  1. Jobs are submitted.

 On the schedd machine to which the jobs are submitted:

 > condor_q

 Are the jobs listed?

 YES: Proceed to step 2. NO:

 Tip: Try condor_q -bet (-better_analyze). This may show some immediate problems, such as a huge memory request, wrong site name, etc. But usually the problems are not that simple.

####  2. The Collector sees the jobs.

 If you are in a pool with HA collectors (meaning: 2 collectors), one of the collector machines will have the negotiator on it (only one of these per pool). Is is usually better to debug from this machine because you also have access to the Negotiator Logs.

 [collector machine] condor_status -schedd

 - Does the collector list the schedd?

 It should look like this:

 Can you see the condor queue of this machine from the collector? Like this:

 YES: good NO: the collector doesn't see the schedd - debug  (COLLECTOR DEBUGGING#NO SCHEDDS).

####  3. The Frontend sees the jobs (and requests glideins).

 On the frontend machine for your pool (there is only one FE per pool):

 Move to the istance directory, usually /home/gfrontend/frontstage/frontend--/

 Is the frontend running?

 [_gfrontend@vocms0167 frontend_CMSG-v1_0]$ ./frontend_startup status Running

 If not, start it: [_gfrontend@vocms0167 frontend_CMSG-v1_0]$ ./frontend_startup start.

 If it doesn't start, see this twiki page: FE_DEBUG#FENOTSTARTING

 If it is running, check the Frontend info and error logs (the job is usually in "main" group)

 [_gfrontend@vocms0167 frontend_CMSG-v1_0]$ less log/group_main/main.info.log

 - Is the log recent? Has it been filled recently? (within the last 10 minutes or so)

 YES: NO:

 (---ADVANCED:

 - Do the total numbers approximately match the pool?

 YES: NO: ---)

 - Grep for the entry/entries that you are trying to run at.

 Let's say I'm trying to run my jobs at FNAL.

 Here are the FNAL entries. The frontend sees 11 jobs that match FNAL (divided by the number of FNAL entries, so it sees 22 in total) - this is represented by Idle under "Jobs in schedd queues".

 We can also see that the frontend is requesting glideins at FNAL - under Request, it asks for 1 idle glidein to be sent to CMS_T1_US_FNAL_ce2@v3_0@<email>, which means it will ask the factory at SDSC to send one glidein to FNAL's ce2.

 Only one glidein seems like too small of a request, but the frontend is actually requesting 1 glidein from every FNAL entry to every factory, which I haven't shown in this log snippet.

 If we grep through one request cycle of the frontend, we see that there are actually 9 FNAL entries listed - FNAL has 3 CEs (ce, ce2 and ce4), and the global frontend has 3 factories working for it (the OSG-GOC factory, and the two CERN factories vocms0305 and vocms32) -- so 9 entries in all.

```
CMS_T1_US_FNAL_ce2@v3_0@<email>
```

```
CMS_T1_US_FNAL_ce4@v3_0@<email>
```

```
CMS_T1_US_FNAL_ce@v3_0@<email>

```

```
CMS_T1_US_FNAL_ce2@v1_0@<email>

```

```
CMS_T1_US_FNAL_ce4@v1_0@<email>

```

```
CMS_T1_US_FNAL_ce@v1_0@<email>

```

```
CMS_T1_US_FNAL_ce2@v1_3@<email>

```

```
CMS_T1_US_FNAL_ce4@v1_3@<email>

```

```
CMS_T1_US_FNAL_ce@v1_3@<email>

```

 The frontend requests 1 glidein per FNAL CE per Factory, so 9 glideins in total. This should easily cover the 10 jobs requesting FNAL (as glideins can be reused, and more glideins will be submitted next cycle, etc).

 So, checking your entries/sites in the frontend logs: Does the frontend see your Idle jobs, and request (any number of) glideins?

 YES: good, move on to (4). NO:

 Check the frontend error logs.

####  4. The Factory recieves requests, and creates glideins.

 This part can be a bit tricky - if your local factory operator is around, might want to ask them.

 Here's a way to quickly check if glideins are being created at the site you request:

####  5. The glideins start up at the Site.

 Again, this part is tricky, and may be outside of your duties. There are a lot of things that could go wrong that are up to the site to fix - problems with their batch system, network, etc.

####  6. The Collector sees the glideins.

 Once the glideins start running, the collector will start collecting them - just as it collects jobs. So it has two lists of jobs and resources (glideins).

####  7. The Negotiator matches glideins to jobs.

 This is the second part of glidein matchmaking.

####  8. The Job starts running.

 The job arrives at the glidein, and starts running.

title: Local Resource Provisioning
body:
If you are experiencing TWiki instability from outside the CERN network, please connect via the CERN internal network - see [KB0010688![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cern.service-now.com/service-portal?id=KB0010688) for details
>![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/web-bg-small.gif) [CMSPublic Web](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WebHome)>[CompOps](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/CompOps)>[CompOpsCentralServicesTeam](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/CompOpsCentralServicesTeam)>[CompOpsGlideinWMS](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/CompOpsGlideinWMS)>[CompOpsLocalSubmission](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/CompOpsLocalSubmission "Topic revision: 7 (2015-09-24 - 17:00:17)") (2015-09-24, )[![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/uweb-o14.gif) Edit](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/CompOpsLocalSubmission?t=1777866015;nowysiwyg=1 "Edit this topic text")[Attach](/twiki/bin/attach/CMSPublic/CompOpsLocalSubmission "Attach an image or document to this topic")[PDF](/twiki/bin/genpdf/CMSPublic/CompOpsLocalSubmission "Create a PDF file for the topic")
# Local Resource Provisioning
* [Use cases for local resource provisioning](#Use_cases_for_local_resource_pro)
* [Proposed Solutions](#Proposed_Solutions)
  + [Non-centrally-launched glideins in depth](#Non_centrally_launched_glideins)
  + [Site-customized glideins in depth](#Site_customized_glideins_in_dept)
    - [Technical details [deprecated]](#Technical_details_deprecated)
  + [News](#News)
# Use cases for local resource provisioning
* Resource-based fair-share and prioritization (see [HTCondor ticket![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://htcondor-wiki.cs.wisc.edu/index.cgi/tktview?tn=4639)). The current glideinWMS work-around using separate frontend groups does not scale, splits the pool with different types of pilots.
  + 95% share for production at Tier-1 sites
  + Higher priority on certain resources for national VOMS groups, local groups, physics groups etc.
* CRAB analysis on sites with no grid access, e.g.  on opportunistic sites
# Proposed Solutions
Proposed Solutions depend on whether CE is needed or not. For sites without a CE, there are only two possibilities, and the first one listed blow is very heavy. For sites with a CE, there are more options, with different costs. Solutions 1-4 come from [this presentation![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://indico.cern.ch/event/285674/session/21/contribution/95/material/slides/0.pdf).
1. Site replicates , submission infrastructure (no CE)
   * Large overhead for the site
2. Site runs local schedd which points to production (CE)
   * Partitions the pool. [Choose glideinWMS pool![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/4565) and/or schedd at submission time.
3. Site-customized glideins (CE)
   * glidein-based solution, only match to prefered users
4. non-centrally-launched glideins (no CE)
   * 's favored solution.
   * Not specific to .
   * Resources provisioned manually or by a script.
   * Jobs submitted by users (which can only run their own jobs) or by the site (with Role=pilot, but a whitelist of allowed users).
5. HTCondor [resource-based fair-share![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://htcondor-wiki.cs.wisc.edu/index.cgi/tktview?tn=4639) (CE)
   * Moves problem from glidienWMS to HTCondor
   * Will it scale?
6. Get glideinWMS frontend groups to scale better? (CE)
7. Sites change their policies and allow grid submissions or deploy a grid CE (no CE)
## Non-centrally-launched glideins in depth
There are a few required pieces here:
* Script to launch a pilot available in CVMFS. Provide a script that can launch a CMS pilot given only a valid proxy. The rest of the information is taken from CVMFS, site-local-config.xml, a site-specific override in SITECONF, and (optionally) a user-specified config file.
  + A prototype of this already exists. However, in order to bootstrap the glidein, we need to know the name of the latest gWMS config file and SHA1 signatures and update these as necessary in CVMFS. These can be taken from a job in queue - i.e., I can write a script that we could execute as a cron on the central CVMFS repo host that would work 80% of the time. We'd want to ask the glideinWMS team to make these centrally available so we can reliably update CVMFS nightly.
* Script to indicate "load".
* "APF-lite" - script that will run in the local HTCondor schedd and submit pilots. This is for sites that have Role=pilot (LPC use case). Note: still some interesting security / scheduling challenges to overcome before this is reality.
## Site-customized glideins in depth
This option allows a site to specify a list of local users; CMS will send an identifiable pilot (special DN and/or VOMS role) and guarantee only the specified users will be able to run jobs on that pilot.The implementation will reuse the existing factory entries and will require only one new group in the frontend (regardless of the number of participating sites).
### Technical details [deprecated]
The "site customized glideins" solution is in production for since September 2015 and here there are the actual details: <https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/CompOpsCustomizedGlideins>The real implementation is currently a simplified version of what explained below which is kept for reference.
1. Setup a new group, “group\_local”. Associate this with a specific DN (could perhaps be Role=uscms or simply we have a special DN).
2. Maintain a new file, /etc/gwms-frontend/group\_mapping. This is line-oriented, two columns. The first column is a group name; the second column is the corresponding site name.
   * The idea is a line like “Nebraska T2\_US\_Nebraska” means jobs in group “Nebraska” are allowed to use the local DN at site T2\_US\_Nebraska.
   * This file will get shipped with the glidein, meaning we need to remember to do a reconfig post-update.
   * This is a N:M mapping. If we define a "uscms-higgs" group, we may want to map it to both UCSD and Nebraska.
3. We map user's jobs to appropriate groups.
   * Once available in 8.3.4 / 8.3.5, we would use the submit features to enforce this. Until then, we can use the job router.
   * The user->group mappings could be periodically populated from sub-files in /cvmfs/cms.cern.ch/SITECONF/$SITENAME//local-users.txt. This allows sites to fully control the list of their local users.
   * We will provide further mechanisms (perhaps e-groups, allowing us to put "" into the "higgs" group) in the future.
4. In the match\_expr for group\_local, we invoke a python function with two arguments: job[“GroupName”] and glidein["attrs"]["GLIDEIN\_CMSSite"] ("GroupName" will need to be added to the job match\_attrs). This python function will have the mappings in group\_mapping cached in memory and return true if the group is mapped to the site.
   * We drop this function into a separate module and reference it from the match\_expr like \_\_import\_\_("modulefoo").match\_group(job[“GroupName”], glidein["attrs"]["GLIDEIN\_CMSSite"]).
5. We add a new validation script which adds a config variable of the form: START = ( $(START) ) && ([GroupName](/twiki/bin/edit/TARGET/GroupName?topicparent=CMSPublic.CompOpsLocalSubmission;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.")=?="group1" || [GroupName](/twiki/bin/edit/TARGET/GroupName?topicparent=CMSPublic.CompOpsLocalSubmission;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.")=?="group2" ...) for the local GLIDEIN\_CMSSite.
6. We ask sites to prioritize the specific DN appropriately and to assume it only contains local users.
   * However, we say that we control the fairshare and group quotas. Caltech doesn't manage the fairshare of [CaltechUserA](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/CaltechUserA?topicparent=CMSPublic.CompOpsLocalSubmission;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") versus [CaltechUserB](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/CaltechUserB?topicparent=CMSPublic.CompOpsLocalSubmission;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.").

An update on this is in this thread [https://hypernews.cern.ch/HyperNews/CMS/get/comp-ops/2031/1/1.html![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://hypernews.cern.ch/HyperNews/CMS/get/comp-ops/2031/1/1.html)-- - 2014-11-14

# Deployment Notes
can be deployed by anyone. This page documents the known deploys by the development team and the CMS computing integration team.
* [Deployment Notes](#CRAB3_Deployment_Notes)
  + - [Known Backends](#Known_CRAB3_Backends)
    - [Access to (pre) production machines](#Access_to_pre_production_machine)
  + [TaskWorkers](#TaskWorkers)
  + [AsyncStageOut](#AsyncStageOut)
    - [Validated HTCondor schedds](#Validated_HTCondor_schedds)
  + [Other Useful Links](#Other_Useful_Links)
###
* **cmsweb.cern.ch: Users should use this frontend**
This is operated and deployed by the HTTP group. This frontend deploys only RPMs from tagged releases, and can only be updated once a month.
* **cmsweb-testbed.cern.ch: Testers should use this frontend**
This is operated and deployed by the HTTP group; help requests should go to cms-service-webtools. This frontend deploys only RPMs from tagged releases, and can only be updated about once a week.
### Known Backends
### Access to (pre) production machines
Access to centrally maintained servers (i.e. other than personal VM's) is regulated via puppet.Here [1] is the puppet config for the machines in production. So basically for the access the membership in these e-groups should be enough. If it does not work for some machine it means that the access to the machine is not configured by-egroup (which is the case for vocms059)
```
[1]
sudo:
   egroups:
     - cms-service-crab3htcondor-admins
sssd::interactiveallowgroups:
   - cms-service-crab
   - cms-service-crab2
   - cms-service-glideinwms
   - cms-service-crab3htcondor
   - cms-voc
```

This wiki pages provides information on CRAB CI/CD setup. Instructions that are provided in this web page are mostly tailored to for managing CRAB .
# CRAB CI/CD flow
CRAB CI/CD flow is made of 4 groups of :
* BUILD - this group of  is triggered manually by creating new release in `CRABServer` GH repository;
* STATICCHECK - This group of  is triggered automatically at every new commit in every PR on dmwm/CRABServer and dmwm/CRABClient. It can calso be triggered manually.
* DEPLOY - this group of job can be either triggered manually or it can also be triggered by `TEST` job which requires to deploy new `crabserber` or `taskworker/publisher` image;
* TEST - this group of job currently is triggered manually and executes tests on CRAB (crabclient, taskworker, publisher, crabserver) code
![CRAB CI/CD flow](/twiki/pub/CMSPublic/Crab3CI/Screenshot_2021-05-05_at_08.22.02.png)</verbatim>
```
STATICCHECK
+------------------------------+ +------------------------------+
|  commit on dmwm/CRABClient   | |  commit on dmwm/CRABServer   |
+------------------------------+ +------------------------------+
  |                                |
  | automatic                      | automatic
  v                                v
+------------------------------+ +------------------------------+
|   DMWM-CRABClient-PR-test    | |   DMWM-CRABServer-PR-test    |
+------------------------------+ +------------------------------+
  |                                |
  |                                |
  v                                |
+------------------------------+   |
| DMWM-CRABServer-PR-pylintpy3 | <-/
+------------------------------+
```
Link and of each job is provided below.
#
#### CRABServer\_BuildOnRelease
[https://cmssdt.cern.ch/dmwm-/job/CRABServer\_BuildOnRelease/![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cmssdt.cern.ch/dmwm-/job/CRABServer_BuildOnRelease/)**:** new release in `CRABServer` GH repo. This job can also be triggered manually**:** Job is triggered by a new release in the `CRABServer` GH repository. Job is responsible for building `RPMs` and storing them in `comp.crab_${BRANCH}` repository where variable `${BRANCH}` represents branch name which was used to create a new release. If `RPM` build and upload succeed, `CRABServer_BuildImage` job is triggered.**Parameters:**
* `RELEASE_TAG`: GH release tag that should be used for building a new image. Value of this parameter should match existing tag in `CRABServer` GH repo.
**:** In case this job fails, investigate failure reason:
* It can fail due to lack of available space in the machine where the job ran. In that case try to run a job on a different machine by manually adjusting job configuration and manually forcing the job to run on a different machine. Parameter to be adjusted - Label Expression. E.g. normally this parameter is always set to `cms-dmwm-cc7`, but you can force a job on a specific machine by changing this value to `cms-dmwm-cc7-XY` where `XY` represents a specific machine number. In general, it is suggested to leave this value by default set to `cms-dmwm-cc7` because that gives a bigger pool of machines to execute your job.
* Job can fail because at the same time when it runs there is another build process running that is trying to build the same HG tag as you. In that case wait some time and retry your job.
**Emails:**
 sends an email to  with the result.
#### CRABServer\_BuildImage
[https://cmssdt.cern.ch/dmwm-/job/CRABServer\_BuildImage/![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cmssdt.cern.ch/dmwm-/job/CRABServer_BuildImage/)**:** CRABServer\_BuildOnRelease job**:** Job is triggered by `CRABServer_BuildOnRelease`. Purpose of the job is to build `crabserver` and `crabtaskworker` images. Those images are pushed to `cmssw/crabtaskworker` and `cmssw/crabserver`  repositories.**Parameters:** n/a**:** Usually if `RPMs` build and upload succeed, this job works as well. So do not happen often. In case it failed, investigate the reason and act accordingly. You can either retry the last failed job or the entire flow starting from the upstream `CRABServer_BuildOnRelease` job (if there is a need for retrying upstream job, what is rarely a case).**Emails:**
 does not send an email. However, this job success/failure is part of `CRABServer_BuildOnRelease` job result and email.
#### CRABServer\_Deploy\_Server
[https://cmssdt.cern.ch/dmwm-/job/CRABServer\_Deploy\_Server/![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cmssdt.cern.ch/dmwm-/job/CRABServer_Deploy_Server/)**:** manually or from the upstream project `CRABServer_SetupTests`**:** Job is used to deploy `crabserver` to a given `` cluster. Be aware that only `crabserver` images where docker image tag is the same as GH release tag can be used in combination with imagebot (which is used by this job) to deploy `crabserver` images. For instance, if you created a GH release called `v3.123456` and then manually created docker image `v3.123456.v1`, imagebot cannot be used to deploy this image. That being said, this job cannot be used :**
* `CRABServer_image`: `CRABServer` image should be deployed. Only tag that should be deployed, e.g. `v3.210212`, should be entered;
* `REST_Instance`: `REST` Instance should be used for new image deployment;
**:** in case this job failed, investigate the reason in the log file and check manually if `crabserver` is running in the given `` cluster.**Emails:**
If triggered manually,  send an email to  with the result. If job was triggered by the upstream project, this job failure/success is reported by the upstream job.
#### CRABServer\_Deploy\_TW
[https://cmssdt.cern.ch/dmwm-/job/CRABServer\_Deploy\_TW/![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cmssdt.cern.ch/dmwm-/job/CRABServer_Deploy_TW/)**:** manually or from the upstream project `CRABServer_SetupTests`**:** Job is used to deploy `TaskWorker` or `Publisher` to one of CRAB machine: `crab-dev-tw01, crab-preprod-tw01, crab-prerpod-tw02`**Parameters:**
* `Service`: which service should be deployed: `TaskWorker, Publisher_rucio, Publisher_schedd`;
* `Image`: which image should be deployed. Enter only tag that should be deployed, e.g. `v3.210212`;
* `Environment`: which CRAB machine should be used for new image deployment.
**:** in case this job failed, investigate the reason in the log file and check manually if [/bin/edit/CMSPublic/TaskWorker?topicparent=CMSPublic. "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") / Publisher is running in given CRAB machine.**Emails:**
If triggered manually,  send an email to  with the result. If job was triggered by the upstream project, this job failure/success is reported by the upstream job.
#### CRABServer\_ExecuteTests
[https://cmssdt.cern.ch/dmwm-/job/CRABServer\_ExecuteTests/![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cmssdt.cern.ch/dmwm-/job/CRABServer_ExecuteTests/)**:** manually**:** job submits CRAB tasks available at [https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/tree/master/test/tasks![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/tree/master/test/tasks) . List of submitted task names is shared via email and can be used for manual status tracking. In case at least one task submission failed, overall job is immediately marked as failed. If all task submission went well, job `CRABServer_CheckTestResults` is triggered that will start running `X` minutes later that will check submitted task status and report it up to `Y` times in `Z` minutes intervals. XYZ are configured in `CRABServer_CheckTestResults` job.**Parameters:**
* `CRABClient_version`: `CRABClient` version used to run test suite;
* `CMSSW_release`: `CMSSW` release which should be used for task submissions
* `DBS_tag`: If you are running `CRABClient` from GH (i.e. `CRABClient_version` set to 'GH'), please enter which `DBS` tag should be use. Otherwise this parameter is not used
* `WMCore_tag`: If you are running `CRABClient` from GH (i.e. `CRABClient_version` set to 'GH'), please enter which `WMCore` tag should be use. Otherwise this parameter is not used
* `REST_Instance`: `REST` instance used for submission;
* `CMSSW_release`: `CMSSW_release` should be used for running CRABCLient commands.
**:** in case job failed, investigate manually. Job can fail because of 2 groups of problems: a) infrastructure problem, in that case retry failed job; b) some task submission failed. In that case investage why it failed and act upon**Emails:**
 sends an email to  with the result.
#### CRABServer\_CheckTestResults
[https://cmssdt.cern.ch/dmwm-/job/CRABServer\_CheckTestResults/![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cmssdt.cern.ch/dmwm-/job/CRABServer_CheckTestResults/)**:** from the upstream project `CRABServer_ExecuteTests`**:** Job is executed maximum `X` times in `Y` min intervals to check if task submitted by the upstream job (`CRABServer_ExecuteTests`) finished running. In case part of the  completed successfully while others are still running, then this job is marked as `FAILED` (even though there are not errors/mistakes in the code as such) and status checking on same list of tasks is executed again `Y` minutes later. Be aware, in case this job failed for some other reason (e.g. `GH` is down and job cannot clone needed directories), then job is not retried - investigate manually and start tests again.**Parameters:**
This job is using parameters set in the upstream job `CRABServer_ExecuteTests`, meaning, that if you set `CRABClient_version` to `GH` in the `CRABServer_ExecuteTests`, then this job will use the same `CRABClient` version.**:** in case job failed, investigate manually. Job can fail because of 2 groups of problems: a) infrastructure problem, in that case retry failed job; b) at the time of test execution, some  are still running. In that case job is marked as failed and retried `Y` minutes later. Nothing to do in this case.**Emails:**
 sends an email to  with the result.--  - 2021-04-12
