## Introduction
All successful jobs in a task produce output which are eventually copied (staged-out) into the CMS namespace in a sites permanent storage element specified in the `Site.storageSite` parameter of the CRAB configuration file. The jobs also produce out/err log from the job running code, which are by default not copied to the permanent storage. The user can force the stage-out of the log to the permanent storage by setting `General.transferLogs = True` in the CRAB configuration file. The user can also disable the stage-out of the output by means of the `General.transferOutputs` parameter, but in that case publication will not be possible. If the output are successfully transferred to the permanent storage, CRAB will automatically (and by default) publish the output dataset in DBS. This is done by the same service (ASO) which does the stage-out. If the user wants to disable the publication, he/she can set `Data.publication = False` in the CRAB configuration file. The only output that CRAB can publish are those of EDM format; other output can be transferred, but will not be published even if `Data.publication` was enabled.
## Logical File Names of output (and log)
All successful (and sometimes also not-successful) jobs produce output (and log) which eventually are copied into the CMS namespace in a user-specified final location. The LFN of these are of the following form:`/store/[user|group|local]/<dir>[/<subdirs>]/<primary-dataset>/<publication-name>/<time-stamp>/<counter>[/log]/<file-name>`For example: `/store/user/atanasi/GenericTTbar/CRAB3_tutorial_MC_analysis_1/140503_173849/0000/output_1.root`.The `log` subdirectory is used for the jobs stdout and stderr log . Each jobs stdout and stderr log are zipped into an archive file together with a framework job report file.Before the are transferred to the permanent storage, a "local" stage-out into a temporary storage in the running site (or another configured site) is performed. The naming of the temporary is the same, except one has to change `/store/[group|local|user/<username>]` by `/store/temp/user/<username>.<DN-hash>` (here, `<DN-hash>` is the SHA-1 hash of the user's DN used to ease the transition for users to new DNs). If the don't have to be transferred, they are discarded and not even copied into the temporary storage.The three LFNs detailed above can be summarized in the following general form:`<lfn-prefix>/<primary-dataset>/<publication-name>/<time-stamp>/<counter>[/log]/<file-name>`The table below provides an explanation of each of the fields appearing in this generic LFN form.
| [Field](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/Crab3DataHandling?sortcol=0;table=2;up=0#sorted_table "Sort by this column") | [Description](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/Crab3DataHandling?sortcol=1;table=2;up=0#sorted_table "Sort by this column") |
| --- | --- |
| `dir` | A directory. For `/store/user/`, by default CRAB will use the CERN primary account username of the user who submitted the task. |
| `subdirs` | A series of (optional) subdirectories. |
| `lfn-prefix` | The first part of the LFN as specified by the user in the `Data.outLFN` parameter in the CRAB configuration file. |
| `primary-dataset` | The primary dataset name as specified in the `Data.outputPrimaryDataset` parameter in the CRAB configuration file (when running over private users input or running MC generation) or as extracted from the `Data.inputDataset` parameter (when running an analysis over an input dataset). For example, the primary dataset name of `/GenericTTbar/HC-CMSSW_5_3_1_START53_V5-v1/GEN-SIM-RECO` is `GenericTTbar`. |
| `publication-name` | The user-specified portion of the publication name of the dataset as specified in the  parameter in the CRAB configuration file. Defaults to `crab_<General.requestName>`. This name is used even if `Data.publication = False`. |
| `time-stamp` | A timestamp, based on when the task was submitted. A task submitted at 17:38:49 on 27 April 2014 would result in a timestamp of `140427_173849`. The timestamp is used to prevent multiple otherwise-identical user tasks from overwriting each others' . |
| `counter` | A four-digit counter, used to prevent more than 1000 residing in the same directory. are kept in directory `0000`; 1000-1999 are kept in directory `0001`; 2000-2999 in directory `0002`; etc. |
| `file-name` | For output , this is the file name specified in the user's CMSSW parameter-set configuration file (or the name of an additional output file specified in the `JobType.outputFiles` CRAB configuration parameter), with the job counter added in. If the parameter-set specifies an output file named `output.root`, the output file name from job N will be `output_N.root`. For log , this is `cmsRun_<ID>.log.tar.gz`, where `<ID>` is the ID of the job within the task. |
## Input Data
The following configuration parameters control the input data behavior:
| [Parameter Name](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/Crab3DataHandling?sortcol=0;table=3;up=0#sorted_table "Sort by this column") | [Default](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/Crab3DataHandling?sortcol=1;table=3;up=0#sorted_table "Sort by this column") | [Explanation](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/Crab3DataHandling?sortcol=2;table=3;up=0#sorted_table "Sort by this column") |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Data.inputDataset` | `None` | The (primary) input dataset for to analyze. |
| `Data.lumiMask` | `None` | The lumi-mask JSON file to apply to the input dataset before analysis. |
| `Data.ignoreLocality` | `False` | Set to `True` to allow jobs to run at any site, regardless of whether the dataset is located at that site. The user-specified whitelist and blacklist are still respected. |
| `Data.inputDBS` | `https://cmsweb.cern.ch/dbs/prod/global/DBSReader` | The URL of the DBS instance for the input dataset. Defaults to the global DBS3 instance. |
| `Data.allowNonValidInputDataset` | `False` | Set to `True` to allow CRAB to run over (the valid of) the input dataset given in `Data.inputDataset` even if its status in DBS is not VALID. |
If the job requires multiple simultaneous input (a RAW-RECO analysis), set `Data.inputDataset` to the primary input. The user is responsible to make sure that the secondary input dataset is available to the job via whitelisting or reliance on AAA.
## Output Data
The following configuration parameters control the output data behavior.
| [Parameter Name](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/Crab3DataHandling?sortcol=0;table=4;up=0#sorted_table "Sort by this column") | [Default](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/Crab3DataHandling?sortcol=1;table=4;up=0#sorted_table "Sort by this column") | [Explanation](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/Crab3DataHandling?sortcol=2;table=4;up=0#sorted_table "Sort by this column") |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Data.publication` | `True` | Whether to publish the EDM output in DBS or not. Notice that for publication to be possible, the corresponding output have to be transferred to the permanent storage element. |
| `Data.publishDBS` | `https://cmsweb.cern.ch/dbs/prod//DBSWriter/` | The URL of the DBS instance where output will be published. |
|  | `crab_` + `General.requestName` | The user-specified portion of the output dataset name; `publication-name` above. |
| `Data.publishWithGroupName` | `False` | If `Data.outLFNDirBase` starts with `/store/group/<groupname>`, use the `groupname` instead of the username in the publication dataset name. |
| `Data.outputPrimaryDataset` | `CRAB_UserFiles` or `CRAB_PrivateMC` | When running an analysis over private input or running MC generation, this parameter specifies the primary dataset name that should be used in the LFN of the output/log and in the publication dataset name. |
| `Site.storageSite` | `None` | The final storage site where should copy outputs. Job outputs will initially go to the *runtime storage*, the site storage where the job was run. |
| `General.transferOutputs` | `True` | Whether or not to transfer the output to the storage site. If set to `False`, the output are discarded and the user can not recover them. |
| `General.transferLogs` | `False` | Whether or not to copy the jobs log to the storage site. If set to `False`, the log are discarded and the user can not recover them. Notice however that a short version of the log containing the first 1000 lines and the last 3000 lines are still available through the monitoring web pages. |
Note that only output produced with the cmsRun PoolOutputModule can be published into DBS.After the job finishes, the AsynchronousStageOut component of will copy the from the runtime site to the user-specified storage site.This will use an external FTS3 server and, for most sites, do the transfer using the SRMv2 protocol. After the stageout is , outputs can be retrieved with `crab getoutput`.
* **TODO** add ASO via Rucio description
After the stageout is , are published into DBS. Partial publication is done; by default, every 100 completed output are published as a new block.
## Publication in DBS
### Output dataset names in DBS
Only output for which cmsRun produced a proper Framework Job Report (i.e. output produced by PoolOutputModule) can be published in DBS. This is because publication in DBS requires proper metadata like list of events, lumis, parents which are contained in that report. This is available for
* [EDM](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/EDM) (i.e. output produced by PoolOutputModule)
* NANOAOD
* DQMIO
When using FTS-based ASO, only one dataset can be published for each task, if configuraiton results in multiple [EDM](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/EDM) , publication will be disabled.When using Rucio-based ASO, multiple dataset publication is supported.For jobs with a single PoolOutputModule instance, the output dataset name has the following format for DBS3:`/<primary-dataset>/<CERN-username_or_groupname>-<publication-name>-<pset-hash>/USER`For jobs with multiple PoolOutputModule instances, the output dataset names have the following format:`/<primary-dataset>/<CERN-username_or_groupname>-<publication-name>-<module-label>-<pset-hash>/USER`For example, if user `bbockelm` has a job with `pset-hash = 12345` analyzing `/GenericTTbar/HC-CMSSW_5_3_1_START53_V5-v1/GEN-SIM-RECO`, with publication name set to `test1`, and with the following output modules defined in the CMSSW parameter-set configuration:
```
process.bar = cms.OutputModule("PoolOutputModule",
 fileName = cms.untracked.string("nothing.root"),
 outputCommands=cms.untracked.vstring("drop *"),
)
.OutputModule("PoolOutputModule",
 fileName = cms.untracked.string("everything.root"),
 outputCommands=cms.untracked.vstring("keep *"),
)
```
then the resulting output datasets would be:`/GenericTTbar/bbockelm-test1-bar-12345/USER``/GenericTTbar/bbockelm-test1-baz-12345/USER`The following table explains the variables in the above templates.
| [Variable](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/Crab3DataHandling?sortcol=0;table=5;up=0#sorted_table "Sort by this column") | [Explanation](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/Crab3DataHandling?sortcol=1;table=5;up=0#sorted_table "Sort by this column") |
| --- | --- |
| `primary-dataset` | The value of the configuration parameter `Data.outputPrimaryDataset`. |
| `CERN-username_or_groupname` | The task owner's CERN username or if `Data.publishWithGroupName = True` and `Data.outLFNDirBase` starts with `/store/group/<groupname>` the groupname extracted from the third field of `Data.outLFNDirBase`. |
| `publication-name` | The value of the configuration parameter . |
| `pset-hash` | The PSet hash for cmsRun job. This is **not** the output of `edmConfigHash` but taken from `edmProvDump`. |
| `module-label` | The module label of the PoolOutputModule. |
The fields `primary-dataset`, `CERN-username` and `publication-name` are the same as used for the naming of the output . The remaining parameter, `pset-hash`, is a hash produced from the CMSSW code used by the cmsRun job. The hash guarantees that every different CMSSW code has a distinct output dataset name in DBS, even if `publication-name` is not changed. It also allows to keep the same `publication-name` when re-doing a dataset after a modification in the CMSSW code (e.g. a modification to fix a bug in the previously produced dataset). Notice also that, by keeping the same `publication-name`, a user can add new to an already published dataset by running a new task, as long as the CMSSW code to produce the new is the same as the one used to produce the original . This is the case in which a user wants to extend a dataset as data become available with time over the course of an LHC run, or when the user wants to run a second task for only the failed jobs of the first task (as opposed to doing a resubmission of the failed jobs).
### ![UPDATED](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/updated.gif "UPDATED") Changing a dataset or file status in DBS ![UPDATED](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/updated.gif "UPDATED") **UPDATED November 2023** ![UPDATED](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/updated.gif "UPDATED")
It is common to publish in DBS datasets that are, sooner or later, not going to be used anymore, or that are buggy to begin with. Or more simply one or more get lost on disk and must be removed from the list of what is processed. A frequent question is then: can a user delete a dataset from DBS? The answer is **no**. We never delete datasets or a from DBS (i.e. completely remove an entry). Instead, what we can do is to invalidate a dataset, or individual in a dataset, after they have published. This corresponds to changing the status in DBS of the dataset or file to invalid. It is important to know that:
* **DATSET STATUS OTHER THAN VALID MAY MEAN THAT ARE STILL THERE, SIMPLY NOT GOOD FOR PHYSICS**
* **ONLY HAVE A YES/NO (`is_file_valid=1/0`) FLAG. WHICH IS USED TO INDICATE DELETED OR UNREADABLE**
* ![UPDATED](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/updated.gif "UPDATED") Invalidating a dataset has no effect on valid/invalid status of ![UPDATED](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/updated.gif "UPDATED")
* The invalidation of a dataset or file is a reversible procedure.
* By default invalidated datasets will not be listed by DAS and not found in CRAB [DataDiscovery](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/DataDiscovery?topicparent=CMSPublic. "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.")
* Invalid datasets can still be used in CRAB (although it requires to set `Data.allowNonValidInputDataset = True` in the CRAB configuration)
* CRAB will always skip invalid . The rational is that a file that is marked as invalid means it is corrupted, deleted, lost or anyhow unreadable. On the other hand, a dataset that is marked as invalid simply means it is not good for physics, but there could be reasons to look at it anyway (e.g. to figure out why it is marked as invalid and if it can be turned into valid by removing some or similar).
Users can change status of datasets and/or using CRAB Client.
By default those commands acts on /datasets published in `` instance of DBS, i.e. where usually CRAB publishes output of tasks. Other DBS instances could be used e.g. for testing by experts, like DBS `int`.
```
crab setdataset status --dataset <datasetname> --status <status>
crab setfilestatus --status VALID|INVALID --file LFN  # will change status for one file
or
crab setfilestatus --status VALID|INVALID --dataset <dataset> # will apply new status to all  in the dataset
```
more info can be obtained as usual with the `crab --help` command:
```
belforte@lxplus805/~> crab setdatasetstatus --help
Usage: crab.py setdatasetstatus [options] [args]
     Set status of a USER dataset in
Options:
  -h, --help           show this help message and exit
  --instance=INSTANCE  DBS instance. e.g. prod/ (default) or int/.
                       Use at your own risk.Unless you really know what you
                       are doing, stay with the default
  --dataset=DATASET    dataset name
  --status=STATUS      New status of the dataset:
                       VALID/INVALID/DELETED/DEPRECATED
  --recursive          Apply status to children datasets and sets all
                       status in thoseto VALID if status=VALID, INVALID
                       otherwise
  --proxy=PROXY        Use the given proxy. Skip Grid proxy creation and
                       myproxy delegation.
belforte@lxplus805/~>
```
![, important](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/.gif ", important") Please be aware that `--recursive` option is not implemented yet, it is listed for compatibility with old command and usefulness is doubtful.
```
belforte@lxplus805/~> crab setfilestatus --help
Usage: crab.py setfilestatus [options] [args]
     Set status of a USER file in
Options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -i INSTANCE, --instance=INSTANCE
                        DBS instance. e.g. prod/ (default) or int/
  -d <dataset_name>, --dataset=<dataset_name>
                        Will apply status to all  in this dataset. Use
                        either -- or--dataset
  -s STATUS, --status=STATUS
                        New status of the file(s): VALID/INVALID
  -f <lfn1[,..,lfnx] or filename>, --=<lfn1[,..,lfnx] or filename>
                        List of  to be validated/invalidated. Can be
                        either a simple LFN or a file containg LFNs or a comma
                        separated list of LFNs. Use either -- or
                        --dataset
  --proxy=PROXY         Use the given proxy. Skip Grid proxy creation and
                        myproxy delegation.
belforte@lxplus805/~>
```
![, important](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/.gif ", important") please note that a file list is not supported yet due to a bug in DBS server
### General remarks about publication in DBS
#### Elevating a dataset from local DBS to global DBS
Users are not allowed to publish data in the global DBS; only dataOperation people can do it. So if a user needs to elevate a dataset, he/she has to first of all publish the  dataset in a local DBS instance and then follow <https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookGroupActivities> to request the transfer of the data to the "right" directory and the publication in the global DBS.
* : The Store Results service used for dataset migration and elevation does not support growing datasets. That means that the dataset has to be completed before the elevation request. One can not make another request for elevation with the same dataset name. If one produces more similar data, one needs to do something like adding \_v1, \_v2, \_v3 etc. to the dataset name.
#### The import of parent dataset is not allowed from a local DBS to another local DBS
One can not publish a user dataset in a local DBS instance, analize it to produce a new user dataset and publish the new dataset in a different local DBS. This is because the import of parents (done by default during publication) can not transfer data from one local DBS to another local DBS; publication will simply fail. The import is allowed only from the global DBS instance to a local DBS instance. One can publish the new dataset only in the same local DBS instance where the "user" parent dataset is published.
##

# Task and States in -HTCondor
|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| : ![5](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/pub/CMS/WebPreferences/complete5.png) | Go to [SWGuideCrab](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideCrab) |
This document covers the various states of a task and in -HTCondor.
## Vocabulary Terms
Although this document assumes a general familiarity with HTCondor and concepts, we outline our definitions of a few vocabulary words that are often confusing.
* **Task**: A unit of work corresponding to the processing or simulation of an input dataset.
* **DAG task**: The realization of a task as a condor\_dagman invocation. When run, the DAG task is logically divided up into many nodes. The condor\_dagman process will attempt to  the DAG task successfully. When the DAG task is done, the task is successful.
* : A portion of the work in a task. The work associated with the does not change during the task lifetime. At any given time when the task is in the SUBMITTED state, a may have either zero or one HTCondor jobs associated with it.
  + The user is reported the states in monitoring and in the output of `crab status -l`.
* **Job**: A job in the HTCondor schedd. This corresponds to an attempt to  a single . A successful job is necessary - but not sufficient - to successfully  a (as the post-job work - such as ASO - as run by condor\_dagman could fail). At most one job may be in the HTCondor schedd per at a time; however, over time, there may be many jobs that attempted to  a .
  + The job states are equivalent to the job states in HTCondor.
* **Resubmit**: A job that is not the first attempt at a where the previous attempt ended normally. A resubmit may either be done manually (if the prior attempt ended with a fatal error) or by condor\_dagman itself (if the prior attempt ended with a recoverable error).
* : A job that is restarted by HTCondor because the previous run ended abnormally (examples: HTCondor lost its network connection to the job or there were ). No user action causes a .
## Task States
* **NEW**, **RESUBMIT**, **KILL**: Temporary statuses to indicate the action ('submit', 'resubmit' or 'kill') that has to be applied to the task.
* **QUEUED**: An action ('submit', 'resubmit' or 'kill') affecting the task is queued in the system.
* **SUBMITTED**: The task was submitted to HTCondor as a DAG task. The DAG task is currently running.
* **SUBMITFAILED**: The 'submit' action has failed ( was unable to create a DAG task).
* **FAILED**: The DAG task completed all nodes and at least one is a permanent failure.
* **COMPLETED**: All nodes have been completed
* **KILLED**: The user killed the task.
* **KILLFAILED**: The 'kill' action has failed.
* **RESUBMITFAILED**: The 'resubmit' action has failed.
## States
States in **bold** are terminal states - nodes will stay in this state unless if there is some human intervention.States in *italics* are transient states - is still attempting to make progress on this . No user interaction is required.
* *unsubmitted*: The is ready to have a job, but condor\_dagman has not yet submitted a job to the HTCondor schedd.
  + This is usually due the task already having too many idle jobs or the DAG task has just recently started up.
* *idle*: The job for this is in the HTCondor schedd queue, but is not running.
* *running*: The job for this is running on a remote worker .
* **finished**: The has had a successful job and transfer.
* **failed**: The had a permanent failure. `condor_dagman` will not resubmit this job without a user intervention (via 'crab resubmit').
* (start state): condor\_dagman is waiting before submitting this job. Typically, this is because either the DAG task is brand new (and condor\_dagman hasn't considered this job yet) or the prior job for this exited with a recoverable error. condor\_dagman will resubmit this job in the future.
* *transferring*: The job has finished and condor\_dagman is running stageout.
* *killing*: condor\_dagman is killing the job associated with this . Killing is typically very quick, but may last several minutes in a few cases.
* **held**: The job associated with this is held in the HTCondor queue due to some fatal error; this will require operator intervention to fix.
Note that, due to implementation details,  is the start state for all nodes. We hope to start all nodes in the *unsubmitted* state in the future.
## State Transitions
The figure below outlines the state transitions in .
![Job_State_diagram.png](/twiki/pub/CMSPublic/Crab3HtcondorStates/Job_State_diagram.png)
## Automatic Resubmit Policies
will examine the results of the job and, for a few known cases, will automatically resubmit the job.will NEVER resubmit if ANY of these are true:
* The last attempt at the job lasted more than 24 hours.
* The cumulative wall time for all attempts is more than 36 hours.
* The last attempt used more than 2GB of memory.
* The job did not produce a usable job report.
* The job hit its resubmit limit (currently, 10 resubmits are allowed after any submit/resubmit).
If none of the above are true, will resubmit if ONE of these are true:
* The job ended with a file open or read error (8021, 8020, 8028)
* The job ended with a stageout error (60307)
* The job did not find the required CMSSW version on the worker (10034)
Note that the wrapper forces the minimum job runtime to be at least 20 minutes; this prevents a single worker from failing too many jobs.Whether a job is resubmitted is determined by the post-job process, run by dagman on the schedd. If the post-job determines the job can be resubmitted, then the resubmit will be done by the dagman process at some time in the future; immediately, however, the job enters the  state.
## Automatic Policies
If the job goes into the hold state, it will automatically be released by the HTCondor schedd for these reasons:
* .
* File stage-in failures.
The job can be released at most once every 5 minutes.If the HTCondor starter process has an unexpected and unrecoverable network disconnect from the schedd (during job startup, job running, or the end of the job), then the HTCondor schedd will requeue the job and attempt to re-run it in the future.
## Automatic Site Blacklist Policies
(NOTE: We are in the process of implementing this policy.)A job may blacklist a site at submit time if ALL of the following conditions are met:
* The previous job for this failed at the site.
* There have been more than 10 completed jobs for this task (failed or successful).
* There are 5 successful jobs for this task. (protects against tasks which are going to fail everywhere).
* The site success rate is less than 50% for this task.
* The site has failed at least 5 jobs.
* The job can match at least one other site.
A 'crab resubmit' will clear all statistics with respect to the automatic blacklist.In the future, the automatic blacklist will be shown in the glidemon monitoring.

## Finding what you need
* Get the full name of the task from the user; this will tell you which schedd to look at.
* Refer to [this page](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/CMSCrabTaskWorker) to the `vocmsXXX` server and log file locations.
## On the schedd
* To deny a user with local unix user name `cms123`, add the following line to `.../config.d/99_banned_users.conf` (create if it does not exist):
```
DENY_WRITE = cms123@*, $(DENY_WRITE)
```
Reload the schedd by sending it a `SIGHUP`.
* To list all jobs in a task named `140221_015428_vocms20:bbockelm_crab_lxplus414_user_17` :
```
condor_q -const ':bbockelm_crab_lxplus414_user_17"'
```
* To a task named `140221_015428_vocms20:bbockelm_crab_lxplus414_user_17` :
```
condor_hold -const ':bbockelm_crab_lxplus414_user_17" && TaskType=?="ROOT"'
```
* To the HTCondor working (spool) directory (different from the web monitor directory; contains things like the raw logfile, postjob, proxy, input files, etc) either :
```
condor_q -const ':bbockelm_crab_lxplus414_user_17"' -af Iwd
```
Or go to the schedd task diretory (such as "~/140221\_015428\_vocms20:bbockelm\_crab\_lxplus414\_user\_17/") and the ll (ls -l) command. It will show some files as symlinked from the HTCondor spool directory:
```
... postjob.14.0.txt -> /data/srv/glidecondor/condor_local/spool/9589/0/cluster129589.proc0.subproc0/postjob.14.0.txt
```
You can simply cd to the shown directory (after deleting the file name, of course), which is the spool directory itself..
* To job one in the task, :
```
condor_q -const ':bbockelm_crab_lxplus414_user_17"&&CRAB_Id=?=1'
```
You can replace `condor_q` with `condor_history` for completed jobs. If you want just the history for retry 2,
```
condor_history -match 1 -const ':bbockelm_crab_lxplus414_user_17"&&CRAB_Id=?=1&&CRAB_Retry=?=2'
```
* To list all tasks for user
```
condor_q cms293
```
* To list a specific task configuration:
```
condor_q -l 179330.0
```
or if the task does not exist anymore, then it should be taken from the condor history:
```
condor_history -l 179330.0
```
* To see the list of users that are allowed to write on the schedd:
```
condor_config_val SCHEDD.ALLOW_WRITE
```
* To see the location of Master log or Schedd log:
```
condor_config_val MASTER_LOG OR condor_config_val SCHEDD_LOG
```
* To see all the schedds known in the glidein-collector.t2.ucsd.ed collector:
```
condor_status -pool glidein-collector.t2.ucsd.edu -schedd
```
* To see all running/idle by username:
```
condor_q -name  -name  -name  -format '%s\n' AccountingGroup | sort | uniq -c
```
* To see all running by username:
```
condor_q -name  -name  -name  -format '%s\n' AccountingGroup -const '(JobStatus=?=2)' | sort | uniq -c
```
* To see all task processes started after a given time:
```
condor_q -con "jobuniverse==7&&qdate>`date -d "Nov 4 08:50" +%s`"
```
* To see all running in the production schedds:
```
condor_q -name  -name  -name   -const '(JobStatus=?=2)' | grep gWMS-CMSRun | wc -l #to count running jobs
```
Job Status explanation:
```
0 Unexpanded U
1 Idle I
2 Running R
3 Removed X
4 Completed C
5 Held H
6 Submission_err E
```
* Users sometimes that their jobs do not . There are several reasons why a specific job does not . These reasons range from failed job or machine constraints, bias due to preferences, insufficient priority, or the preemption ``throttle'' that is implemented by the condor\_negotiator to prevent thrashing. Many of these reasons can be diagnosed by using the `-analyze` option of `condor_q`.
```
condor_q 184439.0 -analyze
```
or if it is not enough information, do
```
condor_q 184439.0 -better-analyze
```
* To see the list of running pilots grouped by site:
```
condor_status -format '%s\n' GLIDEIN_CMSSite  | sort | uniq -c
```
* To see the list of idle pilots for a CE:
```
condor_q -const 'GlideinEntryName=?="CMS_T2_CH_CERN_ce408" && JobStatus=?=1' -pool vocms0305.cern.ch -g
```
* To see the number of tasks each schedd is running:
```
condor_status -schedd -pool vocms097.cern.ch -const 'regexp("", Name)' -af:h Name TotalSchedulerJobsRunning
```
* To see the number of jobs matching a site in one schedd:
```
 condor_q  -pool vocms099.cern.ch -name  -const '(StringListMember("T2_US_Purdue", DESIRED_Sites)=?=True)&&(JobStatus=?=1)'
```
* To see the number of scheduler jobs (dagman) idle and running:
```
condor_status -const 'CMSGWMS_Type=?="crabschedd"' -schedd -af Name TotalSchedulerJobsRunning TotalSchedulerJobsIdle
```
## On the Collector
### Boosting user priority
Boosting user priority can be done from the glideinWMS collector machine in the Global Pool, currently vocms097.cern.ch. User priority works in HTCondor such that jobs from users with the smallest priority number first. The priority number is a combination of two things, a usage-based number which increases with usage and decreases exponentially over a 24h period, and an overall priority scale factor (default=100). Therefore, people with the most recent usage will have the best priority, given that their priority factors are equal.To query user priorities (as any user on the collector machine):
```
condor_userprio -allusers
```
Commands to change user priorities must be executed as user **condor** on the collector machine itself. To reset the user priority factor:
```
condor_userprio -setfactor <user> <val>
```
To zero a user's recent usage:
```
condor_userprio -resetusage <user>
```
For more options please read:
```
condor_userprio -help
```
For example, the user under which the jobs are submitted is given a priority factor of 1, so that jobs almost always before anything else in the Global Pool. This change was made on December 5, 2014, and by the next day over 97% of the jobs started within 2 hours. Before the change, the percentage was only ~80%.N.B.: It you an error like `condor_userprio: Can't locate negotiator in local pool` when doing `condor_userprio` you can specify the pool using `--pool`, for example `condor_userprio -pool cmssrv221.fnal.gov`. Moreover, with recent changes to the global pool negotiator settings now it is not guaranteed this command will (see [https://cms-logbook.cern.ch/elog/GlideInWMS/5018![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cms-logbook.cern.ch/elog/GlideInWMS/5018))

## Crabcache ([UserFileCache](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/UserFileCache?topicparent=CMSPublic.Crab3OperatorDebugging;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it."))
* To get the list of all the users in the crabcache:
```
curl -X GET 'https://cmsweb.cern.ch/crabcache/info?subresource=listusers' --key $ --cert $ -k
{"result": [
 "mmascher"
,"aldo"
]}
```
* To get all the files uploaded by a user to the crabcache and the amount of quota (in bytes) he's using:
```
curl -X GET 'https://cmsweb.cern.ch/crabcache/info?subresource=userinfo&username=mmascher' --key $ --cert $ -k
{"result": [
 {"file_list": ["/data/state/crabcache/files/m/mmascher/69/697a932e19bd2912710fe0322de3eff41a5553f1f9820117a8262f0ebcd3640a", "/data/state/crabcache/files/m/mmascher/14/14571bc71cf2077961408fb1a060b9497a9c7d0cc1dcb47ed0f7fc1ac2e3748d", "/data/state/crabcache/files/m/mmascher/ef/efdedb430f8462c72259fd2e427e684d8e3aedf8d0d811bf7ef8a97f30a47bac", ..., "/data/state/crabcache/files/m/mmascher/05/059b06681025f14ecce5cbdc49c83e1e945a30838981c37b5293781090b07bd7", "/data/state/crabcache/files/m/mmascher/up/uplog.txt"], "used_space": [130170972]}
]}
```
* To get more information about one specific file (the file must be owned by the user who makes the query):
```
curl -X GET 'https://cmsweb.cern.ch/crabcache/info?subresource=fileinfo&hashkey=697a932e19bd2912710fe0322de3eff41a5553f1f9820117a8262f0ebcd3640a' --key $ --cert $ -k
{"result": [
 {"hashkey": "697a932e19bd2912710fe0322de3eff41a5553f1f9820117a8262f0ebcd3640a", "created": 1400161415.0, "modified": 1400161415.0, "exists": true, "size": 1303975}

* To a specific file (currently you can only your files. In the future power users should be able to everything):
```
curl -X GET 'https://cmsweb.cern.ch/crabcache/info?subresource=fileremove&hashkey=697a932e19bd2912710fe0322de3eff41a5553f1f9820117a8262f0ebcd3640a' --key $ --cert $ -k

```
curl -X GET 'https://cmsweb.cern.ch/crabcache/info?subresource=basicquota' --key $ --cert $ -k

 {"quota_user_limit": 10}
]}
```
## Development Oriented Tricks I did not know where to put
### To the preDag on the schedd with debugger
* I only made this after it ran already by itself.
* sketchy notes on what to do there, may be enough:
```
cd SPOOL_DIR
export _CONDOR_JOB_AD=finished_jobs/job.0-1.0
export PYTHONPATH=$PYTHONPATH:/cvmfs/cms.cern.ch/rucio/x86_64/rhel9/py3/current/lib/.9/site-packages/
export TEST_DONT_REDIRECT_STDOUT=True
export =`ls|egrep  [a-z,0-9]{40}`
rm automatic_splitting/processed
vim TaskWorker/Actions/PreDAG.py
and put a breakpoint at some proper place:
import pdb; pdb.set_trace()
import TaskWorker.Actions.PreDAG as PreDAG
PreDAG.PreDAG().execute("processing",5,0)
# or to  it "like DAGMAN does"
./dag_bootstrap.sh PREDAG processing 5 0
```
### To a pre-job on the schedd
* Go to the spool directory on the task in the schedd
* get the user identity in order to access files via  `username`
  + Note: `username` is the schedd username which the task belongs to, for example, cms9999. You can e.g. do
```

* instructions updated and checked: June 2017
* Go to the spool directory of the task in the schedd.

```
=`cat RunJobs.dag | grep "POST Job1" | awk 'BEGIN { FS="MAX_RETRIES" }; {print $2}'`
```
which results in something like:
```
belforte@vocms059/~> echo $
170620_163137:belforte_crab_20170620_183133 1 /store/temp/user/belforte.be1f4dc5be8664cbd145bf008f5399adf42b086f/prova/doppio/slash/GenericTTbar/CRAB3_test-SB/170620_163137/0000 /store/user/belforte/prova/doppio//slash/GenericTTbar/CRAB3_test-SB/170620_163137/0000 cmsRun_1.log.tar.gz conventional kk_1.root
belforte@vocms059/~>

* Identify the file in the spool directory that contains your proxy and set env. var (the file name is a sequence of 40 lower-case letters and/or digits, could e.g. use `` export =`ls|egrep  [a-z,0-9]{40}` ``) and make sure the proxy is still valid (`voms-proxy-info`).

```

* Here is a script which automathize all of the above (but the insertion of `pdb` calls):
  + [https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/master/scripts/Utils/-postjob.sh![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/master/scripts/Utils/-postjob.sh)
* quick recipe to rerun PJ for /pasting
  + do the following once
    ```
    cd SPOOL_DIR
    jobId=1
    jobRetry=0
    export =`pwd`/`ls|egrep  [a-z,0-9]{40}`
    export _CONDOR_JOB_AD=finished_jobs/job.${jobId}.0

    export TEST_POSTJOB_NO_STATUS_UPDATE=True
    jobReturnCode=0
    retryCount=0
    maxRetries=10
    =`cat RunJobs*.*dag | grep "POST Job${jobId} " | awk 'BEGIN { FS="MAX_RETRIES" }; {print $2}'`

    ```
    echo '{"pre": 1, "post": 0}' > retry_info/job.${jobId}.txt
    rm defer_info/defer_num.${jobId}.0.txt
    echo " POSTJOB ${jobClusterId} ${jobReturnCode} ${retryCount} ${maxRetries} $"
    ```
  + and then /paste i.e. execute the output of the last `echo` command.

### How to (re) a task\_process for a single task
In case a certain task has no task\_process running, it can be restarted with a simple `condor_submit` from the schedd. However, it should be done as the user to whom the task belongs, otherwise the task\_process will into a lot of permission issues in the spool directory and ultimately won't work. The procedure is as follows:
```
# Locate the spool dir of the task, for example by using a known ClusterID of the DAG:
cd `condor_q 9454770.0 -af Iwd`
#  the user who submitted the original task
 cms1425
# condor_submit the task_process jdl (called daemon.jdl). It should be done from the parent directory because of paths in the jdl.
condor_submit task_process/daemon.jdl
```
To work on a list of task names for a given user (e.g. in file TL)
```
# setup as that user
sudo /grid/cms1425
# put the list of task names in an env. var:
tList=`cat TL`
# check
for t in $tList ; do eval condor_q -con 'crab_reqname==\"$t\"'; done
#  task_process
for t in $tList ; do echo $; pushd $t/SPOOL_DIR; condor_submit task_process/daemon.jdl; popd; done
```
# condor\_submit the task\_process jdl (called daemon.jdl). It should be done from the parent directory because of paths in the jdl.
condor\_submit task\_process/daemon.jdl
### failed publications
#### see also [CRABStandardCorrectiveActions#DBS\_Migrations\_fail\_causing\_Publ](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/CRABStandardCorrectiveActions#DBS_Migrations_fail_causing_Publ)
**note** directory names here are as seen from inside the Publisher container.Whenever Publisher's `TaskPublish.py` fails to publish one block, it prints the message in its log `/data/srv/Publisher/tasks/<username>/<taskname>.log` and dumps the failing block in `/data/srv/Publisher_files/FailedBlocks/failed-block-at-<timestamp>.txt` where `<timestamp>` is the time in seconds from Epoch and will match the same stamp in the log. Example `/data/srv/Publisher_files/FailedBlocks/failed-block-at-1611258668.34.txt` the date of the failures is
```
date -d @1611258668.34
```
```
Thu 21 Jan 20:51:08 CET 2021
```
Once you have located the block dump file, more info can be obtained via the script `DebugFailedBlockPublication.py` available in [GitHub](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/GitHub). This script takes as input the **file name** without the directory. It will add the proper path internally. Make sure to source the `env.sh` in Publisher home directory.Use the elog [elog/Analysis+Operations/3605![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cms-logbook.cern.ch/elog/Analysis%2BOperations/3605) as an example.a container with (changing the tag if you need it):
```
PUBLISHERTAG=v3.220831
docker  --rm --name Publisher -it --net host --privileged \
 -e SERVICE=Publisher -w /data/srv/Publisher/ \
 -v /cvmfs/cms.cern.ch/SITECONF:/cvmfs/cms.cern.ch/SITECONF \
 -v /data/srv/tmp/:/data/srv/tmp/ \
 -v /etc/grid-security/:/etc/grid-security/ \
 -v /data/certs/:/data/certs/ \
 -v /etc/vomses/:/etc/vomses/ \
 -v /data/srv/Publisher_files/:/data/srv/Publisher_files/ \
 -v /data/container/:/data/container/ \
 registry.cern.ch/cmscrab/crabtaskworker:$PUBLISHERTAG bash
```
Inside the container something similar to
```
[@crab-prod-tw02 Publisher]$ source env.sh
Define environment for Publisher in /data/srv/Publisher

[@crab-prod-tw02 Publisher]$ ls /data/srv/Publisher_files/FailedBlocks/
failed-block-at-1611258668.34.txt

usage: DebugFailedBlockPublication.py [-h] --file FILE
optional arguments:

  --file FILE  file containing the dump of the block
[c#rab3@crab-prod-tw02 Utils]$   /data/repos/CRABServer/scripts/Utils/DebugFailedBlockPublication.py --file failed-block-at-1611258668.34.txt
Block is meant to be added to dataset
/VLLM1100_GENSIM_2018/alaha-VLLM1100_GENSIM_2018_20210121_151743_LHEoutput-f9aa307ba162b2dd3bdd5962c5a7a2f6/USER
Block contains 67 files
file /store/user/alaha/VLLM1100_GENSIM_2018/VLLM1100_GENSIM_2018_20210121_151743/210121_141757/0000/VLLM1100_RAWSIM_444.root found in DBS

1/67 file(s) from input blocks are already in DBS/phys03. Publication will fail

As of March 2021 the most common problem is that some file is already present in DBS in another dataset (like in the example above). This is due to a [shortcoming![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/6307) of new Publisher and there is no fix for it once damage was done. Users need to avoid having multiple output files form CRAB jobs when using publication in DBS, until this is fixed.
Starting with CRABClient version `v3.210323` (not in production yet), such submissions will be prevented.A quick way to check if all files in `/data/srv/Publisher_files/FailedBlocks/` are due to this is
```
for f in `ls /data/srv/Publisher_files/FailedBlocks/fail*`; do echo $f;   /data/repos/CRABServer/scripts/Utils/DebugFailedBlockPublication.py --file `basename $f`|grep present; done
```
and check that for each file there is a line like
```
files present in DBS in another dataset: 6
```
Please move already checked block dump into the `/data/srv/Publisher_files/FailedBlocks/old` directory. Files older than 60 days will be cleaned by crontab, but a long list of failed blocks is confusing.
## HTCondor pools
There are two pools we use: global (i.e. Production) and TB (Integration Test Bed) which are not correlated to CRAB prod/pre-prod/dev instances, CMSWEB testbed etc. The two HTCondor pools are selected by their collector.
### List schedd's in the pool
```
#production pool
condor_status -sched -con 'CMSGWMS_Type=="crabschedd"' -pool cmsgwms-collector-global.cern.ch

schedds=`condor_status -sched -con 'CMSGWMS_Type=="crabschedd"' -pool cmsgwms-collector-global.cern.ch -af machine`
for s in $schedds ; do echo $s; ssh $s -p 2222 "df -h /data"; done
# ITB pool
condor_status -sched -con 'CMSGWMS_Type=="crabschedd"' -pool
```

## old tasks in one schedd
At times we had some things go wrong and tasks end up in a zombie state using up a running dagman slot well beyond the a priori defined lifetime of a task.
Removal of such old taks can be done one schedd at a time with a small adaptation of the previous recipe. Following example removes tasks older than 2 weeks.
```
#from the schedd
condor_q -const 'JobUniverse==7 && JobStatus==2 && (time() - JobStartDate > 14 * 86400)' -af ClusterId  > ~/tasks.txt
cat ~/tasks.txt #to check you grabbed the tasks
for task in `cat ~/tasks.txt` ; do
  condor_hold $task -reason "Task removed by CRAB operator becasue too old"
done
```
That will store a [HoldReason](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/HoldReason?topicparent=CMSPublic.Crab3OperatorDebugging;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") as a [/bin/edit/CMSPublic/ClassAd?topicparent=CMSPublic.Crab3OperatorDebugging;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it."), e.g.
```
root@submit-4 ~# condor_q 22111709 -af HoldReason
Task removed by CRAB operator becasue too old (by user condor)
```
You can also get the list of CRAB task names with e.g.
```
for task in `cat ~/tasks.txt` ; do
  condor_q $task -af CRAB_ReqName
done
```
and use the above list of CRAB task names to insert the [HodReason](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/HodReason?topicparent=CMSPublic.Crab3OperatorDebugging;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") in Oracle so that user will see the message with crab status (do this from lxplus using the example in the previous section).
For sake of example, here's what I did to very old tasks (>20 dasy) on all schedd's:
```
condor_q -const 'JobUniverse==7 && JobStatus==2 && (time() - JobStartDate > 20 * 86400)' -af ClusterId > ~/tasks.txt
cat ~/tasks.txt
for task in `cat ~/tasks.txt` ; do
  condor_hold $task -reason "Task removed by CRAB operator becasue too old"
done
for task in `cat ~/tasks.txt` ; do   condor_q $task -af CRAB_ReqName >> /afs/cern.ch/user/b/belforte/WORK//TC3/dbg/KILLED/tasks.txt; done
```
so I got the final list of all tasks I killed in = /afs/cern.ch/user/b/belforte/WORK//TC3/dbg/KILLED/tasks.txt= and will use that in the Oracle changing script:
```
for task in `cat ~/tasks.txt`; do
     $task
done
```
## crontab with K5/AFS token on VM's
Here's a trick to a script via crontab on a VM when that script needs access to AFS, [EOS](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/EOS), CERNBOX or similar, i.e. a valid CERN K5 ticket
Such think can not be done directly on the VM, but one can use  on lxplus to execute a command remotely on the VM via ssh.
This should be used only for simple tasks, since logging and reporting capabilities are limited. One can e.g. use it to one flle to/from your
AFS area or to/from CERNBOX ([EOS](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/EOS) access requires K5 token). I use it to refresh my proxy etc.Here's an example :
```
#
# this file is ~belforte/public/mybin/.dat
#
#   check  the schedule with  ' -l'
#   update schedule from file with  ' < .dat'
#
# format: minute hour day month day-of-the-week host command
# see man
#  also man -S 5 crontab
#
#
# execute very minimal command every 2 days
20 23 */2 * * lxplus.cern.ch ssh crab-preprod-tw01.cern.ch /usr/bin/klist
```
In the example above stdout is sent me by mail, you can redirect to a file appending = >filename 2>&1= to the command
## Puppet
Commands below need to be as `root`
* puppet: `puppet agent -tv`
* check if puppet is enabled: `cat $(puppet agent_disabled_lockfile); echo ""`
  + if disabled, check since when: `ls -l $(puppet agent_disabled_lockfile)`
* enable puppet: `puppet agent --enable`
* disable puppet: `puppet agent --disable "Stefano says: keep stable"`
  + it is good to set a short note to say why is disabled in the disable command
* tell last time puppet ran: `grep puppet /var/log/messages|tail`
How to tell which puppet env is this machine in, various ways:
1. it is printed when you log in
2. `cat /etc/motd|grep Puppet`
3. `grep env /etc/puppetlabs/puppet/puppet.conf`
For more info see <https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/CRABPuppet>

body:

Contents:
* [Testing infrastructure](#Testing_infrastructure)
  + [Start tests: CRABServer\_ExecuteTests](#Start_tests_CRABServer_ExecuteTe)
  + [Client configuration validation (CCV): CRABServer\_ClientConfigurationValidation](#Client_configuration_validation)
  + [Client validation (CV): CRABServer\_ClientValidation](#Client_validation_CV_CRABServer)
  + [ tracking (TS): CRABServer\_CheckTestResults](#Status_tracking_TS_CRABServer_Ch)
* [Running tests on different CMSSW and SCRAM architectures combinations](#Running_tests_on_different_CMSSW)
* [Results tracking using GH issues](#Results_tracking_using_GH_issues)
* [Build tests container for](#Build_tests_container_for_slc7)
* [How to run test container manually on VM](#How_to_run_test_container_manual)
* [Cleaning storage site data](#Cleaning_storage_site_data)
## Testing infrastructure
Testing infrastructure is based on one master job. This job submits testing tasks and starts needed sub-jobs. All CRAB testing files needed to run tests are stored [https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/tree/master/test![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/tree/master/test)All CRAB testing jobs run under `cms-dmwm-cc7` label in `dmwm-` instance.
### Start tests: CRABServer\_ExecuteTests
[https://cmssdt.cern.ch/dmwm-/job/CRABServer\_ExecuteTests/![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cmssdt.cern.ch/dmwm-/job/CRABServer_ExecuteTests/)Tests can be started using CRABServer\_ExecuteTests job. 4 sections needs to be configured: CRABClient version, REST instance, CMSSW release, which tests should be started.Based on how those 4 sections were configured, this job submits tasks. If at least one task submission failed, then all successfully submitted tasks are killed and this job is marked as failed (task submission operation is considered as an atomic operation) and none of the downstream jobs will be triggered. That being said, if for instance we started all 3 types of tests and tasks were successfully submitted for 2 tests, but failed for the last testing suite, then still this job is considered as failed.If task submission went well, then accordingly which tests were started, appropriate jobs will be triggered.
### Client configuration validation (CCV): CRABServer\_ClientConfigurationValidation
[https://cmssdt.cern.ch/dmwm-/job/CRABServer\_ClientConfigurationValidation/![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cmssdt.cern.ch/dmwm-/job/CRABServer_ClientConfigurationValidation/)
Job is executed 20 minutes after CRABServer\_ExecuteTests finished running and checks if various CRABClient configurations works. Job is executed a maximum of 5 times at 20 min intervals if at least one test needs to be retried. In case at least one of test needs to re-tried or failed, then this job is marked as failed. However, only if there is a test that needs to be retried, this job will retried in 20 minutes.To actually produce tests that will be executed makeTest.py script is used: [https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/master/test/makeTests.py![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/master/test/makeTests.py)
### Client validation (CV): CRABServer\_ClientValidation
[https://cmssdt.cern.ch/dmwm-/job/CRABServer\_ClientValidation/![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cmssdt.cern.ch/dmwm-/job/CRABServer_ClientValidation/)
Job is executed 20 minutes after CRABServer\_ExecuteTests finished running and checks if various CRABClient commands works on the task that was submitted with CRABServer\_ExecuteTests job. This job is executed only once.Client validation test can be found here: [https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/master/test/container/testingScripts/clientValidation.sh![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/master/test/container/testingScripts/clientValidation.sh)
###  tracking (TS): CRABServer\_CheckTestResults
[https://cmssdt.cern.ch/dmwm-/job/CRABServer\_CheckTestResults/![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cmssdt.cern.ch/dmwm-/job/CRABServer_CheckTestResults/)
Job is executed a maximum of 5 times at 60 min intervals to check if task submitted by the upstream job (CRABServer\_ExecuteTests) finished running. In case part of the jobs completed successfully while others are still running, then this job is marked as FAILED (even though there are not errors/mistakes in the code itself) and  checking on same list of tasks is executed again. Be aware, in case this job failed for some other reason (e.g. GH is down), then job is not retried - investigate manually and start tests again.Script that check tasks'  can be found here: [https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/master/test/container/testingScripts/statusTracking.py![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/master/test/container/testingScripts/statusTracking.py)
## Running tests on different CMSSW and SCRAM architectures combinations
CRABClient can be used by users on multiple different CMSSW releases, SCRAM architectures, using python2 or python3 env. etc. That being said, we need to have possibility to test CRABClient on different configurations. Available configurations are stored in file here: [https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/master/test/![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/master/test/) This file stores 4 main attributes:
1. `CMSSW_release:` CMSSW release used for testing. Attribute is the main attribute of the configuration file. This value is selected before starting tests in CRABServer\_ExecuteTests job and accordingly correct configuration line (i.e. , inputDataset, master) is picked by to use for executing tests.
2. `:` SCRAM architecture.  versions that starts with `6` are versions that should be executed on `slc6`, versions that starts with `7` should be executed on  and so on. That being said, we need to support possibility to run tests on different architecture versions. We run tests for `slc6` on Singularity container, while tests for  are executed in our own maintained container built on `cc7` stack (details how to build and run our own container are explained below).
3. `inputDataset:` input dataset which should be used for task submission.
4. `master:` indicates master configuration which currently is used for one purpose: checking CRABServer\_CheckTestResults results can be done from any SCRAM architecture or CMSSW release version regardless of what CMSSW version was used to submit tasks. Configuration line containing `master=yes` line is the one that will be used to run this check (otherwise we have a difficult task of supporting statusTracking.py script, i.e. including CRAB API, to run on different slc versions and dealing with pycurl versions).
## Results tracking using GH issues
Every time we start a new test, GH issue in `dmwm/CRABServer` repository is opened. GH issue name contains which `CRABClient` is being tested, to which `REST` instance tasks were submitted and finally which `CMSSW` version is used. Issue is opened right after job `CRABServer_ExecuteTests` is started, but before the task submission start. If task submission went well, list of task names is added to GH comment, if submission failed, failure is reported via comment.Every test that was started using `CRABServer_ExecuteTests` reports results to the same issue. In case you need to restart one of the tests manually (e.g. 5 times of running TS test was not enough), then you can restart the test and results will be reported to the same issue.For opening and managing issue we use `create-gh-issue.py` script available at [https://github.com/cms-sw/cms-bot/blob/master/create-gh-issue.py![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/cms-sw/cms-bot/blob/master/create-gh-issue.py) This script uses token created for [https://github.com/cmsdmwmbot![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/cmsdmwmbot) GH account. Token is deployed to `cms-dmwm-cc7` label machines.
## Build tests container for
* old instructions
  1. git clone / fetch CRABServer repository
  2. go to the CRABServer directory where testing files are stored
     ```
     cd CRABServer/test/container
     ```
  3. build docker image (use your own DH repository and provide {TAG})
     ```
     docker build . -t ${REPOSITORY}/crabserver_testing:${TAG}
     ```
  4. upload image to your DH repository (create one before)
     ```
     docker push ${REPOSITORY}/crabserver_testing:${TAG}
     ```
* new instructions
  + use [https://cmssdt.cern.ch/dmwm-//CRAB/job/CRABServer\_BuildTestImage/![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cmssdt.cern.ch/dmwm-//CRAB/job/CRABServer_BuildTestImage/)
New docker image has to be built every time new commit is pushed to [https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/tree/master/test/container![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/tree/master/test/container) directory. If you built new image version, please don't forget to update all 4 jobs to use new image version.
## How to run test container manually on VM
You can run testing container on any VM that has access to `/cvmfs`. If your private VM is not configured to access it, you can use CRAB taskworker machines (assuming it does not run any production container as we don't want to mess up with those machines). Setting up and starting container can be done in 3 steps:
1. Set env variables that will be passed to the container
   ```
   export DOCKER_ENV="-e inputDataset -e  -e CRABServer_tag -e Client_Validation_Suite -e Task_Submission_Status_Tracking -e Client_Configuration_Validation -e X509_USER_CERT -e X509_USER_KEY -e DBS_tag -e WMCore_tag -e CMSSW_release -e REST_Instance -e CRABClient_version"
   export DOCKER_VOL="-v $WORK_DIR/artifacts/:/data/CRABTesting/artifacts:Z  -v /tmp:/tmp -v /cvmfs:/cvmfs"
   ```
   \*All the env. variables used in `DOCKER_ENV` should have values set (if you don't want to use `CRABClient_version` set to `GH`, then you don't need to set `DBS_tag` and `WMCore_tag`). Also, be aware that you need to set `WORK_DIR` variable and inside that directory create `artifacts` folder which will be mounted to container and will be used to save testing files.
2. Start container
   ```
   docker run --name testingContainer -d -ti --net host --privileged $DOCKER_VOL $DOCKER_ENV  ddaina/crabserver_testing:211007
   ```
3. Once you have container up and running, you can login to it using below command and do inside whatever is needed (submit tasks/run tests etc)
   ```
   docker exec -it testingContainer bash
   ```
## Cleaning storage site data
Task that are submitted for running tests are configured to store data at :
```
.Site.storageSite = ''
```
So we need to clean space otherwise it will fill up. For cleaning the `eos` space we have job [https://cmssdt.cern.ch/dmwm-/job/cmsbot-eos-cleanup/![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cmssdt.cern.ch/dmwm-/job/cmsbot-eos-cleanup/) that runs every second day at 6:07am and deletes 2 directories `CRABTest/` and `GenericTTbar/` from `/eos/cms/store/user/cmsbot/`Job is configured to delete only two specific directories because `eos` space can be used for other purpose as well and we don't want to delete files that are used by others who has access to `cmsbot` account--  - 2021-12-13

body:
If you are experiencing TWiki instability from outside the CERN network, please connect via the CERN internal network - see [KB0010688![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cern.service-now.com/service-portal?id=KB0010688) for details

# Notes about deployment and potential backward compatibility issues
|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| : ![5](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/pub/CMS/WebPreferences/complete5.png) | Go to [SWGuideCrab](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideCrab) |
There are different pieces of software that gets upgraded every month: the client, the rest interface, the crabcache, the oracle database schema, the task worker, postjobs/WN code(cmscp and job wrapper), ASO, couchdb views.In general everything starts with a CMSWEB updata that brings the new version of the REST interface, the crabcache, and the ASO couchdb views. As soon as the crabcache goes down then submission of CRAB from the client fails. In principle this is not true for the REST interface since there are different crabserver backends and the CMSWEB deployment is done in such a way that at least one backend is always active.Oracle schema usually is updated upfront (say we add a column). Changes to the oracle schema are written hereby developers [https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/master/etc/updateOracle.sql![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/master/etc/updateOracle.sql) and are performed by a operator. Some type of schema changes need to be performed after the development, and in this case developers needs to make sure the REST code is backward compatible and operators needs to test it (for example if we change the type of a column from VARCHAR to CLOB).The next piece of software that gets updated is the task worker. This is done by a operator. Usually the taskworker is shut down from the start to the end of the CMSWEB deployment. This is done as a precaution because new REST code might return data in a different new format that breaks old taskworker (usually "new REST/old TW" works, but developers do not guarantee this). Since the task worker is shut down before the CMSWEB deployment starts, there might be some tasks that are submitted with the "old client/old REST" that goes into the database and are processed by the "new REST/new TW code". Developers needs to take care of this case when they develop the code, and operators need to check things are not broken.The task worker deployment brings the new PJ and the new WN code. This does not mean that everything gets updated since only new task will use the new code! In the schedds and on the WN there are going to be that uses the old code. Again, developers needs to account for this use case when they develop the code and operators needs to check everything works fine.The clients gets updated after REST/TW, so the server side code needs to be backward compatible and work with the previous client version. When doing the validation operators needs to make sure that submission with the old client works.
ASO is also updated after REST/TW, and again we need to make sure that the old postjob running in the schedds writes documents that are well formed and does not break the new ASO code (or better, the new ASO code needs to be backward compatibile).
* Old PJ and old WN code: before the testbed deployment we send tasks that gets processed by old REST/old TW. should be long and so that PJ and WN code will run after the testbed deployment is done=>processed by the new code.
* Old REST (for submission)/new TW: again before the testbed deployment starts we should stop the TW and sent some tasks. These tasks will be processed when the testbed deployment is done and the new TW is switched on.
* Old client: when everything is done the operator needs to make sure the old client is working with the new code as well by sendind a task and checking the basic commands.
* Old ASO: make sure the old ASO code is working well with the new REST/PJ code.
* Old PJ/new ASO: this is because we will have old /PJ in the system that runs the old code and talks to ASO
notes: I don't think we need to go through this every deployment, but IMHO each month we need to evaluate what has changed in the code and decide which of these use cases needs to be checked by the operator.
# Notes about normal validation:
There is a test suite that sends different tasks with different parameters: [https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/tree/master/test/templates![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/tree/master/test/templates)To use it, copy the contents of the templates directory from the CRABServer repo to somewhere else, for example your workspace, where there is more space: `'/afs/cern.ch/work/e/erupeika/public/validationScripts'`
* TAG - refers to the HG tags found here [https://github.com/dmwm/deployment/releases![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/dmwm/deployment/releases) and should match the release that's being validated. This will appear in each task name of submitted tasks. It's cosmetic and only useful for reference when looking at the validation results.
* VERSION - Also cosmetic and appears in the task names, can be used to differentiate between multiple validation runs.
* WORK\_DIR - Where crab tasks, CMSSW and other things are stored, could look like this: `'/afs/cern.ch/work/e/erupeika/public/crabValidation/$TAG'`.
* MAIN\_DIR - should point to where your validation-args.sh, validation.sh and other files are located, for example `'/afs/cern.ch/work/e/erupeika/public/validationScripts'`.
* Sourcing the client - it's important to use the correct version of the client for the validation, that can be done by setting the environment variable CRAB\_SOURCE\_SCRIPT to point to `'/cvmfs/cms.cern.ch//crab_pre_standalone.sh'`. When sourcing the client using the light script ='/cvmfs/cms.cern.ch//crab\_pre.sh', it will use crab\_pre\_standalone.sh instead of crab\_standalone.sh, the latter being incorrect.
* STORAGE\_SITE, INSTANCE - self-explanatory but should also be modified accordingly.
There is also a script to test the client commands, called client\_validation.sh. It sources the pre-prod client and goes through most of the commands using all of the available parameters for the latest task. Some commands/options aren't tested by the script at the moment, like `--dryrun` and proceed, resubmit, , purge, kill, and should be tested by hand.what different validation templates areIn principle as a general coverage we should test every command with every parameter for eac tasks, but that's basically impossible (unless we automate it). The best thing to do is to check each command on a subset of meaningful tasks. However there are some commands that can only be tested once:
* checkusername
* checkwrite
* proceed
* purge
* remake
* tasks
while the other commands should probably be checked for different types of tasks. For example they can be run on the Analysis plugin vs [PrivateMC](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/PrivateMC?topicparent=CMSPublic.Crab3Validation;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it."), os using the userinputfile feature, it really depends on what changed in the code. The list of other commands is:
* kill
* resubmit
* report
* status
* submit
# Validation tasks
These are (more or less) the tasks that currently make up the monthly general release validation. Some of them were made to test specific bugs or features but are not very useful past the initial release.The plan is to narrow down the amount of tasks submitted every month to around ~10 while still covering most of the critical functionality in . The rest of the tasks could prove useful in specific cases so they are also worth keeping around. Finally, I intend to start running two extra tasks each validation by hand: one to publish a dataset in , and another one to analyze it (and also publish the result). This should help ASO.

### Notes
* Things like 'L-T\_O-T\_P-T\_IL-T\_DOC-F' at the end of the tasknames specify various flags with which tasks can be submitted. The validation script currently tries out some combinations of these flags, however, our opinion with is that none of them are useful enough for the general validation. For reference, the flags that can be switched on or off in the current validation script are:
  + transferLogs
  + transferOutputs
  + publication
  + ignoreLocality
  + disableAutomaticOutputCollection (Before, every task was duplicated with this flag switched on and off which doubled the amount of validation tasks I've described above.)
* There exists three templates for LHE use-cases ([PrivateMC](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/PrivateMC?topicparent=CMSPublic.Crab3Validation;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.")\_for\_LHE.py, [PrivateMC](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/PrivateMC?topicparent=CMSPublic.Crab3Validation;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.")\_for\_LHE\_NOLS.py, [PrivateMC](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/PrivateMC?topicparent=CMSPublic.Crab3Validation;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.")\_for\_LHE\_pythia.py) which use a custom input file 'dynlo.lhe' and 'lhe' or 'pythia' splitting modes but I never got them to work and I don't really know how they're different from normal tasks. I am assuming they shouldn't be run every month and we continue to keep them around just in case.
* There exists a skimming task template, 'Skimming\_dataset\_lumi\_based.py'. It uses a special 'skimming\_dataset.py' PSet. This task works fine but I am assuming that it does not need to be run every month, especially if the only thing that's different is the PSet.
* There are two templates which try to use a voGroup (specifically, 'becms' and 'escms') but I don't know how to submit them. I'm also assuming that the functionality itself is working fine and they can be skipped for the monthly validation.
### Summary
* My proposal is to keep / create one task for each of the most critical features / use cases. Such tasks in my opinion would be:
  + Analysis with a parent dataset, [LumiBased](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/LumiBased?topicparent=CMSPublic.Crab3Validation;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") splitting
  + Analysis with a secondary dataset, [LumiBased](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/LumiBased?topicparent=CMSPublic.Crab3Validation;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") splitting
  + Analysis on a custom list of input files, [LumiBased](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/LumiBased?topicparent=CMSPublic.Crab3Validation;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") splitting
  + Analysis on data with a Lumimask and runrange applied, [LumiBased](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/LumiBased?topicparent=CMSPublic.Crab3Validation;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") splitting
  + Analysis on data, [FileBased](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/FileBased?topicparent=CMSPublic.Crab3Validation;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") splitting
  + Analysis on data, [EventAware](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/EventAware?topicparent=CMSPublic.Crab3Validation;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") splitting
  + A [PrivateMC](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/PrivateMC?topicparent=CMSPublic.Crab3Validation;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") task to generate and publish a dataset in
  + Analysis on the dataset from the previous task, [LumiBased](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/LumiBased?topicparent=CMSPublic.Crab3Validation;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") splitting
  + [PrivateMC](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/PrivateMC?topicparent=CMSPublic.Crab3Validation;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") using the 'remote' stageout option (other tasks would use the default 'local' stageout)
  + [PrivateMC](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/PrivateMC?topicparent=CMSPublic.Crab3Validation;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") using 8 cores
  + Analysis using old CMSSW ( CMSSW\_5\_3\_22 )
  + A task that is similar to [HammerClouds](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/HammerClouds?topicparent=CMSPublic.Crab3Validation;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it."), analysis on a [GenericTTBar](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/GenericTTBar?topicparent=CMSPublic.Crab3Validation;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") dataset, extraJDL = ['+CRAB\_JobReleaseTimeout=300', '+CRAB\_NoWNStageout=1', '+CRAB\_HC=True', 'accounting\_group=production', 'accounting\_group\_user=cmsdataops']

# CRAB Asynchronous Stage Out using Rucio
##
## Introduction:
This guide provides basic information and practical guidelines for leveraging Rucio for stage out within CRAB (CMS Remote Analysis Builder). Utilizing Rucio for stage out in CRAB can greatly improve data management during physics analyses.Before proceeding, if you never heard about Rucio, we highly suggest you check its Twiki page:. There, you can find a ['s Guide](CMS.RucioBeginnersGuide "'s Guide") and all the information you might need to manage [your rules](RucioUserDocsRules "manage your rules"), [quota](RucioUserDocsQuotas "quota") and [data](RucioUserDocsData "data").To use Rucio for Stage Out you might need to know:
* **How to use Rucio for stage out:** to enable Rucio for stage out (let Rucio transfer your files) insert "/rucio" in the destination Logical File Name (LFN) (destination file path). To know the LFN allowed see , see also <https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/RucioUserDocsData>.
* **How the Stage out process with CRAB works:** during the execution of a CRAB job, application output files are copied, as usual, from the [/bin/edit/CMSPublic/WorkerNode?topicparent=CMSPublic.CrabASOwithRucio;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") where they run to the local temporary/scratch area "/store/user/temp". This temporary area is known to Rucio as the *Temporary Replica Storage Element* (Temp\_RSE).
* **What happens with post-processing of CRAB jobs:** after the files are copied to the temporary directory, the post-processing of CRAB jobs will add the names of these files to the container, register the local instance in "/store/user/temp" as a file replica in Rucio, and create a Rucio rule. The rule will direct Rucio to replicate the files to the destination storage indicated in the file and keep them forever.
**Note** Rucio has a very nice web page at [https://cms-rucio-webui.cern.ch/![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cms-rucio-webui.cern.ch/) to show status of replication for a given rule. Your task may result in only one rule or multiple ones, so it is not know a-priori if this is something worth starting with. If you want to look, use your X509 certificate to login. A direct link to you favorite rule has the format [https://cms-rucio-webui.cern.ch/rule?rule\_id=9e4a7ac9a4e34c9ca8eba30f9fc9829b![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cms-rucio-webui.cern.ch/rule?rule_id=9e4a7ac9a4e34c9ca8eba30f9fc9829b) where you should replace the long hex string with your rule ID from the first columsn in rucio list-rules.
## Knowing what's going on
When using Rucio for stage out, crab status will print 2 extra lines as in this example as soon as the first job completes, so that user can check on stageout progress.
```
:  user.belforte:/GenericTTbar/belforte-crab_20221014_190156-94ba0e06145abd65ccb1d21786dc7e1d/USER
Tips on how to check on  at https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/CRAB3FAQ#Stageout_with_Rucio
```
The second one simply points to this twiki. The first one reports the name of the (dataset in DBS language) which contains all output files belonging to this task.

##
## Useful Rucio commands
Below are the most useful commands which can be used to check on the contrainer status, content and replication progress.
```
    rucio-list-files  <containername> : lists all file names (LFNs) in the container
    rucio list-content <containername> : shows the datasets/blocks in the contrainer
    rucio list-dataset-replicas <containername> : show replica summary for each dataset/block
    rucio list-rules <containername> : for advanced use, main point is that rules id are needed to delete rules and free disk space
```

# How to deal with GITHUB for CRAB
```
# update your local repository:
git pull --rebase upstream master
# update my remote fork fork to the upstream master discarding any local change:
 cd /tmp/belforte
 git clone :dmwm/CRABServer.git
 cd CRABServer/
 git push --force :belforte/CRABServer.git
# update my local repository
 cd <directory-of-the-local-clone-of-my-fork>
 git checkout --force origin/master
:
The setup should be like this (pseudo-code)
git clone github/belforte/crab (is now called “origin”)
git add remote upstream github/dmwm/crab (is now called upstream)
Then when your repository is out of date with the central:
git checkout master
git fetch upstream            # fetch commits history
git fetch --tags upstream     # also the tags (need two commands)
git merge upstream master     # merge upstream on your local
git push  origin              # move those changes up
git push --tags origin        # also the tags
To develop something (version 1)
git checkout master # start with latest master
git checkout -b my_feature # checkout and start a new branch
git push --set-upstream origin my_feature # track new branch in your github
# [code]
git commit -m “My feature is awesome”
git push origin # put on your github
Then visit github and make a pull request.
To develop something (version 2)
git checkout master
git checkout -b my_feature
# code
git commit -m “My feature is awesome”
git push origin my_feature  # i.e. use the name of the branch
Then visit github and make a pull request.
You’ll notice in my schemed your changes follow this route:
begin on local branch
pushed to remote branch
pulled/merged onto upstream (DMWM repo) by
only arrive on your local master with the merge of upstream/master
then pushed to your github master
 repository locale master branch e' pieno di schifezze e voglio
resettarlo.
1. sistemo il master in origin come scritto all'inizio di questo file
2. forzo il mio master locale con git reset --hard origin/master
vedi: http://stackoverflow.com/questions/1125968/force-git-to-overwrite-local-files-on-pull
per fare una PR per un branch specific, e.g. per 1.1.0_crab in WWCore, :
git checkout crab-branch (or git checkout --track upstream/crab-branch if you don't have crab-branch already)
git checkout -b crab_version_of_feature
git cherry-pick [commit number(s) for feature from master branch]
git push
Now go to GitHub and create a pull request but use the dropdown members to request it be merged on crab-branch instead of master
from
git pull
or
git pull origin crab_branch
before creating the new feature branch.
and
 I suggest you to always start with the master PR, such that you can wait for jenkins to finish to check whether your PR is "sane" and doesn't fail unit tests. Once you're sure it's fine, you can cherry-pick it in the crab branch.
```
