title: RucioGeneralQuestions < CMSPublic < TWiki
body:
-   Introduction
-   How do I make a transfer request?!?!
-   Full Rucio documentation
-   What naming conventions must be used?
-   Is it possible to download a file in Rucio?
-   How can I get the ids of the rules that apply on a file?
-   Will DBS stop being used?
-   How does Rucio know lfn to pfn mapping and how do I publish the update of lfn to pfn mapping?
-   Is Rucio DB filled properly? Rucio and PhEDEx datasvc results are different
-   Are the transfer and deletion log files for Rucio accessible?
-   How does Rucio transfers verify the sanity of transfers? Is it the FTS that does it?
-   How I can modify which FTS Server to Use?
-   Are there any consistency checks for site admins to ensure that numbers are == with local storage?
-   Can the user be assigned to a group 'local' - which means quota is for all local users?
-   Are there any alarms sent to administrators once ~95% of quota usage is reached on one or another quota?
-   How I can set production quota and does it also consider files in /store/unmerged or is a separate quota?
-   How would it work with local user jobs?
-   Is there a way in Rucio to say - never ever do not store any MINIAOD at a specific site and that there is a virtual storage (does not mean that file is present, like xrootd cache) on that specific site.
-   If sites create a rule for the SAM dataset, will Rucio automatically trigger the transfer? Do they have to do anything else?
-   If a site has some missing files, should they delete the rest and re-transfer the entire container or should they only ask for the specific files/datasets?
-   Do files need to be deleted before at the site (in case of corrupted files, etc.)?
-   Can site admins/execs invalidate files themselves?
-   Which certificates will be used by Rucio when replacing Phedex agents? How sites can obtain it?
-   When should I use the CLI and when should I use the python API?

###  Introduction

 To set up rucio and to see example commands, you can check out: https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin/view/CMSPublic/WorkBookFileTransfer. Here, please place any question you might have about Rucio.

###  How do I make a transfer request?!?!

 You don't. Instead you make a rule. See RucioUserDocsRules for more details.

###  Full Rucio documentation

 There is full Rucio documentation available online at https://rucio.cern.ch/documentation/ In particular:

-  https://rucio.cern.ch/documentation/user/using_the_client for CLI usage
-  https://rucio.cern.ch/documentation/html/client_api/accountclient.html for python programmers

###  What naming conventions must be used?

 We have tried to keep Rucio to the same naming conventions used in DBS and the rest of our software. In other words:

-  CMS dataset name and Rucio container names are of form /AlphaNumeric/AlphaNumeric/ALPHABETIC
-  Block names are [container name]#AlphaNumeric
-  File names for users are /store/user/rucio/[USERNAME]/path/to/file.ext

 The actual rules are a little looser as underscores, dashes, and periods are allowed in some contexts, but if you stick to the above, you will be fine.

###  Is it possible to download a file in Rucio?

 See RucioUserDocsLocation

###  How can I get the ids of the rules that apply on a file?

 Please follow an example in GetRuleId.

###  Will DBS stop being used?

 No

###  How does Rucio know lfn to pfn mapping and how do I publish the update of lfn to pfn mapping?

 The trivial file catalog (TFC) that a site specifies in their SITECONF storage.xml is synchronized from PhEDEx into the Rucio RSE definition once per day. In the future, we will move to pulling storage.json from gitlab, so sites are strongly encouraged to make sure the files in PhEDEx and gitlab agree.

###  Is Rucio DB filled properly? Rucio and PhEDEx datasvc results are different

 The reality is that PhEDEx is constantly moving data, and the one-way PhEDEx ->Rucio synchronization is not instantaneous. Some temporary discrepancies will exist.

###  Are the transfer and deletion log files for Rucio accessible?

 As was the case with PhEDEx, ultimately all actual transfers are made with FTS. Rucio keeps track of the FTS transfer IDs that are shown when querying stuck rules. In addition, a high-level overview is available via MONIT infrastructure, e.g. transfer rates and logs in kibana. Also, rucio digests the FTS errors and presents an alternative log [https://monit-kibana.cern.ch/kibana/goto/50ed95d9ea92a0c6516e2ef5f7c2e98d][here]]. Deletion logs are also available in the latter link.

###  How does Rucio transfers verify the sanity of transfers? Is it the FTS that does it?

 FTS is responsible for verifying the transfer was successful and the destination checksum matches both the source and the catalog.

###  How I can modify which FTS Server to Use?

 As of now, there is only the possibility to specify one FTS server per destination RSE. Once storage.json is fully deployed, the setting will be taken from there.

###  Are there any consistency checks for site admins to ensure that numbers are == with local storage?

 A full site to catalog consistency check is being developed for Rucio. It will use xrootd to list the contents of the site storage and compare to the catalog to ensure consistency.

###  Can the user be assigned to a group 'local' - which means quota is for all local users?

 At present, the quota mechanism can target one rucio account at a time. Accounts can be created for users or groups. A shared group "RSE_user" could be made and the appropriate user identities could be attached, such that they share a quota. We are working on a mechanism to use e-groups + CRIC to automate this.

###  Are there any alarms sent to administrators once ~95% of quota usage is reached on one or another quota?

 We can investigate such an alarm

###  How I can set production quota and does it also consider files in /store/unmerged or is a separate quota?

 In the current scheme, /store/unmerged is not managed by rucio. For the remainder, it is part of the DDM quota and the relative share is managed by central operations as needed.

###  How would it work with local user jobs?

 %GREY% Local users have access to a dedicated local queue and they store the same files under the same storage bypassing CRAB and Production.Questions are: How do these files need to be registered in Rucio? Do they need to store under /store/temp and let Rucio to handle transfer from /store/temp/user to /store/user? Or they can manually publish specific Rucio block, like copying himself directly to /store/user? Or does it mean that local users should not have delete/write access on the Site storage? - This seems will not work with Analysis Facilities and needs a solution

 In summary, user files that are managed by Rucio are stored in /store/user/rucio/, which will have local permissions identical to /store/mc or the other global namespace prefixes (see DMWMPG_Namespace for details). As such, there is no conflict with users who only have permissions to /store/user/. When a user injects data they hand over unix permissions to Rucio, at which point they must interact with Rucio to transfer or delete data. Of course, a user can opt-out of this by simply continuing to write to /store/user/ as they do now.

###  Is there a way in Rucio to say - never ever do not store any MINIAOD at a specific site and that there is a virtual storage (does not mean that file is present, like xrootd cache) on that specific site.

 We have not explored site-admin controlled restrictions on DDM space. There is a concept of cache RSEs where Rucio is aware of but does not control the presence of replicas.

###  If sites create a rule for the SAM dataset, will Rucio automatically trigger the transfer? Do they have to do anything else?

 If a site creates a rule, Rucio would start the transfer of the files automatically unless there is some issue. Admins should keep track of the transfer and open a ticket in case they see something is wrong.

###  If a site has some missing files, should they delete the rest and re-transfer the entire container or should they only ask for the specific files/datasets?

 If the admin suspects his/her site has missing or corrupted files, they should open a ticket for Transfer Team. Transfer team will just locally invalidate the files if they have replicas somewhere else, and they will get re-transferred. No need of delete the whole dataset or container.

###  Do files need to be deleted before at the site (in case of corrupted files, etc.)?

 No need to delete, as long as it is a disk site the file will be overwritten by the FTS transfer (corrupt tape site copies would need to be deleted though).

###  Can site admins/execs invalidate files themselves?

 File invalidation at their own sites is now possible. Site admins can follow the procedure described in DMOps docs. The responsibility to ensure files are not wrongly marked corrupted falls on site admins. If the number of invalid files is greater than 10K please create a ticket with CMS Data Management to follow through with the procedure as most probably global invalidation and reporting will be involved.

 For managing SAM dataset rules, perhaps a facilities-shared account is a good solution, otherwise, transfer_ops can make the rule. High-watermark deletions only apply to data not protected by rules, so as long as a rule is active the data will stay.

###  Which certificates will be used by Rucio when replacing Phedex agents? How sites can obtain it?

 Rucio writes data to sites using DN:

```
/DC=ch/DC=cern/OU=Organic Units/OU=Users/CN=cmsrucio/CN=779320/CN=Robot: CMS Rucio Data Transfer

```

 and FQAN:

```
/cms/Role=production/Capability=NULL
/cms/Role=NULL/Capability=NULL
/cms/uscms/Role=NULL/Capability=NULL

```

 Sites should have no need for a certificate because there is no site-resident daemon to run. Sites should ensure that the local account the above certificate maps to has permission via srm/gsiftp/davs/etc. to write and delete all subdirectories of /store listed as "production" in DMWMPG_Namespace

###  When should I use the CLI and when should I use the python API?

 The CLI is designed to be used for one-off operations and it is generally inadvisable to use it in anything load-bearing or for a large looping bash script. Each time the CLI is called it creates a new instance of the client, which can increase run time. If you need to do complicated operations, the python API is encouraged, but a bash script can be used. If you are already writing a python script never call the CLI from the script, this will balloon the run time.

title: The only required part from CRAB to trigger rucio transfer is "/store/user/rucio/"

If you are experiencing TWiki instability from outside the CERN network, please connect via the CERN internal network - see [KB0010688![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cern.service-now.com/service-portal?id=KB0010688) for details

* [Introduction](#Introduction)
* [CRAB output](#CRAB_output)
* [Rucio upload](#Rucio_upload)
### Introduction
Users are allowed to catalog their own data in the Rucio system, and transfer it between sites for which they have quota.
A user's data namespace is separate from the CMS namespace (`cms` scope) and prefixed by their personal scope (e.g. user jdoe has scope `user.jdoe`).
There are various mechanisms for users to inject data into the rucio system, as explained in this page.
### CRAB output
Before proceeding be sure to have requested a quota at your destination site, following this [guide](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/RucioUserDocsQuotas)It is possible to use this feature modifying the CRAB config as follows:
```
from CRABClient.UserUtilities import config, getUsernameFromCRIC
from WMCore.Configuration import Configuration
config = Configuration()
config.section_("General")
config.General.requestName = '<your task name>'
config.General.transferLogs=False
config.section_("JobType")
<your usual JobType section>
config.section_("Site")
<your usual Site section>
config.section_("Data")
<your usual Data section>
# The only required part from CRAB to trigger rucio transfer is "/store/user/rucio/"
# in the config.Data.outLFNDirBase
config.Data.outLFNDirBase = '/store/user/rucio/%s/<choose a folder name>' % (getUsernameFromCRIC())
config.Data.publication = False
# the name of your rucio dataset will be:
# <config.>/rucio/USER#000000
config. = 'NanoTestPost2'
```
### Rucio upload
There is also a direct rucio CLI command, `rucio upload`, which may be used. The exact details of its usage will be added soon.

title: RucioUserDocsLocation < CMSPublic < TWiki
body:
-   Introduction
-   DAS
-   AAA/XRootD
-   CRAB
-   Rucio Web UI
-   Rucio CLI
-   Download a file using rucio
-   LFN to PFN conversion

###  Introduction

 Here we explain the methods of locating and retrieving data with Rucio.

###  DAS

 DAS site ... queries will query Rucio and present results. This will be a transparent transition, although you will start to see the data source rucio displayed in some cases now.

###  AAA/XRootD

 Using redirectors to find data will not change at all, the XRootD system is independent of the data management system. For example, one can always use the global redirector to download a file, given an LFN (here with some debug info -d 1): xrdcp -d 1 -f root://cms-xrd-global.cern.ch/ /dev/null

###  CRAB

 All CMS managed data (cms scope) will continue to be accessible to CRAB without any user-facing changes. Users who wish to use their rucio-managed data (user.myname scope) as an input dataset in CRAB will be able to do so, although this feature is in progress.

###  Rucio Web UI

 The Rucio Web UI (https://cms-rucio-webui.cern.ch/) can be used to query Rucio. The search bar accepts DIDs (files, datasets, or containers) or rule IDs.

 Note: when searching a DID, the scope must be included. For most uses, this will typically be cms: followed by the DID. For example:

 A search for /ZZZ_TuneCP5_13TeV-amcatnlo-pythia8/RunIISummer20UL16NanoAODAPVv9-106X_mcRun2_asymptotic_preVFP_v11-v1/NANOAODSIM will return no result.

 However, a search for cms:/ZZZ_TuneCP5_13TeV-amcatnlo-pythia8/RunIISummer20UL16NanoAODAPVv9-106X_mcRun2_asymptotic_preVFP_v11-v1/NANOAODSIM will return a result for this container.

 NOTE: The Web UI searches for containers and datasets by default and excludes files. To search for files, then, click the search button while the field is empty. This will bring you to a page where you can set search criteria for container, dataset, container & dataset, and files. Choose the appropriate option, then execute the search as normal.

 When searching for a rule ID, a scope does not need to be included.

###  Rucio CLI

 Note: As of Rucio 36.0.0, a new CLI command format was introduced. Using the flag --legacy will force the old command format if necessary, and the pre-36 commands are listed here for continuity. As a rule of thumb, any EL8 and lower system uses Rucio <36.0.0 and EL9 systems use Rucio >=36.0.0. For simplicity, the newer version of commands will be referred to as "For EL9" and the older as "For EL8 and below".

 If you prefer to directly query Rucio (e.g. as a replacement for PhEDEx datasvc) the main entrypoints are the CLI commands list-dataset-replicas --deep and list-file-replicas. NB: there is currently a known issue with list-dataset-replicas that may return incorrect results (extraneous replicas) without the --deep flag, so for now it is recommended to always use this additional flag. An example of each is shown:

 For EL8 and Below

 Note that the CMS dataset (Rucio container) is expanded into each block in the result. To see what files are in a collection DID (container/dataset) one can do rucio list-files DID for EL9 and below, and rucio did content list DID for EL9.

###  Download a file using rucio

 To discover a PFN, given an RSE and LFN,

 EL8 and below

```
rucio list-file-replicas --pfn --expression [RSE] cms:[file DID]

```
 e.g.
```
$ rucio list-file-replicas --pfn --rse T2_DE_DESY cms:/store/mc/RunIIAutumn18NanoAODv5/DYJetsToLL_M-50_TuneCP5_13TeV-madgraphMLM-pythia8/NANOAODSIM/Nano1June2019_102X_upgrade2018_realistic_v19-v1/110000/A5702444-A58D-364F-BF6C-EF28C9C52344.root
srm://dcache-se-cms.desy.de:8443/srm/managerv2?SFN=/pnfs/desy.de/cms/tier2/store/mc/RunIIAutumn18NanoAODv5/DYJetsToLL_M-50_TuneCP5_13TeV-madgraphMLM-pythia8/NANOAODSIM/Nano1June2019_102X_upgrade2018_realistic_v19-v1/110000/A5702444-A58D-364F-BF6C-EF28C9C52344.root

```
 If the RSE supports multiple access protocols, a preferred protocol can be selected via the --protocol option in the above.
 EL9

```
rucio replica list file --pfns --rses [RSE] cms:[file DID]

```
 e.g.
```
$ rucio replica list file --pfns --rses T2_DE_DESY cms:/store/mc/RunIIAutumn18NanoAODv5/DYJetsToLL_M-50_TuneCP5_13TeV-madgraphMLM-pythia8/NANOAODSIM/Nano1June2019_102X_upgrade2018_realistic_v19-v1/110000/A5702444-A58D-364F-BF6C-EF28C9C52344.root
srm://dcache-se-cms.desy.de:8443/srm/managerv2?SFN=/pnfs/desy.de/cms/tier2/store/mc/RunIIAutumn18NanoAODv5/DYJetsToLL_M-50_TuneCP5_13TeV-madgraphMLM-pythia8/NANOAODSIM/Nano1June2019_102X_upgrade2018_realistic_v19-v1/110000/A5702444-A58D-364F-BF6C-EF28C9C52344.root

```
 If the RSE supports multiple access protocols, a preferred protocol can be selected via the --protocol option in the above.

###  LFN to PFN conversion

 For advanced users, there may be a desire to convert an LFN into the appropriate PFN for a given site, regardless of whether a replica actually exists (if a replica exists, it will be discoverable via the above methods). To do so, one can use the Rucio python API as in the following example:

```
$ python
>>> from rucio.client import Client
>>> client = Client()
>>> client.lfns2pfns("T2_US_Wisconsin_Test", ["user.jdoe:asdf.root"])
{u'user.jdoe:asdf.root': u'gsiftp://cms-lvs-gridftp.hep.wisc.edu:2811/hdfs/store/test/rucio/int/user/jdoe/asdf.root'}

```

title: RucioUserDocsQuotas
body:
If you are experiencing TWiki instability from outside the CERN network, please connect via the CERN internal network - see [KB0010688![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cern.service-now.com/service-portal?id=KB0010688) for details
>![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/web-bg-small.gif) [CMSPublic Web](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WebHome)>[WebPreferences](/twiki/bin//TWiki/WebPreferences)>[Rucio](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/Rucio)>[RucioUserDocsQuotas](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/RucioUserDocsQuotas "Topic revision: 8 (2026-02-11 - 23:24:17)") (2026-02-11, )[![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/uweb-o14.gif) Edit](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/RucioUserDocsQuotas?t=1777861268;nowysiwyg=1 "Edit this topic text")[Attach](/twiki/bin/attach/CMSPublic/RucioUserDocsQuotas "Attach an image or document to this topic")[PDF](/twiki/bin/genpdf/CMSPublic/RucioUserDocsQuotas "Create a PDF file for the topic")
* [Introduction](#Introduction)
* [Checking your quota](#Checking_your_quota)
* [Requesting a quota](#Requesting_a_quota)
* [Checking your usage](#Checking_your_usage)
* [Checking usage for a site for all users](#Checking_usage_for_a_site_for_al)
### Introduction
In Rucio, all data is managed or owned by Rucio. This means you use Rucio commands to move or cleanup data, even data that is "yours". You may have a quota at one or more RSEs (Rucio Storage Elements) and you can use this quota as you wish. If you want to make sure an official dataset stays at that site, you make a "rule" to ensure that it does. If you want a dataset that you created to be kept at an RSE, it's no different. That uses the same quota.**Note**: As of Rucio 36.0.0, a new CLI command format was introduced. Using the flag `--legacy` will force the old command format if necessary, and the pre-36 commands are listed here for continuity. As a rule of thumb, any EL8 and lower system uses Rucio <36.0.0 and EL9 systems use Rucio >=36.0.0. For simplicity, the newer version of commands will be referred to as "For EL9" and the older as "For EL8 and below".
### Checking your quota
The Rucio Web UI also allows you to check your quota at each site where you might have one. Either navigate to “Account Usage” under the “Monitoring” tab or use the link: ([https://cms-rucio-webui.cern.ch/account\_rse\_usage![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cms-rucio-webui.cern.ch/account_rse_usage)). This page will list each RSE where the account has a quota or has used space, how much of that space is still available, and the number of files located at that RSE associated with your account.You can list your quota at all sites via the command `-account-limits $`. For example, if you have no quota yet, the command will return:
```
$ -account-limits $
+------------+------------+
| RSE        | LIMIT      |
|------------+------------|
+------------+------------+
+------------------+---------+
| RSE EXPRESSION   | LIMIT   |
|------------------+---------|
+------------------+---------+
```
There are two tables here, the first shows the limit per [RSE![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://rucio.cern.ch/documentation/started/concepts/rucio_storage_element) (a CMS storage site) and the second shows the quota over an [RSE Expression![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://rucio.cern.ch/documentation/started/concepts/rse_expressions), which may match multiple sites. The latter is less common.Here is an example of the result if a quota is available:
```
$ -account-limits $
+----------------------+------------+
| RSE                  | LIMIT      |
|----------------------+------------|
| T1_US_FNAL_Disk      | 100.000 GB |
| T1_US_FNAL_Disk_Test | 100.000 GB |
+----------------------+------------+
+------------------+---------+
| RSE EXPRESSION   | LIMIT   |
|------------------+---------|
+------------------+---------+
```
This is showing a quota of 100 GB at the `T1_US_FNAL_Disk` RSE as well as the `T1_US_FNAL_Disk_Test` RSE.
You can use this quota to store your own data (produced with CRAB) or make sure that experiment data is kept at a site of your choosing.**EL9**
Please use the command `rucio account limit list -a $`. This command also shows the usage and quota left.
### Requesting a quota
NOTE: It is not possible to get a Rucio user quota at T2\_CH\_CERN. Please create a JIRA ticket under the CMSTRANSF project ([https://its.cern.ch/jira/projects/CMSTRANSF/issues/CMSTRANSF-166?filter=allopenissues![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://its.cern.ch/jira/projects/CMSTRANSF/issues/CMSTRANSF-166?filter=allopenissues)) if you think your data needs to be at CERN, indicating which data, why, and for how long.If you do not have quota in the right place (or enough), you should ask for a quota increase at the RSE you would like to use.
To find out who to ask, you can query the RSE attributes to identify the accounts responsible for managing quota. Below is an example:
```
$ -rse-attributes
:         True
cms_type:           real
country:            IT
fts:                https://fts3.cern.ch:8446
lfn2pfn_algorithm:  cmstfc
pnn:
quota_approvers:    calabria,donvito,lecriste
rule_approvers:     calabria,donvito,lecriste
tier:               2
```
The usernames are CERN accounts and can be queried via the usual methods, e.g. [https://phonebook.cern.ch/phonebook/![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://phonebook.cern.ch/phonebook/)
Contact one of the people listed as "quota\_approvers" to grant or increase your quota on a site.**EL9**
Please use the command `rucio rse attribute list $`
### Checking your usage
NOTE: You can only check your own rucio usage with the command `-account-usage` or when using the Web UI.
```
$ -account-usage $
+---------------+----------+------------+--------------+
| RSE           | USAGE    | LIMIT      | QUOTA LEFT   |
|---------------+----------+------------+--------------|
| T3_US_FNALLPC | 3.000 TB | 10.000 TB | 7.000 TB    |
+---------------+----------+------------+--------------+
+------------------+---------+---------+--------------+
| RSE EXPRESSION   | USAGE   | LIMIT   | QUOTA LEFT   |
|------------------+---------+---------+--------------|
+------------------+---------+---------+--------------+
```
**EL9**
Please use the command `rucio account limit list -a $`
### Checking usage for a site for all users
This command lists rucio usage for all users for a particular rucio resource (site)**EL8 and below**
```
-rse-usage --show-accounts T3_US_FNALLPC
```
**EL9**
```
rucio rse show --rse T3_US_FNALLPC
```

body:
If you are experiencing TWiki instability from outside the CERN network, please connect via the CERN internal network - see [KB0010688![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cern.service-now.com/service-portal?id=KB0010688) for details
>![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/web-bg-small.gif) [CMSPublic Web](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WebHome)>[WebPreferences](/twiki/bin//TWiki/WebPreferences)>[Rucio](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/Rucio)>[RucioUserDocsRules](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/RucioUserDocsRules "Topic revision: 13 (2026-02-16 - 22:06:07)") (2026-02-16, )[![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/uweb-o14.gif) Edit](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/RucioUserDocsRules?t=1777861345;nowysiwyg=1 "Edit this topic text")[Attach](/twiki/bin/attach/CMSPublic/RucioUserDocsRules "Attach an image or document to this topic")[PDF](/twiki/bin/genpdf/CMSPublic/RucioUserDocsRules "Create a PDF file for the topic")
* [Introduction](#Introduction)
* [Creating a rule](#Creating_a_rule)
* [ rules](#Querying_rules)
* [Removing rules](#Removing_rules)
### Introduction
In Rucio, the location of file replicas on RSEs (Rucio storage elements, i.e. CMS site storage) is controlled via [rules![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://rucio.cern.ch/documentation/replica_management/).
Please take some time to familiarize yourself with the rule concept as introduced in the aforementioned link before continuing. In short, if you want to ensure some data is available at a specific location, make a rule.NOTE: If your datasets are very large, you may not have enough quota under your personal Rucio account. In this case, you need to notify the Data Management team with a new JIRA ticket [https://its.cern.ch/jira/projects/CMSTRANSF/issues/CMSTRANSF-471?filter=allopenissues![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://its.cern.ch/jira/projects/CMSTRANSF/issues/CMSTRANSF-471?filter=allopenissues), stating explicitly which data you want to be where and for how long.
### Creating a rule
To make a basic rule to copy a CMS dataset or block to a specific site, the easiest method is to use the Rucio Web UI via the “ New Rule” option under the “Data Transfers” tab![search_bar](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/pub/CMSPublic/RucioUserDocsRules/Screen_Shot_2022-04-10_at_9.13.37_PM.png)or using this link: ([https://cms-rucio-webui.cern.ch/r2d2/![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cms-rucio-webui.cern.ch/r2d2/)). The UI will have you fill out each field in order to create a rule, namely:
* The DID for which you are trying to create a rule (either a container or dataset). The scope must precede the name of the DID (usually this will be “cms:”). The Web UI includes the option to create a rule for several DIDs at once; to do this, choose the “List of DIDs” option before entering a DID name.
* Choosing the RSE the rule shall be associated with. The system will check the storage available to your account at the specified RSE. If you do not have any available quota, you can choose the "I want to ask for approval" option to create the rule and alert the site admin.
* All extra options, e.g., lifetime, number of copies, and whether the rule shall be created asynchronously.
To create a rule using the CLI, follow the template below:**Note**: As of Rucio 36.0.0, a new CLI command format was introduced. Using the flag `--legacy` will force the old command format if necessary, and the pre-36 commands are listed here for continuity. As a rule of thumb, any EL8 and lower system uses Rucio <36.0.0 and EL9 systems use Rucio >=36.0.0. For simplicity, the newer version of commands will be referred to as "For EL9" and the older as "For EL8 and below".For EL8 and below:
`rucio add-rule cms:/CMS/DATA/SET/NAME 1 T2_MY_SITE` or `rucio add-rule cms:/CMS/DATA/SET/NAME#BLOCK-NAME 1 T2_MY_SITE`For EL9:
`rucio rule add cms:/CMS/DATA/SET/NAME --copies 1 --rses T2_MY_SITE` or `rucio rule add cms:/CMS/DATA/SET/NAME#BLOCK-NAME --copies 1 --rses T2_MY_SITE`Keep in mind the 'cms:' is required, this is what Rucio calls a 'scope'. All centrally produced CMS data is in the 'cms' scope. Also note that what CMS calls a block, Rucio calls a 'DATASET' and what CMS calls a dataset, Rucio calls a 'CONTAINER'. If dataset is huge please add `--asynchronous` it will allows create rule asynchronously.
Rucio rules are very flexible, so `rucio add-rule --help` will give you more information on what can be done.
This command returns a unique rule ID which you can save and reference later to query the status of a rule.If you do not have a quota, or you have reached your quota limit, you can exceptionally make a rule ** which notifies the site administrator of your  and allows them to approve the rule irrespective of your quota. To do this, add the option '--ask-approval' to the 'add-rule' command above, e.g.For EL8 and below:
`rucio add-rule --ask-approval cms:/CMS/DATA/SET/NAME 1 T2_MY_SITE`For EL9:
`rucio rule add --ask-approval cms:/CMS/DATA/SET/NAME --copies 1 --rses T2_MY_SITE`Your  is more likely to be approved if you also specify a `--lifetime` (in seconds; for reference, 30 days is 2592000 seconds) that you require the data to be protected by the rule, as this lets site administrators know how long the data will occupy space at their site.If you have a rule holding data at a given location, it will not disappear from that location. If you don't have a rule, but data presently exists at some location, there is no guarantee it will stay. Each rule you make contributes to your account's RSE usage, *regardless of whether or not the data is protected by other rules*, so you should be sure to  enough quota to hold all your rules or make each rule with --ask-approval and a --lifetime.
###  rules
* `rucio list-rules --account $RUCIO_ACCOUNT` List all the rules you have and their state. : `rucio rule list --account $RUCIO_ACCOUNT`.
* `rucio rule-info [RULE_HASH]` monitor the progress of your rule and any transfers it may have initiated. : `rucio rule show [RULE HASH]`.
* Using the Web UI, a rule can be queried directly using rule ID, returning info equivalent to the rule-info function. To check your own rules, navigate to the “List my rules” section under the “Data Transfer” tab.
### Removing rules
If you created a rule with an explicit lifetime, it will automatically get cleaned up after it expires. If you created a rule without a lifetime, you may explicitly delete it via the command `rucio rule remove [RULE_HASH]` (or `rucio delete-rule [RULE_HASH]` for EL8 and below). When you delete the rule, your quota will be returned. The data replica may or may not be deleted from the site, depending on the actual storage usage at the site and any other users' rules that apply to the same data at the same site.

## Goals of this page
This page describes how to use the language to create configuration files.For an introductory discussion of configuration files, see the page [WorkBookConfigFileIntro](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookConfigFileIntro). (It covers some topics not covered here, so it might be a good idea to read or skim that before or after reading this page.)
## Introduction
A *configuration document*, written using the language, is used to the *cmsRun* executable. A configuration program specifies which , inputs, outputs and services are to be loaded during execution, how to these and services, and in what order to execute them. It is a file which can be self-contained, or can read in any number of external configuration fragments using 's standard `import` statement. Here is an illustration of the structure of a configuration file:
```
# Import CMS  class definitions such as Process, Source, and EDProducer
import FWCore.ParameterSet. as cms
# Import contents of a file
import Foo.Bar.somefile_cff
# Set up a process, named RECO in this case
process = cms.Process("RECO")
#  the object that reads the input file
process.source = cms.Source("PoolSource",
    fileNames = cms.untracked.vstring("test.root")
)
#  an object that produces a new data object
process.tracker = cms.EDProducer("TrackFinderProducer")
#  the object that writes an output file
process.out = cms.OutputModule("PoolOutputModule",
    fileName = cms.untracked.("test2.root")
)
# Add the contents of Foo.Bar.somefile_cff to the process
# Note that more commonly in CMS, we call process.load(Foo.Bar.somefile_cff)
# which both performs the import and calls extend.
process.extend(Foo.Bar.somefile_cff)
#  a  and endpath to run the producer and output
process.p = cms.(process.tracker)
process.ep = cms.EndPath(process.out)
```
There must be exactly one `cms.Process` with the name `process` in a top level configuration file.

## and SCRAM
To make objects in your files visible to other files, the other files need to import your files. For the import to succeed your files first need to be put in your package's  directory, or a subdirectory of . Then, you need to run `scram build` once in your area, to initialize the symbolic links. You only need to build once. If later you change your file, you won't need to re-build.Many types of objects (e.g. EDProducers) can have a function called fillDescriptions defined in their C++ class. This function specifies which parameters are allowed to exist in the configurations and other things like default values. If this function has been defined for a C++ class, it can trigger automatic generation of the cfi file for of that class. The automatic generation is part of the build that executes when the command `scram build` is given. The automatically generated cfi files are stored in the `cfipython` subdirectory of a CMSSW working area instead of the `src` subdirectory. ## Objects
A configuration program is structured as a hierarchy of *objects*, nested or adjacent with respect to each other. Each object specifies a recognizable component or feature of the *cmsRun* program. Each object is given a name which is used to refer to it
in the code. In CMS we often call those names "labels". Each object has a type. Not all, but many types can
be configured by a and store that . And frequently, a particular object will correspond to one
C++ class that is related but not the same as the type. Commonly, an object definition looks like this:
```
aLabel = pythonType("ClassName",
    aParameterName = anotherPythonType(constructor arguments)
    # more  definitions
    ...
)
```
Below is an example where the label is `VtxSmeared`, the type is
`cms.EDProducer`, and the C++ class name is `VertexGenerator`.
The example also shows that comments may be added within a block's
scope using "#" where the comment continues to the end of the line.
It is clearest to each on a separate line in your configuration file.
```
VtxSmeared = cms.EDProducer("VertexGenerator",
    # Setting parameters:  <-- First comment
    MeanX = cms.double(0.),
    MeanY = cms.double(0.),
    MeanZ = cms.double(0.),
    # Second comment
    SigmaX = cms.double(0.015),
    ),
    SigmaZ = cms.double(53.0)  # in  (as in COBRA/OSCAR) <-- Third comment
)
```
### Labelled vs Unlabelled Objects
I considered deleting this section from the documentation because the terms described here are not often used, but I left it here because there are some obscure places in the code and documentation where you might run into the terms 'Labelled' and 'Unlabelled'.In CMS, a 'label' is the attribute name used in the process to refer to an object. When the process load function or the process extend function is used to attach objects to the process, the label is the same as the variable name assigned to refer to the object (and because they are usually the same that name is often called the label as well). In configurations, every object attached to the process has a label. So the terms 'Labelled' and 'Unlabelled' are really misnomers that have a historical origin. Before 2008, CMS did not use the language for configurations and in the language we used before , some objects attached to the process really did not have labels. These types of objects were called 'Unlabelled' and even now there remains some subtle differences in how these are handled internally (for backward compatibility reasons that are now ancient). Currently in a configuration, an 'Unlabelled' object is one that has a certain label and in some cases the object is required to always have that label. Here are some examples:
* A source must have the label 'source'
* A service must have a label matching its C++ type name
* An ESProducer or ESSource is considered 'Unlabelled' if and only if it has the same label as its type name, although they are allowed to have an arbitrary labels
Most other types are 'Labelable'. The example in the previous section shows a 'Labeled' object. Here is an example
of an 'Unlabelled' object.
```
process.source = cms.Source("PoolSource",
    #  declarations
    ...
)
```
The label of a 'Labelled' object can have an arbitrary value, except that it must be unique within the scope of the process.
### The Process Object
The top-level item of a configuration program is a `Process` object. Each configuration program must have a `Process` object assigned to a variable named `process`. This `process` variable refers to a `Process` object which aggregates all the configuration information for the *cmsRun* executable. The Process object must be named by passing the name as the first argument to the Process class' constructor. This name gets carried along with the output data and is used as a part of the branch name to distinguish between otherwise similar objects in a given event.
```
process = cms.")
```
Official production processes have a standard set of process names which
they use which include but are not limited to the following:
* SIM
* HLT
* RECO
* PAT
User processes are free to select their own process names. Common choices
include TEST and USER. A history of processes which have added data
to the Events, Runs, and LuminosityBlocks is recorded in the output files. New
processes must have names different from all the names in the process history.
### Attribute Declarations for the Process Object
Inside the `process` object there must be exactly one object assigned that has type Source and is used for data input. There may be zero or more objects for each of many other types. In the official production configurations there can be hundreds or even thousands of objects attached to the process. Your job is configured by your choice of objects to construct and attach to the process, and by the configuration of each object. (This may be done via ["import"](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideAboutPythonConfigFile#TheImportStatment) statements or calls to the load function, instead of or in addition to object construction.) Some of the types that may be used to create these objects are listed below:
`Source` object
:   Defines the data input source for the cmsRun executable; i.e., where the data comes from. There must be exactly one and it must be assigned the label `source`. Configured with a C++ type name and for each object.
`EDProducer`, `EDFilter`, `` or `OutputModule` objects
:   The four types are collectively refered to as ''s. Each of the four types corresponds to a specific C++ base class. Configured with a C++ type name and for each object. The C++ type must inherit from the corresponding C++ base class.
`EDAlias` objects
:   Allows mapping of an `EDProducer` from its given label to one or more different labels. Also allows multiple `EDProducers` to share the same label. This is useful for making multiple jobs with different configurations to appear to make the same Event products.
`Service` object
:   Invoke services. They must be assigned to a label which matches their C++ class name. Configured with a C++ type name and for each object.
`PSet` objects
:   sets.
`VPSet` objects
:   vectors of sets.
`SecSource` objects
:   secondary data input source, used only with "mixing " and are typically included as a in the of a mixing instead of being attached directly to the process. Configured with a C++ type name and for each object.
`ESSource` objects
:   Grab information from an external input source, e.g., the calibration database, an xml file, etc. Configured with a C++ type name and for each object.
`ESProducer` objects
:   Describe environmental quantities, e.g., ambient temperature, magnetic field, and so on. Configured with a C++ type name and for each object.
definitions
:   ordered groups of , giving each group a name that may be used in other sequences, paths, or endpaths.
`Task` definitions (in releases that support [Tasks](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideAboutPythonConfigFile#TaskDescription))
:   groups of EDProducers and EDFilters to be run in unscheduled mode. which EDProducers, ESSources, and Services are enabled.
definitions
:   Specify groups of to execute in the order given.
`EndPath` definitions
:   groups of to run, in the order given, after all other named `paths` have been run.
definitions
:   the group of paths and end paths to run. Can be 0 or 1 of these and it must be labelled

### Parameters without defaults
types can be specified without declaring a particular default value using the modifier `required` , `optional` , and `obsolete` . A sample could be
```
import FWCore.ParameterSet. as cms
value = cms.PSet( min = cms.required.int32,
                  ,
                  vebosity = cms.optional.untracked. )
```
Where
* `required` : if the has not been set, an exception will be thrown.
* `optional` : if the is missing, it will not be passed to the C++ code.
* `obsolete` : the (whether set or not) will never be passed to the C++ code.
For `PSet` types, the special `PSetTemplate` keyword can be used to specify not only that a `PSet` is the type but also what are the allowed, or default, parameters within that PSet. The values can be specified by assigning the to a dictionary containing all or some of the parameters which were declared.
```
import FWCore.ParameterSet. as cms
value = cms.PSet( constraints = cms.optional.PSetTemplate(
                          min = cms.required.int32,
                          ),
                  values = cms.required.PSetTemplate(
                          x = cms.required.float
                          y = cms.optional.float)
        )
value.constraints = dict(min = 5,  = 10)
value.values = dict(x=7)
```
```
import FWCore.ParameterSet. as cms
value = cms.PSet( allowAnyLabel_ = cms.required.int32)
value.foo = 5
value.bar = 10
```
### Processing Component Objects
There are four types of dynamically loadable processing components (in addition to the source type which provides the event to be processed). These are known as "". As mentioned above,
* "" is a generic name for 4 types of "workers" (C++ base classes): EDProducer, EDFilter, , and OutputModule.
* Zero or more labelled  blocks can be assigned to a `Process` object.
* The C++ classes that go here would be subclasses of any of the worker base classes.
The component types are:
Producer
:   Based on the EDProducer class; creates new data to be placed in the Event
Filter
:   Based on the EDFilter class; decides if processing should continue on a for an Event
Analyzer
:   Based on the  class; studies properties of the Event
OutputModule
:   Stores the data from the Event
The label given to a may be used elsewhere in the configuration, (e.g., in ,  and *endpath* specifications).For example,:
```
process.filter = cms.EDFilter("PythiaFilter",
    MinMuonPt = cms.untracked.double(20.)
)
process.out = cms.OutputModule("PoolOutputModule",
    fileName = cms.untracked.("mcpool.root"),
    SelectEvents = cms.untracked.PSet(
        SelectEvents = cms.vstring("p")
    )
)
process.p = cms.(process.filter)
process.e = cms.EndPath(process.out)
```
### Service Objects
A service is a facility that performs a well-defined task that is globally acessible and that does not affect physics results. Any number of *services* can be attached to a `Process` object, although only one for each C++ type.This example shows the form of the service object:
```
process.RandomNumberGeneratorService = cms.Service("RandomNumberGeneratorService",
    externalLHEProducer = cms.PSet(
        initialSeed = ),
        engineName = cms.untracked.('HepJamesRandom')
    )
)
```
RandomNumberGeneratorService is the name of the C++ class of the *service* the program will use and also must be the label. The specific parameters required are determined by the class used.An alternative way to a service and attach it to the process follows.
It has the advantage that it sets the label automatically for you. This only
works for services.
```
process.add_( cms.Service("RandomNumberGeneratorService",
        externalLHEProducer = cms.PSet(
            initialSeed = ),
            engineName = cms.untracked.('HepJamesRandom')
        )
    )
)
```

A PSet can be nested inside another PSet. sets are used to a list of parameters. A PSet attached to the Process can be shared by multiple , i.e. can be used to multiple . ### Vector (VPSet) Objects
A vector, VPSet, is a vector (a list) of PSets.     ) ,
    ...

        ... #  declarations for vector entry _n_
    )
)

### EventRange, LuminosityBlockRange, VEventRange, VLuminosityBlockRange objects
These types are used to describe ranges of luminosity sections and events within runs. Both types follow the same syntax which is easiest to explain by looking at the text representation: `cms.EventRange("1:1-5:6")` which is the range begining with event (or lumi) number 1 of run 1 and continuing to event number 6 in run 5. You can also represent this as `cms.EventRange(1, 1, 5, 6)`. The text form also takes a pair of wild-card like options, so `cms.EventRange("1:min-5:")` represents the event number 1 of run 1 through the last event of run 5. This is represented as `cms.EventRange(1, 1, 5, 0)` as well (0 is invalid as a run, event, or lumi section, so we use it as a wildcard).You can also supply vectors of range objects in a VEventRange or VLuminosityBlockRange objects that look like this: `cms.VEventRange("1:2-3:4", "5:MIN-7:")`.The vector forms of these types are used to specify lumis or events to process or skip in the PoolInputSource configuration for CMSSW releases > 3\_0\_0.In release 3\_9\_0 and later, an EventRange may optionally specify luminosity block numbers, in this representation: `cms.EventRange("1:1:1-5:4:6")`. If this form is used, events are ordered by run number, luminosity block number, and event number, in that order of significance. In contrast, if luminosity block numbers are not used, as in: `cms.EventRange("1:1-5:6")`, luminosity block numbers are ignored in determining the range,
If given EventRange specifies a luminosity block number, it must specify it for both ends of the range. However, a given VEventRange may include both types of EventRange.

Note: The initial focus of migrating to use Task has been on EDProducers and

#### Similarities Between Tasks and Sequences
In many ways, Tasks have been implemented to behave like
Sequences. For example, many of the functions in the Task and
classes are named and behave similarly (e.g. replace, dumpPython).
If one uses a visitor on a , , or EndPath, it will
also visit the associated Tasks and one can visit a Task in a
way similar to visiting a . When a attribute
of the process is replaced, the side effects on the Tasks and
Sequences are similar. There are other similarities. The design
intent was that except where necessary, the behavior of Tasks
and Sequences should be the same.There is another similarity between Sequences and Tasks. In the early
stages of a cmsRun job, the configuration is imported and many
manipulations can occur in . But when that is done, there is a point
where the data structures are converted into C++ classes and
passed into the C++ part of cmsRun. During this conversion, both
Tasks and Sequences are eliminated entirely. There is no C++ Task
type. EDProducers and EDFilters that are not run in the ordered
of a or EndPath and not run in unscheduled mode are simply not
defined at all in the C++ ParameterSet. Similarly, Sequences are
expanded away and do not exist in the C++ ParameterSet.
#### Task Design Comments
There is a function with the name convertToUnscheduled.
When run on a configuration, this function first resolves any
SequencePlaceholder objects. Then it removes EDProducers
from Paths and EndPaths and places them on a Task that is
associated with the . It does the same thing for
EDFilters whose filter result is ignored.At the time Task was designed, production processes relied
heavily on the convertToUnscheduled function to run processes
in unscheduled mode. One of the major motivations for the
introduction of the Task class was to make it easier to gradually
migrate away from convertToUnscheduled by using Tasks.
One goal is to eventually eliminate the need for that function entirely.
(Before the implementation of Task, unscheduled were
configured in a different way and the conversion function was also
different. It was difficult to combine configuration fragments
which used unscheduled mode with configuration fragments
that did not and this was making it difficult to incrementally
migrate to configurations explicitly using unscheduled mode.)In the pull request that included the initial implementation of
the top level . This was simply an expedient to move
the development forward faster and also because the code
was implemented by someone who is not an expert in the PAT
code (which was almost the only area whose configurations
were explicitly written to run in unscheduled mode prior to that
pull request). This was not intended to be a pattern to follow.
The intent of the design was that experts will identify which
EDProducers are needed with which sequences and associate
Tasks with the specific Sequences where they are needed.
This will improve the performance and reduce memory usage
of cmsRun by allowing the C++ part of it to only construct
EDProducers (and other types) that are needed instead of
constructing everything defined in the configuration.
### EDAlias
EDAlias allows mapping of an `EDProducer` from its given label (the label the process object uses to refer to it) to one or more different labels which can be used in getByLabel or consumes function calls. Also allows multiple `EDProducers` to share the same label. This is useful for making multiple jobs with different configurations to appear to make the same Event products.The label assigned to the EDAlias is the new label that can be used to lookup the data item. The EDAlias parameters accepted by an EDAlias are of the form
```
   <old  label> = cms.VPSet( cms.PSet( type = cms.(<friendly class name>),
                                            [fromProductInstance = cms.(<old product instance name>)],
                                            [toProductInstance = cms.(<new product instance name>)] ))
```
Where
* `<old label>` is the EDProducer's label from which the data originally derived.
* `<friendly class name>` specifies exactly what class type is to be obtained from the original EDProducer. The name is not the C++ class name and is instead the name used when specifying what data should be stored in the OutputModule. This name also corresponds to the first part of the TBranch name. One can also find the friendly class names of collections available in a job by adding the  to the job.
  + Starting from CMSSW\_11\_2\_0\_pre6 the `type` field can be given a wildcard `'*'` that matches all data product types that also match `fromProductInstance`. An EDAlias is allowed to have many `<old label>` VPSets with wildcards in the `type` field as long as the matched data products have different (type, instance label) pairs.
* `<old product instance name>` specifies the product instance name used by the EDProducer when storing the data product. By default EDProducer's use an empty . If `fromProductInstance` is not specified, the value of `<old product instance name>` defaults to `'*'` and therefore matches all data products of type `<friendly class name>` produced by the Producer with label `<old label>`.
* `<new product instance name>` specifies a product instance name different from the original one used by the EDProducer. If `toProductInstance` is not specified, `<new product instance name>` defaults to the value `'*'` which means the new name should match the old name.
Here is an example where we want to be able to get the data product `Bars` from label `otherbar` but using the label `bar`
```
bar = cms.EDAlias( otherbar = cms.VPSet( cms.PSet(type=cms.('Bars') ) ) )
```
Say the `otherbar` makes two data products of different types `Bars` and `BarExtras`. Then if we want to be able to get both by the label `bar`
```
bar = cms.EDAlias( otherbar = cms.VPSet( cms.PSet(type=cms.('Bars') ),
                                         cms.PSet(type=cms.('BarExtras') ) ) )
```
If you want to make data coming from two different , `foo` and `fee`, appear to come from one , `bar`, where `foo` makes data of type  and `fee` makes data of type `Fees`
```
bar = cms.EDAlias( foo = cms.VPSet( cms.PSet(type=cms.('') ) ),
                   fee = cms.VPSet( cms.PSet(type=cms.('Fees') ) ) )
```
If you want to make data coming from two different , `foo` and `fee`, appear to come from one , `bar`, where both create the same type, `Bars`. If both use the default product instance name then you will need to assign at least one of them to a different instance name.
```
bar = cms.EDAlias( foo = cms.VPSet( cms.PSet(type=cms.('Bars') ) ),
                   fee = cms.VPSet( cms.PSet(type=cms.('Bars'),
                                             fromProductInstance = cms.(''),
                                             toProductInstance = cms.('refined') ) ) )
```
If you want to to data products, of type `Fees` and  coming from one , `bar`, appear to come from two different then you can use two EDAlias both of which refer to the same EDProducer.
```
foo = cms.EDAlias(bar = cms.VPSet( cms.PSet(type=cms.(''))))
fee = cms.EDALias(bar = cms.VPSet( cms.PSet(type=cms.('Fees'))))
```
It is also possible to alias all data products of an EDProducer (since CMSSW\_11\_2\_0\_pre6) with the syntax below. This feature is likely useful only in conjunction with [SwitchProducer](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/SwitchProducer?topicparent=CMSPublic.SWGuideAboutPythonConfigFile;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.").
```
foo = cms.EDAlias(bar = cms.EDAlias.allProducts())
```

### The `import` statement
The standard *import* statement is used to inject the objects from another file into the current file, therefore it can be used to include shared-use configuration fragments. The *import* statements may be "nested", meaning that a configuration document may import a fragment which itself imports another fragment. There is no limit (other than that caused by memory exhaustion) on the number of levels of inclusion allowed. Here is an example:
```
import FWCore..printContent_cfi
```
In the above example, `FWCore` is the subsystem,  is the package, and  is the filename. Note that in the import statement the suffix `.py` of the filename is left out and directories are separated with a "." instead of "/". This is standard . In CMSSW, the environment is configured so that will look for imported files in two places. For example if the release is `CMSSW_8_1_0`, it will look for
```
CMSSW_8_1_0/src/FWCore///
```
Note that the directory named  is not included in the import statement. If and only if it fails to find the file there and if for example the current architecture is `slc6_amd64_gcc530`, then it will also look for
```
CMSSW_8_1_0/cfipython/slc6_amd64_gcc530/FWCore//
```
Automatically generated `cfi` files (discussed below) will be found in subdirectories of the `cfipython` directory.Use of *import* does not guarantee that the objects defined in the configuration file will actually be used to the job. In order to be used to a job, the objects must be attached to the `Process` object which is referenced by the `process` variable. The attachment can either be done for each object individually by assigning them to attributes of `process`, e.g.,
```
import Subsystem.Package.somemodule
process.somename = Subsystem.Package.somemodule.somename
```
or all the variables of a can be attached to a process by using the `extend()` member function
```
import Subsystem.Package.somemodule
process.extend(Subsystem.Package.somemodule)
```
When using 'extend' all the variable names used in the imported are assigned as the 'labels' for the process' attributes. Because the label assigned to a comes from the process attribute's name assigned to the object and not from the original variable to which the object was assigned, the individual object assignment method allows one to 'relabel' a to be different from the imported file
```
import Subsystem.Package.somemodule
process.someothername = Subsystem.Package.somemodule.somename
```
There are several alternative syntaxes for the import statement depending on how you wish to access the variables defined:
```
#must use full name to get to a variable
import Subsystem.package.filename
v = Subsystem.package.filename.variable
#must use short name to get to a variable
import Subsystem.package.filename as shortname
v = shortname.variable
#variable is added directly to this file
from Subsystem.package.filename import variable
p = variable
#all variables are added directly to this file
#deprecated by some because it might bring in too much
#but this is common in CMS configurations
from Subsystem.package.filename import *
p = variable
# Important convenience method to insert every cms object in the  into a process
# In the following example, the  is declared in the file
#     Configuration/StandardSequences//Analysis_cff.py
# Same as import followed by process.extend
process.load("Configuration.StandardSequences.Analysis_cff")
```
An important detail to add is that "import \*" and the process load and extend functions
do not import or attach variables that start with underscore "\_". If you do not want a
variable to be imported or attached to the process, then you can start its name with
an underscore and prevent that unless the name is explicitly used.
#### Blocking imports
```
import FWCore.ParameterSet. as cms
cms.checkImportPermission(allowedPatterns = ['','/Submodule'])
```
where the list can include any number of which are allowed to import the file. A user's top-level \_cfg.py is allowed, by default, to import such a file. This behavior can be changed by setting the value of minLevel = 1 as another to checkImportPermission()
## Including Standard definitions
Every configuration has a top level file called the `cfg` file. By convention its filename ends with the extension `_cfg.py`. This file may the entire configuration or it may include other configuration files by importing them.Configuration File Initializer files (`cfi` files) are used to initialize with all of their default settings. Each is supposed to have one, with the label the first part of its filename and the extension `_cfi.py` as the rest of the filename. This file is intended for use in end-users' `cfg` files; the user can then reset only the parameters that require non-default values. `cfi` files may also be imported into `cff` files.Configuration File Fragment files (`cff` files) are like `cfi` files, but are not associated with one-for-one. They are used to contain (or import) pieces of a configuration which may be either larger than `cfi` files (e.g. import multiple `cfi` files and Sequences and other objects) or smaller than `cfi` files (e.g. contain just one or a few specifications or a PSet). These files may also be included in `cfg` files. The file extension is `_cff.py`.
### For Component developers
The developer of a should make sure that a `cfi` file is available which can be imported. There are two ways to do this. The recommended method is to add a function to the C++ code of the called fillDescriptions. After this has been created, when `scram build` is run a `cfi` file will be automatically generated. There are several advantages to creating the `cfi` file this way. First, the `cfi` is automatically kept consistent with the C++ code. There is no need to remember to change the `cfi` file and less chance for an error to create an inconsistency. The fillDescriptions function is used to validate configurations. This validation can report mistakes, for example if a name was spelled incorrectly.
There is also an executable that will provide information about the possible parameters of which contain a fillDescriptions function, for example `edmPluginHelp -p`  or for brief output `edmPluginHelp -b -p` . This is described in detail here: [SWGuideConfigurationValidationAndHelp](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideConfigurationValidationAndHelp).See above for additional information about [importing files and file locations](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideAboutPythonConfigFile#The_import_statement).`cfi` files should be named
```
<moduleLabel>_cfi.py
```
Developers of ESSources and other components which have no labels should
use the full class name as the first part of the `cfi` file name.For example, the `FWCore/` package has a file named:
```
FWCore///
```
which contains:
```
import FWCore.ParameterSet. as cms
#print what data items are available in the Event
printContent = cms.("",
    #should we print data? (sets to 'true' if verboseForModuleLabels has entries)
    verbose = cms.untracked.(False),
    #how much to indent when printing verbosely
    verboseIndentation = cms.untracked.('  '),
    # used at the beginning of all output of this
    indentation = cms.untracked.('++'),
    #data from which  to print (all if empty)
    verboseForModuleLabels = cms.untracked.vstring(),
    # which data from which  should we get without printing
    getDataForModuleLabels = cms.untracked.vstring(),
    #should we get data? (sets to 'true' if getDataFormModuleLabels has entries)
    getData = cms.untracked.(False)
)
```
### For Component Users
Below is an example of a top level configuration that does not use a `cfi`.
This is an actual working example that you might find useful. It will print
out information about the content of a file named "test.root" (you can change
the filename if you would like). This is a nice way to write a very small
test configuration. It is particularly nice if you planned to manually edit the
parameters of the printContent . But this would be a horrible
approach that would be extremely difficult to develop or maintain
for complex configurations like the ones used in event generation,
```
import FWCore.ParameterSet. as cms
process = cms.Process("TEST")
process.source = cms.Source("PoolSource",
    fileNames = cms.untracked.vstring(
        'file:test.root'
    )
)
process.maxEvents = cms.untracked.PSet(
    input = cms.untracked.int32(1)
)
process.printContent = cms.',
  indentation = cms.untracked.('++'),
  verbose = cms.untracked.(False),
  verboseIndentation = cms.untracked.('  '),
  verboseForModuleLabels = cms.untracked.vstring(),
  getData = cms.untracked.(False),
  getDataForModuleLabels = cms.untracked.vstring(),
  listContent = cms.untracked.(True)
)
process. = cms.(process.printContent)
```
Below is an equivalent `cfg` file that imports a `cfi` file. Notice that
the parameters do not need to be repeated in the top level configuration.
The default values from the `cfi` file are used.
```
import FWCore.ParameterSet. as cms
from FWCore..printContent_cfi import printContent
process = cms.Process("TEST")
process.source = cms.Source("PoolSource",
    fileNames = cms.untracked.vstring(
        'file:test.root'
    )
)
process.maxEvents = cms.untracked.PSet(
    input = cms.untracked.int32(1)
)
process.printContent = printContent
process. = cms.(process.printContent)
```
##
There are many ways modify parameters and it depends on the situation which is best.
In this section, we discuss some of the situations and describe each.First consider the very simple test configuration presented at
the end of the preceding section. For example, if you wanted to change
the text used for indentation from '++' to '\*\*' you could do this:
```
...
from FWCore..printContent_cfi import printContent
...
process.printContent = printContent
process.printContent.indentation = '**'
...
```
You do not need to specify the type of the again because
that was already done in the `cfi` file.Replacement of more than one is allowed. For example,
```
from Configuration.Generator.SingleElectronPt10_pythia8_cfi import generator
generator.PGunParameters. = 5.0
generator.PGunParameters.MaxEta = 50.0
generator.PGunParameters.ParticleID = ( 211, 11 )
```
Multiple values in an object with mulitple parameters can be modified via the use of a `dict`
```
from Configuration.Generator.SingleElectronPt10_pythia8_cfi import generator
generator.PGunParameters = dict( = 5.0,
                                MaxEta = 50.0,
                                ParticleID = ( 211, 11 ) )
```
If there are additional parameters in the object which are not in the `dict` those parameters are not modified.Warning: If you wish to modify a vector and set it equal to a single-element array, then you must insert a comma
after that element:
```
generator.PGunParameters.ParticleID = ( 211, )
```
You may want to replace an entire `ParameterSet`:
```
generator.PGunParameters = cms.PSet(
    MaxPt = cms.double(100.01),
     = cms.double(9.99),
    ParticleID = (11),
    AddAntiParticle = cms.(True),
    MaxEta = cms.double(2.5),
    MaxPhi = cms.double(3.14159265359),
    MinEta = cms.double(-2.5),
    MinPhi = cms.double(-3.14159265359) ## in radians
)
```
All vector style parameters behave like normal lists and therefor allow `append`, `extend` and other list manipulations.The syntax is as follows:
```
a.composers.append("Beethoven")
a.painters.extend( ("Picasso", "da Vinci"))
```
Cloning is strongly recommended when you are developing a `cff` file that
might be used as part of a large complicated configuration. While creating
the clone, one or more parameters can be modified.The standard syntax for **cloning** is
```
from aPackage import oldName
newName = oldName.clone(changedParameter = 42)
```
or
```
from aPackage import oldName as _oldName
newName = _oldName.clone(changedParameter = 42)
```
The second form is better if the symbol oldName is not needed and
this occurs in a fragment that might be imported with the process
load function or a `from aModule import *` statement. Symbols starting
with an underscore are not imported in these cases.Starting from `CMSSW_12_0_0_pre2` the parameters to be changed can be passed in via a ParameterSet
```
from aPackage import oldName as _oldName
pset = cms.PSet(changedParameter = cms.int32(42))
newName = _oldName.clone(pset)
```
Giving two or more ParameterSet object arguments to `clone()` is allowed as long as the ParameterSets have distinct parameters, similar to EDModule constructors.Cloning is important because the object brought in by
an import statement is always the same object. If the same file
is imported in different `cff` files, the object referenced
is the same object. So if one `cff` file changes a value,
then all the referenced in all the `cff` files are affected.
This is very bad. But when a clone is made, the objects
and parameters inside them are distinct objects. When a
value is changed it only affects one instance of the .
In large complicated configurations, this is very important.There are different operating scenarios. There are many parameters
that must have different values in different operating scenarios.
These kind of modifications are handled by "Eras"
which are described here: [SWGuideCmsDriverEras](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideCmsDriverEras). "Eras"
should be used where appropriate instead of other
modification schemes. Before the "Eras" system was created,
customization functions were used. These were functions
that made large scale modifications to configurations to
accommodate different situations. Some still exist and are
effort to replace these with "Eras" or some other mechanism.
The customization functions tended to interfere with each other
when there was more than one, and also make the configuration
hard to understand and maintain.
##  and Paths
Sequences and paths have a "replace()" command, which lets you replace all occurences of a or a within a or with something else.
```
mySequence.replace(oldModule, )
myPath.replace(oldSequence, newSequence)
myPath.replace(oldModule, newSequence)
```
If you wish to replace a or a in a process, and
have the change propagated through to all sequences,
use
```
process.globalReplace("label", newObject)  # note the quotes!!
```
Warning: When replacing sequences or tasks you should use this with care if there are multiple calls to this or other similar functions that modify configurations. Some of these modifications can cause sequences and tasks to be expanded such that the or task no longer exists (although its contents are preserved in the object that contained the or task). Trying to replace one of these expanded sequences or tasks will not work.

## Passing Command Line Arguments Through cmsRun ![UPDATED](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/updated.gif "UPDATED")
Starting in CMSSW\_3\_0\_0, you will be able to pass
command-line arguments through to the system.
For example, if you start your job via this command
```
> cmsRun -m grid my_cfg.py myOpt myValue=True
```
```
import sys
print(sys.argv)
```
and see (starting from )
```
['my_cfg.py', 'myOpt', 'myValue=True']
```
Arguments beginning with '-' or '--' until the configuration file are handled by the C++ options parser in `cmsRun` (and are not visible in the ), and all other options that come after the file are used in . These additional options to file can also begin with '-' or '--'.
Show behavior before 13\_3\_0\_pre4 ![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/toggleopen-small.gif)  Hide behavior before 13\_3\_0\_pre4 ![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/toggleclose-small.gif)
In releases before 13\_3\_0\_pre4 the printout above includes `cmsRun` and its arguments.
```
['cmsRun', '-m', 'grid', 'my_cfg.py', 'myOpt', 'myValue=True']
```
Arguments beginning with '-' or '--' are handled by the C++ options parser in cmsRun, and other options which come after the file are used in . These additional options can begin with '-' or '--' if an unnamed '--' argument directly follows the file name.
### `argparse` (preferred) ![UPDATED](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/updated.gif "UPDATED")
The standard parser `argparse` can be loaded by doing
```
import argparse
```
To understand how to use it, please consult the standard documentation.Beginning from , only the arguments after the file are passed to , and therefore `argparse` can be used directly without any additional tricks
```
parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(...)
...
args = ()

Show behavior before 13\_3\_0\_pre4 ![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/toggleopen-small.gif)  Hide behavior before 13\_3\_0\_pre4 ![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/toggleclose-small.gif)
In releases before, `argparse` could be used with the following trick. To pass arguments unknown to `cmsRun` through `cmsRun` and to , you need to separate any `cmsRun` parameters from your personal parameters by using the unamed '--' argument directly after the script name. These additional parameters can be handled by `argparse` by removing the separating '--' and having `argparse` only handle only arguments it knows. The latter is needed since the arguments seen known by `cmsRun` are still in `sys.argv`
```
parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog=sys.argv[0],...)
...
argv = sys.argv[:]
if '--' in argv:
    argv.remove("--")
```
