This document describes how to use CRAB at CERN for direct submission to the batch system or CERN Analysis Facility (CAF). The responsable of CAF is .
Useful information of CAF can be found in the [CAF twiki page](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin//CMS/CAF).
### Prerequisites
* Dataset you want to access has to be available at the CAF, so it must be registered in the CAF DBS
* If you run on CAF, you have to be authorized to do so. In this page: <https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin//CMS/CAF#User_Permissions> you can find the sub-groups and the correspond leader. If you know your sub-group, you can contact the leader for the authorization.
* CRAB StandAlone (direct submission)
  + has to be submitted from an afs directory, from a node with access for exemple on lxplus
  + Since in this case you are effectively using CRAB as a convenience tool to do submission from your shell, you need to setup the environment as usual:
    - make sure you setup the environment in the following order \*
      ```
      1.source /afs/cern.ch/cms/LCG/LCG-2/UI/cms_ui_env.sh
      2. cmsenv
      3. source /afs/cern.ch/cms/ccs/wm/scripts/Crab/crab.sh
      ```
      * in the above replace `sh` with `csh` if you are using tcsh
  + Please note that you must be sure to have enough quota on your afs area. Large output should be put on castor (look at CAF stageout below)
  + Even if you decided to send the output to castor, the stdout/err and the Framework Job Report will be returned back to your afs area in any case.
  + Removes the requirement to use an AFS directory and a host with access, so can also submit from your desktop/laptop
### Running
The workflow is exactly the same of that you would follow to access data on the Grid (see: [CRAB Tutorial](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin//CMS/WorkBookCRABTutorial)). So you setup your CMSSW area, you develop your code, test it on a (small) part of a dataset and then you configure CRAB to create and submit identical to CAF to analyze the full Dataset.
In the crab.cfg configuration file, you have just to put under the `[CRAB]` section:
`scheduler = caf`
The available CAF queues are:cmscaf1nh
cmscaf1nd
cmscaf1nw
Running on the CAF, using `caf` as scheduler instead of , the longest queue will be selected automatically (cmscaf1nw).
If you need to select a different queue you can fill the parameter `queue` under the `[CAF]` section with either cmscaf1nh or cmscaf1nd (i.e. `queue = cmscaf1nh`).
If you know that your are short, it should be more efficient to use shorter queues.
### CAF stageout
If you are running at CAF then the required stageout configuration is:
* Stage out into CAF user area ( is the offical site name for CAF):
`[USER]`
`copy_data = 1`
`storage_element=T2_CH_CERN`
`user_remote_dir=xxx`
the path where data will be stored is /store/caf/user/<username>/<user\_remote\_dir>There is no support for staging out to the CAF-T1 from the GRID. The above instructions only apply for running on the CAF itself.Further details on CRAB and Stage out configurations available at [this page](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideCrabFaq#4_Stage_out_in_your_own_director).
### CAF publication
You need the following in crab configuration file:
* (NOTE: the storage element where the data are copied have to be ):
```
[USER]
copy_data = 1
storage_element=T2_CH_CERN
publish_data=1
publish_data_name = data-name-to-publish  (e.g. publish_data_name = JohnSmithTestDataVersion666 )
dbs_url_for_publication = https://cmsdbsprod.cern.ch:8443/cms_dbs_caf_analysis_01_writer/servlet/DBSServlet
```
The path where data will be stored is /store/caf/user/<username>/<primarydataset>/<publish\_data\_name>/<PSETHASH>

### Can this new very useful feature be added ? I have this nice idea on how to make Crab2 better, can it be done ?
Crab2 policy is simple: **no new features, only bugs critical for users or operations can be addressed**Offline froze Crab2 development in 2009,
putting all effort on new tools WMAgent and .
Since then only fixes critical for users or operations are being
[AnalysisOperations](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/AnalysisOperations?topicparent=CMSPublic.SWGuideCrabFaq;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it."), in this case Analysis Operations makes the judgment on wether
the gain in daily support effort from any given change is worth the cost.
Moreover supporting what we have is
work enough that we can't add anything that has a chance to
lead to mdrawore debugging/troubleshooting (which is why e.g. there
is no support for multicrab by Analysis Operations).So any (reasonable) need, can only be addressed by:
1. in due time
2. users writing their own small scripts to do what they want with crab output/log.
Users who go for 2. may benefit from using crab client xml report file rather then parsing stdout, see
[http://cmsdoc.cern.ch//ccs/wm/www/Crab/Docs/crab-v2.7.8.html#xml\_report![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmsdoc.cern.ch//ccs/wm/www/Crab/Docs/crab-v2.7.8.html#xml_report)
## Crab2 support policy
### What is supported in Crab2
Read the above FAQ about Crab2 development being frozen since long.
At this point (2011) developers only provide fixes for critical bugs
As of 2011 central support for Crab2 is only offered for mission critical funcionalities.
That means submission using `crab` command with:
* scheduler = glite, or caf
All other functionalities are distributed and available on an "as it is" basis. Users are free to use as long as they work for them. But support either for questions or bugs can only be offered by original developers in a best effort, voluntary basis.
### , local condor, condor\_g, , LSF
* local condor submission is supported only at FNAL LPC by local dedicated effort
* submission to local condor at other sites, to local , PBS and and to local LSF outside CERN is distributed in Crab2 on an as-it-is base. Those functionalities have been added via the work of interested local communities who are expected to care for keeping functionaties as operating systems and local scheduler and setup evolve
### Multicrab
* There is no support for multicrab or any other user-made wrapper around crab. Problems will only be addresses if the users can provide a procedure to reproduce them with simple crab commands.
## Prerequisites
### Get a certificate and the registration to VO
CRAB submits to the (LCG), so you need to run it from an User Interface, with a valid certificate, issued by your appropriate Certification Authority, and have a valid . You need also to be registered on VORMS server. To get a certificate from CERN CA and register to VO, you can find detailed instruction in the [SWGuideLcgAccess](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideLcgAccess) page. If you get a certificate from another Certification Authority, the procedure to register to VO with your certificate should be the same.
### Setup your certificate for LCG
See instructions in [this page](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookStartingGrid#ObtainingCert)
### Import the certificate into the browser
See [http://lcg.web.cern.ch/lcg/loading\_certifs.htm![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://lcg.web.cern.ch/lcg/loading_certifs.htm)
### Test your certificate
1. Is your personal certificate able to generate proxies? To find out, after having setup your environment run this command:
   ```
   --init - -verify
   ```
   In case of failure, the possible causes are:
   * the certificate/key pair is not installed in `$/.globus/usercert.pem $/.globus/userkey.pem` (a.k.a. "pem ")
   * the certificate has expired
   * the certificate and the private key do not matchIn the first case, you either do not have a certificate at all or have to install it on the UI; in the second case, you should get a new certificate; in the third case you probably have incorrectly installed your certificate.
2. Are you a member of the VO? To see if this is the case, you can execute this command:
   ```
   voms--init -voms
   ```
   If you get an , chances are that you did not register to the VO, or your registration expired. In this case, please follow the instructions in the [SWGuideLcgAccess](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideLcgAccess) page
3. You can verify the expiration date of your certificate with:
   ```
   openssl x509  -subject -dates -noout  -in $/.globus/usercert.pem
   ```
4. see also: <https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideVomsFAQ>
### Test the code locally
Before launching a million event analysis job on , be sure to test your code locally in a clean area.
1. Build a new CMSSW area (for example, CMSSW\_7\_4\_15\_...; pick as appropriate to your job):
   ```
   cmsrel CMSSW_7_4_15
   cd CMSSW_7_4_15/src
   cmsenv
   ```
2. -out from the cvs repository only the code or configuration you need to modify, and build your local libraries including your analysis code.
3. Make sure that the code you -out is compatible with the CMSSW version you are using.
4. Make sure that the CMSSW version you are using is compatible with the data you intend to read.
5. Prepare a test job accessing the data you will access in your job. There are several ways to read the proper data:
   * The easiest way is to use the xrootd service to read data directly from a remote site. How to do this is explained in [Using Xrootd Service for remote Data Accessing](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookXrootdService).
   * You can also use the xrootd service to copy a data file from a suitable dataset to your local machine (to work w/o network e.g.), as explained in [File download with command-line tools](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookXrootdService#DownCmd).
   * If no suitable exist, you can generate some events using the configuration file which is available from the [DAS![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cmsweb.cern.ch/das/) service.
6. Test your CMSSW configuration file locally in order to avoid problems with the ParameterSet parsing.
7. Run the job interactively (e.g. at CERN on lxplus):
   ```
   cmsRun your-pset-config-file.py
   ```
###  a CMSSW config file
In CRAB2, a user can  its CMSSW configuration file by launching `crab -validateCfg` after creating the task with `crab -create`. In this way the configuration file will be controlled and validated by a corresponding python API. Note that it is **not** enough to that the configuration file runs interactively, because in interactive mode CMSSW is too tolerant with python errors in that configuration file.
At times a user may worry that the is in CRAB or CRAB validation rather than in the configuration file; in this case, one can use the following test, which does not involve CRAB:
```
edmConfigHash your-pset-config-file.py
```
Note that this is needed, but not necessarely sufficient, to have a valid CMSSW configuration file.
Other could be related to some hidden charatecters (^M) in the configuration file, overall if it was downloaded from the web. To discover them you can use the command
```
cat -v your-pset-config-file.py
```
and remove them with the command
```
perl -pi -e 'tr/\cM//d;' your-pset-config-file.py
```
Then you can revalidate the configuration file again.

### How do I clean all my proxies
It may happen that in order to /fix some subtle Crab support asks you to delete all your proxies and start afresh. Or you may decide you simply want to try this.

##
### Should I use crab server or not ?
All CRAB server instances have been shut down. We suggest using `scheduler=remoteGlidein` instead.
### Which scheduler shall I use; glite or (or maybe something else)?
We recommend utilizing `scheduler=remoteGlidein`.If you want to google for more details on those two schedulers, use the strings "glite WMS" and "glideinWMS"
Both are supported and have relative strengths and weaknesses. We welcome users to try both and see what works best for you.
A quick summary of differences is:
* As of Crab 2\_8\_3 is also available without server using `scheduler=remoteGlidein` and `use_server=0`
* There may be difference in time-to-completion for your tasks (note that use of *may* vs *will* is intentional)
  + picks sites based on where run. Your may run sooner.
  + glite choice of submission site is based on information provided by the site's information system which may lead to unoptimal and possibly poor decisions. Your may run later.
* may need to be resubmitted by you more often when using glite
* With glite are sent immediately to some site, so you see that they are pending in local queue, with stay in global condor queue until they start and you do not know if it is because a site is busy or no site is matching or there is a
Other schedulers:CRAB also supports a few other schedulers, but these can only be used on certain systems and usually cannot be used with use\_server = 1
* caf: This is used only for submissions on the CERN CAF. You must have an acount on the CERN CAF to use it.
* condor\_g: This scheduler uses OSG tools to reach OSG sites. In practice this means it can only reach the FNAL Tier1 and the US Tier2/Tier3 sites. It has one less intermediate layer than glite and can be more reliable.
* condor: This submits to a local condor batch system. The main use for this is at the FNAL LPC CAF. You must have an account on the local system. This is usually very reliable as there is no intervening at all.
* and pbs: Like condor but for other batch systems. These modes are not supported either by or the core CRAB developers, so the status and deployment is unknown.
## remoteGlidein
### What is remoteGlidein scheduler and how it works ?
* It is the equivalent of direct submission to gLite.
* Job sandbox is copied to a remote submission host where the frontend (condor) runs and a remote condor\_submit command is issued.
* It is only a technical detail internal to Crab2 that we needed a new scheduler name instead of using scheduler=; use\_server=0
* Every crab command then issues a condor command via a remote ssh connection to the submission host, of course if remote host is down there is no access to job information, while will keep running.
* If you are used to gLite, think or remote submission host like a gLite WMS, only larger and (hopefully) faster and more solid.
* Each crab -status command will also push a new on the remote submission host for usage by the .

If you are using more than 50% of disk quota on the remoteGlidein servers, you will be notified with an email with the information of the server you have clean up. The moment you reach the quota, you will be unable to run and outputs from which complete may get lost. In order to avoid that, you have to clean up your directory at the server with following commands. If you do nothing, will be automatically deleted once 15-days old, but if you need space sooner, only you can decide what is to be kept and what can go. You need to know the name of the machine where you have disk , e.g. `submit-2.t2.ucsd.edu` or `vocms83.cern.ch`, this name will be in the mail that you receive.

## Running CRAB
### Disk space for output
Most problems in using Crab originates from the need to store output data . Usually users are faced with the of transferring a single output file from the WN where it is produced to some permanent space. Smaller help here. But there is also a with many small since in the end total disk space matters.
Normally output root are staged out to a Tier-2 site where a user has a space allocation. In the crab.cfg file, this is set in the USER section, for example, with:
```
return_data=0
copy_data = 1
storage_element = T2_US_UCSD
```
There also exists an option, to be used mainly for debugging a small number of , to send the output root back to the submission machine with `return_data=1`. This operation can concentrate an unknown amount of data in a single place (condor submitter or gLite WMS) which is dangerous. This is why size of the output each job can transfer in this way is limited.Be aware that with `return_data=1` output does not go directly from a remote WN to your desktop, but always goes through a buffer on some machine shared with others. Details and problems are different according to different schedulers:
#### remoteGlidein
(the recommended scheduler) outputs are initially sent to the submission server used for each task, i.e. the machine where condor schedd runs. Each user has a disk allocation of only 100GB on the servers. If this fill up, which is easy to do with this `return_data=1` and very large tasks, then all of the user's will fail from then on until space is cleared. from old tasks are removed automatically after not having been modified for two weeks. This is sufficient for normal usage with `copy_data=1`. Users who need to use `return_data=1` need to be careful and may have to remove outputs before the two weeks expiration following [these instructions](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideCrabFaq#How_to_clean_up_your_directory_i). We will try to notify by mail users who reach a high level of disk quota.
#### gLite
outputs are initially collected on a gLite WMS machine, those have usually a very limited disk space ) and are continously deleted as needed to keep disk occupancy arount 80%. There is no guranteed minimum time for which are kept, experience says that it is very unlikely to find output after one week.
#### condor/LSF/CAF/PBS/
here details are implementation dependent, may change from site to site, but usually outputs are directed immediately to your local directory and will simply fail if you fill your quota, see e.g. [this FAQ](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideCrabFaq#When_using_scheduler_condor_on_F)

* the CRAB -report option returns to the user the information about data analyzed by the task. The report analyzes the fjr returned by correctly finished (it means you can use this option only after the retrieval of outputs) and creates in the res dir of crab working dir, the file called containing the processed runs and luminosity sections. If the task was originally splitted by lumi, the option creates in the same directory other two : the inputLumiSummaryOfTask containing all the runs and lumis that the task had to analyze and the file containing the missing runs and lumis due to failed . ## crab.cfg questions
### Space at beginning of line in `crab.cfg`
Just don't do it. Do not put any white space at the beginning of line, otherwise, you will experience funny errors.
### Running over selected luminosity blocks: how and why to use the lumimask file
Datasets of real data can be splitted by run or lumi, not by event.
A luminosity section (aka lumisection, aka lumi, plural lumis) is a fixed range of time of a run of data acquisition (~90 sec) during which time the instantaneous Luminosity of LHC is assumed not to change.
The production data will contain one or many whole luminosity sections, a lumisection is never split among multiple .
A run is composed by many lumisection. In general not all the lumis are good data. Data quality is assessed by the DQM group which provides lumimask , each containing the list of valid run and lumisection for a certain data acquisition period. As not analysis are equal, quality criteria, and hence lumimask to use, may vary, please verify with your physic group what is most appropriae in your case.The lumimask is a text file in format (hence it has extentions `.`), whose content is like
{[run\_a:[lumisection\_x - lumisection\_y], [lumisection\_a, ]], [run\_b:[]......]}
```
{
"1": [[1, 33], [35, 35], [37, 47], [49, 75], [77, 130], [133, 136]],
"2": [[1,45],[50,80]]
}
```
Note that format dictactes the syntax in the file, unless you are an expert never edit this file
but always use proper tools to manipulate lumi lists in format.This file is the "filter" to select the valid data from a dataset.CRAB is able to use the lumimask file. If you add the lumimask file in your crab.cfg file
CRAB will create that only run on the data included in the valid ranges. In practice
the lumi list in the lumimask is ANDed with the lumi list from DBS to get a final list passed
to the CRAB splitting algorithm.
```
[CMSSW]
lumi_mask=Your_JSON_mask_file
total_number_of_lumis = N
lumis_per_job = M
number_of_jobs = L
datasetpath= Your/Dataset/Path
```
You can only specify 2 of the 3 settings total\_number\_of\_lumis, lumis\_per\_job, and  and you should remove any settings like total\_number\_of\_events and events\_per\_job. Also, be aware that CRAB will only use your "lumis\_per\_job" & "" as a suggestion. Each job will have at least M LS, but each job will process whole , so you may see something a little different than you expect. Your total task will run on either N or M\*L luminosity blocks depending on what you specify.The original lumimask can be manipulated by users, e.g. in order to take only a sub-part of it.In case of huge dataset, that could need a big crab task to be analyzed, the user can use the sub-lumimask to create different small tasks that analyze data from the same dataset. In this case the load of the "original" task will be splitted in subtask, each one of them using a different sub-lumimask file.
These tasks will analyze a sub-selection of data of the dataset.
The lumimask usage guarantes to analyze only different data without duplication.Link of official lumimask page:[https://-service-dqm.web.cern.ch/-service-dqm/CAF/certification/![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://-service-dqm.web.cern.ch/-service-dqm/CAF/certification/)
###
### About `se_white/black_list` vs `ce_white/black_list`
General rule: Always stick to se\_white/black\_list.
* ce\_white/black\_list only works for submissions using scheduler=glite (soon to be deprecated). Use it only if you know what you are doing and why.
The and CE b/w lists work pretty much the same way: white list means select those only,
black list means pick whatever you want except those.
The string in the b/w list is used as a filtering regular expression, and both host names (domains) or
site names are accepted. Hence you can use things like
```
se_white_list=infn.it   # run only at sites in infn.it domain
se_black_list=T3       # do not run at T3'1s
se_white_list=T1       # only run at T2's
se_white_list=T2_DE_DESY # only run there
se_black_list=.unl.edu # do not run at UNL (Nebraska)
```
This also means that you can only refine the list of 's which host the dataset selected in crab.cfg. You can not use SE\_white\_list to force to run at a site where data is not present.
### Force to one specific CE when using remoteglidein
When using remoteGlidein there is usually no reason to worry about CE's, sort of due to the way a pilot system is implemented, user see the WN's and which resources they connect to, not the middleware. Anyhow there are specific special cases where selecting only pilots sent to one particular CE is needed, in that case the [] part of crab.cfg needs to look like in this example:
```
 []
additional_jdl_parameters = +DESIRED_Gatekeepers="ce208.cern.ch:8443/cream-lsf-grid_cms"
data_location_override=None
```
this will remove matching based on site/ and will pick the execution CE you indicated. Note that full CE specification is needed and it must exactly match the string used in the factory. Also make sure not to have any black/white list. **Note**: this is a ugly hack. If you simply want to force an execution site, not a particular CE (gatekeeper), better use `se_white_list`, possibly in combination with `data_location_override`
### output and their automatic handling
CRAB handle only the output which is declared in `crab.cfg` So if you produce any output that you want back you have to declare it in `crab.cfg` (`[USER].output_file`).Eg. if your job produce a file named `summary.root` put:
```
output_file = summary.root
```
The job will run using the "normal" name, ie. summary.root; after the
job is done, it will be renamed taking into account the job number, and
CRAB will then take care to retrieve the renamed output, so you will get
many output like
```
summary_001.root, summary_002.root, summary_003.root ...
```
Starting from CRAB 26x, if a `PoolOutputModule` is present, namely if an [EDM](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/EDM) output file is produced, this file has to be added to the output to be handled (either explicitly, or via `[CMSSW].get_edm_output`). If not, CRAB will raise an and will not create . This is done to prevent user to produce potentially huge and useless output on the WN, which can give trouble to the WN themself.
## Guided tour of the crab task directory
crab creates a directory for every task on the local disk where you create your job.
The following will provide (hopefully) useful debugging info based on information that is in that directory.
```
job
log
res
share
```
The job directory contains the actual shell script (CMSSW.sh) that crab executes on the worker node.
This is probably only of academic interest.The log directory contains a log of all crab commands you executed for this task, as well as the return information you got.
This is quite useful when you are trying to understand what happens, and to proof it to somebody, e.g. crabFeedback list.
The share directory contains all the information that crab sends out on your behalf.
E.g., if you ever wonder what exactly job 85 was supposed to run on, you can look it up in share/arguments.xml .
This file contains the list of instructions of what each job is supposed to do. E.g., it allows you to run those last that
have not worked by hand after pulling the corresponding to your local disk using .FileMover.
The res directory contains all your stdout, stderr, and fjr after you do crab -get .

analysis can be run at over 50 Tier-2 centers and many Tier-3
sites world-wide. Each of these sites has its own requirements and
limitations on which run there, the most important of which are
limits on wallclock run time of the and resident memory usage. Only
some of these limits are published at this time, so it is not always
easy or even possible for a user to know what these limitations are
ahead of time.
#### glite scheduler
analysis submitted with the gLite scheduler will abort when
site limitations on run time or memory usage are exceeded.
####
The submission system matches user analysis to pilot
schedulers running at Tier-2 and Tier-3 sites that are hosting the
desired data set. The system has been configured to
maximize the chances of analysis job success by setting reasonable
limits that work at almost all sites:
* Wallclock time: can run for a maximum of 23 hours. Most Tier-2 sites have limitations of 24h maximum job run time.
* Memory: There is no explicit resident memory limitation on . However, most Tier-2 sites impose strict limitations on resident memory usage, as low as 1.6GB. If a job is re-queued after having failed at least once, and has an Image Size of greater than 2GB, the job will not be rescheduled, since presumably it was killed for excessive memory usage and will not run successfully if resubmitted.
Currently terminated by for those reason have  code `50117`
#### Recommendation
To make the most efficient use of Tier-2 resources and maximize the
chances of job success, whether they use gLite or submission,
analysis users are encouraged to tailor their so that:\* run for approximately 6 hours.\* use no more than 1.5GB of resident memory.
#### Next steps
In the future, we will work with sites that can allow larger limits
on wallclock time and memory and match those sites to pilots.

### My are running since long time
make sure you do not call running the time sometimes it takes to wait in local queue at a site before it starts running, which can change a lot totally outside of your control, and beware the time it may take (alas at times forever) to copy output file to remote storage element. Then of course sometimes something special/different happens. The previous FAQ tells you how to find more information about queued/running (when available).Let's make an attempt of explaining some of the delays you might experience:
* **Delays before a job starts running on a batch slot:**
  + When submitting via CRAB it offers you two schedulers "scheduler=glite" and "scheduler=". These two schedulers have two different scheduling philosophies. Let's assume your data is located at sites A,B,C, and you blacklisted site B. CRAB will thus consider sites A,C for running your . glite will pick the site less used (in some not optimal way), will submit what we call a "pilot" to both sites, and start your job at whichever site comes back first with a batch slot for you. I.e. in glite you queue up at the site, while in you queue up in the condor global pool.
  + Causes for delays:
    - if C is less used then A but A or C misreport their usage level, glite may pick A accidentally
    - If A is less used overall than C and your are sent to A but you personally have run at A a lot, and thus your "priority" in A's queue is low than you can get stuck at the site for a long time using glite, and you'd be better off using as scheduler.
    - If you have special privileges at A and C, e.g. because you are part of the Australian group and these two sites are in Australia where you have preferred CPU access to some part of these clusters, then you are probably better off using glite. as scheduler does not take those special privileges into account when submitting the pilot to the site.
* **Delays while running:**
  + a job can sometimes get stuck during reading or stageout. See entry [How can I tell what my are doing at a site ?](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin///SWGuideCrabFaq#How_can_I_tell_what_my_jobs_are) for more info. You're basically out of luck if this happens.

### Understanding crab\_fjr file
Sometimes it is useful to take a look at the "framework job report" (fjr) file that comes back for a job.
This file is the authoratative summary of what happened with your job.
It contains among many other things:
* the processed
* the output created, and the lnf where they were written
*  codes for cmssw as well as stageout
* The first line of the fjr file tells you if the job overall was successfull:
```
 < Status="Failed">
```
or
```
 < Status="Success">
```
* The second line of the fjr file is complete nonsense. It claims to give you the overall [ExitCode](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/ExitCode?topicparent=CMSPublic.SWGuideCrabFaq;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") but in fact is just plain nonsense.
* Instead, the real  codes are deep inside the fjr file:
```
        <FrameworkError ExitStatus="60303" Type="WrapperExitCode"/>
        <FrameworkError ExitStatus="0" Type="ExeExitCode"/>
```
The meaning of these  codes is explained [here](/twiki/bin///JobExitCodes)

### When I retrieve the root file from the sandbox it is always truncated at ~ 50 MB or I got the message: gzip: stdin: unexpected end of file
There is a limit of 50MB on the size of the output sanbox which is imposed by the policy. If your ouptut size will exeed this limit it will be truncated, and you will loose it. To avoid this is recommended to transfer the output directly to a .
### When using scheduler=condor on FNAL LPC I get crab: Output for job ... seems corrupted.
With local condor scheduler job output is sent directey to the user's work area even before crab -get is executed. This usually means that during job execution the user ran out of disk space (quota). Users should that, and verify what is actually there on `crab_0_.../res`, additional hints can be found in (if any) in `crab_0_.../share/.condor_temp` (note the dot `.` this is a hidden directory). In there you should also look at `CMSSW_xx.log` which have the details of the condor execution. If nothing helps, please contact LPC support since this is anyhow an LPC specific .
### When using scheduler=condor on FNAL LPC I get `macro SYSTEM_PERIODIC_REMOVE expression evalute to TRUE`
This usually happens toghether with the corrupted outut above and it is found in the `CMSSW_xx.log` file in `.condor_temp`. Typically the message is
```
009 (70734.046.000) 07/04 05:50:35 Job was aborted by the user.
        The system macro SYSTEM_PERIODIC_REMOVE expression '(JobStatus == 2 && JobUniverse == 5 && ((CurrentTime - EnteredCurrentStatus) > 86400*2)) || (JobRunCount > 10 || (JobStatus==5 && (CurrentTime - EnteredCurrentStatus) > 86400*7) || DiskUsage > 40000000 || ( (ImageSize > 3000000 && BigMemoryJob =!= TRUE) || ImageSize > 4000000 ))' evaluated to TRUE
```
In this case "user" means condor. Local scheduler aborted the because it exceeded one of the preset limits on DiskUsage, ImageSize or WallClockTime indicated, DiskUsage refers to disk space on the local WN, not on the stage out disk. In general the cure is to use smaller . The `.log` file reports periodically the [ImageSize](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/ImageSize?topicparent=CMSPublic.SWGuideCrabFaq;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") of the job, this can help you figure out if the [ImageSize](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/ImageSize?topicparent=CMSPublic.SWGuideCrabFaq;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") limit is the reason of the job termination.
To find specific reason one may also benefit from [ too![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cmsjobmon.fnal.gov/condor_t1/overview.html)l. Please contact LPC support for more details about policy for user at FNAL LPC and condor debugging tips.
## Stageout and publication
CRAB allows you to copy your analysis outputs directly to a Tier2 or Tier3 Storage Element.
You can decide to store them in a Storage Element of an "Official site" or in some of your
choosing. The difference between the two is technical, not political. "Official site" simply means a site
fully described in data transfer tool ().
If the target site has a working node connected to the stageout location, then the
site is listed in [SiteDB](/twiki/bin///SiteDB) and crab can discover all the details needed for the stageout from the site
name in the format `Tx_CC_SiteName`, where `x` is the tier number (usually 2 or 3)
and CC is the country code, e.g. `T2_IT_Pisa`, `T2_US_UCSD`, `T3_IT_Trieste` etc.
If the target Storage Element is not known to , you will have to indicate full contact details
in crab.cfgThe various options are:
#### 1. Stage out to an "official site" *without* publication in DBS
you have to configure the crab.cfg with:
```
     [USER]
     copy_data = 1
     storage_element = The  site name
     user_remote_dir = subdirectory where your output will be stored
```
* The site names are reported in the .SiteDB [list![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cmsweb.cern.ch/sitedb/sitelist/). The mapping between the StorageElement name and site names is reported [here![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cmsweb.cern.ch/sitedb/reports/showReport?reportid=se_cmsname_map.ini).
* The area in which your output file will be written is:
  ```
          site's endpoint +  /store/user/<username>/<user_remote_dir>/<output-file-name>
  ```
  where the site's endpoint is discovered by CRAB and your username is extracted form [SiteDB](/twiki/bin///SiteDB).
**Important Note**: you need to be registered in [SiteDB](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SiteDB). The instructions to register in [SiteDB](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SiteDB) are in: [SiteDBForCRAB](/twiki/bin///SiteDBForCRAB) .For example:
```
   storage_element = T2_ES_CIEMAT
   user_remote_dir = myTestDir
```
will write the output into:
```
   ://.ciemat.es:8443///ciemat.es/data//store/user/<username>/myTestDir/<output-file-name>
```
#### 2. Stage out to an "Official site" *with* publication in DBS
you have to configure the crab.cfg with:
```
    [USER]
    copy_data = 1
    storage_element = The official  site name
    publish_data=1
    publish_data_name = data name to publish
    dbs_url_for_publication = your local dbs_url
```
* The official site names are reported in the .SiteDB [list![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cmsweb.cern.ch/sitedb/sitelist/). The mapping between the StorageElement name and site names is reported [here![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cmsweb.cern.ch/sitedb/reports/showReport?reportid=se_cmsname_map.ini).
* The dbs\_url\_for\_publication is one of the physics analysis DBS instances (for example: [https://cmsdbsprod.cern.ch:8443/cms\_dbs\_ph\_analysis\_02\_writer/servlet/DBSServlet![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cmsdbsprod.cern.ch:8443/cms_dbs_ph_analysis_02_writer/servlet/DBSServlet)). You can find the appropriate URLs here: <https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin///DBSInstanceAccessList#Detailed_list_of_URLs_and_allowe>
* The directory and LFN of your output file are by default enforced to be:
```
      site's endpoint +  /store/user/<username>/<primarydataset>/<publish_data_name>/<PSETHASH>/<output_file_name>
```
where the site's endpoint is discovered by CRAB and your username is extracted form [SiteDB](/twiki/bin///SiteDB).In you need more information about publication as how to publish your data in a different directory i.e /store/group/groupname/.... please read the [SWGuideCrabForPublication](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideCrabForPublication).
#### 3. Stage out and publication to a "non Official site"
i.e. a Storage Element which is not a functioning endpoint.That means a site not included in the [SiteDB](/twiki/bin///SiteDB) *without* and *with* publication, you have to write in the crab.cfg:
```
    [USER]
    copy_data = 1
    storage_element = the complete Storage Element name
    storage_path= the full path of the Storage Element writeable by all
    user_remote_dir = the directory or tree of directories that !CRAB will create under the storage path of the .
```
where *storage\_path* is the mountpoint of the (i.e. ///psi.ch//trivcat)
and *user\_remote\_dir* is the directory or tree of directories that CRAB will create under the storage path of the (user\_remote\_dir=/store/user/). The user\_remote\_dir should start with "/store" since it's the LFN naming convention.Without the publication, the PFN and LFN are:
* PFN:
  ```
   storage_path/user_remote_dir/<output_file_name>
  ```
* LFN:
  ```
   user_remote_dir/<output_file_name>
  ```
With the publication CRAB will add to user\_remote\_dir the username, the primarydataset and the publish\_data\_name. The final PFN and LFN will be:
* PFN:
  ```
   storage_path/user_remote_dir/<username>/<primarydataset>/<publish_data_name>/<PSETHASH>/<output_file_name>
  ```
* LFN:
  ```
   user_remote_dir/<username>/<primarydataset>/<publish_data_name>/<PSETHASH>/<output_file_name>
  ```
It is user responsability to "create" the correct LFN using the correct user\_remote\_dir according to the TrivialFileCatalog of the remote site, to guarantee published data can be re-read for analysis.Publication in DBS make sense if the data are accessible via a Computing Element.
#### 4. Stage out in your own directory in EOS at CERN
You can run job in the distributed environment and copy the produced output to your area in your user area in [EOS](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/EOS) at CERN.
In we have three possibilities for [EOS](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/EOS) user space:
* - <https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin///T2CHCERN#Right_of_access_to_CERN_CMS_T2>
* CAF - <https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin///CAF>
* T3\_CH\_CERN - <https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin///CERNCMST3>
The parameters to be configured in crab.cfg file are
```
  [USER]
  copy_data = 1
  storage_element=
  user_remote_dir=subdirectory where your output will be stored
```
* The area in which your output file will be written is:
  ```
          site's endpoint +  /store/user/<username>/<user_remote_dir>/<output-file-name>
  ```
  where the site's endpoint is discovered by CRAB and your username is extracted form [SiteDB](/twiki/bin///SiteDB).
#### 6. **CAF** Stage out
If you are running at CAF then the required stageout configuration is:
* Stage out into CAF user area ( is the offical site name for CAF):
`[USER]`
`copy_data = 1`
`storage_element=`
`user_remote_dir=xxx`
the path where data will be stored is /store/caf/user/<username>/<user\_remote\_dir>There is no support for staging out to the CAF-T1 from the . The above instructions only apply for running on the CAF itself.

This is described here:<https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin/viewauth//SWGuideCrabForPublication#Invalidate_a_dataset_in_DBS>

### stageout time out issue
In CRAB the timeout for remote staging operations from Worker Node to remote is set at 2400 seconds. This parameter is, for now, not configurable. If you want to stage out , perhaps on long distances also, you could have timeout . The users however can control output size (with the splitting parameters). Output size of CRAB ~200MB usually works well.
### Duplicated and duplicate output
see following FAQ:
### Oddly named, multiple versioned, output in remote [![UPDATED](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/updated.gif "UPDATED")]
staged out to remote have names like `filename_id_count_rand.filetype` where
* `filename.filetype` is defined by the user's . the others are added by Crab
* `id` is the job id inside the task (1...N)
* `count` is the resubmission count for resubmission originated in crab (user command or server)
* `rand` is a random string created run time to guarantee unique file name even if job was resubmitted outside crab control (*some schedulers and local batch systems do that*)
* examples : `MySelecteData_1_1_qbu.root`
Therefore output in the may be present in multiple copies, even with same `id` and `count`. Crab always knows which is the right one, i.e. the one corresponding to the crab\_id.xml framework job report (fjr) file that it retrieves in the .../res directory upon crab -get and whose status is reported by crab -status command.
* If you use crab -publish to put output in a dataset in local scope DBS, everything is done transparently and you do not need to care.
* If you want to use those in a -made script/code (root ntuple e.g.) you will need to eliminate duplicates. Rather than deleting extra from it is better to simply make a list of good ones using crab\_X.fjr and pass this to your tool, then delete the whole directory when appropriate. We have developed a simple tool `find_goodfiles.py` which is part of the CRAB client distribution since version 2\_8\_1 . `find_goodfiles.py` should be used as:
```
find_goodfiles.py -c crab_0_120226_162216/ -q
://-.cern.ch:8443//managerv2?SFN=/castor/cern.ch//user/s/sarkar/VHTauTau/20Feb2012/DoubleMu_2011B_V1/DoubleMu_2011B_V1_1_1_yVc.root
://-.cern.ch:8443//managerv2?SFN=/castor/cern.ch//user/s/sarkar/VHTauTau/20Feb2012/DoubleMu_2011B_V1/DoubleMu_2011B_V1_10_4_UxU.root
://-.cern.ch:8443//managerv2?SFN=/castor/cern.ch//user/s/sarkar/VHTauTau/20Feb2012/DoubleMu_2011B_V1/DoubleMu_2011B_V1_100_1_jrg.root
.....
etc.
```
We have furthermore included a bash script `find_dupl.sh` which will do the hard work for you and find a list of duplicate that can be safely removed from the remote location. Usage:
```
find_dupl.sh -c crab_0_120226_162216/ -q
```
* The following external Perl script also serves the same purpose and can be used until the official tool becomes available in the CRAB client distribution.
  + [PerlToolToListGoodOutputFilesInCrabTask](/twiki/bin///PerlToolToListGoodOutputFilesInCrabTask)
### Tool to copy output Root from local stage-out area to the designated remote [![UPDATED](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/updated.gif "UPDATED")]
Starting from CRAB client version 2.7.4 we now have a stand-alone tool `retry_stageout.py` that copies the output Root , that failed remote stage-out and hence were stage-out locally, from local stageout area to the original destination . In order for this to work, local stage-out must be enabled in the first place in `crab.cfg` as follows:
```
[USER]
local_stage_out        = 1
```
Refer to [http://indico.cern.ch/getFile.py/access?contribId=8&sessionId=4&resId=0&materialId=slides&confId=103635![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://indico.cern.ch/getFile.py/access?contribId=8&sessionId=4&resId=0&materialId=slides&confId=103635) for details of the tool. Typical usage:
```
retry_stageout.py -c crab_0_120223_184129/ -q
```
Note that `retry_stageout.py` updates the `crab_fjr_n.xml` on successful local-to-remote transfer ( status 60308 -> 0) but does not update the CRAB DB. Therefore, commands like `crab -report`, `crab -publish`,  which work with the CRAB DB won't not see the update. In other words, the tool is not useful for data for which luminosity calculation is essential or for publication of user dataset. It is however, useful for analysis level Root-tuple production for MC events.
### [Use the CRAB publication to DBS](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideCrabForPublication)
See the [SWGuideCrabForPublication](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideCrabForPublication) for full information about publishing, using, removing, managing user/group-created datasets in CRAB (i.e. datasets that are not managed by official Data Production).
#### [Publication warnings and known issues](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideCrabForPublication#Warnings_and_known_issues)
### how can I run CRAB to produce events from LHE file?
First you have to put the LHE in the local storage (/store/...), so that the worker nodes can see it. Then, use this cmsDriver.py spell (tailor it for your own needs, of course):
```
cmsDriver.py Configuration/GenProduction/python/EightTeV/ADPS.py
--filetype=LHE \
--step GEN,SIM --beamspot Realistic8TeVCollision --conditions START52_V9::All \
--pileup NoPileUp --datamix NODATAMIXER \
--eventcontent RAWSIM --datatier GEN-SIM --no_exec \
--customise=Configuration/GenProduction/
```
and this crab.cfg:
```
[CRAB]
jobtype = cmssw
scheduler = remoteglidein
use_server = 0
[CMSSW]
datasetpath=None
generator=lhe
pset=TASK_NAME.py
events_per_job = 210
number_of_jobs = 200
get_edm_output = 1
[USER]
copy_data = 1
return_data = 0
storage_element = YOUR_FAVORITE_T2_HERE
user_remote_dir = /TASK_NAME
check_user_remote_dir = 0
publish_data = 1
publish_data_name = TASK_NAME
ui_working_dir = TASK_NAME
```
The crab.cfg has the crucial string "generator=lhe", which is instrumental to properly skip events in the LHE for the job splitting.You have to whitelist in crab.cfg the site where the LHE file is in order to ensure that you run there:
```
[]
se_white_list=THE_SE_WHERE_FILE_IS
```
In case that your LHE file is in [EOS](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/EOS) at CERN there is no need that you run at CERN but then you have to specify the complete path of the file in your PSET:
```
#  source
process.source = .Source("LHESource",
                            fileNames = .untracked.vstring('root://eoscms.cern.ch//eos//store/user/xxx/xxx.lhe')
```

## Dealing with remote storage
### Removing from a remote
To remove a file from a remote you can use the lcg-del command in the following format:
```
lcg-del -b -l -D srmv2 ://$FQDN:$PORT//managerv2?SFN=$PFN
```
* $FQDN is the fully qualified domain name of the your file is on, e.g.
* $PORT is the port for  on that , e.g.
  + 8446
* $PFN is the physical file name of the file you wish to delete, e.g.
  + /dpm/in2p3.fr///trivcat//store/group/exoticagroup/SD\_Photon20\_\_EMPt20to30/QCD\_EMEnriched\_Pt20to30/EXOEleSkimOct09/b666b818d81962741c75e3ccef05abdd/EXOEleOct09\_251.root
You can find information on the FQDN, port and storage paths at<https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin///AnalysisOpsPriorityuser#Tier_2_Sites_Responsibility>
### Listing at a remote
To list on a remote you can use the lcg-ls command in the following format:
```
lcg-ls -l ://$FQDN:$PORT//managerv2?SFN=$PFN
```
* $FQDN is the fully qualified domain name of the your file is on, e.g.
* $PORT is the port for  on that , e.g.
  + 8446
* $PFN is the physical file name of the directory you wish to list, e.g.
  + /dpm/in2p3.fr///trivcat//store/group/exoticagroup/SD\_Photon20\_\_EMPt20to30/QCD\_EMEnriched\_Pt20to30/EXOEleSkimOct09/b666b818d81962741c75e3ccef05abdd/
You can find information on the FQDN, port and storage paths at<https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin///AnalysisOpsPriorityuser#Tier_2_Sites_Responsibility>
### Copying from a remote
To copy on a remote you can use the lcg-cp command in the following format:
```
lcg-cp -b -D srmv2 ://$FQDN:$PORT//managerv2?SFN=$PFN file://`pwd`/localfile.root
```
* $FQDN is the fully qualified domain name of the your file is on, e.g.
* $PORT is the port for  on that , e.g.
  + 8446
* $PFN is the physical file name of the directory you wish to list, e.g.
  + /dpm/in2p3.fr///trivcat//store/group/exoticagroup/SD\_Photon20\_\_EMPt20to30/QCD\_EMEnriched\_Pt20to30/EXOEleSkimOct09/b666b818d81962741c75e3ccef05abdd/
You can find information on the FQDN, port and storage paths at<https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin///AnalysisOpsPriorityuser#Tier_2_Sites_Responsibility>

###  Verbosity ([MessageLogger](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/MessageLogger?topicparent=CMSPublic.SWGuideCrabFaq;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it."))
You can reduce the printouts of "processing event X" by including/modifying the following lines in your CMSSW config file. The example below will reduce the printouts to every 1000 events only instead of every 1 event.
```
process.load("FWCore.MessageLogger.MessageLogger_cfi")
process.MessageLogger.cerr.threshold = ''
process.MessageLogger.cerr.FwkReport.reportEvery = 1000
```

## How to publish user data to DBS (updated for )
Users can publish output files produced with CRAB as datasets in  instance.
### Prerequisites
You need to:
* Be a registered user in [SiteDB](/twiki/bin//CMS/SiteDB) (the instructions to register in SiteDB are in [CMS.SiteDBForCRAB](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin//CMS/SiteDBForCRAB)).
* Know where you can store your data:
  + You can use an "official element" (the site name list is [CMS.SiteDB sitelist![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cmsweb.cern.ch/sitedb/sitedb/sitelist/)).
  + You can use your "private Storage element", but in this case you should contact your "local" Tier2 asking that the StorageElement supports the /store/user LFN namespace (in addtion to the /store/mc LFN namespace that is regularly used to store official MC production data). You can get site's contacts from [CMS.SiteDB sitelist![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cmsweb.cern.ch/sitedb/sitedb/sitelist/).
* Decide to publish data at the job creation time (it is not possible to do it at the end of jobs).
### Details on the dataset name
* how CRAB creates the name of your dataset:
  + user data will be published as
    ```
    /<primarydataset>/<yourHyperNewsusername>-<publish_data_name>-<PSETHASH>/USER
    ```
    where <publish\_data\_name> is the name you provide in crab.cfg, as described [below](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin/edit/CMS/CrabNewHowTo#Modify_the_crab_cfg).
     and <primarydataset> is the primary dataset of the dataset you are reading (the first part of the datasetpath in crab.cfg) If you are running with datasetpath=None then the <primarydataset> is set equal to <publish\_data\_name>
    ```
    /<publish_data_name>/<yourHyperNewsusername>-<publish_data_name>-<PSETHASH>/USER
    ```
### How to use CRAB to publish
#### Modify the crab.cfg
##### Publish data stored in an "official CMS site"
###### Default way to work: data under /store/user dir
* By default data will be stored under the **/store/user** directory. The complete path and the LFN to associate with the output files will be created by CRAB.
  You have to modify the following entries:
```
     [USER]
     copy_data = 1
     storage_element = "official_CMS_site_name"  (e.g. T2_IT_legnaro)
     publish_data=1
     publish_data_name = data_name_to_publish
```
* + storage\_element is the name of the SE reported in the CMS.SiteDB [https://cmsweb.cern.ch/sitedb/sitelist/![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cmsweb.cern.ch/sitedb/sitelist/) . The mapping between the [StorageElement](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/StorageElement?topicparent=CMSPublic. "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") name and CMS site names is reported [here![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cmsweb.cern.ch/sitedb/reports/showReport?reportid=se_cmsname_map.ini). Note that there is one exception: you have to use T2\_RU\_IHEP\_Disk instead of T2\_RU\_IHEP.
  + publish\_data = 1, instructs CRAB that you wish to publish your output\_files to DBS.
  + publish\_data\_name is a descriptive string that will appear in the dataset name when published (e.g. myprocessingCMSSW\_1\_6\_8).
  + in this case the storage\_path where user can store data is automatically discovery by CRAB.
  + The directory and LFN of your output file are enforced to be:
    ```
    PFN = site's endpoint +  /store/user/<yourHyperNewsusername>/<primarydataset>/<publish_data_name>/<PSETHASH>/<output_file_name>
    ```
    ```
    LFN = /store/user/<yourHyperNewsusername>/<primarydataset>/<publish_data_name>/<PSETHASH>/<output_file_name>
    ```
###### No default way: data under /store/group/groupname dir
* You need to store your data under a different dir, as **/store/group/groupname** directory
  + the changes to crab.cfg files are similar to "no official CMS site". It means you have to specify the complete name of storage, storage\_path and user\_remote\_dir.
  + a smart script [GetStorageCfgFromTFC.py![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmssw.cvs.cern.ch/cgi-bin/cmssw.cgi/UserCode/RWTH3b/GridTools/GetStorageCfgFromTFC.py?=co) to check how to write the requiered paramenters has been provided. Please read the detailed instruction at [WorkBookGroupActivities](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookGroupActivities)
##### Publish data stored in a "not official CMS site"
You have to modify following entries:
```
     [USER]
     copy_data = 1
     storage_element = the_storage_element_name ()
     storage_path= the_storage_element_path where the user can write (i.e/srm//cmsfarm1.ba.infn.it/data/cms/phedex/)
     user_remote_dir = the_user_directory or tree of directories that CRAB will create under the storage path of the SE (i.e /store/user/fede_test)
```
```
     publish_data=1
     publish_data_name = data_name_to_publish  (i.e  myprocessingCMSSW_1_6_8)
```
* + The directory of your output file is enforced to be:
    ```
     PFN=storage_path+user_remote_dir+<yourHyperNewsusername>/<primarydataset>/<publish_data_name>/<PSETHASH>
    ```
  + The LFN of your output file is enforced to be:
    ```
            LFN=user_remote_dir+<yourHyperNewsusername>/<primarydataset>/<publish_data_name>/<PSETHASH>/<output_file_name>
    ```
    - Warning: the user\_remote\_dir will be the first part of the LFN of published files. It is the responsibility of the user to check the correct conversion from LFN to PFN (according to the trivial file catalog of the remote site) when data will be re-read. The user\_remote\_dir should start with "/store" since it's the CMS LFN naming convention.
#### Use the -publish option
You need first to:
* create and submit all jobs
* retrieve the outputs of the finished jobs
Then you can issue:
```
   crab -publish
```
It will look for the CMS.FrameworkJobReport ( /res/crab\_fjr\_\*.xml ) produced by each job
and extract from there the information (i.e. number of events, LFN,....) to publish.**Note that partial publication is also supported**:It is not compulsory to wait until the end of all jobs to issue the "crab -publish" command.
For instance when N-M jobs have finished the "crab -publish" will publish in DBS the corresponding N-M files and once the remaining M jobs have finished issuing "crab -publish" will publish the remaining M files. In this case two fileblocks will be registered in DBS: the first with N-M files and the second with the remaining M files.
#### Check the result of data publication
To check if your data have been correctly published you can use the DAS web page at this
[URL![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cmsweb.cern.ch/das/request?=list&limit=10&instance=prod%2Fphys03&input=dataset+dataset%3D%2Ffoo%2Fbar%2FUSER)
### Run analysis on your published dataset
* in the crab.cfg you have to specify
  + as dbs\_url, the URL for the DBS instance used in publication: `dbs_url=`
  + as dataset\_path the name of your dataset published by CRAB
    ```
    [CMSSW]
    datasetpath=<primarydataset>/<publish_data_name>/USER
    dbs_url =
    ```
* create and submit job as usual.
### Delete a dataset from DBS
Users to do not have permissions to delete datasets from DBS (i.e. completely remove entries).
Users can instead invalidate datasets and/or files in them, i.e. mark them in DBS as invalid (see below how).Invalid datasets can still be used in CRAB, but any invalid file will be skipped.
Rational is that invalid file means file is corrupted, deleted, lost or anyhow unreadable. On the other hand, an invalid dataset simply means that it is not good for physics, but there could be reasons to look at it, e.g. to figure out why it is marked as invalid and if it can be turned into valid by removing some files or similar.
### Invalidate a dataset in DBS
**Note**: The instructions in this section are independent on whether the publication was done with , with , or any other service.**NOTE**: This procedure currently requires the environment. If you are using : open a new shell, setup cmsenv, then , then issue the commands below. Soon this will work inside client as well, but not yet.Every user who published a dataset in DBS can mark it (or files in it) as invalid.
* Invalidation is a reversible procedure.
* Invalidated files will not be used as input by CRAB.
* By default invalidated datasets will not be listed by Data Discovery
Dataset invalidation is supported via the following script. Requires CMSSW\_6\_1\_0 or higher
```
python $CRABPYTHON/DBS3SetDatasetStatus.py
e.g.
python $CRABPYTHON/DBS3SetDatasetStatus.py --dataset=<datasetname> --url=https://cmsweb.cern.ch/dbs/prod//DBSWriter --status=INVALID --recursive=False
see
python $CRABPYTHON/DBS3SetDatasetStatus.py --help
```
the same script can be used to turn dataset status back to `--status=VALID`N.B. All files in the dataset are also set to invalid.Invalidation is a status update procedure in the local DBS, it can be undone by the user.
#### Invalidate individual files in a dataset in DBS
You can invalidate single files with the following script. Requires CMSSW\_6\_1\_0 or higher
```
python $CRABPYTHON/DBS3SetFileStatus.py
python $CRABPYTHON/DBS3SetFileStatus.py --url=https://cmsweb.cern.ch/dbs/prod//DBSWriter --status=invalid --recursive=False  --files=<lfn;>
see
python $CRABPYTHON/DBS3SetFileStatus.py --help
```
####  individual files in a dataset in DBS
Can be done with the same procedure as above by using `--status=valid`
### Elevate a dataset from local DBS to global DBS
Users are not allowed to publish data in the global DBS, only dataOperation people can do it.
So if you need to elevate your dataset, you have first of all to publish your complete\* dataset in your local DBS and then follow the <https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookGroupActivities> to require the transfert of your data to the "right" directory and the publication in the global DBS.
* Warning: The Store Results service used for dataset migration and elevation does not support growing datasets. That means that your dataset has to be completed before the elevation request. You can not make another request for elevation with the same dataset name. If you produce more similar data you need to do something like adding \_v1, \_v2, \_v3 etc. to the name.
###  and known issues
#### Only EDM files are published
* CRAB publishes only EDM files (in the FJR they are written in the tag <File>)
#### All output go in a single dataset (multiple skim output streams not supported).
* CRAB publishes in the same USER dataset more EDM files if they are produced by a job and written in the tag <File> of FJR.
  + It is not possible for the user to select only one file to publish, nor to publish two files in two different USER datasets.
#### The import of parent dataset isn't allowed from local dbs to local DBS
* You can not publish your user dataset in a local DBS, analize it to produce a new user dataset and publish this new dataset in a different local DBS because the import of parent, done by default during publication, can not transfert data from a local DBS to another one. The import is allowed only from global DBS to a local one, so your publication will fail. You can publish your new dataset only in the same local DBS where "user" parent dataset is published.
#### Default setting of publication step
* By default the publication of user data is done importing all parents tree of user dataset.
* By default the publication step publishes also containing 0 events. The parameter [USER].publish\_zero\_event=1 in CRAB.cfg is deprecated
 - 16 Oct 2008

# Using CRAB to generate [/bin//CMS/MonteCarlo) events
* [Using CRAB to generate )
  + [Random numbers](#Random_numbers)
  + [How to generate different event identifiers](#How_to_generate_different_event)
  + [How to add more data to a previous generation run](#How_to_add_more_data_to_a_previo)
  + [How to set run number in CMSSW](#How_to_set_run_number_in_CMSSW)
In order to generate MC events with CRAB it is sufficient to indicate the dataset parameter as `none`:
```
[CMSSW]
datasetpath = none
```
## Random numbers
Unless the user supplies the settings to increment/preserve seeds, which are there to produce repeatability, each job gets a random set of random seeds and thus events should be unique. To increment/preserve seeds, use the CRAB configuration parameters `increment_seeds` and `preserve_seeds` respectively. A short explanation on how to use these configuration parameters can be found in the [CRAB Online Manual![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmsdoc.cern.ch/cms/ccs/wm/www/Crab/Docs/crab-online-).
## How to generate different event identifiers
If you want different runs for different sets of jobs, you have to set the run number yourself in the CMSSW configuration file like explained in section [How to set run number in CMSSW](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideCrabMonteCarlo#How_to_set_run_number_in_CMSSW) below.
Crab (from the 2.7.1 series) doesn't have parameters that act on the run number, but instead it allows to work on the lumisection. Since an event is identified by a triple <run, lumi, event number>, incrementing the lumi ensures that there are not duplicate events, even if the run and the event number remain constants.
Setting the parameter `first_lumi` under `[CMSSW]` section, the first job will generate events with lumi section number and subsequent jobs will increment the lumi section number. For more information on how to use the `first_lumi` parameter, see item description in the [CRAB Online Manual![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmsdoc.cern.ch/cms/ccs/wm/www/Crab/Docs/crab-online-).
## How to add more data to a previous generation run
Generating another set of jobs with an increased `first_lumi` is the correct thing to do.
## How to set run number in CMSSW
Your config file should look like :
```
  RandomNumberGeneratorService = cms.Service(
     "RandomNumberGeneratorService",
     #  is to initialize the random engine of the source
     generator = cms.PSet(
         initialSeed = cms.untracked.uint32(123456789),
         engineName = cms.untracked.string('TRandom3')
     ),
     #  is to initialize the random engines used for
     VtxSmeared = cms.PSet(
         initialSeed = cms.untracked.uint32(123456789),
         engineName = cms.untracked.string('TRandom3')
     ),
....
```
For furter details refer to HN:
[https://hypernews.cern.ch/HyperNews/CMS/get/crabFeedback/3075/1/1/1/1/1/1/1/1/2.html![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://hypernews.cern.ch/HyperNews/CMS/get/crabFeedback/3075/1/1/1/1/1/1/1/1/2.html)-- - 14-Apr-2010

| combinedSVTagInfos | [![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmssdt.cern.ch/SDT/doxygen/redirect.php?r=1_6_12&c=CombinedSVTagInfo&K={reco}) ([lxr![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmslxr.fnal.gov/lxr/source/DataFormats/BTauReco/interface/CombinedSVTagInfo.h) [cvs![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmssw.cvs.cern.ch/cgi-bin/cmssw.cgi/CMSSW/DataFormats/BTauReco/interface/CombinedSVTagInfo.h?rev=HEAD&cvsroot=CMSSW&content-type=text/vnd.viewcvs-markup)) | contains a list of tagging variables containing information about track impact parameters and results from an attempted secondary vertex fit |
| combinedSVJetTags | [reco::JetTag![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmssdt.cern.ch/SDT/doxygen/redirect.php?r=1_6_12&c=}) ([lxr![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmslxr.fnal.gov/lxr/source/DataFormats/BTauReco/interface/JetTag.h) [cvs![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmssw.cvs.cern.ch/cgi-bin/cmssw.cgi/CMSSW/DataFormats/BTauReco/interface/JetTag.h?rev=HEAD&cvsroot=CMSSW&content-type=text/vnd.viewcvs-markup)) | Result of application of a likelihood estimator to the tagging variables for the three possible algorithm outcomes (tracks only, pseudo vertex from at least two tracks or successful secondary vertex fit) |
| combinedSVMVAJetTags | [reco::JetTag![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmssdt.cern.ch/SDT/doxygen/redirect.php?r=1_6_12&c=}) ([lxr![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmslxr.fnal.gov/lxr/source/DataFormats/BTauReco/interface/JetTag.h) [cvs![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmssw.cvs.cern.ch/cgi-bin/cmssw.cgi/CMSSW/DataFormats/BTauReco/interface/JetTag.h?rev=HEAD&cvsroot=CMSSW&content-type=text/vnd.viewcvs-markup)) | uses the [PhysicsTools](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/PhysicsTools)/MVAComputer framework to compute a discriminator from the [CombinedSVTagInfos](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/CombinedSVTagInfos?topicparent=CMSPublic.SWGuideDataFormatRecoBTag;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") with an uptodate calibration from the the CMS conditions database, making use of more general multivariate analysis techniques, like neural networks |

The collection is unpreselected and contains electrons reconstructed either by or by PF algorithm. |
| gsfElectrons | [reco::GsfElectronCollection![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmssdt.cern.ch/SDT/doxygen/redirect.php?r=4_4_2&c=GsfElectron&K={reco}) | Offline electron containing all the relevant observables and corrections. Each electron has also a reference to the corresponding "core" partner. (**standard offline electron collection**) |
| electronGsfTracks | [reco::GsfTrackCollection![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmssdt.cern.ch/SDT/doxygen/redirect.php?r=4_4_2&c=GsfTrack&K={reco}) | GsfTracks for GsfElectrons (**produced in a dedicated module in the standard reconstruction sequence**). They have been produced from the electronMergedSeeds described below. |
| eidTYPE |  | ValueMaps containing a reference to a CMS.GsfElectron and the result of the electron ID. The event has one per identification TYPE (eidLoose, eidRobust...) (**standard electron ID computed in standard sequence**) |
| siStripElectronToTrackAssociator | [reco::ElectronCollection![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmssdt.cern.ch/SDT/doxygen/redirect.php?r=4_4_2&c=Electron&K={reco}) | Electrons reconstructed using tracks seeded in the Si strip layers (**not produced in standard sequence**) |
| egammaCTFFinalFitWithMaterial | [reco::TrackCollection![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmssdt.cern.ch/SDT/doxygen/redirect.php?r=4_4_2&c=Track&K={reco}) | Tracks for Si strip seeded electrons (**not produced in standard sequence**) |
| siStripElectrons | [reco::SiStripElectronCollection![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmssdt.cern.ch/SDT/doxygen/redirect.php?r=4_4_2&c=SiStripElectron&K={reco}) | Intermediate object for Si Strip electron reconstruction containing information about Si strip hits associated to the  (**not produced in standard sequence**) |

| photons | [reco::PhotonCollection![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmssdt.cern.ch/SDT/doxygen/redirect.php?r=4_4_2&c=Photon&K={reco}) | Photons with all the related observables like vertex, shower shapes, isolation. (**standard reconstructed photon collection**) |
| conversions | [reco::ConversionCollection![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmssdt.cern.ch/SDT/doxygen/redirect.php?r=4_4_2&c=Conversion&K={reco}) | Converted photons |
| ckfOutInTracksFromConversions | [reco::TrackCollection![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmssdt.cern.ch/SDT/doxygen/redirect.php?r=4_4_2&c=Track&K={reco}) | Conversion tracks from outside-in tracking. |
| ckfInOutTracksFromConversions | [reco::TrackCollection![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmssdt.cern.ch/SDT/doxygen/redirect.php?r=4_4_2&c=Track&K={reco}) | Conversion tracks from inside-out tracking. |

They are used as input for the production of electronGsfTracks. |

Three instances are created (corresponding to the calo-tower component): `ecal`, `hcal`, and `ho` |

| muons | edm::ValueMap<[reco::MuonTimeExtra![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmssdt.cern.ch/SDT/doxygen/redirect.php?r=4_4_2&c=MuonTimeExtra&K={reco})> | timing information for DT, CSC, and combined, defined in DataFormats/MuonReco/interface/MuonTimeExtra.h |
| cosmicsVeto | edm::ValueMap<unsigned int> | Index of the partner track found in the opposite hemisphere, used by the cosmic- identifier |
| cosmicsVeto | edm::ValueMap<[reco::MuonCosmicCompatibility![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmssdt.cern.ch/SDT/doxygen/redirect.php?r=4_4_2&s=})> | Information used by the cosmic- identifier, defined in DataFormats/MuonReco/interface/MuonCosmicCompatibility.h |
Each reco::TrackCollection has two extra collections associated to it: reco::TrackExtra (both in RECO and AOD for standard reconstructions algorithms, only in RECO for cosmic algorithms) and TrackingRecHitsOwned (both in AOD and in RECO for "standAloneMuons", only in RECO for all other collections). These collections should not be accessed directly but only through the reco::Track methods.

## Contacts
