 types for physics objects are defined in [/EgammaCandidates![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmslxr.fnal.gov/lxr/source//EgammaCandidates/interface/).
## and Software Architecture
### Default sequences used for Electron/Photon Reconstruction
* [SWGuideEgammaStandardSequences](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideEgammaStandardSequences)
###
* [SuperCluster Reconstruction](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideEcalRecoClustering), description of the SuperCluster reconstruction, starting point for ECAL based Electron and Photon reconstruction
* [Principles of the standard electron reconstruction](/twiki/bin//CMS/ElectronRecoPrinciples).
* [Software tools and process of the standard electron reconstruction](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideElectronRecoSoftware).
* [Photon Reconstruction](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuidePhotonReco), brief description of the standard Photon reconstruction
* [Electron Identification](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideElectronID), description of the standard Electron Identification
* [Photon Identification](/twiki/bin//CMS/PhotonIDAnalysis), description of the standard Photon Identification
* [Electron/Photon Isolation](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideEgammaIsolation), description of the standard Electron/Photon Isolation
* , description of the
* [HFElectrons](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideHFElectrons), description of electromagnetic identification in HF
### Standard Electron/Photon physics objects
The standard collections of electrons and photons are intended to be
efficient for electrons with pt>5GeV and prompt photons with pt>10GeV.
The photons are based on ECAL superclusters. Electrons are reconstructed
by matching ECAL superclusters to track seeds found in, or close to, the
pixel detectors. On these seeds tracks are reconstructed using the GSF
tracking algorithm. To this collection of electrons are added the electrons
found by the track based algorithm developed in the PFlow group. The majority
of electrons in the merged collection are found by both .The preselection of both collections, photons and electrons, is rather
loose and both collections are dominated by fakes (where "fake" is taken
to include non-prompt photons e.g. from pizeros, and electrons from conversions). Also:
most (in 31X: **all** [to be verified]) superclusters of ECAL supercluster seeded electrons
with pt>10 appear also in the photon collection.A more detailed description of electron objects is available [here](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideGsfElectronObject).Further electron and photon identification, beyond preselection, generally
needs to be specific to use cases. This is because a) the relatively large
fake rate and numerous imperfect identification variables gives much elasticity in tradeoffs between efficiency and purity, and
b) different cuts are needed for different pt ranges. The most developed
identification for electrons is for the 20<pt<70GeV regime appropriate
for electrons from W and Z decay.
### Package Architecture
Subsystem: [RecoEgamma![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmslxr.fnal.gov/lxr/source/RecoEgamma/)Packages within RecoEgamma:
* [Configuration![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmslxr.fnal.gov/lxr/source/RecoEgamma/Configuration/) - Standard electron and photon reconstruction sequences; Standard event content for electrons and photons
* [EgammaElectronAlgos![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmslxr.fnal.gov/lxr/source/RecoEgamma/EgammaElectronAlgos/) - for electron reconstruction
* [EgammaElectronProducers![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmslxr.fnal.gov/lxr/source/RecoEgamma/EgammaElectronProducers/) - Producers for electron collections
* [ElectronIdentification![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmslxr.fnal.gov/lxr/source/RecoEgamma/ElectronIdentification/) - and Producers for electron identification by track matching and shower-shape criteria
* [EgammaIsolationAlgos![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmslxr.fnal.gov/lxr/source/RecoEgamma/EgammaIsolationAlgos/) - for computation of ECAL, HCAL and tracker-based isolation sums around electrons and photons
* [EgammaHLTAlgos![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmslxr.fnal.gov/lxr/source/RecoEgamma/EgammaHLTAlgos/) - specific to HLT reconstruction
* [EgammaHLTProducers![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmslxr.fnal.gov/lxr/source/RecoEgamma/EgammaHLTProducers/) - Producers specific to HLT reconstruction
* [EgammaPhotonAlgos![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmslxr.fnal.gov/lxr/source/RecoEgamma/EgammaPhotonAlgos/) - for photon reconstruction
* [EgammaPhotonProducers![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmslxr.fnal.gov/lxr/source/RecoEgamma/EgammaPhotonProducers) - Producers for photon reconstruction
* [EgammaHFProducers![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmslxr.fnal.gov/lxr/source/RecoEgamma/EgammaHFProducers) - Producers for HF Electrons
* [PhotonIdentification![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmslxr.fnal.gov/lxr/source/RecoEgamma/PhotonIdentification/) - and Producers for photon selection

title: Standard Sequences
body:
If you are experiencing TWiki instability from outside the CERN network, please connect via the CERN internal network - see [KB0010688![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cern.service-now.com/service-portal?id=KB0010688) for details
>![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/web-bg-small.gif) [CMSPublic Web](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WebHome)>[SWGuide](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuide)>[SWGuideEgamma](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideEgamma)>[SWGuideEgammaStandardSequences](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideEgammaStandardSequences "Topic revision: 9 (2009-09-24 - 21:58:46)") (2009-09-24, )[![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/uweb-o14.gif) Edit](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/SWGuideEgammaStandardSequences?t=1777862459;nowysiwyg=1 "Edit this topic text")[Attach](/twiki/bin/attach/CMSPublic/SWGuideEgammaStandardSequences "Attach an image or document to this topic")[PDF](/twiki/bin/genpdf/CMSPublic/SWGuideEgammaStandardSequences "Create a PDF file for the topic")
# Standard Sequences
Complete: ![3](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/pub/CMS/WebPreferences/complete3.png)
[Detailed Review status](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideEgammaStandardSequences#ReviewStatus)
## Contents
* [Electron standard reconstruction sequence](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideEgammaStandardSequences#ElectronStanSeq)
* [Photon standard reconstruction sequence](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideEgammaStandardSequences#PhotonStanSeq)
* [Conversion standard reconstruction sequence](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideEgammaStandardSequences#ConversionStanSeq)
* [Examples of reconstruction code](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideEgammaStandardSequences#EleAna)
* [Review Status](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideEgammaStandardSequences#ReviewStatus)
## Electron standard reconstruction sequence
The standard sequence to be executed is *electronSequence*, defined in [electronSequence\_cff.py![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmslxr.fnal.gov/lxr/source/RecoEgamma/EgammaElectronProducers/python/electronSequence_cff.py). Actually, this is a referenceing *gsfElectronSequence*, defined in [gsfElectronSequence\_cff.py![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmslxr.fnal.gov/lxr/source/RecoEgamma/EgammaElectronProducers/python/gsfElectronSequence_cff.py), and the former is made of two modules:
```
gsfElectronSequence = cms.Sequence(gsfElectronCores*gsfElectrons)
```
The first module (*gsfElectronCores*) produces the GsfElectronCoreCollection while the second (*gsfElectrons*) the GsfElectronCollection.Worth to note: the reconstruction of electron depends on previous execution of *electronGsfTracking*, defined in [GsfElectronTracking\_cff.py![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmslxr.fnal.gov/lxr/source/TrackingTools/GsfTracking/python/GsfElectronTracking_cff.py). This tracking depends on mixed seeds coming from both and particle-flow, this is why this sequence is not integrated in electron sequence, but defined by tracking and directly integrated into the reconstruction standard sequence. Whatsoever, the subset of seeds is defined in [ecalDrivenElectronSeeds\_cfi.py![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmslxr.fnal.gov/lxr/source/RecoEgamma/EgammaElectronProducers/python/ecalDrivenElectronSeeds_cfi.py), in the same directory as [electronSequence\_cff.py![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmslxr.fnal.gov/lxr/source/RecoEgamma/EgammaElectronProducers/python/electronSequence_cff.py).
## Photon standard reconstruction sequence
The standard sequence to be executed is *photonSequence*:
```
photonSequence = cms.Sequence(photonCore+photons)
```
It is described in [photonSequence\_cff.py![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmslxr.fnal.gov/lxr/source/RecoEgamma/EgammaPhotonProducers/python/photonSequence_cff.py?v=CMSSW_3_1_0_pre5)
The first module (*photonCore*) produces the PhotonCoreCollection while the second (*photons*) the final PhotonCollection.
The *photonCore* stores Ref to conevrsions. So in order for those reference to be corrected attached, the conversionSequence needs to be run **prior** to the photonSequence as is indeed done in the complete reco sequence (see [http://cmslxr.fnal.gov/lxr/source/RecoEgamma/Configuration/python/RecoEgamma\_cff.py![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmslxr.fnal.gov/lxr/source/RecoEgamma/Configuration/python/RecoEgamma_cff.py)
## Conversion standard reconstruction sequence
The standard sequence to be executed is *conversionSequence*:
```
conversionSequence = cms.Sequence(ckfTracksFromConversions*conversions)
```
It is described in [conversionSequence\_cff.py![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmslxr.fnal.gov/lxr/source/RecoEgamma/EgammaPhotonProducers/python/conversionSequence_cff.py?v=CMSSW_3_1_0_pre5)
## Examples of reconstruction code
Examples on how to run the above sequences and details on the reconstruction algorithms can be found in: [SWGuideElectronRecoSoftware](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideElectronRecoSoftware) and [SWGuidePhotonReco](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuidePhotonReco) respectively for Electrons and Photons.

# Event Generation Offline Guide
## Introduction
A variety of event generators are currently used in CMS. They range from general-purpose ones (Pythia8, Herwig++, ) to more specific ones (Matrix Element calculators like Alpgen, MadGraph5\_aMCatNLO, generators for diffractive physics, cosmic muon generators, and so on).
The objective of general-purpose event generators is to provide as accurate as possible a description of what happens in a particle collision.
They contain theory and models for a number of physics aspects, such as hard and soft interactions, parton distributions, initial and final state parton showers, multiple interactions, fragmentation and decay. They are also used for hadronization of the parton-level events modeled with one or another ME generator.
In CMSSW, generators are incorporated as external, well-encapsulated packages, while CMS-specific software provides an interface to one or another packge and allows to tune it to generate events of a desired topology, via a set of generator-oriented configuration cards.
As many uncertainties are involved here, we do not speak of the "algorithms" but rather refer to activities in the area of fine-tuning and validating various MC tools, via links to relevant documents.
Neither is it possible to provide a uniform recipe for modifying parameters/settings.
* The main generator page is [here](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin/viewauth/CMS/GeneratorMain)
* A tutorial on how to generate events in 30 minutes is [here](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookGenIntro)
* A more detailed tutorial on how to generate events is [here](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookGeneration)

# Relevant cmsDriver options
The `cmsDriver.py` command is documented [here (outdated)](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideCmsDriver) and [here (incomplete)](/twiki/bin//CMS/PdmVCmsDriverStandardCommands) and in `cmsDriver.py --help` . The next table lists and explains the options relevant for .Example `cmsDriver.py` commands for the fast simulation are available on [SWGuideFastSimulationExamples](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideFastSimulationExamples).
|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| `GENFRAGMENT.py` (1st argument) | Define the "genfragment" that configures the event gen-content. For more info see [below](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideFastSimulation#How_to_configure_the_gen_level_c) |
| `--fast` | tells cmsDriver.py to use (default is FullSim). This option is in place since `CMSSW_6_2_X`. For the old syntax, see [examples](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideFastSimulation#Examples). |
| `-s STEP1,STEP2,...` | **note**: in CMSSW\_7\_5\_0\_pre2 the step syntax changes, documentation is provided here: [SWGuideFastSimulationSteps75X](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideFastSimulationSteps75X). Comma separated sequence of steps. Each step itself is a sequence of algorithms for event generation (GEN), detector simulation (SIM), reconstruction (RECO), ... . The available steps and their definitions are listed [here (outdated)](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideCmsDriver) and [here (incomplete)](/twiki/bin//CMS/PdmVCmsDriverStandardCommands). Most purposes are covered by one of the following combinations of steps. **Commonly used combinations of steps** :  * `-s GEN,SIM`, run generation and detector simulation * `-s GEN,SIM,RECO`, the above + event reconstruction * `-s GEN,SIM,RECO,HLT:GRun`, the above + HLT * `-s GEN,SIM,RECO,HLT:GRun,VALIDATION`, the above + production of validation plots (DQM) * `-s GEN,SIM,HLT:GRun`, run generation, detector simulation and HLT * `-s HARVESTING:validationHarvestingFS`, "Harvest" validation plots, see examples for usage. Harvesting turns the complicated DQMio files into plain root files)  Note: for the old syntax, < `CMSSW_6_2_X`, see [examples](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideFastSimulation#Examples). **Selecting the HLT menu** The HLT menu is selected in the steps with the syntax HLT:<MENU>. Some examples for CMSSW\_7\_X:  * `-s GEN,SIM,RECO,HLT:GRun --conditions=auto:startup_GRun` to use the development HTL menu * `-s GEN,,HLT:2013 --conditions=auto:startup_2013` to use the frozen HLT menu "2013"  To find out which HLT menus are available for in your favourite release: each available HLT menu `XXX` has a corresponding file `HLTrigger/Configuration/python/HLT_X_Famos_cff.py`. Note that, in the examples above, there is a correspondence between the HLT menu name and the last part of the `--conditions` option.This correspondance is not obligatory, but usually it is recommended. The HLT depends on the conditions for e.g. subdetector calibrations, channel mappings, geometry, and, at higher-level for e.g. jet energy corrections etc. **WARNING related to VALIDATION step** It is currently not possible to run the VALIDATION step in a standalone manner. Please run validation together with GEN,SIM and RECO steps. |
| `--conditions=CONDITIONS` | Define the conditions, such as calibration, alignment and noise levels. See [SWGuideFrontierConditions](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideFrontierConditions) for available conditions.(Missing: most common examples. syntax: what's before the colon what's after it what is the meaning of "startup" and why is the trigger menu specified there) |
| `--pileup=PUSCENARIO` | define pileup scenario. All pileup scenarios available for FullSim are automatically available for .Pileup scenarios are defined in `Configuration/StandardSequences/python/Mixing.py`. For each available pileup option `X` there is a line `addMixingScenario("X","Y")`, where `Y` points to the configuration file or provides parameters that define the pileup scenario.==addMixingScenario("FS\_X","Y")==, where `Y` points to the configuration file or provides parameters that define the pileup scenario.See [PdmVPileUpDescription](/twiki/bin//CMS/PdmVPileUpDescription) to find out which PU scenario is used in which production campaign. |
| `--eventcontent=EVENTCONTENT` | defines which information of the events will be written to the output file. see header of `Configuration/EventContent/python/EventContent_cff.py` for available options and their definition. |
| `--datatier=DATATIER` | A flag to specify metadata in your output file. Not much to care about. |
| `-n` | number of events to be produced/processed |
| `--no_exec` | only produce the CMSSW configuration file, do not run it. |
| `--filein=FILE` | read input files from FILE **examples**  * `--filein=file:YourLHEFile.lhe --filetype=LHE` when using lhe files as input * `--filein=mcdb:ID` for LHE files in [mcdb![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://mcdb.cern.ch/), where ID corresponds to the article ID * `--filein=file:YourEDMFile.root` read gen information from existing [EDM](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/EDM) files ( **see bug warning** ) Note that when using lhe files as input, your genfragment must be configured to perform showering and hadronization, depending on how your lhe files were generated.See option `GENFRAGMENT.py` for more info about genfragments. **bug warning:** reading from [EDM](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/EDM) files results in double vertex smearing, leading to a significant reduction of track reconstruction efficiencies. You can fix this as explained [here](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideFastSimFAQ#I_want_to_use_existing_events_as)  TODO: how to read files from das |
| `--filetype=FILETYPE` | use this option when using an input file that is not in [EDM](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/EDM) format, see option `--filein` for use cases |
| `--geometry=GEOMETRY` | NOTE: This option has no effect on |
| `--customise=PACKAGE.FUNCTION` | Apply function FUNCTION from package PACKAGE at the end of the simulation configuration. E.g. `--customise=SLHCUpgradeSimulations.Configuration.postLS1Customs` configures for run2 (after 2014) by applying the function `postLS1Customs(process)` in the directory `SLHCUpgradeSimulations/Configuration/python` |
| `--magField=MAGFIELD` | Use magnetic field description MAGFIELD. The default description is the run1 description (before 2013). To load the run2 description (after 2014) use `--magField=38T_PostLS1` |

## **Goal**
The goal of this page is to describe the specific software that is used in the analysis done in Forward Physics Group. The main group page is [CMS Forward physics](/twiki/bin//CMS/FwdAndSmallxQCDPhysics).
## **Analysis software**
The common Forward physics analysis software resides in the [CMSSW/DiffractiveForwardAnalysis![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmssw.cvs.cern.ch/cgi-bin/cmssw.cgi/CMSSW/DiffractiveForwardAnalysis/?cvsroot=CMSSW) package in the CMSSW cvs directory. It contains subdirectories for performed analysis. Below one can find links to each analysis Software Page.
* [Exclusive dilepton software page](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideFwdExclusiveDilepton), see also the physics analysis page for this analysis - [here](/twiki/bin//CMS/ExclusiveDileptonsCSA07Analysis)
* [Upsilon photoproduction software page](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideFwdUpsilonPhotoproduction), see also the physics analysis page for this analysis - [here](/twiki/bin//CMS/UpsilonPhotoproduction)
* [Luminosity measurement with exclusive muon pairs software page](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideFwdLumiDimuons), see also the physics analysis page for this analysis - [here](/twiki/bin//CMS/LuminosityMeasurementWithDimuons)
* [Single diffractive W production software page](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideFwdSingleDiffractiveW), see also the physics analysis page for this analysis - [here](/twiki/bin//CMS/SingleDiffractiveWAnalysis)
* [Single diffractive dijet production software page](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideFwdSingleDiffractiveDijet), see also the physics analysis page for this analysis - [here](/twiki/bin//CMS/SingleDiffractiveDiJetAnalysis)
* [Forward jets software page](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideFwdForwardJets), see also the physics analysis page for this analysis - [here](/twiki/bin//CMS/ForwardJets)
* [software page](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideFwdJetGapJet), see also the physics analysis page for this analysis - [here](/twiki/bin//CMS/JetGapJet)
* [Exclusive diffractive B+](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideFwdExclusiveDiffractiveB) production software page, see also the physics analysis page for this analysis - [here](/twiki/bin//CMS/ExclusiveBAnalysis)
* [Underlying event and multi-parton interactions](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideFwdUnderlyingEvents) production software page, see also the physics analysis page for this analysis - [here](/twiki/bin//CMS/UnderlyingEvents)
## **Simulations**
### **Detector and transport**
* [HECTOR](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin//CMS/HECTOR) - a stand-alone code to simulate the proton transport through the LHC beamline up to 420m from the interaction point. It resides in the [CMSSW/SimTransport![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmssw.cvs.cern.ch/cgi-bin/cmssw.cgi/CMSSW/SimTransport) directory of the CMSSW cvs repository. Here are the instructions on [how to run HECTOR](/twiki/bin//CMS/HectorCMSSW) in CMSSW.
* The [Proton taggers](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin//CMS/SWGuideFastSimProtonTaggers) - package provides a method to simulate the acceptance of detectors installed 420 and 220 m from IP5 (in both beam directions). The code for Fast Simulation resides in the [CMSSW/FastSimulation/ProtonTaggers![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmssw.cvs.cern.ch/cgi-bin/cmssw.cgi/CMSSW/FastSimulation/ProtonTaggers) directory of CMSSW cvs repository. Code for Full Simulation is not yet available.
### **MC generators**
* [![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://www.isv.uu.se/thep//) is an PYTHIA based event generator that simulates elastic parton–parton scattering by hard color singlet exchange, calculated from the BFKL equation. Here are the instructions on [how to use](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/HARDCOLInterface?topicparent=CMSPublic.SWGuideFwdPhysics;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.")  in FWD PAG group.
* [![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://www..com/) is a modified version of [HERWIG![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://hepwww.rl.ac.uk/theory/seymour/herwig/) which can generate diffractive interactions. All standard HERWIG hard subprocesses are available for pomeron-proton, photon-pomeron and pomeron-pomeron collisions. The interface for this generator resides in [CMSSW/GeneratorInterface/PomwigInterface![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmssw.cvs.cern.ch/cgi-bin/cmssw.cgi/CMSSW/GeneratorInterface/PomwigInterface/) directory of the CMSSW cvs repository. Here are the instructions on [how to run PomwigInterface](/twiki/bin//CMS/PomwigInterface) in CMSSW.
* [ExHuME![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://projects.hepforge.org/exhume/) is a simulation of central exclusive production. It implements the [Khoze-Martin-Ryskin![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/0111078) pQCD calculation of p p → pXp, where X is a centrally produced colour singlet system. Its interface resides in  [CMSSW/GeneratorInterface/ExhumeInterface![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmssw.cvs.cern.ch/cgi-bin/cmssw.cgi/CMSSW/GeneratorInterface/ExhumeInterface/) directory of the CMSSW cvs repository. Here are the instructions on [how to run ExhumeInterface](/twiki/bin//CMS/ExhumeInterface) in CMSSW.
* [EDDE![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://arxiv.org/abs/0711.1794) is a event generator for different Exclusive and Semi-Inclusive Double Diffractive processes. The interface for this generator resides in [CMSSW/GeneratorInterface/EDDEInterface![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmssw.cvs.cern.ch/cgi-bin/cmssw.cgi/CMSSW/GeneratorInterface/EDDEInterface/) directory of the CMSSW cvs repository. Here are the instructions on [how to run EDDEInterface](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/EDDEInterface?topicparent=CMSPublic.SWGuideFwdPhysics;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") in CMSSW.
* Madgraph/Pythia [procedure for generating two-photon processes](/twiki/bin//CMS/MadgraphTwoPhoton) and using the result in CMSSW.
* Procedure for using [LPAIR two-photon processes](/twiki/bin//CMS/LPAIRTwoPhoton) using the [HepMC](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/HepMC?topicparent=CMSPublic.SWGuideFwdPhysics;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") interface prior to the 3\_1\_X LHE  migration.
* Procedure for using [LPAIR two-photon processes](/twiki/bin//CMS/LPAIRTwoPhotonLHE) with CMSSW after the 3\_1\_X LHE  migration.
* Procedure for [generating photoproduced upsilons](/twiki/bin//CMS/UpsilonPhotoproduction) with Phiti and Starlight MC generators in CMSSW.

## CVS Subsystems and reserved for Heavy Ions in
![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/toggleopen-small.gif)Show Details...  ![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/toggleclose-small.gif)Hide Package Details
**/SimDataFormats/HiGenData** ( [CVS![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://.cvs.cern.ch/cgi-/.cgi//SimDataFormats/HiGenData/), [LXR![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmslxr.fnal.gov/lxr/source/SimDataFormats/HiGenData/) ): Generated Data
* This is the CVS area for data formats related to *generated & simulated* events (so far, this package contains: generated vertex & sub-event information)
**/DataFormats/HeavyIonEvent** ( [CVS![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://.cvs.cern.ch/cgi-/.cgi//DataFormats/HeavyIonEvent/), [LXR![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmslxr.fnal.gov/lxr/source/DataFormats/HeavyIonEvent/) ): For Reconstructed Data
* This package is for all kinds of data formats that are common for both generated and reconstructed data. This includes:
  + Centrality : Various detector deposits and assigned centrality
  + Event Plane : Various event plane angle values corresponding to different measures
**/RecoHI** ( [CVS![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://.cvs.cern.ch/cgi-/.cgi//RecoHI/), [LXR![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmslxr.fnal.gov/lxr/source/RecoHI/) ) :
* Subsystem for algorithms (EDProducers and related tools) that are used to produce data formats of the kinds that are in DataFormats/HeavyIonEvent. include: [HiCentralityAlgos![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://.cvs.cern.ch/cgi-/.cgi//RecoHI/HiCentralityAlgos), [/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://.cvs.cern.ch/cgi-/.cgi//RecoHI/HiEvtPlaneAlgos), [![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://.cvs.cern.ch/cgi-/.cgi//RecoHI/), [HiEgammaAlgos![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://.cvs.cern.ch/cgi-/.cgi//RecoHI/HiEgammaAlgos), [HiJetAlgos![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://.cvs.cern.ch/cgi-/.cgi//RecoHI/HiJetAlgos)
**/CondFormats/HIObjects** ( [CVS![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://.cvs.cern.ch/cgi-/.cgi//CondFormats/HIObjects/), [LXR![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmslxr.fnal.gov/lxr/source/CondFormats/HIObjects/) ) : For Conditions Database Objects
* Package to hold conditions objects that are related to Heavy Ions.
**/CondCore/HIPlugins** ( [CVS![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://.cvs.cern.ch/cgi-/.cgi//CondCore/HIPlugins/), [LXR![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmslxr.fnal.gov/lxr/source/CondCore/HIPlugins/) ) : To register conditions objects**/HeavyIonsAnalysis/Configuration** ( [CVS![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://.cvs.cern.ch/cgi-/.cgi///HeavyIonsAnalysis/), [LXR![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmslxr.fnal.gov/lxr/source/HeavyIonsAnalysis/) ): For Physics Analysis
* For high level heavy ion analysis code, EDAnalyzers and configurations
* Currently keeping analysis code in UserCode e.g. `UserCode/CmsHi/JetAnalysis`
## Generators
**PYQUEN**
* The [PYQUEN event generator![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://lokhtin.web.cern.ch/lokhtin/pyquen/) is integrated into . Main contacts: / / Igor Lokhtin.

**HYDJET**
* The [HYDJET event generator![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://lokhtin.web.cern.ch/lokhtin/hydro/) is integrated into . Main contacts: / / Igor Lokhtin.

* Interface info available [here](/twiki///CMSPublic/SWGuideHijingInterface)

* Interface info available [here](/twiki///CMSPublic/SWGuideAMPTInterface)
**J/Ψ, ϒ and Z generation**
* Generation can follow a flat particle gun or a distribution file of our choice (like Ramona Vogt's distribution for example). Details can be found [here](/twiki///CMSPublic/SWGuideHeavyIonDileptonGeneration)
**Generator **
* Tools for heavy ion event generation which are not specific to an individual generator, e.g. HiCentralityBiasFilter, GenEvtSelectors. Details can be found [here](/twiki///CMSPublic/SWGuideHeavyIonGeneratorTools)

**Full Simulation**

A reminder or maybe new information for people that are just  started with  on sources of information to find (back) ) The CMS Offline [WorkBook](/twiki///CMSPublic/WorkBook)**[https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki///CMS/WorkBook](/twiki///CMSPublic/WorkBook)A very complete introduction to  and computing in CMS.
Explains how many things work in the generation, simulation,
digitisation and reconstruction. Also contains many pointers.**2) The CMS Offline Guide**[https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki///CMS/SWGuide](/twiki///CMSPublic/SWGuide)Not quite as complete in all areas, but explains a lot
about the [EDM](/twiki///CMSPublic/EDM) (Event Data Model) and the Framework that
form the basis of .**3) The LXR Cross Referencer**[http://cmslxr.fnal.gov/lxr/source/![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmslxr.fnal.gov/lxr/source/)The fastest (only) way to quickly find your away around the
 source code and . It allows the lookup
of identifiers and random text for any version of .
It is also great to just browse and read.**4) Google**A very efficient way to find info about CMS/
add "site:twiki.cern.ch" to find things in the CMS
twiki. For example, search formixingmodule site:twiki.cern.ch/twiki///CMSreturns a top three of highly relevant pages documenting
mixing/pileup in  (try for yourself!)**5) Example and Standard configuration samples**The [ repository![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://.cvs.cern.ch/cgi-/.cgi//) contains default and example configuration
files you can use and derive from. In particular see:

## Introduction
This wiki topic collects and provides information about (the software implementation of) the High Level (HLT) of CMS in the CMS software framework/EDM.
The HLT is discussed in the [TSG](/twiki/bin//CMS/TriggerStudies) ( studies group), see [INDICO server![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://indico.cern.ch/categoryDisplay.py?categId=1576) for the presentations. The HLT algorithms and performance are described in **CERN/LHCC 2007-021** ( [pdf![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cdsweb.cern.ch/record/1043242/files/lhcc-2007-021.pdf)).Operation of the HLT follows that of the [Level-1](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideL1Trigger) . The output of the online process is the so-called RAW data tier, which contains the raw data plus triggers plus some high-level objects reconstructed during HLT running for accepted events.The updated recipes on how to get and the HLT menu is available at [SWGuideGlobalHLT](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideGlobalHLT)The general information about the TSG (triggers studies group) is available at [TriggerStudies](/twiki/bin//CMS/TriggerStudies)
## HLT Description
### How it works
The HLT contains many paths, each corresponding to a dedicated (such as a prescaled single-electron or a 3-jets-with-MET ).
A path consists of several steps (software modules), each module performing a well-defined task such as unpacking (raw to digi), reconstruction of physics objects (electrons, muons, jets, MET, etc.), making intermediate decisions triggering more refined reconstructions in subsequent modules, or calculating the final decision for a path.
The CMSSW Framework/EDM ensures that if an intermediate filter decision on a path is negative, the rest of the path is not executed (skipped) and the specific is regarded as rejecting the event. In order to save CPU time, each reconstruction step is followed by a filter in order to avoid running time-consuming reco code if it is already clear it will not be needed.In general it is expected that all HLT paths are , even if the event is already accepted by a path. In case this turns out to be too time-consuming, a truncated mode of HLT operations should be foreseen where the HLT short-circuits after the first accept (and after the triggers needed to classify the event for a primary data set and output stream are computed) and does not the rest of the triggers. Presumably, the triggers not online could be in the offline reconstruction step to compute all bits (for events written out) in order to get a complete picture allowing efficiency studies.Each HLT path must be seeded by one or more L1 bit seeds: the first filter module in each HLT path is looking for a suitable L1 seed (consisting of L1 bit[s] and L1 object[s]) as a starting point for that specific HLT .
### Technical Aspects
The HLT is configured by specifying the paths, being built from individual software modules and/or already defined sequences of modules, using the parameter set configuration language (see [WorkBookConfigFileIntro](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookConfigFileIntro)).For example, a hypothetical di-jet + MET may look like this:
```
  myPrescJetMet    = cms.EDProducer("PrescJetMet", ...  // config of prescaler module
  myL1seedFilter   = cms.EDFilter("L1seedFilter", ...  // config of filter module
  myJetReco        =  cms.EDProducer(" ...  // config of reconstruction module
   =  cms.EDFilter(" ...  // config of filter module
  myMetReco        = cms.EDProducer(" ...  // config of reconstruction module
  myMetFilter      = cms.EDFilter(" ...    // config of filter module
  path dijetMET = {myPrescJetMet, myL1seedFilter, myJetReco, , myMetReco, myMetFilter}
```
It is possible to have different instances of any module (algorithm) if different values of their module parameters are needed. Each software module is either an [EDProducer](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideEDProducer) (reconstruction modules) or an [HLTFilter![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/blob/HEAD/HLTrigger/HLTcore/interface/HLTFilter.h) (subclassed from [EDFilter![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/blob/HEAD/FWCore/Framework/interface/EDFilter.h), to filter on conditions and do related book-keeping), getting its input (an EDProduct) from the Event, and, in case of an EDProducer, putting its output (another EDProduct) into the Event.For accepted events, either all intermediate and final EDProducts of all paths are written out - aka HLTDEBUG event content (CMS.RelVal, fraction of real data events) or only the highest-level collections (aka "L3" collections) and highest-level filter decisions (aka "L3" filters) are packed up in a single EDProduct and saved (MC bulk production), also depending on data tier - DEBUG, RAW, RECO, AOD.
In the HLTDEBUG case, the original collections are saved; thus it is possible to trace back from intermediate and final HLT filter decisions of a to the individual reconstructed objects (members of collections of reconstructed physics objects) used in that decision. Especially in case of "accept" decisions, the physics objects leading to the accept (EDProducts or members thereof) are accessible just knowing the and filter module.
The possible number of reconstructed objects or amount of detailed object information which is to be saved in the non-HLTDEBUG case (and cross-referenced from the results) depends on time and progress in understanding the needs.Modules performing reconstruction tasks (EDProducers, making new collections of reconstructed objects) should ideally be taken from the standard off-line reconstruction, with parameters configured for HLT, unless more drastic optimisation (in terms of memory and CPU time usage) is needed. By the same token, reconstructed objects in the HLT are thus standard reconstruction objects. The high-level cuts - as opposed to low-level reconstruction cuts - are implemented as HLT filters (subclassed in turn from EDFilters, making intermediate decisions to proceed on the path or making the final decision of the path).
### Services provided by the framework/EDM
Modules (EDProducers or HLTFilters) with different module (algorithm) parameters are considered different module instances. The Framework/EDM ensures that each module instance is called only once, and that the results, in case they are needed again, are simply re-used, see: [SWGuideEDMPathsAndTriggerBits](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideEDMPathsAndTriggerBits)Pre-scaling: A generic EDFilter module performing a configurable prescale is available, see the description at [SWGuideEDMPathsAndTriggerBits#Generic\_prescale\_module](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideEDMPathsAndTriggerBits#Generic_prescale_module). However, within the HLT context, the [PrescaleService![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/blob/HEAD/FWCore/PrescaleService/) must be used involving additional book-keeping, hence within the HLT one must use only instances of the [HLTPrescaler![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/blob/HEAD/HLTrigger/HLTcore/interface/HLTPrescaler.h) class and module. The configured module instance is inserted as a filter into the HLT path of the to be prescaled. If this module is at the very end of the path, the decision for the event from that path is still computed, allowing the study of efficiencies with higher statistics. However, in order to save the processing time, the prescale module is usually put at the beginning of the path.Basic timing and memory-usage services are provided by the framework, see: [SWGuideEDMTimingAndMemory](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideEDMTimingAndMemory). The framework counts events as they progress through each path and module instance, and provides a summary printout at the end of the , see: [SWGuideEDMPathsAndTriggerBits#Summary\_report](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideEDMPathsAndTriggerBits#Summary_report). This printout includes the time taken by each module and path, averaged over all events processed.A MessageLogger service is available as well ([SWGuideMessageLogger](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideMessageLogger)), which must be used instead of "cout/clog/cerr".
## Persistent
Depending on use case, two or three persistent HLT products are available:
* A [TriggerResults![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/blob/HEAD/DataFormats/Common/interface/TriggerResults.h) product (subclassed from [HLTGlobalStatus![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/blob/HEAD/DataFormats/Common/interface/HLTGlobalStatus.h) object, described in this section), containing all the usual decision bits,
* A [TriggerEvent![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/blob/HEAD/DataFormats/HLTReco/interface/TriggerEvent.h), summarising the "L3" collections and "L3" filter decisions,
* A [TriggerEventWithRefs![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/blob/HEAD/DataFormats/HLTReco/interface/TriggerEventWithRefs.h) product, summarising the Refs to all collections and all filter decisions (requires the pointed-to collections to be present, i.e., only useful on files with the HLTDEBUG event content).
The TriggerResults product (one, available for events written to output) allows access to the configuration and decisions, i.e., all the usual " bits", including:
* Final decision of individual path and of full table
* Which triggers were (some triggers may not due to lack of a corresponding L1 seed or HLT running in truncated mode)
* For each rejecting the event, (the index of) which intermediate or final module instances on the path rejected the event
* For each encountering an error condition, (the index of) which module instances on the path encountered un-recoverable errors (leading the event to be also routed to an error stream)
The rationale for the (predecessors to the) TriggerEvent and TriggerEventWithRefs products is described [here](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideHLTGlobalObject); the technical implementation is by now different. In particular, we now use explicit typing instead of polymorphism.Old class documentation is here: [SWGuideDataFormatHLTrigger](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideDataFormatHLTrigger)The package [HLTrigger/HLTcore![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/blob/HEAD/HLTrigger/HLTcore/plugins/) contains several analyzers pulling out the information.
You can use the corresponding analyzers directly - see their `cfi` files in the python subdirectory - or copy relevant code pieces into your
modules.
* `TriggerSummaryAnalyzerAOD` - analyser printing the content of the TriggerEvent product
* `TriggerSummaryAnalyzerRAW` - analyser printing the content of the TriggerEventWithRefs product
* `HLTEventAnalyzerAOD` - analyser combining the information from TriggerResults and TriggerEvent products
* `HLTEventAnalyzerRAW` - analyser combining the information from TriggerResults and TriggerEventWithRefs products
The `HLTEventAnalyzer` \* plugins make use of the helper class `HLTConfigProvider` (also in `HLTrigger/HLTcore`), which extracts the HLT configuration (paths, modules) from the [provenance](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookCMSSWFramework#ProvenanceTrackingLink). **Note:** this helper class must be initialised calling it's `init(...)` from the `beginRun()` method of your plugin using this helper class. The reason that it has to be (re-)initialised in `beginRun()` is that the HLT configuration can (only) change at the boundary between runs. See the `HLTEventAnalyzer` \* plugins as examples on how to use the `HLTConfigProvider` class.
## Policies and rules for HLT code
### Location of code in repository
As discussed above, each HLT path is a sequence of reconstruction and filter module instances. Modules correspond to C++ classes with each module instance by the corresponding to a different setting of the module configuration parameters.Reconstruction modules used in HLT paths reside either in some package of their subdetector subsystem or in some other, higher-level reconstruction subsystem/package, even if they are different from the corresponding standard offline reconstruction modules (due to the requirement of using variants of algorithms optimised for CPU-time or other constraints of the online system).
This should allow tighter integration and comparison as well as coherent development with the corresponding offline reconstruction modules.In contrast, however, the filter modules on an HLT path all reside in packages within the subsystem HLTrigger:
* HLT framework code resides in [HLTrigger/HLTcore![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/blob/HEAD/HLTrigger/HLTcore/).
* Example and important generic HLT filters are provided in [HLTrigger/HLTfilters![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/blob/HEAD/HLTrigger/HLTfilters/).
* Example modules are provided in [HLTrigger/HLTexample![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/blob/HEAD/HLTrigger/HLTexample/)
* Specific HLT filter modules and for *TriggerGroup* s such as CMS.JetMET, Egamma, , btau, etc., reside in their respective Package under HLTrigger: HLTrigger/\_TriggerGroup\_.
* Configuration of the global table resides in [HLTrigger/Configuration![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/blob/HEAD/HLTrigger/Configuration/)
### HLT filters (and producers)
Filtering (i.e., implementation of any kind of "" cuts) must be performed by HLT filter modules, providing also the required book-keeping of physics objects used in filter decisions (see below for the details!). Therefore, do not use offline-analysis-oriented [Generic Selector /SWGuideGenericSelectors) or similar, because these are not HLT-aware. Also, do not "hide" high-level filter logic in producer modules.Further conventions enforced for HLT filter modules are:
* HLT filter classes (HLT filter modules) must derive from class `HLTFilter` in `HLTrigger/HLTcore` (attention: NOT EDFilter class).
* The C++ names of HLT filter classes must start with "HLT" .
* The module label (instance name) must start with "hlt".
* Any prescaling filtering must be performed using the `HLTPrescaler` filter class in `HLTrigger/HLTcore` (attention: NOT Prescaler class).
* Each HLT path must contain its own instance of an `HLTPrescaler`
* Each HLT filter class module is accompanied by an example `cfi` configuration file in the python directory (see also [here![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://hypernews.cern.ch/HyperNews/CMS/get/edmFramework/231/1.html) for conventions on file naming and suffixes such as `cfg`, `cfi` and `cff`).
* For reasons of performance as well as control over verbosity, any printout must only use  or `LogTrace` provided by the [MessageLogger](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideMessageLogger) service.
* EDProducts used by HLT filter modules as inputs must be identified using the InputTag type from the configuration language (see the example filters), not strings.
* Parameter names, as used for HLT filter module configuration in , must follow the naming convention MinName, MaxName, such as , `MaxEta`, or `MinN`, etc. (note capitalisation), with all filters using the same name for the same quantity. This helps to get a faster overview on the configuration of different HLT filters.
* The C++ names of such configuration variables, as they are data members of the filter class, should start with a lower-case letter and end in an underscore (e.g., `min_Pt_`, `max_Eta_`, `min_N_`, in direct correspondence to the name used in the ), for easy identification in the class code. Again, all filters should use the same name for the same quantity.
* In general, the CMSSW [rules![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmsdoc.cern.ch/cms/cpt/Software/html/General/CodingAndStyleRules.pdf) on naming, coding and style are to be followed.
* Instead of writing several different filter classes for similar filter algorithms, use (or extend) existing filters, or template it.
* Each HLT filter module must put an [TriggerFilterObjectWithRefs![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/blob/HEAD/DataFormats/HLTReco/interface/) into the Event, which records "L3" collection tags as well as Refs pointing to those "L3" physics objects which passed this filter module. See the example filters for the C++ code on how this is done. This requires the pointed-to physics objects to be classes available in [TriggerRefsCollection![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/blob/HEAD/DataFormats/HLTReco/interface/)
* HLT filter classes may not perform any heavy time-consuming computations. Typically, they acquire a collection of objects, loop over them and apply simple cuts on quantities derived from the objects in the collection. In case these quantities turn out to require heavy computing, one should factor out that computation into a separate reconstruction module (for example, in a reconstruction module producing an WorkBookAssociationMap - see [DataFormats/Common![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/blob/HEAD/DataFormats/Common/) - associating the newly calculated variables to objects in an existing collection, which makes these quantities available for re-use by other modules in the same or in another HLT path). As a consequence, HLT filter classes contain very little code (Rule of thumb: if the code of the filter class does not fit on a screen, it's too long!).
* Conversely, producer modules should not implement cuts (as opposed to low-level reconstruction cuts).
### Access by the HLT to Level-1 informations
* Each HLT path starts out with its specific module instance of the general `HLTLevel1GTSeed` filter module (class located in [HLTfilters![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/blob/HEAD/HLTrigger/HLTfilters/src) ), configured for the specific HLT path
* The `HLTLevel1GTSeed` filter module takes as configuration the list of Level-1 bits of interest for the given HLT path. The module's `cfi` file is available [here![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/blob/HEAD/HLTrigger/HLTfilters/python/hltLevel1GTSeed_cfi.py). The module accesses the Level-1 data using the [l1extra](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideL1Extra) classes to obtain
  + the L1 decision for the set of Level-1 triggers requested in its configuration, and
  + the Level-1 physics objects (L1 EM, jets, muons, taus in the Candidate hierarchy) whiche fired the requested Level-1 set.
* The Boolean filter decision of the `HLTLevel1GTSeed` filter module is simply the combination of the requested Level-1 triggers
* The HLT filter object placed into the Event by the `HLTLevel1GTSeed` filter contains refs to all the physics objects found at Level-1 which fired the requested L1 triggers. Through the persistent references kept in the filter object as well, one can go down to the specific l1extra objects and their collections, and, if really needed, from there then further down to the level of the Level-1 internal objects. HLT modules should make use of the filter object placed by the `HLTLevel1Seed` filter and access the selected L1 objects through that, rather than accessing L1 classes directly.
* Hence this HLT filter object provides a list of seed objects for regional unpacking and/or regional reconstruction, etc., of interest for the specific HLT path; it can of course be used by any module on the path.
## Event selection using bits
In case you want to select events based on Level-1 bits, simply use the `HLTLevel1Seed` filter described above.The `TriggerResultsFilter` is able to parse any logical expression composed of L1 algorithmic triggers (e.g., `L1_SingleMu3`), L1 technical triggers (e.g., `L1Tech_BSC_minBias_OR`) and HLT paths (e.g., `HLT_Mu9` or `AlCa_EtaPi0`). More information is provided in its own [twiki](/twiki/bin//CMS/TriggerResultsFilter) page.For a list of HLT names, look here: [SWGuideGlobalHLT](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideGlobalHLT) .
## Event selection using a (new) tighter HLT path
The filter `HLTSummaryFilter` allows to cut on the 4-momentum representation of objects having fired an L3 filter. This is useful for studies of new triggers resembling existing triggers but with higher thresholds on the final objects. [here![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/blob/HEAD/HLTrigger/HLTfilters/python/hltSummaryFilter_cfi.py).
## Access to the HLT configuration - the HLTConfigProvider
The [HLTConfigProvider![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/blob/HEAD/HLTrigger/HLTcore/interface/HLTConfigProvider.h) is a helper class allowing your CMSSW code access to the HLT configuration with which the data was taken, such as streams and data sets, paths and filters, configurations of paths and their modules, etc. (including HLT prescale sets). The information is extracted from the [provenance](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookCMSSWFramework#ProvenanceTrackingLink), which itself is stored inside the data (or MC) event files.The `HLTConfigProvider` class is located in the package [HLTrigger/HLTcore![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/blob/HEAD/HLTrigger/HLTcore/). For both efficiency reasons and allowing proper initialization, you must put an instance of this class as a data member in your producer/analyzer/filter plugin (beware: it is really very inefficient to put it as a local variable in any method of your class!), for example:
```
#include "HLTrigger/HLTcore/interface/HLTConfigProvider.h"
...
class  : public EDAnalyzer {
...
/// Make this a configurable module parameter of your plugin:
string processName_; // process name of (HLT) process for which to get HLT configuration
/// The instance of the HLTConfigProvider as a data member
HLTConfigProvider hltConfig_;
...
}
```
The HLTConfigProvider is then initialized in your plugin's `beginRun(.)` method. This is done because the
HLT configuration can change between Runs, and you need to pick up the new configuration.
```
::beginRun(edm:: const & iRun, edm::EventSetup const& iSetup)
{
  bool changed(true);
  if (hltConfig_.init(iRun,iSetup,processName_,changed)) {
    // if init returns TRUE, initialisation has succeeded!
    if (changed) {
     // The HLT config has actually changed wrt the previous , hence rebook your
     // histograms or do anything else dependent on the revised HLT config
     ...
    }
  } else {
    // if init returns FALSE, initialisation has NOT succeeded, which indicates a problem
    // with the file and/or code and needs to be investigated!
    ") << " HLT config extraction failure with process name " << processName_;
    // In this case, all access methods will return empty values!
  }
}
```
The `init` method (if it returns `true`) of the `HLTConfigProvider` unpacks and caches all HLT configuration information internally, allowing fast and efficient access via the `HLTConfigProvider` 's const-ref access methods. Therefore it is a waste of resources (CPU time and RAM memory) to use local variables or data members simply to hold the HLT information accessed through the `HLTConfigProvider`. Since the HLT configuration is identical for all events of a , your setup work depending on the HLT configuration should all be done in your plugin's `beginRun` method. If the init method returns false, the internal caches of the `HLTConfigProvider` will be cleared and reset to empty/zero. Hence you need to check the return value of `init` and take appropriate action in your plugin, such as skipping booking/filling histograms or any other processing depending on a valid HLT configuration (experience shows that many -time problems reported are due to developers NOT paying attention to the return value of `init`).Once successfully initialized in `beginRun`, you can then call in your plugin's `begin` / `endRun`, `begin` / `endLumiBlock`, or `analyze` / `produce` / `filter` methods any of the various public const accessor methods of the HLTConfigProvider to get information on the HLT configuration. For a list of available access methods providing all the information, see the header file [HLTConfigProvider.h![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/blob/HEAD/HLTrigger/HLTcore/interface/HLTConfigProvider.h).
### HLT Prescales
HLT prescales in force when the data was taken are also accessed through the `HLTConfigProvider` helper class (see above) in CMSSW, but in a special way described in the following. The HLT configuration contains several pre-configured sets of prescale values, to cover different instantaneous luminosities - say, *N* sets of prescale values, with prescale value set indices running from 0 to *N* -1. For real data, the prescale sets are saved in the Provenance (and thus available through the `HLTConfigProvider` class) only since 136393 when `CMSSW_3_5_7_onlpatch4` was put online (28-May-2010). For MC, these are available since `CMSSW_3_5`, but note that on MC all L1 and HLT prescales are set to 1 anyway.**HOWEVER:** The index number of which prescale set is currently in use is stored in an **L1 Event** data product: the same index is used to select the L1 prescale set as well as the HLT prescale set. While the access to the HLT prescale sets is available as any other HLT configuration information (i.e., after a successfull init of the `HLTConfigProvider` class), the active prescale set index number and thus the currently active HLT prescale set (prescale value for each HLT path) are thus ONLY available through `HLTConfigProvider` accessors expecting also the Event data-structure (ie, these accessors can not be called in `begin` / `endRun` nor `begin` / `endLumiBlock`, but only in the `produce` / `analyze` / `filter` methods). It also means the relevant L1 product must be in the input data file (either directly or unpacked from the raw data collection before your plugin comes along).The following accessors for HLT prescales are available as methods of the `HLTConfigProvider` class:
```
  /// prescale value for a given set index number (in case you know it from elsewhere)
  /// and a given  path
  unsigned int prescaleValue(unsigned int set, const std::string& ) const;
  /// getting the current (active) prescale set index number (needs Event/EventSetup as parameters)
  int prescaleSet(const edm::Event& iEvent, const edm::EventSetup& iSetup) const;
  /// in case a negative number such as -1 is returned, the prescale set index number could not be obtained
  /// getting directly the currently active prescale value for a given  path
  /// (calls above prescaleSet and prescaleValue methods internally)
  unsigned int prescaleValue(const edm::Event& iEvent, const edm::EventSetup& iSetup, const std::string& ) const;
```
Note: the prescale set index number itself can only change between luminosity sections, for events within a lumi section it stays constant!To get the current prescale set index number from the L1 data, the L1 helper class [L1GtUtils](/twiki/bin//CMS/SWGuideL1TriggerL1GtUtils) is used internally by the `HLTConfigProvider`. This is a class similar in spirit to HLT's `HLTConfigProvider` class but for L1 information, including L1 prescales. This L1 helper class requires the corresponding L1 data product to be in the input file (either directly, or unpacked from the raw data collection before your plugin comes along) - if this is not the case, the method `prescaleSet()` returns -1, and `prescaleValue()` falls back to returning 1. Hence you should always check `prescaleSet()` first before using `prescaleValue()`.
### L1T and HLT Prescales for HLT paths
In recent versions of the `HLTConfigProvider` class (see the header file [HLTConfigProvider.h![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/blob/HEAD/HLTrigger/HLTcore/interface/HLTConfigProvider.h)
for the CMSSW release you are using), an additional method is available which also returns the prescale of the L1 seeding an HLT path. This obviously works only for HLT paths which are seeded by exactly (at most) one L1 physics bit. The `HLTConfigProvider` will print an informative LogError message in case something goes wrong. The corresponding accessor method is:
```
  /// Combined L1T (pair.first) and HLT (pair.second) prescales per HLT path
  std::pair<int,int> prescaleValues(const edm::Event& iEvent, const edm::EventSetup& iSetup, const std::string& ) const;
  // any one negative => error in retrieving this (L1T or HLT) prescale
```
In the CMSSW 7 series, a further prescale accessor, `prescaleValuesInDetail()`, has been added, which is usefull in the case the L1 seed condition of an HLT path is a complicated Boolean expression, such as `'L1_DoubleEG5 OR L1_SingleEG10'`. This new accessor:
```
std::pair<std::vector<std::pair<std::string,int> >,int> prescaleValuesInDetail(const edm::Event& iEvent, const edm::EventSetup& iSetup, const std::string& ) const;
```
takes the HLT path name, figures out its L1 seed condition, and returns a vector of pairs, with the first component being the individual L1 name (such as L1\_DoubleEG5) and the second component the L1 prescale valaue for it, this for all [L1Ts](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/L1Ts?topicparent=CMSPublic.SWGuideHighLevelTrigger;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") used in the seed expression. This vector is then combined, with the (single) HLT prescale used at HLT level for the HLT path in question, in another pair, and retuned to the user.The usage of this accessor is best described as follows: in almost all cases of a complex L1 seed Boolean expression, the expression is an OR of several [L1Ts](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/L1Ts?topicparent=CMSPublic.SWGuideHighLevelTrigger;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it."), say n of those. In such a case, the HLT path can be regarded as a short hand notation of n HLT paths, each with a single [L1T](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/L1T?topicparent=CMSPublic.SWGuideHighLevelTrigger;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") as seed condition. An analysis user would pick ONE
of those paths and derive the corresponding overall prescale as the product of [L1T](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/L1T?topicparent=CMSPublic.SWGuideHighLevelTrigger;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") prescale and HLT prescale, select events based on passing both the single [L1T](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/L1T?topicparent=CMSPublic.SWGuideHighLevelTrigger;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") condition and the (combined) HLT path, and calculate the effective luminosity.As before, the helper class [L1GtUtils](/twiki/bin//CMS/SWGuideL1TriggerL1GtUtils) is used internally, so the above remarks on `L1GtUtils` apply here as well.

body:
If you are experiencing TWiki instability from outside the CERN network, please connect via the CERN internal network - see [KB0010688![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cern.service-now.com/service-portal?id=KB0010688) for details
>![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/web-bg-small.gif) [CMSPublic Web](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WebHome)>[SWGuide](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuide)>[SWGuideCrab](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideCrab)>[SWGuideLcgAccess](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideLcgAccess "Topic revision: 64 (2026-03-31 - 10:54:10)") (2026-03-31, )[![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/uweb-o14.gif) Edit](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/SWGuideLcgAccess?t=1777851196;nowysiwyg=1 "Edit this topic text")[Attach](/twiki/bin/attach/CMSPublic/SWGuideLcgAccess "Attach an image or document to this topic")[PDF](/twiki/bin/genpdf/CMSPublic/SWGuideLcgAccess "Create a PDF file for the topic")
# How to get access to WLCG
Contents:
* [How to get access to WLCG](#How_to_get_access_to_WLCG)
  + [Summary](#Summary)
  + [Getting an account on a User Interface](#Getting_an_account_on_a_User_Int)
  + [Getting a personal certificate](#Getting_a_personal_certificate)
  + [How to register in the CMS VO](#How_to_register_in_the_CMS_VO)
    - [Registration](#Registration)
    - [AUP](#AUP)
    - [groups](#groups)
      * [Technical note](#Technical_note)
    - [CERN Human Resources registration](#CERN_Human_Resources_registratio)
  + [Troubleshooting -- Solutions to common problems](#Troubleshooting_Solutions_to_com)
## Summary
Three things are needed to have access to WLCG:
1. an account on a User Interface (any machine with the WLCG commands installed).
2. a personal certificate, used to authenticate with the Grid;
3. having your personal certificate registered in the CMS Virtual Organisation;
These steps are here explained in detail.Note: in order to obtain a Grid certificate, and later to register with CMS Virtual Organization, you will need to use your web browser.
The Certification Authority which your institution will refer you to will provide instructions from their side.
But eventually you will need to point your browser to servers hosted at CERN, for this you must be sure that your browser trusts the CERN certificates. Please follow instructions in <https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideVomsFAQ#CERN_Authority_root_certificate> . A direct link to CERN iinstructions is [https://cafiles.cern.ch/cafiles/certificates/list.aspx?ca=grid![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cafiles.cern.ch/cafiles/certificates/list.aspx?ca=grid)Note that the proper procedure, regardless of which browser you are using, is NOT just to grant exceptions for each and every site you visit on a case-by-case basis, but instead it is important to use the certificate authority files as described above to set up the proper trust anchor paths for your browser and operating system.
## Getting an account on a User Interface
A machine with the WLCG commands installed is, by definition, a User Interface (UI). Many institutes have local UIs; at CERN and LPC the needed commands are installed on the interactive login nodes, they are also available inside CMS Singularity apptainers (`/cvmfs/cms.cern.ch/common/cmssw-*`).
## Getting a personal certificate
A personal certificate consists of a pair of files, the private key (userkey.pem) and the certificate itself, containing the public key (usercert.pem). To obtain a certificate, a request has to be made to a Certification Authority recognized by WLCG. You have three options, ordered from most preferred to least preferred:
1. request a certificate from the CERN CA using your CERN computer account ( [instructions here](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/PersonalCertificate));
2. find out from the list of recognized [International Grid Trust Federation Certification Authorities![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://www.igtf.net) the one that provides service to your country and request a certificate from that CA following the procedures published on their web site;
3. request a certificate from the WLCG catch-all CA if no CA exists for your country and you do not have a CERN NICE/lxplus account.
Special note for German collaborators: If you are a member of a German CMS institution, they require you to use a certificate from the [German CA![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://www.gridka.de). You can contact your local institution for more details.
## How to register in the CMS VO
**NEW AS OF JUNE 2024
### Registration
If you are a valid CMS member with a CERN computer account you are automatically registerd in CMS VO with the CERN certificate corresponding to your CERN primary account (almost all people have only one account and do not need to care what primary means).If you want to use (also) a non-CERN certificate, you need to add it to your CERN account profile as described in <https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/UsernameForCRAB#Adding_your_DN_to_your_profile>
* currently (June 2024) Robot certificate need special care.
  1. adding them to your CERN account profile will only work for certificates from other CA's then CERN
  2. robot certificates from CERN need to be added manually into CRIC by CMS CRIC admins. Those certificate will then automatically propagate to IAM (to allow `voms-proxy-init`) and will be able to access CMSWEB and to authenticate witth CERN [EOS](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/EOS).
  3. To contact CMS CRIC admins use the  [forum![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cms-talk.web.cern.ch/c/offcomp/comptools/87)
### AUP
As a new user you need to sign the Grid Acceptable Usage Policy (AUP), and to sign it again every year. If you have not done it or your signature expired, when you do `voms-proxy-init -voms cms` you will see this message : `User ... needs to sign AUP for this organization in order to proceed.` (alternately, this has been observed when a signature is needed: `None of the contacted servers for cms were capable of returning a valid AC for the user`)
* use your browser to visit [cms-auth![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cms-auth.cern.ch) server (a.k.a. CMS IAM server) and login using CERN's SSO
* you will be automatically prompted with a page were to to sign
  + if not (e.g. you want to re-sign before expiration) visit [https://cms-auth.cern.ch/iam/aup/sign![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cms-auth.cern.ch/iam/aup/sign) A button for singing AUP is also available in your home page in [IAM![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cms-auth.cern.ch/dashboard#!/home) (a.k.a. `cms-auth`) if you scroll down a bit
* Done. You can now user your CERN certificate to access CMS VO resources**
### groups
pick your VOMS groups and roles if needed
* Most CMS user should not select any group nor role, but some national organization have specific rules (below), user can contact directly their institution for doubts. Note that this particular part may change later as we learn how best to use the new IAM tool
|  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- |
| User from | should select group | and role |
| US-CMS | /cms/uscms | None |
| Germany | /cms/dcms | None |
| Spain | /cms/escms | None |
| Belgium | /cms/becms | None |
#### Technical note
There are 3 services involved in making you able to use a Grid certificate
* CERN LDAP server shows that your primary CERN account is a valid CMS Member and lists your additional non-CERN certificates
* [CRIC![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cms-cric.cern.ch) lists all CMS members, their DN's, groups and is used to feed [IAM![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cms-auth.cern.ch) and the list of DN's who cam access CMSWEB and CMS [EOS](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/EOS)
* [IAM![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cms-auth.cern.ch) replaces old VOMS servers to allow you to get am X509 proxy via `voms-proxy-init -voms cms` that you can use to use grid tools from CLI (rather then browser), like CRAB, dasgoclient, gfal, xrootd .
### CERN Human Resources registration
All new CMS users will be registered automatically in CERN Human Resource database. In rare cases this may not work or be delayed. If you believe that you are affected, please contact CERN's User Office after having made sure that your CMS status is good.To check if you are already registered in HR, follow these steps:
1. go to [http://graybook.cern.ch![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://graybook.cern.ch) ;
2. enter your family name in the "Find in Greybook" box a top right;
3. make sure that you appear in the resulting list with CMS in the Experiment Name column
## Troubleshooting -- Solutions to common problems
You can find [here](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideRunningGridPrerequisites#Test_your_grid_certificate) hints on how to verify that your grid certificate is working.If you try that and get an error message that you do not understand, and if you are sure that you have properly followed the VOMS registration procedure, the following are possible reasons:If you are getting an authorisation error when using WLCG commands, the cause can be one among many:
1. your proxy certificate has expired;
2. your personal certificate has expired (`None of the contacted servers for cms were capable of returning a valid AC for the user.` can be an error in that case);
   1. check your certificate's expiration date with this command: `openssl x509 -in ~/.globus/usercert.pem -noout -enddate`
3. you have renewed your certificate but you are still using your OLD private key;
4. your membership in the CMS-VO has expired, or you have not re-signed the grid [AUP![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cms-auth.cern.ch/iam/aup/sign) - connecting to that website will bring up a popup to re-sign the AUP.
You should be able to easily detect and solve those.
If there is any problem with your data in the CERN HR database, contact CERN User Office.If you really have a problem that you can not solve yourself, contact the CMS on CMS Talk (cmstalk+)
