## Contacts
* **TOSCA computation**:
* **CMSSW interface**: Nicola Amapane
## The CMS magnetic field map
The magnetic field map used in simulation, HLT and reconstruction is based on a FEM simulation that has been tuned to reproduce the measurements of the mapping campaign and compared to flux-loops and NMR measurements.<>In order to model the discontinuity at the iron-air boundaries **in the yoke, the field is obtained from a cubic interpolation** in a grid defined appropriately and separately for each magnetic volume.<>For speed and smoothness reasons, the field in the **tracker region** is obtained with a **parametrization** which models the and components with reasonable accuracy (neglecting the small b\_phi component and assuming phi symmetry).<>More details can be found in these presentations:
* [22/9/2014![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://indico.cern.ch/event/328166/session/1/contribution/24): Description of the map (current model cf slide 25 and onwards)
* [16/3/2010![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://indico.cern.ch/event/87530/#2-accuracy-of-the-magnetic-fie): accuracy of the map in the tracker region and comparison of different parametrizations.
## Usage
The python configuration to get the default field map is:
```
process.load("Configuration.StandardSequences.MagneticField_cff")
```
This sets the the map so that the I/ map is chosen automatically based on the GT, and the nominal working point is set automatically depending on the magnet current stored in the conditions DB (RunInfo). Nominal working points are:
* 0 T
* 2 T (9500 A)
* 3 T (14340 A)
* 3.5 T (16730 A)
* 3.8 T (18164 A)
* 4 T (19140 A)
**For the MC**, the magnet current in conditions is fixed, and corresponds to the 3.8 T working point; so the above always results in the 3.8 T map for MC GTs.In order to force **zero field (magnet off) in MC** one needs to replace the config with:
```
process.load("Configuration.StandardSequences.MagneticField_0T_cff")
```
Other nominal working points can be forced by replacing the "valueOverride" parameters that are set in the same file.
### Access to the map
The magnetic field map is available in CMSSW from the EventSetup as an object of type . An example of getting the magnetic field in CMSSW is available in
```
/Engine/test/queryField.cc
/Engine/test/queryField.py
```
This is everything needed for the general user.
### Alternative parametrizations of the field in the tracker region
The following parametrizations can be used for specific tasks and are valid only **within the tracker**.Note that the default map uses a reasonably fast and accurate parametrization in the tracker region ([OAEParametrizedMagneticField](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/OAEParametrizedMagneticField?topicparent=CMSPublic.SWGuideMagneticField;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.").cc) which is phi-symmetric and neglects the B\_phi components. This parametrization is found to be accurate at the level of 1 per mille [ [16/3/2010![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://indico.cern.ch/event/87530/#2-accuracy-of-the-magnetic-fie), slides 6-9].**Fast parametrization: [ParabolicParametrizedMagneticField](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/ParabolicParametrizedMagneticField?topicparent=CMSPublic.SWGuideMagneticField;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.")**For special tasks where speed is desired at the cost of some accuracy, **a very fast parametrization** is available in the standard sequence with the `'ParabolicMf'` label [ [code![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/blob/master/Configuration/StandardSequences/python/MagneticField_cff.py#L13-L15)]. It is used in standard sequences for some tracking tasks.This is based on a simple parabolic formula of (z), neglecting the and components, and is thus extremely fast.The component actually contributes to the transverse bending with an effect opposite of that of and a magnitude that can reach 1.4% of the field integral across a track at very large eta. For this reason the parametrization is tuned to **reproduce as closely as possible the field integral** ([BdL](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/BdL?topicparent=CMSPublic.SWGuideMagneticField;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") computed over a straight path originated in (0,0,0) and across the whole tracker) rather than the exact value. This choice has two potential shortcomings:
* If point-value of is needed, the parametrization will return a slightly lower value than the actual , since this component is reduced in the tuning to compensate to the missing effect of
* Tuning the parametrization to reproduce the total bending power is expected to give a more accurate prediction of the deflection angle, but not necessarily of the extrapolated position error: the bending power is "rearranged" along the path in order to get the same total bending power, but this can be done in infinite ways, that will give a different displacement after a given distance. The tuning in this case is done maintaining the constrain that the (z) dependence is parabolic.
The following plot shows some comparisons between the fast and default parametrizations.![](data:image/png;base64...)*Comparison of field integral between fast and default parametrization*![](data:image/png;base64...)<>*Zoom of the above plot*![](data:image/png;base64...)<>*Difference in total field integral for pointing paths in the tracker* *between fast and default parametrization***Detailed parametrizations of mapping data: [PolyFit2D](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/PolyFit2D?topicparent=CMSPublic.SWGuideMagneticField;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") and [PolyFit3D](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/PolyFit3D?topicparent=CMSPublic.SWGuideMagneticField;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.")**These detailed parametrizations reproduce accurately the measurements conducted during in 2006. A detailed comparison of these options with the default parametrization can be found in this presentation [ [16/3/2010![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://indico.cern.ch/event/87530/#2-accuracy-of-the-magnetic-fie)].
* **PolyFit2D:** Assumes phi-symmetry, B\_phi = 0. It is 4x slower than the standard parametrization.
* **PolyFit3D:** Models B\_phi and the smal phi-asymmetry of and , at a 50x cost in speed w.r.t the standard parametrization.
The following plot shows the **PolyFit3D/default** discrepancy in the [BdL](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/BdL?topicparent=CMSPublic.SWGuideMagneticField;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") integral for pointing tracks in the tracker [from ]. In terms of curvature, the ratio would translate in 1/z axis.![](data:image/png;base64...)It should be kept in mind that the measurements were done **on surface**, without HF, rotating shielding, YE-3, and (which was added in ). <>Monitoring of fixed NMR probes within the coil shows a field increase between mapping and I operating conditions of about 0.7~0.8 per mille [ [16/3/2010![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://indico.cern.ch/event/87530/#2-accuracy-of-the-magnetic-fie), slide 10]. <>According to the FEM simulation, the addition of changed the field integral in the tracker by less than 0.1 per mille [ [22/9/2014![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://indico.cern.ch/event/328166/session/1/contribution/24), slide 24].
## Internals
The following sections include developer documentation and are not relevant for users.
### How the field map works
Concrete implementations ("engines") of `a MagneticField` are available to deliver different maps in either the whole CMS or in specific parts of it. The default map is called VolumeBasedMagneticField, and is based on a geometrical description of the solenoid and yoke volumes, with a separate "field provider" for each volume. Normally a field provider is based on interpolation over a grid of points tabulated with a finite-element computation.<> Providers can however also be based on e.g. parametrizations. <>A special region is the inner tracker region. Here, VolumeBasedMagneticField allows to specify an ad-hoc parametrization to replace the normal volume/field provider mechanism, for either speed or accuracy purposes. Technically this is implemented by overlaying a "slave field engine" with a defined spatial validitity region.A **"static" map**, representing the for a given era ( I or ) and current, can be created explicitly with e.g. `MagneticField/Engine/python/volumeBasedMagneticField_160812_cfi.py` ( [link![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/blob/CMSSW_11_0_X/MagneticField/Engine/python/volumeBasedMagneticField_160812_cfi.py)). This cfi defaults to 3.8T, [RunII](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/RunII?topicparent=CMSPublic.SWGuideMagneticField;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") map.It sets:
* geometry reader
* the parametrized map to be used in the tracker region
* the actual [VolumeBased](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/VolumeBased?topicparent=CMSPublic.SWGuideMagneticField;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") map, whose configuration includes specification of the field data tables to be used (`version`) and how tables are associated to volumes (`gridFiles`).
Static maps should **not** be used in production.The **default map is dynamic** and built with `Configuration.StandardSequences.MagneticField_cff`, which retrieves the appropriate geometry and configuration from DB for the given GT and IOV.
The internals of this builder is docomented in the following section.
### Map sets and configuration in db
A map set consists of six maps for the five nominal operation currents, corresponding to 2, 3, 3.5, 3.8 and 4T, plus a zero-field map. The configuration for each map is stored in the condition DB in a MagneticFieldConfig object i, which includes:
* a geometry version (int);
* a data table version (string);
* a map of table names to be associated to volumes;
* optional scaling factors for specific tables;
* name and parameters of a slave parametrized field for the tracker region.
In each GT, configuration for all six maps of the set must be present. They are stored as separate MagneticFieldConfig objects with the pre-defined labels "0T", "2T", "3T", "3.5T", "3.8T", "4T".
The appropriate one is retrieved by label based on the coil current stored in the RunInfoRecord,The geometry version of the required configuration is used to retrieve the correct geometry from the db by label. Each GT thus contains all required geometries, attached to the record MFGeometryFileRcd, with labels like "180812", "90322", etc.To find what maps are included in a given GT, search fror the GT in conddb, eg for data and Run1/Run2 MC:
* data: [100X\_dataRun2\_HLT\_v3![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cms-conddb.cern.ch/cmsDbBrowser/list/Prod/gts/100X_dataRun2_HLT_v3)
* MC, run1: [90X\_mcRun1\_design\_v2](https://cms-conddb.cern.ch/cmsDbBrowser/list/Prod/gts/100X_mcRun1_design_v2 "100X_mcRun1_design_v3")
* MC, run2: [100X\_mcRun2\_design\_v2![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cms-conddb.cern.ch/cmsDbBrowser/list/Prod/gts/100X_mcRun2_design_v2)
Search for "MagFieldConfigRcd" in the Tags List table. You should get six entries with the labels "0T","2T", "3T", "3.5T", "3.8T", "4T" for the six maps of the set.Note that for data, the map should have IOVs for Run1/Run2 as needed. For MC, there should be only 1 valid IOV, since there are different GTs for Run1 or Run2.Available geometries can instead be found searching for "MFGeometryFileRcd".The following table summarizes the currently used map sets.

#### Summary of geometries currently loaded in the DB
XML files for the different geometry versions are located under [MagneticField](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/MagneticField?topicparent=CMSPublic.SWGuideMagneticField;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") /GeomBuilder/data:
* version 90322: `MagneticFieldVolumes_1103l.xml`. This geometry is suitable for rarely used maps (currently, only 2T and 4T)
* version 120812: `MagneticFieldVolumes_1_v7_large.xml`, `MagneticFieldVolumes_2_v7_large.xml` - no longer in use, should be removed from future GTs
* version 130503: `MagneticFieldVolumes_1_v9_large.xml`, `MagneticFieldVolumes_2_v9_large.xml` - no longer in use, should be removed from future GTs
* version 160812: `MagneticFieldVolumes_160812_1.xml`, `MagneticFieldVolumes_160812_2.xml` Current up-to- geometries.
### Data tables
The actual field data is stored in tables that are published under: [https://github.com/cms-data/MagneticField-Interpolation![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/cms-data/MagneticField-Interpolation)The grids in use in current releases are:grid\_11103l\_071212\_2t<>grid\_11103l\_071212\_4t<>grid\_160812\_3t<>grid\_160812\_3\_5t<>grid\_160812\_3\_8t<>grid\_160812\_3\_8t\_Run1The following grids are no longer used and can be removed:grid\_1103l\_071212\_3t<>grid\_1103l\_071212\_3\_5t<>grid\_1103l\_071212\_3\_8t<>grid\_120812\_3\_8t\_v7\_large<>grid\_120812\_3\_8t\_v7\_small<>grid\_130503\_3\_8t\_v9\_large<>grid\_130503\_3\_8t\_v9\_small<>grid\_1103l\_090322\_3\_8t
## Development workflow
The steps described below must be followed, in their order, to prepare, validate and deploy a new set of maps, assuming the starting point is a new xml geometry and a corresponding set of TOSCA grid tables in txt format.
For new tables for an already existing geometry, the first part can be skipped.
### Preparing a new geometry
Add the new xml file(s) in `Magfield/GeomBuilder/data`. Test geometry building by preparing a config file like `MagneticField/Engine/python/volumeBasedMagneticField_160812_cfi.py`, specifying:
* the new xml files in `magfield.geomXMLFiles`
* an empty `VolumeBasedMagneticFieldESProducer.gridFiles` list
Set this cfi in `MagneticField/Engine/test/testMagneticField_cfg.py` instead of the default one, and set `process.VolumeBasedMagneticFieldESProducer.debugBuilder = True` .
this and search for errors (“ERROR”). Some WARNINGs are normal if mismatches are small (normally <0.04 cm; can get up to 0.2 cm) .The `debugBuilder` flag activates the test `MagGeoBuilderFromDDD::testInside`, which tests that the center of a volume is inside it and outside all other volumes. There must be no error.Also with `process.testVolumeGeometry = cms.EDAnalyzer("testMagGeometryAnalyzer")`. This calls `MagGeometryExerciser::testFindVolume`, which checks random points: the corresponding volume should be found, and the points must be inside() one and only one volume. There must be no error. Note: internally this uses uses `MagGeometry::findVolume`, that has a retry mechanism with increased tolerance to avoid tiny gaps.
### Table conversion
To convert txt tables (extracted from TOSCA), use `MagneticField/Interpolation/test/BinaryTablesGeneration/convertTables.py`. Check for ERROR s in the output.
Note that files are provided both with cartesian (xyz) and cylindrical coordinates (rpz). They are equivalent, but it is better to use rpz for all volume types except than for and Trapezoid volumes.Once conversion is completed with no error, copy the new set of maps into `MagneticField/Interpolation/data` following the existing directory structure. Edit the cfi file (eg.
`MagneticField/Engine/python/volumeBasedMagneticField_130503_cfi.py`) and set `VolumeBasedMagneticFieldESProducer.version` to the name of the newly created directory in `MagneticField/Interpolation/data`, and specify the matching between grid files and volumes, eg:
```
    gridFiles = cms.VPSet(
           cms.PSet(
               volumes   = cms.string('1001-1464,2001-2464'),
               sectors   = cms.string('0') ,
               master    = cms.int32(0),
               path      = cms.string('s[s]/grid.[v].bin'),
           ),
```
With this syntax, all volumes numbered with range 1001-1464 and 2001-2464 for all sectors (0=all) are associated to the file s[sector]/grid.[volumeNumber].bin. The `master` specification can be used to use the table for a given sector for other sector as well by rotation, in order to save memory; 0 means that each sector will use its own specific table.`testMagneticField_cfg.py` with `debugBuilder = True` as explained above. It should now try to build interppolators for all volumes, reading the data tables. In addition a test is done, that each grid point should be inside() the corresponding volume. Search for ERRORs. They can be either due to errors in the tables (e.g. irregular grid spacing), or in the geometry (volume boundaries not matching the actual grid).
To debug possible problems with the grid tables, `MagneticField/Interpolation/test/BinaryTablesGeneration/GridFileReader.cpp` can be used to dump table grid and values. To dump the memory representation of the yable, opem `MagneticField/Engine/test/testMagneticField.cc` and uncomment/edit the block containing `vol->provider()` according to specific needs.The final check is to a regression of the field map vs the data tables, using `Interpolation/test/BinaryTablesGeneration/validateField_TOSCATables.py`. Set the cfi.py for the new geometry; the list of tables is taken from a file `tableList.txt`, that is written during conversion by `convertTables.py`.
Numerical discrepancies can be present in a handful of cases up to ~0.00065 T, especially in rotated tables. This could be be due to the appearance of spurious ~0 step parameters due to rounding in rotations. This level of accuracy is acceptable. Further study/development is needed to understand how to avoid these roundings.
#### Table optimization
Reading all the separate files for the table map can be time consuming. To optimize read back, all the files for a given table map can be merged together using `MagneticField/Interpolation/test/BinaryTablesGeneration/mergeFieldTable.cc`. To use, go into the directory containing the separate `s[sector]/` subdirectories and the command
```
mergeFileTable . merged
```
This will generate two files in the directory, `merged.index` and `merged.bin`. Once this is complete, rerun the same test as described in the above section.
### Publishing new tables for release
Once data tables are ready, they should be published submitting a PR to [https://github.com/cms-data/MagneticField-Interpolation![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/cms-data/MagneticField-Interpolation).
### Conversion of the geometry to db
Edit and `MagneticField/GeomBuilder/test/mfxmlwriter,py` and `mfwriter.py`. The first writes the geometry in a single, self-contained xml ; the second converts it into a .db file and creates the corresponding metadata faile for upload to the condition db.To load the geometry in the database:
```
uploadConditions.py <mfGeometryXXXXX.db>
```
### Preparing a db configuration
See above for an explanation of how map configuration is stored in the condition DB.A map configuration can be written into a .db file with `/CondFormats/MFObjects/test/writeMagFieldConfigDB.py`. The the corresponding metadata faile for upload to the condition db is also created.In general, before uploading to the condition db this .db file needs to be combined with others to get a single file with all IOVs for I and II maps.
## Debugging tools
### Regression Testing
Regression testing is available to validate changes that are not expected to change the field numerically in any point. It is done comparing the field returned by the map with a reference file created for each map. To the regression testing, use [https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/blob/master/MagneticField/Engine/test/regression.py]]![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/blob/master/MagneticField/Engine/test/regression.py%3C/a%3E%3C/span%3E)options:
* `producerType`: options are 'static\_DDD', 'static\_DD4Hep', 'fromDB', 'fromDB\_DD4Hep'
* `era`: either 'RunI' or 'RunII'
* `current`: Magnet current (nominal values: 18164=3.8T; 16730=3.5T; 14340=3T; 9500=2T).
 are reported in the standard output.Regression files are maintained in [cms-data/MagneticField-Engine/![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/cms-data/MagneticField-Engine/).In case outliers are found, they can be visualized with gnuplot in this way (old recipe-to be updated)
```
cmsRun regression.py > ! output.txt
grep Disc output.txt | cut -f 7 -d' ' | tr '(,)' ' ' > ! outliers
cat <reference_table.txt> | cut -d' ' -f 1,2,3 > ! allpoints
```
and in gnuplot:
```
set terminal png
set xlabel "x coordinate (cm)"
set ylabel "y coordinate (cm)"
set zlabel "z coordinate (cm)"
set output "viewXY.png"
set  0,90
splot 'allpoints','outliers'
set output "view3D.png"
set  30,60
splot 'allpoints','outliers'
set output "viewXZ.png"
set  90,0
splot 'allpoints','outliers'
```
### Visualization of the field map in CMSSW
The magnetic field and geometry can be visualized in Eve. The field visualization is implemented in `Fireworks/Geometry/plugins/DisplayGeom.cc`. An example .py configuration can be with:
`cmsRun [MagneticField](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/MagneticField?topicparent=CMSPublic.SWGuideMagneticField;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") /GeomBuilder/test/Visualization/displayMFGeom_cfg.py`.Some notes:
* In the Eve window, click " Home" in the bottom left panel to reset the position (to return to this panel later, double-click on Viewers and select Viewer 1).
* To hide the geometry, deselect in the browser. To select/deselect individual volumes, double-click on the node in the browser and again on each level of the hierarchy.
* To choose a pre-defined perspective or orthographic , hover with the mouse on the bar below the "Viewer 1" tab. A new menu bar appears, with predefined views under . Toggle auto-hide un-ticking "File->Hide Menus" in this bar, or with the command:<>
  ```
  ((TGLSAViewer*)gEve->GetDefaultGLViewer())->DisableMenuBarHiding()
  ```
* If the job fails with a message: `MESA-LOADER: failed to open swrast`, re-try after setting `LD_PRELOAD="/lib64/libLLVM-17.so"`
* Help on visualization shortcuts (zooming, panning, rotation, wireframe mode, etc) can be found under Help in the menu bar mentioned above.
* Exit with .q from the root shell (closing the graphical window causes a crash).
## Release history
The following section are kept for keeping track of past (obsolete) usage and development, and are not relevant for current users.
### Configuration in older releases
In releases prior to CMSSW\_7\_4\_3 and CMSSW\_7\_5\_0\_pre5, default configurations used to be:
* `Configuration.StandardSequences.MagneticField_AutoFromDBCurrent_cff`: I maps with automatic choice of nominal working point for data; fixed 3.8T for MC
* `Configuration.StandardSequences.MagneticField_38T_PostLS1_cff`: map for 3.8T only.
When moving to CMSSW\_7\_4\_3 and CMSSW\_7\_5\_0\_pre5, please replace these with `Configuration.StandardSequences.MagneticField_cff` as mentioned above.
Configurations for fixed nominal working points, eg. 0 T, did not change (cf above).
### History of map versions
Here is a brief description of the different development and production versions.<><>A detailed description of the CMS FEM model, with all details of the model features and its evolution over time can be found in [Symmetry 2021, 13(6), 1052![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://www.mdpi.com/2073-8994/13/6/1052).A collection of documents related to the field map computation, mapping, and comparison with measured data can be found [here](/twiki/bin//CMS/MagneticField#Documentation) .
###### Version 85l\_030919 ("old 4T map"; obsolete, no longer supported)
The 4T field map used in COBRA/ORCA and in CMSSW up to series 2.0.X included is based on a TOSCA finite-element computation performed in 2003. It is based on a geometric model ("magnetic field geometry") of 271 volumes representing one 30 degree-sector in z<0 only (1/24 of CMS), thus the model is Z-symmetric and 12-fold phi-symmetric. For each volume, the field is computed on a regular (non-cartesian) grid defined appropriately. The CMSSW field interface returns the field at an arbitray point using 3D linear interpolation within the grid cell containing the point inside each volume. The nominal B value in this map (4T) cannot be changed. A parametrization of the TOSCA computation (by ) can be optionally used in the region r<1.2 m, |z|<3.0 m in place of the interpolation; the main advantage is speed (and it also provides smoother derivatives than the interpolation).This has been the only full field map available after 2003 and before CMSSW\_2\_1\_0.This version is no longer supported after CMSSW\_2\_2\_10.
###### Version 1103l\_071212 (Pre-CRAFT-2009 default; 3.8T version deprecated since 3\_1\_X; still used for some nominal operating points other than 3.8T)
This map is in use since CMSSW 2.2. and includes improvements based on the experience of the Magnet Test, which included a mapping campaign of the field within the solenoid, as well as measurements in the yoke (with flux loops during fast discharges, and with probes). It is based on a TOSCA finite-element computation with a model that includes the Z-asymmetry of the coil spires and more accurate description of a full half (x>0) of CMS including chimneys. However field data is still provided only for sector 1 (30 degrees, representing 1/12 of CMS with a total of 312 volumes), so the CMSSW map is 12-fold phi-symmetric (but not Z-symmetric).The map with this model is available for several nominal field values: 2, 3, 3.5, 3.8 and 4T. The latter is expected to be different (more realistic) w.r.t. the previous 4T computation (85l\_030919). <>A parametrization of the TOSCA computation within r<1.15 m, |z|<2.8 m is available for all field values (). This parametrization matches very well with the computed data (difference of ~5mT at the edges of the validity region) and **is used as a slave field in the default configuration** (cf section above), mainly to save CPU time in production and HLT.<>A different parametrization of the **real mapping data** () is available **as an option**. It is defined in the region r<1.9 m, |z|<3.5m, excluding the "corners" |z|+2.5\*r>6.7 m. This parametrization reproduces the mapping data more precisely, but is slower; it is the suggested option for application where ultimate precision is necessary and CPU speed can be sacrificed. The agreement of this map with the mapping data is better than 0.4 mT (agreement to ~10^-4) in the tracker region and up to 0.8 mT at the edges of the validity region. To activate it specify the following:
```
process.ParametrizedMagneticFieldProducer.version = 'PolyFit2D'
process.ParametrizedMagneticFieldProducer.parameters = cms.PSet(
         BValue = cms.double(3.81143)
)
process.VolumeBasedMagneticFieldESProducer.useParametrizedTrackerField = True;
```
(the latter card is actually set to True by default in the standard config).In 3.1.X releases and later, where this map version is superseeded by 1103l\_090322\_2pi\_scaled, it can be activated using:
```
process.load("MagneticField.Engine.volumeBasedMagneticField_1103l_cfi").
```
The  **geometry** for this map was (a-posteriori) labelled version **90322** and is implemented in `MagneticFieldVolumes_1103l.xml`.
###### Version 1103l\_090216 (Intermediate development; no longer supported)
Improved computation w.r.t. 1103l\_071212, with enlarged radius (R=30 m) of the total region where the field is computed, plus some additional details outside CMS (e.g. iron plate in the 's floor). The same 312-volume 12-fold phi-symmetric geometry is used in the CMSSW interface. This map shows much better agreement with measurements with tracks in the iron yoke. This version was used for development only, and is no longer supported.The map was still based on geometry version 90322.
###### Version 1103l\_090322 (deprecated)
Based on 1103l\_090216 this computation is done in volume extended also in |Z| (up to 35 m). The same 312-volume 12-fold phi-symmetric geometry is used in the CMSSW interface. Changes w.r.t. 1103l\_090216 are visible basically only in the forward region.<>This version was used for development only, and is deprecated in favor of later versions.<>
<>
This version was available starting from recent 2\_2\_X versions with the configuration:
```
process.load("MagneticField.Engine.volumeBasedMagneticField_1103l_090322_cfi")
```
The map was still based on geometry version 90322.
###### Version 1103l\_090322\_2pi (deprecated)
Based on 1103l\_090322, uses different tables for the barrel yoke iron layers in the chimney sectors (S3, ) and for S9, S10, S11 in the third barrel layer and in the endcaps. This version was used for development only, and is deprecated in favor of later versions.
###### Version 1103l\_090322\_2pi\_scaled ( I default for 3.8T, adopted starting from 3\_1\_0)
Same as 1103l\_090322\_2pi; in addition the field is scaled with factors measured from CRAFT data.This version was used by default in CMSSW\_3\_1\_0 and later releases for 3.8T (while 1103l\_071212 remained the default for other nominal points) and was superseded by new map staring from version 120812.The map was still based on geometry version 90322.
###### Version 1103l\_090601 (Intermediate development; no longer supported)
Same as 1103l\_090322\_2pi; with small correction of the TOSCA geometry in L3 of barrel sectors 9,10,11. Since in S9,S1 the thicker L3 plates extend into air volumes 297-307, a finer grid was used for these volumes/sectors. Tables with this configuration were specified in  \_07\_2pi\_air.xml.Two sets of scaling factors were prepared, based on CRAFT08 ([ScalingFactors](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/ScalingFactors?topicparent=CMSPublic.SWGuideMagneticField;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") \_090601\_091022\_cfi.py) and CRAFT08+09 ([ScalingFactors](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/ScalingFactors?topicparent=CMSPublic.SWGuideMagneticField;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") \_090601\_091116\_cfi.py). These were however never released.Configuration (no longer supported)
```
process.load("MagneticField.Engine.volumeBasedMagneticField_090601_cfi")
```
```
process.load("MagneticField.Engine.volumeBasedMagneticField_090601_scaled_cfi")
```
The map was still based on geometry version 90322.
###### Version 090812 (Intermediate development; no longer supported)
Full TOSCA model made of two halves ( \_1 for X>0 and \_2 for ). Has not been released into CMSSW.
###### Version 120812 (Default for since CMSSW\_6\_2\_0; replaced for data since 743/750pre5)
Full TOSCA model made of two halves ( \_1 for X>0 and \_2 for ). Volume numbers are 1001-1360 and 2001-2360.Two version exist, with the additional plate (post-LS1) and without (2010-2012 geometry.)To use it in CMSSW\_6\_2\_0, you had to use:
```
process.load("MagneticField.Engine.volumeBasedMagneticField_120812_largeYE4_cfi")
```
and for the 2010/2012 geometry:
```
process.load("MagneticField.Engine.volumeBasedMagneticField_120812_cfi")
```
The map was based on a new  **geometry version 120812** (implemented in `MagneticFieldVolumes_1_v7_large.xml, [MagneticFieldVolumes](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/MagneticFieldVolumes?topicparent=CMSPublic.SWGuideMagneticField;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") _2_v7_large.xml`), which is no longer in use.
###### Version 130503 (Default for 3.8T data only, starting from 743/750pre5)
Full TOSCA model of the entire CMS; reduced memory footprint cf. [this presentation![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://indico.cern.ch/event/328166/session/1/contribution/24).
804 volumes per sector; volumes outside any detector are replicated starting from sector 1 (volumes extending from R~7.6 m to to R=9 m, ie 1011, 1028-1029,1034-1035,1042-1043,1050-1051,1058-1059,1064-1065,1072-1073,1078-1079; volumes beyond |Z|>10.86 ie 1084-1129,1136-1137; and the corresponding +1000).
(for the volume outside CASTOR) are replicated from sector 4 instead than 1, to avoid aliasing effects due to the plates in the cylinder gap.The map was based on the new  **geometry version 130503** (implemented in `MagneticFieldVolumes_1_v9_large.xml, [MagneticFieldVolumes](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/MagneticFieldVolumes?topicparent=CMSPublic.SWGuideMagneticField;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") _2_v9_large.xml`), which is no longer in use.
###### Version 160812 (Current default for 3.8, 3.5 and 3T, both data and MC since later releases in the 93X series)
Updated TOSCA model, cf. [this presentation![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://indico.cern.ch/event/642366/contributions/2606389/):
* Extend the description of the rotating shielding and TAS up to |Z|=22 m (was up to |Z|=17.86 m in the previous map)
* Add the 18 kA current leads in the chimney in YB-1 S3
The map was computed for 3.8T, 3.5T, 3T in the [RunII](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/RunII?topicparent=CMSPublic.SWGuideMagneticField;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") configuration and for 3.8T only in the [RunI](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/RunI?topicparent=CMSPublic.SWGuideMagneticField;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") configuration.
It is currently used for all nominal points except for 2T for both [RunI](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/RunI?topicparent=CMSPublic.SWGuideMagneticField;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") and II.The map was based on the new  **geometry version 160812** (implemented in `MagneticFieldVolumes_160812_1.xml, [MagneticFieldVolumes](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/MagneticFieldVolumes?topicparent=CMSPublic.SWGuideMagneticField;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") _160812_2.xml`).
###### <>Version 170812
The geometrical model is identical to version 160812 (thus geometry version = 160812, see above) the only difference is the use of an updated BH-curve for s400 steel in the TOSCA computation. The difference in the calculated field is of 1-2% within endcap yoke disks for the 3.8 T map, and 1-3% for the 2 T map.<><>
###### Version 190812
This version was developed to test the effect of the addition of HGCal absorbers with MUrel = 1.005 in Phase 2. It was found that these cause a very small variation of the field in the tracker region; e.g. only 0.03% for the central value B\_0 (3.8094 vs 3.8104 T). This model is not available in CMSSW.

## Fancy use cases
### How to load two field maps in the same job
Any number of different maps can be loaded in the same job and accessed in parallel, for e.g. comparison. One of them will be the "standard" one which is visible by all modules; it will be the one with a null label., the others are available in the job using their specific non-null label. In the following example we specify a second map with label '090216\_3\_8t' in addition to the standard one (default 3.8T map).
```
# The standard one
process.load("Configuration.StandardSequences.MagneticField_38T_cff")
# The new one with label "090216_3_8t"
# Note I use a different process name than what us used in the default.
process.VolumeBasedMagneticFieldESProducerNew =
cms.ESProducer("VolumeBasedMagneticFieldESProducer",
   timerOn = cms.untracked.bool(False),
   useParametrizedTrackerField = cms.bool(False),
   label = cms.untracked.string('090216_3_8t'),
   version = cms.string('grid_1103l_090216_3_8t'),
   debugBuilder = cms.untracked.bool(False),
   cacheLastVolume = cms.untracked.bool(True),
   scalingVolumes = (),
   scalingFactors = cms.vdouble()
)
```
In the code, you will then be able to get both fields maps:
```
ESHandle<> magfield;
setup.get<IdealMagneticFieldRecord>().get(magfield);
ESHandle<> newMagfield;
setup.get<IdealMagneticFieldRecord>().get("090216_3_8t",newMagfield);
```
### How to apply per-volume rescaling factors
A scaling factor for |B| can be specified independently for each of the 312 volumes in each sector. <> <>The scaling is provided with two matching vectors. The first vector lists the volumes, encoded as (100\*volume number + sector). Entries with sector=0 will match all sectors for which a specific sector entry is not set.<>The second vector specifies the corresponding scaling factors.<><>The volume numbers for the iron yoke plates can be obtained from this [schema![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmsdoc.cern.ch/cms/Physics/muon/www/Magfield/transverse.pdf).In version, 1103l\_090322\_2pi\_scaled, the default scaling factors are implemented in [MagneticField/Engine/python/ScalingFactors\_090322\_2pi\_090520\_cfi.py![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmssw.cvs.cern.ch/cgi-bin/cmssw.cgi/CMSSW/MagneticField/Engine/python/ScalingFactors_090322_2pi_090520_cfi.py?revision=1.2&=markup). If you need to test modified scaling factor, please use this file as a starting point.Annotated lists of volumes (actual factors are NOT significant):
* [all barrel yoke iron volumes, including brackets](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/pub/CMS/CMS.MagneticFieldIssues/MagnetScalingFactors.py.txt).
* [endcap iron disks volumes](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/pub/CMSPublic/SWGuideMagneticField/EndcapScalingFactors.py.txt)

## Goals of this page:
how to perform segment reconstruction in the drift tubes () and in the cathode strip chambers (), and hit reconstruction in the resistive plate chambers (RPC), starting from digis or raw data.
## Introduction
The reconstruction in the system starts from the reconstruction of the hits within the cell (DTRecHit1D) for the , from the 2-Dimensional hits on the plane (CMS.CSCRecHit2D) and 1D rechits in the RPCs (RPCRecHit). At this stage some ambiguities must be solved, therefore a combinatorial pattern recognition is performed ( and segment reconstruction).
The segments are then used as input for the seed/track reconstruction.This example shows how to:
* Create the 1D rechits in the Resistive Plate Chambers ([RPCRecHit![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmsdoc.cern.ch/cms/sw/slc3_ia32_gcc323/cms/cmssw/CMSSW_1_2_2/doc/html/classRPCRecHit.html))
* Create the 1D rechits in the Drift Tubes ([DTRecHit1DPair![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cms-service-sdtweb.web.cern.ch/cms-service-sdtweb/doxygen/CMSSW_1_7_1/doc/html/de/dd0/classDTRecHit1DPair.html))
* Create the 2D-segments in the Drift Tubes ([DTSLRecSegment2D![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cms-service-sdtweb.web.cern.ch/cms-service-sdtweb/doxygen/CMSSW_1_7_1/doc/html/dd/d0f/classDTSLRecSegment2D.html) and [DTChamberRecSegment2D![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cms-service-sdtweb.web.cern.ch/cms-service-sdtweb/doxygen/CMSSW_1_7_1/doc/html/d9/d64/classDTChamberRecSegment2D.html))
* Create the 4D-segments in the Drift Tubes ([DTRecSegment4D![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cms-service-sdtweb.web.cern.ch/cms-service-sdtweb/doxygen/CMSSW_1_7_1/doc/html/d4/d78/classDTRecSegment4D.html))
* Create the 2D rechits in the Cathode Strip Chambers ([CMS.CSCRecHit2D![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmsdoc.cern.ch/cms/sw/slc3_ia32_gcc323/cms/cmssw/CMSSW_1_2_2/doc/html/classCSCRecHit2D.html))
* Create the 4D-segments in the Cathode Strip Chambers ([/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmsdoc.cern.ch/cms/sw/slc3_ia32_gcc323/cms/cmssw/CMSSW_1_2_2/doc/html/classCSCSegment.html))
* Write a small module to read and analyze the segments.
the corresponding CMS.DataFormat object is given between parenthesis.
Further information are available on the CMSSW reference manual about: local reconstruction in ([DTRecHit![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmsdoc.cern.ch/Releases/CMSSW/CMSSW_0_8_0/doc/html/RecoLocalMuon_DTRecHit.html), [/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmsdoc.cern.ch/Releases/CMSSW/CMSSW_0_8_0/doc/html/RecoLocalMuon_DTSegment.html))

![Concept schema](/twiki/pub/CMSPublic/SWGuideMuonLocalReco/DT_CSC_tree.gif)[Global](/twiki/pub/CMSPublic/SWGuideMuonLocalReco/globalview.png)
## Let's start!
### Set up your Environment
```
scramv1 project CMSSW CMSSW_1_8_0_pre2
cd CMSSW_1_8_0_pre2/src
eval `scramv1 runtime -csh` or eval `scramv1 runtime -sh`, depending on your shell
project CMSSW
```
This tutorial has been updated to run in CMSSW\_1\_8\_0\_pre2. Please be aware that changes may be required for newer or older releases of CMSSW.
In particular
* in CMSSW\_1\_6\_X considerable modifications were introduced to use conditions data (e.g. calibration data) for both real and simulated data.
* from CMSSW\_1\_7\_X to CMSSW\_1\_8\_X there were big modifications to the configuration files for local reconstruction.
* minor modifications have been made to the Calibration for simulated data passing from from CMSSW\_1\_7\_X to CMSSW\_1\_8\_X
### Samples
You can use your favorite sample, or you can generate one (cf.  and
 [Digi](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin//CMS/CSCTutorial) tutorials).For this tutorial we assume that the sample used in the following already contains:
* the digis
* the digis
* the RPC digis
### Get the required Configuration Files
The `CalibMuon/Configuration/data` package contains blocks of configuration files and sequences needed for the and Calibration and Alignment.
The `RecoLocalMuon/Configuration/data` package constains the blocks of configuration files and sequences needed for the Local Reconstruction.
These files contain default values for the parameters, and can be included in .cfg files. The user is not supposed to modify these files, but can override a card using the `replace` keyword in the .cfg.An example of .cfg file to perform Local Reconstruction (loading the required calibration constants for simulated data) is
`RecoLocalMuon/Configuration/test/RecoLocalMuon.cfg`. You can [Checkout](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookSetComputerNode#Access_Modules_from_CVS_Reposito) it with the command
```
cvs co -r V00-01-11  RecoLocalMuon/Configuration/test
```
With the `-r` option you checkout the specified version of the package; without this option you checkout the HEAD (last committed) version of the package which might -- and is likely to -- have been modified since this tutorial was prepared.
### How the config files work: includes and parameters
In general, to run the segment producers starting from a file containing the digis, the configuration file should contain
* `source` block to specify a digi file
* the magnetic field and the geometry cfi files
* the module blocks included via cfi files to read the Calibration constants
* the module blocks included via cfi files for the actual reconstruction
  + the 1DRecHit producer module for the (`dt1DRecHits`)
  + the 2DRecHit producer module for the (`csc2DRecHits`)
  + the 2D and the 4D segments producer modules for the (`dt2DSegments` and `dt4DSegments`)
  + the segment producer module for the (`cscSegments`)
  + the 1D RecHit producer module for the RPC (`rpcRecHits`)
* the named `module` out to define an output file
* the execution `path` to instantiate the modules
The module blocks for Calibration and Alignment are
```
#  Calibration
include "CalibMuon/Configuration/data/DT_FakeConditions.cff"
#  Calibration
include "CalibMuon/Configuration/data/CSC_FakeConditions.cff"
#  alignment
include "CalibMuon/Configuration/data/Muon_FakeAlignment.cff"
```
The magnetic field and geometry cfi files as well as the
cfi files for the actual reconstruction are included via the
```
include RecoLocalMuon/Configuration/data/RecoLocalMuon.cff
```
The `muonlocalreco` path is also defined in the cff file as `sequence muonlocalreco = {dtlocalreco & csclocalreco & rpcRecHits}`
which is a list of the following composite sequences
```
#  sequence
sequence dtlocalreco = {dt1DRecHits, dt2DSegments, dt4DSegments}
#  sequence
sequence csclocalreco = {csc2DRecHits, cscSegments}
```
Therefore if you put the `muonlocalreco` sequence in your path (as is done in `RecoLocalMuon.cfg`)
you will get the **full local reconstruction chain** in the system.
Of course you can leave out the part related to DTs or CSCs or RPCs if you are interested in one subsystem only.You may also want to add one or more analyzer modules. To do this you have to specify them and to add them at the end of the execution path.
### Alignment
The alignment constants loaded in the `CalibMuon/Configuration/data/Muon_FakeAlignment.cff` are the fake ones, i.e. they reproduce a perfectly aligned detector.
In order to have a more realistic simulation you can include the
`CalibMuon/Configuration/data/Muon_FrontierAlignment.cff` file and then you can load your favourite set of Alignment constants using the replace parameter, see for example
`Configuration/StandardSequences/data/Frontier100pbConditions.cff`
(more info in the  [Alignment twiki](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin//CMS/SWGuideMuonAlignAlgos)).
### Calibration
The calibration conditions loaded in the `CalibMuon/Configuration/data/DT_FakeConditions.cff` are the fake ones, i.e. they reproduce the ideal behaviour of the detector (no mis-calibration at all).
In order to have a more realistic simulation you can include the
`CalibMuon/Configuration/data/DT_FrontierConditions.cff` file and then you can load your favourite set of calibration constants using the replace parameter, see for example
`Configuration/StandardSequences/data/Frontier100pbConditions.cff`
(more info in the  [Calibration twiki](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin//CMS/SWGuideDTCalib)).
### DTRecHits and DTSegments
Currently two kinds of 1D reconstruction algorithm are available:
* **Linear Drift Velocity**: assumes a costant drift velocity to compute a position from the drift time
  + you can use the same fixed value of drift velocity for all the detectors
  + you can read from database at different value of drift velocity for each superlayer (obviously you must have created the database before!)
* **Parametrized Drift Velocity**: uses the GARFIELD parametrization of the cell. The distance from the wire is a function of the digi time, the local magnetic field and the incidence angle.
Both 2D and 4D segment producers depend on the 1D algos. They update the 1D rechits when more information is available (second step: info on incidence angle, third step: info on position along the wire). You can choose what algo you prefer simply including the apropriate .cfi in your .cfg:
* For the 2D-segments reconstruction one of:
```
  include "RecoLocalMuon/DTSegment/data/dt2DSegments_CombPatternReco2D_ParamDrift.cfi"
  include "RecoLocalMuon/DTSegment/data/dt2DSegments_CombPatternReco2D_LinearDrift.cfi"
  include "RecoLocalMuon/DTSegment/data/dt2DSegments_CombPatternReco2D_LinearDriftFromDB.cfi"
```
* For the 4D-segments reconstruction one of:
```
  include "RecoLocalMuon/DTSegment/data/dt4DSegments_CombPatternReco4D_ParamDrift.cfi"
  include "RecoLocalMuon/DTSegment/data/dt4DSegments_CombPatternReco4D_LinearDrift.cfi"
  include "RecoLocalMuon/DTSegment/data/dt4DSegments_CombPatternReco4D_LinearDriftFromDB.cfi"
```
If you want to modify the parameters of the algos you can use the `replace` key-word. For example, in the 4D producer, you can directly extract the theta-segments from the event (if they have been produced) avoiding to re-reconstruct them. The following line modifies the default parameter `AllDTRecHits = true`.
```
replace dt4DSegments..AllDTRecHits = false
```
All the parameters can be replaced in this way. For more info on the cfg key-words, refer to [Cfg File Usage](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideAboutConfigFile).
### CSCRecHits
The current default algorithm for reconstruction of space points (hits) in the system is CSCRecHitB. The older package, CSCRecHit, which was
ported from ORCA, does not make use of realistic conditions data, and was also slower due to its use of Minuit for fitting cluster shapes on strips.
### CSCSegments
There are several possible reconstruction algorithms for the -segment reconstruction, as described in the
[CSCSegment Reference Manual Page![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmsdoc.cern.ch/Releases/CMSSW/latest_nightly/doc/html/RecoLocalMuon_CSCSegment.html).
(This page is unfortunately not yet up-to-.)
The particular choice is made by including one of
* "RecoLocalMuon/CSCSegment/data/CSCSegmentAlgorithmSK.cfi"
* "RecoLocalMuon/CSCSegment/data/CSCSegmentAlgorithmTC.cfi"
* "RecoLocalMuon/CSCSegment/data/CSCSegmentAlgorithmDF.cfi"
* "RecoLocalMuon/CSCSegment/data/CSCSegmentAlgorithmST.cfi"
To switch from one to the other you can simply override the `algo_type` card, which is defined in the CSCSegmentProducer:
* `replace cscSegments.algo_type = 1` for the SK algo
* `replace cscSegments.algo_type = 2` for the algo
* `replace cscSegments.algo_type = 3` for the DF algo
* `replace cscSegments.algo_type = 4` for the ST algo
The current recommended default algorithm is the ST algorithm (type 4).
## Run the Producers all together!
In the following we will run an example job to produce RPC, and rechits and segments:
1. Modify the `RecoLocalMuon/Configuration/test/RecoLocalMuon.cfg` file in order to use your sample and decide where to write the output file:
   1. Modify the `source` section to point to your favorite sample
   2. Modify the `PoolOutputModule`: `untracked string fileName ="/tmp/RecoLocalMuon.root"`
2. Run the job: `cmsRun RecoLocalMuon.cfg >&! $SCRATCH/RecoLocalMuon.out &` in the RecoLocalMuon/Configuration/test/ directory.
At the end of the job the `/tmp/RecoLocalMuon.root` output file will contain all the objects produced by the local reconstruction.
You can then analyze it either using your favourite analyzer or browsing it with a ROOT TBrowser.
## Run starting from Raw Data
With very few changes it is possible to run the reconstruction starting from the raw data. What we need is:
* change the input source
* include the raw data unpacker (to create digis), and put it at the beginning of the execution path
* include the proper calibration files
An example of .cfg file to perform Local Reconstruction (loading the needed calibration constants for real data) is
`RecoLocalMuon/DTSegment/test/testDTRecSegment_fromData.cfg`.
You can [Checkout](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookSetComputerNode#Access_Modules_from_CVS_Reposito) it with the command
```
cvs co -r V02-01-07 RecoLocalMuon/DTSegment/test/
```
Within the testDTRecSegment\_fromData.cfg file we can recognize the above items:
* the input source:
  + `source = DaqSource{ ... }`
* the es\_sources:
  + `es_source roMapping = PoolDBESSource { ... }` for the channel mapping
  + `es_source TTrig = PoolDBESSource { ... }` for the ttrig calibration
  + `es_source t0 = PoolDBESSource { ... }` for the t0 calibration
* the unpacker:
  + `module dtunpacker = DTUnpackingModule{ ... }`
* the new execution path:
  + `path p = {dtunpacker, dt1DRecHits, dt2DSegments, dt4DSegments}`
To run it type the command
`cmsRun testDTRecSegment_fromData.cfg >&! out_from_data.log &`
in the RecoLocalMuon/DTSegment/test/ directory.
## Run the visualization
There are two ways to run the [visualization](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookEventDisplay):
* starting from a file which already contains the segments (for example one produced with the above procedure)
  + e.g. [/VisMuonDT/test/visRecoDT.cfg![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmssw.cvs.cern.ch/cgi-bin/cmssw.cgi/CMSSW//VisMuonDT/test/visRecoDT.cfg?rev=1.2&cvsroot=CMSSW&content-type=text/vnd.viewcvs-markup)
* reconstructing the rechits and the segments from the digi/raw-data on-the-fly.
  + from the real raw-data: [/VisMuonDT/test/visRecoDT\_fromDigis2Segments.cfg![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmssw.cvs.cern.ch/cgi-bin/cmssw.cgi/CMSSW//VisMuonDT/test/visRecoDT_fromDigis2Segments.cfg?rev=1.2&cvsroot=CMSSW&content-type=text/vnd.viewcvs-markup)
  + from the simulated digis: [/VisMuonDT/test/visRecoDT\_fromCosmicData.cfg![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmssw.cvs.cern.ch/cgi-bin/cmssw.cgi/CMSSW//VisMuonDT/test/visRecoDT_fromCosmicData.cfg?rev=1.2&cvsroot=CMSSW&content-type=text/vnd.viewcvs-markup)
If you have a look at the above files you could see that they aren't different with respect to the ones used for the production of the segments, in fact we can use them as well. Then, where is the difference? Just in the exe command: for the visualization we have to use `iguana` instead of `cmsRun`. So for example (in RecoLocalMuon/DTSegment/test/):`iguana -p testDTRecSegment_fromData.cfg`... and enjoy!

## Contacts
* **Conveners**: See the appropriate Muon subdetector DPG : [), [CSC-DPG](/twiki/bin//CMS/MuonDPGCSC) and [RPC-DPG](/twiki/bin//CMS/MuonDPGRPC).
* **Hypernews forum**: ![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif) ()
## Introduction
There are three muon subdetectors: the Drift Tubes (DT), the Cathode Strip Chambers (CSC) and the Resistive Plate Chambers (RPC). The DT's are used in the barrel region, the CSC's in the end caps, and the RPC's are found in both regions. For more information about the hardware, see the [Muon Technical Design Report](/twiki/bin//CMS/MuonTDR) tWiki .These technologies were developed by independent groups, so currently (2007) there are three *Detector*  (DPG's) for the muon systems. You can find more information about these groups from the corresponding tWiki pages: [), [CSC-DPG](/twiki/bin//CMS/MuonDPGCSC) and [RPC-DPG](/twiki/bin//CMS/MuonDPGRPC).The DPG's are responsible for the reconstruction of muons up to the level of segments in individual chambers - the so-called *local reconstruction*. The [Muon Physics Object Group (POG)](/twiki/bin//CMS/MuonPOG) is responsible for linking segments together to form *stand-alone muons* and then linking those to silicon tracker tracks to form *global muons*.This software guide therefore addresses only the codes needed for local reconstruction.
## Tutorials
* [Local Reconstruction](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideMuonLocalReco)
* [SWGuideMuonSystemRecoTutorials](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideMuonSystemRecoTutorials)
## RECO/AOD collection
* [RECO collections](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideRecoDataTable)
* [AOD collections](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideAodDataTable)
## and Software Architecture
The basic reconstruction path is as follows. Raw data is unpacked by the **unpacker** routines which create **digi's**, which are an organized arrangement of digital data at the per-channel level. These digis are then combined to form **recHits** which give the *local* X and Y coordinates and related information. These recHits are then associated into groups by some pattern recognition algorithm to form **segments** which give the straight-line parameters for a candidate muon producing those hits. The digi's, recHits and segments are similar but not identical for the DT's, CSC's and RPC's.

## Introduction
This page provides a summary of the used to reconstruct muons in CMS, describes the collections of muons produced during the processing of data and samples, and includes links to other useful information on reconstruction.
## Tutorials
* [rel="nofollow" reconstruction](http://indico.cern.ch/getFile.py/access?contribId=21&resId=0&materialId=slides&confId=46651)  by , Jan. 2009 (FNAL).
* [rel="nofollow" Analysis of muons in CRAFT data](http://indico.cern.ch/getFile.py/access?contribId=86&sessionId=22&resId=0&materialId=slides&confId=46769) by J. Piedra, Dec. 2008 (CERN).
* [rel="nofollow" Introduction to muons](http://indico.cern.ch/getFile.py/access?contribId=12&resId=0&materialId=slides&confId=42388) by , Oct. 2008.
## General Talks about and Identification
* [rel="nofollow" reconstruction and identification](http://indico.cern.ch/materialDisplay.py?contribId=1&materialId=slides&confId=60388) by , Jun. 2009 (CERN).
## RECO/AOD collections
Data collections available for reconstructed muons are described in [SWGuideDataFormatRecoMuon](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideDataFormatRecoMuon). The full list of products can be found in the following pages:
* [RECO collections](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideRecoDataTable)
* [AOD collections](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideAodDataTable)
Full definition of the -related content in the event record can be found [at this link![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmssw.cvs.cern.ch/cgi-bin/cmssw.cgi/CMSSW/RecoMuon/Configuration/python/RecoMuon_EventContent_cff.py).
## and Software Architecture
The software resides mostly in the [/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmssw.cvs.cern.ch/cgi-bin/cmssw.cgi/CMSSW/RecoMuon) and [DataFormats/MuonReco![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmssw.cvs.cern.ch/cgi-bin/cmssw.cgi/CMSSW/DataFormats/MuonReco) repositories in CMSSW.
### Standard sequences used in default reconstruction (pp collisions)
* [Muons in High Level Trigger (HLT)](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideMuonHLT)
* [Standalone reconstruction](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideStandAloneMuonReco) <--- [WorkBook section](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookMuonAnalysis#StandAlone)
* Global reconstruction <--- [WorkBook section](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookMuonAnalysis#GlobalMu)
* Reconstruction of high-pT muons <--- [WorkBook section](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookMuonAnalysis#TevMu)
* [Reconstruction of "tracker muons"](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideTrackerMuons) <--- [WorkBook section](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookMuonAnalysis#TrackMu)
* Reconstruction of "calo muons" <--- [WorkBook section](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookMuonAnalysis#CaloMu)
* [isolation](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideMuonIsolation) <--- [WorkBook section](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookMuonAnalysis#MuonIs)
A short description of each sequence can be found in the WorkBook by clicking [here](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookMuonAnalysis#InTro) or on the "Workbook section" links above; in some cases, when more details are available in TWiki, they can be viewed by clicking on the sequence name. Direct link to the definition of standard sequences in CMSSW is [here![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmssw.cvs.cern.ch/cgi-bin/cmssw.cgi/CMSSW/RecoMuon/Configuration/python/RecoMuon_cff.py).
### Standard sequences used in cosmic reconstruction (CRUZET, CRAFT, and dedicated cosmic runs, as well as corresponding MC samples)
* [Cosmic reconstruction](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideCosmicMuonReco)
### Baseline selections recommended by the POG
* Description of selections in [SWGuideMuonId](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideMuonId)
* [Links to reference efficiencies](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin//CMS/MuonReferenceEffs) for baseline selections and isolation
### for measuring reconstruction performance from data
*(These are not run as a part of standard reconstruction)*
* Efficiency measurements:
  + [Tag-and-probe package](/twiki/bin//CMS/MuonTagAndProbe)
* -momentum scale calibration:
  + [MuScleFit package](/twiki/bin//CMS/MuonScaleCalib)
  + [SIDRA package](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SidraFit)
## Analysis and Validation
* [MC Truth association](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideMuonTrackMCTruth): detailed tools used for validation, software development, ...
* [Analysis-level association tools](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideMuonAnalysisMuonAssociators) for matching reconstructed muons to trigger info, MC or other offline objects.
* [Standard tool for inclusive plots](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideMuonInclusivePlotsTools) of variables and for data/mc comparisons.
* POG release validation:
  + Instructions on how to run RECO validation are at [this link](/twiki/bin//CMS/RecoMuonValidationSuite). ![NEW](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/new.gif "NEW")
  + Instructions on how to run the HLT validation are at [this link](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin/viewauth/CMS/MuonHLTOfflineDQM). ![NEW](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/new.gif "NEW")
  + Part of the validation is done using analyzers under the [DQMOffline](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin//CMS/MuonsDQM) branch. Description of the relevant plots can be found at [this link](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin//CMS/MuonsDQMPlots). ![NEW](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/new.gif "NEW")
  + Release-validation plots for reconstruction (standalone, global and high-pT muons, isolation, algorithmic HLT efficiencies, etc.) are at [this link![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cmsdoc.cern.ch/cms/Physics//CMSSW/Performance/RecoMuon/Validation/val).
  + (OBSOLETE) Release-validation plots for identification (tracker muons) are at [this link![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmsdoc.cern.ch/cms/Physics//CMSSW/Performance/RecoMuon/MuonIdentification/navigation.html).
  + (OBSOLETE) Release-validation plots for HLT are at [this link![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cms-muonhltval.web.cern.ch/cms-muonhltval).
## Documents
* [rel="nofollow" **CMS AN 2008/097**](http://cms.cern.ch/iCMS/jsp/db_notes/noteInfo.jsp?cmsnoteid=CMS%20AN-2008/097): *G. Abbiendi et al., " Reconstruction in the CMS Detector".* Detailed description of reconstruction for standalone, global and tracker muons, and of their performance.
* [rel="nofollow" **CMS AN 2008/098**](http://cms.cern.ch/iCMS/jsp/db_notes/noteInfo.jsp?cmsnoteid=CMS%20AN-2008/098):  *et al., " Identification in CMS".* Description of recommended selection criteria for global muons and tracker muons.

Phys. (2008) 449![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://www.springerlink.com/content/33335l32709047t2).) Description of dedicated cosmic- reconstruction algorithm. Written in Sep. 2007, so certain parts may be outdated.

## Reconstruction
The minimal recommended tags for reconstruction can be found [below](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuidePFTauID#Recommended_tags_for_2011_data_t).If you want to use on top, the analysis tools (PAT) please check the recommended tags here [SWGuidePATRecipes](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuidePATRecipes).A dedicated analysis package for Ztautau, Wtaunu and studies can be found here [SWGuideTauAnalysis](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideTauAnalysis).The recommended working points by the POG can be found in [TauIDRecommendation](/twiki/bin//CMS/TauIDRecommendation), [TauIDRecommendation13TeV](/twiki/bin//CMS/TauIDRecommendation13TeV).
![UPDATED](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/updated.gif "UPDATED")  The github area for code development is [https://github.com/cms--pog![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/cms--pog)![HELP](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/help.gif "HELP") An introduction to how to use git for development is in this [talk![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://indico.cern.ch/getFile.py/access?contribId=2&resId=0&materialId=slides&confId=272322)Check the section on discriminators below to understand their proper usage.
### Rerunning of the ID on AOD event content ![IDEA!](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/tip.gif "IDEA!")
The collections contained in the simulated samples are often outdated. The most recent ID is in general contained in the releases, so to benefit from all new features and bugfixes, you should re- the PFTau on RECO/AOD. Because the the most up-to-date software is almost always contained in the production releases, **there is no need to merge in any code from other repositories**.To re- the in, you need to add following few lines to your config file
```
process.load(".Configuration.RecoPFTauTag_cff") #loading the configuration
from PhysicsTools.PatAlgos.tools.tauTools import * # to get the most up-to-date discriminators when using patTaus
switchToPFTauHPS(process) # this line and the one above can be ignored when running on reco::PFTauCollection directly
...
process.p = cms.(   #adding to the
....
        process.PFTau*
....
)
```
![, important](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/.gif ", important") When running in *un-scheduled mode* it is enough to add `process.load(".Configuration.RecoPFTauTag_cff")` to the config file.
### Rerunning of the ID on MiniAOD event content in CMSSW 8\_0\_X ![NEW](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/new.gif "NEW")
While it is not possible to fully rebuild taus from jets given MiniAOD event content, it is possible to recompute the BDT output of both isolation and anti-electron discriminators for new trainings made available starting from CMSSW 8\_0\_X onwards. While for releases from 8\_1\_X onwards the necessary infrastructure is included in official CMSSW releases, for 8\_0\_X one has to merge developments from the following cms--pog branch: `cms--pog/CMSSW_8_0_X_tau-pog_tauIDOnMiniAOD-legacy-backport-81X` . In your CMSSW\_8\_0\_X/src/ area do:
```
-topic -u cms--pog:CMSSW_8_0_X_tau-pog_tauIDOnMiniAOD-legacy-backport-81X     # compliant with CMSSW_8_0_26
-topic -u cms--pog:CMSSW_8_0_X_tau-pog_tauIDOnMiniAOD-legacy-backport-81Xv2   # compliant with CMSSW_8_0_29
```
Note that the backport branch of choice depends on the CMSSW version that you are using. The `-u` is necessary to avoid that git checks out all packages that depend on any of the ones touched in this branch since this would lead to a very long compilation. Then compile everything.In order to be able to access the latest and greatest BDT output for the isolation discriminators and save it in your ntuples, you need to add a to your python config file and some code to your analyzer. You can find an [example analyzer![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/cms--pog/cmssw/blob/CMSSW_8_0_X_tau-pog_tauIDOnMiniAOD-legacy-backport-81X//RecoTau/test/rerunMVAIsolationOnMiniAOD.cc) and the corresponding [/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/cms--pog/cmssw/blob/CMSSW_8_0_X_tau-pog_tauIDOnMiniAOD-legacy-backport-81X//RecoTau/test/rerunMVAIsolationOnMiniAOD.py) in /RecoTau/test. Note that the backport include two features to facilitate the acces to the new discriminators:
* From the example you can see, how to embed the new discriminators into a re-created *pat::* collection. FROm that point on you can access the new discriminators as usual from their names as parts of the new pat:: object.
* In case you want to re- the the anti-electron MVA6 discriminator from miniAOD event content, you might face the problem, that one low level varibale, the phi angle at the ECAL entrance is not saved in the miniAOD. In this case you can bypass this flaw by recalculating it on-the-fly, by track extrapolation. For this purpose in the configuration of the discriminator set the parameter *usePhiAtEcalEntranceExtrapolation* to True.

### Rerunning of the ID on MiniAOD event content in CMSSW 9\_4\_X ![NEW](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/new.gif "NEW")
While it is not possible to fully rebuild taus from jets given MiniAOD event content, it is possible to recompute the BDT output of the isolation discriminators for new trainings done with the 2017 simulations v1.In order to be able to access the latest and greatest BDT output for the isolation discriminators and save it in your ntuples, you need to add a to your python config file and some code to your analyzer. The recipe is similar to the one for CMSSW 8\_0\_X, with the exception that the discriminator payload needs to be loaded in the python config file.Most simple and direct recipe can be found [in the attached presentation](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/pub/CMSPublic/SWGuidePFTauID/2017v2-recipe.pdf). The steps can be summarised as following the example with 2017v2 inclusion:1. Download and place in YOUR python directory module that constructs a configuration for rerunning the for different discriminators [runTauIdMVA.py![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/greyxray/TauAnalysisTools/blob/CMSSW_9_4_X_tau-pog_RunIIFall17/TauAnalysisTools/python/runTauIdMVA.py) script2. Add to your PSet initialisation
```
from <your >.runTauIdMVA import *
na = TauIDEmbedder(process, cms, # pass tour process object
    debug=True,
    toKeep = ["2017v2"] # pick the one you need: ["2017v1", "2017v2", "newDM2017v2", "dR0p32017v2", "2016v1", "newDM2016v1"]
)
na.runTauID()
```
3. Define handles to access discriminators in your analysis module:
```

byVVLooseIsolationMVArun2017v2DBoldDMwLT2017 = cms.string('byVVLooseIsolationMVArun2017v2DBoldDMwLT2017'),

byTightIsolationMVArun2017v2DBoldDMwLT2017 = cms.string('byTightIsolationMVArun2017v2DBoldDMwLT2017'),

```

```

    * process.rerunMvaIsolationSequence
    * process.NewTauIDsEmbedded # *getattr(process, "NewTauIDsEmbedded")
    <rest of your processes>)

**Following IDs are accessible with this recipe:**
|  | [Name in pat:: accessed via .tauID(name)](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuidePFTauID?sortcol=1;table=2;up=0#sorted_table "Sort by this column") | [Name in NanoAOD](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuidePFTauID?sortcol=2;table=2;up=0#sorted_table "Sort by this column") | [Notes](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuidePFTauID?sortcol=3;table=2;up=0#sorted_table "Sort by this column") |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| vs jets | *byDeepTau2017v2p1VSjetraw* | rawDeepTau2017v2p1VSjet | Raw DNN score |
|  | *by[WP]DeepTau2017v2p1VSjet* | idDeepTau2017v2p1VSjet | WP=VVVLoose,VVLoose,VLoose,Loose,Medium,Tight,VTight,VVTight |
| vs e | *byDeepTau2017v2p1VSeraw* | rawDeepTau2017v2p1VSe | Raw DNN score |
|  | *by[WP]DeepTau2017v2p1VSe* | =VVVLoose,VVLoose,VLoose,Loose,Medium,Tight,VTight,VVTight |
| vs μ | *byDeepTau2017v2p1VSmuraw* | rawDeepTau2017v2p1VSmu | Raw DNN score |
|  | *by[WP]DeepTau2017v2p1VSmu* | idDeepTau2017v2p1VSmu | WP=VLoose,Loose,Medium,Tight |
Working points against a given source of fakes are measured requiring the loosest working point against other sources (e.g. to measure VSjet WPs, VVVLoose VSe and VLoose VSmu were required). This procedure excludes the part of the parameter space which is very far from the signal region, where the MC modeling can be less accurate and, also the correlations between VS e, mu, jet are stronger. The loosest working points have very high efficiency for the real taus, so it is recommended to always apply them, i.e. to use only candidates that pass at least VVVLoose VSe, VLoose VSmu and VVVLoose VSjet.
### Running of the MVA decay mode identification on MiniAOD event content ![NEW](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/new.gif "NEW")
This section explains how to access the MVA decay mode identification discriminants which can be used as an alternative to the HPS decay mode.**Note:** MVA-DM development branch bases on CMSSW\_10\_2\_22 (10\_6\_17), so use this or newer version from 10\_2\_X (10\_6\_X) release series.1. area
```
cmsrel CMSSW_10_2_22 # or CMSSW_10_6_17
cd CMSSW_10_2_22/src # or CMSSW_10_6_17/src
cmsenv
# add MVA DM code and xml training files
-topic -u cms--pog:CMSSW_10_2_X_tau-pog_MVAdm # or cms--pog:CMSSW_10_6_X_tau-pog_MVAdm
# compile
scramv1 b -j 8
```
2.Add MVA-DM discriminants to your CMSSW python configuration using the ***runTauIdMVA.py*** tool like this:
```
[...]
updatedTauName = "slimmedTausNewID" #name of pat:: collection with new
import .RecoTau.tools.runTauIdMVA as tauIdConfig
tauIdEmbedder = tauIdConfig.TauIDEmbedder(process, cms, debug = ,
                    updatedTauName = updatedTauName,
                    toKeep = [ "MVADM_2017_v1" ]) #other tauIDs can be added in parallel.
tauIdEmbedder.runTauID()
#  and EndPath definitions
process.p = cms.(
    process.rerunMvaIsolationSequence *
    getattr(process,updatedTauName)
)
[...]
```
This will create a new collection called "slimmedTausNewID" with all new discriminants added. The discriminants will be added for version MVADM\_2017\_v1 which was trained on 2017 94X samples.The discriminant and MVA scores added for each are described below:
| [Name in pat:: accessed via .tauID(name)](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuidePFTauID?sortcol=0;table=3;up=0#sorted_table "Sort by this column") | [notes](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuidePFTauID?sortcol=1;table=3;up=0#sorted_table "Sort by this column") |
| --- | --- |
| MVADM2017v1 | This is the MVA decay-mode which is analogous to the decay-mode from the HPS algorithm. It is given as the decay-mode with the highest MVA score and has values of -1, 0, 1, 2, 10, 11. The numbering follows the convention used for the ordinary decay modes with the only exception being the addition of DM=-1 which corresponds to the "others" category - this consists of a small fraction of the events where the MVA does not classify the as any of the main decay-modes |
| MVADM2017v1DM0raw | The MVA score for the DM=0 category (->pi) |
| MVADM2017v1DM1raw | The MVA score for the DM=1 category (->rho->pi+pi0) |
| MVADM2017v1DM2raw | The MVA score for the DM=2 category (->a1->pi+2pi0) |
| MVADM2017v1DM10raw | The MVA score for the DM=10 category (->a1->3pi) |
| MVADM2017v1DM11raw | The MVA score for the DM=11 category (->3pi+pi0) |
| MVADM2017v1DMotherraw | The MVA score for the DM=-1 category ("other" decays) |
For the best results using the 2017v1 version, you should use in conjunction with "newDecayModeFinding". In the newDecayModeFinding, a fraction of DM=10,11 taus have <3 charged PF candidates (instead using tracks and/or PF neutral hadrons). These taus are also included in the training and MVA decay mode assignment, but some of the input variables are set to default values. The performance of the MVA on these events is expected to be poor.More information on the MVA decay mode identification can be found on its AN ([http://cms.cern.ch/iCMS/user/noteinfo?cmsnoteid=CMS%20AN-2020/086![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cms.cern.ch/iCMS/user/noteinfo?cmsnoteid=CMS%20AN-2020/086)) and DPS notes ([https://cds.cern.ch/record/2727092![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cds.cern.ch/record/2727092)).

### Running of the bug-fix version of boosted reco and Id on MiniAOD event content ![NEW](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/new.gif "NEW")
[contact: ]As has been reported in [a POG meeting![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://indico.cern.ch/event/922955/contributions/3890993/attachments/2052364/3441649/BoostedTauValidation_abdollah.pdf), all of the legacy 2016, 2017 and 2018 samples are impacted by a bug in the boostedTau Reconstrcution. The bug was introduced as part of an effort to speed up the cross-cleaning between a boosted pair. The bug is found and fixed and UL samples are expected to get fixed, however none of the legacy samples are usable unless, the cross-cleaning is applied. As the boosted reco is part of the [MiniAOD](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/MiniAOD) and is on AOD samples, the bug-fix can not be used on [MiniAOD](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/MiniAOD) samples. Inseatd we have developed a workaround that can be on the [MiniAOD](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/MiniAOD) sample. [Here![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://indico.cern.ch/event/968998/) is a report on description of the workaround.

##
The recommended ID algorithm is based on [ParticleFlow](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/ParticleFlow?topicparent=CMSPublic.SWGuidePFTauID;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") and is called [HPS](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/MatthiasEdelhoffSandboxSWGuidePFTauIDHPS?topicparent=CMSPublic.SWGuidePFTauID;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.")).The reconstruction code can be found in:
* [DataFormats/TauReco![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmssw.cvs.cern.ch/cgi-bin/cmssw.cgi/CMSSW/DataFormats/TauReco/) - Definition of the dataformats (see event content)
* [/RecoTau![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmssw.cvs.cern.ch/cgi-bin/cmssw.cgi/CMSSW//RecoTau/) - Implementation of the discriminators and decay mode finder.
### Creation
Rerun the sequences, load the steering in your cfg file:
process.load(".Configuration.RecoPFTauTag\_cff")On RECO level [reco::PFTaus![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmssdt.cern.ch/SDT/doxygen/CMSSW_3_8_4/doc/html/dd/d63/classreco_1_1PFTau.html) are used to store all possible taus jets. The result of the various discriminators is stored in [reco::PFTauDiscriminator![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmssdt.cern.ch/SDT/doxygen/CMSSW_3_8_4/doc/html/d3/d9d/classreco_1_1PFTauDiscriminator.html).The initial PFTaus collection will first contain one candidate for each reconstructed PFJet (using the anti-kt algorithm with a cone size of 0.5). The jet direction is set to the direction of the leading charged hadron in the jet (highest pT), which should be within ∆R = 0.1 with respect to the jet axis. In this stage the signal- and isolation cones as well as the decay mode are defined. Subsequently the various algorithms create [PFTauDiscriminators](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/PFTauDiscriminators?topicparent=CMSPublic.SWGuidePFTauID;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") which can be used to select a collection of PFTaus.
Explanation of signal- and isolation cones ![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/toggleopen-small.gif)  Hide ![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/toggleclose-small.gif)
![hadrTauJetIsol.png](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/pub/CMSPublic/SWGuidePFTauID/_500___hadrTauJetIsol.png "hadrTauJetIsol.png")
### Usage
in your event loop (e.g. the `analyze(const edm::Event& iEvent)` method of your analyzer) do
Recipe ![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/toggleopen-small.gif)  Hide ![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/toggleclose-small.gif)
```
// read PFTau collection (set tauSrc_ in to an edm::InputTag before)
    edm::Handle taus;
    iEvent.getByLabel(tauSrc_, taus);
//read one PFTauDiscriminator (set discriminatorSrc_ in to an edm::InputTag before)
    edm::Handle discriminator;
    iEvent.getByLabel(discriminatorSrc_, discriminator);
// loop over taus
    for ( unsigned iTau = 0; iTau < taus->size(); ++iTau ) {
        reco::PFTauRef tauCandidate(taus, iTau);
// check if  candidate has passed discriminator
        if( (*discriminator)[tauCandidate] > 0.5 ){
        // do something with your candidate
        }
    }
```
## Discriminators
The PFTauDiscriminators are used store the result of the various tagging algorithms and select jets that likely originate from a hadronic decay. By definition they are real numbers between 0 and 1 where higher numbers indicate a more positive outcome of the discriminator. Note that most discriminators are in fact binary thus taking just values of 0 (=did not pass) and 1 (=passed).The names PFTauDiscriminator collections follow the `<algorithm-prefix>` + `<discriminator name>` convention. (e.g. the `AgainstElectron` collection can be accessed via )
