## Special Procedures
### Rerun a job with the same random numbers
 By default the random number state is saved in the Event in all the jobs. Then to rerun a job using exactly the same random numbers you have just to configure properly the random number service.For pre-331 jobs, the easiest procedure to restore the state of the random number generators is based on adding these lines at the end of your configuration file:
```
def customise(process):
    if hasattr(process,"RandomNumberGeneratorService"):
        del process.RandomNumberGeneratorService.theSource
    else:
        process.load("IOMC/RandomEngine/IOMC_cff")
        del process.RandomNumberGeneratorService.theSource
    process.RandomNumberGeneratorService.restoreStateLabel = cms.untracked.string('randomEngineStateProducer')
    return(process)
# End of customisation function definition
process = customise(process)
```
N.B. The if statement is mandatory up to now, as presently it is not possible to use the restore mechanism for the part.Post 3\_3\_2, the part of the workflow is no longer in the source, but a separate module, so the deletion of theSource is unnecessary. The line
```
process.RandomNumberGeneratorService.restoreStateLabel = cms.untracked.string('randomEngineStateProducer')
```
should be all that is required.
### How reproduce the Digi and/or DigiSimLink from a production DataSet
 There are basically two different use cases to reproduce the Digi.
* The digitization conditions have changed and you want to evaluate the effects.
* You need to access the Digi and/or DigiSimLink for validation.
The first case is the so called REDIGI work flow. Once you know the input DataSet, there exists a cmsDriver.py command that allows you to do that. The command is:
```
cmsDriver.py test -n 10 --filein output_file_of_step1_of_interesting_dataset.root -s DIGI,L1,DIGI2RAW,RAW2DIGI,RECO --eventcontent RECOSIM --customise Configuration/StandardSequences/DigiToRecoNoPU.py --no_exec
```
This command produces a configuration file that runs over the output of step1 and produces as output two separate files: a new RAW file (step1 output) and a new RECO file ( output). In case you want to change the event content of the new RECO file, you have just to change the --eventcontent option of the cmsDriver.py command. Instead, if you wanted to change the event content of the new RAW file, you have to manipulate the configuration file produced by the cmsDriver.py command. In this case search for the string ***outputCommands = process.RAWSIMEventContent.outputCommands,*** and replace RAWSIM with your favorite event content.Please remind that changing the event content from ***RAWSIM*** to one of the ***FEVT\**** family will produce as output an enormous file. Then, before doing that, evaluate carefully the disk space that you have.In the second use case, instead of producing a new RAW file to be used for the validation, the best strategy is to redo the digitization on the fly. In fact the digitization is really a fast step ( ~ 2 sec/evt for TTbar events). To do so you have to modify as follows the configuration file that you are using for the validation:
1. Add the following includes\*\*
   ```
    process.load('Configuration/StandardSequences/Digi_cff')
    process.load('Configuration/StandardSequences/MixingNoPileUp_cff')
   ```
2. In the definition add this line
   ```
    process.digitisation_step = cms.(process.pdigi)
   ```
3. In the schedule as first operation to do put the digitization i.e.
   ```
    process.schedule = cms.Schedule(process.digitisation_step,
   ```
4. At the end of the file add the lines described in [the previous paragraph](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideSimulation#RandomNumber)
In case you are interested to rerun only a particular digitizer you have to replace the point 2 above with one of the following lines:
* If you are interested only to tracker digis
  ```
   process.digitisation_step = cms..SequencePlaceholder("mix")*process.trDigi*process.trackingParticles)
  ```
* If you are interested only to calorimeter digis
  ```
   process.digitisation_step = cms..SequencePlaceholder("mix")*process.calDigi)
  ```
* If you are interested only to muon digis
  ```
   process.digitisation_step = cms..SequencePlaceholder("mix")*process.muonDigi*process.trackingParticles)
  ```
\*\* If you are interested to redigitize events with PU you have to change the include of MixingModule with the appropriate configuration (i.e. , ,...) and, in addition, to specify in the MM configuration the same files that have been used for the PU during the production. Finally you have to add this line in your configuration file
```
 process.mix.playback = cms.untracked.bool(True)
```
### Pre-Mixing Instructions
 Pre-Mixing is a way of circumventing the need for juggling a huge number of input files of Minbias events for Pileup simulation. "Pre-Mixed" files contain single events that are an overlay of a pre-determined number (or spectrum) of minbias events, so each event represents "pure pileup" at a given luminosity. One of these events is then overlaid on a single hard- event to produce a MC sample. The required inputs are (all with `GEN-SIM` event content):
* A large sample of minbias events
* The target hard- MC sample
To create the Pre-Mixed sample, the overlay sample has to be done first. In order to get the right number of interactions, overlay on SingleNeutrino events is the correct thing to do:
```
cmsDriver.py step1 --evt_type SingleNuE10_cfi  --conditions auto:upgradePLS1 --pileup_input das:/RelValMinBias_13/CMSSW_6_2_0_patch1-POSTLS162_V1_30Aug2013HS-v3/GEN-SIM  --eventcontent PREMIX  -s GEN,SIM,,L1,DIGI2RAW --datatier GEN-SIM-DIGI-RAW --pileup AVE_10_BX_25ns_m8 --customise SLHCUpgradeSimulations/Configuration/postLS1CustomsPreMixing.customisePostLS1 --geometry Extended2015 -n 10 --magField 38T_PostLS1 --no_exec
```
Note that it's very important that there be no detector in this file; otherwise it will be added twice. This makes a file in RAW format so that it is smaller. (Note: new event content. Updated 23 April 2014)
```
cmsDriver.py   --datamix PreMix --conditions auto:upgradePLS1 --pileup_input das:/RelValPREMIXUP15_PU25/CMSSW_7_0_6_patch3-PU25ns_PLS170_V7AN1-v1/GEN-SIM-DIGI-RAW --eventcontent PREMIXRAW -s DIGIPREMIX_S2,DATAMIX,L1,DIGI2RAW,HLT:@relval,RAW2DIGI,L1Reco --datatier PREMIX-RAW --customise SLHCUpgradeSimulations/Configuration/postLS1CustomsPreMixing.customisePostLS1 --geometry Extended2015 --magField 38T_PostLS1 -n 10 --no_exec
```
Note that the input file is expected to have GENSIM content.**For [PostLS1](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/PostLS1?topicparent=CMSPublic.SWGuideSimulation;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") Customisation:** For all steps, the modified customisation `--customise [SLHCUpgradeSimulations](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/SLHCUpgradeSimulations?topicparent=CMSPublic.SWGuideSimulation;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.")/Configuration/postLS1CustomsPreMixing.customisePostLS1` should be used in the `cmsDriver.py` command set, instead of `postLS1Customs`. This keeps the necessary collections for PreMixing while side-stepping the current problem of the missing CSC [Raw2Digi](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/Raw2Digi?topicparent=CMSPublic.SWGuideSimulation;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") and [Digi2Raw](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/Digi2Raw?topicparent=CMSPublic.SWGuideSimulation;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") converters for the post LS1 configuration.For validation purposes, one can use the standard additional tag `DIGIPREMIX_S2:pdigi_valid` on the digitisation step.
#### Pre-Mixing Documentation
The table below contains a description of what [/bin/edit/CMSPublic/PreMixing?topicparent=CMSPublic.SWGuideSimulation;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") does for each subdetector. A short overview of the mixing steps:
1. [/bin/edit/CMSPublic/PreMixing?topicparent=CMSPublic.SWGuideSimulation;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it."): "Standard" minbias events in RAWSIM format (with just and [/bin/edit/CMSPublic/SimHits?topicparent=CMSPublic.SWGuideSimulation;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") as input) are overlaid on empty single neutrino events using a chosen pileup configuration (# of interactions, # of bunch crossings, etc.). For most subdetectors (except muons and some  settings), no detector or pedestals are introduced in this step. Zero suppression thresholds in the calorimeter are set to zero. The digis made in this step are converted to RAW format to save space (with the exception of the RPCs, for which packing-unpacking is not a reversible process). There is a special `PREMIX` event content that is an extension of `GENRAW`, which contains the extra RPC digis and the pileup playback information.
2. Mixing: In this step, a single [PreMixed](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/PreMixed?topicparent=CMSPublic.SWGuideSimulation;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") event (which represents all of the "extra" signals that would come from pileup at the chosen configuration) is combined with one MC Hard- event. This is effectively done at the Digi level, using the [DataMixer](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/DataMixer) machinery. A RawToDigi conversion is done on-the-fly for the [PreMixed](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/PreMixed?topicparent=CMSPublic.SWGuideSimulation;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") events within the Secondary Input Stream used for the overlay. The pileup information for the bunch crossings in the [PreMixed](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/PreMixed?topicparent=CMSPublic.SWGuideSimulation;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") event and the associated pileup playback information are passed through the [DataMixer](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/DataMixer) to the final event. A more detailed description of what happens for each subdetector is given in the table below.

#### Reading Back Event Information in Pre-Mixed Samples
The `CrossingFrameInfoExtended` object is made by the [MixingModule](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/MixingModule?topicparent=CMSPublic.SWGuideSimulation;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") and contains a list of which events are used in each of the beam crossings. This information is pretty easy to extract from the event. However, one needs to know **exactly** which minbias files were used to make the original sample in order to find the correct events. In any case, a stand-alone analyzer `PlayBackRead.cc`, its header `PlayBackRead.h` and a config script  are all attached to this page. They work in 7\_0\_7 and later. Links to files: , [PlayBackRead.cc](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/pub/CMSPublic/SWGuideSimulation/PlayBackRead.cc), [PlayBackRead.h](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/pub/CMSPublic/SWGuideSimulation/PlayBackRead.h)
## [FullSim](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/FullSim?topicparent=CMSPublic.SWGuideSimulation;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") multi-treaded
Within \_7\_2\_GEANT10 branch development of multi-threaded simulation is carried out. For details see [working notes](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin/viewauth/CMS/MKGeant4Notes).
## Releases
Visit the  [Release Web Page](/twiki/bin//CMS/ReleaseSchedule) for up-to-date information on dates for CMS software releases. We also collect records on the evaluation of the CMS simulation application based on different Geant4 releases; for details, visit [the CMS-Geant4 document![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmsdoc.cern.ch/cms/cpt/Software/html/General/simulation/CMSG4Releases.html). Additional information on monitoring technical aspects of the /Simulation performance can be found through the [Simulation Performance Suite Reports![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cms-service-sdtweb.web.cern.ch/cms-service-sdtweb/performance/simulation).Please visit also pages below with the list of feature/goals planned and implemented for the various release cycle.Validation of different Geant4 versions is performed by PPD group
[PdmV](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin/viewauth/CMS/PdmVExternalsValidation).

# Stand-Alone Muon Reconstruction
Complete: ![5](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/pub/CMS/WebPreferences/complete5.png)
Contents:
* [Goals of this page](#Goals_of_this_page)
* [Contacts](#Contacts)
* [Introduction](#Introduction)
* [Set up your environment](#Set_up_your_environment)
* [Samples](#Samples)
* [Configuration file](#Configuration_file)
* [The Production Chain](#The_Production_Chain)
* [Run an Example Production Job](#Run_an_Example_Production_Job)
* [)
## Goals of this page
This tutorial shows how to run the reconstruction of muon tracks in the CMS muon spectrometer (muon system alone) and to analyze its output.
## Contacts
Riccardo Bellan ()
## Introduction
The muon reconstruction chain starts with the "local reconstruction", i.e. the reconstruction of hits in DTs, CSCs and RPCs. Hits within each DT and CSC chamber are then matched to form "segments" (track stubs).In the offline reconstruction, the segments reconstructed in the muon chambers are used to generate "seeds" consisting of position and direction vectors and an estimate of the muon transverse momentum. These initial estimates are used as seeds for the track fits in the muon system, which are performed using segments and hits from DTs, CSCs and RPCs and are based on the Kalman filter technique. The result is a collection of [reco::Track![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmsdoxygen.web.cern.ch/cmsdoxygen/CMSSW_9_2_3/doc/html/dd/d5b/classreco_1_1Track.html) objects reconstructed in the muon spectrometer, which are referred to as **"standalone muons"**. To improve the momentum resolution, a beam-spot constraint can be applied in the fit. Two collections of "standalone muons", with and without the beam-spot constraint, are available in the event record (in both RECO and AOD). A more detailed description of the reconstruction of tracks in the muon system alone can be found in Section 4 of  [CMS AN 2008/097![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cms.cern.ch/iCMS/jsp/db_notes/noteInfo.jsp?cmsnoteid=CMS%20AN-2008/097).Standalone muon tracks are then matched with tracker tracks to form ["global muons"](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookMuonAnalysis#GlobalMu). A schematic of the steps of muon reconstruction is shown below.![MuonReco.gif](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/pub/CMSPublic/SWGuideStandAloneMuonReco/MuonReco.gif)The local reconstruction chain and all details of the production of DT and CSC segments are presented in the [tutorial on local muon reconstruction](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideMuonLocalReco). In the present tutorial we focus on the standalone muon track reconstruction, starting from a data file containing already reconstructed segments.
## Set up your environment
Set your runtime environment (shown for release %WBRELEASENEW%):
`cd CMSSW_%WBRELEASENEW%/src`
`cmsenv`
* [Full instructions](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookSetComputerNode)
* [Summary for every login session](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookSetComputerNode#StepSummary)
* [Access modules from the CVS repository](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookComputingConcepts#Access_Modules_from_CVS_Reposito).
You don't need to checkout and compile any package to run the reconstruction, you simply need an input sample and a configuration file.
## Samples
You can use your favorite already-available sample, or generate one from scratch.
The output of the [tutorial on local muon reconstruction](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideMuonLocalReco) can be used as input for this step.For this tutorial we assume that the sample used in the following already contains:
* the DT segments
* the CSC segments
* the RPC rechits.
## Configuration file
Checkout the following package:
```
/StandAloneMuonProducer
cvs co -r V01-00-05-04 RecoMuon/StandAloneMuonProducer/test/StandAloneMuon_cfg.py
```
This package contains the blocks of configuration files and sequences needed to run the standalone muon reconstruction. These files contain default values for the parameters, and can be included in user's configuration files. The user is not supposed to modify these files directly, but can override a card modifying the values of parameters in the cfg file.
* `python/` directory: contains `cff` files that you can include in your `cfg` file to run the standalone muon reconstruction;
* `test/` directory: provides some `cfg` files as example.
In the following we will use the `StandAloneMuon_cfg.py` configuration file.
## The Production Chain
In general, to run the Standalone Muon production starting from the output of the local muon reconstruction the cfg file needs to contain:
* the `Source` block to specify a file containing DT, CSC and RPC segments and rechits
* the magnetic field and geometry `cfi` files, and some services
* the module blocks included as `cfi` files for the actual reconstruction:
  + the Muon Seed producer module (`MuonSeed`)
  + the Standalone Muon Track producer module (`standAloneMuons`)
* the `OutputModule` to define an output file
* the  defining the sequence of modules to be executed
  + `process.p = cms.(process.MuonSeed * process.standAloneMuons)`
You can get the configuration files for these modules with the simple include statement:
```
process.load("RecoMuon.Configuration.RecoMuon_cff")
```
You may also want to add one or more analyzer modules. To do this you have to specify them and to add them at the end of the execution .
## Run an Example Production Job
In the following we will run the example job:
```
RecoMuon/StandAloneMuonProducer/test/StandAloneMuon_cfg.py
```
which produces the Muon Seeds and Standalone Muon Tracks.To run the job you must:
1. Modify the `StandAloneMuon_cfg.py` file in order to use your sample and decide where to write the output file:
   1. Modify the `Source` section to point to your favorite sample
   2. Modify the `OutputModule`: `fileName = cms.untracked.string('/tmp/RecoSTAMuons.root')`
2. Run the job: `cmsRun -p StandAloneMuon_cfg.py > & ! $SCRATCH/StandAloneMuon.out &`
At the end of the job the `/tmp/StandAloneMuon.root` output file will contain all the objects produced by the standalone muon reconstruction. You can then analyze it either using a CMSSW analyzer or browsing it with a ROOT TBrowser.
##
We also add a simple analyzer to fill a histogram of the pT resolution of the muons. It is implemented in: `RecoMuon/StandAloneMuonProducer/test/` [STAMuonAnalyzer.h![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmssw.cvs.cern.ch/cgi-bin/cmssw.cgi/CMSSW/RecoMuon/StandAloneMuonProducer/test/STAMuonAnalyzer.h?rev=HEAD&cvsroot=CMSSW&content-type=text/vnd.viewcvs-markup)
and
[STAMuonAnalyzer.cc![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmssw.cvs.cern.ch/cgi-bin/cmssw.cgi/CMSSW/RecoMuon/StandAloneMuonProducer/test/STAMuonAnalyzer.cc?rev=HEAD&cvsroot=CMSSW&content-type=text/vnd.viewcvs-markup).**Note:** you can have a look at the code to find an example about how to access the collection of muon `reco::Track` in the event, loop on it and extract relevant information.In the configuration file, the analyzer is specified as:
```
process.STAMuonAnalyzer = cms.",
                                         DataType = cms.untracked.string('SimData'),
                                         StandAloneTrackCollectionLabel = cms.untracked.string('standAloneMuons'),
                                         MuonSeedCollectionLabel = cms.untracked.string('MuonSeed'),
                                         rootFileName = cms.untracked.string('STAMuonAnalyzer.root')
                                         )
```
You can add it to the  defined in the production cfg file to combine reconstruction and histogramming tasks in the same job.
**Note:** you will find both the analyzer module and the corresponding *commented* in `StandAloneMuon_cfg.py`. You only need to uncomment them (and comment the default ) to have the analyzer run.The analyzer produces the output file STAMuonAnalyzer.root containing the pT and 1/pT resolution plots.![res.gif](/twiki/pub/CMSPublic/SWGuideStandAloneMuonReco/res.gif)

##
The  of this page is to describe the specific software that is used in analyses done in the Top Physics Analysis Group (TopPAG). The main group page concerned with the organization of the group can be found is [CMS.TWikiTopQuark](/twiki/bin//CMS/TWikiTopQuark).
##  (TQAF)
To facilitate access to objects and tools used in the analysis of top quarks the TopPAG provides a common  ( [TQAF](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideTQAF)) based on [PAT](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuidePAT) objects. The code resides in the [CMSSW/TopQuarkAnalysis![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/tree/CMSSW_7_3_X/TopQuarkAnalysis) system of CMSSW. It comprises several packages to facilitate the analysis reconstruction and interpretation of events containing top antitop quarks. To find out more about the TQAF have a look to the [SWGuideTQAF](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideTQAF) page.Instructions on how to get started using the TQAF can be found on the [SWGuideTQAF#HowTo](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideTQAF#HowTo). Several PAG specific tutorials exsist in the meantime on the CMS [indico![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://indico.cern.ch/categoryDisplay.py?categId=2063). To find out more about the Physics Analysis Toolkit (PAT) on which the TQAF relies have a look to the [SWGuidePAT](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuidePAT).
## Practical information and some PAT Examples
* Running on first data:
  + [WorkBookPATOnData](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATOnData) (tutorial)
  + [Collisions2010Analysis](/twiki/bin//CMS/Collisions2010Analysis) (most up-to-date information)
* In case you would like to use PAT Object Selectors :
  + [SWGuidePATSelectors](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuidePATSelectors) (General overview)
  + [Tutorial for using Selectors in FWLite](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin/viewauth/CMS/WorkBookFWLiteExamples#Example_3_Using_Selectors)
  + [High-level example of doing a V+Jets Selection](/twiki/bin//CMS/VplusJetsSelectors)

This page summarizes all the twiki documentation of reconstruction in CMS. It points to examples/tutorials, code implementation descriptions, validation and visualization how-tos, FAQ, ...

## RECO/AOD collection
Information on the tracker data format can be found in
* [Data Formats Table in RecoTracker](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideDataFormatRecoTracker) ([more details](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideDataFormatRecoTrackExplanation))
The full list of products can be found in the following pages:
* [RECO collections](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideRecoDataTable)
* [AOD collections](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideAodDataTable)
## and Software Architecture
The software for reconstruction resides in the following cvs domains:
* RecoTracker (core of the )
* TrackingTools (tracking utilities useful also for muon tracking)
### Description of default sequences used for reconstruction
#### Collision data
* [Reconstruction steps Overview](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideTrackRecoSequences#RecOvw)
* [Local Reconstruction](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideTrackRecoSequences#LocalReco)
* [Reconstruction](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideTrackRecoSequences#TrackReco)
* [How to run the Reconstruction Process](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideTrackRecoSequences#RunReco)
#### Cosmic data
Cosmics data were reconstructed using most of tracking code developed for collisions with some modifications due to the different characteristics of cosmic tracking.
The main difference is that the [IterativeTracking](/twiki/bin//CMS/IterativeTracking) approach was disabled and the reconstruction was performed with three different : [CMS.CtfForCosmic](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideCtfForCosmic), [CMS.CosmicTF](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideCosmicTF), [CMS.RsForCosmic](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideRsForCosmic).
Check the actual sequence used in the file [RecoTracker/Configuration/python/RecoTrackerP5\_cff.py![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmssw.cvs.cern.ch/cgi-bin/cmssw.cgi/CMSSW/RecoTracker/Configuration/python/RecoTrackerP5_cff.py?cvsroot=CMSSW&only_with_tag=CMSSW_7_4_15).
### Documentation of
1. **Digitization and Local Reconstruction**
   * [ Reconstruction](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuidePixelReco)
   * Strip Reconstruction: (Domenico,?)
     + [SiStrip Calibration Main Page](/twiki/bin//CMS/SiStripCalibration)
     + [SiStrip Local Reconstruction Page](/twiki/bin//CMS/SiStripLocalReconstructionPage)
2. **Global Reconstruction**
   * *General purpose tracking for LHC collisions*
     + [CMS.IterativeTracking](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideIterativeTracking) (, M.Pioppi) - Description of the CMS tracking approach.
     + [CMS.CtfTracking](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideCtfTracking) (B.Mangano) - The main reconstruction algorithm, Combinatorial Finder.
     + [CMS.RsTracking](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideRsTracking) () - Road Search reconstruction algorithm.
   * *Dedicated tracking for LHC collisions*
     + [CMS.DafTracking](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideDafTracking) (C.Genta, A.Tropiano) - reconstruction algorithm for high pT jets.
     + (W.Adam) - reconstruction and fitting for electrons.
   * *Non-collision Tracking*
     + [CMS.CtfForCosmic](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideCtfForCosmic) (G.Petrucciani, B.Mangano) - Customization of CTF for cosmics.
     + [CMS.CosmicTF](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideCosmicTF) (M.Pioppi) - reconstruction algorithm dedicated to cosmics.
     + [CMS.RsForCosmic](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideRsForCosmic) () - Customization of RS for cosmics.
     + [/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideCtfForBeamHalo) (J.Vlimant) - reconstruction algorithm dedicate to beam halo muons.
3. **Modules of the reconstruction sequence**
   * *Trajectory Seeding*
     + [Seeding from Hit Pairs](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideSeedingFromHitPairs) (M.Konecki) - seed finding using hits pairs.
     + [Seeding from Hit Triplets](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideSeedingFromHitTriplets) (M.Konecki) - seed finding using hits triplets.
     + [Seeding modifications for Displaced Tracks](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideSeedingForDisplacedTracks) (, ) - Seeding configuration for tracks from secondary vertices far from the interaction region.
   * *Trajectory Building*
     + (B.Mangano, W.Adam) - Default pattern recognition for CTF.
     + [Trajectory Builder](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideCkfTrajectoryBuilder) (B.Mangano, W.Adam) - Simple version of the pattern recognition, ignoring hits in tracker layer overlaps.
     + [Building modifications for Displaced Tracks](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideTrkBuildingForDisplacedTracks) (, ) - Pattern recognition configuration for tracks from secondary vertices far from the interaction region.
   * *Trajectory Fitting*
     + [CMS.KfTrackProducer](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideKfTrackProducer) (G.Cerati) - Final fit description (Kalman filter).
     + [CMS.OutliersRejection](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideOutliersRejection) (G.Cerati) - Algorithm for high-chi2 hits removal during the final fit.
   * *Selection*
     + [CMS.FinalTrackSelectors](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideFinalTrackSelectors) (, P.Azzurri) - Module to mark tracks with quality labels.
4. **Tracking tools and services**
   * [RefitterWithConstraints](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideRefitterWithConstraints) (G.Cerati) - Refit tracks adding a momentum or vertex constraint.
   * [CMS.PropagatorsForTracking](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuidePropagatorsForTracking) (W.Adam, B.Mangano, I.Tomalin) - Propagation of parameters in space.
   * [MeasurementTracker](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideMeasurementTracker) (J.Vlimant) - Access the hits in the whole tracker.
   * (J.Vlimant, G.Petrucciani) - Access the hits in particular region of the tracker.
   * [TrajectoryCleaning](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideTrajectoryCleaning) (J.Vlimant) - Remove trajectory duplicates during pattern recognition.
   * [TrajectoryFiltering](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideTrajectoryFiltering) (J.Vlimant) - Chioce of the trajectory to be continued or stopped during pattern recognition.
   * (J.Vlimant) - Tracker layer navigation along the direction.
5. **Description of some advanced topics**
   * [Refitting Tracks](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideTrackRecoSequences#RefTr) (G.Cerati) - Perform a new final fit on the hits.
   * [Electron tracking and GSF](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideTrackRecoSequences#GsfTr) (W.Adam) - Electron reconstruction.
   * [Regional and partial tracking (for HLT)](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideTrackRecoSequences#RegionalTracking) (J.Vlimant) - Fast reconstruction in a subset of the tracker.
   * [Accessing the hit pattern of a](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookTrackAnalysis#HitPattern)  () - Get the hit information from a reconstructed .
   * [Accessing the trajectory at each detector layer](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookTrackAnalysis#TrajLay) () - Get the parameters at each measurement point.
   * [Accessing the trajectory at any point in space](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookTrackAnalysis#TransTrack) (???) - Get the parameters at any point.
   * [Common matrix/vector classes used by tracking code](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideAlgebraicSymMatrix55) (???) - Vector and matrices used to optimize tracking code.
   * [Cluster splitting](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/ClusterSplitting) (, ) - Splitting of merged clusters ( and strip)

# Unscheduled Execution
Complete: ![2](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/pub/CMS/WebPreferences/complete2.png)
Contents:
* [Explanation](#Explanation)
* [Usage](#Usage)
* [Circular Dependence Errors](#Circular_Dependence_Errors)
* [Converting Scheduled to Unscheduled](#Converting_Scheduled_to_Unschedu)
* [Review Status](#Review_Status)
## Explanation
The [EDM](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/EDM) Framework allows two ways to setup the order in which EDProducers, EDFilters, EDAnalyzers run): scheduled and unscheduled
* **scheduled** the configuration file explicitly states the order of modules on Paths and EndPaths
* **unscheduled** Some EDProducers and EDFilters which have not been explicitly placed on a Path or EndPath will be run the first time someone asks for their data (this is known as 'lazy evaluation').
The important thing to understand about unscheduled execution is it appears works exactly like if you had placed all the unscheduled modules that were not explicitly scheduled at the beginning of the path AND in exactly the correct order. Behind the scenes, however, the system actually only runs the unscheduled modules when its data is requested for the first time for the Event.
## Usage
Prior to release 9\_1\_0, one would add the following line to a Python configuration
file to enable 'unscheduled' execution in cmsRun:
```
   process.options = cms.untracked.PSet( allowUnscheduled = cms.untracked.bool(True) )
```
In release 9\_1\_0 and later the above line is obsolete and no longer has any effect. As a
matter of cleanup it should be deleted anywhere it occurs (although it is harmless). In release
9\_1\_0 and later unscheduled execution is always 'enabled'.Prior to release 9\_1\_0, one configured an EDProducer to run unscheduled by defining it and
attaching it to the Process, but not putting it on any Path or EndPath.In release 9\_1\_0 and later one configures an EDProducer or EDFilter to run unscheduled by
also putting it in a Task and associating the Task to a Path, EndPath, Sequence, or .
The details are described here: [SWGuideAboutPythonConfigFile#Task\_Objects](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideAboutPythonConfigFile#Task_Objects).In release 9\_1\_0, unscheduled execution behaves as follows. When an EDProducer
or EDFilter is run unscheduled, it is executed immediately before execution of the first module
that declares it consumes a product the module produces. This includes the case when an
OutputModule declares it consumes a product only to write it to an output file.The filter decision of an EDFilter is ignored when it is run in unscheduled mode. You must
put the EDFilter on a Path to make use of its filter decision.If a module is both on a Path or EndPath and also on a Task, then the module is run
on the Path or EndPath and not run unscheduled. The fact that it is on a Task is ignored
in this case.
## Circular Dependence Errors
If an EDProducer with label A needs a product produced by an
EDProducer with label B and also EDProducer B needs a product
produced by EDProducer A, there is a circular dependence.
The code that manages unscheduled execution checks for
these circular dependences and will throw a fatal exception
if one is encountered. If it didn't, then when A was executed it would ask
for data from B and B would be executed, then B would ask
for A's data so A would be executed again (while it is already
running on the stack), then A would ask for B's data and
B would be executed again ... This pattern would continue
until memory was exhausted and the process would die for
that reason.A circular dependence could involve any number of modules.
Module A could need module B which needs module C which
needs module D which needs module A. The problem is the
same. Also if module A tries to get data it produces itself,
the same problem occurs. The circular dependence could
involve only one module.The best way to avoid or fix these circular dependences
is to use getByToken or getByLabel to request data from the
Event and specify the module label, instance, and type for
each data request. Then the logical dependences between
modules should be designed in such a way that there are
no circles. Finally, if the module label, instance, and type
uniquely defined a product and its EDProducer, there will
be no circular dependences.If a circular dependence error occurs, there are several
things that can be done. First, one should examine to
ensure that all the data requests are actually needed and
used. One link in the circle may be unnecessary or a mistake.
The second thing one should consider is redesigning the
dependences to break the circle. There are a few
other things that can be done.One way for these circular dependences to occur is if
the same module label, instance, and type are produced
in different processes. In this case, one could specify the
process name in the getByLabel or getByToken call and
this might serve to resolve the circular dependency.
In some cases, the intent is that one product involved in
the circle always be retrieved from input file and never produced in
the current process. Starting in 6\_2\_X, one can require this
using an InputTag in the configuration as follows:
```
  cms.InputTag("theModuleLabel", processName=cms.InputTag.skipCurrentProcess())
```
Note that using the same label, instance, and type in multiple processes
restricts the flexibility to move modules between processes
or combine multiple processes into one or use differing
process names.Circular dependences can be caused by using the function getManyByType
or GetterOfProducts and only specifying the product type.
In these cases, the data request is too general and can
end up requesting unneeded products and causing unscheduled
EDProducers to run to produce them. In this case, the
recommended solution is to replace that call with getByLabel
or getByToken where the module label is specified.One last option is to place some or all of the EDProducers in
the circle on a path in the . One should also place
other EDProducers that depend on data from these EDProducers
in the . This is a bad option if many things depend
on the modules placed in the .
## Converting Scheduled to Unscheduled
A convenience python function is available to automatically convert a `cms.Process` from scheduled to unscheduled mode. The function is `FWCore.ParameterSet.Utilities.convertToUnscheduled`. Simply pass the function the `cms.Process` instance you want converted.
Prior to release 9\_1\_0 the function will:
* Remove all modules not on Paths or EndPaths
* Pull EDProducers not dependent upon EDFilters off of all Paths
* Drop any Paths which are made empty by the change
* Fix up the if needed
In release 9\_1\_0 and later releases the function will:
* Resolve SequencePlaceholders
* Remove EDProducers and ignored EDFilters from Paths and EndPaths
* Add removed modules to a Task

### 310 details
* The DQM for TkAl\* ALCARECOs is partially broken as of CMSSW\_3\_1\_0\_pre11. Matthias investigated and observed that none of the histograms that should be created by DQM/TrackingMonitor are filled. This is (as it seems from the cvs comments) due to a rewriting going on in their DQM.
* MuAl\* content is OK, but the DQM is not present. Same problem as TkAl\* ALCARECO since it uses DQM/TrackingMonitor too.
* Number of valid HO tower is low in moving wheels.
### 311 details
* The DQM for TkAl\* ALCARECOs is partially broken. The same problem as of CMSSW\_3\_1\_0.
* Number of valid HO tower is low in moving wheels (could not recover since 3\_1\_0\_pre10).
### 313 details
* MuAl\* content is OK, but the DQM is not present. It looks like the tag V01-01-04 in Alignment/CommonAlignmentProducer/python/ALCARECOMuAl\* did not get into the 31X series but it did in the 32X and 33X ones.

**Status of 351/2/3, 360pre1/2 stays the same as for 350 as there is no major changes in these subsequent versions.**
###### 35X details:
###### **358**
* Fix: now the [TrackExtra](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/TrackExtra?topicparent=CMSPublic.SWGuideValidationTableFastSim;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") collection is saved in the event for pixelTracks
###### **357**
* Fix for very high-energy (>1 [TeV](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/TeV?topicparent=CMSPublic.SWGuideValidationTableFastSim;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.")) particles energy losses in case of big energy deposits in ECAL
###### **355/356**
* Improvements in the iterative tracking algorithms;
* Improvements in  hits multiplicities and in the L1/L2  efficiencies
###### **354** plots and materials can be found via the agenda of the Fast Simulation meeting on March, 16
[here![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://indico.cern.ch/conferenceDisplay.py?confId=87176)
###### **350pre5** plots and materials can be found via the agenda of the Fast Simulation meeting on February, 9
[here![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://indico.cern.ch/conferenceDisplay.py?confId=76879#4)
###### **350pre5** (MUONS):
* Release specific issues:
  + Problem with L1 efficiency and spectra (not a issue, being also observed in the validation, and to be dealt with by L1  group)
* Remaining issues in the Fast/Full sim comparison:
  + L1,L2,L3 muons slightly overefficient in
  + Calo deposits not correctly associated to muons
  +  segments (used in  Id) too close to the extrapolation of the tracker track
###### **350pre5** (CMS.):
* Observed discrepancies (known since some time)
  + Slightly lower energy scale in HB/HE for low-to-medium pT (since chnage in ECAL part of hadron shower in 350pre1)
  + Soft part of the HO spectrum is now wll reproduced for very high-pT jets
  + HF energy scale is OK, but not energy sharing between L and S fibers (even though improved since 331)
  + As a consequence of the above issue, CaloEmEtInHF in MET is softer, while other MET-related distributions demonstrate quite a good agreement
  + Number of constituents is lower than in since long time due to the discrepancy in the hadron transverse shower shape
  + has substantially lower "neutral ", which makes quite low the overall energy scale, while regular an agreement in CMS.CaloJets is quite satisfactory
###### **350pre5** (HLT):
* Good overall performance
* Observed discrepancies
  + of Electron efficiency at the edge of pixels
  + The track-matching step performs below full sim expectations in the barre/endcap transition region
  + TTBar sample HLT evaluation confirms electron and  observations ( over- and Electron under-efficiency respectively)
###### **350pre5** (Tracking):
* Validation with single pions and single muons: still showing large endcap inefficiencies in iterations 4 and 5. Failed.
###### **350pre5** (Electron):
* Overall good performance
* Few problems observed:
  + GSF track outermost stat: discrepancies visible in the pout and distributions; to some extent in the deltaeta (SC-track\_out) as well. The inefficiency of the pattern recognition should be emulated
  + Shower shape in the endcap: Showers too narrow in the Fast Sim. Long standing issue. Need dedicated tuning (unconverted photons)
  + ECAL mis-calibration absent in startup scenario: Problem in the cmsDriver. Fixed by
  + Delta-eta vs eta distribution inverted wrt full sim. Beam position problem ?
###### **350** (Tracking)
\* SUCCESS: endcap inefficiency solved. Note: tracking changed, small tuning still needed. Higher efficiency still observed in the barrel.-- - 2009-09-22

#### Automated validation
![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/toggleopen-small.gif)show guidelines  ![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/toggleclose-small.gif)hide
Guidelines for developers are described in [SWGuideTriggerSoftwareValidation](/twiki///CMSPublic/SWGuideTriggerSoftwareValidation).
 Including: (i) dqm sources, (ii) dqm clients, (iii) dqm gui: [layouts, quality tests, renders](/twiki///CMSPublic/SWGuideTriggerSoftwareValidation#Recipe_for_preparing_layouts_ref).Validation results are shown in the [DQM Offline GUI![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cmsweb.cern.ch/dqm/offline/). To them:
1. Install [grid](/twiki///CMS/DQMGUIGridCertificate) certificates (one time)
2. Open [the GUI![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cmsweb.cern.ch/dqm/offline/)
3. Click on `Run #`
4. In the search box, enter `relval ttbar 3_3_0`
5. Click on `Any` and confirm the dataset
6. In `Workspace`, select `HLT`
7. Navigate to the subsystems' report layout
8. Compare releases, by clicking on the cms logo and selecting references

#### Readiness of Validation Code
To be considered "at full readiness," the validation code needs to either
* Reliably produce filled histograms that accurately reflect the trigger behavior in the DQM GUI OR
* Reliably produce results that can be quickly analyzed using a standalone package
To be considered "not at full readiness," the validation code is present, but either
* The histograms are not reliably filled in the DQM GUI, and/or they do not accurately reflect the trigger behavior OR
* The results are produced by standalone packages, but these packages take a non-negligible amount of time to run
There is a further category for packages that currently lacking active development work

##### Details of Readiness Table
* Electron/!Photon: Validation currently relies on standalone analysis to produce results, results take some time to obtain.
* : Upcoming work on L1 propagator, protection of module labels in configuration for automatic path recognition. Results can be used in the meantime
* : Some empty histograms, active development to address this
* MET: Same issue as . Stadalone code exists as backup to provide validation results
* : Generally ready; most recent [RelVals](/twiki//edit/CMSPublic/RelVals?topicparent=CMSPublic.SWGuideValidationTableHLT;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") only in DQM tier, needed (Looks like it might be an event content issue)
* Top, Higgs: Validation contact still needed to develop these packages
* [SUSY](/twiki///CMSPublic/SUSY): Basic path efficiency counts for MC selection for each RA analysis
* Exotica: Done by standalone analysis; validation package not yet integrated in [HLTriggerOffline](/twiki//edit/CMSPublic/HLTriggerOffline?topicparent=CMSPublic.SWGuideValidationTableHLT;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.")

###### 4.4.0 details
* : previous major issue fixed!
* : higher (2-3%) efficiency wrt , using h130gg. [comment![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://espace.cern.ch/cms-trigger/validation/Lists/TrigVal/DispForm.aspx?ID=344) by A.Perrotta There are indeed some (a few %) differences, not only in the photon, but also in the electron triggers. I see that the L1 part seems to behave correctly. For the electron paths those filters are tracker seeded, and the several approximations we had initially put in the first implementation of those filters was indeed one of the main reason why I was asking since longtime to get a detailed validation of the HLT performance in . We are actually working with the specific customization of the seeding of the HLT tracking algorithm, and try to see whether some fix/tuning can be applied there. Re the photon paths, which do not contain tracking modules, same unmodified "" HLT modules are also used in , and thus harder to understand. experts are looking into it.

* Photon : Still generally 2-3% higher efficiency wrt . Only the path HLT\_Photon20\_CaloIdVT\_IsoT\_Ele8\_CaloIdL\_CaloIsoVL which contains a PixelMatch filter has 3% lower efficiency.

#### 4\_1\_X vs 3\_11\_1\_hltpatch1
* ![Yes / Done](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/choice-yes.gif "Yes / Done") - HLT accepts agree to per cent.
* Comparison of HLT results in RelVal 4\_1\_1 vs 4\_1\_2 are given: [This file](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/pub/CMSPublic/SWGuideValidationTableHLT/menudiff_short.txt) shows the difference in accept rate between 4.1.1 and 4.1.2. The differences are most likely due to the additional HLT-related tags needed to run the same menu configuration in 4.1.1 [tag list found here![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://hypernews.cern.ch/HyperNews/CMS/get/hlt/2009.html). The path-by-path differences broken down by the modules within the paths are contained in [this file](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/pub/CMSPublic/SWGuideValidationTableHLTmenudiff.txt).
##### Dependence of accept rates on tower thresholds in 3\_11\_1\_hltpatch1 - ![/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/choice-no.gif "No")
[This file](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/pub/CMSPublic/SWGuideValidationTableHLT/diff_3_11_1_hltPath1_threshold_dependence.log) shows how the accept rates per path differ in ttbar MC for normal tower thresholds and for increased tower thresholds. Accept rates can be affected by over 10% for the hadronic paths, with the higher thresholds (right arrows in the log file) leading to lower accept rates across the whole pT spectrum for , MET, and HT.
#####  to 4\_1\_1 with tags -![Yes / Done](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/choice-yes.gif "Yes / Done")
[This file](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/pub/CMSPublic/SWGuideValidationTableHLT/diff_311X_41X.log) shows the difference in accept rates for 4\_11\_1 + aforementioned tags compared to the 3\_11\_1\_hltpatch1 values (default tower thresholds). Though the HLT-report has changed between releases, the path accept rates are identical.
#####
4\_1\_3 includes v6 of the 5e32 menu. Compared to the previous version of the menu from above, the version of many cross-channel and paths changed. For the paths that can be directly compared:
* HLT\_JetX paths have a slightly different accept rate (few/10k events)
* HLT\_DijetAveU have an identical accept rate
* HLT\_DoubleJet60\_ForwardBackward\_v2 accepts an event
* Very small difference in accept rate for paths
* A few more events are taken by the HLT\_DiJetX\_PTY, [DijetX](/twiki//edit/CMSPublic/DijetX?topicparent=CMSPublic.SWGuideValidationTableHLT;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.")\_METY paths
* The accept rates for the paths HLT\_QuadJet40\_IsoPFTau40\_v1, HLT\_QuadJet40\_BTagIP both higher by ~20%
* HLT\_QuadJet path accept rates generally lower by ~1%
* HLT\_Mu paths take a few more events
* Newer versions of electron paths have significantly higher accept rate (~ 250/6000)
The list of path accept rates is [here](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/pub/CMSPublic/SWGuideValidationTableHLT/413_short.log); while [this](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/pub/CMSPublic/SWGuideValidationTableHLT/413.log) is the full list of modules within the paths.

###### 3.10.0pre3 details
Many of the harvesting jobs failed for this cycle, so the number of reports expected is limited.
###### 3.10.0pre1 details
 ? : There is an increase in the level 2.5 efficiency from 20% to 40% which is believed to be due to a change in the [TauRegionalPixelSeedGenerator](/twiki//edit/CMSPublic/TauRegionalPixelSeedGenerator?topicparent=CMSPublic.SWGuideValidationTableHLT;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") which is meant to recover the inefficiency due to a displaced beam spot.

###### 384 details
For 384, the MC-based menus HLT\_8E29 and HLT\_1E31 were deprecated and replaced with HLT\_GRun. POGs and PAGs should examine their paths in the MC-based HLT\_GRun menu and adapt their validation code accordingly.
 ? : Since the trigger paths in the current DQM are not available in GRUN, was validated using the L1 and L2 turn on curves.
 ? Susy: we still have to adapt the validation code. Using the old validation code: L1 EG: better in 384 than in 380 for EG triggers (lower efficiency bits are just swapped w.r.t. 380, they are not real lowe efficiency bits). L1 : L1SingleJet30 decreases (from more than 90% to ~87%). Same for L1SingleJet50.
: L1TauJet30 decreased (from >60% to 50%). HLT Electron: Ele10\_SW\_L1R: 70% in 380, 40% in 384. HLT Photon: Photon10\_Cleaned: 80% in 380, 50% in 384. DoublePhoton10: 50% in 380, 20% in 384. DoublePhoton15: 40% in 380, 12% in 384. HLT : Jet30 slightly decreased (>90% to <90%). Same for Jet50 and Jet110.

###### 360pre3 details
 ? : same issue with an L1 inefficiency as seen since 3.5.0.pre5
 ? Update on Muons for 35X and 36X: The issue that has been seen at L1 in the validation package is really an issue of seeding at L2. In 35X, the L1 pattern recognition was changed to take more L1s, resulting an expected higher ghost rate. The L2 seed cleaner would occasionally keep the L2 seeded by the ghost and remove the L2 seeded by the good L1. The temporary fix is to revert the L1 code, which should be done for 3.6.0.pre4 or pre5, and maybe for 3.5.5. The permanent fix, being worked on by the L2 people is to improve or remove the seed cleaner at L2.
 ? Susy: Comparison with 350. Decrease of efficiency in many L1 bits: taus, xtriggers, etm, ett, ht, . Decrease in efficiency in many HLT paths: electrons, photons, , met and ht, btag, xtriggers. Discrepancies in many distributions of objects for many trigger paths

 ? Electron, : overall good agreement with full-sim, except for minor issues: in pixel end-caps, and track matching step, which perform below full-sim expectations
 ? Electron, updates on pixel-less seeding:
looking at the map of the [dead channels](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki//viewauth/CMS/SiStripBadComponentForMC#Realistic_Bad_Components_for_900), the efficiency loss looks compatible with the damages in the [phi coordinate![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://mmozer.web.cern.ch/mmozer/EgammaDQM/CMSSW_350pre3/efficiency_hltL1NonIsoHLTNonIsoSingleElectronSiStripEt15PixelMatchFilter_vs_phi_MC_matched.gif);
whereas for the [eta coordinate![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://mmozer.web.cern.ch/mmozer/EgammaDQM/CMSSW_350pre3/wenu_350pre3_ia32/DQMData/Run%201/HLT/Run%20summary/HLTEgammaValidation/HLT_Ele15_SiStrip_L1RDQMWenu/efficiency_hltL1NonIsoHLTNonIsoSingleElectronSiStripEt15PixelMatchFilter_vs_eta_MC_matched.gif) the loss appears mainly in the TIB+ while the majority of dead channels are in the TIB-; this could be explained, though, if the seeding does not look for all layers, but gives priority (or is exclusive) to TIB inner layers; in this case the leaking cooling loop of TIB+ L2 could explain the fact. (from R.Covarelli)
confirmed () that seeding does not look in all layers (use first two rings of TIB, all rings of TID, and the first two rings of the first three wheels of TEC), and does give priority to TIB rings 1 and 2 through various cuts. This is done to reduce execution time and seed multiplicity, but makes the algorithm suffer when there are such hardware problems.
 ? , update of L1 inefficiency:
the source of the problems appears to have been [identified![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://hypernews.cern.ch/HyperNews/CMS/get/L1TriggerSW/76/2/1.html) as related to introduction of RPC cosmic patterns which affected the GMT muons (from Vasile); the temporary solution being implemented involves updating a GMT record from the global tag (requiring a new global tag for 35X); a more persistent solution should also be envisaged in the future.
 ? BPAG: of ~10% efficiency in the barrel at L2 in , HLT\_Mu9 and HLT\_DoubleMu3 paths due to the presence of L1 ghosts.
###### 350pre3 details
 ? Electrons: In addition to the track matching problem seen in recent releases there is now an additional problem with the pixelless seeding (as seen for HLT\_Ele15\_SiStrip\_L1RD).
Checked not to be related to 32 vs 64 bit archs.
traced these problem to the transition from 'STARTUP3X\_V15::All' to 'STARTUP3X\_V14::All'.
###### 350pre1,2 details
 ? Electrons: track matching has efficiency problems
 ? Top: HLT\_IsoMu9 efficiency seems to be slightly lower (~2-3%) wrt 340.
 ? Higgs: HLT\_Ele10\_LW\_EleId\_L1R efficiency not yet recovered.

a significant change to the tracker mis-alignment scenario between [STARTUP3X](/twiki//edit/CMSPublic/STARTUP3X?topicparent=CMSPublic.SWGuideValidationTableHLT;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.")\_V11 and [STARTUP3X](/twiki//edit/CMSPublic/STARTUP3X?topicparent=CMSPublic.SWGuideValidationTableHLT;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.")\_V12 is confirmed by [DavidF](/twiki//edit/CMSPublic/DavidF?topicparent=CMSPublic.SWGuideValidationTableHLT;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.")., the latter has a more realistic (and smaller) misalignment obtained by running the CRAFT alignment procedures on cosmics MC initially smeared as in STARTUP\_3X\_V11;
this change in alignment appears yo be the cause; the formerly large APE's masked the fact that the KF tracking in the trigger does not cope well with radiation in the electron tracks; now that the APEs are smaller fewer tracks are linked to superclusters; after artificially inflating the APEs, track matching step in 340 was brought into agreement wrt 340pre5; experts are investigating towards devising a long term solution.  ? Higgs:  efficiency recovered but HLT\_Mu9 still 2-3% lower wrt 3.1.2
 ? : in general is consistent with previous release, there are some small differences: (i) /L1 has an increase of ~2%, (ii) L2Iso/L2Reco has a decrease of ~ 3%; the overall efficiency has a decrease of ~1%

###### 3\_5\_0\_pre5 details
* in muon efficiency in the barrel part: a ~10% observed by HLT validation.
  The problems are related to RPC trigger in conjunction with the merging of regional candidates in GMT. The introduction/addition of the cosmic patterns for RPC trigger (in addition to non-cosmic patterns) affected the GMT muons, due to an optimization of rate in GMT when merging the regional muons. The solution proposed by is to update one of the GMT records from the global tag, controlling the merging, which involves new global tags for 35X. More evolved changes in merging could be eventually envisaged, but the proposed solution should fix now the in efficiency. produced already the DB tags for the corresponding record and asked for new global tags. RelVals will be produced to test the fix. RPC PACT, GMT, GT and [L1Extra](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/L1Extra?topicparent=CMSPublic.SWGuideValidationTableL1;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") are marked as bad.

## Goal
## Contacts
For vertex fitting, secondary vertex finding & offline primary vertex finding (B- POG):
* **Group home page**: [BtagPOG](/twiki/bin//CMS/BtagPOG)
* **Contact persons**: T.Speer (Uni Zurich), ()
* **Hypernews forum**: [)
* **Mailing list**: mailto:
For beam-spot determination, V0 reconstruction and online & offline primary vertex finding (Tracking POG):
* **Group home page**:
* **Contact persons**: , B.Magano (. of California)
* **Hypernews forum**: [https://hypernews.cern.ch/HyperNews/CMS/get/recoTracking.html![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://hypernews.cern.ch/HyperNews/CMS/get/recoTracking.html)
* **Mailing list**: mailto:
## Introduction
Vertex reconstruction usually involves 2 steps, vertex finding and vertex fitting. Vertex finding involves grouping tracks into vertex candidates. The vertex-finding can be
very different depending on the physics case (primary or secondary vertex finding, reconstruction of exclusive decays, etc.). Vertex fitting involves determining the best estimate of
the vertex parameters (position, covariance matrix, and track parameters constrained by the vertex position and their covariances) for a given set of tracks, as well as indicators of the fit quality (total chi2, number of degrees of freedom, or track weights).For a basic introduction to vertex reconstruction, see the [Vertexing Section of the CMSSW Workbook](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookVertexReco).
## RECO/AOD collection and the standard sequence.
Only he primary vertex reconstruction step is part of the default sequence, and it will write a VertexCllection into the event. Information on the vertex data format can be found in:
* [Full offline vertex reconstruction](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideDataFormatRecoVertex)
* [HLT vertex reconstruction](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideDataFormatRecoPixelVertexing)
The full list of products can be found in the following pages:
* [RECO collections](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideRecoDataTable)
* [AOD collections](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideAodDataTable)
## and Software Architecture
A beginners guide to vertex finding and fitting is given in the CMSSW Workbook [Vertex reconstruction](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookVertexReco). More detailed information is given below:Note that for all high-level (b-tagging, vertex reconstruction), [TransientTracks](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideTransientTracks) have to be used instead of the persistent reco::Tracks.
### Offline vertex reconstruction
* [Beam-spot reconstruction](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideFindingBeamSpot) (F.Yumiceva)
* [Vertex fitting](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideVertexFitting) (T.Speer, W.Waltenberger): fit of a vertex from a given set of tracks
  + [Track-refit with vertex constraint](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideVertexFitTrackRefit)
* [Offline Primary Vertex reconstruction](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideOfflinePrimaryVertexProduction)
* [Offline secondary vertex finding](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideOfflineSecondaryVertexFinding): search of vertices from a set of tracks
* [Kinematic vertex fit](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideKinematicVertexFit) (T.Speer): fit of a vertex from a given set of tracks using additional constraints
* [Additional Tools](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideVertexTools): Several tools not described above
### Online (HLT) vertex reconstruction
In the HLT, very fast tracking and vertexing is used, based on the Tracker alone. This is described below:
* [track finding and fitting](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuidePixelHitTripletFinding) (M.Konecki)
* [Primary vertex finding and tagging](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuidePVFindingAndTagging) (A.Dominguez, C.Lundstedt)
## MC association and information
* [and TrackingVertices](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideTrackingTruth): MC Truth of tracks and vertexes.
* [Hit and Track Associators](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideTrackMCTruth): tools to compare reconstructed tracks with the corresponding simulated ones.
* [Vertex Associator](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideVertexAssociation): tools to compare reconstructed tracks with the corresponding simulated ones.
* [Track/Vertex history](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideTrackVertexHistoryManual): accessing detailed MC information for reco tracks(vertexes) and tracking particles(vertexes).
## Use of FWLite for Vertex Studies
* [Track parameter and covariance inspection in FWLite mode](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookOfflinePrimaryVertexFinding#PrimVtxAnalysis)
* [Vertex position, error and pull inspection in FWLite mode](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookOfflinePrimaryVertexFinding#PrimVtxAnalysis)
## Vertex Analysis and Validation
A software package exists for producing vertex performance plots. This is useful both to evalulate performance and to verify new software releases. It is described in [SWGuideBtagValidation](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideBtagValidation).
## V0 Reconstruction
* [V0 reconstruction using V0Producer](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideV0Producer)
## Generic Displaced Vertex reconstruction and Nuclear Interactions
* [Nuclear Interactions reconstruction](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin//CMS/NuclearInteractions)
## Tutorial
* An introduction to vertex reconstruction: [link![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://indico.cern.ch/getFile.py/access?contribId=6&resId=0&materialId=slides&confId=42388) (Data and analysis flow tutorials, October 2008)
* A complete introduction to vertex reconstruction, including some details on the internal framework: [link![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://indico.cern.ch/getFile.py/access?contribId=1&resId=0&materialId=slides&confId=15416) (b  and (FNAL), July 2007)
### Old documents
* Some information on the basic elements on the framework (mostly ORCA, but most is still valid in CMSSW) are available on the old vertexReco page ([here![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmsdoc.cern.ch/cms/Physics/btau/management/activities/reconstruction/vertex/vertex.html)). It contains the the presentations from past workshops, tutorials and various other information from ORCA/P-TDR times. Some of it may be a bit outdated though

## Introduction
IGUANA goal is to solve all event display needs of CMS for online and offline monitoring, debugging, simulation, reconstruction, and analysis. Make it trivial to use with a professional quality interface design, possibility to use one command, and wizards to help with configurations and data fetching. Also for developers: easy to extend the functionality. Make it available to all collaborators: e.g. well packaged (together with CMSSW) and Web client to avoid local installations.The basic idea behind IGUANA is that an application is configured at run-time from iglets (a.k.a. plugins). Say, a user wants to display Tracks, (s)he tells IGUANA (in the configuration file) to load the iglet which knows how to display Tracks. The iglets group a set of (a class which knows how to display a type of a data collection). For example, the CSC iglet contains all related to CSC data , such as a [VisCSCStripDigiTwig![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmslxr.fnal.gov/lxr/source/VisReco/VisMuonCSC/interface/VisCSCStripDigiTwig.h?v=CMSSW_1_5_2) class which displays [CSCStripDigi![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmslxr.fnal.gov/lxr/source/DataFormats/CSCDigi/interface/CSCStripDigi.h?v=CMSSW_1_5_2), etc.IGUANACMS - Interactive Graphics and User ANAlysis for CMS - a SCRAM-based project for CMS specific visualization based on ORCA and OSCAR. The IGUANACMS code has been migrated to the new Event Data Model and is now part of the CMSSW project.IGUANA - Interactive Graphics for User ANAlysis - in development since 1999. First public presentation during CHEP 2000. Developed by , , , , , and .

### Multiple tree browsers
The default event display tree for displaying both CMS event data and geometry is large. The dynamic is even larger. The proposed feature separates the first from the latter in two different tree browsers: "CMS Event and Detector" and "Provenance". The text browser is moved to the bottom docking area to allow better visibility of the tables it usually displays.The "CMS Event and Detector" tree is open by default. To open another tree the user clicks on the tree title, for example, "Provenance". See the snapshots attached.This picture shows IGUANA event display at startup (MTCC II setup):
![GUI](/twiki/pub/CMSPublic/SWGuideVisualization/iguana-gui-trees.)This picture shows HCAL barrel and endcap rechits displayed and selected to display the rechits table:

![GUI](/twiki/pub/CMSPublic/SWGuideVisualization/iguana-gui-provenance.)

### Glossary
**NURB** (**N**on**U**niform **R**ational **B**-spline) A type of b-spline that is very flexible. NURB curves can represent any shape from a straight line to a circle or ellipse with very little data. They can also be used for guiding animation paths, for approximating data and for controlling the shapes of 3D surfaces. NURBs are known for their ability to control the smoothness of a curve.**Spline** In computer graphics, a smooth curve that runs through a series of given points. The term is often used to refer to any curve, because long before computers, a spline was a flat, pliable strip of wood or metal that was bent into a desired shape for drawing curves on paper.**B-spline** In computer graphics, a curve that is generated using a mathematical formula that assures continuity with other b-splines.
