# VOMS vs. CMSWEB/CRAB/CRIC/SiteDB
## My VOMS membership is OK but still I can't access CMSWEB or CRAB commands fail with a `can't find username` errpor
If you have problems with your certificate-to-username mapping as needed to access to CMSWEB or use CRAB you should check
<..ch/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/UsernameForCRAB>
and in particular
<..ch/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/UsernameForCRAB#Warning>
## I need to register in SiteDB
There is no such need since end of 2018. Forget about [SiteDB](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SiteDB)
## I tried to register in CMS VO and never got any email
Make sure to check your email (or whichever email has registered as your main email). email: [https://mmm..ch![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://mmm..ch)
If the email still cannot be found (also check junk), For issues with VOMS registration, please email to project-lcg-vo-cms-admin at .ch
# Contacting VOMS server via the browser
# **Common Actions**
## I need to re-sign my AUP
* VOMS policy requires that you sign AUP at least once a year. If you fail to do in time, your membership is suspended, but as long as you are a valid CMS member in datases and have a valid grid certificate, you can re-sign and your membership will be immediately restored. For this try again the "re-sign Grid usage rules" using one of the equivalent URL's:
  + [sign-aup![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](sign-aup)
  + [https://voms2..ch:8443/voms/cms/sign-aup![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://voms2..ch:8443/voms/cms/sign-aup)
* No confirmation mail is sent after you re-sign. You can verify the status of your membership at [https://voms2..ch:8443/voms/cms/user/home.action![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://voms2..ch:8443/voms/cms/user/home.action)
## I have renewed my certificate
* your personal certificate is only valid for 1 year. Every year you will have to get a new one from your VO
* it does not matter if your old certificate is still valid or expired, this may affect how you communicate with your Vo to get the new certificate (e.g. for CA it does not matter) but it is fully irrelevant for VOMS
* You do not need to do anything in VOMS. VOMS simple stores the indentity (DN) from your certificate, as long as that does not change, no action is needed here.
* Simply start using your new certificate by importing it in your browser and creating new `.pem` files and point to those for `voms-proxy-init`, see [WorkBookStartingGrid#ObtainingCert](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookStartingGrid#ObtainingCert)
* Make sure to remove old certificate from your browser to make sure it does use an expired credential !!
* This is independent from the yearly re-signing of AUP, which anyhow requires a valid certificate in your browser
* see more information in [WorkBookStartingGrid#RenewingGridCert](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookStartingGrid#RenewingGridCert)
## I have a new, **different** ! certificate
* **different** is what matters. If you renew your certificate (usually needed every year) and new one has the same DN, no action is needed in VOMS
* if you switch to a new DN becasue you are using a different CA or changed your name or whatever, you need the actions below
  + **Important:** **do not create a new membership !**  If you visit VOMS Admins web page using your new certificate, it will see that it does not know it and will prompt you to register as a new user. Having multiple membership for the same physical person in unfortunately possible, but tricky to properly manage, additionally, besides very very few special use cases, it is never useful and usually it only leads to confusion and errors.
  + what you should do is to [add your certificate to your current /bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideVomsFAQ#Add_a_new_certificate_to_my_memb). Then VOMS will accepts either certificate on equal grounds and you can safely stop using one as convenient for you. Later you can delete old certificates at your leisure simply to keep things tidy.
## Add a new certificate to my membership
1. make sure that you still have the old certificate (the one which VOMS knows you by) in your browser, so that you can authenticate to VOMS as a member
2. make sure you have made the PEM files from your new certificate (see [this link](..ch/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookStartingGrid#ObtainingCert) )
3. go to your [VOMS home page![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](user/home.action) and scroll down a bit until you can select the "add new certificate" button as in the screeshot below (or use this quick link: [user/request-certificate.action![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](user/request-certificate.action) )
    ![VOMS-add-an-additional-certificate.png](/twiki/pub/CMSPublic/SWGuideVomsFAQ/VOMS-add-an-additional-certificate.png)
4. you will be directed to this page where you should upload a PEM encoded certificate (see the blue pointer)
    ![VOMS-certificate.png](/twiki/pub/CMSPublic/SWGuideVomsFAQ/VOMS-add-certificate.png)
5. do not try to Enter a DN, CA couple, it is difficult to do it right
    ![VOMS-add-certificate-1.png](/twiki/pub/CMSPublic/SWGuideVomsFAQ/VOMS-add-certificate-1.png)
6. select the `usercert.pem` file which you created in the first step, like this
    ![VOMS-upload-pem.png](/twiki/pub/CMSPublic/SWGuideVomsFAQ/VOMS-upload-pem.png)
7. click on the (unfortunately badly named) "Request certificate" button at bottom right to request the addition of this certificate to your membership
    ![VOMS-RequestCertificateButton.png](/twiki/pub/CMSPublic/SWGuideVomsFAQ/VOMS-RequestCertificateButton.png)
8. the request to add the certificate will be sent to CMS VOMS Administrators which will approve (unfortunately we do not have a way to take humans out this loop)
#
## Basic help
* The CA web page at [https://ca..ch/ca/![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://ca..ch/ca/) has an [HELP tab![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://ca..ch/ca/Help/) in which points to very useful, even browser specific, information. Look there first.
## Can not open VOMS home page in my browser
there can be many reasons, here are some debugging tips. If you are an expert with little time, jump to [#QuickTroubleshoot](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideVomsFAQ#QuickTroubleshoot)
### Wrong URL
* make sure you use `https`, not plain `http` and start from one of these equivalent URL's
  + [https://voms2..ch:8443/voms/cms/![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://voms2..ch:8443/voms/cms/)
  + [https://lcg-voms2..ch:8443/voms/cms/![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://lcg-voms2..ch:8443/voms/cms/)
### Possibly OS issues
* if you get the message "This site can’t be reached: `lcg-voms2..ch` unexpectedly closed the connection." and you are running on Windows, it is likely that your anti-virus program cut in and interfered with your connection (see also "?" below). In that case, moving to a Linux distribution (e.g. ) or a and connecting from there is the fastest way to get going.
### Browser issues
#### Browser kind ?
* We recommend to use a recent version of . There is little to no experience with e.g. among CMS VOMS administrators. has sometimes it's own of what security should mean and can cause trouble. Feel free to use it, but in case of problems, first try .
#### Personal certificate ?
* Make sure you have a valid **personal** certificate in your browser
* If you have and expired certificate in your browser, you will get the same errors as if you have none. Always make sure that you keep the certificate in your browser up to date whenever you get a new one from your CA
* if your certificate expired and you are not sure how to get a new one, please see <..ch/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookStartingGrid#ObtainingCert>
* The way to import/delete/inspect **Your certificate** is heavily browser (version) dependent, although e.g. and have a very similar look and fell for those things at least in recent (2020 e.g.) versions. maintains up-to-date instruction in [https://ca..ch/ca/Help/![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://ca..ch/ca/Help/) just look in the menu at the left of the page for your browser, e.g. for the item is called `Import and export certificates using`
#### Authority root certificate ?
* Make sure that you load and trust root certificates in there. Instructions for various browsers can be find here : [https://cafiles..ch/cafiles/certificates/list.aspx?ca=grid![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cafiles..ch/cafiles/certificates/list.aspx?ca=grid)
  + some more tips for can be found here, note that nor CMS nor maintains this page : [)
* **\*Please Note\***: you might have an older Root CA Certificate stored in your browser, which expired in spring 2023. You will need to explicitly remove that and re-install the new one from the CA page above in order to connect to the CMS VOMS server.
#### Security Exception ?
* The VOMS server uses a certificate from the Grid Certificate Authority (CA), and this is not "known" to the browsers by default, so sometimes you get a warning that the site is "insecure" or "untrusted" (see below). To fix this warning, you can install the Grid CA's root certificate using the instructions in the links at: [https://cafiles..ch/cafiles/certificates/![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cafiles..ch/cafiles/certificates/) -- this will also fix the same issue with other sites on the LHC Computing Grid.
* Alternatively, if the page says "This Connection is Untrusted" or similar, you may try the shortcut offered at the last line of the same page, "I Understand the Risks" as in reality there is no risk to try. Click it, and from the next page select "Add Exception". The sub-page will ask you to "Confirm Security Exception". So you confirm, and you should be able to get in.
####  ?
* Check your  and http proxy settings
#### cookies ?
* Clear the History, Cache and Cookies of and restart the browser
#### ?
* Beware your . Especially when you are using Windows. We have seen cases in which an tool (usually ) interferes with the browser making it impossible to securely connect to servers even if you trusted all CA's as indicated above. For details and cure see [this ticket![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://ggus.eu/index.php?mode=ticket_info&ticket_id=123597#update#24) . There are also reports that on [MacOS](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/MacOS?topicparent=CMSPublic. "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") interferes destructively with CA certificates, see [https://hypernews..ch/HyperNews/CMS/get/computing-tools/6139/2/1/1.html![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://hypernews..ch/HyperNews/CMS/get/computing-tools/6139/2/1/1.html)
#### [KeyChain](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/KeyChain?topicparent=CMSPublic. "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") error (on ) ?
* we had one report (Nov 2021) of the obscure error in the following screenshot, which was solved as: After some googling I found that there is a bug, first reported in 2009, that still seems to be present on my new . Using the command line tool as described here seemed to work for me: [http://www.openradar.me/7092640![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://www.openradar.me/7092640)
 ![.png](/twiki/pub/CMSPublic/SWGuideVomsFAQ/.png)
### Certificate issues
* Make sure that you have the root certificate of the Grid Authority installed in your browser, see for example [https://ca..ch/ca/Help/?kbid=040110![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://ca..ch/ca/Help/?kbid=040110) to do this for .
* Make sure you have imported your current personal certificate in your browser (i.e the one you want to be registered as CMS VO member)
* A usual problem is that your personal certificate in your browser has expired. The browser my warn you about this, but it is worth to check explicitly:
  + Start the , and from the generic part follow the chain:  `-> Preferences -> Advanced -> Encryption -> certificates -> Your certificates -> Expires on ...` There are listed all your certificates, with their end-dates. Please observe that the CMS-VO membership and its end-date are independent of the Certificate end-date.
  + If your personal certificate has indeed expired, then you need a new certificate from one of the Certificate Authorities (CA) to be downloaded into your browser. Here is the start-up procedure which you probably know: <..ch/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookStartingGrid#BasicGrid>
  + if you need to ask the Certificate from some other place than , then these addresses may be useful:
    - [http://lcg.web..ch/LCG/digital.htm![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://lcg.web..ch/LCG/digital.htm)
    - [http://www.eugridpma.org/members/worldmap/![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://www.eugridpma.org/members/worldmap/)
    - [)
### Test page
* Try to verify your certificate by visiting this page
  + [https://cmsweb..ch/auth/trouble/![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cmsweb..ch/auth/trouble/)
* And if needed, use [CMSWEB Diagnostic tips](..ch/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/UsernameForCRAB#CMSWEB_common_problems_and_solut)
### Error messages and screenshots of
#### PR\_END\_OF\_FILE\_ERROR in
* Recent versions of print this very obscure message when simply there is no valid user (personal) certificate in the browser (see screenshot below). **\*\*Please make sure you have your (valid) certificate installed in .\*\***
#### Check your certificate
* Start from the VOMS Admin home page at [https://voms2..ch:8443![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://voms2..ch:8443) . While access to that page requires a proper SSL connection and a valid certificate, it does not require CMS VO memberhsip, so you can use it to separate VOMS problems from certificate/SSL problems. Click on `cms` Most will be one of the following screenshots
##### No certificate (or expired certificate) in your browser (older browsers)
![Voms home No Certificate](/twiki/pub/CMSPublic/SWGuideVomsFAQ/VOMS-nocert.png)
##### No certificate (or expired certificate) in your browser (newer versions e,g, 68 ))
![Voms home No Certificate](/twiki/pub/CMSPublic/SWGuideVomsFAQ/VOMS-nocert-2.png)
##### Valid certificate not known to VOMS yet
![Voms home Not Member](/twiki/pub/CMSPublic/SWGuideVomsFAQ/VOMS-home-newcert.png)
#### Check your certificate using the tab in VOMS page
* You will see one of the following possibilities:
##### 1 No valid certificate in your browser (older version)
![](/twiki/pub/CMSPublic/SWGuideVomsFAQ/VOMS-CertInfo-nocert.png)
##### 2 No valid certificate in your browser (newer versions)
![](/twiki/pub/CMSPublic/SWGuideVomsFAQ/VOMS-Certinfo-nocert-2.png)
##### 3 Valid certificate, but not known to VOMS
![/SWGuideVomsFAQ/VOMS-CertInfo-notmember.png)
##### 4 All OK
![/pub/CMSPublic/SWGuideVomsFAQ/VOMS-certinfo-OK.png)
### Still need help
* **It is impossible to help based on reports like "I got error" or "this link does not work".**
* If you need to report a problem to support, provide the specific and details error messages you get, possibly attaching screenshots. And describe the diagnostics steps you already took and what they produced.
## The connection to voms2..ch:8443 was interrupted while the page was loading
* this is usually due to using `http` in place of `https`, see [#Wrong\_URL](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideVomsFAQ#Wrong_URL) above
* there are also cases where a simply browser restart can fix it
## I get an empy page when connecting to VOMS
* this is most likely a browser issue, se [#/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideVomsFAQ#Browser_issues) above
* it is also possible that the VOMS server was temporarely overloaded, try the other equivalent URL ( see [#Wrong\_URL](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideVomsFAQ#Wrong_URL) above ) and try again after some random time. If problem persists contact support (see [#/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideVomsFAQ#Still_need_help) above)
## Can not open VOMS page (quick guide for experts)
1. Make sure the personal certificate is in your browser (and please use or , other browsers are known to have issues) and that the certificate is valid:
   * From the generic part of the (similar on ) follow the chain:  `-> Preferences ->  Advanced -> Encryption ->  certificates  -> “Your Certificates”` there, check that the certificate you want to use has a date for “Expires” which is in the future.
1. If not, you have to get a new one from any of the Certificate Authorities (CA), for example from : [https://ca..ch/ca/![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://ca..ch/ca/)
1. Then try again the "re-sign Grid usage rules" (see FAQ above about signing AUP)
# Contacting VOMS server via the `voms-proxy-init` command
Your grid certificate needs to be present in two places:
* the VOMS server, via the registration as VO member (see above)
* the `~/.globus` directory in the machine which you use to issue the `voms-proxy-init` command.
Most problems originate from having different certificates listed in those places, usually as a result of an incomplete attempt to update to a new certificate.
* + If you have probolems with the `voms-proxy-init` command, make sure that you follow instructions in <..ch/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookStartingGrid#ObtainingCert> about how to properly install your certificate in the `~/.globus` directory
Typical error messages in those cases are:
* `cms: User unknown to this VO.`
* `User credential is not valid!`
You can verify what you have in `~/.globus` with the command
* `openssl x509  -subject -dates -noout  -in ~/.globus/usercert.pem`
You should compare the Subject it prints with what you used when registering in VOMS. If you need help in figuring out, please send the output of that command toghether with the one from `voms-proxy-init -voms cms`

## About Schedd
Schedds are just an HTCondor Schedd with some custom configs.
### Usage scenario of schedds and hardware requirements
submission is done in unit of "tasks". A task is one workflow aimed at processing one dataset and is
expanded into up to a maximum of 10k HTCondor jobs managed by one HTCondor DAGMAN metascheduler.
Those DAGMAN processes run on the schedd in the scheduler universe and compete with memory with the schedd and the
condor shadow processes. For this reason we the number of tasks which can run at same time
on each schedd (as of April 2020 at 200) and select machines with large RAM. CPU requirements are usuallyschedd's also need disk space to host the log files which are needed for DAGMANs and jobs status tracking and
the logs returned from the remotey executed jobs which are made available to users and operators for debugging.
Since disk access for HTCondor is critical, we decided to protect it by using two separate disk .
One volume has all condor logs, pointed to as the SPOOL\_DIR for each task, and select a CEPH High I/O volume for this.
One other volume is used as home directory for the various pool accounts and (potentially largish) user jobs log files
are moved there once retrieved by condor schedd. This is called WEB\_DIR.
The WEB\_DIR for each task is made accessible on the web via HTTP (hence the name) via an httpd Apache
daemon running on each schedd.
For easy navigation each task's webdir is `/home/grid/cmsxxx/taskname` and contains a symbolic link to SPOOL\_DIR for that task,
and each SPOOL\_DIR has a symbolic link to the WEB\_DIR for that task.
For security reasons, those apache servers are not exposed outside CERN firewall and access to those
files is proxied through CMSWEB wich provides a secure redirection, see: <https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/ScheddDeployment#Redirection_rules_for_CMSWEB>
## Deployment of Schedd for operators
### Machine details
This machine should be managed by so you need to ask VOC  to provide a machine in openstack project with the following :
|  |
| --- |
| Table 1 |
|  | |
| Flavor | m2.3xlarge |
| Flavor ID | 28936 |
| RAM | 58.6GB |
| VCPUs | 32 VCPU |
| Disk |  |
|  | |
| Imagen Name | [2015-09-04] |
| landb-mainuser | CMS-SERVICE-CRAB3HTCONDOR |
| landb-responsible | CMS-SERVICE-CRAB3HTCONDOR-ADMINS |
| tenant-name | CMS |
|  Attached | |
| HighIO volume attached To | <your-brand-new-vm>\_high on /dev/vdb |
| Standard volume attached To | <your-brand-new-vm>\_standard on /dev/vdc |
Why you cannot create the VM by yourself since you have access to project? Simple, those  are not available for you and neither the HighIO . The instructions here were tested and they work for a VM which follow the specifications listed on table 1.Be sure that file .pp on master branch ([https://gitlab.cern.ch/ai/it--hostgroup-vocmsglidein/blob/master/code/manifests/modules/.pp![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://gitlab.cern.ch/ai/it--hostgroup-vocmsglidein/blob/master/code/manifests/modules/.pp)) is up to date with the attached  info, the HighIO volume must be mounted on /data and standard volume on /home/grid. If is not updated ask VOC to update it otherwise you will need to do it by youself. is a code snippet that need to be inserted on .pp by VOC, please pay attention to the block devices used by HighIO volume(/dev/vdb) and /vdc).
These lines will take care of create a partition table and a ext4 FS.
```
  elsif $::hostname == 'pvtschedd' {
    exec {'/sbin/mkfs.ext4 -L "STANDARD-VOL" /dev/vdc':
      unless => '/sbin/blkid -t TYPE=ext4 /dev/vdc'
    }
    exec {'/sbin/mkfs.ext4 -L "HIGH-IO-VOL" /dev/vdb':
      unless => '/sbin/blkid -t TYPE=ext4 /dev/vdb'
    }
    mount { "/mnt":
      ensure => absent,
    }
    file{"/data":
      ensure => directory,
      mode => 0755,
    }
    mount {"/data":
      device => "/dev/vdb",
      fstype => "ext4",
      ensure => "mounted",
      options => "defaults",
      atboot => "true",
      require => File['/data']
    }
    file{"/home/grid":
      ensure => directory,
      mode => 0755,
    }
    mount {"/home/grid":
      device => "/dev/vdc",
      fstype => "ext4",
      ensure => "mounted",
      options => "defaults",
      atboot => "true",
      require => File['/home/grid']
    }
  }
```
Once you get the machine you need to create a yaml file for it, you can just copy and paste from another vm, for instance vocms0106.Bear in mind that there are 2 kinds of schedds, production schedds(the ones in master branch) and ITB schedds(the ones on qa branch).To deploy production schedds you should write an yaml file like this:
Show yaml file sample![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/toggleopen-small.gif)  Hide yaml file sample![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/toggleclose-small.gif)
```
gwms_type: crabschedd
cernfw_landbset: it_cc_cms_glideinwms
glidecondor_pool: global
condor_version: 8.5.4-1.el6
sssd::interactiveallowusers:
   - cmsprd
sssd::interactiveallowgroups:
   - cms-service-
   - cms-service-crab2
   - cms-service-crab3htcondor
   - cms-service-glideinwms
```
and to deploy an ITB schedds one like this:
Show yaml file sample![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/toggleopen-small.gif)  Hide yaml file sample![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/toggleclose-small.gif)
```
gwms_type: crabschedd
cernfw_landbset: it_cc_cms_glideinwms
glidecondor_pool: itb
condor_version: 8.5.4-1.el6
sssd::interactiveallowusers:
   - cmsprd
sssd::interactiveallowgroups:
   - cms-service-
   - cms-service-crab2
   - cms-service-crab3htcondor
   - cms-service-glideinwms
```
In case you are deploying an dev schedd use this yaml file to avoid submissions to FNAL LPC:
Show yaml file sample![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/toggleopen-small.gif)  Hide yaml file sample![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/toggleclose-small.gif)
```
gwms_type: crabschedd
cernfw_landbset: it_cc_cms_glideinwms
glidecondor_pool: itb
condor_version: 8.5.4-1.el6
lcp_submit: false
sssd::interactiveallowusers:
   - cmsprd
sssd::interactiveallowgroups:
   - cms-service-
   - cms-service-crab2
   - cms-service-crab3htcondor
   - cms-service-glideinwms
```
Now go to your cloned repo of [https://gitlab.cern.ch/ai/it--hostgroup-vocmsglidein![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://gitlab.cern.ch/ai/it--hostgroup-vocmsglidein) and write the yaml file.
```
cd it--hostgroup-vocmsglidein/data/fqdns
git checkout master
git pull
cp vocms0106.cern.ch.yaml <your-brand-new-vm>.cern.ch.yaml
```
Do the necessary changes to have either a production or a ITB schedd and commit your changes to gitlab, remember for production schedds push your changes to master branch for ITB schedds push to qa branch.
```
git add <your-brand-new-vm>.cern.ch.yaml
git commit -m 'a nice description for your commit'
git push origin master
```
### first run
After create the yaml file you are ready to run for the first time. This will setup the machine, install condor and all default configs, create all users home directories under /home/grid, install cron jobs, install lemon alarms and sensors. Most probably you will need to run at least 3 or 4 times until all dependent services get installed and configured. Please during the run pay attention to all outputs.
```
sudo -s
 agent -tv
```
Once you dont get any errors, create the ***/etc/grid-security/condorkey.pem***, this file is necessary to allow the schedd to contact argus and get a grid user name for a particular user DN. Run the following command for that:
```
cp /etc/grid-security/hostkey.pem /data/srv/condorkey.pem.tmp; mv /data/srv/condorkey.pem.tmp /etc/grid-security/condorkey.pem; chown condor:condor /etc/grid-security/condorkey.pem
```
This command comes from the cron job installed by ,
# Configuration details
All config files are located at ***/etc/condor/config.d/*** folder but only ***82\_cms\_schedd\_crab\_generic.config*** is specific for . Usually you dont need to touch these files and if you need to apply custom changes for a specific schedd you should write your changes on ***99\_local\_tweaks.config*** and if after some time you decide that this custom change needs to be applied to all schedds is better to move the change to ***82\_cms\_schedd\_crab\_generic.config*** and leave ***99\_local\_tweaks.config*** much cleaner as possible.82\_cms\_schedd\_crab\_generic:
Show ![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/toggleopen-small.gif)  Hide ![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/toggleclose-small.gif)
```
########################################################
# HTCondor configurations specific to  schedd
# Adding JobStatus to significant attributes to help  sort out
# idle jobs per user
# Adeed 2015-07-29
ADD_SIGNIFICANT_ATTRIBUTES=$(ADD_SIGNIFICANT_ATTRIBUTES),CRAB_UserHN
# Accounting group settings for
use_x509userproxy = true
accounting_group = analysis
SUBMIT_EXPRS = $(SUBMIT_EXPRS) use_x509userproxy accounting_group
# To cache Argus results and prevent GSI authorization callout
# related timeouts.
# Added by  - Nov. 25, 2014
GSS_ASSIST_GRIDMAP_CACHE_EXPIRATION=7200
# Overwriting the system periodic remove expression for
SYSTEM_PERIODIC_REMOVE = ((JobUniverse=!=7)&&(((NumJobStarts>9)=?=True)||((NumShadowStarts>19)=?=True)))
SYSTEM_PERIODIC_REMOVE = ($(SYSTEM_PERIODIC_REMOVE)) || ((DiskUsage>27000000)=?=True)
#  version of Condor used a lower default
GSI_DELEGATION_KEYBITS = 1024
#  full  delegation,
# but keep the delegation to worker nodes limited and short
DELEGATE_FULL_JOB_GSI_CREDENTIALS = True
SHADOW.DELEGATE_FULL_JOB_GSI_CREDENTIALS = False
DELEGATE_JOB_GSI_CREDENTIALS_LIFETIME = 0
SHADOW.DELEGATE_JOB_GSI_CREDENTIALS_LIFETIME = 86400
#  the  servers
SCHEDD.ALLOW_WRITE = */vocms052.cern.ch, */vocms045.cern.ch, */vocms0118.cern.ch, */vocms0119.cern.ch, */$(FULL_HOSTNAME)
SCHEDD.HOSTALLOW_WRITE =
#  the number of dagmans
START_SCHEDULER_UNIVERSE = TotalSchedulerJobsRunning < 250
Used_Gatekeeper = "$$(GLIDEIN_Gatekeeper:Unknown)"
JOB_CMSSite = "$$(GLIDEIN_CMSSite:Unknown)"
# the userlog will have Used_Gatekeeper defined at job runtime
# and MATCH_GLIDEIN_Gatekeeper at job termination
# but never both
JOB_Gatekeeper = ifthenelse(\
 substr(Used_Gatekeeper,0,1)=!="$", Used_Gatekeeper, \
   ifthenelse(\
       MATCH_GLIDEIN_Gatekeeper=!=UNDEFINED,MATCH_GLIDEIN_Gatekeeper,\
           "Unknown"))
SUBMIT_EXPRS = $(SUBMIT_EXPRS) JOB_Gatekeeper JOB_CMSSite Used_Gatekeeper
# this assumes noone else is defining the list
job_ad_information_attrs = MATCH_GLIDEIN_Gatekeeper, JOB_Gatekeeper,\
# in the Condor logic, this is a user-provided attribute
# so tell the schedd to treat it as such
SUBMIT_EXPRS = $(SUBMIT_EXPRS) job_ad_information_attrs
# Disabling FSYNC() call for logs
# Added 2015-FEB-09
CONDOR_FSYNC = false
#  specific job throttle parameters
# Added 2015-FEB-09
JOB_START_DELAY = 2
JOB_START_COUNT = 10
# Used by  for HTTP access to log files
# Added 2015-FEB-16
CRAB_StorageRules = ^/home/grid,http://vocms0106.cern.ch/mon
HISTORY_HELPER=$(LIBEXEC)/condor_history_helper
#  this so it reverts to default of 10k
# ELOG: https://cms-logbook.cern.ch/elog/GlideInWMS/3413
#HISTORY_HELPER_MAX_HISTORY=1000000
#  on 2015-08-04
# libsnoopy.so has been updated, so no longer needed
# ELOG: https://cms-logbook.cern.ch/elog/GlideInWMS/2472
# USE_CLONE_TO_CREATE_PROCESSES=false
# To help retrieve condor logs for
KILLING_TIMEOUT = 300
# Enabling OVERFLOW for  machines only
CMS_ALLOW_OVERFLOW = "True"
OVERFLOW_US = ifthenelse(regexp("T[1,2]_US_",DESIRED_Sites),"True",UNDEFINED)
OVERFLOW_IT = ifthenelse(regexp("T[1,2]_IT_",DESIRED_Sites),"True",UNDEFINED)
OVERFLOW_UK = ifthenelse(regexp("T2_UK_London_",DESIRED_Sites),"True",UNDEFINED)
DESIRED_Overflow_Region = strcat( ifthenelse(OVERFLOW_US=?="True","US", "none"), ",",", "none"), ",", ifthenelse(OVERFLOW_UK=?="True","UK", "none") )
SUBMIT_ATTRS = $(SUBMIT_ATTRS) OVERFLOW_US OVERFLOW_IT OVERFLOW_UK CMS_ALLOW_OVERFLOW DESIRED_Overflow_Region
# To monitor the number of overflow jobs
OVERFLOW_CHECK = ifthenelse(MATCH_GLIDEIN_CMSSite isnt undefined, ifthenelse(stringListMember(MATCH_GLIDEIN_CMSSite,DESIRED_Sites),FALSE,TRUE), FALSE)
SUBMIT_ATTRS = $(SUBMIT_ATTRS) OVERFLOW_CHECK
# Adding PER_JOB_HISTORY_DIR feature
PER_JOB_HISTORY_DIR=/data/srv/glidecondor/condor_local/job_history/
# Number of jobs Dagman will submit to condor_q
DAGMAN_MAX_SUBMITS_PER_INTERVAL = 100
```

In this case we have this configurations
| [knob](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/ScheddDeployment?sortcol=0;table=3;up=0#sorted_table "Sort by this column") | [Effect](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/ScheddDeployment?sortcol=1;table=3;up=0#sorted_table "Sort by this column") |

All schedds needs to be added to Global Pool central managers and and also to tier0 Central Managers and for that is sufficient to create an elog on [https://cms-logbook.cern.ch/elog/GlideInWMS![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cms-logbook.cern.ch/elog/GlideInWMS) with the following content:

Please add the schedd <your-brand-new-vm>.cern.ch to global pool central managers and  and also to tier0 central managers and .

```
## Configurations changes on LPC firewall
Since now all scheeds run job router they need to be whitelisted in the FNAL firewall, so write a email to <> and <> asking then to include the new schedd on the firewall .

to proceed you need to fork [https://github.com/dmwm/deployment![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/dmwm/deployment) repo and then clone your forked repo and create a pull request with your changes.
```
git clone https://github.com/jmarra13/deployment.git
cd deployment
git remote -v
git remote add upstream https://github.com/dmwm/deployment
git remote -v
```
In this example I cloned my own fork, you should adjust the url **https://github.com/jmarra13/deployment.git** to your own.
```
git checkout -b redirect-rule-vocms0121
vim frontend/backends-prod.txt
```
Then add a line with the redirect rule, like this one:
```
^/auth//scheddmon/0121/ vocms0121.cern.ch
```
then save the file and push your changes to your newly created branch.
```
git add frontend/backends-prod.txt
git commit -m 'some description of your changes'
git push origin redirect-rule-vocms0121
```
Then go to your fork, in my case [https://github.com/jmarra13/deployment![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/jmarra13/deployment), and click on ![pull_request_test_highlighted.png](/twiki/pub/CMSPublic/ScheddDeployment/pull_request_test_highlighted.png)
## Free memory script for populating a schedd [ClassAd](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/ClassAd?topicparent=CMSPublic.ScheddDeployment;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") [TotalFreeMemoryMB](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/TotalFreeMemoryMB?topicparent=CMSPublic.ScheddDeployment;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.")
On each schedd is a condor cronjob (much like a regular cronjob, except it's managed by condor and defined in condor syntax) which reports how much free memory is available on the machine. This is mainly used for load balancing across different schedds in the schedd picker function which should select the least loaded schedd to submit a task to.
```
SCHEDD_CRON_CONFIG_VAL = $(RELEASE_DIR)/bin/condor_config_val
SCHEDD_CRON_JOBLIST = $(SCHEDD_CRON_JOBLIST) TOTAL_FREE_MEMORY_MB
SCHEDD_CRON_TOTAL_FREE_MEMORY_MB_EXECUTABLE = /data/srv/SubmissionInfrastructureScripts/total_free_memory.sh
SCHEDD_CRON_TOTAL_FREE_MEMORY_MB_PERIOD = 300s
```
The script itself is puppetized, it is located in this repo ![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif).
Note that enabling this cron requires a condor restart. After it is defined in a config file (for example in the 99\_local\_tweaks), condor\_reconfig is not enough for it to start running.-- - 2016-08-09

body:
If you are experiencing TWiki instability from outside the CERN network, please connect via the CERN internal network - see [KB0010688![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cern.service-now.com/service-portal?id=KB0010688) for details
>![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/web-bg-small.gif) [CMSPublic Web](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WebHome)>[Dashboard](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/Dashboard?topicparent=CMSPublic.StandardExitCodes;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.")>[JobExitCodes](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/JobExitCodes)>[StandardExitCodes](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/StandardExitCodes "Topic revision: 1 (2018-06-13 - 15:57:04)") (2018-06-13, )[![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/uweb-o14.gif) Edit](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/StandardExitCodes?t=1777852153;nowysiwyg=1 "Edit this topic text")[Attach](/twiki/bin/attach/CMSPublic/StandardExitCodes "Attach an image or document to this topic")[PDF](/twiki/bin/genpdf/CMSPublic/StandardExitCodes "Create a PDF file for the topic")
## List of Standard Exit Codes from bash script.
Non authoritative list compiled by unknown people in the CRAB eary days
* + -1 - Error return without specification
  + 1 - Hangup (POSIX)
  + 2 - Interrupt (ANSI)
  + 4 - Illegal instruction (ANSI)
  + 5 - Trace trap (POSIX)
  + 6 - Abort (ANSI) or IOT trap (4.2BSD)
  + 7 - BUS error (4.2BSD)
  + 8 - Floating point exception (ANSI)
  + 9 - killed, unblockable (POSIX) kill -9
  + 11 - segmentation violation (ANSI) (most likely user application crashed)
  + 15 - Termination (ANSI)
  + 24 - Soft CPU limit exceeded (4.2 BSD)
  + 25 - File size limit exceeded (4.2 BSD)
  + 30 - Power failure restart (System V.)
  + 50 - Required application version not found at the site.
  + 64 - I/O error: cannot open data file (SEAL)
  + 65 - End of job from user application (CMSSW)
  + 66 - Application exception
  + 73 - Failed writing to read-only file system
  + 81 - Job did not find functioning CMSSW on worker node.
  + 84 - Some required file not found; check logs for name of missing file.
  + 85 - Job failed to open local and fallback files.
  + 90 - Application exception
  + 92 - Job failed to open local and fallback files.
  + 126 - Permission problem or command is not an executable
  + 127 - Command not found
  + 129 - Hangup (POSIX)
  + 132 - Illegal instruction (ANSI)
  + 133 - Trace trap (POSIX)
  + 134 - Abort (ANSI) or IOT trap (4.2 BSD) (most likely user application crashed)
  + 135 - Bus error (4.2 BSD)
  + 136 - Floating point exception (e.g. divide by zero)
  + 137 - SIGKILL; likely an unrelated batch system kill.
  + 139 - Segmentation violation (ANSI)
  + 143 - Termination (ANSI)(or incorporate in the msg text)
  + 147 - Error during attempted file stageout.
  + 151 - Error during attempted file stageout.
  + 152 - CPU limit exceeded (4.2 BSD)
  + 153 - File size limit exceeded (4.2 BSD)
  + 155 - Profiling alarm clock (4.2 BSD)
-- - 2018-06-13

# Username for CRAB
**If you are reading this page due to an error message from [CRAB](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideCrab) you need to that your DN is correctly registered with CMS (see section [Adding your DN to your profile](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/UsernameForCRAB#Adding_your_DN_to_your_profile) below). If you are certain this is already done and still have CRIC problems, follow the [trouble shooting guide](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/UsernameForCRAB#If_you_still_have_problems) below.**
* [Username for CRAB](#Username_for_CRAB)
  + [What is this](#What_is_this)
  + [VERY important note about certificates](#VERY_important_note_about_certif)
  + [What is CRIC?](#What_is_CRIC)
  + [Accessing CRIC](#Accessing_CRIC)
  + [Adding your DN to your profile](#Adding_your_DN_to_your_profile)

    - [Warning: if your DN contains special characters (comma, apostrophe, accented letter,...) the string stored in CERN internal tool may not be the same as what e.g. voms-proxy-info reports, causing authentication failures in CMSWEB. If this is the case use following instructions to verify and contact CRIC experts via CMS-Talk to get things resolved](#Warning_if_your_DN_contains_spec)
    - [which certificate is mapped to your CERN account](#Check_which_certificate_is_mappe)
  + [Verifying your certificate using your browser](#Verifying_your_certificate_using)
  + [CMSWEB common problems and solutions](#CMSWEB_common_problems_and_solut)

    - [in your browser](#in_your_browser)
    - [in CRAB](#in_CRAB)
  + [If you still have problems](#If_you_still_have_problems)
  + [How to report problems with CRIC](#How_to_report_problems_with_CRIC)
## What is this
This page explains what you need to do so that CRAB and other CMS tools which like CMSWEB can extract your **username** from your authentication credential.
Since February 2020 CMS relies on X509 certificates with VOMS extensions as credential and looks up CRIC in order to to a username.
A globally unique username is needed for proper identification and isolation of CRAB tasks and outputs and we will use your CERN computer account username for that. The procedure to extract such username from your certificate or proxy relies currently on [CRIC](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/UsernameForCRAB#What_is_CRIC)If you look for a general introduction to how to get a certificate, a VOMS membership, use those with CMSWEB and/or CRAB etc., please look in the CMS Offline Workbook at [CMS.WorkBookGetAccount#AccessGrid](/twiki/bin//CMS/WorkBookGetAccount#AccessGrid)
## VERY important note about certificates
A valid GRID certificate is needed in order to access services hosted on CMSWEB and many other services.
You **MUST** be aware that different client tools will look for the certificate in different places and formats.
In particular
* web browsers request you to import a certificate and then use their own internal copy of it
* commands, script etc. from Linux shell will look for `.pem` files in your `~/.globus` directory
You must make it sure that same certificate is in both places, in particular if you switch to a new certificate from a different CA or if you simply renew your certificate (which you have to every year) the new one has to be put im both places.
Only you can make this . Please do it before you report any problem.Relations between certificate in browser and in `~/.globus`, converstion to/from `pem` format etc. are described in [this twiki page](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookStartingGrid#ObtainingCert)
## What is CRIC?
CRIC is a database and web interface that CMS uses to track sites and the people responsible for maintaining them. It is also used by CRAB to find out the primary account username associated with the DN of the user. The username is a string used to create the endpoint for the stageout and publication (see for example [stageout and publication with CRAB2](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideCrabFaq#Stageout_and_publication) or [Data handling in](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/Crab3DataHandling) ).CRIC is also used to define groups and to define people's roles within that group.
## Accessing CRIC
CRAB or other tools will access information from CRIC via programmatic API's, but in order to or your informaiton or to diagnose problems you will want to access it from CMSWEB.This requires that your browser is properly configured to trust CERN CA's and to present your valid personal grid certificates.
Those requirements applies in many other instances as well, you can find instructions and debugging tips in
* <https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideVomsFAQ#Browser_issues>
* <https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideVomsFAQ#Certificate_issues>
## Adding your DN to your profile
User information mapping "username - DN" are automatically stored in CRIC querying the CERN users database through the public information in LDAP.
This means
* CMS users with a CERN grid certificate are automatically registered in CRIC, with their CERN certificate associated to their primary CERN account.
* CMS users with a non-CERN certificate (i.e. issued by DOE Grids, GermanGrid, INFN, etc.) should their certificates to their corresponding primary CERN account via the CERN Grid Certification Authority page [https://ca.cern.ch/ca/![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://ca.cern.ch/ca/).
* **New: There is no need to add DN's in VOMS admin interface (as it was required before May 2024)**
**Note**: If the user's primary account is not attached to the CMS group, the user may need to follow the steps [here![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://resources.web.cern.ch/resources/Help/?kbid=067030) to enable access to CMS resources (like [EOS](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/EOS)).Useful instructions for steps above are:
1. **Access CERN Grid CA**
    go to the CERN Grid Certification Authority page [https://ca.cern.ch/ca/![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://ca.cern.ch/ca/), authenticate (use `SignIn` link at top right) and you should see a page like this:
    ![CERN_CA.png](/twiki/pub/CMSPublic/UsernameForCRAB/CERN_CA.png)
2. **Add a certificate mapping**
    click on " a non-CERN certificate to your account" (see red hand icon in the image above) which should lead you to a page which looks like the image below. To add a new mapping, use the " Certificate" tab and then use the "Browse..." (or "Choose File") and "Submit" buttons to upload your `usercert.pem` file (which is what the page refers to with "Base64 format"). This file is usually found in the `~/.globus` directory in the machine(s) you use for grid work
    ![Certificate_Mapping.png](/twiki/pub/CMSPublic/UsernameForCRAB/Certificate_Mapping.png)
3. **a certificate mapping**
    To an existing mapping, use the "Settings" tab. There will be a cyan `[delete]` buttton to click. See image below and notice postion of the red cursor:
    ![Remove_Mapping.png](/twiki/pub/CMSPublic/UsernameForCRAB/Remove_Mapping.png)
### Warning
1. If you have multiple CERN user accounts, be aware that CRAB is only tested to work with certificates mapped to your primary account, as far as we know there is no satisfactory way to use a CERN non-primary account name as userame in CRAB
2. the certificate using the instructions at point 2. of the previous section.
   * Whatever certificate users would like to use must be mapped to the primary account and that same certificate must be installed in your browser.
3. if the association is ok in the [CRIC people page![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cms-cric.cern.ch/accounts/account/list/).
   * Please **allow some time for CRIC to update**. If you have changed/updated your DN, it could take up to 4 hours to show your changes in CRIC.
4. Users with a different username in lxplus and their local site may need to get new arrangements with their home T2 administrators in order to identify the stageout area in `/store/user/`.
### Warning: if your DN contains special characters (comma, apostrophe, accented letter,...) the string stored in CERN internal tool may not be the same as what e.g. `voms-proxy-info` reports, causing authentication failures in CMSWEB. If this is the case use following instructions to verify and contact CRIC experts via [CMS-Talk![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cms-talk.web.cern.ch/c/offcomp/comptools/87) to get things resolved
### which certificate is mapped to your CERN account
You can what is mapped to your CERN account at the CERN CA page using instructions above,
but if you want a quicker, no graphical way, or need to someone else's situation, you can access
CERN LDAP service from lxplus (make sure you do not have CMSSW setup as it messes up ldap) with:
```
ldapsearch -LLL -x -o ldif-wrap=no -h xldap.cern.ch -b "DC=cern,DC=ch" "cn=USERNAME" altSecurityIdentities | grep altSecurity
```
make sure to replace `USERNAME` string in command above with your CERN user name. If you did not indicate an alternative identity, the mapping the output will not be very telling, and that's OK. But if you did, it will be shown first in the list like in the following example:
```
belforte@lxplus100/~> ldapsearch -LLL -x -o ldif-wrap=no -h xldap.cern.ch -b "DC=cern,DC=ch" "cn=belforte" altSecurityIdentities | grep altSecurity
dn: CN=belforte,OU=Users,OU=Organic Units,DC=cern,DC=ch
altSecurityIdentities: X509:<I>C=NL,S=Noord-Holland,L=Amsterdam,O=TERENA,CN=TERENA eScience Personal CA 3<S>DC=org,DC=terena,DC=tcs,C=IT,O=Istituto Nazionale di Fisica Nucleare,CN=
altSecurityIdentities: =ch,DC=cern,CN=CERN Certification Authority<S>DC=ch,DC=cern,OU=Organic Units,OU=Users,CN=lsfcert
altSecurityIdentities: =ch,DC=cern,CN=CERN Certification Authority<S>DC=ch,DC=cern,OU=Organic Units,OU=Users,CN=acronmc
altSecurityIdentities: =ch,DC=cern,CN=CERN Trusted Certification Authority<S>DC=ch,DC=cern,OU=Organic Units,OU=Users,CN=pkinitor,CN=653930,CN=Pkinit Kerberosservice
belforte@lxplus100/~>
```
## Verifying your certificate using your browser
* Install your X509 grid certificate in your web browser and enable it for cmsweb.cern.ch; [DQMGUIGridCertificate](/twiki/bin//CMS/DQMGUIGridCertificate) outlines some of the key steps. This recipe there should work at least in Firefox, and .
* Visit [https://cmsweb.cern.ch/auth/trouble![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cmsweb.cern.ch/auth/trouble) and make sure it shows valid certificate which has been registered as a CMS VO member. The X509 DN shown here should be the same as displayed in the previous step, and must match the grid certificate you use for job submission. You need to have everything reported ok line here before you can proceed to the next step.
  ![Need to authenticate](/twiki/pub/CMSPublic/UsernameForCRAB/auth-verify.png)
## CMSWEB common problems and solutions
### Authentication to CMSWEB fails
* Most CMSWEB servicies (DAS, DBS.. ) requires authentication via a certificate. If your browser is not properly setup you will see ill see something like
  ![Need to authenticate](/twiki/pub/CMSPublic/UsernameForCRAB/NeedToAuthenticate.png)
* Solution: Click as indicated in the page to Diagnose certificate p4roblems, you will be redirecte to [https://cmsweb.cern.ch/auth/trouble![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cmsweb.cern.ch/auth/trouble) where more diagnotic will appear as indicated below
### You have no valid certificate
* Either you do not have a personal certificate in the browser, or it is expired.
* you will see something like
  ![no certificate](/twiki/pub/CMSPublic/UsernameForCRAB/NoCert.png)
* Solution: make sure that your personal certificate is imported in the browser and that it is not expired. Best to have only one certificate in the browser
### Your certificate is not in VOMS
* you will see something like
  ![cert not in VOMS](/twiki/pub/CMSPublic/UsernameForCRAB/ValidCertNotInVoms.png)
* Solution: if you never registered in CMS VOMS, do so. If you registered already and your membership is not expired, maybe you registered with a a different certificate. It is better to use only one certificate for everything. Make your mind which one you want to use and keep only that in your browser. You can always add a certificate to your CERN account as indicated above if you want/need to use a non-CERN-issued certificate
## username extraction from CRIC
First of all make sure that you have same certificate in your browser and in `~/.globus`, see [UsernameForCRAB#VERY\_important\_note\_about\_certif](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/UsernameForCRAB#VERY_important_note_about_certif)
### in your browser
that CRIC recognises you at [https://cms-cric.cern.ch/api/accounts/user/query/?json&preset=whoami![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cms-cric.cern.ch/api/accounts/user/query/?json&preset=whoami) this should show both your username account ("login") and certificate ("dn").
### in CRAB
In order to if your username can be extracted from CRIC, please use the `crab checkusername` command (you need to have setup UI, cmsenv and CRAB in the proper order and have created a valid proxy).
## If you still have problems
* that your CRAB configuration and environment is correct by following  [username extraction from CRIC](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/UsernameForCRAB#Check_username_extraction_from_CRIC) above.
* that your DN is correctly reported at [https://cmsweb.cern.ch/auth/trouble![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cmsweb.cern.ch/auth/trouble)
* Please **allow some time for things to update**, it could take up to 4hrs to show your changes if you have changed/updated your DN.
* if you have a problem which you still can not solve, report it to the  [forum![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cms-talk.web.cern.ch/c/offcomp/comptools/87) providing as many details as possible and make sure to include the exact command or action which fails, add screenshots if relevant etc.
## How to report problems with CRIC
If the `whoami` above works then your problem is in CRAB. Report the issue to the  [forum![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cms-talk.web.cern.ch/c/offcomp/comptools/87l).If you have troubles adding your DN to your account, or break something while doing that, report the problems by filing a [GGUS ticket![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://ggus.eu/?mode=ticket_submit) and choose the following settings in the mask:
* Type of issue: 'OTHER'
* Support Unit: 'WLCG: CRIC'
In the text field make sure you include:
* The CRIC keywork in the subject.
* A description of the problem as detailed as you can.
* Your username.
* Your certificate DN.
* Your email address.
Not including this information will make solving your problem slower/impossible.

# **TROTA performance**
[Link to DPS note on CDS![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cds.cern.ch/record/2938823)
## Introduction
Identifying boosted hadronic top quarks poses a significant challenge within the CMS physics program, particularly in Standard Model measurements and searches for new phenomena. There are many excellent tools available for identifying wide-angle jets with top quark flavor. However, to enhance reconstruction and selection efficiencies for signal events including top quarks, an approach extending beyond large radius jets is necessary. From a physics standpoint, this necessity stems from the fact that the three quarks hadronize separately, resulting in lower momentum for the top quark and a greater spread of the three resulting jets within the detector. Consequently, these jets are clustered into separate objects. In the most extreme case, the anti-kT algorithm clusters the three quarks into three distinct small radius jets. However, there is also an intermediate regime in which the number of jets can vary. For example, one large radius jet may contain the products of the W boson, while one small radius jet may represent the b quark. This regime is not well-defined due to the jet clustering algorithm's sensitivity to performance. In this work, we propose an approach to include the top quark from the fully resolved to the intermediate regime. This represents one of the first attempt to reconstruct Top quark in a wide pT range using standard jets. The algorithm is based on neural networks and utilizes information from jet kinematics and [ParticleNet](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/ParticleNet?topicparent=CMSPublic.WebTopicCreator;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") taggers. This approach is referred to as Top Reconstruction: an Object Tagger Algorithm (TROTA). Its performance was studied using simulations of the 2018 data-taking period of the CMS experiment.

# 0.1 Acknowledgements
The CMS Collaboration would particularly like to thank the original editor for leading the workbook project from its creation and throughout the 2006 shut down year. She provided much of the workbooks content as well as helped to organize contributions from many experts in areas of CMS and CMSSW. Starting any large documentation project is an intimidating task - working out what to put in, how to structure it, and getting people to actually write contributions. From 2007 onwards the work of this task is easy - update, improve, expand, which is done with the help of CMS participators like you. Based at Fermilab, is now involved in the OSG (Open Science Grid) project.The initial structure and content of the CMS WorkBook was closely modeled on the ATLAS WorkBook, following the design of similar projects of BaBar and OPAL.Many thanks to (ATLAS) for providing code, layout advice, twiki explanations and much ongoing assistance in producing the first version of the CMS workbook. Much gratitude is also due to (ATLAS) for enabling the workbook (and the rest of the CMS web) to have customized left sidebars. Thanks also to Traudl Hansl-Kozanecka (ATLAS) for assistance with coding, advice and general structure. And last but not least, many thanks for the CERN twiki support and for the continuous support.And a big thank you to all the CMS scientists and code developers who have provided information, written, reviewed, edited, and otherwise assisted with creating and maintaining these workbook tutorials and topics for their fellow collaborators.

# 4.1 Data Analysis in the
Complete: ![4](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/pub/CMS/WebPreferences/complete4.png)
[Detailed Review Status](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookAnalysisInFullFramework#ReviewStatus)

## Goals of this page
This page provides an up-to-date overview of the role of CMSSW Framework (aka ) in user's analysis.
## Introduction
The is CMS's main tool for data processing and is thus intimately connected with user's analysis in a number of ways:
1. it is used to produce data`upstream' of the user's analysis: in HLT, Reconstruction, and Skimming
2. it is used in PAT-tuple production in group and user skims
3. it could also be used for making histograms and plots
4. it could be used by the user to further adjust the content of the PAT files used in the analysis
The objective of this whole chapter is to demonstrate the key applications of the in points #3 and #4 above.
## Making plots in , and the Interactive Analysis
The is capable of creating and filling histograms, and is able to manage many histograms produced by a number of ED Analyzers. There are two ways to utilize this capability:
* monitoring and validation of jobs
* interactive use
The CMS Framework is perfectly suited for creating and filling lots of histograms that can be used to keep track of what is happening in the event processing. The histograms produced this way can be used to quickly identify whether the job is working correctly and whether the output file makes sense (without analyzing the output file more thoroughly in FW Lite). This can be extended to a more detailed validation as well. In fact, the is a great tool for making many *known* plots.That being said, if the analysis requires the use of detailed Geometry, Alignment, and other kinds of Calibration Constants (possibly requiring database access), the only way to achieve it is in the .
## Adjusting the content of the user's PAT-tuple
The users will naturally want to control what is in their analysis data sample (*e.g.,* PAT-tuples), as that defines what is possible in the interactive stage of the analysis. In addition, having data sample which is too large also slows down the interactive analysis, simply because, due to a larger I/O, it takes longer to process the same number of events. So the key is to learn how to
* add the necessary information (in terms of other ED products, or CMS.UserData attached to PAT objects)
* remove the unnecessary information (in terms of making PAT objects which are `just right' in size)
These topics will be covered in detail in the PAT workbook sections below.-- Main.Altan Cakir - 09 Oct 2017

# 3.1 Analysis Overview: an Introduction
Complete: ![5](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/pub/CMS/WebPreferences/complete5.png)
[Detailed Review status](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookAnalysisOverviewIntroduction#ReviewStatus)
## Goals of this page:
This page presents a big-picture overview of performing an analysis at CMS.
* The first task is to describe how the data flows within CMS, from data taking through various layers of skimming. This also introduces a concept of a data tier (, AOD) and [WorkBookDataFormats](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookDataFormats) defines all of them. It also introduces the Physics Analysis Toolkit (PAT) data format which is described in detail in [Chapter 4](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPAT). This is the scope of this section.
* We need to understand the most important CMS data formats, and AOD, so they are described next. PAT and are also mentioned, although it will be described in detail later.
* Finally, we explore three options for a quantitative analysis of CMS events:
  + Framework Lite (FW Lite) -- using ROOT enhanced with libraries that can understand CMS data formats and aid in fetching object collections from the event
  + The full Framework -- using C++ modules in cmsRun
  + for based analysis -- references to other pages are given.
## The data flow, from detector to analysis
(For a more thorough overview, please see [WorkBookComputingModel](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookComputingModel); this section necessarily distills the information which was presented there in much more detail.)To enable the most effective access to CMS data, the data are first split into Physics Datasets (PDs) and then the events are filtered. The division into the Physics Datasets is done based on the trigger decision. The primary datasets are structured and placed to make life as easy as possible, e.g. to minimize the need for an average user to run on very large amounts of data. The datasets group or split triggers in order to achieve balance in their size.Even after splitting into various Primary Datasets the data are too large for a reasonable or even feasible direct access by users. The main strategy in dealing with such a large number of events is to filter them, and do that in layers of ever-tighter event selection. (After all, the Level 1 trigger and HLT are doing the same online.) The process of selecting events and saving them in output is called `skimming'. The intended modus operandi of CMS analysis groups is the following:
1. The primary datasets and skims are produced; they are defined using the trigger information (for stability) and produced centrally on [Tier 1](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookComputingModel#TierOne) systems.
2. The secondary skims are produced by the physics groups (say a Higgs group) by running on the primary skims; the secondary skims are usually produced by group members running on the [Tier 2](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookComputingModel#TierTwo) clusters assigned to the given group.
3. Optionally, the user then skims once again, applying an ever tighter event selection.
4. The final sample (with almost final cuts) can then be analyzed by FW Lite (see [WorkBookFWLite](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookFWLite)) or other analysis specific . It can also be analyzed by the full CMSSW framework, however we recommend using FW Lite, or similar, as it is more interactive and far more portable.
The primary skims (step 1 above) reduce the size of the primary datasets in order to reduce the time of subsequent layers of skimming. The target of the primary skims is a reduction of about a factor of 10 in size with respect to the primary datasets.The secondary skimming (step 2 above) must be tight enough to make the secondary skims feasible in terms of size. And yet it must not be too tight since otherwise certain analyses might find themselves starved for data. However, in this case what is `tight' is analysis-dependent, so it is vital for the group members to be involved in the definition of their group's secondary skims!The user selection (step 3) is made on the [Tier 2](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookComputingModel#TierTwo) by the user, and it's the main opportunity to reduce the size of the samples the user will need to deal with (and lug around). In many cases, this is where the preliminary event selection is done, and thus it is the foundation of the analysis. It is expected that the user may need to re-run this step (*e.g.,* in case of finding out that the cuts were too tight), but this is not a problem since the tertiary skims are being run on the secondary skims which are already reduced in size.That being said, it is important to tune the user's skim to be as close to `just right' as possible: the event selection should be looser than they are expected to be after the final cut optimization, but not too loose -- otherwise the skimming would not serve its purpose.
If done right, this will not only save your own time, but also preserve the collaboration's CPU resources.
## Reduction in event size: CMS Data Formats and Data Tiers
(For a more thorough overview, please see [WorkBookComputingModel](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookComputingModel); this section necessarily distills the information which was presented there in much more detail.)In addition to the reduction of the **number** of events, in steps 1-3 it is also possible to reduce the **size** of each event by
* unneeded collections (e.g. after we make PAT candidates, for most purposes the rest of the AOD information is not needed); this is called ***stripping*** or ***slimming.***
* unneeded information from objects; this is called ***thinning*** . It is an advanced topic; it's still experimental and not covered in here.
Starting from the detector output ("RAW" data), the information is being refined and what is not needed is being dropped. This defines the CMS **data tiers**. Each bit of data in an event must be written in a supported data format. A data format is essentially a C++ class, where a class defines a data structure (a data type with data members). The term *data format* can be used to refer to the format of the data written using the class (e.g., data format as a sort of template), or to the instantiated class object itself. The [DataFormats![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/tree/master/DataFormats) package and the [SimDataFormats![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/tree/master/SimDataFormats) package (for simulated data) in the CMSSW repository contain all the supported data formats that can be written to an Event file. So, for example, if you wish to add data to an Event, your [EDProducer module](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookEDMTutorialProducer) must instantiate one or more of these data format classes.Data formats (classes) for reconstructed data, for example, include `.Track`, `.TrackExtra`, and many more. See the Offline Guide section [SWGuideRecoDataTable](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideRecoDataTable) for the full listing.
## Data Tiers: Reconstructed () Data and Analysis Object Data (AOD)
Event information from each step in the simulation and reconstruction chain is logically grouped into what we call a *data tier*, which has already been introduced in the section describing [the Computing Model](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookComputingModel). Examples of data tiers include `RAW` and , and for MC, `GEN` (generation), `SIM` (simulation) and `DIGI` (digitalization). A data tier may contain multiple data formats, as mentioned above for reconstructed data. A given dataset may consist of multiple data tiers, e.g., the term `GenSimDigi` includes the generation (MC), the simulation (Geant) and digitalization steps. The most important tiers from a physicist's point of are  (all reconstructed objects and ), `AOD` (a smaller subset of  which is needed by analysis) and `MiniAOD/` (even smaller tiers, containing only high level objects).data contains objects from all stages of reconstruction. AOD data are derived from the information to provide data for physics analyses in a convenient, compact format. [MiniAOD](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/MiniAOD) amd  tiers further slim the number and type of objects saved. Typically, physics analyses don't require you to rerun the reconstruction process on the data. Most physics analyses can run on MiniAOD or /pub/CMSPublic/WorkBookAnalysisOverviewIntroduction/whats_in_aod_reco.gif)NB: the image does not show the MiniAOD and tiers yet.
###
is the name of the data-tier which contains objects created by the event reconstruction program. It is derived from RAW data and provides access to reconstructed physics objects for physics analysis in a convenient format. Event reconstruction is structured in several hierarchical steps:
1. Detector-specific processing: Starting from detector data unpacking and decoding, detector calibration constants are applied and cluster or hit objects are reconstructed.
2. Tracking: in the silicon and muon detectors are used to reconstruct global tracks. Pattern recognition in the tracker is the most CPU-intensive task.
3. Vertexing: Reconstructs primary and secondary vertex candidates.
4. Particle identification: Produces the objects most associated with physics analyses. Using a wide variety of sophisticated algorithms, standard physics object candidates are created (electrons, photons, muons, missing transverse energy and jets; heavy-quarks, tau decay).
The normal completion of the reconstruction task will result in a full set of these reconstructed objects usable by CMS physicists in their analyses. You would only need to rerun these algorithms if your analysis requires to take into account such things as trial calibrations, novel algorithms etc.Reconstruction is computationally expensive because of heavy use of CPU by tracking algorithms. The data-tier provides compact information for analysis to avoid the necessity to access the RAW data for most analysis. Following the hierarchy of event reconstruction, contains objects from all stages of reconstruction. At the lowest level, these are the reconstructed , clusters and segments. Based on these objects, reconstructed tracks and vertices are stored. At the highest level, reconstructed jets, muons, electrons, b-jets, etc. are stored. A direct reference from high-level objects to low-level objects is possible, to avoid duplication of information. In addition, the format preserves links to the RAW information.The data includes quantities required for typical analysis usage patterns such as: track re-finding, calorimeter reclustering, and jet energy calibration. The event content is documented in the Offline Guide at  [Data /SWGuideRecoDataTable).
### AOD
AOD are derived from the information to provide data for physics analysis in a convenient, compact format. AOD data are usable directly by physics analyses. AOD data will be produced by the same, or subsequent, processing steps as the ones producing the data; and AOD data will be made easily available at multiple sites to CMS members. The AOD will contain enough information about the event to support all the typical usage patterns of a physics analysis. Thus, it will contain a copy of all the high-level physics objects (such as muons, electrons, taus, etc.), plus a summary of the information sufficient to support typical analysis actions such as track refitting with improved alignment or kinematic constraints, re-evaluation of energy and/or position of ECAL clusters based on analysis-specific corrections. The AOD, because of the limited size that will not allow it to contain all the , will typically not support the application of novel pattern recognition techniques, nor the application of new calibration constants, which would typically require the use of or RAW information.The AOD data tier will contain physics objects: tracks with associated , calorimetric clusters with associated , vertices, jets and high-level physics objects (electrons, muons, Z boson candidates, and so on).Because the AOD data tier is relatively compact, all Tier-1 computing centres are able to keep a full copy of the AOD, while they will hold only a subset of the RAW and data tiers. The AOD event content is documented in the Offline Guide at  [AOD Data /SWGuideAodDataTable).
### PAT, [MiniAOD](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/MiniAOD)
The information is stored in and AOD in a way that uses the least amount of space and allows for the greatest flexibility. This is particularly true for DataFormats that contain objects that link to each other. However, accessing these links between or AOD objects requires more experience with C++. To simplify the user's analysis, a set of new data formats are created, which aggregate the related information. These new formats, along with the tools used to make and manipulate them, are called **Physics Analysis Toolkit**, or PAT. The PAT is *de facto* the way how the users will access the physics objects which are the output of .PAT's content is *flexible* -- it is up to the user to define it. For this reason, *PAT is not a data tier*. The content of PAT may change from one analysis to another, let alone from one PAG (Physics Analysis Group) to another. However, PAT **defines a standard** for the physics objects and variables stored in those physics objects. It is like a menu in a restaurant -- every patron can choose different things from the menu, but everybody is reading from the same menu. This facilitates sharing both tools and people between analyses and physics groups.PAT is discussed in more detail in [/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATTupleCreationExercise). Here we continue the story of defining the user content of an analysis, in which PAT plays a crucial role.[MiniAOD](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/MiniAOD) is a dataformat bases on PAT. Starting from 2014 it replaces PAT for most analysis. It holds the same ideas as PAT and uses its code. Unlike a restaurant where you can choose your dishes, it is like a mensa with fixed menu. Like it or not, gotta eat it.
###
 is a plain, -like format, readable with bare ROOT and containing per-event information needed in most generic analyses. is not a CMSSW [EDM](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/EDM) format. However, several EDM features are available in this simplified format too.More details on the  format can be found here: [CMSPublic/WorkBookNanoAOD](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookNanoAOD)
### Group and user skims: , AOD and PAT-tuples
Now we can refine the descriptions of primary, group and user-defined skims, with some examples. In almost all cases the primary skims will read AOD and produce other AOD with a reduced number of events. (During the physics commissioning, the primary skims may also read and write instead of AOD.) The group and user skims may also read and write AOD (or ). However, they could also produce PAT-tuples, as decided by the group or the user. As an illustration, these steps could be:
1. Primary skims read AOD, write reduced AOD.
2. A group-wide skim filters events in AOD, and produces PAT with lots of information. (Such PAT-tuples are sometimes called for as they need to benefit multiple efforts within the group)
3. The user modifies the PAT workflow to read PAT and produce another version of PAT, but with much smaller content (stripping/slimming), and possibly even a compressed PAT object (thinning).
All the operations that involve skimming, stripping, and thinning are done within the full-Framework. Therefore, every user needs to at least know what these jobs do in each of the steps, even if they do not need to make any changes to any of the processing steps. However, it is more likely that some changes will be needed, especially in the last stage where the skimming and further processing is ran by the user. In some cases, the user may even need to write Framework modules like EDProducers -- to add new DataFormats to the events, or EDAnalyzers -- to compute quantities that require access to conditions.In the above example, the end of the skimming chain produces a "PAT-tuple", which should be small enough to easily fit onto a laptop. Moreover, it should also fit within a memory of the ROOT process, thus facilitating interactive speed on par with TTrees. However, to be able to read CMS data (, AOD or PAT) from ROOT, we need to teach ROOT to understand CMS DataFormats by loading the DataFormats libraries themselves, accompanied also by a couple of helper classes that simplify the user's manipulation of CMS "events" in ROOT. ROOT with these additional libraries installed is called Framework-lite, or **[FW Lite](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookFWLite)**.
### Tools for interactive analysis: FW Lite, ,
The interactive stage is where most of the *analysis* is actually done, and where most of the `analysis time' is actually spent. Every analysis is different, and many take a number of twists and turns towards its conclusion, solving an array of riddles on the way. However, most analyses need (or could benefit from):
* A way to examine the content of CMS data files, especially PAT-tuples. CMS has several tools that can examine the file content, including stand-alone executables [edmDumpEventContent](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookEdmInfoOnDataFile) (which dumps a list of the collections present in the file to the terminal), and  (which has a nice graphical interface).
* A way to obtain the history of the file. The CMS files contain embedded information sufficient to tell the history of the objects in the file. This information is called *[provenance](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookCMSSWFramework#ProvenanceTrackingLink)*, and is crucial for the analysis, as it allows the user to establish with certainty what kind of operations (corrections, calibrations, algorithms) were performed on the data present in the file. The stand-alone executable [edmProvDump](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookEdmInfoOnDataFile) prints the provenance to the screen.
* A way to visualize the event. The main objective of  is to display analysis-level quantities. Moreover, is well-suited for investigating events in CMS data files, since it can read them directly.
* A way to manipulate data quantitatively. In High-energy physics (HEP), most quantitative analysis of data is performed within the ROOT framework. ROOT has, over the years, subsumed an impressive collection of statistical and other tools, including the fitting package [RooFit](/twiki/bin//CMS/RooFit), or a collection of multi-variate analysis tools, TMVA. ROOT can access the CMS data directly, provided the DataFormats libraries are loaded, turning it into FW Lite.
* For a data analysis based on the files, you can refer to the [recommendations![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cms-analysis.docs.cern.ch/dproc/recommendations/) by the CAT group.
The following pages in this Chapter of the  will illustrate each of these steps, especially data analysis (including making plots) in [FW Lite](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookFWLite). But first, [the choice of a release is discussed](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookWhichRelease), and [the ways to get data are illustrated](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookDataSamples). At the end of the exercise in [WorkBookDataSamples](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookDataSamples), we will end up with one or more small files, which we explore next, first using command-line utilities, and then [with graphical tools like](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookEdmInfoOnDataFile)  and  [event display](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookFireworks).

# 5.3 Data Analysis Work Flow
Complete: ![5](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/pub/CMS/WebPreferences/complete5.png)
[Detailed Review status](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookAnalysisWorkFlow#ReviewStatus)
## Goals of this page
When you finish this page, you should understand:
* The steps that you need to follow in order to run an analysis job on grid resources.
* The basics about how CRAB (Cms Remote Analysis Builder) works.
**This page does not teach you how to use CRAB. It only provides background material on how things work.**To learn how to use CRAB see Chapter ["Analysis with CRAB"](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookRunningGrid).
## Contents
* [/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookAnalysisWorkFlow#InTro)
* [Workflow Illustration](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookAnalysisWorkFlow#WorkFlow)

* [Job Preparation by CRAB](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookAnalysisWorkFlow#JoB)
