## Introduction
The present page deals with the analysis of electron data produced with CMSSW 94X. It shows examples of some simple analysis code reading the standard collection of reconstructed electron objects whose reconstruction is performed by default by CMSSW. For further details about the reconstruction process, have a look at [SWGuideElectronRecoSoftware](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideElectronRecoSoftware).
##
### Access to computing environment
First make sure that you have access to either [cmslpc![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://uscms.org/uscms_at_work/physics/computing/getstarted/), or [lxplus![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://information-technology.web.cern.ch/services/lxplus-service). You will also need a [github![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://-sw.github.io/faq.html#how-do-i-subscribe-to-github) account to checkout the code. To check if you’re using bash, tcsh, sh, csh, ksh, or . You can request for a change in shell ([cmslpc![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://uscms.org/uscms_at_work/computing/setup/setup_software.shtml#shell),[lxplus account self-service tool![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://account.cern.ch/account/)).You might as well get a proxy now as you will need it later.
```
voms-proxy-init -voms  --valid 192:00
```
If you do not have grid access see [LcgAccess](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideLcgAccess)
## Analysis in CMSSW 94x
### Set-up CMSSW Release
Below is a recipe for setting up the analysis for the release:
```
cmsrel CMSSW_9_4_4
cd CMSSW_9_4_4/src
cmsenv
```
### Create Ntuples using the ggNtuplizer
## Bare ROOT access
At this point you should have set up your computing environment and perhaps have a centrally produced miniAOD ROOT file. the simplest thing to do with an edm ROOT file is to open it with ROOT interpreter (do not care about the numerous warnings about the lacking dictionaries). You can look within the file, for instance look at the tree called "Events". But what we really want to do is to the datasets. An is simply a collection of events, where different variables (momentum, Energy, etc..) corresponding to each events are kept. With these Ntuples, one can make plot meaningful distributions and perform an analysis.To make Ntuples, one can write an [EDAnalyzer](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookWriteFrameworkModule). However, making a complete one from scratch takes time so there is a standard for doing photon and electron analysis called the ggNtuplizer.
### Create Ntuples using the ggNtuplizer
First we build the ggNtuplizer in the latest CMSSW version it’s available in:
[https://github.com/cmkuo/ggAnalysis/tree/94X![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/cmkuo/ggAnalysis/tree/94X)This step may take some time.
```
-topic lsoffi:CMSSW_9_4_0_pre3_TnP
-topic guitargeek:ElectronID_MVA2017_940pre3
scram b -j8
cd $/external/slc6_amd64_gcc630
git clone https://github.com/lsoffi/RecoEgamma-PhotonIdentification.git data/RecoEgamma/PhotonIdentification/data
cd data/RecoEgamma/PhotonIdentification/data
git checkout CMSSW_9_4_0_pre3_TnP
cd $/external/slc6_amd64_gcc630/
git clone https://github.com/lsoffi/RecoEgamma-ElectronIdentification.git data/RecoEgamma/ElectronIdentification/data
cd data/RecoEgamma/ElectronIdentification/data
git checkout CMSSW_9_4_0_pre3_TnP
cd $/src
-topic -egamma:EGM_94X_v1
cd EgammaAnalysis/ElectronTools/data
git clone https://github.com/ECALELFS/ScalesSmearings.git
cd ScalesSmearings/
git checkout Run2017_17Nov2017_v1
cd $/src
git clone https://github.com/cmkuo/HiggsAnalysis.git
git clone -b 94X https://github.com/cmkuo/ggAnalysis.git
scram b -j8
```
You can now make Ntuples using a configuration file. You can open it with a text editor like vim,
```
vi ggAnalysis/ggNtuplizer/test/run_data2017_94X.py #or
vi ggAnalysis/ggNtuplizer/test/run_mc2017_94X.py
```
If you want to learn what the does you can check out,
```
vi ggAnalysis/ggNtuplizer/plugins/ggNtuplizer_photons.cc.
```
One dataset we could run on is `DYJetsToLL_M-50_TuneCP5_13TeV-amcatnloFXFX-pythia8/MINIAODSIM/94X_mc2017_realistic_v10-v1/00000/005DC030-D3F4-E711-889A-02163E01A62D.root` (see  [Data Aggregation system![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cmsweb.cern.ch/das/)).In the `run_mc_94X.py` configuration file, comment out the original input file and the file we want to process.
```
process.source = .Source("PoolSource",
                            fileNames = .untracked.vstring(
        #'file:/data4/cmkuo/testfiles/DYJetsToLL_M-50_RunIIFall17.root'
        '/store/mc/RunIIFall17MiniAOD/DYJetsToLL_M-50_TuneCP5_13TeV-amcatnloFXFX-pythia8/MINIAODSIM/94X_mc2017_realistic_v10-v1/00000/005DC030-D3F4-E711-889A-02163E01A62D.root'
        ))
```
Let's set the `process.maxEvents` to just run over 10000 events. To execute the process go to the source directory and do `cmsRun`,
```
 cd $/src/
cmsRun ggAnalysis/ggNtuplizer/test/run_mc2017_94X.py
```

### Analyzing the Ntuples
One way to access the information contained in the directly is through the command line using ROOT interactively. Try these commands and draw the electron pt and see the effect of adding some cuts.
```
$ root -l ggtree_mc.root
root [1] .ls
root [2] ggNtuplizer->cd()
root [3] EventTree->Print()
root [4] EventTree->Draw("elePt")
root [5] EventTree->Draw("elePt","elePt>20") #  a cut at 20 GeV
```
You can apply a mask cut and select events with a tighter electron ID by doing this:
```
root [6] EventTree->Draw("elePt","(eleIDbit & 8)== 8")
```
You can learn a little more about `eleIDbit` and do more exercises in this link [FNALHATS2017EGM](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin/viewauth//FNALHATS2017EGM)).
To understand more about the effects of the different levels of cuts, (Loose, Tight, Medium), let's superimpose the plots of the variable =sigmaIetaIetaFull5x5".
```
EventTree->SetLineColor(kBlack)
EventTree->Draw("eleSigmaIEtaIEtaFull5x5","(eleIDbit & 2)== 2")
EventTree->SetLineColor(kRed)
EventTree->Draw("eleSigmaIEtaIEtaFull5x5","(eleIDbit & 4)== 4","same")
EventTree->SetLineColor(kBlue)
EventTree->Draw("eleSigmaIEtaIEtaFull5x5","(eleIDbit & 8)== 8","same")
```
We can also use a simple plotting script to make the plots we did above.
```
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/uzzielperez/CMSSW-workbook-practice/master/ElectronAnalysis/simple_plotter.py
```
Using the simple plotter, we can reproduce and see the effect of putting a cut at 20 [GeV](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/GeV?topicparent=CMSPublic.WorkBookElectronAnalysis;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it."). Making a few modifications with the script, we can make comparisons on the effect of different levels of
cuts on different variables. In the script below, you can edit the variable name, "var".
```
wget
```
From the plots, what can you say about "fake" electrons in the high pT region? How does the "" distribution compare for electrons and jets?
### Z->ee Exercise
The Z->ee channel is an important final state that is often used for calibration and systematic uncertainty measurements. In this exercise, we will be reconstructing the Z boson. We expect a resonance peak at around 91.1 [GeV](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/GeV?topicparent=CMSPublic.WorkBookElectronAnalysis;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.").To do this, make sure you are in the CMSSW environment created for this page and copy a simple plotting script for this purpose.
```
cmsenv
voms-proxy-init -voms  --valid 192:00
cd $/src/ggAnalysis/ggNtuplizer/test
xrdcp root://cmseos.fnal.gov//store/user/drberry/HATS/makePlots.py .
# or download a copy from Github
wget
```
The input file would be the `ggtree_mc.root` which we made in the previous section. (Note: If you want to change the input file you can do `python makePlots.py -I <filename.root>`. To check command line options do, `python makePlots.py -h`). Running this script will output `plots.root` which has 3 the histograms
for the pT, and the mass. Have a look at the mass distribution in particular and confirm that it peaks at around the expected mass of the Z.plots\_loose.root and plots\_tight.root. This time, we'll be running on background MC.
```

## Tag and Probe Efficiency Measurement
The tag and probe method is a data-driven approach to measuring selection ID efficiencies. It exploits resonances that decay into two identical final states, like the JPsi or Z (to dilepton), to select a certain (tag) particles and probe the efficiency of a particular selection criterion being applied to them. The "tag" are often golden objects that need to pass a tight selection, has a very low fake rate, while the probe has a selection criteria that could be very loose. Resonances are used by reconstructing them in pairs with one final state being a "tag" (passing tight ID) while the other passes a loose ID is a probe. Lineshapes of (tag+"passing probes") and (tag+"passing probes") are then created and are separately fit with a signal + background model. The efficiency is then computed from the ratio of the number of "passing probes" and the total (passing + failing probes). These can be done in bins of different probe variables (e.g. pT, η ...).

## [NanoAOD](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/NanoAOD)
It's good to familiarize oneself with the recently developed [NanoAOD](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/NanoAOD) data tier. You can learn more about it in the [WorkBookNanoAOD](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookNanoAOD#Electrons). A plethora of nTuplizers have been written over the past few years, all essentially extracting similar information from [MiniAOD](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/MiniAOD). In an attempt to reduce code maintenence burden, a common , [NanoAOD](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/NanoAOD) was created. It contains less information than [MiniAOD](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/MiniAOD), and is a much more compact file format, averaging 1-2 kB per event vs. [MiniAOD](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/MiniAOD)'s 30-50 kB per event. In addition, [NanoAOD](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/NanoAOD) saves all information in basic types (like int, float, etc.) rather than the [EDM](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/EDM) format used for all parent datatiers. This means that no CMSSW environment is necessary to read these files. In fact, we will not even use the ROOT framework to analyze these files in this exercise!
In this exercise, we will examine photon and electron identification and study how these objects are used in physics analyses. This exercise is completed via a jupyter notebook. The exercise and a README with installation instructions can be found at [https://github.com/gracecummings/CMSDAS\_EGamma![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/gracecummings/CMSDAS_EGamma). ...

# 3.5.1 Getting Started with FWLite
Complete: ![5](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/pub/CMS/WebPreferences/complete5.png)
## Contents
* [3.5.1.1 The goals of this page](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookFWLite#ScOpe)
* [3.5.1.2 What is FWLite](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookFWLite#OverView)
* [3.5.1.3 How to download FWLite for your laptop](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookFWLite#InstalLation)
* [3.5.1.4 How to setup your environment](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookFWLite#ConFigure)
* [3.5.1.5 Your first plot in FWLite](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookFWLite#InterActive)
[Detailed Review status](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookFWLite#ReviewStatus)
## 3.5.1.1 The goals of this page:
In this section you will learn:
* what FWLite is.
* how to download it if you want to install it as a stand-alone package on your personal computer (laptop or desktop).
* how to set up the ROOT environment (by adding commands to rootlogon.C).
* how to explore CMS data interactively -- analogous to TTree::Draw().
FWLite can be downloaded with `apt-get` using instructions from [this link](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SDTCMSSW_aptinstaller). You can also jump directly to instructions how to write ROOT macros that analyze CMS data directly -- analogous to the result of TTree::MakeClass() -- in [WorkBookFWLiteEventLoop](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookFWLiteEventLoop) or to examples in [WorkBookFWLiteExamples](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookFWLiteExamples).
## 3.5.1.2 What is FWLite
FWLite is plain ROOT that is capable to read CMS DataFormats together with some helper classes. You can use FWLite to analyse the data. CMS uses ROOT to make data objects persistent. CMS data formats are thus "ROOT-aware"; that is, once the shared libraries containing the ROOT-friendly description of CMS data formats are loaded into a ROOT session, these objects can be accessed and used directly from within ROOT like any other ROOT class!FWLite (pronounced "framework-light") is just that -- a ROOT session with CMS data format libraries loaded. In addition, CMS provides a couple of classes that greatly simplify the access to the collections of CMS data objects. Moreover, these classes (Event and Handle) have the same name as analogous ones in the ; this mnemonic trick helps in making the code to access CMS collections very similar between the FWLite and the (CMSSW). To learn about ROOT have a look to  or to the [ROOT homepage![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://root.cern.ch/).
## 3.5.1.3 How to downloading FWLite for your laptop
So now you are curious and would like to try FWLite. You want to analyse your data file -- say, a file with skimmed PAT-tuples that your group has produced -- and you may be in one of these two situations:
1. You are on a Scientific Linux system with CMSSW installed.
2. You are on some other machine, your own desktop or even more likely your own laptop.
Read the subsection below which applies to your case.
### FWLite on a machine with CMSSW installed
If you are using a machine with CMSSW installed (currently available on either Scientific Linux 4 or Scientific Linux 5), then you don't have to do anything! FWLite is a part of the (CMSSW).
### Installing CMSSW
If you wish to install the CMSSW , you can follow the link [here](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SDTCMSSW_aptinstaller) to install via `apt-get`.
### FWLite on other flavors of Linux, Windows, and
The final stage of the analysis is usually very interactive, does not require access to conditions, and is based on skimmed, stripped (and possibly thinned) data samples. The size of such sample is usually small enough to be copied to your desktop or laptop. Analysis in ROOT is particularly suitable for laptops, and could proceed without a network connection. The traditional way of exploring the data interactively is to make a TTree in the , copy the ROOT file with it to one's laptop, install ROOT, and run. Since we want to enhance ROOT with CMS data format libraries, we need to install the CMS version of ROOT (which is safer anyway as CMS patches ROOT when required) and also install the libraries with the CMS data format and with the helper classes.Most laptops run either Windows, or OS, or one of the modern flavors of Linux (e.g. ). The pages below dedicated to installations on each of these systems:
* Non SL-flavors of Linux (via [CERNVM emulator![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cernvm.cern.ch/cernvm))
* OS (via [CERNVM emulator![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cernvm.cern.ch/cernvm))
* Windows (via [CERNVM emulator![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cernvm.cern.ch/cernvm))
You are encouraged to try them out and give feedback to the Software Development Tools group by sending email to the sw-developmenttool HN.
## 3.5.1.4 How to setup your environment
*(Note: this is a copy of [WorkBookSetComputerNode#RooT](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookSetComputerNode#RooT), but with additional libraries loaded in rootlogon.C file.)*Before running ROOT on your data file, set up ROOT in order to load all the necessary CMS-specific libraries by default, by
creating a file `$HOME/rootlogon.C` file with the following commands:
```
{
  // Set up FW Lite for automatic loading of CMS libraries
  // and data formats.   As you may have other user-defined setup
  // in your rootlogon.C, the CMS setup is executed only if the CMS
  // environment is set up.
  //
  TString cmsswbase = getenv("CMSSW_BASE");
  if (cmsswbase.Length() > 0) {
    //
    // The CMSSW environment is defined (this is true even for FW Lite)
    // so set up the rest.
    //
    cout << "Loading FW Lite setup." << endl;
    gSystem->Load("libFWCoreFWLite.so");
    FWLiteEnabler::enable();
    //AutoLibraryLoader::enable();
    gSystem->Load("libDataFormatsFWLite.so");
    gSystem->Load("libDataFormatsPatCandidates.so");
   }
}
```
Then edit your `.rootrc` file (this file can be in your home directory or in the current working directory, the latter taking the precedence - if it does not exist yet, you can create it) to point to `rootlogon.C`; e.g., add the line:
```
#  Tell ROOT where to find rootlogon.C:
Rint.Logon: $(HOME)/rootlogon.C
```
```
$ root -l              #the -l, lower case L, is optional, and if used, omits the logo
```
and you are ready to play!
### Additional information for OS X Users
There are a few additional steps that are useful for OS X users that are outlined in the README.txt of the FWLite tarballs, emphasized here. Instead of the usual CMSSW setup, please use (assuming you downloaded CMSSW\_4\_1\_3\_FWLITE and moved that folder under /Applications/FWLite ):for csh:
```
setenv  osx106_amd64_gcc421
setenv VO_CMS_SW_DIR /Applications/FWLite/CMSSW_4_1_3_FWLITE/
cd $VO_CMS_SW_DIR/
source $VO_CMS_SW_DIR/fwlite_setup.csh
```
for bash:
```
export =osx106_amd64_gcc421
export VO_CMS_SW_DIR=/Applications/FWLite/CMSSW_4_1_3_FWLITE/
cd $VO_CMS_SW_DIR/
source $VO_CMS_SW_DIR/fwlite_setup.sh
```
This will allow you to use FWLite effectively on the . You can then do as normal:
```
cd $VO_CMS_SW_DIR/work/CMSSW_4_1_3_FWLITE/src/
cmsenv
```
or make a new project area as you prefer.There are a few tricks you may have to do (depending on your OS X version) to get python working correctly. These must be set again after each "cmsenv" command.
These are the known fixes if you have python problems:
```
setenv PYTHONDIR /Applications/FWLite/CMSSW_3_5_6_FWLITE/osx105_ia32_gcc401/external/python/2.6.4-cms
setenv PYTHONHOME /Applications/FWLite/CMSSW_3_5_6_FWLITE/osx105_ia32_gcc401/external/python/2.6.4
setenv LD_LIBRARY_PATH $/lib:$PYTHONDIR/lib:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH
setenv PYTHONPATH $/lib:$PYTHONPATH
```
## 3.5.1.5 Your first plot in FWLite
From the ROOT prompt, open the [MYCOPY.root![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmsdoc.cern.ch/~eliza/MYCOPY.root) file that you made in [WorkBookDataSamples](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookDataSamples). It contains a collection of RECO objects. Opening the file may take some time.
```
root[0] TFile f("MYCOPY.root");
```
Look at the ROOT TBrowser to see which collections are in the file.
```
root[1] new TBrowser;
```
Double-click on *ROOT Files*, then *MYCOPY.root*, then *Events* (the event tree). down through
`recoTracks_generalTracks__RECO` to `recoTracks_generalTracks__RECO.obj`.
![recoTracks_generalTracks_fwlite.png](/twiki/pub/CMSPublic/WorkBookFWLite/recoTracks_generalTracks_fwlite.png)What you see here are the methods of the stored recoTracks. Since `covariance()` returns a class, the icon shows a folder.While you still have the ROOT browser displayed, go back to your ROOT session and set an alias for each of the branches you want to access (we'll choose `recoTracks` and `recoTrackExtras`). Use the branch name that's visible in the TBrowser, and add `obj` at the end, as follows:
```
root [8] Events->SetAlias("tracks","recoTracks_generalTracks__RECO.obj");
root [9] Events->SetAlias("trackExtras","recoTrackExtras_generalTracks__RECO.obj");
```
**Note:** SetAlias commands work only if the ROOT browser is still up.You can look at the examples contained in the file `PhysicsTools/RecoExamples/test/trackPlots.C`, and see how some of the examples work. Note that name of objects in trackPlots.C could be different. But gives you sense how to Draw etc.
```
// plot chi-squared divided by  of freedom
root [10] Events->Draw("tracks.normalizedChi2()", "tracks.chi2()<1000")
```
![](/twiki/pub/CMSPublic/WorkBookFWLite/tracks_generaltracks_norm_chi2.png)(This image is shown for all the 20 events, each containing several tracks, from the full MYCOPY.root file.)Now if you run this same "Events.Draw(...)" command in Bare ROOT (after setting the alias), you'll get the message
`Part of the Variable "tracks.chi2()" exists but some of it is not accessible or useable`.Now run:
```
root[5] Events.Draw("trackExtras.recHitsSize()");
```
![](/twiki/pub/CMSPublic/WorkBookFWLite/trackExtras_generalTracks_recHitSize.png)Of course, this approach does not scale when you want to simultaneously make more than a couple of histograms, and, especially, if you need to compute anything non-trivial. Eventually, you'll need to have a ROOT macro, which will do all the work. This is covered in section [3.5.2 Event Loop in FWLite](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookFWLiteEventLoop).

# 3.5.2 Event Loop in FWLite
Complete: ![5](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/pub/CMS/WebPreferences/complete5.png)
## Contents
* [3.5.2.1 The goals of this page](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookFWLiteEventLoop#ScOpe)
* [3.5.2.1 The structure of a FWLite macro](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookFWLiteEventLoop#StructureOfAFWLiteMacro)
* [3.5.2.2 Compling the macro with ACliC](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookFWLiteEventLoop#CompilingWithAclic)
* [3.5.2.3 Running over a list of files](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookFWLiteEventLoop#ListOfFilesViaChainEvent)
* [3.5.2.4 Using edm::EventBase](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookFWLiteEventLoop#EventBase)
[Detailed Review status](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookFWLiteEventLoop#ReviewStatus)
## The goals of this page:
In this page you will learn how to
* write ROOT macros that analyze CMS data directly
* compile these ROOT macros to make them faster and safer
Those users who like command line options, can have a look at [SWGuideCommandLineParsing](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideCommandLineParsing) for command line parsing instructions.
## The structure of a FWLite macro
Let us illustrate the access to [EDM](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/EDM) collections in FWLite with an example. But before we begin, the following lines need to be executed from within ROOT
```
{
   gSystem->("libFWCoreFWLite.so");
   FWLiteEnabler::enable();
   gSystem->("libDataFormatsFWLite.so");
   gSystem->("libDataFormatsPatCandidates.so");
}
```
as discussed in the previous section, it is best to place these lines inside the *rootlogon.C* file, so that they are executed automatically and you don't need to worry about them.Here's a sketch of a macro that loops over events, and in each event retrieves an ED object:
```
void print_data()
{
   #include "DataFormats/FWLite/interface/Handle.h"
   TFile file("MYCOPY.root");
   fwlite::Event ev(&file);
   for( ev.toBegin(); ! ev.atEnd(); ++ev) {
       fwlite::Handle<std::vector<...> > objs;
       objs.getByLabel(ev,"....");
       // now can access data
       std::cout <<" size "<<objs.ptr()->size()<<std::endl;
       ...
   }
}
```
![ALERT!](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/warning.gif "ALERT!") **Note:**
When building a macro, there is a particular order of calls to ROOT methods which are required in order for ROOT to function properly:
1. Start the autoloader
2. Create the TFile
3. in the helper library `gSystem->("libDataFormatsFWLite")`
4. Include "DataFormats/FWLite/interface/Handle.h" to get the `fwlite::Handle`
5. Create an `fwlite::Event` by passing to the constructor a pointer to the TFile. The fwlite::Event allows you to use the same information you use when accessing data in cmsRun using the edm::Event.
6. Create a for loop over **events**
   1. Start loop by calling `toBegin()` on the `fwlite::Event`
   2. For each iteration of the loop call `atEnd` on the `fwlite::Event`
   3. At the end of each iteration, increment the `fwlite::Event` by using the operator++ method
7. When looping over the events
   1. Create an `fwlite::Handle< ... >` where the template argument is the C++ class you want to get from the event
   2. Call the `getByLabel` method of the `fwlite::Handle` passing the event and the strings or *edm::InputTag* used to specify the object
   3. The object retrieved from the handle is either a single number, or a collection of CMS objects (e.g. Tracks). In the latter case, you can loop the vector of objects using the standard iterator notation (same as in the FullFramework).
If you save the above macro in a file called print\_data.C, you can it and execute it from the interactive ROOT session with
```
root[] .L print_data.C
print_data()
```
or simply
```
.x print_data.C
```
* The macro will be significantly faster, as ACliC invokes the native compiler (so on it's the same version of GCC used to build ROOT)
* *CINT* is good, but ii is not 100% reliable in its computations, and it is better not to risk running into one of the rare cases which are not correctly handled by *CINT*
* Compiled code can be debugged, profiled, or processed with *valgrind* (especially when linked into a standalone executable)
## Compling the macro with ACliC
Compiling the macro on the fly (while it's being loaded) is trivial. One simply adds a "+" at the end of the macro name:
```
   TFile f("....root");
   .x print_data.C+
```
ROOT then first invokes GCC from the release, makes a shared library, and loads it. Note that "++" would always cause compilation, while "+" would recompile an already existing macro only if the source code is newer than the compiled code, just like /pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/warning.gif "ALERT!") **Note:**
There are several pieces of information you need to know about how ROOT compiles a macro:
1. ROOT runs the *CINT* interpreter over the macro before compiling it in order to determine if it needs to generate dictionaries for some of the classes/functions mentioned in the macro. Unfortunately many of CMS's header files contain code that *CINT* can not parse. This means we must hide those headers from *CINT* but make sure they are visible to the compiler.
2. After compiling the code, ROOT links the compiled macro against all libraries which have been loaded. If the macro uses a function or variable from a library which has not yet been loaded, then ROOT will issue a 'missing symbol' error.
With the above in mind, here are the steps needed to arrive at a compiled ROOT macro:
1. Protect all headers using a
   ```
   #if !defined(__CINT__) && !defined(__MAKECINT__) #endif
   ```
   block
2. Introduce the macro block as a function with the same name as the file (this keeps *CINT* from trying to fully parse the internals of the routine)
3. In ROOT
   1. and start the autoloader
   2. `libDataFormatsFWLite`
   3. Create a `TFile` from one of the files you want to read. This will cause all the libraries for every class in the file to be loaded.
   4. Compile/link/execute the macro by doing `.x <filename>++`
An example macro template is shown below. The example assumes that the file is named print\_data.C
```
#if !defined(__CINT__) && !defined(__MAKECINT__)
#include "DataFormats/FWLite/interface/Handle.h"
#include "DataFormats/FWLite/interface/Event.h"
//Headers for the data items
...
#endif
void print_data() {
  TFile file("....root");
   fwlite::Event ev(&file);
   for( ev.toBegin(); ! ev.atEnd(); ++ev) {
       fwlite::Handle<std::vector<...> > objs;
       objs.getByLabel(ev,"....");
       //now can access data
       std::cout <<" size "<<objs.ptr()->size()<<std::endl;
       ...
   }
}
```
![ALERT!](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/warning.gif "ALERT!") **Note:**
A note on the preprocessor switches (testing on ***CINT*** and ): The first step that ROOT takes when compiling a macro is to run the *CINT* interpreter over the macro in order to determine what class or function 'dictionaries' it must create. After that step, the regular C++ compiler is used to build the code. Unfortunately, *CINT* is incapable of properly parsing many of our header files. However, it turns out the headers are not needed by *CINT* but only by the compiler, therefore adding
```
#if !defined(__CINT__) && !defined(__MAKECINT__)
...
#endif
```
around the header files avoids the problem with *CINT*.
## Running over a list of files
The fwlite::ChainEvent allows you to use the same information you use when accessing data in *cmsRun* using *edm::Event*:
1. Start the autoloader
2. in the helper library `gSystem->("libDataFormatsFWLite")`
3. Create a `std::vector<std::string>` to hold the list of file names
4. Include "DataFormats/FWLite/interface/Handle.h" to get the `fwlite::Handle`
5. `push_back` each file name into the `std::vector<std::string>`
6. Create an `fwlite::ChainEvent` by passing to the constructor the `vector`
7. Create a for loop
   1. Start loop by calling `toBegin()` on the `fwlite::ChainEvent`
   2. For each iteration of the loop call `atEnd` on the `fwlite::ChainEvent`
   3. At the end of each iteration, increment the `fwlite::Event` by using the operator++ method
8. When looping over the events
   1. Create an `fwlite::Handle< ... >` where the template argument is the C++ class you want to get from the event
   2. Call the `getByLabel` method of the `fwlite::Handle` passing it the event and the strings used to denote the object
An example macro template is shown below:
```
{
   gSystem->("libFWCoreFWLite.so");
   AutoLibraryLoader::enable();
   gSystem->("libDataFormatsFWLite.so");
   #include "DataFormats/FWLite/interface/Handle.h"
   vector<string> fileNames;
   fileNames.push_back("....root");
   fwlite::ChainEvent ev(fileNames);
   for( ev.toBegin(); ! ev.atEnd(); ++ev) {
       fwlite::Handle<std::vector<...> > objs;
       objs.getByLabel(ev,"....");
       //now can access data
       std::cout <<" size "<<objs.ptr()->size()<<std::endl;
       ...
   }
}
```
The compilation is identical to what is done for the case of a single file above, except in the macro you replace the use of `fwlite::Event` with `fwlite::ChainEvent`. ![ALERT!](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/warning.gif "ALERT!") **Note:** You must still pick one of the files to be used in the `fwlite::ChainEvent` and open it with a `TFile` on the ROOT command line in order to force the proper dictionaries to be opened.
## 3.5.2.4 Using edm::EventBase
It is now possible to use the `edm::EventBase` such that the user does not need to use the *fwlite::Handle* any more. This allows the user to write functions that can be used directly in FWLite or in the full framework and use the same "get" methods. Note that this does not function if one uses *CINT* to interprete the macros. A snippet of how to do this is given below:
```
for (ev.toBegin(); ! ev.atEnd(); ++ev) {
    edm::EventBase const & event = ev;
    // This snippet can be used in EITHER FWLite or the Full Framework
    edm::Handle<vector<reco::Vertex> > vertices;
    ( edm::InputTag("offlinePrimaryVertices"), vertices);
    // ...
  }
```
In the meantime FWLite and full framework can indeed be used in parallel on tha bases of truely compiled executables! If you want to know more about this have a look for a bunch of examples of compiled executables with FWLite on [WorkBookFWLiteExamples](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookFWLiteExamples).

# 3.5.4 FWLite.Python (using PyROOT)
Contents:
* [3.5.4 FWLite.Python (using PyROOT)](#3_5_4_FWLite_Python_using_PyROOT)
  + [Goals of this page:](#Goals_of_this_page)
  + [Introduction](#Introduction)
  + [Simple Annotated Example](#Simple_Annotated_Example)
  + [References](#References)
  + [Review status](#Review_status)
 [Detailed Review status](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookFWLitePython#ReviewStatus)
## Goals of this page:
In this section you will learn how to use FWLite.Python.For the impatient: you can also jump directly to instructions how to Run macros that analyze [MiniAOD](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/MiniAOD) CMS data directly in [MyFWLite\_12![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/jmejiagu/MyFWLite_12)
## Introduction
This document assumes that you already know python (although you may be able to learn a fair bit just following the examples). Please see [references](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookFWLitePython#References) for some links for learning Python.Why Python? CMS already uses it for its configuration files. It is a powerful language that many consider both much easier to read and easier to write than C++. FWLite.Python also provides a possibility to interactively *play with* CMS data.**Note:** Many people are already using 's Cint to interactively access CMS data. This is fine if one is only using the `TBrowser` or `Draw()` command, but for anything more complicated, Cint is **very** unreliable (meaning it crashes if you are lucky or runs without any error messages but gives you the wrong answer if you are not).FWLite.Python is designed to be intuitive if you are both experienced with Python and FWLite or the full framework.
## Simple Annotated Example
For a complete example, see [patZpeak.py![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/blob/master/DataFormats/FWLite/examples/patZpeak.py). This can be used either as a script or typed in interactively.To start, we want to import and the needed pieces of FWLite.Python:
```
import
from DataFormats.FWLite import Events, Handle
```
You then create an Events object by giving it either:
* `VarParsing` options object (see [Command line option parsing](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideCommandLineParsing) twiki for details)
* A string containing an input file
* A list of strings containing input files
In this case, I'll use a single input file
 (see other options in [MyFWLite\_12![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/jmejiagu/MyFWLite_12))
```
events = Events ('MuMu_miniaod-230-1.')
```
We then create a handle. Unlike `cmsRun` and `FWLite` in C++, this is a cpu-intensive operation so it is recommend to do this outside of the event loop.
```
# create handle outside of loop
handle  = Handle ('std::vector<pat::Muon>')
```
Now we make a label
```
# a label is just a tuple of strings that is initialized just
# like and edm::InputTag
label = ("slimmedMuons")
```
By default, [PyRoot](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/PyRoot) will open windows. Make sure you tell if you don't want to do this:
```
.gROOT.SetBatch()        # don't pop up canvases
```
Create any histograms you want to :
```
# Create histograms, etc.
.gROOT.SetStyle('Plain') # white background
zmassHist = .TH1F ("zmass", "Z Candidate Mass", 50, 20, 220)
```
And now the event loop:
```
# loop over events
for event in events:
```
Let's get the data as we would in FWLite and `cmsRun`:
```
    # use getByLabel, just like in cmsRun
    event.getByLabel (label, handle)
```
Now use what you got:
```
    # get the product
    muons = handle.product()
```
Since I'm running over Z → μμ, let's make a Z peak:
```
    # use muons to make Z peak
    numMuons = len (muons)
    if numMuons < 2: continue
    for outer in xrange (numMuons - 1):
        outerMuon = muons[outer]
        for inner in xrange (outer + 1, numMuons):
            innerMuon = muons[inner]
            if outerMuon.charge() * innerMuon.charge() >= 0:
                continue
            inner4v = .TLorentzVector (innerMuon.px(), (),
                                           innerMuon.pz(), innerMuon.energy())
            outer4v = .TLorentzVector ((), outerMuon.py(),
                                           outerMuon.pz(), outerMuon.energy())
            zmassHist.( (inner4v + outer4v).M() )
```
Groovy. Let's make a plot and quit:
```
# make a canvas, draw, and save it
c1 = .TCanvas()
zmassHist.Draw()
c1.Print ("zmass_py.png")
```
## References
Python introductions:
* Python tutorial (for programming beginners): [https://docs.python.org/3/tutorial/index.html![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://docs.python.org/3/tutorial/index.html)
* Dive Into Python (for programmers): [http://diveintopython.org/toc/index.html![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://diveintopython.org/toc/index.html)

# 6.5 Simulating and Reconstructing events with Fast Simulation
* Find the users guide here: [SWGuideFastSimulation](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideFastSimulation) (public)
* Find the general start page here:  (CMS only)
* The outdated workbook page has been moved to [WorkBookFastSimulationArchive](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookFastSimulationArchive) (public)
## Recipe for 13TeV ()
Please check with your PAG/POG if they require specific conditions.
```
cmsrel CMSSW_9_2_10
cd CMSSW_9_2_10/src
cmsenv
```
No packages need to be checked, but for the sake of being more organized, you can create and work within `FastSimulation/GenProduction`.For simulating a [MinBias](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/MinBias?topicparent=CMSPublic.WorkBookFastSimulation;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") sample with no PU, use the following cmsDriver command. You always can replace the [MinBias](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/MinBias?topicparent=CMSPublic.WorkBookFastSimulation;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") generator fragment with your favorite fragment.**SIMULATION WITHOUT PU:**
```
cmsDriver.py MinBias_13TeV_pythia8_TuneCUETP8M1_cfi --conditions auto:run2_mc --fast -n 1000 --era Run2_25ns --eventcontent AODSIM -s GEN,SIM,RECOBEFMIX,DIGI:pdigi_valid,RECO --datatier GEN-SIM-DIGI-RECO --beamspot Realistic25ns13TeVEarly2017Collision
```
To simulate physics samples with PU we show the standard mixing method and we need a [MinBias](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/MinBias?topicparent=CMSPublic.WorkBookFastSimulation;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") sample to proceed with this example. In the meanwhile private [MinBias](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/MinBias?topicparent=CMSPublic.WorkBookFastSimulation;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") samples can be generated using the example below.
```
cmsDriver.py MinBias_13TeV_pythia8_TuneCUETP8M1_cfi --conditions auto:run2_mc --fast -n 1000 --era Run2_25ns --eventcontent FASTPU \
-s GEN,SIM,RECOBEFMIX,DIGI:pdigi_valid,RECO --datatier GEN-SIM-RECO --beamspot Realistic25ns13TeVEarly2017Collision
```
**SIMULATION WITH PU:**
```
cmsDriver.py MinBias_13TeV_pythia8_TuneCUETP8M1_cfi --conditions auto:run2_mc --fast -n 100 --eventcontent AODSIM -s GEN,SIM,RECOBEFMIX,DIGI:pdigi_valid,RECO --datatier AODSIM --beamspot Realistic25ns13TeVEarly2017Collision --era Run2_25ns --pileup_input file:MinBias_13TeV_pythia8_TuneCUETP8M1_cfi_GEN_SIM_RECOBEFMIX_DIGI_RECO.root --pileup AVE_35_BX_25ns
```

## Goals of this page:
This page is intended to familiarize you with making a rule and monitoring the progress of transfers to a site. In particular, you will learn:
* what is
* how to make a rule at a site
* how to monitor transfers
## Contents

## What is ?
is the current CMS data placement tool, taking the place of  in the autumn of 2020. It sits above various grid middleware [SRM (Storage Resource Manager), FTS (File Transfer Service)] to manage large-scale transfers between CMS centres. At its core, is a collection of daemons that each perform specific tasks, including triggering transfers, tracking data placement, and so on.While is multifaceted, it can be summarized as having a few main roles: triggering and tracking the transfer of data files between CMS institutions, remembering where all copies of data files have been placed (if any), how much storage at each institution is being used, and how much storage individual users are taking up. Put another way, CMS users can use to find data that they need, transfer it to their institution, and hold it there in the storage space allotted to them. Then, when said  of the data is flagged as no longer being needed, can dynamically free up the storage space by deleting the replica. Every CMS institution exists within as an RSE ( Element), and facilitates the transfer of data between RSEs.A more thorough review of and its fundamentals can be found [here](/twiki/bin//CMS/IntroToRucio).
## Why do I need to transfer MC sample or Data files?
For general analysis, CMS collaborators can use T1 or T2 sites. Though, if users need to access data locally rather than remotely, or if they need to ensure a dataset is safely protected on disk, they can use  to make these requests.If you run a [CRAB](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideCrab) job and find that your MC sample or data is not located at a desired site, you can request to have it transferred there using .You **do not** need to have your MC sample or data at "your" institution to run analyses; CRAB will be able to run on it in any location. However, if necessary, you may request a  be made at your local site.
## A with
### Finding Data to Request
The easiest way to find needed data is to use [DAS![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cmsweb.cern.ch/das/), or the Data Aggregation Service. DAS combines information from DBS and to provide the names and locations of datasets, blocks, and files. A complete review of using DAS (both the web version and client version) can be found [here](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookLocatingDataSamples).
### Requesting a Transfer with
moves and tracks data using a set of policies called rules. Rules are so-called because will at all times, to the best of its ability, attempt to follow all valid rules. The most immediate reason to create a rule, then, is to transfer data; a new rule that dictates that a particular dataset should exist at a particular site will cause to trigger a data transfer so as to satisfy that rule. A helpful consequence of this system is that can automatically correct situations where data goes missing. Since is attempting to follow a rule, rather than fulfill a one-time transfer, it will re-transfer data if it ever detects any amount has disappeared. Put another way, in the instance of data loss, will automatically replace that data so long as a valid rule is still in place.**Note**: In order to successfully create a rule and request a transfer, the user must have enough storage allotted to them at the destination site to house the requested data. If this condition is not met, the rule cannot be created. See the **Ask**  section below for more information.
#### Rule Requirements
There are three pieces of information that **must** be provided by a user to successfully create a rule. These are:
* **The DID to be transferred**
   The Data IDentifier (DID) is the name of the piece of data the user wishes to transfer. A DID consists of two pieces, the first being a scope. The scope designates the namespace in which the data resides. One can also think of a scope as being how the data is categorized. Centrally produced and managed data often has the `cms` scope, while user-produced data often has the scope `user.username`, where the latter portion will be the creator (this will be the scope of CRAB data that has been injected into , for example). The second part of a DID is the name; this will be the actual name of the dataset/block/file in question. A complete did has the form `<scope:name>`.
* **The number of copies**
   For the majority of users, the correct number of copies to request is `1`. In the rare case where a DID is to be placed at multiple sites, more copies may be requested.
* **The destination RSE**
   In , CMS sites are represented by (RSEs). RSEs for T2 and T3 sites will usually follow a pattern of `TIER_COUNTRY_INSTITUTION`. Some examples include the CERN T2 (`T2_CH_CERN`) and the Florida T2 (`T2_US_Florida`). T1 sites are slightly different as they generally have disk and tape endpoints. The FNAL T1, for example, has a disk endpoint (`T1_US_FNAL_Disk`) and a tape endpoint (`T1_US_FNAL_Tape`). Other T1s follow the same pattern.
##### Optional Additions and Best Practices
* **Rule Lifetime**
   Rules may be created with a lifetime so that they will expire on a given . Once data is no longer protected by a rule, will mark it for cleanup to free up storage space at the site in question. **Best Practice**: Always create a rule with a lifetime. This will help prevent unused data from accumulating and make sure that a user does not unintentionally use the entirety of their quota. The owner/creator of a rule can always extend the lifetime of a rule if the data is still needed.
* **Rule Comment**
   Rules may be created with a descriptive comment. This comment will be saved and is viewable along with other rule information. **Best Practice**: Always create a rule with a comment. Comments can help users, operators, and site administrators understand the details of a rule. This can be especially helpful during periods of storage cleanup, where a descriptive comment might save a rule from being deleted.
* **Ask**
   When creating a rule, a user may ask for for the creation of a rule. Doing so will always allow the rule to be created, no matter if the user has adequate storage allotted to them at the destination RSE. However, will not request a transfer of the data until a site administrator approves the rule.
#### Option 1: Using the Command Line Interface
**Note**: As of 36.0.0, a new CLI command format was introduced. Using the flag `--legacy` will force the old command format if necessary, and the pre-36 commands are listed here for continuity. As a rule of thumb, any EL8 and lower system uses <36.0.0 and EL9 systems use >=36.0.0. For simplicity, the newer version of commands will be referred to as "For EL9" and the older as "For EL8 and below".The CLI can be used anywhere that has a `cvmfs` mount (though lxplus is recommended). Begin by first initiating a CMS VOMS proxy with a valid grid certificate:`voms-proxy-init --voms cms --valid 192:00`You can then set up with the following commands:
```
source /cvmfs/cms.cern.ch//setup-py3.sh
export RUCIO_ACCOUNT=<cern_username>
```
The CLI should now be available, and a full list of commands be found using  `-h`. If running  `whoami` shows a list of your account information (email, account name, account creation , etc) you have successfully logged in.Upon confirming a successful setup, a rule can be created using the command  `rule add` (Or  `--legacy add-rule` for EL8 and below). A full invocation of this command will look like
  `rule add cms:/ZMM/Summer11-DESIGN42_V11_428_SLHC1-v1/GEN-SIM --copies 1 --rses T2_CH_CERN --lifetime 15780000 --comment 'This is an example comment' --ask-`
 This command is placing one  of the dataset `/ZMM/Summer11-DESIGN42_V11_428_SLHC1-v1/GEN-SIM` at the RSE `T2_CH_CERN` for a period of 6 months (**Note**: The CLI requires the lifetime to be provided in seconds). A comment is included, and is being requested.If the rule is created successfully, an alphanumeric hash will be returned. This is the rule ID, and should be saved for later reference. If you need to look up a rule for a DID, you can use  `rule list [target DID] --account [Your Account]` (or  `--legacy list-rules` for EL8 and below=
#### Option 2: Using the WebUI
The WebUI provides a streamlined way to request one or more transfers. The starting page of the UI can be found [here![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cms--webui.cern.ch/).![dropdown_menu](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/pub/CMSPublic/WorkBookFileTransfer/WebUI_Landing_Page.png)
* Clicking "Request new rule" will lead to a form for the user to fill out. The first section is where the needed DID(s) are provided.
   ![did_selection](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/pub/CMSPublic/WorkBookFileTransfer/webui_did_selection.png)
   A single DID can be searched for and selected using the "DID Pattern Search" tab. Wildcards may be used in the provided DID to help the user find a particular DID if they do not already have the complete scope and name combination. : does not use the traditional CMS naming conventions. Next to the search bar are two radio buttons; "Container" refers to a CMS dataset, and "Dataset" refers to a CMS block. Choose accordingly based on the data being searched.
   By choosing "List of DIDs", multiple DIDs can be provided (one per line) in order to create multiple rules at once.
* Once the DIDs, have been selected, the user will be presented with a field where the destination RSE can be chosen.
   ![rse_selection](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/pub/CMSPublic/WorkBookFileTransfer/webui_rse_selection.png)
   The UI will provide a dropdown list of RSEs matching what has been typed thus far, helping to autocomplete the RSE search.
   The UI will then check if the user has enough remaining storage quota at the chosen RSE to house the selected DID(s). If this is the case, the next field will appear. If not, the user will be prompted to ask for on the rule(s) being created before continuing.
* The final step is the "Options" section. Here, the user must first specify the grouping of their rule. Briefly, grouping determines how individual files will be distributed when multiple RSEs are chosen as the destination for a rule. For the majority of users, who will be specifying a single RSE, the "All" choice will be sufficient. Next, the lifetime of the rule is specified (provided here in days). Copies should generally be left at one, and a comment can be provided.
A summary recap of the rule creation process will be provided, after which the UI will move on to create the rule(s).
#### Option 2: Using the Python API
Set up of the with Python can be found [here](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin//CMS/RucioWithPython).To request a rule:
 `from .client.client import Client`
 `client = Client()`
 `client.add_replication_rule(did, copies, rse_expression, lifetime, comment, ask_approval, source_replica_expression)`
#### Auto of Rules
supports a service where users can have their rules automatically approved for transfer. There is a predetermined quota of 50 TB per site for this service, and several additional requirements for rules to be successfully approved:
* Users **must** specify a Tier 1 or Tier 2 RSE when making the rule. Rules listing T0 or T3 sites will be denied.
* The lifetime **must** be specified, and will be six months or less
* The `grouping` of the rule **must** be set to `ALL`
With this in mind, using the Auto Approve service is simple in practice.
* For rules made in the CLI, the following arguments should be included:
  + `--grouping 'ALL'`
  + `--ask-`
  + `--activity 'User AutoApprove'`
  + `--lifetime <less than six months>`
At present, the `Activity` of a rule cannot be specified when making a rule via the WebUI, so the Auto Approve service can only be used when making a rule via the CLI.
### Monitoring a Transfer
#### Option 1: Using the Command Line Interface
**Note**: As of 36.0.0, a new CLI command format was introduced. Using the flag `--legacy` will force the old command format if necessary, and the pre-36 commands are listed here for continuity. As a rule of thumb, any EL8 and lower system uses <36.0.0 and EL9 systems use >=36.0.0. For simplicity, the newer version of commands will be referred to as "For EL9" and the older as "For EL8 and below".The CLI can be used anywhere that has a `cvmfs` mount (though lxplus is recommended). Begin by first initiating a CMS VOMS proxy with a valid grid certificate:`voms-proxy-init --voms cms --valid 192:00`You can then set up with the following commands:
```
source /cvmfs/cms.cern.ch//setup-py3.sh
export RUCIO_ACCOUNT=<cern_username>
```
The CLI should now be available, and a full list of commands be found using  `-h`. If running  `whoami` shows a list of your account information (email, account name, account creation , etc) you have successfully logged in.Upon confirming a successful setup, the status of a rule can be checked using the command  `rule show` ( `--legacy rule-info` for EL8 and below). A full invocation of the command will look like
 `rule show <rule_id>`
This will result in a table containing general information about the rule. The fields to pay attention to are `State` and `Locks OK/REPLICATING/STUCK`. `Locks` give the number of constituent files in the `OK`, `REPLICATING`, and `STUCK` states, respectively.
* `OK` locks are files that have successfully transferred to their destination.
* `REPLICATING` locks are files still queued or in the process of transferring.
* `STUCK` locks are files whose transfer has failed.
The overall `State` of the rule reflects these; an `OK` rule has successfully transferred all files, a `REPLICATING` rule has at least one file still transferring but none `STUCK`, and a `STUCK` rule has at least one `STUCK` file. If the rule is `STUCK`, an will be provided in a dedicated  field. Otherwise, this field will return `None`.If the rule ID is not readily available, it can be found using the command  `rule list --account  <username>` ( or  `--legacy list-rules --account <username>` for EL8 and below). This will return a list of all rules belonging to the provided username, and the pertinent ID can be used with  `rule show`.
#### Option 2: Using the WebUI
The WebUI provides a streamlined way to monitor one or more transfers. The starting page of the UI can be found [here![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cms--webui.cern.ch/).![dropdown_menu](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/pub/CMSPublic/WorkBookFileTransfer/WebUI_Landing_Page.png)Clicking "List my rules" will bring the user to a page listing all of their rules that were created within a particular time frame (14 days by default). The number of days can be increased to find older rules, and the account name can be changed to find rules made by other users. This page will show the overall `State` of the rules, as well as the status of the various `Locks`. More information on a particular rule can be viewed by clicking on it.
#### Help with Stuck Rules
Rules can be `STUCK` (i.e., fail to transfer) for a variety of reasons. will resubmit and retry `STUCK` rules periodically; if this fails to solve the issue, users are encouraged to first consult their site administrators. If the rule remains `STUCK`, submit a JIRA ticket in the CMS Data Transfer Requests project, found [here![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://its.cern.ch/jira/projects/CMSTRANSF/summary). Please provide a thorough description of the issue, as well as the relevant rule ID.
### Helpful CLI Commands
To see where a user has quota (and how much), the command  `account limit show <username>` (or  `--legacy list-account-usage <username>` for EL8 and below) can be used. This will return a table showing all RSEs where the user has quota, how much they've been allotted, and how much is remaining.To see a list of all RSEs currently available in (including T1, T2, and T3 sites), the command  `rse list` (or  `--legacy list-rses` for EL8 and below) can be used.To delete a rule that is no longer needed, the command  `rule remove <rule_id>` (or  `--legacy delete-rule <rule_id>` for EL8 and below) can be used. This can only be done if the user has permission to do (e.g., is the owner of the rule).To update a rule, the command  `rule update <rule_id>` (or  `--legacy update-rule <rule_id>` for EL8 and below) can be used - the most common arguments will be `--comment` to update the attached comment and `--lifetime` to increase or decrease the remaining lifetime (in seconds). This can only be done if the user has permission to do (e.g., is the owner of the rule).To see storage availability of a particular RSE, the command  `rse show <rse>` (or  `--legacy list-rse-usage <rse>` for EL8 and below) can be used. The optional argument `--show-accounts` can be used to include each of the individual accounts that are holding data at the RSE. This will return a table showing the various storage statistics of a site, including:
* Expired Storage: The amount of space at an RSE filled by data not protected by a rule. This data will be cleared when space is required for new, incoming data.
* Obsolete Storage: The amount of space at an RSE filled by data that is marked for immediate deletion. The reported value is a subset of Expired Storage.
* : The sum total of all storage space in use by , including data protected by rules and data that is available for deletion (i.e. Expired and Obsolete)
* Static Storage: The maximum amount of storage space available to ; above this amount, will aggressively delete unprotected data until is less than or equal to Static Storage
* Unavailable Storage: The amount of space filled by data that is locked by because it is involved in a transfer.
allows for containers themselves to be grouped together under a single parent container. This can be useful for bookkeeping (i.e. keeping track of a large number of containers for an analysis). When requesting a very large number of containers for transfer, this strategy can be used to reduce the total number of requests. However, this strategy should be used sparingly. Doing this will reduce the extent to which the data can be managed. Most importantly, unneeded data will not be able to be deleted without deleting the rule for the entire container. Use this option only for very large requests for which all of the constituent data will be needed throughout the entirety of the set lifetime. Instructions can be found [here](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/RucioUserDocsContainers).
## Other Resources
The official documentation can be found [here](/twiki/bin//CMS/). It contains several pages with information on specific tasks and actions.A dedicated beginner's guide can be found [here](/twiki/bin//CMS/RucioBeginnersGuide). This page goes more in-depth on and its fundamentals, as well as giving a broader overview of as accessed via the CLI and Python. There is also a glossary of terms that can be referenced.The core documentation can be found [here![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://.cern.ch/documentation/).
##  files from other sites using gfal- command
Instructions are on the  [FAQ twiki](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/CRAB3FAQ#How_to_list_copy_remove_files_di) on how to use gfal tools to find and  files from another site's Storage Element.
### Instructions for FNAL-LPC
The [copyfiles.py![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/FNALLPC/lpc-scripts/blob/master/copyfiles.py) script can be used to  single files or a directory of files using gfal- or xrdcp from another site to T3\_US\_FNALLPC.The [getSiteInfo.py![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/FNALLPC/lpc-scripts/blob/master/getSiteInfo.pyttps%3A//github.com/FNALLPC/lpc-scripts/blob/master/getSiteInfo.py) script can be useful to get the information of the site's endpoint to obtain a single file through gfal-, it is used by the copyfiles.py script above.

# 3.4 Physics Analysis Oriented Event Display ( / [FireworksWeb](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/FireworksWeb) )
## Contents
* [FireworksWeb](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookFireworks#FWWFireworksWeb)
  + [WebServices](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookFireworks#FWWWebService)
  + [Documentation](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookFireworks#FWWDocumentationDirect): Direct link [FireworksWeb UserGuide![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/alja/FireworksWeb/blob/master/doc/UserGuide.md), [/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/alja/FireworksWeb/issues)

  + [Presentations](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookFireworks#FWWDocumentation)
* [LegacyFireworks](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin//CMS/FireworksTwikiOldBaq)
* [UserSupport](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookFireworks#SupportFeedback)
 is the CMS event-display project and **cmsShow** is the official name of the executable. Both names are used interchangeably so don't get confused.The core of is built on top of the Event Data Model ([EDM](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/EDM)) and the light version of the software framework (FWLite). Event Visualization Environment (EVE) of ROOT is used to manage 3D and 2D views, selection, and user-interaction with the graphics windows. Several EVE components were developed by in collaboration between and ROOT. In event display operation simple plugins are registered into the system to perform conversion from [EDM](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/EDM) collections into their visual representations. As a guiding principle, shows only what is available in the [EDM](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/EDM) event-data, no reconstruction or result enhancement is performed internally. Visibility of collection elements can be filtered via a generic expression (PAT parser is used internally).
## FireworksWeb
**FireworksWeb** is a rewrite of that transfers visualization object data from server to client in two stages: first, the part for descriptive data, then a set of binary C-style buffers that are passed from server process to the WebGL implementation in the user's browser.
### WebServices
CERN site: [https://.cern.ch![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://.cern.ch)

# 3.4.3 Geometry
* [Producing Geometry File](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookFireworksGeometry#FwGeoCreate)
* [Viewing with cmsShow](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookFireworksGeometry#FwGeoView)
  + [Browsing detector /bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookFireworksGeometry#FwGeoCmsShow)
* [Presentations](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookFireworksGeometry#FwGeoPresentations)
### Introduction
This document is a user guide how to produce and efficiently visualize cms geometries in a . With first step DDD geometry is converted to TGeo format and then display in Geometry Table . Note, this is not the geometry format which is used for drawing rec hits and detectors in projected views.
### Producing TGeo files
Geometry files can be produced with cmsRun. The configuration script scrips take an argument which specifies geometry configuration. Output of cmsRun is cmsSimGeo<tag>.root and cmsTGeoRecoGeom<tag>.root for simulation and reconstruction geometry.
* **Simulation Geometry**
```
   cmsRun /Geometry/python/dumpSimGeometry_cfg.py tag=<prod>
```
* **Reconstruction Geometry**
```
   cmsRun /Geometry/python/dumpRecoGeometry_cfg.py tag=<prod>
```
### Viewing with cmsShow
can display the simulation geometry and flag any overlaps.
By default cmsShow takes cmsSimGeom-14.root from a tarball or CMSSW project area to display the geometry. If you want to use another file, use the `--sim-geom-file <file-name>` command-line option.
You can display the geometry by running cmsShow, creating a geometry table , and selecting 3D from the table menu. Alternatively you can use pre-prepared configurations available in the CMSSW project area and cmsShow tarball.
```
./cmsShow -c simGeo.fwc --sim-geom-file <geometry-file>
```
#### Moving over node hierarchy
In the default configuration all nodes are drawn up to specified visibility depth. Instead of swiching visibility off for the subtestectors which can clutter a , you can move top node to the subdetector yoou want to investigate. Top node setting is saved and restored in configuration file.
[![TopNode1.png](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/pub/CMSPublic/WorkBookFireworksGeometry/_600___TopNode1.png)](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/pub/CMSPublic/WorkBookFireworksGeometry/TopNode1.png " detector as a top node.")
detector as a top node.
[![TopNode2.png](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/pub/CMSPublic/WorkBookFireworksGeometry/_600___TopNode2.png)](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/pub/CMSPublic/WorkBookFireworksGeometry/TopNode2.png "! detector is top node. Can move back to top by clicking CdTop button.")
detector is top node. Can move back to top by clicking CdTop button.
#### All children visibility On/Off
Geometry table popup menu has an option for switching visibility of all child nodes. This is in particular useful for volumes with large number of daughter nodes.
[![AllChld3.png](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/pub/CMSPublic/WorkBookFireworksGeometry/_600___AllChld3.png)](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/pub/CMSPublic/WorkBookFireworksGeometry/AllChld3.png "Disable rendering of all ecal cells")
Disable rendering of all ecal cells
[![AllChld2b.png](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/pub/CMSPublic/WorkBookFireworksGeometry/_600___AllChld2b.png)](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/pub/CMSPublic/WorkBookFireworksGeometry/AllChld2b.png "Select only cells with eta index -4")
Select only cells with eta index -4
#### Visibility depth
Value of default visibility depth level in cmsShow is 3. It is intentionally set low to prevent rendering of too many nodes.
[![VisLevel1a.png](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/pub/CMSPublic/WorkBookFireworksGeometry/_600___VisLevel1a.png)](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/pub/CMSPublic/WorkBookFireworksGeometry/VisLevel1a.png "Open geometry table  controller accessed from the table  .")
Open geometry table controller accessed from the table .
[![VisLevel2a.png](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/pub/CMSPublic/WorkBookFireworksGeometry/_600___VisLevel2a.png)](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/pub/CMSPublic/WorkBookFireworksGeometry/VisLevel2a.png "Increase visibility depth to 2.")
Increase visibility depth to 2.
#### Filter Material
also has an option to draw nodes which match given material or shape. In simulation geometry it is large variety of materials. In TGeo reco geometry material is set only to define color and has a name matching a detector name.
[![Filter.png](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/pub/CMSPublic/WorkBookFireworksGeometry/_600___Filter.png)](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/pub/CMSPublic/WorkBookFireworksGeometry/Filter.png "Select nodes wich match dtxb material name.")
Select nodes wich match dtxb material name.
#### Checking overlaps
Overlaps can be displayed with table . It makes sense to trace overlaps only in simulation geometry since reco geometry no concept of mother volumes.
```
./cmsShow -c overlaps.fwc
```
![overlaps1.png](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/pub/CMSPublic/WorkBookFireworksGeometry/_500___overlaps1.png "overlaps1.png")
### Presentations
The geometry capability was presented at the 2012 CHEP conference:
* [Displaying of simulation geometry in (CHEP 2012)![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cms.cern.ch/iCMS/jsp/openfile.jsp?type=CR&year=2012&files=CR2012_087.pdf)
* [poster (CHEP 2012)](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/pub/CMSPublic/WorkBookFireworksGeometry/SimGeoCms-Poster.pptx)

# 3.4.6 Problems running -- This information is OUTDATED March, 2025
## OpenGL and problems
### Indirect (remote) rendering disabled by default in newer XOrg versions (including XQuartz)
The error shows up like this:
```
 (~ ): glxgears
X Error of failed request:  BadValue (integer parameter out of range for operation)
  Major opcode of failed request:  150 (GLX)
  Minor opcode of failed request:  3 (X_GLXCreateContext)
  Value in failed request:   number of failed request:  23
  Current serial number in output stream:  24
```
This can be fixed by adding the `+iglx` option to the line that starts the X server on the local machine. There is currently no configuration file option (it will be added to xorg-1.19 and probably backported to older versions).**OSX**
 or make sure it is not running. After the installation run the following command:
```
defaults write org.macosforge.xquartz. enable_iglx -bool true
```
**You may find you need to reboot your machine to have that take effect. Also note that XQuartz installation requires logout/log back in after installation for its changes to take effect.******
this depends on a distribution, for Ubuntu see the link below. We will update this entry for other distributions as needed. Replacing `/usr/bin/xorg` with a script should work everywhere, as descibed here [hard hack![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://forums.fedoraforum.org/showthread.php?t=224526&highlight=-ignoreABI) (substitute `-ignoreABI` with `+iglx`).Links:
[Original XOrg change![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cgit.freedesktop.org/xorg/xserver/commit/?id=d0da0e9c3bb8fe0cd4879ecb24d21715bfaa209b),
[Phoronix article![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://www.phoronix.com/scan.php?page=news_item&px=Xorg-IGLX-Potential-Bye-Bye),
[Ubuntu forum![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://askubuntu.com/questions/745135/how-to-enable-indirect-glx-contexts-iglx-in-ubuntu-14-04-lts-with-nvidia-gfx),
[Apple forum![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://lists.apple.com/archives/-users/2016/May/msg00060.html).
### Running remotely on CC7 machines (also lxplus7.cern.ch)
There is a problem with the Mesa GL version on lxplus (probably all CC7 machines) that manifests as SEGV in LLVM pipeline during early stage of startup:
```
#4  <signal handler called>
#5  0x00007fab213cf5ba in __memcpy_ssse3_back () from /lib64/libc.so.6
#6  0x00007fab09412bdb in llvm::WritableMemoryBuffer::getNewUninitMemBuffer(unsigned long, llvm::Twine const&) () from /usr/lib64/libLLVM-6.0-rhel.so
#7  0x00007fab09412caf in getMemBufferCopyImpl(llvm::StringRef, llvm::Twine const&) () from /usr/lib64/libLLVM-6.0-rhel.so
#8  0x00007fab09412d30 in llvm::MemoryBuffer::getMemBufferCopy(llvm::StringRef, llvm::Twine const&) () from /usr/lib64/libLLVM-6.0-rhel.so
```
Setting the following environment variables disables usage of LLVM renderer in Mesa GL:
```
export LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1
export GALLIUM_DRIVER=softpipe
export DRAW_USE_LLVM=0
```
###  specific issues
#### drivers
On board Inter graphic drivers are known to be buggy. To check if this is the case run `lspci` and look if there is intel graphic card listed. Also check `glxinfo` to get list of GL extensions (should be 50 or more of them). Try to disable hardware rendering with **LIBGL\_ALWAYS\_INDIRECT** environment variable:
```
export LIBGL_ALWAYS_INDIRECT=1
```
Alternatively you can use cmsShow option **--soft**, which exports the same environment variable.If you still have problems and `glxgears` run without errors, send output of `lspci`, `glxinfo`, and `dpyinfo` to support mailing list ().
#### Window refresh does not work properly
* On some window managers window refresh does not work properly. For example if window is covered by another window, the window stays black after the covering window is removed. To fix the problem open file `/etc//xorg.conf` and remove line `Option "BackingStore" "on"` in the Device section. Restart X session when finish changes in `xorg.conf` file.
#### Ubuntu shows only empty graphics views
* The advanced window manager now default in Ubuntu interferes with OpenGL programs. The problem can be fixed by going to **System Preferences** -> **Appearances** -> **Visual Effects** and set the option to **None**
### Mac OS specific issues
CmsShow is not running natively on Big Sur (OSXI)
See [docker![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/alja/-docker#readme) solution.* **or later required for 8x mac tarball**The following error is printed with 2.7.8 or older:
  ```
  ./cmsShow data.root
  dyld: Library not loaded: /opt//lib/libXt.7.dylib
    Referenced from: /Users/alja/cms-dev/standalone/cmsShow-8.1/libexec/cmsShow.exe
    Reason: image not found
  ```
* **Visuals problems**. If you see the following error printed to the terminal after running cmsShow
  Error in <TGLWidget::CreateGLContainer>: No good visual found!
  terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::runtime\_error'
   what(): No good visual found!
  Then probably you have restricted the number of colors is allowed to use. To change this do the following:
  1. Make .app the active application
  2. Choose the menu item **->Preferences...**
  3. In the preference dialog choose the **Output** tab
  4. In the selection box next too **Colors:** make sure to select **From Display**
  5. Restart .app
## Problems saving images
### FBO error saving into png/gif files
When save image into png or gif file, you can get the following error:
```
Error in <TGLEmbeddedViewer::TGLViewer::SavePictureUsingFBO>:
TGLFBO::Init maximum size supported by GL implementation is 0.
```
The problem is a consequence of false information in GL query. You can avoid the problem by using system tools to create screenshot or to disable FBO in your .rootrc file, by adding the following line:
```
OpenGL.SavePicturesViaFBO: false
```
###  and ps format
Save to  or ps file formats is not supported and will be removed as an option from ROOT file dialog. It is not supported because transparent object and textures are not correctly converted. If you need , the convert command from ImageMagick tools can create a  encapsulating the binary image.
### Alternatives to save image into file
* **** All  distibution ship `xwd` command line tool to capture an image. Bellow are two examples of usage:
  ```
       xwd  -root | convert - screenshot1.png
       xwd  | convert - screenshot1.png
  ```
* **Mac**
   Command-Shift-3 :Take a screenshot of the screen, and save it as a file on the desktop
   Command-Shift-4, then select an area: Take a screenshot of an area and save it as a file on the desktop

## 3.4.7 Archive of cmsShow release notes
: ![5](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/pub/CMS/WebPreferences/complete5.png)
* **2011-03-09:** `cmsShow-3.11-2` released
  + options for  splitting in RhoZ projections.
  + Change DataFormats version to CMSSW\_3\_11\_2.
* **2011-02-24:** `cmsShow-3.11-1` released
  + Support usage of TriggerResults from all processes in event filtering.
  + Fish-eye transformation for projected views.
  + Support multiple detail views.
  + Show current file and event index in window title-bar.
* **2011-02-03:** `cmsShow-3.11-stable` released
  + Use 3\_11\_0 data-formats.
  + Fix problem with scaling of MET objects (note that some MET collections do have E != Et).
  + Improve calorimeter energy scale determination for projected views.
* **2010-12-17:** `cmsShow39-` released
  + Do not show HO contribution to CaloTower in HCal purpose - provide special "HCal Outer" purpose for that.
  + Fix inactive filter-entry problem in "Event Filter" dialog. This only occurred when configuration was reloaded.
* **2010-12-06:** `cmsShow39-stable` released
  + Several minor improvements and bug-fixes.
* **2010-11-25:** `cmsShow39-beta2` released
  + Updated ParticleFlow visualization: new "PF " and "PF RhoPhi" views showing ECal RecHits (purpose PFEcalRecHit).
  + Fix flickering of table-views.
  + "Invariant mass dialog" (available from "Window" menu).
  + Improved debug option -- attach gdb on terminal signal.
* **2010-10-29:** `cmsShow39-beta` released
* **2010-09-29:** `cmsShow39-alpha` made available for download
## cmsShow38
Release highlights:
* addition of iSpy ;
  + ability to show calorimeter rec-hits & clusters;
  + ability to show muon rec-hits;
* addition of / Tech trigger table ;
* addition of HF ;
* addition of calo-tower detail ;
* visualization of particle-flow objects;
* cross- highlight;
* detailed calo-tower feedback / tooltip;
* most [EDM](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/EDM) collections can be viewed in table ;
* improved configuration file format;
* configuration reload at runtime, e.g. ispy.fwc;
* filtering in dialog for adding collections;
* control of transparency for collections and objects.
There are no known major issues or known bugs so please report any problems to hn-cms-visualization or fill out a bug report in savannah [https://savannah.cern.ch/projects/fireworks/![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://savannah.cern.ch/projects/fireworks/).
### ChangeLog
* **2010-09-06:** `cmsShow38-` released
  + for ROOT bug in number entry that prevented specifying of event-id containing more than nine digits.
  + checks for existence of -extra information for muons.
* **2010-09-01:** `cmsShow38-stable` released
  + Update data-formats to 3\_8\_2.
  + Small fixes in ROOT 3D graphics (drawing of calo-towers).
* **2010-08-20:**  released
  + Fix a problem in  propagation. This affected propagation of muons when magnetic filed was zero (cosmics).
  + Several significant optimizations of object management were implemented. Simulated heavy-ion data was used for performance testing.
* **2010-07-21:** `cmsShow36` released
  + tooltips and improve legend of  detail-.
  + Fix positioning of RPC rec-hits -- chambers themselves are not drawn as correct geometry is not available.
  + Increase precision of the default -propagator from 1mm to 0.1mm.
  + Read coil current needed to scale the magnetic field from data-file when available (present for files produced with 3\_6).
* **2010-06-22:** `cmsShow36-beta-3` released
  + tarball was still shipped with 3\_6\_1\_patch4 data-formats.
  + Improved particle-flow configuration.
  + Improved scaling of particle-flow objects in -.
  + Allow viewing of calo-towers and particle-flow particles in the same -.
  + Make muon chambers assigned to a  transparent.
  + optional axis guides - enable them from the controller dialog.
  + Improved legends, colors and tooltips in detail-views.
  + Fix display of pixel-tracks.
  + Fix display of Si-strip barrel modules attached to a .
  + detailed controls for event handling in GL windows (to be put in rootrc):
     OpenGL.EventHandler.ArrowKeyFactor: 1.0
     OpenGL.EventHandler.MouseDragFactor: 1.0
     OpenGL.EventHandler.MouseWheelFactor: 1.0
* **2010-06-18:** `cmsShow36-beta-2` released
  + Update FWlite to tag CMSSW\_3\_6\_3 (was 3\_6\_1\_patch4 before).
  + control of transparency for collections and objects.
  + Fix placement of windows when restoring configuration (problem with determination of title-bar height).
  + prescale column to trigger table.
  + option to switch from scene-centric to viewer-centric controls in GL viewer. To switch from default, put the following line into your `~/.rootrc`:
     OpenGL.EventHandler.ViewerCentricControls: 1
* **2010-06-11:** `cmsShow36-beta-1` released
  + Update ROOT shipped in the tarball to avoid crashes due to missing dictionaries.
  + Update pflow.fwc to include PF MET.
* **2010-06-10:** `cmsShow36-beta` released

body:
If you are experiencing TWiki instability from outside the CERN network, please connect via the CERN internal network - see [KB0010688![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cern.service-now.com/service-portal?id=KB0010688) for details
