The [MiniAOD](/twiki/bin//CMS/MiniAOD) format was originally created in spring 2014, its format evolved, thanks to user feedback and in order to account new CMS reconstruction features, between the time of the original proposal and the starting of Run2.
In this heavy development period the across releases was not kept and users are expected to read a [MiniAOD](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/MiniAOD) sample with the same release that produced it or a newer bug fix release of the same series (i.e. only the last digit of the release number can be different).Documentation for the different versions of miniAOD are provided below as well as a table.
| [page](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookMiniAOD?sortcol=0;table=1;up=0#sorted_table "Sort by this column") | [Purpose](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookMiniAOD?sortcol=1;table=1;up=0#sorted_table "Sort by this column") | [CMSSW Release](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookMiniAOD?sortcol=2;table=1;up=0#sorted_table "Sort by this column") |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [WorkBookMiniAOD2017](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookMiniAOD2017) | 2017 Data & MC   2016 Data & MC re-miniAOD | 94X |
| [WorkBookMiniAOD2016](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookMiniAOD2016) | 2016 Data & MC (Moriond 2017 dataset) | 80X |
|  | 2015 Data & MC | 74X and 76X |
| [WorkBookMiniAOD2014](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookMiniAOD2014) | and CSA campaigns of 2014 | 72X and earlier |
## table
Note: this table lists only the main MC productions and data processings. Smaller productions or reprocessings used e.g. for release validation are not listed here
### 2017 and 2016 re-miniAOD (94X version 2 ![Processing](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/processing.gif "Processing"))
* Produced with CMSSW `9_4_5` or later; see below for global tags
* **Main changes with respect to 94X [MiniAOD](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/MiniAOD) v1** ([twiki with details](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin//CMS/94XMiniAODv2)):
  + JEC updates, as listed below depending on the specific dataset, MET significance update, and -weighted jet multiplicities
  + E/gamma 2017 v1 electron and photon IDs are precomputed and saved
     Energy calibration and smearing are precomputed and saved, but **not** applied to the 4-vector of the electron and photon objects.
     For a description of the new content, please read the [EgammaMiniAODV2](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin//CMS/EgammaMiniAODV2) twiki.
  + Added summary [DeepCSV](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/DeepCSV?topicparent=CMSPublic.WorkBookMiniAOD;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") discriminators (`pfDeepCSVDiscriminatorsJetTags:xxx` where xxx is `BvsAll`, `CvsB`, `CvsL`)
    Added Deep Flavour Tagging (`pfDeepFlavourJetTags:probxxx`, where xxx is `b`, `bb`, , `c`, `uds`, `g`)
  + Tau ID: updated training of the [MVArun2v1DBoldDMwLT](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/MVArun2v1DBoldDMwLT?topicparent=CMSPublic.WorkBookMiniAOD;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") series of discriminators (2017 v1)
  + Fixed access to L1 prescale values and hit-level dE/dx information for isolated tracks.
#### 2017 MC re-miniAOD 12Apr2018 (94X version 2 ![Processing](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/processing.gif "Processing"))
* DAS query: `[dataset=/*/RunIIFall17*12Apr2018*/MINIAODSIM![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cmsweb.cern.ch/das/request?=list&limit=50&instance=prod%2Fglobal&input=dataset+dataset%3D%2F*%2FRunIIFall17*12Apr2018*%2FMINIAODSIM+status%3D*)`
* Produced with CMSSW `9_4_6`; **Global tag**: `94X_mc2017_realistic_v14`, cmsDriver eras `Run2_2017,run2_miniAOD_94XFall17`
  + JECs used: Fall17\_17Nov2017\_V6\_MC
* **Recommended release**: `9_4_6_patch1` or later, **Global tag**: `94X_mc2017_realistic_v14`
#### 2017 Data re-miniAOD 31Mar2018 (94X version 2 ![Processing](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/processing.gif "Processing"))
* DAS query: `[dataset=/*/Run2017*31Mar2018*/MINIAOD![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cmsweb.cern.ch/das/request?=list&limit=50&instance=prod%2Fglobal&input=dataset+dataset%3D%2F*%2FRun2017*31Mar2018*%2FMINIAOD+status%3D*)`
* Produced with CMSSW `9_4_5`; **Global tag**: `94X_dataRun2_v6`, cmsDriver eras `Run2_2017,run2_miniAOD_94XFall17`
  + JECs used: Fall17\_17Nov2017BCDEF\_V6\_DATA
* **Recommended release**: `9_4_6_patch1` or later, **Global tag**: `94X_dataRun2_v6`
#### 2016 Data legacy re-miniAOD 17Jul2018 (94X version 2 ![NEW](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/new.gif "NEW") ![Processing](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/processing.gif "Processing"))
* DAS query: `[dataset=/*/Run2016*17Jul2018*/MINIAOD![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cmsweb.cern.ch/das/request?=list&limit=50&instance=prod%2Fglobal&input=dataset+dataset%3D%2F*%2FRun2016*17Jul2018*%2FMINIAOD+status%3D*)`
* Produced with CMSSW `9_4_9`; **Global tag**: `94X_dataRun2_v10`, cmsDriver eras `Run2_2016_HIPM,run2_miniAOD_80XLegacy` for B-F, `Run2_2016,eras.run2_miniAOD_80XLegacy` for G-H
* Note that the input AODs are from the 17Aug2017 re-reco of 2016 data with improved alignment and calibrations, not the 23Sep2016+PromptReco AODs which were used for the Moriond 2017 dataset
#### 2016 MC legacy re-miniAOD [RunIISummer16MiniAODv3](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/RunIISummer16MiniAODv3?topicparent=CMSPublic.WorkBookMiniAOD;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") (aka 94X version 2 ![NEW](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/new.gif "NEW") ![Processing](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/processing.gif "Processing"))
* DAS query: `[dataset=/*/RunIISummer16MiniAODv3*/MINIAODSIM![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cmsweb.cern.ch/das/request?=list&limit=50&instance=prod%2Fglobal&input=dataset+dataset%3D%2F*%2FRunIISummer16MiniAODv3*%2FMINIAODSIM+status%3D*)`
* Produced with CMSSW `9_4_9`; **Global tag**: `94X_mcRun2_asymptotic_v3`, cmsDriver eras `Run2_2016,run2_miniAOD_80XLegacy`
* Note that the input AODs are the same as used for the Moriond 2017 dataset, i.e. there has been no re-reconstruction of the MC. They are labelled [MiniAODv3](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/MiniAODv3?topicparent=CMSPublic.WorkBookMiniAOD;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") since the [MiniAODv2](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/MiniAODv2) was used for 80X version 2.
### 2016 MC for Moriond 2017 (80X)
#### Run2 Moriond17 re-digi-reco campaign (new 80X version 2 - CMSSW 8\_0\_21 or later)
* DAS query: `[dataset=/*/RunIISummer16MiniAODv2*PUMoriond17_80X_mcRun2_asymptotic_2016_TrancheIV_v6*/MINIAODSIM![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cmsweb.cern.ch/das/request?=list&limit=50&instance=prod%2Fglobal&input=dataset%3D%2F*%2FRunIISummer16MiniAODv2*PUMoriond17_80X_mcRun2_asymptotic_2016_TrancheIV_v6*%2FMINIAODSIM)`
* Produced with `8_0_21= or later; Global tag: =80X_mcRun2_asymptotic_2016_TrancheIV_v6-, cmsDriver era ==Run2_2016`
* **Recommended 80X release**: `8_0_25` or later, **Global tag**: `80X_mcRun2_asymptotic_2016_TrancheIV_v6`
* **Changes with respect to older 80X version (8\_0\_19 or earlier)** ([slides![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://indico.cern.ch/event/565391/contributions/2295305/attachments/1332245/2002682/gp-xpog-06Sep16.pdf):
  + b-tagging now uses a relaxed track selection that improves the performance in the presence of strip tracker dynamic inefficiencies.
  + Tau updates to allow re-running some IDs from MiniAOD [talk![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://indico.cern.ch/event/565391/contributions/2295302/attachments/1332235/2002666/TauPOG-2016-09-06-XPOG.pdf)
  + Several MET filters have been updated; MET and MET significance have been updated
  + Updated and BoostedDoubleSV tagger
  + PackedCandidates of pt > 0.95 now also store the number of tracker and pixel layers and not just the number of hits [code![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/pull/15641)
  + Instantaneous luminosity from the scales is now saved [code![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/blob/CMSSW_8_0_X/PhysicsTools/PatAlgos/python/slimming/MicroEventContent_cff.py#L67-L68)
  + Muon mothers have been added to the pruned (relevant only for muon-enriched QCD samples)
### 2016 Data for Moriond 2017 (80X)
#### Run2016 03Feb2017 Re-miniAOD (80X version 2 - CMSSW 8\_0\_26\_patch1 )
* DAS query: `[dataset=/*/Run2016*-03Feb2017-v*/MINIAOD![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cmsweb.cern.ch/das/request?=list&limit=50&instance=prod%2Fglobal&input=%2F*%2FRun2016*-03Feb2017-v*%2FMINIAOD)` [![Statistics](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/statistics.gif "Statistics")![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cms-pdmv.cern.ch/pmp/historical?r=03Feb2017)
  + Covers all 2016 data in the B-H eras.
  + For **Run2016B**, you will find 2 datasets called `Run2016B-03Feb2017_ver1` and `Run2016B-03Feb2017_ver2` ; these map to the RAW `Run2016B-v1` and `Run2016B-v2`
     **You can skip the ver1 dataset** as it does not contain any runs in the golden JSON.
  + For **Run2016H**, you will find two datasets called `Run2016H-03Feb2017_ver2` and `Run2016H-03Feb2017_ver3`; these map to the `PromptReco-v2` and `PromptReco-v3` AODs.
     **You should use both datasets**, as they do not overlap.
* Produced with: `8_0_26_patch1`; Global tag: `80X_dataRun2_2016SeptRepro_v7` (eras B-G) `80X_dataRun2_Prompt_v16` (era H); the global tags are an update the 23Sep20216 and [PromptReco](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/PromptReco?topicparent=CMSPublic.WorkBookMiniAOD;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") ones to includes the **23Sep20216 V3 JECs** on top .
* Recommended 80X releases `8_0_25` or later; Global tag: `80X_dataRun2_2016SeptRepro_v7` (eras B-G) `80X_dataRun2_Prompt_v16` (era H)
* Re-miniAOD to address issues found in 23Sep2016 re-reco. See [PPD Talk![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://indico.cern.ch/event/602633/contributions/2462363/attachments/1406424/2149060/gp-reminiAOD-020217.pdf) and **detailed documentation in [ReMiniAOD03Feb2017Notes](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/ReMiniAOD03Feb2017Notes) twiki**
#### Run2016 23Sep2016 of eras B-G (80X version 2 - CMSSW 8\_0\_20 or later )
* DAS query: `[dataset=/*/Run2016*-23Sep2016-v*/MINIAOD![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cmsweb.cern.ch/das/request?=list&limit=50&instance=prod%2Fglobal&input=%2F*%2FRun2016*-23Sep2016-v*%2FMINIAOD)` [![Statistics](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/statistics.gif "Statistics")![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cms-pdmv.cern.ch/pmp/historical?r=23Sep2016)
  + This covers all the 80X version 2 prompt-reco data, and has no overlap with the 80X version 3 prompt-reco (Run H v2 and v3). For **Run2016B**, be sure to use the `v3` of the datasets, not the older `v1` or `v2`.
* Produced with: `8_0_20`; Global tag: `80X_dataRun2_2016SeptRepro_v4` for [Run2016B](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/Run2016B?topicparent=CMSPublic.WorkBookMiniAOD;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it."), `80X_dataRun2_2016SeptRepro_v3` for all the others.
* Recommended 80X releases `8_0_25` or later; Global tag: `80X_dataRun2_2016SeptRepro_v4` (note: does not yet include the final JECs for this )
* **Known features** of miniAOD, in addition to any other possible issue affecting the detector or the reconstruction:
  + prescale values are not correct, check with [WBM![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cmswbm.web.cern.ch/cmswbm/cmsdb/servlet/RunSummary) if you are using them for any purpose.
    The prescale column can be retrieved as documented under [WorkBookMiniAOD2016#](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookMiniAOD2016)
#### , eras H-v2 and later (new 80X version 2 - CMSSW 8\_0\_20 or later)
* DAS query: `[dataset=/*/Run2016H-PromptReco-v*/MINIAOD![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cmsweb.cern.ch/das/request?=list&limit=50&instance=prod%2Fglobal&input=%2F*%2F*Run2016H-PromptReco-v*%2FMINIAOD)` **starting from v2**.
  The [Run2016H](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/Run2016H?topicparent=CMSPublic.WorkBookMiniAOD;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.")-PromptReco-v1 datasets still have the 80X v2 miniAOD, but they don't contain any stable beam collisions, so they can be ignored.
* Produced with: `8_0_20` or later; Global tag: `80X_dataRun2_Prompt_v14` or later,
* Recommended 80X releases `8_0_25` or later; Global tag: `80X_dataRun2_Prompt_v14` or later
* **for 2016 data analysis for summer conferences**: [POGRecipesICHEP2016 twiki](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin/viewauth/CMS/POGRecipesICHEP2016)
* **Known features** of miniAOD, in addition to any other possible issue affecting the detector or the reconstruction: \* prescale values are not correct, check with [WBM![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cmswbm.web.cern.ch/cmswbm/cmsdb/servlet/RunSummary) if you are using them for any purpose.
  The prescale column can be retrieved as documented under [WorkBookMiniAOD2016#](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookMiniAOD2016)
### 2015 MC
#### Run2 Fall15 [MiniAOD](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/MiniAOD) v2 campaign (76X version 2)

* DAS query: `[dataset=/*/RunIISpring16MiniAODv2*reHLT*/*![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cmsweb.cern.ch/das/request?=list&limit=50&instance=prod%2Fglobal&input=%2F*%2F*RunIISpring16MiniAODv2*reHLT*%2F*)`

# 5.8 Job Monitoring with
Complete: ![5](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/pub/CMS/WebPreferences/complete5.png)
[Detailed Review Status](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookMonitoringTutorial#ReviewStatus)
## Contents
* [provides a web interface for Job Monitoring](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookMonitoringTutorial#WebInterface)
* [How to follow the progress of your tasks](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookMonitoringTutorial#FollowProgress)
* [If you see any discrepancy between information in the and the output of the Crab status command](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookMonitoringTutorial#DisCrepancy)
* [Using](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookMonitoringTutorial#DashInterface)
## provides a web interface for Job Monitoring
Most of the CMS Job Submission Systems, including CRAB and PA, are instrumented to send monitoring information
to the . In addition to reports of the CMS Job Submission Systems, collects information from the Monitoring systems.
Monitoring data is stored in the central database and there is a web interface running on top of it and allowing CMS users to follow the progress of their jobs.
For the monitoring you do not need to setup any environment. The only thing you need is a web browser.
In case you see a problem, please submit a bug in savannah:
[https://savannah.cern.ch/projects/![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://savannah.cern.ch/projects/) mail to
## How to follow the progress of your tasks
* After submission of your task to the CRAB server you get back the task monitoring link, which you can follow in order to get information about progress of your task.
* If you want to find information about multiple tasks submitted during a particular time range you can enter the application via the entry task monitoring page:
[http://dashb-cms-job-task.cern.ch//request.py/taskmonitoring![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://dashb-cms-job-task.cern.ch//request.py/taskmonitoring)
* Choose your identiy in the "Select a User" window and the time window to define the tasks submitted during a given time range. You should get at the screen the list of all your tasks submitted over the time range you have chosen.
As a rule, on the UI, user identity is defined by user name and family name. But it is not always the case. User identity is retrieved from the certificate subject and depends on it's format.
To check your user identifier, go to the interactive job monitoring page:[http://dashb-cms-job.cern.ch//request.py/jobsummary![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://dashb-cms-job.cern.ch//request.py/jobsummary)Click on the bar with the 'analysis' label and sort by user. Looking on the user names listed next to the bars or in the table below, you will find out your identifier. At the task monitoring page you see the list of all your tasks with the distribution of jobs by their current status.You can bookmark the link to task monitoring application containing information only about your tasks:
[http://dashb-cms-job-task.cern.ch//request.py
/taskmonitoring#action=tasksTable&usergridname=USERNAME](http://dashb-cms-job-task.cern.ch//request.py/taskmonitoring#action=tasksTable&usergridname=USERNAME)where USERNAME is your identifierYou can also bookmark the link to a particular task:
[http://dashb-cms-job-task.cern.ch//request.py/
taskmonitoring#action=taskJobs&usergridname=USERNAME&taskmonid=TASKMONITORID](http://dashb-cms-job-task.cern.ch//request.py/taskmonitoring#action=taskJobs&usergridname=USERNAME&taskmonid=TASKMONITORID)where TASKMONITORID is project name in CRAB.
* The front page shows the overview of all tasks submitted during the selected time range (3 days by default) in table and graphical form.
Every page is reloaded every few minutes providing the most up-to-date information.
* Clicking on the information icon next to the task name you get the **meta information** of a particular task, like name of the input dataset, CMSSW version to be used, time stamp when task had been registered in the .
* Clicking on the number of jobs corresponding to a given status gives you a detailed information of all jobs of a chosen category: job id, identifier of the job inside the task, how many times the job had been resubmitted, site where job is processed, time stamps of the job processing (UTC).
* In case when the job was **resubmitted multiple times**, clicking at the number at the "Submission Attempts" column allows you to see all resubmissions corresponding to a given job inside the task. Here we are referring not to the resubmissions triggered by resource broker, but to resubmissions done by the user.
* The application provides various graphs showing distribution of jobs by site, time, failure reason, and graphs showing time consumed by the task, the graph showing progress of the task in terms of processed events. Th plots either generated by default on a appropriate page or can be selected clicking on the "Plot Selection" link in the table. Graphs can be zoomed-in and zoomed-out.
* Jobs listed in the **"Successful"** category are those which had accomplished properly from the application point of and for which did not get evidence that the job had been aborted by the .
* The jobs listed as **"Failed"** are those which either failed from the application point of or had been aborted by the or cancelled by the user/crab\_server. By failure from the application point of we mean non 0 status from the CMS application or problems related to the saving of the output files at the storage element, or problems while sourcing of the CMS environment at the site. To discover the **reason of failure** of the particular job, click on the number of jobs in the "Failed" category, you get the list of all failed jobs with the status and application exit code. Moving cursor at the status value you get more detailed reason of failure.
* Please, pay attention, for back navigation between the task monitoring pages do not use "back" button in the browser, use buttons provided on the task monitoring pages.
* On the task page showing the overview of all jobs belonging to a task next to the task name you see the small logo icon. Clicking on it you get the **bar plot** of distribution of jobs of the task by a chosen attribute, like site, computing element or resource broker. Sometimes this distribution can help you to find the problem of a given site, CE or resource broker and can allow you to exclude the problematic service or site when you resubmit your jobs. See more details in the section "Using ".
## If you see any discrepancy between information in the and the output of the Crab status command
Sometime you can notice the discrepancy of the information in the and the Crab status command.
* does not have user credentials and can not directly query and Bookkeeping system to get status about a particular job. It relies on the job status reports sent to the either from the jobs themselves or job status information of the monitoring systems like RGMA or ICRTM. That is why if you see non-consistent data in Crab and related to the status of a given job, you should believe Crab.
* On the other hand gets real time information about jobs which is reported to the from the jobs running at the worker nodes. So when you see that according to the the job had terminated while Crab still considers the job to be running, it means that the job had already finished on the worker node and sent it's exit status, while and Bookkeeping system did not yet update the job status. If you see that a delay in update of crab status for the job which had terminated according to takes too long (more than half a hour), the problem can be related to the services.
* For some sites, e.g. , nothing is reported to until the job is done.
You can follow the [CRAB3 Troubleshooting guide](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/CRAB3Troubleshoot) for more on how to troubleshoot your job and contact crab support.
## Using
One of the purposes of the is to show the correlations of the job failures or inefficiencies in processing (pending too long in the queue for example) with a particular site or service like Resource Broker.When you see that all jobs of a particular task are failing and it is not clear to you whether it is a problem of your code or the problem related to the site misconfiguration, can help you to find it out.
* First thing you can check is whether jobs of other users are failing at the same site with the same failure code. Go to:
<http://dashb-cms-job.cern.ch//request.py/jobsummary>By default on the interactive user interface you see all jobs submitted during the selected time window. If you tick the checkbox 'terminated' then you would see all jobs which are currently either in pending or running status or those which had been terminated from the date selected as the beginning of the time range to now regardless the time when the jobs had been submitted. Be aware that all dates in including UI are UTC.
You can sort the jobs by user, site, computing element, resource broker, application, task. Clicking at any bar of the plot would allow you to sort the subset of jobs shown in a particular bar by various attributes. Clicking at any number in the table would allow you to get detailed information about the selected subset of jobs, like processing time stamps, exit code of application, job id etc...
If you sort your jobs by task and then click on a particular task name in the table, the task monitoring page for this task would be opened.
* Trying to understand the reason of the failures
Click on the bar with the 'analysis' label and sort by site. Dark green colour corresponds to the jobs which finsihed properly, pink one corresponds to the jobs which were properly handled by the , but failed from the application point of . Red colour corresponds to the jobs aborted by the . Clicking on the number corresponding to the failed or aborted jobs in the table below gives you the list of all failed or aborted jobs with their failure reason.
* Example:
Looking at the plot provided via link below you can see that there are no jobs which succeeded in Taipei<https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/pub/CMSPublic/WorkBookMonitoringTutorial/tut0.pdf>Let's sort Taipei jobs by user<https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/pub/CMSPublic/WorkBookMonitoringTutorial/Tut1.pdf>You see that there were several users running their jobs at the site and nobody managed to run the jobs properly.
Clicking on the number of the failed jobs in the table we get the detailed of the failed jobs with application exit code 8000, which very often indicates the data access problems (**beware** those images are from some time ago with older CMSSW releases, now failure to open file gives exit code=8020). So failures of the jobs could be related to the site misconfiguration rather than to a problem in the user code. If the problematic site does not represent the only location of data required by your task you can put the site in the black list (**ce\_black\_list=Site\_Name**) of the Crab configuration file and resubmit the task. If you feel you have to do this black listing, also contact the crab support team, more information at the [CRAB3 Troubleshooting page](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/CRAB3Troubleshoot).

# 4.1.1 More on CMSSW Framework
Complete: ![5](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/pub/CMS/WebPreferences/complete5.png)
[Detailed Review Status](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookMoreOnCMSSWFramework#ReviewStatus)
## Contents
|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| * [Goals of this page](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookMoreOnCMSSWFramework#GoAls) * [/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookMoreOnCMSSWFramework#InTro)   + [Modular Event Content](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookMoreOnCMSSWFramework#ComponentArch)   + [Identifying Data in the Event](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookMoreOnCMSSWFramework#IdentifyData)   + [Getting Data from the Event](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookMoreOnCMSSWFramework#GetData)   + [Sample EDAnalyzer Code](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookMoreOnCMSSWFramework#SampleCode) | * [The Processing Model](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookMoreOnCMSSWFramework#ProcModel) * [Framework Services](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookMoreOnCMSSWFramework#FrameWork)   + [ServiceRegistry System](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookMoreOnCMSSWFramework#ServiceRegistry) * [Provenance Tracking](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookMoreOnCMSSWFramework#ProvenanceTrackingLink) * [Review Status](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookMoreOnCMSSWFramework#ReviewStatus) |
## Goals of this page
When you finish this page, you should understand:
* the modular architecture of the CMSSW framework and the Event Data Model ([EDM](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/EDM))
* how data are uniquely identified in an Event
* how Event data are processed - AOD and miniAOD structures
* the Framework Services, including the EventSetup
## Introduction
The overall collection of software, referred to as CMSSW, is built around a Framework, an Event Data Model (EDM), and Services needed by the simulation, calibration and alignment, and reconstruction modules that process event data so that physicists can perform analysis. The primary goal of the Framework and [EDM](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/EDM) is to facilitate the development and deployment of reconstruction and analysis software.
### Modular Event Content
It is important to emphasize that the event data architecture is modular, just as the framework. Different data layers (using different [data formats](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookDataFormats)) can be configured, and a given application can use any layer or layers. The branches (which map one to one with event data objects) can be loaded or dropped on demand by the application. The following diagram illustrates this concept:
![](/twiki/pub/CMSPublic/WorkBookMoreOnCMSSWFramework/)
You can reprocess event data at virtually any stage. For instance, if the available AOD doesn't contain exactly what you want, you might want to reprocess the RECO (e.g., to apply a new calibration) to produce the desired AOD.
![reprocess.gif](/twiki/pub/CMSPublic/WorkBookMoreOnCMSSWFramework/reprocess.gif)
Custom quantities (data produced by a user or analysis group) can be added to an event and associated with existing objects at any processing stage (RECO/AOD -> candidates -> user data). Thus the distinction between "CMS data" and "user data" may change during the lifetime of the experiment.
![user_data_in_event.gif](/twiki/pub/CMSPublic/WorkBookMoreOnCMSSWFramework/user_data_in_event.gif)
### Identifying Data in the Event
Data within the Event are uniquely identified by four quantities:
**C++ class type of the data**
:   E.g., edm::PSimHitContainer or reco::TrackCollection.
**module label**
:   the label that was assigned to the module that created the data. E.g., "SimG4Objects" or "TrackProducer".
**product instance label**
:   the label assigned to object from within the module (defaults to an empty string). This is convenient if many of the same type of C++ objects are being put into the edm::Event from within a single module.
**process name**
:   the process name as set in the job that created the data
For example if you do (you can find the file MYCOPY.ROOT [here![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cms-service-sdtweb.web.cern.ch/cms-service-sdtweb/validation/physicstools/PATVALIDATION/MYCOPY.root)) :
```
edmDumpEventContent MYCOPY.root
```
you get this output:
```
vector<reco::TrackExtra>          "electronGsfTracks"     ""            "RECO."
vector<reco::TrackExtra>          "generalTracks"         ""            "RECO."
vector<reco::TrackExtra>          "globalMuons"           ""            "RECO."
vector<reco::TrackExtra>          "globalSETMuons"        ""            "RECO."
vector<reco::TrackExtra>          "pixelTracks"           ""            "RECO."
vector<reco::TrackExtra>          "standAloneMuons"       ""            "RECO."
vector<reco::TrackExtra>          "standAloneSETMuons"    ""            "RECO."
vector<reco::TrackExtra>          "tevMuons"              "default"     "RECO."
vector<reco::TrackExtra>          "tevMuons"              "firstHit"    "RECO."
vector<reco::TrackExtra>          "tevMuons"              "picky"       "RECO."
```
In the above output:`vector<reco::TrackExtra>` is the C++ class type of the data`globalMuons"` is the module label`firstHit` is the product instance label`RECO` is the process name
### Getting data from the Event
There is a simple example of how to get data in an EDProducer [here](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookEDMTutorialProducer#BooK). One gets data in the same way in an EDAnalyzer. An EDAnalyzer cannot put or emplace data, but the various types of get\* functions are the same in EDAnalyzers, EDProducers, and EDFilters.There is a thorough description of how to get data from the Event [here](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideEDMGetDataFromEvent).
## The Processing Model
Events are processed by passing the Event through a sequence of modules. The exact sequence of modules is specified by the user via a `path` statement in a configuration file. A `path` is an ordered list of Producer/Filter/Analyzer modules which sets the exact execution order of all the modules. When an Event is passed to a module, that module can get data from the Event and put data back into the Event. When data is put into the Event, the provenance information about the module that created the data will be stored with the data in the Event. The components involved in the framework and [EDM](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/EDM) are shown here:
![fw_edm.gif](/twiki/pub/CMSPublic/WorkBookMoreOnCMSSWFramework/fw_edm.gif)The Standard Input Source shown above uses a ROOT I/O. The Event is then passed to the execution paths. The paths can then be ordered into a list that makes up the schedule for the process. Note that the same module may appear in multiple paths, but the framework will guarantee that a module is only executed once per Event. Since it will ask for exactly the same products from the event and produce the same result independent of which path it is in, it makes no sense to execute it twice. On the other hand a user designing a trigger path should not have to worry about the full schedule (that could involve 100's of modules). Each path should be executable by itself, in that modules within the path, only ask for things they know have been produced in a previous module in the same path or from the input source. In a perfect world, order of execution of the paths should not matter. However due to the existence of bugs it is always possible that there is an order dependence. Such dependencies should be removed during validation of the job.
## Framework Services
### ServiceRegistry System
The ServiceRegistry is used to deliver services such as the error logger or a debugging service which provides feedback
about the state of the Framework (e.g., what module is presently running). Services are informed about the present state of the Framework, e.g., the start of a new Event or the completion of a certain module. Such information is useful for producing meaningful error messages from the error logger or for debugging. The services to be used in a job and the exact configuration of those services are set in the user's configuration file via a ParameterSet. For further information look [here](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin//CMS/SWGuideFrameWork#EventSetup_and_Services).
###
To be able to fully process an event, one has to take into account potentially changing and periodically updated information about the detector environment and status. This information (non-event data) is not tied to a given event, but rather to the time period for which it is valid. This time period is called its *interval of validity* or IOV, and an IOV typically spans many events. Examples of this type of non-event data include calibrations, alignments, geometry descriptions, magnetic field and conditions recorded during data acquisition. The IOV of one piece of non-event data is not necessarily related to that of another. The EventSetup system handles this type of non-event data for which the IOV is longer than one Event. (Note that non-Event data initiated by the DAQ, such as the Event or a transition, are handled by the Event system.)The figure illustrates the varying IOVs of different non-event data (calibrations and alignments), and how their values at the time of a given event are read by the EventSetup system.
![ from  presentation](/twiki/pub/CMSPublic/WorkBookMoreOnCMSSWFramework/event_setup.gif)The EventSetup system design uses two categories
of modules to do its work: *ESSource* and *ESProducer*. These components are
configured using the same configuration mechanism as their Event counterparts, i.e., via a
ParameterSet.
ESSource
:   is responsible for determining the IOV of a Record (or a set of Records). (A Record is an EventSetup construct that holds data and services which have identical IOVs.) The ESSource may also deliver data/services. For example, a user can request the ECAL pedestals via an ESSource that reads the appropriate values from a database.
ESProducer
:   an ESProducer is, conceptually, an algorithm whose inputs are dependent on data with IOVs. The ESProducer's algorithm is whenever there is an IOV change for the Record to which the ESProducer is bound. For example, an ESProducer is used to read the ideal geometry of the tracker as well as the alignment corrections and then create the aligned tracker geometry from those 2 pieces of information. This ESProducer is told by the EventSetup system to create a new aligned tracker geometry whenever the alignment changes.
For further information look [here](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin//CMS/SWGuideEventSetupHowTos).
## Provenance Tracking
The CMS Offline framework stores provenance information within CMS's standard ROOT event data files. The provenance information is used to track how every data product was constructed including what other data products were read in order to do the construction. We record information to understand the history of how data were produced and chosen. Provenance information does not have to be sufficient to allow an exact replay of a process. Storing provenance in output files is very crucial to insure trust in the data, given the large scale, highly distributed nature of production, especially for physicists' personal skims which are not centrally managed. Using Provenance information one can track the source of a problem seen in one file but not another one, guarantee compatibility when reading multiple files in a job, confirm that an analysis was done using the proper data, track why two analyses get different results etc. A good source of info is a [talk![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://indico.cern.ch/getFile.py/access?contribId=55&sessionId=59&resId=0&materialId=slides&confId=35523) by at given at CEHP09. Also refer to [WorkBook 2.3](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin//CMS/WorkBookCMSSWFramework#ProvenanceTrackingLink). Also see [http://iopscience.iop.org/1742-6596/219/3/032011](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/FileLevelProvenanceTrackingInCMS).

## Goals of this page
This document explains how to get access to tracks and associated information available in the event record, which can be used for identification purposes as well as analyses. Brief summary of reconstruction algorithms and of selectors is provided. (See [WorkBookSetComputerNode](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookSetComputerNode) for instructions on how to set up a proper CMSSW computing environment.)Nota bene: There are three formats that one might use for performing an analysis: [miniAOD](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookMiniAOD) (a high-level data tier containing high level physics objects (leptons, photons, jets, ETmiss), with detailed information for retuning of identification criteria, a full list of particles reconstructed by the ParticleFlow, MC truth and the trigger informations),  (a flat tree containing only the final and most general information) and AOD (similar to miniAOD but containing much more raw level information in order to allow analyzers to perform some of the reconstruction steps by themselves). Looking first at miniAOD will give you good knowledge and will allow you to be more flexible in case you want to design your own selection in the future. We will access information in miniAOD files. Please, check the information stored in the [miniAOD](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookMiniAOD2017#Muons). This link [here](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin/viewauth/CMS/MuonHATSatLPC2017#Exercise_1_Getting_familiar_with) could also be very useful to get familiar with muons in the miniAOD.
## Introduction to reconstruction
reconstruction overview:![muonreco.png](/twiki/pub/CMSPublic/WorkBookMuonAnalysis/muonreco.png)The reconstruction chain starts with the "local reconstruction". First, hits in DTs, CSCs and RPCs are reconstructed from digitized electronics signals. Hits within each DT and CSC chamber are then matched to form "segments" (track stubs). The production of hits and segments in sub-systems is discussed in detail in the [tutorial on local reconstruction](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideMuonLocalReco). The reconstruction of the tracks inside the silicon  is described in the [tutorial on track reconstruction](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookTrackAnalysis). A good description of CMS detection, reconstruction, and identification is presented in this [talk](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/pub/CMS/SWGuideCMSDataAnalysisSchoolPisa2019MuonsExercise/Muons_CMSDAS_Pisa_v1.pdf).
### Standalone muons
In the offline reconstruction, the segments reconstructed in the chambers are used to generate "seeds" consisting of position and direction vectors and an estimate of the transverse momentum. These initial estimates are used as seeds for the track fits in the system, which are performed using segments and hits from DTs, CSCs and RPCs and are based on the Kalman filter technique. The result is a collection of [reco::Track![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmsdoxygen.web.cern.ch/cmsdoxygen/CMSSW_9_2_3/doc/html/dd/d5b/classreco_1_1Track.html) objects reconstructed in the spectrometer, which are referred to as **"standalone muons"**. To improve the momentum resolution, a beam-spot constraint can be applied in the fit. Two collections of "standalone muons", with and without the beam-spot constraint, are available in the event record (in both RECO and AOD). A more detailed description of the reconstruction of tracks in the system alone can be found in Section 4 of  [CMS AN 2008/097![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cms.cern.ch/iCMS/jsp/db_notes/noteInfo.jsp?cmsnoteid=CMS%20AN-2008/097).
A tutorial explaining how to run standalone reconstruction and to analyze its results is available at [this link](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideStandAloneMuonReco).
### Global muons
For each standalone track, a search for tracks matching it among those reconstructed in the inner tracking system (referred to as **" tracks"**, **"inner tracks"** or **"silicon tracks"**) is performed, and the best-matching  track is selected. For each " track" - "standalone " pair, the track fit using all hits in both tracks is performed, again based on the Kalman filter technique. The result is a collection of [reco::Track![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmsdoxygen.web.cern.ch/cmsdoxygen/CMSSW_9_2_3/doc/html/dd/d5b/classreco_1_1Track.html) objects referred to as **"global muons"**. More details on the reconstruction of global muons can be found in Section 5 of  [CMS AN 2008/097![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cms.cern.ch/iCMS/jsp/db_notes/noteInfo.jsp?cmsnoteid=CMS%20AN-2008/097).References to the matching  tracks, standalone tracks, and global tracks are assembled into one single collection of [reco::![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/blob/master/DataFormats/MuonReco/interface/.h) objects described [below](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookMuonAnalysis#RecoMuon).
###  muons
An approach complementary to the global- reconstruction consists in considering all  tracks to be potential candidates and in checking this hypothesis by looking for compatible signatures in the calorimeters and in the system.  tracks identified as muons by this method are referred to as **" muons"**. A detailed description of the reconstruction of  muons can be found in Section 6 of  [CMS AN 2008/097![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cms.cern.ch/iCMS/jsp/db_notes/noteInfo.jsp?cmsnoteid=CMS%20AN-2008/097).The - algorithm is particularly useful for the identification of low-pT muons (with pT of the order of several ), which may not leave enough hits in the stations for a standalone to be reconstructed. The default criteria for tagging a  track as " " are very loose (in CMSSW\_3\_X\_Y series, every track with p > 2.5 and pT > 0.5 matched with at least one segment in the stations is labeled as " "), so  muons should in general not be used without further requirements. Several sets of such requirements recommended by the POG are described in Sections 6-8 of  [CMS AN 2008/098![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cms.cern.ch/iCMS/jsp/db_notes/noteInfo.jsp?cmsnoteid=CMS%20AN-2008/098); the corresponding flags can be retrieved from the [reco::![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/blob/master/DataFormats/MuonReco/interface/.h) object (see [WorkBook section on ID](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookMuonAnalysis#MuonId)).
#RPCMu
### RPC muons
An approach similar to  Muons is followed to define the RPC Muons: in this case a match is sought between the extrapolated inner track and hits on the RPC detectors.
A description of the algorithm and the performance measurements is contained in the  [CMS AN-2012/482 ![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cms.cern.ch/iCMS/jsp/db_notes/noteInfo.jsp?cmsnoteid=CMS%20AN-2012/482).
The effects of including the RPC hits in the global reconstruction have also been studied and are described in  [rel="nofollow" M.S.Kim, JINST 8 (2013) T03001](http://iopscience.iop.org/1748-0221/8/03/T03001/).
The main twiki page documenting the RPC algorithm is linked  [HERE](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin/viewauth/CMS/RPCMuon) .
### Calorimeter-based muons
Calorimeter-based muons, or **"calo muons"** for short, represent a subset of all  tracks reconstructed in the event, which includes tracks with energy depositions in the calorimeters compatible with those of a minimum-ionizing particle. The fake rate of these candidates is high and they should not be used when purity is essential. A typical use case for "calo muons" is the reconstruction of the J/ψ decaying to low-momentum muons that have little or no information in the system, thus improving signal to background ratio compared with the inner tracks. In the event record, "calo muons" are stored in a collection of dedicated objects, [reco::CaloMuon![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/blob/master/DataFormats/MuonReco/interface/CaloMuon.h)'s.
## Available information
**The information on various types of muons discussed above is assembled in one single collection of [reco::![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/blob/master/DataFormats/MuonReco/interface/.h) objects, "muons". This collection serves as the main entry point for accessing -related information in CMSSW: various quantities are either directly included in the reco:: objects, or can be accessed from there via provided references.** One exception to this rule is "calo muons", which are stored in a separate collection of [reco::CaloMuon![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/blob/master/DataFormats/MuonReco/interface/CaloMuon.h) objects. **The full list of collections available in the event record is available in [SWGuideDataFormatRecoMuon](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideDataFormatRecoMuon).**
### reco::
Full description of the reco:: class can be found here: [DataFormats/MuonReco/interface/.h![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/blob/master/DataFormats/MuonReco/interface/.h).Brief summary of available information:
* Methods to check to which category of candidates a given reco:: object belongs: `isStandAloneMuon(), isGlobalMuon(), isTrackerMuon()` (`isCaloMuon()` is currently not used). *Note that a single object can belong to more than one category.*
* References to the corresponding reco::Track objects for tracks reconstructed in the inner  ( track), system alone (standalone track with a beam-spot constraint), and to a combined - fit (global track). High-pT muons can be accessed through `isHighPtMuon`.
* For  muons:
  + Energy depositions in ECAL, HCAL and HO in crossed elements as well as 3x3 shapes around them.
  + Compatibility with hypothesis based on energy depositions in calorimeters.
  + Vector of segments matched with the extrapolated  track and some other track-segments matching information.
* Summary of isolation information: sums of pT/ET and numbers of tracks and jets for two cones of dR = √(dφ^2 + dη^2) = 0.3 and 0.5 around the trajectory (see [below](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookMuonAnalysis#MuonIs)).
* Identification flags (see [below](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookMuonAnalysis#MuonId)).
* Timing information (see [below](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookMuonAnalysis#TimingInfo)).
### reco:: timing information
Timing information is calculated from information in the DT, CSC and ECAL (RPC timing information is not available for offline at all; efforts to implement HCAL timing are currently under way). Information is stored in [reco::MuonTime![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/blob/master/DataFormats/MuonReco/interface/MuonTime.h) format. It contains a summary of the combined fit of all subdetector data with two estimates of time at the interaction point and its error, assuming an outside-in or inside-out β=1 particle, plus an estimate of the 's direction.More detailed information about timing (time, velocity with and without the assumption of the being produced in-time, etc.) separated into subsystems is available in a set external products of type [reco::MuonTimeExtra![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/blob/master/DataFormats/MuonReco/interface/MuonTimeExtra.h) linked to the muons via association maps. If necessary, these objects can be regenerated independent of the reconstruction chain using the [MuonTimingProducer![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/blob/master/RecoMuon/MuonIdentification/plugins/MuonTimingProducer.cc).For a simple example of accessing all the information, please take a look at MuonTimingValidator.cc in [here![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/blob/master/RecoMuon/MuonIdentification/test/MuonTimingValidator.cc). For more details on the interpretation of the different quantities and performance in early data, see [CMS IN-2010/003![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cms.cern.ch/iCMS/jsp/openfile.jsp?type=IN&year=2010&files=IN2010_013.pdf).
## identification
Detailed information about identification and the various selection algorithms can be found in the [CMS AN-2008/098![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cms.cern.ch/iCMS/jsp/openfile.jsp?tp=draft&files=AN2008_098_v1.pdf) analysis note. There is a detailed accounting of changes made to the --based identification algorithms since AN-2008/098 (over 1.5 years ago as of this writing) at [SWGuideTrackerMuons](/twiki/bin//CMS/SWGuideTrackerMuons#Changes_with_respect_to_the_abov). Below is a brief summary.There are several categories of identification algorithms that have been developed:
* Cut-based ID for global muons, which consists of a set of track-quality requirements
* Likelihood-based ID for  muons, which uses compatibility of the calorimeter response with the hypothesis and the presence of matched segments in the system
* Cut-based ID for  muons, which selects muons on the basis of the track-penetration depth in the detector
The id selection function and selection types exist outside of the reco:: object. This means that one should use an external function
```
bool ::isGoodMuon( const reco::& , ::SelectionType type )
```
which returns true if the passes the given selection type. The following selection types are available:
```
namespace  {
enum SelectionType {
All = 0,                      // dummy options - always true
AllGlobalMuons = 1,           // checks isGlobalMuon flag
AllStandAloneMuons = 2,       // checks isStandAloneMuon flag
AllTrackerMuons = 3,          // checks isTrackerMuon flag
TrackerMuonArbitrated = 4,    // resolve ambiguity of sharing segments
AllArbitrated = 5,            // all muons with the   arbitrated
GlobalMuonPromptTight = 6,    // global muons with tighter fit requirements
TMLastStationLoose = 7,       // penetration depth loose selector
TMLastStationTight = 8,       // penetration depth tight selector
TM2DCompatibilityLoose = 9,   // likelihood based loose selector
TM2DCompatibilityTight = 10,  // likelihood based tight selector
TMOneStationLoose = 11,       // require one well matched segment
TMOneStationTight = 12,       // require one well matched segment
TMLastStationOptimizedLowPtLoose = 13, // combination of TMLastStation and TMOneStation
TMLastStationOptimizedLowPtTight = 14, // combination of TMLastStation and TMOneStation
GMTkChiCompatibility = 15,    // require tk stub have good chi2 relative to glb track
GMStaChiCompatibility = 16,   // require sta stub have good chi2 compatibility relative to glb track
GMTkKinkTight = 17,           // require a small kink value in the  stub
TMLastStationAngLoose = 18,   // TMLastStationLoose with additional angular cuts
TMLastStationAngTight = 19,   // TMLastStationTight with additional angular cuts
TMOneStationAngLoose = 20,    // TMOneStationLoose with additional angular cuts
TMOneStationAngTight = 21,    // TMOneStationTight with additional angular cuts
TMLastStationOptimizedBarrelLowPtLoose = 22, // combination of TMLastStation and TMOneStation with low pT optimization in barrel only
TMLastStationOptimizedBarrelLowPtTight = 23  // combination of TMLastStation and TMOneStation with low pT optimization in barrel only
};
}
```
The `isGoodMuon` method and the available selection types are defined in [DataFormats/MuonReco/interface/MuonSelectors.h![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/blob/master/DataFormats/MuonReco/interface/MuonSelectors.h), so one must include this header file to utilize the selectors.**The -identification algorithms recommended by the POG can be found in [SWGuideMuonId](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideMuonId)**. - selectors (`TMLastStationLoose`, etc.) are described in [SWGuideTrackerMuons](/twiki/bin//CMS/SWGuideTrackerMuons). `GlobalMuonPromptTight` consists of the following requirements, designed to suppress hadronic punch-throughs and muons from decays in flight:
```
() && .globalTrack()->normalizedChi2() < 10. && .globalTrack()->hitPattern().numberOfValidMuonHits() > 0
```
that is:
* the track is identified as a global
* χ2/ndof of the global fit < 10
* number of valid -detector hits used in the global fit > 0
The following additional track-quality cuts using the -track information are recommended to further suppress non-prompt muons, although they are not explicitly included in the selection types above:
* Transverse impact parameter of the  track (or global ) relative to the beam spot position, |d0|, < 2 mm. This loose cut preserves efficiency for muons from decays of b and c hadrons.
* Number of hits in the  track, Nhits, > 10.
One can also impose cuts on the last point in the global fit to reject punch-throughs that terminate in the first station of the detector:
```
// barrel region
if ( ) < 660 && r > 400 && r < 480)  keepMuon = false;
// endcap region
if ( ) > 600 && ) < 650 && r < 300)  keepMuon = false;
if ( ) > 680 && ) < 730 && r < 480)  keepMuon = false;
```
This can reduce the fake rate by ~20% with minimal loss in efficiency.
More information can be found in  [CMS AN 2008/098![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cms.cern.ch/iCMS/jsp/db_notes/noteInfo.jsp?cmsnoteid=CMS%20AN-2008/098), in [SWGuideTrackerMuons](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideTrackerMuons), and in several dedicated talks: ["Muons in CMSSW\_2\_1\_X"![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://indico.cern.ch/getFile.py/access?contribId=6&resId=1&materialId=slides&confId=33471), ["Global Selections"![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://indico.cern.ch/getFile.py/access?contribId=3&resId=1&materialId=slides&confId=40770) and ["Summary of the ID Note"![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://indico.cern.ch/getFile.py/access?contribId=4&resId=0&materialId=slides&confId=46065).The -identification criteria used by the Vector-Boson Task Force of the Electroweak PAG follow closely -POG recommendations and can be found [here](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/EWKVBTF#Baseline_selections).
## isolation
For each candidate, a number of quantities is computed that can help to distinguish isolated muons from the muons embedded in jets. The following data can be obtained directly from the reco:: class:
* Scalar sum of pT of all tracks reconstructed in cones of R = 0.3 and 0.5 around the direction of a , and the number of such tracks.
* Scalar sum of transverse energy depositions ET in ECAL, HCAL, and HO in cones of R = 0.3 and 0.5, and the total number of jets in these cones.
Additional information allowing to calculate other isolation-related quantities is stored in the event record as associations (IsoDepositMap); a detailed descripition can be found in [SWGuideMuonIsolation](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideMuonIsolation).
## Muons in missing ET calculations
* [Link](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookMetAnalysis#HeadingFour) to the corresponding section in MET [WorkBook](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBook).
## Muons in Physics Analysis Tools
* [Link](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATDataFormats#PatMuon) to the corresponding section in PAT [WorkBook](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBook).
## Examples
The example provided is for "CMSSW\_9\_2\_3\_patch2", it allows for quick demonstration of some basic concepts on how to get access to information.
We will created an EDAnalyzer within our CMSSW work area. The analyzer should iterate over the reconstructed muons stored in the miniAOD and fill histograms with the momenta components of the reconstructed muons. Use the [TFileService](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/TFileService?topicparent=CMSPublic.WorkBookMuonAnalysis;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") object to store the histograms. We also make a vertex to reconstruct the "Jpsi" particle (see [figure](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/pub/CMSPublic/WorkBookMuonAnalysis/Jpsimass.png)).
```
source /cvmfs/cms.cern.ch/cmsset_default.sh
export SCRAM_ARCH=slc6_amd64_gcc530
cmsrel CMSSW_9_2_3_patch2
cd CMSSW_9_2_3_patch2/src/
cp -r /afs/cern.ch/user/j/jmejiagu/public/miniAODmuonexample/CMSSW_9_2_3_patch2/src/myAnalyzers .
cmsenv
voms-proxy-init -voms cms -valid 192:00
scram b -j8
cd myAnalyzers/JPsiKsPAT/test/
cmsRun miniAODmuonsRootupler.py
```

# **The CMS data tier**
consists of an Ntuple-like format, readable with bare root and containing the per-event information needed in most generic analyses. A is not a CMSSW [EDM](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/EDM) file, but several [EDM](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/EDM) features are available in this simplified format, too.The size per event of is order of 1Kb, they can be produced in O(weeks) time, central production can be triggered a few times per year if many new features are made available in "hot periods". Users can easily extend for their specific study making a private production when needed (suggested for specific studies on samples that are not too large or for some special needs) or can in the central format (suggested when need to run on multi billion events) by writing on the [XPOG CMStalk category![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cms-talk.web.cern.ch/c/physics/phystools/137), or by opening an issue in the [XPOG coordination gitlab![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://gitlab.cern.ch/cms-/xpog-coordination/-/issues).
