## Event selection
For the event selection we make use of the file [analyzeTopSelection\_cfg.py![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/blob/CMSSW_8_1_X/PhysicsTools/PatExamples/test/analyzeTopSelection_cfg.py) in the *test* directory of the *PatExamples* package. It contains the pre-processed PAT tuples for the simulated ttbar events as input, you can just execute it as it is:
```
cmsRun PhysicsTools/PatExamples/test/analyzeTopSelection_cfg.py
```
We are going to have a closer look into the structure of the file while the first job is running. Apart from the obligatory input source and *TFileService* declaration it consists of four sections. We will go through them step by step in the following:**analyzerTopSelection\_cfg.py**
```
## ----------------------------------------------------------------
## Apply object selection according to  reference selection
## for ICHEP 2010. This will result in 5 additional collections:
##
## * goodJets
## * vetoElecs
## * vetoMuons
## * looseMuons
## * tightMuons
##
## Have a look ont the cff file to learn more about the exact
## selection citeria.
## ----------------------------------------------------------------
process.load("PhysicsTools.PatExamples.topObjectSelection_cff")
process.topObjectProduction = cms.Path(
    process.topObjectSelection
)
```
![ALERT!](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/warning.gif "ALERT!") **Note:**
In this section all objects that will be needed for the event selection are created beforehand. These are object collections for which we applied the object requirements as defined in the selection table [above](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATExampleTopQuarks#SelectionTable). We have chosen the module labels pretty self-explaining if you have the above table in mind:
* tightMuons
* looseMuons
* vetoMuons
* vetoElecs
* goodJets
All of them are *pat::Candidate* collections that have the corresponding default *selectedPatCandidate* collections as input. You can find their definitions in the indicated *cff* file. We will only discuss the  collections here, the others are derived in an analogue **
```
## ---
##
## this cff file keep all object selections used for the
## reference selection for ICHEP 2010
##
## ---
from PhysicsTools.PatAlgos.cleaningLayer1.muonCleaner_cfi import *
looseMuons = cleanPatMuons.clone(
    preselection =
    'isGlobalMuon & isTrackerMuon &'
    'pt > 20. &'
    'abs(eta) < 2.1 &'
    '(trackIso+caloIso)/pt < 0.1 &'
    'innerTrack.numberOfValidHits > 10 &'
    'globalTrack.normalizedChi2 < 10.0 &'
    'globalTrack.hitPattern.numberOfValidMuonHits > 0 &'
    ') < 0.02',
    checkOverlaps = cms.PSet(
      jets = cms.PSet(
        src                 = cms.InputTag("goodJets"),
        algorithm           = cms.string("byDeltaR"),
        preselection        = cms.string(""),
        deltaR              = cms.double(0.3),
        checkRecoComponents = cms.bool(False),
        pairCut             = cms.string(""),
        requireNoOverlaps   = cms.bool(True),
      )
    )
)
tightMuons = cleanPatMuons.clone(
    src = 'looseMuons',
    preselection = '(trackIso+caloIso)/pt < 0.05'
)
from PhysicsTools.PatAlgos.selectionLayer1.muonSelector_cfi import *
vetoMuons = selectedPatMuons.clone(
    src = 'selectedPatMuons',
    cut =
    'isGlobalMuon &'
    'pt > 10. &'
    'abs(eta) < 2.5 &'
    '(trackIso+caloIso)/pt < 0.2'
)
```
![ALERT!](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/warning.gif "ALERT!") **Note:**
We start off from the *looseMuons* collection for which we clone the *cleanPatMuons* as defined in the *python/cleaningLayer1* directory of the *PatAlgos* package. We do this to implement the ΔR(μ,jet)>0.3 requirement between the  and the closest selected jet in <η, φ> space. As this is a requirement on a relation between two objects we cannot simply apply it via the [SWGuidePhysicsCutParser](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuidePhysicsCutParser). The cut is applied in the parameter set *checkOverlaps*, where the jet collection we want to check the muons against (*goodJets*), the overlap checking algorithm (*byDeltaR*) and the value of *deltaR* are defined. The *requireNoOverlaps* takes care that muons, which have an overlap are indeed discarded from the collection. For the rest of the selection we make use of the *preselection* parameter of the *cleanPatMuons* module. Thus the PAT cleaning that you encountered in [**Exercise 7**](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuidePATCrossObjectCollectionExercise) appears in a new light here!For convenience the *tightMuons*, which only adds stronger requirements on top of the *looseMuons* have the latter as input. We do not have to apply the full selection strings again. Note that all parameters, which are not replaced remain the same as defined in the *looseMuons* module. Note that for the *vetoMuons* collection there is no ΔR(μ,jet) requirement. It is therefore enough to stay with the *selectedPatMuon* module. Also for the jet collection and the electron veto collection there is no need to make use of the cleaning module, as there all requirements are applied just on the objects themselves. Accordingly you will see that we cloned the corresponding *selectedPatCandidate* modules as defined in the *python/selectionLayer1* directory of the *PatAlgos* package to configure the modules for these collections.We now come to the second block in the**analyzerTopSelection\_cfg.py**
```
## ----------------------------------------------------------------
##  the steps for the  reference selection for ICHEP
## 2010. Have a look at the WorkBookPATExampleTopQuarks. These
## are event selections. They make use of the object selections
## applied in the step above.
## ----------------------------------------------------------------
##  bit (HLT_mu9)
from HLTrigger.HLTfilters.hltHighLevel_cfi import *
process.step1  = hltHighLevel.clone(TriggerResultsTag = "TriggerResults::HLT", HLTPaths = ["HLT_Mu9"])
##  requirement
process.  = cms.EDFilter("VertexSelector", src = cms.InputTag("offlinePrimaryVertices"), cut = cms.string("!isFake && ndof > 4 && abs(z) < 15 && position.Rho < 2"), filter = cms.bool(True))
## Exact one tight
from PhysicsTools.PatAlgos.selectionLayer1.muonCountFilter_cfi import *
process.step3a = countPatMuons.clone(src = 'tightMuons', minNumber = 1,  = 1)
## Exact one loose
process.step3b = countPatMuons.clone(src = 'looseMuons', minNumber = 1,  = 1)
## Veto on additional muons
process.  = countPatMuons.clone(src = 'vetoMuons' ,  = 1)
## Veto on additional electrons
from PhysicsTools.PatAlgos.selectionLayer1.electronCountFilter_cfi import *
process.step5  = countPatMuons.clone(src = 'vetoElecs' ,  = 0)
## Different jet multiplicity selections
from PhysicsTools.PatAlgos.selectionLayer1.jetCountFilter_cfi import *
process.step6a = countPatJets.clone(src = 'goodJets'   , minNumber = 1)
process.step6b = countPatJets.clone(src = 'goodJets'   , minNumber = 2)
process.step6c = countPatJets.clone(src = 'goodJets'   , minNumber = 3)
process.  = countPatJets.clone(src = 'goodJets'   , minNumber = 4)
```
![ALERT!](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/warning.gif "ALERT!") **Note:**
Here we the event selection steps, making use of the *candidateCountFilters* as defined in the *python/selectionLayer1* directory of the *PatAlgos* package.
You can very easily connect the module names with the selection steps defined in the selection table. Note that these modules are event filters! While the modules for object selection were producers that created new collections containing the objects that passed the imposed requirements (which could also result into an empty collection) these modules will really discard events in cases where the collections do not fulfill the requirements.In the third section we configure a set of modules to fill a set of very basic monitoring histograms, with according replacements for the input collections. ## ----------------------------------------------------------------
##  the analysis paths: we  two selection paths to
## monitor the cutflow according to the  reference selection
## for ICHEP 2010. All necessary object collections have been pro-
## duced in the cms.Path topObjectProduction before hand. The out-
## put report is switched on to get a quick overview of the number
## number of events after each selection step.
## ----------------------------------------------------------------
##  output report on
process.options   = cms.untracked.PSet( wantSummary = cms.untracked.bool(True) )
##  loose event selection path
process.looseEventSelection = cms.Path(
    process.step1      *
    process.      *
    process.step3b     *
    process.      *
    process.step5      *
    process.step6a     *
    process.step6b     *
    process.step6c
    )
##  tight event selection path
process.tightEventSelection = cms.Path(
    process.monStart   *
    process.step1      *
    process.monStep1   *
    process.      *
    process.monStep2   *
    process.step3a     *
    process.monStep3a  *
    process.      *
    process.monStep4   *
    process.step5      *
    process.monStep5   *
    process.step6a     *
    process.monStep6a  *
    process.step6b     *
    process.monStep6b  *
    process.step6c     *
    process.monStep6c  *
    process.      *
    process.monStep7
    )
```

## More complex analyses of top quarks
In the above example we followed a very of an analysis, the selection of events containing top quarks pairs. For high level analyses of top quark pair quantities the  supports an own toolkit:The **Top Quark Analysis Framework (TQAF)** is a toolkit to facilitate the analysis of final states containing top quark pairs in the dileptonic, semi-leptonic and full hadronic decay channel. It is an integral part of CMSSW and build up on the Physics Analysis Toolkit (PAT). For more details on the TQAF have a look to the [SWGuideTQAF](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideTQAF). You will find the links to a set of examples on the use of the Top Quark Analysis Framework (TQAF) below. ## A
**addJetCollection:**[pat::Tool](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATGlossary#PatTools) to **add an arbitrary jet collection** to the [pat::EventContent](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATGlossary#PatEvent) and . The source code is located in the [tools![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/tree/CMSSW_5_3_X/PhysicsTools/PatAlgos/python/tools) directory of the [PatAlgos](/twiki/bin/edit/CMSPublic/A?topicparent=CMSPublic.WorkBookPATGlossary;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.") package. You can find a full description of the tool at [/SWGuidePATTools#Jet_Tools).
## B
## C
**pat::Candidate:**The CMSSW Event Data Model ([EDM](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/EDM)) is optimised for space consumption. The Data Formats of reconstructed objects contain only very basic information, while additional information might be added in form of extra Data Formats, which themselves might be distributed over the whole event content. This makes it difficult for the end user to access all information, which is necessary and available for analysis. The **pat:.Candidate is the common Data Format** of [PAT](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATGlossary#PaT). Each pat::Candidate is derived from a corresponding [reco::Candidate![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmssdt.cern.ch/SDT/doxygen/redirect.php?r=5_3_14&c=Candidate&K={reco}) including a user configurable set of extra information. This extra information might already be part of the event content (only being re-keyed) or newly created before being folded into the pat::Candidate Data Format. Examples for such information are:
* isoDeposits.
* electronId.
* b-tag information.
* truth matching.
* object resolutions.
* jet energy correction factors.
Apart from the generic support of  [truth matching](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATGlossary#McMatching) and [object disambiguation](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATGlossary#CrossCleaning) one of the key features of PAT is [object](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATGlossary) . At the moment the following reco::Candidate Data Formats are canonically supported:
| [reco collection type](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATGlossary?sortcol=0;table=1;up=0#sorted_table "Sort by this column") | [pat collection type](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATGlossary?sortcol=1;table=1;up=0#sorted_table "Sort by this column") | [selectedPatCandidate label](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATGlossary?sortcol=2;table=1;up=0#sorted_table "Sort by this column") | [cleanPatCandidate label](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATGlossary?sortcol=3;table=1;up=0#sorted_table "Sort by this column") |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [reco::Photon![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmssdt.cern.ch/SDT/doxygen/redirect.php?r=5_3_14&c=Photon&K={reco}) | [pat::Photon![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmssdt.cern.ch/SDT/doxygen/redirect.php?r=5_3_14&c=Photon&K={pat}) | `selectedPatPhotons` | `cleanPatPhotons` |
| [reco::GsfElectron![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmssdt.cern.ch/SDT/doxygen/redirect.php?r=5_3_14&c=GsfElectron&K={reco}) | [pat::Electron![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmssdt.cern.ch/SDT/doxygen/redirect.php?r=5_3_14&c=Electron&K={pat}) | `selectedPatElectrons` | `cleanPatElectrons` |

The pat::Candidtate collections are produced during the . The main collections are the [selectedPatCandidate](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATGlossary#SelectPatCands) and the [cleanPatCandidate](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATGlossary#CleanPatCands) collections. Due to the feature of the size of a pat::Candidate collection as well as the whole [pat::EventContent](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATGlossary#PatEvent) is configurable, ranging between 6kB/evt and 36kB/evt for reasonable configurations. The persistent output of of the  is often referred to as [pat::Tuple](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATGlossary#PatTuple). To learn more about the size estimate of a pat::Tuple have a look to [SWGuidePATEventSize](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuidePATEventSize). To learn more about the Data Formats have a look to [WorkBookPATDataFormats](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATDataFormats).
**cleanPatCandidates:**This is a common **reference to the collection labels** of a common [PAT Candidate](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATGlossary#PatCand) collection that contain extra information about object disambiguation. This information is fully user configurable. You can find all currently supported cleanPatCandidate collection labels under the description of the [pat::Candidate](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATGlossary#PatCand). A suggested configuration exists in the [cleaningLayer1![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/tree/CMSSW_5_3_X/PhysicsTools/PatAlgos/python/cleaningLayer1/) directory of the [PatAlgos![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/tree/CMSSW_5_3_X/PhysicsTools/PatAlgos) package. To learn more about the support of object disambiguation by PAT have a look to [SWGuidePATCrossCleaning](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuidePATCrossCleaning).
**Cross Cleaning:**By construction energy deposits in the CMS detector may be interpreted differently depending on the analyst's or the corresponding analysis purpose. For several analysis, which mostly aim for the interpretation of a combination of different objects it is necessary to resolve such ambiguities. **The disambiguation of overlapping objects is often referred to as object Cross Cleaning**. This name is a bit misleading as the disambiguation of objects does not necessarily mean, that elements will be erased from object collections. PAT supports object disambiguation by adding extra information about overlapping objects, which is well defined and completely user configurable. No elements are removed from the object collections in the default configuration. A typical example of overlapping objects is an electron, which may be interpreted as a photon or a jet at the same time. To learn more about the support of object disambiguation by PAT have a look to [SWGuidePATCrossCleaning](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuidePATCrossCleaning).
## D
## E
**pat::Electron:**[pat::Candidate](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATGlossary#PatCand) corresponding to the [reco::GsfElectron![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmssdt.cern.ch/SDT/doxygen/redirect.php?r=5_3_14&c=GsfElectron&K={reco}). You can learn more about the *pat::Electron* at [WorkBookPATDataFormats#PatElectron](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATDataFormats#PatElectron).
**:**The **Event Data Model ([EDM](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/EDM))** is optimised for disc space consumption. High level analysis objects like electrons are reconstructed from basic reconstruction objects like super clusters or tracks that might again consist of base clusters or reconstructed hits. All higher level analysis objects consist of **smart links (pointers)** to the lower level reconstruction objects they are made up from. In addition extra information like track might be removed from the track object and kept in an extra data format in order to keep the track data format small. There is no other correlation between different object collections but via such smart pointers. As parts of these collections might be dropped from the event content at later steps of the event processing, these smart pointer correlations might be broken (*dangling*) and pointing nowhere. This architecture makes it extremely complicated for standard users to keep track of where the information of the high level analysis objects might be localised, as it might be distributed all over the event content, thus **complicating to drop information**, which might not be needed for the analysis. Moreover it reduces the flexibility of reducing the event size, which also has influence on the runtime performance of the analysis frame: the user might be interested in the calorimeter towers of which the jets in a certain jet collection are made up from. So he/she should keep the calorimeter tower collection in the event content, which requires a sizable amount of disc space even if the fraction of calorimeter towers of interest might be much smaller. **is the answer** that PAT has to issues of this kind. Via configuration the user may **choose to embed certain object information** into the [pat::Candidate](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATGlossary#PatCand) during the production step. This information will be hard copied into the *pat::Candidate* and may now be dropped from the event content. In the example of the jet collection only the calorimeter towers, which are part of the jet will be kept. This process is fully transparent to the user: All member function of the *pat::Candidate* will be used the same way independent from whether the corresponding information has been embedded before or internally is still called by reference. To learn more about object within PAT have a look to the [WorkBookPATWorkflow](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATWorkflow) or to the [WorkBookPATConfiguration](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATConfiguration). To learn more about how works have a look to the [SWGuidePATEmbeddingExercise](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuidePATEmbeddingExercise).
**pat::EventContent:**Event content of a [pat::Tuple](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATGlossary#PatTuple) as defined in the file [https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/blob/CMSSW\_5\_3\_X/PhysicsTools/PatAlgos/python/patEventContent\_cff.py![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/blob/CMSSW_5_3_X/PhysicsTools/PatAlgos/python/patEventContent_cff.py) when making the event content persistent . In the default configuration all [cleanPatCandidtates](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATGlossary#CleanPatCands) are written to the event. When removing [pat::Cleaning](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATGlossary#CrossCleaning) from the [workflow](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATGlossary#PatWorkflow) the [selectedPatCandidates](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATGlossary#SelectedPatCands) will be made persistent instead. To get an impression of what the size of a typical *pat::Tuple* as derived from the standard ttbar input files is have a look [here![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://www.desy.de/~rwolf/pat/output_360_V07-13-09.html). In the *patEventContent\_cff.py* file also other vectors of useful event information are pre-defined. Of course the user is further free to customize the event content to his/her needs. To learn more about the customization of the event content of your personal *pat::Tuple* have a look at [SWGuidePATConfigExercise](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuidePATConfigExercise). To learn more about tools how to estimate the size of your private *pat::Tuple* have a look to [SWGuidePATEventSize](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuidePATEventSize).

**pat::Jet:**[pat::Candidate](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATGlossary#PatCand) corresponding to the [reco::Jet![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmssdt.cern.ch/SDT/doxygen/redirect.php?r=5_3_14&c=Jet&K={reco}). The *pat::Jet* may carry the extra information of a *reco::CaloJet*, a *reco::PFJet* or a *reco::JPTJet*. It can carry much more information depending on the choice of the user. You can learn more about the *pat::Jet* at [WorkBookPATDataFormats#PatJet](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATDataFormats#PatJet).

 **truth matching:**Association of generated event information to reconstructed object information for simulated events. Note that generator information (generator particles or generator particle based jets) are matched to reconstructed objects and not vice verse. The Analysis Tools packages provide sophisticated tools to cover all issues of matching. Have a look to [WorkBookMCTruthMatch](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookMCTruthMatch) to learn more about these. To learn more about how PAT exploits the analysis tools of MC matching have a look to [SWGuidePATMCMatching](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuidePATMCMatching). You can find the files, that provide the default configuration of MC matching in the [mcMatchLayer0![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/tree/CMSSW_5_3_X/PhysicsTools/PatAlgos/python/mcMatchLayer0) directory of the [PatAlgos![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/tree/CMSSW_5_3_X/PhysicsTools/PatAlgos) package.

You can learn more about the  at [WorkBookPATDataFormats#](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATDataFormats).

You can learn more about the *pat::Muon* at [WorkBookPATDataFormats#PatMuon](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATDataFormats#PatMuon).

## P
**PAT:****The Physics Analysis Toolkit (PAT)** is a high-level analysis layer providing the Physics Analysis Groups (PAGs) with easy access to the algorithms developed by Physics Objects Groups (POGs) in the framework of the CMSSW offline software. It aims at fulfilling the needs of most CMS analyses, providing both ease-of-use for beginners and flexibility for advanced users. PAT is fully integrated into CMSSW and an integral part of any release of CMSSW. You can find more information about PAT in the [WorkBookPAT](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPAT) and the complete documentation in the [SWGuidePAT](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuidePAT).
**pat:**The minor letter abbreviation [pat![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cms-service-sdtweb.web.cern.ch/cms-service-sdtweb/doxygen/CMSSW_3_5_8/doc/html/d8/d06/namespacepat.html) is the common namespace label for [PAT](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATGlossary#PaT). You mostly find it as namspace label for the [pat::Candidates](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATGlossary#PatCand), but we also use it sometimes for more abstract expressions like [pat::Tuple](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATGlossary#PatTuple), [pat::EventContent](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATGlossary#PatEvent) or [pat::Workflow](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATGlossary#PatWorkflow)
**Patification:**The act of creating a [pat::Tuple](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATGlossary#PatTuple) or running the  on the fly. You can call this a true slang expression that should not be used. Nevertheless you might stumble over it from time to time.
**PF2PAT:**Common abbreviation for a tool that makes [pat::Candidates](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATGlossary#PatCands) from particle flow objects only. Already without the use of PF2PAT you have the possibility to add jet collections made from particle flow constituents or to make use of of particle flow MET (pfMET). (Have a look to the [pat::Tools](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATGlossary#PatTools) to see how to do this.) But PF2PAT gives you the most consistent interface of the particle flow algorithms to PAT. To learn more about the use of [PF2PAT](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/PF2PAT) have a look to the [SWGuidePF2PAT](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuidePF2PAT).
**pat::Photon:**[pat::Candidate](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATGlossary#PatCand) corresponding to the [reco::Photon![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmssdt.cern.ch/SDT/doxygen/redirect.php?r=5_3_14&c=Photon&K={reco}). You can learn more about the *pat::Photon* at [WorkBookPATDataFormats#PatPhoton](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATDataFormats#PatPhoton).**PU:** - Pile Up

## R
## S
**selectedPatCandidates:**This is a common **reference to the collection labels** of a common [PAT Candidate](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATGlossary#PatCand) collection that has passed the selection step of the  but does not contain any extra information about object disambiguation. In the default configuration there is no selection applied to the reconstructed objects. To learn more about this phase of have a look to [WorkBookPATWorkflow#SelectedCandidate](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATWorkflow#SelectedCandidate). You can find the configuration [selectionLayer1![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/tree/CMSSW_5_3_X/PhysicsTools/PatAlgos/python/selectionLayer1) directory of the [PatAlgos![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/tree/CMSSW_5_3_X/PhysicsTools/PatAlgos) package. To learn more about tool to switch from the PAT default configurastion including information about object disambiguation ([[/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATGlossary#CleanPatCands)) to the *selectedPatCandidates* have a look to the [SWGuidePATTools#CMS.Core\_Tools](/twiki/bin/edit/SWGuidePATToolsCMS/Core_Tools?topicparent=CMSPublic.WorkBookPATGlossary;nowysiwyg=1 "this topic does not yet exist; you can create it.").
**switchJetCollection:**[pat::Tool](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATGlossary#PatTools) to **switch the default jet collection (ak5Calo)** to an arbitrary jet collection in the . The source code is located in the [tools![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/tree/CMSSW_5_3_X/PhysicsTools/PatAlgos/python/tools/) directory of the [PatAlgos![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/tree/CMSSW_5_3_X/PhysicsTools/PatAlgos) package. You can find a full description of the tool at [SWGuidePATTools#Jet\_Tools](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuidePATTools#Jet_Tools).
## T
**pat::Tau:**[pat::Candidate](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATGlossary#PatCand) corresponding to the [reco::PFTau![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmssdt.cern.ch/SDT/doxygen/redirect.php?r=5_3_14&c=PFTau&K={reco}). You can learn more about the *pat::Tau* at [WorkBookPATDataFormats#PatTau](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATDataFormats#PatTau).
**pat::Tools:**A common expression for a large set off tools to modify and customize the  and/or [event content](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATGlossary#EventContent). You can apply these tools just in your config file or in a more intuitive way via the [edmConfigEditor](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookConfigEditor). To learn more about the available *pat::Tools* have a look to [SWGuidePATTools](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuidePATTools). It includes also tools to process input files from earlier versions of CMSSW.
**pat::TriggerEvent:**In addition to the [trigger::TriggerEvent![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmssdt.cern.ch/SDT/doxygen/redirect.php?r=5_3_14&c=TriggerEvent&K={trigger}) PAT provides a *pat::TriggerEvent* to facilitate access to L1 and HLT trigger information. The pat::TriggerEvent is the common entry point to all trigger information in PAT. To learn more about it have a look to [SWGuidePATTrigger](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuidePATTrigger).
**pat::Tuple:**This is the common expression of the **Persistent Layer of PAT**, characterized by the [pat::EventContent](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATGlossary#EventContent). Whenever you create an EDM file containing [pat::Candidates](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATGlossary#PatCands) during the workbook exercises we refer to it as a *pat::Tuple*. In real life the *pat::Tuple* is an EDM file that contains *pat::Candidates* and is taylored to the user's needs. It sustains full event provenance information and can be used with full CMSSW, FWLite, or plain *root*. As the content of a *pat::Tuple* can be very different from configuration to configuration (even down to the content of a *pat::Candidate* within a certain collection) it is not comparable to a data Tier like RECO or AOD. You should rather it as **better replacement of a flat user ntuple**, that keeps all features of the EDM and can still be transformed into a flat ntuple at later stages of the analysis. Studies show that this is not necessary though: containing the same event information, there is hardly any performence differences in data access and runtime performance compared to a flat ntuple. Have a look [here![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://www.desy.de/~rwolf/pat/output_360_V07-13-09.html) to get an idea of the current size of a *pat::Tuple* in the default configuration. It is of course not necessary to make the *pat::Tuple* persistent to work with *pat::Canddiate* collections. At your choice you can produce the *pat::Tuple* also on the fly.
## U
## V
## W
**pat::Workflow:**This is the common workflow for the creation of a *pat::Tuple*. It consists of a preparation phases followed by three further phases:
* **Phase 1**: creation of plain [pat::Candidates](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATGlossary#PatCands).
* **Phase 2**: a first selection phase to create [selectedPatCandidates](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATGlossary#SelectedPatCands).
* **Phase 3**: a object disambiguation phase to add object overlap information and to create [/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATGlossary#CleanPatCands).
When adding  information fo the *pat::Candidates* it might go through another phase. Have a look to [WorkBookPATWorkflow](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATWorkflow) to learn more about the details.

# 4.2.5. Using PAT On Data
## Contents
* [4.5.1. Prescription](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATOnData#PreScription)
* [4.5.2. Input files](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATOnData#FiLes)
* [4.5.3. Making PAT-tuples](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATOnData#MakingPAT)
* [4.5.4. Running with FWLite](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATOnData#RunFWLite)
This is an example for how to run on data in the `Jet` PD.
## 4.5.1. Prescription
To know more about what data are available for analysis and what are the conditions under which they have been taken have a look to the [PdmV2012Analysis](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin/viewauth/CMS/PdmV2012Analysis) page of the PPD.
A prescription to run the first data in CMSSW\_7\_4\_15 is available on [SWGuidePATReleaseNotes41X](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuidePATReleaseNotes41X). Please follow this link to keep up to date with latest updates. Due to the rapidly changing start-up conditions in software it is beneficial to check this often for the next few weeks.
## Input files
The triggers for the `Jet` PD are listed [here![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/blob/CMSSW_4_2_X/HLTrigger/Configuration/python/HLT_FULL_data_cff.py).

## Making PAT-tuples
The PAT-tuples are made (without DCSTRONLY for the moment) with [this configuration file![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/blob/CMSSW_4_2_X/PhysicsTools/PatExamples/test/patTuple_data_cfg.py). This file will produce `pat::Jets` from `reco::PFJets` and use
the [PFJetIDSelectionFunctor![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/blob/CMSSW_5_3_X/PhysicsTools/SelectorUtils/interface/PFJetIDSelectionFunctor.h) in the [full framework](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuidePATSelectors#New_Using_Selector_to_write_sele) to write out only jets that pass jet ID. Thus it is unnecessary to apply jet ID in FWLite.To run it do the following:
```
cmsRun PhysicsTools/PatExamples/test/patTuple_data_cfg.py
```
This will create a file called "jet2011A\_aod.root" out of the first 1000 events. The event content is:

## Running with FWLite
In order to analyse this in FWLite, use [this executable![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/blob/CMSSW_4_2_X/PhysicsTools/PatExamples/bin/PatBasicFWLiteJetAnalyzer.cc) and [this configuration file![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/blob/CMSSW_4_2_X/PhysicsTools/PatExamples/bin/analyzePatJetFWLite_cfg.py).
```
PatBasicFWLiteJetAnalyzer PhysicsTools/PatExamples/bin/analyzePatJetFWLite_cfg.py
```
This will make some distributions of the `Jets` in the event and write to the file `analyzePatBasics.root`. The histograms are:
```
 KEY: TH1F   jetPt;1   pt
 KEY: TH1F   jetEta;1   eta
 KEY: TH1F   jetPhi;1   phi
 KEY: TH1F   disc;1   : TH1F   constituentPt;1   Constituent pT
```
Have fun!!!-- - 21-Mar-2011

**This exercise runs a CRAB job to create a pat::Tuple from the AOD data.**

## Introduction
This does not teach the details of GRID nor is a CRAB tutorial. For CRAB tutorial you must refer to [WorkBookCRAB2Tutorial](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookCRAB2Tutorial). A complete guide to CRAB is at [SWGuideCrab](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideCrab). This exercise runs CRAB job to create a PATtuple from (skimmed) data and is part of the PAT tutorial exercises. The purpose of these exercises is to show PAT users how they can use Grid tools in creating their for CMS analysis.
Having your storage space set up may take several days, Grid run with some latency, and there can be problems. You should
set aside about a week to complete these exercises. The actual effort required is not the whole week but a few hours. For
CRAB questions unrelated to this twiki, please use the links [ FAQ](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin//CMS/SWGuideCrabFaq) and .
## Pre-requisite for this exercises
To perform this set of exercises you need a Grid Certificate, CMS VO membership and SiteDB registration. It is also assumed that you have CERN account. You must have a space to write out your output files to , say `castor`. All `lxplus` users have account on `castor` where they can write their CRAB output.
### Obtain a CERN account
* Use the following link for a CMS CERN account: [CMS CERN account![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cernaccount.web.cern.ch/cernaccount/Externals.aspx)
  + A CERN account is needed, for example, to login in to any e-learning web-site, or obtain a file from the afs area. A CERN account will be needed for future exercises.
  + **Obtaining a CERN account can be time-consuming. To expedite the process please ask the relevant institutional team leader to perform the necessary "signing" after the online form has been submitted and received for initial processing by the secretariat.**
### Obtain a Grid Certificate, CMS VO membership and [SiteDB](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SiteDB) registration
* A Grid Certificate, CMS VO membership and SiteDB registration will be needed for the next set of exercises. The registration process can be time-consuming (actions by several people are required), so it is important to start it as soon as possible. There are three main requirements which can be simply summarized: A certificate ensures that you are who you claim to be. A registration in the VO recognizes your (identified by your certificate) as a member of CMS. A SiteDB is a database and web interface that CMS uses to track sites and also used by CRAB publication step to find out the hypernews username of a person from their Grid Certificate's DN (Distinguished Name) etc.. Please look at [Get Your Grid Certificate, CMSVO and SiteDB registration](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin//CMS/SWGuideRunningGridPrerequisites) to complete these three steps. All three steps are needed to be completed before you successfully submit on the Grid.

## Step 1 - Setup a release, setup CRAB environment and verify your grid certificate is OK
To setup a `CMSSW` release for our purpose, we will execute the following instructions:Login to `lxplus.cern.ch` ad go to your working area ( preferably `scratch0` area, for example `/afs/cern.ch/user/m/malik/scratch0/`). Then execute the following commands. We will call `/afs/cern.ch/user/m/malik/scratch0/` as `YOURWORKINGAREA`.Create a directory for this exercise (to avoid interference with code from the other exercises).
```
mkdir exercise04
cd exercise04
```
Create a local release area and enter it.
```
setenv SCRAM_ARCH slc5_amd64_gcc462
cmsrel CMSSW_7_4_1_patch4
cd CMSSW_7_4_1_patch4/src
```
Set up the environment.
```
source /afs/cern.ch/cms/LCG/LCG-2/UI/cms_ui_env.csh
cmsenv
```
More on setup local Environment and prepare user analysis code are given [here](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin//CMS/WorkBookCRABTutorial#SetUpEnv).To setup CRAB execute the following command. The explanation of this command is given [here](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin//CMS/WorkBookCRABTutorial#SetUpCRABEnv).
```
source /afs/cern.ch/cms/ccs/wm/scripts/Crab/crab.csh
```
To verify that your certificate - It is assumed that you have successfully installed and followed the above instructions for setup. Now you verify that your GRID certificate has all the information needed.Initialize your proxy
```
voms-proxy-init -voms cms
```
You should the following output:
```
Enter GRID pass phrase:
Your identity: /DC=org/DC=doegrids/OU=People/CN= 503653
Creating temporary proxy .......................... Done
Contacting  lcg-voms.cern.ch:15002 [/DC=ch/DC=cern/OU=computers/CN=lcg-voms.cern.ch] "cms" Done
Creating proxy ................... Done
Your proxy is valid until Fri Jul  1 22:41:34 2011
```
Now run the following command
```
voms-proxy-info -all | grep -Ei "role|subject"
```
The output should look like this:
```
subject   : /DC=org/DC=doegrids/OU=People/CN= 503653/CN=proxy
subject   : /DC=org/DC=doegrids/OU=People/CN= 503653
attribute : /cms/Role=NULL/Capability=NULL
attribute : /cms/uscms/Role=NULL/Capability=NULL
```
## Step 2 - Know your data set name in the DBS
The data set name is needed to run the CRAB job.In this exercise, we will use the data set used =/Jet/Run2011B-PromptReco-v1/AOD=.I picked up this dataset from the twiki [PhysicsPrimaryDatasets](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin//CMS/PhysicsPrimaryDatasets#Primary_Datasets_7_TeV_Runs_from). Further, this dataset is also used in the script [PhysicsTools/PatExamples/test/patTuple\_data\_cfg.py![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://cmssw.cvs.cern.ch/cgi-bin/cmssw.cgi/CMSSW/PhysicsTools/PatExamples/test/patTuple_data_cfg.py?revision=1.6&=markup&pathrev=CMSSW_4_2_4). This script is a standard script provided by PAT group to work with collision data and hence I picked it.Before moving further, it would be interesting to see how to find this dataset in the DAS.To do this open the [DAS![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cmsweb.cern.ch/das/) in a browser. In the `ADVANCED KEYWORD SEARCH` type the following :`dataset dataset=/Jet/Run2011B*` A page pops up ( after few seconds). There are several datasets listed on this page. The one we use is listed as `/Jet/Run2011B-PromptReco-v1/AOD` You can also make use of the DBS Command Line Interpreter (CLI):
* Having set your CMSSW environment invoke the dbs command:
```
cd exercise04/CMSSW_7_4_1_patch4/src
cmsenv
dbs search --query "find dataset where dataset=/Jet/Run2011B*"
```

## Step 3 - Run your PATtuple config file locally to make sure it works
First copy the python script `patTuple_data_cfg.py` to your local area. To do this, execute the following command:
```
cvs co -r CMSSW_7_4_1_patch4 PhysicsTools/PatExamples/test/patTuple_data_cfg.py
```
Before executing the python script `patTuple_data_cfg.py`, we need to edit this script and make **three** modifications. If you are daring, try to run the config file **without** and **with modifications one by one** and see the error messages you might get. These modifications are:1. **Change the line for global tag**
```
process.GlobalTag.globaltag = 'GR_R_42_V12::All:'
```
**to**
```
process.GlobalTag.globaltag = 'GR_R_44_V11::All'
```
because we to use the appropriate gobal tag. More on global tag is [SWGuideFrontierConditions](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideFrontierConditions#Global_tags_for_collision_da_AN2).2. **Change**
```
inputJetCorrLabel = ('AK5PF', ['L1Offset', 'L2Relative', 'L3Absolute', 'L2L3Residual'])
```
**to**
```
inputJetCorrLabel = ('AK5PF', [])#NO jet energy correction yet
```

If successful, this will create an output file `.root` of size about `79MB` with `1000 events`.Now you prepare the CRAB configuration file
## Step 4 - Prepare your crab.py script for CRAB job submission
Your crab config files to submit CRAB job should look like this [crab.cfg](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/pub/CMSPublic/WorkBookPATTupleCrabExercise/crab_424.cfg.txt).In this `crab.cfg` file, the name of the output file is `.root`. Make sure that this name of the output file is the same as defined in the line `process.out.fileName = cms.untracked.string(''.root")` in the file `patTuple_data_cfg.py`.To look at what each of the line in `crab.cfg` means, refer to [CRAB Tutorial](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin//CMS/WorkBookCRABTutorial#SetConfiguration).This `crab.cfg` file contains `storage_path` as `/srm/managerv2?SFN=/castor/cern.ch/user/m/malik/pattutorial/` that we create in the next step. In this exercise we run over the data set name `/Jet/Run2011A-PromptReco-v4/AOD`. This `crab.cfg` also uses a file called `Cert_160404-167151_7TeV_PromptReco_Collisions11_JSON.txt`. This file that describes which luminosity sections in which runs are considered good and should be processed. In CMS, this kind of file is in the format. ( stands for  Notation).To find the most current good luminosity section files in format, please visit [https://cms-service-dqm.web.cern.ch/cms-service-dqm/CAF/certification/Collisions11/![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cms-service-dqm.web.cern.ch/cms-service-dqm/CAF/certification/Collisions11/).To know on how to work with files for Good Luminosity Sections in format please look at the twiki [SWGuideGoodLumiSectionsJSONFile](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideGoodLumiSectionsJSONFile).Instructions on how to setup your crab over selected lumi section is [Running over selected luminosity blocks](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin//CMS/SWGuideCrabFaq#Running_over_selected_luminosity).You can find the official (centrally produced) format files [here![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cms-service-dqm.web.cern.ch/cms-service-dqm/CAF/certification/) or on afs at the CAF area `/afs/cern.ch/cms/CAF/CMSCOMM/COMM_DQM/certification`. At the same locations as the format file you can also find the txt file reporting the history of the quality and DCS selection and at the bottom the snippet to configure any CMSSW application for running on the selected good .
## Step 5 - Get format file, creating writable directory in `castor` and setup `CRAB` environment
Get the  file to you `WORKINGDIRECTORY/exercise04/CMSSW_7_4_1_patch4/src` area
```

```
**Notice** how character "s" was removed from "https". `wget` command does not like "https" somehow.Create a directory in `castor` called `pattutorial`

# 4.2.4.2 Exercise 02: How to create a
## Contents
* [Setting up the environment](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATTupleCreationExercise#SetUp)
* [Having a look at the PAT configuration file](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATTupleCreationExercise)
* [Having a deeper look at the PAT configuration](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATTupleCreationExercise#CloserLook)
* [Running pat::Candidate production on top of RECO/AOD](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATTupleCreationExercise#RunNing)
* [Inspecting the output of pat::Candidate production](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATTupleCreationExercise#InSpecting)
* [Exercises](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATTupleCreationExercise#ExerCises)
* [Review status](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATTupleCreationExercise#ReviewStatus)
##
From this example you will learn **how to create a**  on your own. The PAT team provides standard configuration files to create , which contain already sensible default values for many parameters. The default output of a standard are the most important collections of high analysis objects like photons, electrons, muons, tau leptons, jets, MET. We will go through the different production steps and change a few basic parameters. This example will provide you with the following information:
* How to run PAT with a standard configuration.
* Basic understanding of the configuration.
* Basic understanding of the output.
We will first run the configuration file to create a default *patTuple.root* file as provided by the PAT team and then go through this configuration file step by step to learn more about it's insides and about tools to control what it is doing. A few questions will help you to check your learning success. After going though these explanations you should be well equipped to solve the [Exercises](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATTupleCreationExercise#ExerCises) at the end of this page.![ALERT!](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/warning.gif "ALERT!") **Note:**This web course is part of the [PAT Tutorial](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATTutorial), which takes regularly place at cern and in other places. When following the PAT Tutorial the answers of questions marked in RED should be filled into the exercise form that has been introduced at the beginning of the tutorial. Also the solutions to the [Exercises](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATTupleCreationExercise#ExerCises) should be filled into the form. The exercises are marked in three colours, indicating whether this exercise is basic (obligatory), continuative (recommended) or optional (free). The colour coding is summarized in the table below:
| [Color Code](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATTupleCreationExercise?sortcol=0;table=1;up=0#sorted_table "Sort by this column") | [Explanation](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATTupleCreationExercise?sortcol=1;table=1;up=0#sorted_table "Sort by this column") |
| --- | --- |
| ![red](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/pub/TWiki/SmiliesPlugin/red.gif "red") | Basic exercise, which is obligatory for the PAT Tutorial. |
| ![yellow](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/pub/TWiki/SmiliesPlugin/yellow.gif "yellow") | Continuative exercise, which is recommended for the PAT Tutorial to deepen what has been learned. |
| ![green](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/pub/TWiki/SmiliesPlugin/green.gif "green") | Optional exercise, which shows interesting applications of what has been learned. |
Basic exercises ( ![red](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/pub/TWiki/SmiliesPlugin/red.gif "red") ) are obliged and the solutions to the exercises should be filled into the exercise form during the PAT Tutorial.
## Setting up of the environment
First of all connect to `lxplus` and go to some work directory. You can choose any directory, provided that you have enough space. You need ~500 MB of free disc space for this exercise. We recommend you to use your *~/scratch0* space. In case you don't have this (or do not even know what it is) check your quota typing `fs lq` and follow [this link![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://cmsdoc.cern.ch/comp/help/doc/disk_space.shtml) or change your quota [here![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://account.cern.ch/account/Services/MyServices.aspx) (click manage near "Linux and AFS" -> Increase quota to 2 GB). If you don't have enough space, you may instead use the temporary space ( */tmp/your\_user\_name*), but be aware that this is lost once you log out of lxplus (or within something like a day). We will expect in the following that you have such a *~/scratch0* directory.
```
ssh
[ ... enter password ... ]
cd scratch0/
```
Create a directory for this exercise (to avoid interference with code from the other exercises).
```
cd exercise02
```
Create a local CMSSW release area and enter it.
```
cmsrel CMSSW_7_4_1_patch4
cd CMSSW_7_4_1_patch4/src
```
The first command creates all directories needed in a local CMSSW release area. Setting up the CMSSW environment is done by invoking the following script:
```
cmsenv
```
## Having a look at the PAT configuration file
To check out the recommended modules and configuration files we want to use do the following:
```
 PhysicsTools/PatAlgos
 FWCore/GuiBrowsers
git cms-merge-topic -u CMS-PAT-Tutorial:CMSSW_7_4_1_patTutorial
scram b -j 4
```
This will checkout and compile the standard PAT, its workflow, and the necessary classes. The standard PAT sequence is run on standard AOD/RECO input files, specified in `PhysicsTools/PatAlgos/test/patTuple_standard_cfg.py`. Have a look at this file with your favourite editor, for example xemacs:
```
xemacs PhysicsTools/PatAlgos/test/patTuple_standard_cfg.py
```
You will see that this configuration file does not contain too much code:
```
## import skeleton process from PhysicsTools.PatAlgos.patTemplate_cfg import *
## let it run process.p = cms.Path( process.patDefaultSequence )
## from PhysicsTools.PatAlgos.patInputFiles_cff import filesRelValProdTTbarAODSIM process.source.fileNames = filesRelValProdTTbarAODSIM # process.maxEvents.input = 100
## output file process.out.fileName = 'patTuple_standard.root'
```
We left out the commented regions on the screen. This is due to the fact that most information you might have expected to see from a typical *cmsRun* cfg file (like the *cms.OutputModule* to write output to an edm output file) are imported from another file: the `patTemplate_cfg.py`. We import it in the very first line. You may want to have a closer look into the `patTemplate_cfg.py` file (which is indeed imported for all example files in the test directory of the *PatAlgos* package). The `patTemplate_cfg.py` file provides defaults so that any python script (in the test directory) in which it is included runs fine. But of course you can override these defaults by parameter replacements at any time. We will do this later during this exercise. It is indeed the recommended way to change parameters by replacements instead of editing the files the parameters were defined in. The reason is obvious: editing the source file would change the parameter for any further cfg file which imports the source file - no chance to control what you did.Try the following:
```
cmsRun PhysicsTools/PatAlgos/test/patTuple_standard_cfg.py
```
In case *cmsRun* gives a message that the file patTemplate\_cfg.py does not exist check the following: Did you setup your environment properly? Did you forget to type *cmsenv*? You can test this checking the variable environment variable CMSSW\_RELEASE\_BASE ( echo $CMSSW\_RELEASE\_BASE) and see whether it points into the release you are expecting to work with (which is */afs/cern.ch/cms/slc5\_amd64\_gcc462/cms/cmssw/CMSSW\_7\_4\_1\_patch4* in our case).To have a look into the `patTemplate_cfg.py` file open it with your favourite editor:
```
xemacs PhysicsTools/PatAlgos/python/patTemplate_cfg.py &
```
We now come to the content of the `patTemplate_cfg.py` file. At the top level the process is defined:
```
import FWCore.ParameterSet. as cms
process = cms.Process("PAT")
```
Followed by the configuration of the [SWGuideMessageLogger](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideMessageLogger) and the output report.
```
## MessageLogger process.load("FWCore.MessageLogger.MessageLogger_cfi")
## Options and Output Report process.options = cms.untracked.PSet( wantSummary = cms.untracked.bool(True) )
```
This will just print a timing and trigger summary at the end of the job.For this example we will only loop over 100 events from this test input file. The tool *pickRelValInputFiles* will just pick up an up to RelVal file and return a string corresponding to the I/o protocol and the logical filename (LFN). You could replace it for the code fragment to look like this:
```
## Source
process.source = cms.Source("PoolSource", fileNames = cms.untracked.vstring( '/store/relval/CMSSW_7_4_0_pre8/RelValProdTTbar_13/AODSIM/MCRUN2_74_V7-v1/00000/44E1E4BA-50BD-E411-A57A-002618943949.root' ) )
## Maximal Number of Events
process.maxEvents = cms.untracked.PSet( input = cms.untracked.int32(100) )
```
For more information on how to configure the input source, have a look at the relevant section of [SWGuidePoolInputSources](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuidePoolInputSources). If you wish to only change the input files, you can start from the **top level** configuration (patTuple\_standard\_cfg.py),by adding the lines:
```
process.source.fileNames = ['/store/relval/CMSSW_7_4_0_pre8/RelValProdTTbar_13/AODSIM/MCRUN2_74_V7-v1/00000/44E1E4BA-50BD-E411-A57A-002618943949.root']<span data-mce-mark="1"><span data-mce-mark="1"><span data-mce-mark="1">
```
and replace the example file by the file(s) of your choice. Note that the RECO or AOD content may have changed from release to release. So there is no guarantee that you will still be able to use a input file which has been produced with an older release that the one you are using.In the following section of the patTemplate\_cfg.py configuration file additional information is loaded to the process, which is needed by some components during the pat::Candidate production steps as explained in [WorkBookPATWorkflow](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATWorkflow):
```
## Geometry and  (needed for a few patTuple production steps) process.load("Configuration.Geometry.GeometryIdeal_cff") process.load("Configuration.StandardSequences.FrontierConditions_GlobalTag_cff") from [[Configuration.AlCa.GlobalTag]] import GlobalTag process.GlobalTag = GlobalTag (process.GlobalTag, 'auto:startup') process.load("Configuration.StandardSequences.MagneticField_cff")
```
![ALERT!](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/warning.gif "ALERT!") **Note**: In this section the geometry information, calibration and alignment information (note the *global tag*) and magnetic field information is loaded into the process, which is needed for the calculation of Jet/MET corrections for instance. For the simulation, the *global tag* should always correspond to the *global tag* used for the reconstruction of these events. This can be inferred from the dataset name, or by looking at the "Configuration files" linked in DBS. For data, the latest set of calibration constants and frontier conditions can be found at [SWGuideFrontierConditions](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuideFrontierConditions), which is maintained by the calibration and alignment group.Typically the line that defines the *global tag* to be used would look like this:
```
process.GlobalTag.globaltag = cms.string('auto:run2_mc')
```
We are using the so called *autoCond* struct to do this automatically for us here. In the following part of the configuration file the sequence for the production of pat::Candidates is loaded and made known to the process:
```
## Standard PAT Configuration File process.load("PhysicsTools.PatAlgos.patSequences_cff")
```
The last part of the configuration file is concerned with the configuration of the output file:
```
process.out = cms.OutputModule("PoolOutputModule", fileName = cms.untracked.string('patTuple.root'),
## save only events passing the full path
#SelectEvents = cms.untracked.PSet( SelectEvents = cms.vstring('p') ),
## save PAT output; you need a '*' to unpack the list of commands
##'patEventContent'
outputCommands = cms.untracked.vstring('drop *', *patEventContentNoCleaning ) )
process.outpath = cms.EndPath(process.out)
```
We want to save the produced layer of pat::Candidates in the output file. We will only save those events, which passed the whole path, and by default we drop everything else. Finally, we add the output module to the *end path* of our process.

![Question](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/question.gif "Question")  How can you increase the number of events from 100 to 1000? process.maxEvents.input = 1000
```
![red](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/pub/TWiki/SmiliesPlugin/red.gif "red") **Exercise 2 b)**: Add a clone of the *selectedPatJets* collection (the default *pat::Jet* collection without object disambiguation) to the event content, with the collection label *goodPatJets*. You can achieve this by cloning the [selectedPatJet![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/blob/CMSSW_7_4_1_patch4/PhysicsTools/PatAlgos/python/selectionLayer1/jetSelector_cfi.py) module in your configuration file. Have a look to [WorkBookConfigFileIntro](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookConfigFileIntro) if you don't know how to clone a module. What is the mean jet multiplicity in your event sample for this new jet collection? ![ALERT!](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/warning.gif "ALERT!") **Note:** Make sure that your new collection will be written to the event output. You can use the feature of cloning modules together with the string selection feature to apply object and event selections in your analysis in a very elegant and human readable way.You will find the solution here:
Show ![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/toggleopen-small.gif)  Hide ![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/toggleclose-small.gif)
Add the following lines to your *patTuple\_standard\_cfg.py* file:
```
## jet selector
from PhysicsTools.PatAlgos.selectionLayer1.jetSelector_cfi import *
<!--verbatim14-->

```

## uncomment the following line to add different jet collections

# 4.2.4 Physics Analysis Toolkit (): Tutorial
##  tutorials were discontinued in 2016, replaced by expanded CMSDAS, HATS etc
## Contents
* [/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATTutorial#IntroDuction)
* [Lectures](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATTutorial#PatLectures)
* [Exercises](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATTutorial#PatExercises)
* [More Exercises](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATTutorial#MoreExercises)
* [Review status](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATTutorial#ReviewStatus)
## Introduction
There exists a series of ** Tutorials**, which are held at cern. You can find the next  Tutorial announced on [SWGuidePAT](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuidePAT). Have a look at [indico![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](http://indico.cern.ch/categoryDisplay.py?categId=2063) and [the CMS elearning area![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://espace.cern.ch/learncms/default.aspx) to more about the Tutorials that have already taken place. On this page you can find a set of lectures, documentation and exercises for your personal studies. The following pages might be of help before getting started:
* [WorkBookPATGlossary](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATGlossary): more about commonly used  expressions.
* [WorkBookBasicCPlusPlus](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookBasicCPlusPlus): Find a good start into the basics of C++ needed for this Tutorial.
* [WorkBookConfigFileIntro](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookConfigFileIntro): Find a good summary about the python configuration language.
* [WorkBookPATDataFormats](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATDataFormats): Get an overview of the  Data Formats.
* [WorkBookPATWorkflow](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATWorkflow): Get an overview of the  .
* [WorkBookPATConfiguration](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATConfiguration): how to configure  Data Formats and .
* [WorkBookTroubleShooting](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookTroubleShooting): In case of trouble when compiling/running modules.
If you have more question or need more of support have a look at [SWGuidePAT#Support](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuidePAT#Support).
## Lectures
You can find a list of recent lectures and documentation pages about  below:
1. [Lecture 1.1![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://indico.cern.ch/getFile.py/access?contribId=22&sessionId=2&resId=0&materialId=slides&confId=255899):  introduction.  **(Jul2013)**
2. [Lecture 1.2![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://indico.cern.ch/getFile.py/access?contribId=1&sessionId=3&resId=1&materialId=slides&confId=255899): how to access *::Candidates* with an EDAnalyzer or FWLite executable.  **(Jul2013)**
3. [Lecture 2.1![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://indico.cern.ch/getFile.py/access?contribId=50&sessionId=4&resId=0&materialId=slides&confId=255899): more about how  supports object cross cleaning.  **(Jul2013)**
4. [Lecture 2.2![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://indico.cern.ch/getFile.py/access?contribId=17&resId=0&materialId=slides&confId=138838): more about how to configure the and event content of a *::Tuple*.  **(Jul2013)**
5. [Lecture 3.2![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://indico.cern.ch/getFile.py/access?contribId=0&resId=0&materialId=slides&confId=159741): more about how  supports matching to trigger objects or truth information.  **(Jul2013)**
6. [Lecture 4.1![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://indico.cern.ch/getFile.py/access?contribId=49&resId=0&materialId=slides&confId=217169): something about triggers, especially HLT, in CMS from the software point of .  **(Jul2013)**
7. [Lecture 4.2![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://indico.cern.ch/getFile.py/access?contribId=2&resId=0&materialId=slides&confId=217169): more about the production, configuration and use of the *::TriggerEvent*.  **(Jul2013)**
8. [Lecture 4.3![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://indico.cern.ch/getFile.py/access?contribId=38&resId=0&materialId=slides&confId=187161): more about trigger matches to *::Candidates*.  **(Jul2013)**
9. [Lecture 5![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://indico.cern.ch/getFile.py/access?contribId=21&resId=0&materialId=slides&confId=138838): more about access to particle flow objects in  (PFBRECO).  **(Jul2013)**
These lectures are being updated for each  Tutorial every ~6 Month. The of last update is indicated in brackets.
## Exercises
You can find a set of TWiki based Tutorial Exercises below. All exercises require:**Requirements**
* A working cern account.
* At least *2GB* of free space in your afs directory. In case you need some more space increase your quota here: [CERN Resources Portal: AFS Workspaces![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://resources.web.cern.ch/resources/Manage/AFS/Settings.aspx)
* Some knowledge of C++. Have a look to [WorkBookBasicCPlusPlus](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookBasicCPlusPlus) to get a quick overhaul of the C++ you need.
* Some minimal knowledge of CMSSW.
![ALERT!](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/warning.gif "ALERT!") **Note:**This web course that is presented below is part of the [ Tutorial](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATTutorial), which takes regularly place at cern and in other places. When following the  Tutorial the answers of questions marked in RED on these TWiki pages should be filled into the exercise form that has been introduced at the beginning of the tutorial. Also the solutions to the Exercises found on these TWiki pages should be filled into the form. The exercises are marked in three colours, indicating whether this exercise is basic (obligatory), continuative (recommended) or optional (free). The colour coding is summarized in the table below:
| [Color Code](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATTutorial?sortcol=0;table=1;up=0#sorted_table "Sort by this column") | [Explanation](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATTutorial?sortcol=1;table=1;up=0#sorted_table "Sort by this column") |
| --- | --- |
| ![red](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/pub/TWiki/SmiliesPlugin/red.gif "red") | Basic exercise, which is obligatory for the  Tutorial. |
| ![yellow](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/pub/TWiki/SmiliesPlugin/yellow.gif "yellow") | Continuative exercise, which is recommended for the  Tutorial to deepen what has been learned. |
| ![green](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/pub/TWiki/SmiliesPlugin/green.gif "green") | Optional exercise, which shows interesting applications of what has been learned. |
Basic exercises ( ![red](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/pub/TWiki/SmiliesPlugin/red.gif "red") ) are obliged and the solutions to the exercises should be filled into the exercise form during the  Tutorial.**Pre-exercises:**If you are feeling unsafe about how to do the preparation you have to do for the exercises indicated below you can follow the
* [WorkBookPATTutorialPreExercises](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATTutorialPreExercises) (responsible: )  **()** .
**Week exercise**For the [Tutorial![](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/external-link.gif)](https://indico.cern.ch/event/314115/) there is an over-spanning exercise from the area of Top-Physics that the participants should work on during the week. You can find this example on [WorkBookPATWeekExercise](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATWeekExercise) (responsible: )  **()** .**:**
* **Week exercise**: In this exercise you should apply learnt knowledge on a simplified physics problem: [WorkBookPATWeekExercise](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATWeekExercise).
* Monday
  + [Exercise 01]: [WorkBookPATDocNavigationExercise](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATDocNavigationExercise): Use of the  documentation
     (responsible: Till Arndt, Justin Pilot)  **(Jun2015)** .
  + [Exercise 02]: [/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATTupleCreationExercise): How to create a standard  tuple
     (responsible: Till Arndt, Justin Pilot)  **(Jun2015)** .
  + [Exercise 03]: [SWGuidePATConfigExercise](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuidePATConfigExercise): More detailed exercise on how to configure your own  tuple
     (responsible: Till Arndt, Justin Pilot)  **(Jun2015)** .
  + [Exercise 04]: [WorkBookPATAccessExercise](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATAccessExercise): How to access objects from a standard  tuple
     (responsible: Till Arndt, Justin Pilot)  **(Jun2015)** .
* Tuesday:
  + [Exercise 05]: [SWGuidePATCrossObjectCollectionExercise](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuidePATCrossObjectCollectionExercise): More detailed exercise on object disambiguation support in
     (responsible: , )  **()** .
  + [Exercise 06]:  [SWGuidePATAnalysisTasksExercise](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuidePATAnalysisTasksExercise): More detailed exercise on embedding extra information in
     (responsible: , )  **()** .
* Wednesday:
  + [Exercise 07]: [SWGuidePATFWLiteMiniaodExercise](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuidePATFWLiteMiniaodExercise): exercise on FWLite and MINIAOD
     (responsible:   **(Jul2015)** . (Before the june 2015 tutorial, there was a dedicated exercise on the PF2PAT , [SWGuidePATPF2PATExercise](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuidePATPF2PATExercise).)
* Thursday:
  + [Exercise 08]: [SWGuidePATMCMatchingExercise](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuidePATMCMatchingExercise): More detailed exercise on the support of MC truth matching in
     (responsible: )  **(Jul2015)** .
  + [Exercise 09]: [WorkBookPATTriggerExercise](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATTriggerExercise): more detailed exercise on the consideration of HLT paths in analysis
     (responsible: , , )  **()** .
  + [Exercise 10]: [SWGuidePATTriggerEventExercise](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuidePATTriggerEventExercise): more detailed exercise on the creation and configuration of the  trigger event
     (responsible: , )  **()** .
* Friday:
  + [Exercise 11]: [SWGuidePATTriggerMatchExercise](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuidePATTriggerMatchExercise): more detailed exercise on the support of trigger object matching in
     (responsible: , )  **()** .
The [WorkBookPAT](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPAT) exercises form a basic set of what you have to know about the production of *::Tuples* and the access to *::Candidates*. The [SWGuidePAT](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/SWGuidePAT) exercises are more comprehensive demonstrations and examples of the features and the use of .
## More Exercises
You can find some more comprehensive examples of the use of  within special POG and PAG applications below:**PAG Applications of :**In this section you can find a set of links to tutorials illustrating the typical use of  within your Physics Analysis Group (PAG):
* [WorkBookPATExampleQCD](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATExampleQCD): Analysis example for QCD
   (responsible: ).  **()**
* [WorkBookPATExampleTopQuarks](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATExampleTopQuarks): Analysis example for Top Physics outdated
   (responsible: ).  **(Apr2011)**
* [WorkBookPATExampleSUSY](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATExampleSUSY): Analysis example for SUSY
   (responsible: ).  **()**
* [WorkBookPATExampleZMuMu](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATExampleZMuMu): Analysis examples based on Z-->μμ event
   (responsible: ).  **()**
* [WorkBookPATExampleElectroweak](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATExampleElectroweak): Analysis example for EWK Physics
   (responsible: ).
* [WorkBookPATExampleExotica](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATExampleExotica): Analysis example for Exotica
   (responsible: ).
* [WorkBookPATExampleHiggs](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATExampleHiggs): Analysis example for Higgs Physics
   (responsible: Nicola de Filippis).
**POG Applications of :**
* [WorkBookPATExampleJet](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATExampleJet): how to do a simple analysis with ::Jets.  **()**
* [WorkBookPATExampleMET](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATExampleMET): how to do a simple analysis with .
* [WorkBookPATExamplePhoton](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATExamplePhoton): how to do a simple analysis with ::Photons.
* : how to do a simple analysis with ::Electrons.
* [WorkBookPATExampleMuon](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATExampleMuon): how to do a simple analysis with ::Muons.
* [WorkBookPATExampleTau](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATExampleTau): how to do a simple analysis with ::Taus.
* [WorkBookPATExampleTrigger](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATExampleTrigger): how to do a simple analysis with the ::TriggerEvent.
* [WorkBookPATExampleTrackBJet](/twiki/bin//CMSPublic/WorkBookPATExampleTrackBJet): how to do a simple analysis including tracking, vertexing and b-tagging.
![ALERT!](/twiki/pub/TWiki/TWikiDocGraphics/warning.gif "ALERT!") **Note:**These tutorials will cover the typical but only basic use of  in a simple POG/PAG specific application. They provide you with the following information:
* A small number of EDAnalyer(s) or EDProducer(s) of manageable complexity.
* A , which highlights one or two PAG specific analysis aspects.
* The typical content of ::Candidate, which your PAG has agreed upon.
* A short summary how the ::Candiates were configured (when different from the  default).
* The PAG specific use of ::Candidates and tools (e.g. certain aspects of cleaning, or a special use of isolation variables).
* Links to further PAG specific information.
The examples may refer to other parts of official code.
